Develop communication skills through oral and written presentations.

Evaluate different engineering situations and judgments based on ethical codes and professional responsibilities.

Propose ideas/solutions for real-life problems based on the learned knowledge.

ARCH503.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH503 Building Construction Detailing
ARCH503.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH503
Study of different construction methods of architectural spaces and the selection of suitable finishing materials related to function; evaluation of technical and aesthetic aspects of interior and exterior finishing materials; technical criteria for selection and evaluation of finishing materials; architectural working details and workshop drawings.
Building Construction Detailing (ARCH503) > Credit Hours : 3

Building Construction Detailing (ARCH503) > Prerequisites
ARCH425 with a minimum grade D
Building Construction Detailing (ARCH503) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply technical construction methods and information necessary to produce accurate building details.

Undertake professional drafting for the final stage of construction drawings.

Examine architectural working details technically, and coherently.

Use online sources in solving technical problems of construction methods and material selection of interior finishes

ARCH509.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH509 Modeling and Simulation
ARCH509.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH509
This course focuses on advanced levels of experimentation, analysis, synthesis and application of existing and emerging digital applications for simulating urban & building form and performance at an integrated level. Areas of emphasis include 3D modeling tools, modeling of urban, building, environmental, acoustical and visual performance, as well as energy consumption and production. Projects focus on resolving complex and integrated urban and engineering design solutions through digital simulations.
Modeling and Simulation (ARCH509) > Credit Hours : 3

Modeling and Simulation (ARCH509) > Prerequisites
ARCH335 with a minimum grade D
Modeling and Simulation (ARCH509) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop knowledge, skills and competencies using current digital tools and technologies that enable more creative design.

Analyze design concepts using integrated professional design software.

Use advanced building information modeling technologies to model and retrieve building information in the building lifecycle from design to facility management.

ARCH510.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH510 Desert Landscape Design and Water Management
ARCH510.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH510
This course addresses on the integrated design of water-conscious landscapes in the built environment within arid and hot climate contexts, with particular emphasis on the United Arab Emirates. It examines water as a critical resource across buildings, landscapes, and urban systems, highlighting its environmental and energy interdependencies. Students explore water use and performance through evaluation frameworks and develop strategies for improving efficiency in building and landscape contexts. The course then expands into landscape design across scales, addressing public and private realms, user needs, and the role of landscape as a functional, social, and productive system. Building on this foundation, students develop climate-responsive landscape design solutions with a focus on desert environments and xeriscaping, including plant selection, hydrozoning, and irrigation integration. Through hands-on exercises and a comprehensive design project, students produce integrated proposals that balance environmental performance, water management, and design quality. AI-supported tools are introduced to assist in design exploration, plant selection, and visualization.
Desert Landscape Design and Water Management (ARCH510) > Credit Hours : 3

Desert Landscape Design and Water Management (ARCH510) > Prerequisites
ARCH335 with a minimum grade D
Desert Landscape Design and Water Management (ARCH510) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze water uses and flows in the built environment within arid contexts.

Evaluate water performance using established frameworks and assessment methods.

Apply strategies to improve water efficiency in building and landscape contexts.

Design integrated, climate-responsive landscape solutions incorporating plant selection, water management, environmental considerations, and AI-supported design exploration.

Communicate design proposals through visual, graphical, and oral presentation methods, including AI-assisted visualization techniques.

ARCH515.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH515 Artificial Intelligence Applications in Architectural Engineering
ARCH515.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH515
This course provides an advanced Application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) based on applicable methodologies in Architectural Engineering. Students investigate machine learning, generative AI, optimization algorithms, computer vision, large language models, and AI-assisted decision-making for architectural design, construction management, building performance analysis, and intelligent building operation. Through lectures, laboratory sessions, computational modelling, programming, and project-based learning, students develop AI-enabled workflows, integrate AI with Building Information Modeling (BIM) and simulation platforms, and evaluate AI-driven engineering solutions using quantitative performance metrics. The course also addresses ethical, legal, sustainability, and professional implications associated with AI implementation in the built environment while exposing students to emerging research and professional practice.
Artificial Intelligence Applications in Architectural Engineering (ARCH515) > Credit Hours : 3

Artificial Intelligence Applications in Architectural Engineering (ARCH515) > Prerequisites
GENG215 with a minimum grade D

ARCH335 with a minimum grade D
Artificial Intelligence Applications in Architectural Engineering (ARCH515) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate Artificial Intelligence methodologies and determine their suitability for solving complex architectural engineering problems.

Integrate AI techniques into architectural engineering workflows for building design, construction, building performance analysis, and intelligent building operation.

Develop AI-assisted computational models using programming environments and professional AI software to support engineering analysis, decision-making, and optimization.

Assess AI-generated engineering solutions by considering technical performance, sustainability, ethics, professional responsibility, and societal impacts within the built environment.

ARCH525.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH525 Life Cycle Assessment in the Built Environment
ARCH525.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH525
This course introduces the principles and applications of Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) in the built environment. It examines how environmental impacts are evaluated across the life cycle of materials, systems, and projects, from raw material extraction and manufacturing to use, maintenance, and end-of-life. Students are introduced to key LCA concepts, standards, system boundaries, functional units, inventory data, and impact categories. The course also explores environmental product declarations (EPDs), whole-project LCA, and links to circular economy and sustainability frameworks. Through lectures, case studies, and practical exercises, students learn to interpret LCA results and apply life-cycle thinking to design and decision-making.
Life Cycle Assessment in the Built Environment (ARCH525) > Credit Hours : 3

Life Cycle Assessment in the Built Environment (ARCH525) > Prerequisites
GENG315 with a minimum grade D
Life Cycle Assessment in the Built Environment (ARCH525) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the fundamental principles, terminology, and methodological framework of Life Cycle Assessment in the built environment.

Analyze the life cycle environmental impacts of materials, components, systems, and project alternatives using appropriate LCA boundaries, data, and indicators.

Evaluate design, material, and system alternatives based on life cycle environmental performance and sustainability considerations.

Apply life cycle thinking to support decision-making related to material selection, design development, and environmental performance in the built environment.

Communicate LCA-based findings and recommendations effectively through written, graphical, and oral presentation formats.

ARCH526.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH526 Specification and Quantity Surveying
ARCH526.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH526
This course aims at introducing the principles and theories of preparing Specification and Bill of Quantities documents for construction projects involving building components such as site work, concrete, masonry, steel, glass, finishes, and carpentry. Bidding requirements, construction contracts, methods of specifying, substitutions, and warranties with emphasis on building codes as applied to construction projects. Use of relevant application software packages.
Specification and Quantity Surveying (ARCH526) > Credit Hours : 3

Specification and Quantity Surveying (ARCH526) > Prerequisites
GENG315 with a minimum grade D
Specification and Quantity Surveying (ARCH526) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate the principles and theories on preparing Specification and Bill of Quantities documents.

Illustrate the use of Specification and BOQ within construction project as part of the contract and the bidding requirements.

Develop a bottom-up quantity take-off for different building component material, using a real project.

Develop a BOQ for a real project per CSI breakdown, along with a specification manual.

ARCH530.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH530 Selected Topics In Architecture Engineering
ARCH530.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH530
This course aims at offering an opportunity to study selected architectural topics of interest. Topics are related to one area of architecture education. Application varies depending on selected topics and conducted under the supervision of a faculty member.
Selected Topics In Architecture Engineering (ARCH530) > Credit Hours : 3

Selected Topics In Architecture Engineering (ARCH530) > Prerequisites
GENG315 with a minimum grade D
Selected Topics In Architecture Engineering (ARCH530) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify potential issues in architectural engineering impacting the design, construction and indoor climate.

Apply finding of research and critical analysis to formulate a comprehensively effective solution addressing a particular issue.

Analyze the solution based on environmental, resource and energy efficiency constraints.

Present and defend the solution effectively based on merits of environmental friendliness and resource efficiency.

ARCH532.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH532 Sustainable Architecture & Urban Environments in Hot Climate
ARCH532.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH532
Characteristics of hot climates and analysis of comfort conditions. Employing natural resources to improve harsh desert conditions. Studying the adverse impact on energy costs, greenhouse gas emissions, and environmental problems. Learning sustainable design and urbanism from vernacular architecture and settlements and new innovative constructions. Integrative design with performance analysis using simulation tools. Detailing design and technologies to shape the built environment: cool microclimates and greenery, advanced building skins, building materials, passive cooling and integration with energy efficient active systems.
Sustainable Architecture & Urban Environments in Hot Climate (ARCH532) > Credit Hours : 3

Sustainable Architecture & Urban Environments in Hot Climate (ARCH532) > Prerequisites
ARCH433 with a minimum grade D
Sustainable Architecture & Urban Environments in Hot Climate (ARCH532) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the environmental impacts of urbanization / buildings and discuss implications of using non-renewable energy.

Categorize the appropriate urban and architectural responses in hot arid and hot humid climates.

Demonstrate the requirements of Green buildings and choose optimum strategies.

Analyze critically the strategies used in green buildings that responds to climate and meets the fundamental requirements of energy efficiency and water conservation.

ARCH542.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH542 Housing and Urban Design
ARCH542.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH542
This course aims at introducing housing and urban design theories. Topics include housing typologies, organizations and processes, housing management and development, characteristics of urban spaces, strategic management, public policy analysis, housing research and innovations in housing and urban spaces.
Housing and Urban Design (ARCH542) > Credit Hours : 3

Housing and Urban Design (ARCH542) > Prerequisites
ARCH335 with a minimum grade D
Housing and Urban Design (ARCH542) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Define housing and urban design strategies, theories, policies and practices driven from the literature and multiple case studies.

Assess an urban design and housing setting in the UAE based on learned planning theories and practices.

Connect planning information with urban design and housing projects needs and development.

Generate and analyze a master plan for an existing/proposed urban design and housing area based on various approaches that emphasize sustainable development

Present and communicate the city in both two and three-dimensional drawings.

ARCH551.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH551 Urban Planning & Infrastructure
ARCH551.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH551
This course aims at introducing city planning theories and processes, including topics such as city forms, neighborhoods, urban systems; land use planning. Basic principles of infrastructure planning, operation and design of physical infrastructure system including roads, services, public transportation, public open spaces and facilities
Urban Planning & Infrastructure (ARCH551) > Credit Hours : 3

Urban Planning & Infrastructure (ARCH551) > Prerequisites
ARCH335
Urban Planning & Infrastructure (ARCH551) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe physical form and space to make connections with history and planning theories towards urban planning practices.

Assess and interpret residential neighborhood in the Emirates, and elsewhere, based on different planning and design standards.

Evaluate data towards informed decision-making planning process.

Work in teams to analyze, discuss and communicate planning problems and views, on neighborhood level, based on multiple approaches and presentations techniques.

Comprehend the impact of planning on society and sustainable development at various levels.

ARCH585.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH585 Design and Critical Thinking in Architectural Engineering
ARCH585.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH585
This course develops a capstone design project related to the real needs of society. An engineering design process is initiated through research, and then developed though literature review, data gathering, analysis, initial design development, assessment of alternatives and project documentation. This course emphasizes research, analysis, identification of applicable codes and standards, conceptual design development, evaluation of alternative concepts, and the production of a preliminary technical report and visual presentation materials. ARCH590.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH590 Capstone Engineering Design Project
ARCH590.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH590
This course develops a final capstone design based on initial development previously prepared during the Graduation Project I course. Further project research is conducted, detailed engineering design solutions are prepared, design alternatives are evaluated in compliance with local and international building codes and standards, and performance verification is conducted. Capstone Engineering Design Project (ARCH590) > Credit Hours : 3

Capstone Engineering Design Project (ARCH590) > Prerequisites
ARCH585 with a minimum grade D
Capstone Engineering Design Project (ARCH590) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Independent of faculty involvement, manage a team of students in the analysis, design, representation and expression of a design solution to a multi-disciplinary engineering problem [1,3,4,5]

Responsibly apply math, science and engineering principles, techniques, skills and tools to the design an engineering system, component or process to meet desired needs in a global and societal context [1,2,4,6]

Take a leadership role in developing engineering analysis and design work in relevant project-specific sub-topics [1,2,6,7]

ARCH600.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH600 Research Methods
ARCH600.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH600
The course constructs on critical thinking to advance research design and methods approaches. It provides students’ guidance and recognition to identify a research problem, form a research question, and select a relevant method to test a particular hypothesis. It deals with qualitative, quantitative, and mixed research methods. In particular, students learn multiple research tools, analyzing evidence, drawing conclusions, and presenting results. The course also deals with academic skills such as research presentation, writing of literature review, research proposal, time management, and ethical issues in research.
Research Methods (ARCH600) > Credit Hours : 3

Research Methods (ARCH600) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate the value of research in architectural engineering.

Apply multiple research methods customized to solve real world challenges.

Illustrate that theory, epistemology, and methodology are interrelated aspects of inquiry.

Define particular research question and develop research proposal towards problem solving and implementation of actual research design and field work.

ARCH601.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH601 Graduate Research Seminar
ARCH601.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH601
Students present and debate advanced architectural research topics within the graduate program field under the facilitation and steering of a faculty. Guest speakers including faculty may be invited as appropriate to address current research issues pertaining to architectural engineering
Graduate Research Seminar (ARCH601) > Credit Hours : 0

Graduate Research Seminar (ARCH601) > Corequisites
ARCH600 with a minimum grade C
Graduate Research Seminar (ARCH601) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Critically analyze research papers and presentations in architectural engineering.

Explain research strategies, approaches and findings.

Recognize State-Of-The-Art Research Topics related to the Built Environment.

ARCH602.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH602 Sustainable Urbanism
ARCH602.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH602
This course focuses on the concepts and practices of sustainable urbanism associated with high performance buildings. The course examines the processes that shape the form and function of the built environment in its full complexity that collectively make up planning and design of contemporary cities, neighborhoods and settlements. The course provides students with experiential learning in the application of the current theories, models and methods used in science, engineering, architecture and urban planning to specific, real-world issues of sustainable urbanism globally and locally in the UAE region.
Sustainable Urbanism (ARCH602) > Credit Hours : 3

Sustainable Urbanism (ARCH602) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate a general understanding of the complexities and crucial issues of sustainable urbanism concepts and challenges.

Develop awareness and advance of multiple driving forces that affect shaping the built environment performance towards equality, ecological balance and energy efficiency.

Describe the impact of environmental crucial issues using tools of sustainable urbanism.

Develop the skills to address the interdisciplinary aspect to provide scenarios and development plan that are appropriate to society and cities urban context.

ARCH603.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH603 High Performance Buildings
ARCH603.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH603
The course integrates all major high-performance building attributes including energy efficiency, durability, life-cycle performance, occupant wellbeing, and productivity, and emerging sustainable technologies. The course specifically addresses buildings sustainability issues existing in the UAE desert environment such as the excessive heat in the indoors/outdoors, the shortage of water and the excessive dust/air pollution. The course strengthens knowledge on sustainable sites and integrates passive and low energy strategies/renewable energy systems for conserving energy, water and other natural resources. The course emphasizes on mitigating potential negative impacts on the human health/comfort and the environment considering local and international sustainable building codes, standards and rating certification systems.
High Performance Buildings (ARCH603) > Credit Hours : 3

High Performance Buildings (ARCH603) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate advanced knowledge of energy efficiency, durability and life-cycle performance of engineering activities.

Analyze impact of incorporating high performance engineering practices on occupant wellbeing and environment through critical analysis.

Demonstrate advance research and team work skills involving peer reviews and oral presentations.

ARCH608.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH608 Design Management for the Built Environment
ARCH608.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH608
This course focuses on current and developing approaches to design management, with special focus on high performance built environment which optimizes life-cycle performance. The course considers: client engagement and control, briefing processes and approaches, and the organization of integrated multi-disciplinary design processes, tasks, and teams. While different levels of the built environment from buildings to cities are considered, the interface of design with policy and business, and with construction and operation is also explored.
Design Management for the Built Environment (ARCH608) > Credit Hours : 3

Design Management for the Built Environment (ARCH608) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Define current challenges and opportunities for design management of high performance built environment.

Explain the principles of managing multi-disciplinary teams and processes for buildings and urban environments with high performance attributes.

Recognize the different roles and responsibilities of multiple stakeholders engaged in the development of high performing built environment.

Describe different approaches and phases for design and briefing of high performance built environment.

ARCH614.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH614 Sustainable Community Develop
ARCH614.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH614
Concepts and techniques, spatial aesthetics, social, cultural, technical and marketing issues, integration into existing urban system morphology of today?s urban development in the Gulf, common patterns and forms of urban development within the Gulf urban environments, investigation of magnets and forces that induce the interest in the development of urban spaces. Topics include: impact on suburb cities, urban master plans, spatial composition and infrastructures, real estate development, urban growth control and management, role of critical analysis, assessment, valuing through community participation feedback in creating appropriate development, case studies
Sustainable Community Develop (ARCH614) > Credit Hours : 3

Sustainable Community Develop (ARCH614) > Prerequisites
ARCH602 with a minimum grade C
Sustainable Community Develop (ARCH614) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Comprehend the main principles and schools of thought of sustainable community development.

Understand the major challenges facing the realization of sustainable community development.

Gain knowledge about the key role of neighborhood planning in socio-culturally, environmentally and economically sustainable community development.

Develop appropriate solutions for the problems hindering realization of sustainable community development appropriate of the studied community.

ARCH616.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH616 Impact Assessment for the Built Environment
ARCH616.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH616
This course introduces a systematic process for predicting, and evaluating the significant environmental consequences of a proposed action or undertaking in the built environment. It provides the students with an understanding of the guidelines for EIA; ecologically sustainable built environment; impact evaluation in terms of environmental criteria; procedures, techniques and future directions. Mitigation measures identified to avoid, minimize or remedy adverse impacts on the environment.
Impact Assessment for the Built Environment (ARCH616) > Credit Hours : 3

Impact Assessment for the Built Environment (ARCH616) > Prerequisites
ARCH602 with a minimum grade C
Impact Assessment for the Built Environment (ARCH616) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) & Mitigation processes and stages in the built environment.

Conduct the screening, scoping and report review stages of EIA based on existing requirements.

Discuss the stages and operation of EIA & M processes in the context of sustainable built environment.

Communicate the EIA and Mitigation strategies.

ARCH617.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH617 Selected Topics in Architectural Engineering
ARCH617.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH617
Variable content course addressing in depth analysis of selected topics pertaining to the architectural engineering graduate research with a specific theme indicated by course title listed in program semester course offering Schedule. Course can be taken only once.
Selected Topics in Architectural Engineering (ARCH617) > Credit Hours : 3

Selected Topics in Architectural Engineering (ARCH617) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate discussion and presentation skills.

Discuss graduate research process.

Demonstrate familiarity with a program research specialization.

Develop research and writing skills.

ARCH623.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH623 Integrated Construction Tools and Processes
ARCH623.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH623
This course provides the students with the knowledge and skills for the use of information management and technology tools and processes for the development of high-performance built environment. This includes information management and visualization tools and technologies for integrated multi-disciplinary work and teams across the whole life-cycle of the built environment. The course provides the students with hands-on experience of digital modelling and simulation tools to coordinate and manage digital information for an enhanced delivery of high performing buildings and urban infrastructure.
Integrated Construction Tools and Processes (ARCH623) > Credit Hours : 3

Integrated Construction Tools and Processes (ARCH623) > Prerequisites
ARCH608 with a minimum grade C
Integrated Construction Tools and Processes (ARCH623) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Define challenges, opportunities and complexities of integrated construction supply chain and working in multi-disciplinary teams utilizing appropriate digital processes and tools.

Appraise established and emerging information management and digital tools for coordinating design, construction and operations of high performance built environment.

Describe the challenges of inter-operability and integrating operating systems across the supply chain.

Apply advanced skills in developing and interrogating technology and information management tools to facilitate integrated, better valued, design and construction of built assets.

ARCH631.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH631 Advanced Illumination and Daylighting
ARCH631.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH631
The course provides in-depth understanding of advanced topics on lighting issues and systems design and integration in high performance buildings. The covered topics include energy efficiency, visual quality and comfort, integration of lighting/daylighting, energy benefits and integration with other passive/active systems, innovative illumination concepts and design, advanced topics of photometry, colorimetry, measurement and control of light, daylight autonomy and analysis, climate-based daylight models, design skies, modeling and simulation techniques of daylight, advanced systems of fenestration design, skylights and atria daylight design, impact of daylight on building indoor lively quality.
Advanced Illumination and Daylighting (ARCH631) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Illumination and Daylighting (ARCH631) > Prerequisites
ARCH602 with a minimum grade C

ARCH603 with a minimum grade C
Advanced Illumination and Daylighting (ARCH631) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply advanced skills in developing and interrogating technology and information management tools to facilitate integrated, better valued, design and construction of built assets.

Design high performance lighting systems, components, or technologies to meet desired standards and client needs.

Apply effectively lighting and energy simulations tools to evaluate design problems and compare among several solutions.

Solve lighting availability and visual comfort problems.

Communicate effectively design and research ideas.

ARCH632.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH632 Climate Research in Build Energy Efficiency
ARCH632.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH632
The interrelationship between thermal and architectural design of buildings with respect to planning, design, operation and energy management. estimating building energy demands and predicting energy performance. Effect of climate on human comfort. Overall energy performance and climate-responsiveness as a design strategy for energy conservation, building envelope components' design for minimal energy consumption, Operation dynamics, and impact of building sub-systems integration on building's overall thermal efficiency. Energy operation, auditing and management, new directions in building energy conservation.
Climate Research in Build Energy Efficiency (ARCH632) > Credit Hours : 3

Climate Research in Build Energy Efficiency (ARCH632) > Prerequisites
ARCH602 with a minimum grade C

ARCH603 with a minimum grade C
Climate Research in Build Energy Efficiency (ARCH632) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Critically describe the relationship and impacts of climate and the built environment

Assess present applicability of passive design strategies in traditional built environment

Recognize issues and strategies of reducing carbon emissions in the built Environment

Assess issues and opportunities for zero energy buildings

Demonstrate professional and ethical written and oral communication skills, with the aptitude to convey complex ideas clearly, and logically

ARCH633.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH633 Water Efficiency in the Built Environment
ARCH633.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH633
The course advances students’ knowledge and skills on current and emerging issues of water management, water efficiency and water and energy nexus in the built environment. The course covers water resources and challenges, water quality, water and health, integrated site and building water management, innovative water collection and regeneration, advanced water conservation practices and applications indoors and outdoors, water treatment and recycling systems and desert landscaping and irrigation. The course involves substantial literature research on developing topics through assignments.
Water Efficiency in the Built Environment (ARCH633) > Credit Hours : 3

Water Efficiency in the Built Environment (ARCH633) > Prerequisites
ARCH602 with a minimum grade C

ARCH603 with a minimum grade C
Water Efficiency in the Built Environment (ARCH633) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate knowledge of water resources, quality, conservation and reclaim through detailed literature research

Identify advanced solutions for water related issues in built environment

Apply statistical and numerical skills to evaluate solutions based on resource and energy efficiency

Communicate complex concepts and solution effectively

ARCH634.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH634 Building Science Experiment Research Lab
ARCH634.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH634
Building science experimental exercises pertaining to testing, analyzing and assessing building materials and components, topics cover thermal, acoustical, and luminous characteristics of building materials and building interiors. Exercises on instrumentation, measurement and logging techniques for environmental data gathering inside labs and outside in the field. Typical exercises introduce students to the measurement of temperature, air flow and humidity as well as lighting flux, intensity, distribution, acoustical measurements, heat flux meters, flow meters, energy meters, infrared thermo-graphic camera.
Building Science Experiment Research Lab (ARCH634) > Credit Hours : 3

Building Science Experiment Research Lab (ARCH634) > Prerequisites
ARCH603 with a minimum grade C
Building Science Experiment Research Lab (ARCH634) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Formulate problems related to the built environment

Analyze data qualitatively and quantitatively related to energy efficiency and conservation in building

Conduct experimentation of building energy analysis using comprehensive computer energy simulation tools

Conduct economic analysis based on the life-cycle cost building components

Perform parametric analysis to evaluate the effects of building components on energy use

ARCH635.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH635 Fenestration Analysis & Design
ARCH635.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH635
Fenestration thermal, acoustical and optical properties, monolithic, laminated, insulating glazing, thermal resistance and U-factor, daylight utilization potential and visual performance, fenestration components and systems, single and multi-pane window systems, window frames, glass types, low-E, and tinted low-E glazing. Windows, glass doors, curtain wall, and skylights design. Performance analysis of transparent thermal envelope design, thermal and optical simulations of fenestration systems and effect of overhangs. Analysis of the annual energy usage and peak demand as a function of glazing type, size, and control strategy, measurements of the net heat flow through glazing, infrared thermograph, fenestration energy ratings, electrochromic, gas filled, vacuum glazing and fenestration recent advances.
Fenestration Analysis & Design (ARCH635) > Credit Hours : 3

Fenestration Analysis & Design (ARCH635) > Prerequisites
ARCH603 with a minimum grade C
Fenestration Analysis & Design (ARCH635) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the relationship between fenestration solutions and occupants’ comfort and needs.

Recognize the energy rating and certification process of windows and fenestration systems

Select fenestration systems for optimizing energy savings and daylighting performance

Analyze the energy and environmental benefits of advanced fenestration systems

Demonstrate written and oral communication skills, with the aptitude to convey complex ideas clearly, and logically.

ARCH636.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH636 Building Ventilation
ARCH636.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH636
Natural, mechanical and hybrid ventilation, climatic influences, uncontrolled air infiltration and exfiltration, building air tightness, airflow behavior around buildings, occupancy patterns and pollutant emission characteristics as determinants of ventilation requirements and demands, ventilation strategies, design, analysis and performance of ventilation systems for comfort and cooling, optimal ventilation utilization and air energy recovery for achieving energy-efficient building design, analytical methods, Ventilation Performance Indicators, Standards and Regulations and key selected topics in building ventilation, relevant to all building types computing tools.
Building Ventilation (ARCH636) > Credit Hours : 3

Building Ventilation (ARCH636) > Prerequisites
ARCH603 with a minimum grade C
Building Ventilation (ARCH636) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the physical fundamentals of natural and mechanical ventilation and its relationship to human comfort.

Comprehend basic HVAC terminology, systems and design processes and apply these fundamentals to practical design problems

Compute cooling loads and AC energy consumption using fundamental heat and mass balances on buildings and system components

Recognize usefulness and limitations of airflow network tools and Apply CFD to assess the passive and active ventilation potential of a building

ARCH695.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH695 Technical Project
ARCH695.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH695
This course emphasizes independent work on Architectural Engineering project, where students take the lead in designing, simulating, modelling, developing, or conducting experiments. The student is responsible for planning and executing the project with guidance from a faculty member. The student applies engineering principles to solve real-world problems, utilizing tools and techniques specific to their field. The student also manages project timelines, resources, and communication, while the faculty member supervising the project provides technical oversight to ensure quality, accuracy, and feasibility. The course concludes with a detailed written report and an oral presentation of the project’s outcomes.
Technical Project (ARCH695) > Credit Hours : 6

Technical Project (ARCH695) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop a work plan for a technical project in the field of Architectural Engineering.

Apply advanced design skills to a specific problem related to the high performance-built environment.

Report findings in a well written technical report.

Present results at a high level of proficiency.

ARCH698.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH698 Research Based Design Project
ARCH698.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH698
Design of built form with emphasis on research based issues related to architectural design and planning. This includes theoretical issues, in urban planning, urban design, project management, building technology, and architectural issues such as meaning, principles of order; alternative means of enclosing architectural space; synthesis of space, light, structure, materials, and environmental control systems. Design as a form of inquiry integrating all knowledge gained by student inside and outside the design disciplines.
Research Based Design Project (ARCH698) > Credit Hours : 3

Research Based Design Project (ARCH698) > Prerequisites
ARCH600 with a minimum grade C

ARCH601 with a minimum grade P

ARCH602 with a minimum grade C

ARCH603 with a minimum grade C

ARCH605 with a minimum grade C

ARCH608 with a minimum grade C
Research Based Design Project (ARCH698) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate the health and safety practice in construction project planning and delivery time.

Demonstrate Professional And Ethical Research And Scientific Writing And Oral Skills.

Identify Problems And Propose Solutions To Problems Pertaining To The Built Environment.

Synthesize The Interrelationships Among Theories And Practices Pertaining To Built Environment.

Devise a research plan for addressing an environmental or urban problem.

ARCH699.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH699 Thesis
ARCH699.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH699
The course includes the stages of defining, articulating and applying multiple research methods customized to solve real world challenges in a selected topic of the Built Environment. It includes formulating a problem statement, selecting and reviewing relevant literature, designing an empirical study as well as performing it, including data collection analyzing the empirical data, make theoretical conclusions and finally write a thesis that contributes to knowledge in the identified field. Students are responsible for developing independently a satisfactory thesis proposal, which provides an in-depth examination of the research area.
Thesis (ARCH699) > Credit Hours : 9

Thesis (ARCH699) > Prerequisites
ARCH601 with a minimum grade C

ARCH600 with a minimum grade C
Thesis (ARCH699) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate knowledge of key advanced concepts in a specialized field pertaining to the built environment.

Transform an environmental or urban problem or question into a research plan.

Propose solutions to problems pertaining to the built environment.

Synthesize the interrelationships among theories and practices pertaining to built environment.

Demonstrate professional and ethical research and scientific writing and oral skills.

ARCH710.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH710 Advanced Qualitative Research Methods
ARCH710.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH710
An advanced introduction to qualitative research, focusing on the philosophical underpinnings of qualitative inquiry, the principles of qualitative research practice, and the use and effectiveness of specific research paradigms. Narrative, phenomenological, ethnographic and case study approaches will be discussed. Qualitative techniques including participant observation, field notation, reflective narrative, interview method and document/image analysis will be discussed. Relationships between broad qualitative approaches and specific techniques will be examined. Research design, data collection, analysis and representation, ethical issues and evaluation standards will be covered. The course will emphasize application of advanced qualitative methods to student research problems
Advanced Qualitative Research Methods (ARCH710) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Qualitative Research Methods (ARCH710) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate alternative qualitative paradigms for applicability to emerging research topics

Critique and extend existing qualitative techniques for investigation of novel research problems

Create comprehensive qualitative research designs appropriate to original research contributions

Develop and present critical self-evaluations of research quality, ethics and social implications

Initiate, lead and manage peer discussions on contemporary research issues and challenges

ARCH711.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH711 Behavior and Building Performance
ARCH711.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH711
The focus of this course is upon the ever-increasing professional and research interest in the sector which is the interrelationships between people and the built environment. It equips professionals with the skills, knowledge and networks needed to drive sustainable innovation for health and wellbeing in the design, retrofit and operation of buildings. During the course students will examine the built environment's impacts on health and wellbeing, within the context of sustainability; key design, engineering and health principles; use tools applicable in professional practice, including standards, benchmarking, modelling and monitoring methods; consider factors affecting for healthy and sustainable built environment.
Behavior and Building Performance (ARCH711) > Credit Hours : 3

Behavior and Building Performance (ARCH711) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss the concepts and methodologies of the health and wellbeing in sustainable built environment.

Assess effectiveness of the indoor environment impact on performance of building user.

Identify the health and comfort indoor environment and its drivers.

Practice to develop a research methods and analysis for specific building typology.

Initiate and lead peer discussions on health and wellbeing in built environment.

ARCH712.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH712 Advanced Critical Thinking in the Built Environment
ARCH712.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH712
Advanced Critical Thinking in the Built Environment introduces the students to the importance of criticality in design of built environment. Introducing design as a medium of critical inquiry, the course familiarizes the students with key critical design thinking theories of appearance, reality, form, function, place creativity and meaning. Appreciating the underlying principles and foundational skills of scholarly research, the students will learn the different critical design thinking practices based on contemporary movements, ideas and protagonists. This includes rational critical thinking practices using laboratory experimentation, human centered experimentation and logical argumentation reasoning - processes, methods, techniques and types of studies used. Extending the role of science for the society, the students develop capacities in understanding and challenging prevailing practices in architecture. By opening up questions of objectivity and judgment, the students are impelled to communicate their ideas using graphic or written means of expression.
Advanced Critical Thinking in the Built Environment (ARCH712) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Critical Thinking in the Built Environment (ARCH712) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate an advanced understanding of the key influences, theories, approaches and protagonists in critical design thinking.

Identify the prevailing critical design thinking practices within the built environment and devise an appropriate critical thinking strategy supporting an area of research.

Design, develop and carry out the chosen critical thinking practice applicable to address issues within the architectural discourse.

Employ well-developed skills and fluency in research to propose and defend issues and findings through a convincing graphic or written proposition.

Communicate and lead peer discussions on critical thinking in contemporary built environment practices.

ARCH713.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH713 Planning for Urban Resilience
ARCH713.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH713
The course introduces students to the theory and practice of building urban resilience. The course is in two parts: part one (theory) reviews the concepts, approaches and methodological understandings that underpin the resilience approach, as well as the application of resilience by different urban actors across the world. The course will critically examine the main features that help build resilient urban societies. Enabling cities to integrate individual and community capacities into broader urban resilience assessments. The second part of the course (practice) concerns undertaking a resilience assessment, using a case study. Students will work in teams using participatory assessment tools. The assessment involves identifying the main hazards, threats, vulnerabilities, capacities and actors (from government, civil society and emergency services), followed by the development of resilience action plans for presentation to key actors
Planning for Urban Resilience (ARCH713) > Credit Hours : 3

Planning for Urban Resilience (ARCH713) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss the concepts and methodologies of the urban planning resilience

Examine the main features that help to build resilient urban societies

Assess the resilience of existing urban contexts

Develop resilience action plans for specific urban contexts

Initiate and lead peer discussions on urban planning resilience

ARCH714.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH714 Housing and Urbanization
ARCH714.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH714
The course examines housing policy and planning in urban societies around the world and especially in the Global South. The first part of the course is devoted to history and theory. We examine the historical emergence of the twin problems of slums and housing in Europe during its era of intense urbanization; the export of Western housing and anti-slum policies to the developing world; the furious debate over the nature of informal settlements in the Global South; and the fundamental concepts of land use and housing policy. In the second part of the course, we take up the practical application of housing policies in different national environments around the globe. Students will work in teams to evaluate specific housing programs in some defined cities to propose a planning strategy to improve particular sites
Housing and Urbanization (ARCH714) > Credit Hours : 3

Housing and Urbanization (ARCH714) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Examine fundamental concepts of land use and housing policies in world urban societies

Critically review the Western housing and anti-slum policies in the developing world.

Assess specific housing programs in some defined cities

Develop a planning strategy to improve particular urban housing sites

Initiate and lead peer discussions on housing policy and planning in urban societies

ARCH715.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH715 Energy Optimization in Built Environment Design
ARCH715.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH715
This course is oriented towards the practical solution of optimization problems arising when designing an energy system or component applicable to the built environment. The general methodologies are provided, useful for a wide range of problem scales, with a focus on multi-variable mono-objective and multi-objective problems. These may include Optimum energy use strategies for buildings / cities, hourly energy simulation methods, building envelope and HVAC system energy optimization by computer simulation techniques; life-cycle cost analysis of building energy systems; case studies in building and urban applications
Energy Optimization in Built Environment Design (ARCH715) > Credit Hours : 3

Energy Optimization in Built Environment Design (ARCH715) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss current research in the field of energy efficiency of buildings

Formulate an optimization problem to the energy and built environment nexus and critically assess energy performance in the built environment

Use common methods and tools to perform energy efficiency measure with life-cycle cost analyses for the construction and/or renovation of buildings

Develop a design or retrofit proposal that integrates state of the art environmentally friendly technologies from the perspective of sustainable development

ARCH716.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH716 Advanced Intelligent Built Environment Systems
ARCH716.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH716
This course focusses on smart solutions in the built environment, and on principles for successful implementation of these solutions with emphasis on design, operation and evaluation of these intelligent systems and the factors affecting integrated building design in relation to sustainable operation. The course will involve mechanism self-sensing, electrically switching and mechanical actuation for enhanced building response to climatic and operation demands. The students will learn the skills involved to evaluate performance and integration aspects of several intelligent systems applicable to the built environment and gain knowledge of advanced building simulation and integrated design tools.
Advanced Intelligent Built Environment Systems (ARCH716) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Intelligent Built Environment Systems (ARCH716) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss the concepts and methodologies of the intelligent systems in built environment.

Demonstrate advanced skills in smart technology systems for building performance assessment.

Assess performance of modern facades with intelligent glazing system concepts.

Apply modern energy management technique for building load management.

Effectively integrate intelligent systems in the built environment.

ARCH850.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH850 Candidacy Exam
ARCH850.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH850
The Candidacy Exam for the PhD in Architectural engineering is a non-credit Pass/Fail exam. Students have up to two trials to pass the course; upon passing the exam, the student becomes a PhD candidate. The course is structured to evaluate the student’s breadth and depth of fundamental knowledge in the area(s) closely related to the thesis work. The course committee, in consultation with the advisor, decides on the topic(s) of the course. The PhD student prepares a concise and comprehensive research proposal that clearly defines the research problem and objectives and outlines the research methodology that he/she plans to follow. The concerned PhD student should present and defend his/her proposal in front of the course committee.
Candidacy Exam (ARCH850) > Credit Hours : 0

Candidacy Exam (ARCH850) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate the depth and breadth of their knowledge in the field of architectural engineering relevant to student’s research topic.

Propose a well-structured research project that outlines clear objectives, a detailed plan, and an appropriate methodology.

Demonstrate sufficient communication skills relevant to field of study and the research topic.

ARCH900.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH900 Dissertation Doctoral Research
ARCH900.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH900
Open to students who have successfully completed the comprehensive exam. PhD student conducts original research under the direction of a supervisory committee. Credits are determined in consultation with the dissertation supervisor.
Dissertation Doctoral Research (ARCH900) > Credit Hours : 30

Dissertation Doctoral Research (ARCH900) > Prerequisites
ARCH810 with a minimum grade P

ARCH901.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH901 Dissertation Doctoral Research
ARCH901.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH901
The PhD student conducts original research under the direction of an advisory committee. Credits registered in each semester are determined in consultation with the dissertation advisor.
Dissertation Doctoral Research (ARCH901) > Credit Hours : 42

Dissertation Doctoral Research (ARCH901) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Conduct independent research in a specific research area.

Produce a dissertation of publishable academic quality.

ARCH910.title: UAEU Catalog — ARCH910 Dissertation Defense
ARCH910.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2898.shtml?id=ARCH910
Two part exam, open and close, to defend the results of PhD research work.
Dissertation Defense (ARCH910) > Credit Hours : 0

Dissertation Defense (ARCH910) > Prerequisites
ARCH850
Dissertation Defense (ARCH910) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Assess primary literature and explain areas of active research in the chosen field

Discuss research design, including results, recommendations, and conclusions

Communicate research outcomes logically and persuasively both in writing and orally

Evaluate the study results in line with the research design, including ethical and professional considerations

BMB601.title: UAEU Catalog — BMB601 Techniques in Biochemistry
BMB601.text:
This course is designed to introduce students to a range of experimental techniques that are in routine use in a functioning biochemistry laboratory with the objective that they can understand basic principles behind these techniques and are able to understand their applicability in their future research. Whenever possible, the course combines lectures illustrating the scientific principles underlying a particular technique with the demonstration of the methodology in the laboratory.
Techniques in Biochemistry (BMB601) > Credit Hours : 2

Techniques in Biochemistry (BMB601) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Design appropriate strategies for cloning, expressing and purifying proteins of interest and their characterization.

Demonstrate the mechanisms of nucleic acid-protein interactions and their applications in solving a research problem.

Compare the best strategy for cell fractionation, protein isolation and purification.

Describe the techniques for cell culture and assays for cell death.

Apply the techniques for protein/enzyme analysis in research and development.

BMB602.title: UAEU Catalog — BMB602 Advanced Molecular Biology
BMB602.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2901.shtml?id=BMB602
The field of Molecular and Cellular Biology has given scientists unprecedented control over species manipulation and development. This course will have an in-depth coverage of the structure, function, and synthesis of DNA, RNA, and proteins. In this course, we will discuss the nature of genes and chromosomes (the repositories of genetic information) and the mechanics of DNA synthesis and genome replication, followed by discussions on repair, recombination and transposition. We will also discuss the pathways of gene expression (transcription, RNA processing, and translation) and the mechanisms of regulating these pathways, with special emphasis on transcriptional control. Latest literature on these topics will be covered.
Advanced Molecular Biology (BMB602) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Molecular Biology (BMB602) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain and discuss how gene structure is important in determining function and how molecular biology techniques are used to elucidate gene organization into cells.

Discuss the current literature in understanding DNA replication, gene transcription, and translation, and plan and design techniques used to study these processes.

Compare and discuss the latest understanding of how gene expression is regulated in prokaryotes and eukaryotes.

Discuss the different types of mutations and their repair mechanisms, and understand recombination, transposition, in relation to the pathophysiology of cancer.

Explain the role of non-coding RNAs in the regulation of gene expression and their significance to medicine and biomedical research.

Evaluate data, generate hypotheses, and design experiments to investigate a scientific problem in molecular biology.

Develop an in-depth literature review and present advanced knowledge in the specialized fields of molecular biology.

BMB603.title: UAEU Catalog — BMB603 Advanced Cell Biology
BMB603.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2901.shtml?id=BMB603
This course will focus on the cellular biochemistry of higher organisms: mechanisms of cellular communication, intracellular signaling, cell growth and oncogenic transformation. During the course, two basic cellular structures will be discussed: membrane and mitochondria, two important key players in cell signaling and cell death. Concepts like cell signaling, cell cycle, oxidative stress and cell death will be reviewed. The course will end with an introductory lecture on stem cell biology. Recent experimental findings and new approaches used to investigate how cells work will be emphasized. Students will also be taught how to explore the cell biology literature and to critically evaluate scientific publications in some of the topics.
Advanced Cell Biology (BMB603) > Credit Hours : 2

Advanced Cell Biology (BMB603) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze the structure of cellular membranes and the different transport mechanisms in eukaryotic cells.

Classify the signaling pathways by which cells communicate and respond to external signals and their role in cancer cell survival.

Summarize the post-translational modifications and folding mechanism of proteins and how they are transported to their respective target membranes and organelles in a cell.

Analyze the molecular mechanisms that regulate cell cycle and the alterations that can lead to cancer.

Discuss the functions of mitochondria and oxidative stress in cellular defense and cell survival.

Compare the different signaling processes involved in the development and destruction of eukaryotic cells.

BMB604.title: UAEU Catalog — BMB604 Advanced Topics in Biochemistry
BMB604.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2901.shtml?id=BMB604
This course is designed to prepare students in learning advanced cellular biochemistry and metabolism under physiological and pathophysiological conditions for successful careers in academia and biotechnology industries. The course also provides enhanced education opportunities for students who wish to extend their knowledge, experience, and opportunities as independent scientists in academic research at universities, biotechnology and pharmaceutical industries, health/biomedical science management or teaching. In this course, advanced cellular biochemistry will be explained to signify the importance of metabolism in normal physiology and pathophysiological conditions. Faculty lectures and students reports will focus on these.
Advanced Topics in Biochemistry (BMB604) > Credit Hours : 2

Advanced Topics in Biochemistry (BMB604) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply the knowledge of Biochemistry to advance the understanding the role of nutrition in health diseases.

Evaluate the role of different organs/tissues in coordinating the body metabolism in health and diseases.

Determine the key metabolic changes in etiology and pathophysiology of common diseases such as blood, liver disorders, obesity and diabetes.

Analyze the metabolic changes in diseases associated with lipid, protein, carbohydrates, amino acids and nucleic acids metabolism.

Apply the knowledge of cellular metabolism in stem cell self- renewal and differentiation in biomedical research.

BMB606.title: UAEU Catalog — BMB606 Special topics in Biochemistry
BMB606.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2901.shtml?id=BMB606
This course will provide students the chance to rotate through the laboratory of a potential supervisor to learn about the various projects in progress in that laboratory with emphasis on acquainting themselves with the type of research work and techniques being used. Regular attendance (one hour per week) and active participation of the student in observing and learning about these projects is of great importance. The students should study the literature provided by their respective supervisors and familiarize themselves with the research activities being carried out in the laboratory chosen by them.
Special topics in Biochemistry (BMB606) > Credit Hours : 1

Special topics in Biochemistry (BMB606) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Illustrate the projects being carried out in the chosen laboratory

Evaluate the various techniques being conducted in the laboratory to achieve its stated goals

Analyze the literature provided by the supervisor to study the research topic(s) under study

Apply the knowledge gained during the laboratory rotation to develop a potential thesis project along with the involvement of the supervisor

BMSC700.title: UAEU Catalog — BMSC700 Recent Advances in Molecular Biology
BMSC700.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2901.shtml?id=BMSC700
The field of Molecular and Cellular Biology has given scientists unprecedented control over species manipulation and development. This course will have an in-depth coverage of the structure, function, and synthesis of DNA, RNA, and proteins. We will discuss the nature of genes and chromosomes (the repositories of genetic information) and the mechanics of DNA synthesis and genome replication, followed by discussions on repair, recombination and transposition. We will also discuss the pathways of gene expression (transcription, RNA processing, and translation) and the mechanisms of regulating these pathways, with special emphasis on transcriptional control.
Recent Advances in Molecular Biology (BMSC700) > Credit Hours : 3

Recent Advances in Molecular Biology (BMSC700) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

In depth and comprehensive knowledge of molecular biology, including DNA replication, recombination, and repair, transcription, translation, and gene regulation, as well as the emerging role of regulatory RNAs in these processes.

Up-to-date on current literature on advanced concepts in molecular biology, application of techniques used to study these processes, and their significance to biomedical research and medicine.

Well-versed in implications of advances in molecular biology in terms of challenges, trends, and developments in the fields of biomedical sciences and molecular medicine.

Advanced skills in data evaluation, hypotheses generation, and experimental design development to solve scientific problems in molecular biology.

Integration of acquired knowledge in molecular biology to deepen new concepts and methodologies and/or identify new research opportunities/problems in the student’s area of research.

In-depth understanding of how to analyze, evaluate, interpret, and critique primary scientific literature in specialized fields of molecular biology.

Can demonstrate competency in using knowledge in molecular biology and skills to analyze problems involving biomedical sciences and molecular medicine, articulate these with peers/team members/other stake holders, and undertake remedial measures/studies, etc.

Can evaluate, construct, and solve contemporary problems related to molecular biology that can be used to prevent and treat diseases.

Can implement methodologies and/or practices to illustrate the relationship of molecular biology to allied fields.

BMSC701.title: UAEU Catalog — BMSC701 Advanced Research Techniques
BMSC701.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2901.shtml?id=BMSC701
This course aims to give a broad but comprehensive introduction to the majority of the important techniques used today in biomedical research. It aims to give a background in the theory, practise and applications of the various techniques, as well as their limitations and pitfalls. It is hoped that, after having completed the course, students will be well equipped to embark upon research projects with a useful knowledge of the techniques covered and how to apply them to address specific research-based questions, and also how to interpret the data derived from these applications. It is not the aim of the course to teach students how to perform various procedures - this can only be achieved with extensive, repeated, supervised, hands-on laboratory training which is obviously not feasible in this context. The format of each session may vary according to the individual needs of each topic or presenter. Most session will commence with a tutorial covering the principles and practice of the technique at hand, followed by a less formal session where instrumentation can be seen in operation, experimental examples can be examined, and raw data can be viewed and discussed.
Advanced Research Techniques (BMSC701) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Research Techniques (BMSC701) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Master advanced research techniques to help address specific research questions.

Evaluate, Interpret and use the results obtained from advanced research techniques.

Demonstrate competency in presenting research articles and topics of current and future significance in biomedical sciences.

BMSC702.title: UAEU Catalog — BMSC702 Advances in General Pathology
BMSC702.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2901.shtml?id=BMSC702
The course is mainly General histopathology, which deals with the basic concept of the various disease processes. This program offers the students a comprehensive review of the theoretical and practical aspects of general histopathology. The students will be exposed to formal lectures and laboratory practicals, which will emphasize the most modern concepts and methodologies in the fields of cell injury, inflammation, tissue repair, infection, hemodynamic changes, vascular disorders, environmental disorders and neoplasia.
Advances in General Pathology (BMSC702) > Credit Hours : 3

Advances in General Pathology (BMSC702) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Nature of cell injury and the various responses a living cell may undertake when subjected to injury.

Mechanisms and systems available for fending off and responding to various forms of challenges in injury including the inflammatory response, immune response, function of the phagocytic cells, participation of the complement and clotting systems and other serum factors.

Functions of various organ systems, their interact with one another, and mechanism diseases.

Methods to prevent nutritional and occupational disorders.

Basic pathologic processes that underlie the development of neoplasia, thrombosis, infarction, and pathologic immune response.

Foundation of knowledge of the basic pathologic processes on which subsequent studies of systemic disease can be built.

BMSC703.title: UAEU Catalog — BMSC703 Microbial Pathogenesis and Host Defense
BMSC703.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2901.shtml?id=BMSC703
This course will explore ways in which microbial pathogens, particularly bacteria and viruses, interact with their hosts. Topics that will be covered include bacterial-host cell interactions, role of bacterial toxins in pathogenicity, viral infections and escape strategies, emerging and re-emerging viral infections, host defense and innate/adaptive immunity, exaggerated immune responses and immunopathology, virus-host cell interactions in cancerogenesis, and strategies for vaccine development.
Microbial Pathogenesis and Host Defense (BMSC703) > Credit Hours : 3

Microbial Pathogenesis and Host Defense (BMSC703) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

The concepts of virulence, pathogenicity, commensalism, symbiosis, opportunism, parasitism, emerging/re-emerging infections, and the role of pathogenic microbes in cancerogenesis.

Of diverse mechanisms used by pathogenic microbes to invade hosts.

The molecular mechanisms pathogenic microbes use to evade the mammalian host immune response.

The defense mechanisms employed by the host against microbial infections.

Classical and contemporary strategies that can be used to control, prevent, and treat infections resulting from pathogenic microbes and be able to critically evaluate, concisely construct, and clearly present these ideas

BMSC704.title: UAEU Catalog — BMSC704 Current Advances in Pharmacological Sciences
BMSC704.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2901.shtml?id=BMSC704
Pharmacology is an interdisciplinary field. This PhD course tackles major recent findings in divers’ area of pharmacology with a focus on cancer pharmacology, neurodegeneration and cognitive functions, cardiovascular and metabolic diseases. This course emphasis is on the molecular mechanism of action of the most recent applied and experimental drugs including monoclonal antibodies, tissue engineering advances, and genome editing progress. Therefore, the contents of the course will remain dynamic and evolve from year to year depending on what is viewed as significant advances in that year. It is intended that the seminar should provide a more didactic and interactive meeting. During this course, students will also be introduced to the most advanced research methodologies and will have extensive training to develop their skills, including ethics and communication that will be achieved via written assessments and oral presentations and discussions.
Current Advances in Pharmacological Sciences (BMSC704) > Credit Hours : 3

Current Advances in Pharmacological Sciences (BMSC704) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate comprehensive and critical analysis of the most advanced knowledge in cancer research and oncology.

Demonstrate comprehensive and critical analysis of the most advanced knowledge in the pharmacology of monoclonal antibodies and natural drugs, tissue engineering, and genome editing.

Demonstrate comprehensive and critical analysis of the most advanced knowledge in neurodegenerative disease, cognitive functions, cardiovascular and metabolic diseases.

Evaluate, critique, and suggest ideas for the improvement of advanced methodologies in cancer research, neurodegenerative, cognitive, cardiovascular, and metabolic diseases.

Comprehend, interpret, critically evaluate, and clearly present recent scientific advances in pharmacological sciences, identify new research opportunities and demonstrate adherence to high ethical standards.

BMSC705.title: UAEU Catalog — BMSC705 Advances in Genetics
BMSC705.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2901.shtml?id=BMSC705
This course is designed to cover selected topics and recently published articles that are influencing in a significant manner our understanding of human genetics and genomics with emphasis on recent advances in genomic technologies and disease mechanisms. Therefore, the contents of the course might vary from year to year depending on what is viewed as a significant advance in that year.
Advances in Genetics (BMSC705) > Credit Hours : 3

Advances in Genetics (BMSC705) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate comprehensive knowledge in genetics and genomics by competently demonstrating the ability to identify and succinctly summarize as well as clearly present the latest advances in the field.

Critically evaluate and expertly summarize research and review articles with significant impact on our understanding of genomic variation in human health and disease including disease pathogenesis.

Concisely construct and clearly present scientific material that demonstrates the latest technological and conceptual advances in genetics and genomics.

Independently identify, interpret and clearly present research findings and topics of current and future significance in genetics and genomics.

BMSC706.title: UAEU Catalog — BMSC706 Advanced Cancer Biology
BMSC706.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2901.shtml?id=BMSC706
This course will focus on cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying cancer progression, metastasis, and recurrence. Advances in cancer treatment, including targeted therapy and immunotherapy will also be discussed. This course will be based around seminars and interactive discussion sessions focused on the latest developments in the field accompanied by critical evaluation of published research articles. The content of the course will evolve from year to year depending on the latest advances in the field. During the interactive group sessions, there will be a round table discussion of selected research papers (which will be pre-circulated to all students) concerning important topics in cancer.
