The students will learn to dissect the study’s major aims, methodology and logic employed to address the question, the strengths and weaknesses of the results, and their implications. The emphasis will be on the methodological, conceptual and practical aspects of the research papers in the field. An important part of this course will be to develop the student’s ability to critically evaluate published research papers. The manuscript for evaluation will be selected by the course coordinators and provided to each student at the beginning of the course. In consultation with the course coordinator and co-coordinator, each student will also select a research paper/topic and prepare it for presentation to the whole class at the end of the course.
Advanced Cancer Biology (BMSC706) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Cancer Biology (BMSC706) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Appraise the recent advances related to the cellular and molecular mechanisms of cancer progression, metastasis, and recurrence.

Explain and evaluate the principles underlying personalized medicine approaches in cancer management.

Demonstrate in depth knowledge of the cutting-edge methodologies, including bioinformatics tools, used in cancer research, understand the positive and challenging sides of experimental and animal models in cancer research and employ the relevant laboratory methods to address research objectives.

Independently formulate a research question in the area of cancer research, identify relevant methods to address the issue and, based on this, write a project plan including relevant background information, an appropriate aim, and a realistic work plan.

Critically analyze and discuss articles within the field of cancer research and prepare presentations on selected key topics.

BMSC707.title: UAEU Catalog — BMSC707 Medical Cell and Tissue Biology
BMSC707.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2901.shtml?id=BMSC707
This course will guide students in learning advanced information on the microscopic structure of the cells and tissues of the human body and the biological features of their components. The correlation of structure and function at the cellular and molecular levels will be emphasized in lectures and laboratory sessions. The application of cell and tissue biology to research and clinical disciplines will be emphasized. For each topic, an introduction to the cellular architecture and specialized function of a given tissue will provide the necessary background that will explore contemporary research into the molecular and cellular basis of human diseases involving that tissue.
Medical Cell and Tissue Biology (BMSC707) > Credit Hours : 3

Medical Cell and Tissue Biology (BMSC707) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Compare the structural and functional components of body cells and tissues.

Explain the molecular control of major cell biological events.

Analyze the cellular and subcellular features in a tissue section using microscope.

Design an experiment for tissue analysis.

Evaluate research article investigating cell biological features.

BMSC708.title: UAEU Catalog — BMSC708 Advanced Topics in Neuroscience
BMSC708.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2901.shtml?id=BMSC708
Advanced Topics in Neuroscience is a course that focuses on specific contents that are particularly relevant to modern neuroscience and pathophysiology of the nervous system, allowing students to discuss, critique, and interpret primary research literature in the field. Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to demonstrate comprehensive and integrated knowledge at the frontier of this discipline and explain critically the highly complex and diverse matters in this field. In addition, the course will explore training and practice on translational idea generation and refinement. It is a modular course that provides broad base to sample contemporary understanding and developments on normal and abnormal brain functioning, allowing each student to focus on selected topic of interest. The course will focus on specific contents that are especially relevant to gain a deeper understanding of ourselves, how the nervous system works and what controls our behaviors, including consciousness learning and memory, brain plasticity, and motor functions. However, it also covers the most recent developments in the neurobiology of diseases, including neurodegeneration, movement disorders, autism, depression, stress related diseases and other neurological and psychiatric diseases. The course will also cover principles of the most recent cutting-edge technologies available to study brain function like connectomics, super-resolution microscopy, functional MRI, EEG, electrophysiology and calcium imaging. The course is composed of weekly seminar series in which various topics about modern neuroscience are discussed. Seminars are also presented by students or when suitable by visiting outside neuroscientists. At the end of the course, student will submit a reflection paper on a chosen topic of special interest/thesis relevance. The reflection paper can be structured as a literature synthesis, opinion paper, theoretical paper, or a research grant proposal. Together, the seminars and reflection paper will prepare the student for the course assessment during which the candidate will be examined on deep comprehension and critical thinking of a broader research topic/paper.
Advanced Topics in Neuroscience (BMSC708) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Topics in Neuroscience (BMSC708) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate comprehensive and overreaching knowledge of selected neuroscience topics.

Discuss and compare current research advances in selected neuroscience topics.

Evaluate and interpret the implications of the primary field of study in terms of challenges, trends, and developments in a social or global context.

Demonstrate integration of the acquired knowledge in Neuroscience to develop new concepts and methodologies and/or identify new research opportunities/problems in student’s area of research.

Apprise, critique, and interpret primary research literature in Neuroscience related to student’s area of research.

Demonstrate competency in using Neuroscience knowledge and skills to analyze problems involving the nervous system, articulate these with peers/team members/other stake holders, and undertake remedial measures/studies, etc.

BMSC709.title: UAEU Catalog — BMSC709 Advanced Pathophysiology
BMSC709.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2901.shtml?id=BMSC709
Pathophysiology identifies the changes that occur when a function of the body is compromised by disease, injury or other abnormality. In Advanced Pathophysiology course students will explore the application of advanced knowledge of the complex physiological functions and pathophysiological processes to understand the fundamental mechanisms of organ health and disease. The course will be focusing on pathophysiology of three bodily systems, including the cardiovascular, respiratory and gastrointestinal system as major focus points of research in the department. Selected topics from other bodily systems will also be explored. The course will enable students to discuss, critique, interpret and eventually contrast primary research literature in each and between those fields. At the end of the course students will be able to demonstrate comprehensive and integrated knowledge at the frontier of pathophysiology and explain critically the highly complex and diverse matters in this field. The course has modular structure with up 30% of the topics modifiable aiming to provide broad yet targeted knowledge and understanding of abnormal bodily functioning. Particular attention is given to the most recent cutting-edge technologies available to examine the alterations in function as well as adaptive, integrative and regulatory mechanisms of bodily dysfunction at the molecular, cellular, organ and system levels. The course combines seminars, lectures and presentations, and focused integration sessions led by students and faculty. At the end of the course, students will have to submit a reflection paper on a chosen topic of special interest/thesis relevance. The reflection paper can be structured as a literature synthesis, opinion paper, theoretical paper, or a research grant proposal. Finally, the course will insert a small focused discussion, training and practice on translational idea generation and refinement; here the main emphasis will be on comparative research of underlying pathophysiological processes across bodily systems. At the end of the course, students are expected to demonstrate deep comprehension and critical thinking of a pathophysiologic processes.
Advanced Pathophysiology (BMSC709) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Pathophysiology (BMSC709) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply comprehensive knowledge of main concepts related to physiological alterations and pathophysiological processes in different diseases manifested across the lifespan.

Apprise current research in pathophysiology related to selected pathophysiological processes across the lifespan.

Elaborate normal and abnormal compensatory mechanisms as the body response to disease.

Analyze the impact of cultural, developmental, genetic, environmental, behavioral, and economic factors that may influence pathophysiological alterations and contribute to increased risk of disease.

Demonstrate all-encompassing knowledge of methodologies used to examine pathophysiological processes at different levels of complexity.

Demonstrate integration of the acquired knowledge in pathophysiology to develop new concepts and methodologies and/or identify new research opportunities/problems in student’s area of research.

BMSC710.title: UAEU Catalog — BMSC710 Computational Biochemistry and Artificial Intelligence for Medical Applications
BMSC710.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2901.shtml?id=BMSC710
Computational sciences and artificial intelligence have been integrated in ubiquitous applications in the fields of sciences and medicine. This technology serves as a powerful tool to mark advancements in research, discoveries and medical practice. This course is composed of two parts: Computational Biochemistry and Artificial Intelligence. The first part covers computational sciences with focus on molecular docking, molecular dynamics, and quantum mechanics. It is a combination of theory and computational practical sessions. The theory will include the fundamentals and limitations of each of the methods, and the practical sessions will involve hands-on applications on chemical or biochemical systems. The second part covers artificial intelligence and its applications. It includes the fundamentals of statistics and machine learning algorithms. The theory of this part will be complemented by hands-on sessions that involve model building, technique validation and decision analysis, with focus on medical applications.
Computational Biochemistry and Artificial Intelligence for Medical Applications (BMSC710) > Credit Hours : 3

Computational Biochemistry and Artificial Intelligence for Medical Applications (BMSC710) > Prerequisites
CHEM113 with a minimum grade D

BIOC160 with a minimum grade D
Computational Biochemistry and Artificial Intelligence for Medical Applications (BMSC710) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss the fundamentals of computational biochemical sciences and their applications.

Build advanced knowledge about the current applications and the future of artificial intelligence.

Construct scientific hypotheses, and design experiments to tackle scientific problems through computational tools.

Integrate acquired knowledge to simulate and analyze experiments related to computational biochemistry as well as to evaluate artificial intelligence models.

Reflect competency in using computational skills to evaluate, construct and answer contemporary scientific and medical research questions.

Debate advances, methodologies and practices with peers.

BMSC711.title: UAEU Catalog — BMSC711 Advanced Human Microbiome
BMSC711.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2901.shtml?id=BMSC711
The microbiome is the genomic content of all microorganisms (microbiota) inhabiting different parts of the human body. Alterations in microbiome composition have been associated with many diseases including inflammatory bowel disease, autoimmune diseases, cancers and diabetes. Multi-omics techniques, including genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic analyses, are used to better understand how the microbiota are acting on and interacting with the hosts in health and disease. This course will provide the students with deep understanding of microbial communities causing different types of diseases, their diversity, interaction with the immune system, modulation and impact on human health. Students will be exposed to modern molecular techniques and bioinformatics tools for profiling and analyzing microbiome data. They will also learn how to integrate these data to develop a holistic understanding of the interactions between host and microbial communities in both health and disease states.
Advanced Human Microbiome (BMSC711) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Human Microbiome (BMSC711) > Prerequisites
MMIM601 or MMIM602 or
Advanced Human Microbiome (BMSC711) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the importance of healthy human microbiome, composition and function

Evaluate and assess the complexity of the human microbiome communities using next generation sequencing

Adapt and integrate different bioinformatics tools for the analysis of microbiome data

Discuss microbiota interaction with the immune system

Discuss the links between human microbiome and diseases

Describe the methods used in the modulation of human microbiome and their impact on health

Critically evaluate, discuss, and interpret primary research literature in the field of microbiome

BMSC712.title: UAEU Catalog — BMSC712 Advanced Molecular and Cellular Virology
BMSC712.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2901.shtml?id=BMSC712
Virology is a dynamic and rapidly evolving field. This course is tailored for PhD students seeking to deepen their understanding of cutting-edge developments in virology, and to explore the intricate molecular and cellular mechanisms governing viral infections and associated diseases. The course will provide an in-depth examination of the latest breakthroughs and methodologies in virology research, encompassing a diverse range of topics, including viral entry and replication, host-pathogen interactions, immune evasion strategies, oncogenic viruses and antiviral therapies. Additionally, students will learn how to identify potential areas of novel research, how to write a seed grant and identify appropriate funding bodies.
Advanced Molecular and Cellular Virology (BMSC712) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Molecular and Cellular Virology (BMSC712) > Prerequisites
MMIM603 or BMB602 or MMIM602 or BMB603 or BMSC700
Advanced Molecular and Cellular Virology (BMSC712) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss the principles of viral epidemiology, transmission, replication, gene expression.

Demonstrate how viruses enter cells and can lead to cell injury and death

Compare how different viruses adopt different strategies to evade the immune responses.

Explain in detail the current understanding of the mechanisms involved in the pathogenesis of important viral diseases affecting humans.

Design laboratory experiments to investigate virus biology

Critically evaluate and present research findings to peers and faculty.

Identify novel areas of research and prepare grant proposals

BMSC713.title: UAEU Catalog — BMSC713 Advanced Immunology
BMSC713.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2901.shtml?id=BMSC713
The field of immunology has witnessed a huge surge in knowledge over the past 50 years, becoming one of the most dynamic and exciting areas of medical sciences. Dysregulated immune reactions are the basis of many human diseases, including cancer, inflammation, autoimmunity, allergy, neurodegeneration and immunodeficiencies. The Advanced Immunology course provides an intensive and in‐depth examination of fundamental concepts in immunology, including (1) the interplay between innate and adaptive immune systems; (2) function of immune regulatory circuits; and (3) immunopathogenesis of selected human diseases. Our improved understanding of the immune system has provided the foundation for the development of new modalities for treating chronic diseases such as cancer, autoimmunity and autoinflammatory disorders.
Advanced Immunology (BMSC713) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Immunology (BMSC713) > Prerequisites
MMIM601

MMIM602

BMB603

MMIM608

MMIM609
Advanced Immunology (BMSC713) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the cellular and molecular basis of the innate and adaptive immune systems

Illustrate the integration of immune responses in the setting of microbial infections and the requirements for protective immunity

Discuss neuroimmune interactions and their role in the regulation of inflammatory disorders

Explain the cellular and molecular basis of autoimmune disorders

Analyze the interplay between the immune system and cancer and the development of cancer immunotherapy as a novel treatment modality

Evaluate the methods used to assess immune status in health and disease

Appraise and evaluate primary research publications in the field of immunology

BIOC100.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOC100 Basic Biology I
BIOC100.text:
This course aims at developing the basic concepts that form the crux of life from both structural and functional perspectives. It includes cellular functioning and organization and the transformation of energy. It also introduces the student to the continuity of life from genetic and molecular perspectives.
Basic Biology I (BIOC100) > Credit Hours : 3

Basic Biology I (BIOC100) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the outcome of the testing of hypotheses and theories that are under constant scrutiny and subject to revision based on new observations.

Explain scientific knowledge and how it relates to real world laws of chemistry and physics.

Define the basis of eukaryotic cell biology.

Describe the importance to further study advanced biology courses.

BIOC155.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOC155 Biology Laboratory 1
BIOC155.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOC155
This laboratory course aims at introducing the students to the general biology laboratory I knowledge, skills and measurements in common use in life sciences; applying these knowledge and skills in writing of laboratory reports, using the light microscope and making measurements, using of pipettes and preparing of solutions. The major theme will be devoted to describe and analyze the molecules of life, light microscopy, fine cell structure and function, cell membranes structure and function, cell division and staining procedures. Also, students study some of the physiological concepts in animals and plants e.g. photosynthesis, respiration, and osmosis.
Biology Laboratory 1 (BIOC155) > Credit Hours : 1

Biology Laboratory 1 (BIOC155) > Prerequisites
BIOC100 with a minimum grade D
Biology Laboratory 1 (BIOC155) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop writing skills by allowing them to prepare practical laboratory reports and analyzing data independently and in a team.

Plan and conduct biological experiments.

Identify the physical and chemical properties of the macromolecules and detecting their presence qualitatively in unknown samples.

Develop a biological knowledge base common to contemporary biologists, encompassing microscopy, cell structure, cellular membranes, and nucleic acids biology.

Explain how living systems function and how they interact with the physical environments.

Apply knowledge of contemporary social and ethical issues related to biology and the professional responsibilities of a biologist.

BIOC160.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOC160 Biology II
BIOC160.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOC160
Biology II covers diverse topics including evolution, systematic, diversity of life, plant form and function, animal form and function, and conservation biology. The course is intended to complement Basic Biology I (which covers cellular and biochemical basis of life) by covering the basic concepts relating to whole-organism topics.
Biology II (BIOC160) > Credit Hours : 4

Biology II (BIOC160) > Prerequisites
BIOC100
Biology II (BIOC160) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain and list the criteria used in the science of systematics. This includes: the kingdom systems of classification and the three main taxonomy domains, binomial nomenclature, phylogenetic and how molecular data are revolutionizing taxonomy.

Discuss the diversity of life and demonstrate that while all living creatures utilize the same biochemical and basic metabolic pathways, they can be so diverse in form and function.

Explain the relationship between plant structure and some of the main functions.

Outline plant life cycles (such as non-seed and seed plants) and define alternation of generations.

Discuss animal diversity, structure and function particularly those regulating the animal life and homeostasis.

BIOC165.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOC165 Biology Laboratory 2
BIOC165.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOC165
This laboratory course aims at introducing the students to the general biology laboratory II knowledge, skills and safety; applying these knowledge and skills in writing of laboratory reports, and using of light microscope. The major theme will be devoted to describe and analyze the plant ecological adaptations, plant growth and anatomy, Animal dissection, structure and function of tissues, plants and animals diversity.
Biology Laboratory 2 (BIOC165) > Credit Hours : 1

Biology Laboratory 2 (BIOC165) > Prerequisites
BIOC160

BIOC155 with a minimum grade D
Biology Laboratory 2 (BIOC165) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop writing skills by allowing them to prepare practical laboratory reports and analyzing data independently and in a team.

Plan and conduct biological experiments.

Identify the different processes and stages that occur during animal development.

Use a biological knowledge base common to contemporary biologists in cellular, sub-organismic, organismic, and systems levels of biological organization.

Categorize the major groups of plants and animals and know their taxonomy, structures, ecology and adaptations in relation to the habitats.

BIOC250.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOC250 Basic Ecology
BIOC250.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOC250
This course focuses on the science of ecology with historical background and its relationships with the other relative sciences. It examines ecosystem structure and functions, energy flow and matter transfer within the food chain among different trophic levels. The course covers the biogeochemical cycles and their components, examples of the different ecosystems in the world biomes. The course contents also cover population attributes such as density, age structure, mortality, natality and population growth rate within an evolutionary context. Community attributes such as succession, food web, community assembly and diversity are examined. A laboratory session (3 hours per week) is included in this course.
Basic Ecology (BIOC250) > Credit Hours : 3

Basic Ecology (BIOC250) > Prerequisites
BIOC160 with a minimum grade D
Basic Ecology (BIOC250) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe basic concepts relating to ecosystems linking biotic and abiotic components.

Explain basic principles of population biology, biogeography and ecosystem function using appropriate terminology.

Analyze complex interactions through case studies and focused literature reviews.

Recognize scientific approaches to the study of organismal interactions through examples of manipulative experiments

Critically evaluate ecological literature and interpret case studies in the context of ecological theory, through discussions, presentations and reports

BIOC270.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOC270 General Genetics
BIOC270.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOC270
This course aims at developing a clear understanding of genetics. It includes Mendelian genetics, modern genetics and molecular basis of genetics, the applications of genetics in the field of medicine in terms of detection of genetic diseases, prevention, treatment and other applications as well.
General Genetics (BIOC270) > Credit Hours : 3

General Genetics (BIOC270) > Prerequisites
BIOC160 with a minimum grade D or BIOL105 with a minimum grade D
General Genetics (BIOC270) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain The Basic Concept Of Genetic Inheritance And Variation.

Identify Terminologies Associated With Genetics

Interpret And Solve Genetics Problems

Perform Tasks Relating To Reading And Writing Capabilities In Genetics

BIOC275.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOC275 Genetics Laboratory
BIOC275.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOC275
This course is designed to examine the gene as a unit of transmission, a unit of function, and a unit of mutation. The course emphasizes the relationship between classical Mendelian genetics and the modern molecular understanding of gene structure and function. Illustrates the principles of genetics through student experiments; utilizes classical genetic techniques as well as molecular techniques to study the nature of genetic material. Genetics lab meets for three hours per week.
Genetics Laboratory (BIOC275) > Credit Hours : 1

Genetics Laboratory (BIOC275) > Prerequisites
BIOC165 with a minimum grade D or BIOC214 with a minimum grade D
Genetics Laboratory (BIOC275) > Corequisites
BIOC270
Genetics Laboratory (BIOC275) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Assess the Mendelian concept of dominance-recessiveness, segregation and independent assortment.

Predict the genotype, phenotype and probability of progeny as a result of mono-, di- or tri-hybrid crosses.

Perform basic molecular biology techniques such as genomic DNA isolation, restriction and digestion, polymerase chain reaction.

Analysis of the experimental data and Identify different stages of mitosis.

BIOC280.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOC280 Computing and Data Analysis for Biology
BIOC280.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOC280
Biology now routinely produces a vast amount of data. Thus, it is essential for a biologist to be equipped with the skills necessary to manipulate, analyze and visualize this data to make meaningful conclusions. This course will first introduce students to the basic concepts of programming and statistics and then apply these skills to analyze real life biological datasets with genomic, gene expression and ecological applications.
Computing and Data Analysis for Biology (BIOC280) > Credit Hours : 3

Computing and Data Analysis for Biology (BIOC280) > Prerequisites
BIOC100 with a minimum grade D

STAT235 with a minimum grade D
Computing and Data Analysis for Biology (BIOC280) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate knowledge of the basic concepts of programming, logic and data structures

Perform simple statistical tests using biological data

Write scripts and code to analyze various biological datasets

BIOC290.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOC290 Cell and Molecular Biology
BIOC290.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOC290
This course aims at providing an overview of the molecular basis to cell structure and function. This course will approach this discipline by exploring a series of basic questions, which will provide a conceptual framework for dealing with our evolving understanding of cells. This course will describe classical and modern experiments provide a basis for our present understanding of how cells function at the molecular level. Upon completion of this course, the student will be able to demonstrate the competencies in the following subjects: cell organization and cell communication, cycle control and programmed cell death, DNA replication, transcription, and protein synthesis.
Cell and Molecular Biology (BIOC290) > Credit Hours : 3

Cell and Molecular Biology (BIOC290) > Prerequisites
BIOC275 with a minimum grade D

BIOC270 with a minimum grade D
Cell and Molecular Biology (BIOC290) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Correlate cytoskeletal structures to different cellular Functions.

Differentiate between prokaryotes and eukaryotes.

Discriminate between types of gene expressions

Recognize various structures of the cell and differentiate between them.

BIOC480.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOC480 Research Project
BIOC480.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOC480
This course aims to cultivate investigative skills, giving students the opportunity to conduct an original scientific research project under the guidance of an experienced member of faculty. This is not a course about existing knowledge: it is a course in which students pioneer the unknown; formulating an original question, thinking through and implementing innovative ways to answer it, interpreting results, and communicating the whole investigation by means of a written report and an oral presentation.
Research Project (BIOC480) > Credit Hours : 3

Research Project (BIOC480) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Formulate and explain an original research question, highlighting its novelty and its importance with respect to contemporary thinking.

Develop, implement, and explain logical methods to solve relevant problems and thereby answer the question.

Interpret and explain the results of the investigation.

Present the whole investigation as a coherent argument, both in a written report and as an oral presentation.

BIOC490.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOC490 Advanced Bio-applications
BIOC490.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOC490
The course consists of laboratory work. This practical part of this course aims at providing students with important practical skills that benefit them in their future work as well as for future postgraduate studies. The course will consist of three modules that cover advanced techniques of the three tracks of the department: Cell and Molecular Biology, General Biology and Environmental Sciences.
Advanced Bio-applications (BIOC490) > Credit Hours : 2

Advanced Bio-applications (BIOC490) > Prerequisites
BIOC480
Advanced Bio-applications (BIOC490) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop knowledge about theories learned by the students in the previous years.

Analyze and discuss experimental results.

Use experimental techniques to study molecular genetics

Synthesize knowledge of physical and chemical processes of oceans and the biology of organisms to ask questions about natural history and ecology.

BIOC500.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOC500 Internship
BIOC500.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOC500
The internship consists of practical training in a real working environment. Students complete eight weeks of training at an approved training site. The internship is offered in the second half of the final semester of study. Any condensed courses offered in the same semester must be completed during the first half of the semester in which the internship is undertaken. Internships are available in both the Spring and Fall semesters.
Internship (BIOC500) > Credit Hours : 6

Internship (BIOC500) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explore career opportunities prior to graduation.

Integrate theory and practice.

Assess interests and abilities in their field of study.

Develop appropriate workplace attitudes necessary for the job success

Develop communication and critical thinking skills in the job.

Build a record of work experience

Acquire employment contacts leading directly to full-time job following graduation from college.

Identify, write, and carry out performance objectives related to their job assignment.

BIOE212.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE212 Biology of Invertebrates
BIOE212.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE212
This course takes an integrative approach towards understanding animals. We will explore fundamental questions about animals from the perspective of different organizational levels and experimental approaches. We will also examine a wide diversity of animals, including their ecology, phylogeny, extending our interest beyond the well-known model organisms. A three-hour laboratory component is included in this course that will include a survey of all major invertebrate groups, with special emphasis on functional morphology in relation to phylogenetic relationships.
Biology of Invertebrates (BIOE212) > Credit Hours : 3

Biology of Invertebrates (BIOE212) > Prerequisites
BIOC160
Biology of Invertebrates (BIOE212) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Interpret classification of all major invertebrate groups

Describe morphological characteristics of different invertebrate groups and explain their functions

Analyze the relationship between form and function and explain their interaction with adaptation and constraint

Discuss evolution of invertebrates through scientific studies

Critically evaluate biological literature and interpret case studies in invertebrate biology, through discussions, presentations and reports

BIOE214.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE214 Biology of Vertebrates
BIOE214.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE214
This course focuses on the origin and diversity of vertebrates, with emphasis on ‎functional morphology and locomotor apparatus; solutions to problems of heat and cold, ‎osmotic stress, and oxygen availability; sensory systems and communication; growth and ‎development; life history and modes of reproduction. Students are introduced to the ‎relationships between all chordates through a close examination of form and function ‎from an evolutionary perspective. Emphasis is placed on the link with evolutionary ‎adaptation and constraints that permitted certain groups to thrive in certain ‎environments. A three-hour laboratory will examine specimens of all major vertebrate ‎groups, with special emphasis on functional morphology, phylogeny and adaptive ‎radiation within and between major vertebrate groups.‎
Biology of Vertebrates (BIOE214) > Credit Hours : 3

Biology of Vertebrates (BIOE214) > Prerequisites
BIOC160
Biology of Vertebrates (BIOE214) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

‎Interpret classification of all major chordates ‎

Describe morphological characteristics of different vertebrate groups and explain their functions

Analyze the relationship between form and function and explain their interaction with adaptation ‎and constraint

Discuss evolution of vertebrates through scientific studies

Critically evaluate biological literature and interpret case studies in vertebrate biology, through ‎discussions, presentations and reports

BIOE230.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE230 Microbiology
BIOE230.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE230
This course aims at studying the history and scope of microbiology, and microscopy. It includes studying the structure of prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, microbial nutrition and types of microbial growth, metabolism and energy generation, microbial control by physical and chemical agents, the bases of bacterial taxonomy and genetics and an introduction to the general characteristics and diversity of the various groups of microorganisms including bacteria, fungi, viruses, protozoa and micro-algae.
Microbiology (BIOE230) > Credit Hours : 3

Microbiology (BIOE230) > Prerequisites
BIOC160 with a minimum grade D

BIOC165 with a minimum grade D or BIOL105 with a minimum grade D

BIOL114 with a minimum grade D
Microbiology (BIOE230) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

‎Identify the different groups of microorganisms in nature and to demonstrate familiarly with these ‎microorganisms.‎

Discuss and evaluate the impact of microorganisms on human affairs.‎

Evaluate all factors affecting microbial growth, nutrition and metabolism.‎

Identify and recognize the methods of microbial cultivation, purification and assay.‎

Explain the impacts of physical and chemical environmental factors on microbial growth.‎

Relate the theoretical science with the practical applied science.‎

Perform microbiological laboratory experiments including statistical analysis and results interpretation.

BIOE240.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE240 Principles of Environmental Science
BIOE240.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE240
This course attempts to provide an overview of environmental science: the interactions between humans and the environment, with an emphasis on the natural science elements of environmental issues. More specifically, this course is an introduction to the various ways that humans depend on the earth's natural resources, and how human activities directly and indirectly affect the earth and its human and non-human inhabitants. In addition, the course will explore how policy, individual behavior, and technology can prevent, control, and reverse environmental harm.
Principles of Environmental Science (BIOE240) > Credit Hours : 3

Principles of Environmental Science (BIOE240) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze The Complexity Of The Relationships Between The Environment And Mankind

Assess The Effect And Importance Of Individual Behavior In Environmental Issues

Explain The Impact Of Major Global Environmental Problems On Human And Ecosystems Health And Functions

Identify Major Local, Regional And Global Environmental Policies And Regulations To Protect The Environment.

Identify The Major Local, Regional And Global Environmental Problems

BIOE250.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE250 Biodiversity and Evolution
BIOE250.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE250
This course aims at covering the diversity at the species, genetic, and ecosystem levels. Evolutionary processes controlling biodiversity and extinction are also explained. Topics covered include hereditary mechanisms leading to genetic diversity, description of biodiversity in different kingdoms, mechanisms leading to divergence of species and diversification, evolution of different life history patterns, and the conditions that lead to extinction of species.
Biodiversity and Evolution (BIOE250) > Credit Hours : 3

Biodiversity and Evolution (BIOE250) > Prerequisites
BIOC100 with a minimum grade D
Biodiversity and Evolution (BIOE250) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate the underlying principles of classifying living organisms in different biological kingdoms.

Criticize the evidence in support of the different theories of evolution.

Explain the contribution of genetics to the modern evolutionary theory.

Specify how natural selection and genetic drift can lead to speciation.

BIOE310.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE310 Insect Diversity, Ecology, and Systematics
BIOE310.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE310
This course introduces students to the biology of insects. It discusses classification, ecology, structure, and function of insects. In addition, students will learn about insect diversity, their role in natural ecosystems, the basics of their physiology, development, and behavior, and the many important ways they affect human life. A three-hour laboratory component is included in this course that will emphasize functional morphology and adaptations of different insect taxa.
Insect Diversity, Ecology, and Systematics (BIOE310) > Credit Hours : 3

Insect Diversity, Ecology, and Systematics (BIOE310) > Prerequisites
BIOC250
Insect Diversity, Ecology, and Systematics (BIOE310) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe insect body parts and their modifications (external morphology).

Discuss insect diversity and its role in ecosystems.

Discuss the interactions between insects, plants, insects, animals, and humans.

Describe and identify the characteristics of different insect taxa and use them in insect identification (insect taxonomy).

BIOE320.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE320 Population and Community Ecology
BIOE320.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE320
Community ecology allows us to understand the natural world in terms of different species interacting with each other and with their physical environments. In this course, we will explore the principles of how communities are assembled, how species influence each other through competition, predation, or mutualism, how energy and matter flow through communities, and how this all relates to the structure of communities. We will consider the stability and complexity of ecological communities, and explore the dynamics which can arise through the interactions between the component parts of an ecological community. Students will have the opportunity to apply what they learn to real environmental issues; working actively in the lab to investigate real ecological communities and propose reasoned solutions based on their own original hands-on analysis. A three laboratory component is included in this course highlighting laboratory and field based exercises examining interactions within ecological communities.
Population and Community Ecology (BIOE320) > Credit Hours : 3

Population and Community Ecology (BIOE320) > Prerequisites
BIOC250
Population and Community Ecology (BIOE320) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze ecological communities and present reasoned arguments about the nature of interactions between the component species.

Identify key physical elements of the natural environment, and explain how these key elements are transferred between different types of organism within the community.

Investigate real environmental issues and propose reasoned solutions based on the principles of community ecology.

BIOE330.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE330 Diversity and Biology of Fungi
BIOE330.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE330
This course aims at introducing a complete idea about fungi. It includes the definition of fungi, their structure, nutrition, growth, reproduction, economic and medical importance, and a taxonomic study of the major fungal groups through studying the life cycle and properties of one or more important fungi from each group family.
Diversity and Biology of Fungi (BIOE330) > Credit Hours : 3

Diversity and Biology of Fungi (BIOE330) > Prerequisites
BIOE230 with a minimum grade D
Diversity and Biology of Fungi (BIOE330) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify and recognize the different groups of fungi in different habitats.

Demonstrate familiarly with beneficial and harmful fungi.

Describe the impact of fungi on human affairs from the medical, agricultural and environmental point of views.

Describe the basic concepts of fungal cell structures and functions.

Recognize and analyze all laboratory techniques.

Perform laboratory experiments including statistical analysis and results interpretation.

BIOE332.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE332 Biology of Parasites
BIOE332.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE332
The course starts by introducing the biology of parasites including the history of the discipline, its relationship, and contributions to other sciences as well as its underlying concepts and terms. A concise overview of immunology, pathology, and epidemiology are then followed to comprehend the various facets of a host-parasite relationship. The core of the course will be given to detailed discussions of some micro- and macro-parasites that cover the major parasitic groups. The aspects to be covered include taxonomy, biology, ecology, pathology, immunology, social and economic impact, life cycle and mode of transmission, epidemiology, diagnosis, and treatment. The problem of drug resistance, control, and prevention, efforts for vaccine development; will be discussed wherever appropriate. The course ends with a discussion of the interplay between parasites and their hosts. A three-hour laboratory component examining major parasite groups is included in this course.
Biology of Parasites (BIOE332) > Credit Hours : 3

Biology of Parasites (BIOE332) > Prerequisites
BIOC250 with a minimum grade D
Biology of Parasites (BIOE332) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

‎Classify and identify the parasitic specimen.‎

Define And Explain The Main Concepts And Definitions Within The Discipline.

Infer current research questions in parasitology using published books and original papers and present them orally and in writing.

Compare how parasites affect physiological, behavioral and ecological adaptations in the ‎host.‎

‎Evaluate the importance of parasites from evolutionary and ecological perspectives.‎

BIOE340.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE340 Biology and Diversity of Mammals
BIOE340.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE340
This course provides a survey of mammals’ major taxa, where it explores the diversity, taxonomy, distribution, and status of living mammals. There will be special emphasis on the mammals of Arabia. Specimens of teeth and other bones will be presented in class for identification purposes, pending resource/time availability. This will ensure the students have some practical hands-on experience of the functional morphology of mammals.
Biology and Diversity of Mammals (BIOE340) > Credit Hours : 3

Biology and Diversity of Mammals (BIOE340) > Prerequisites
BIOE250 with a minimum grade D
Biology and Diversity of Mammals (BIOE340) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the main characteristics of mammals.

Identify the major steps in mammalian evolution.

Explain the differences among mammalian orders and use of dichotomous keys to identify mammals.

Describe basic mammalian anatomy, physiology, and reproduction.

Discuss mammalian behavior and conservation efforts of endangered species.

BIOE350.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE350 Plant Anatomy and Physiology
BIOE350.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE350
Students will study the processes involved in plant growth and development from cells ‎and tissues to plant communities, the functional anatomy and adaptations of plants and ‎the ecophysiology of natural and managed ecosystems. Students will gain an ‎understanding of the vital link between the function of a plant and its anatomy and ‎morphology and the transfer processes of the soil-plant atmosphere system.‎
Plant Anatomy and Physiology (BIOE350) > Credit Hours : 3

Plant Anatomy and Physiology (BIOE350) > Prerequisites
BIOC160
Plant Anatomy and Physiology (BIOE350) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe and explain basic concepts in plant anatomy and physiology

Explain generative and vegetative plant multiplication, reproduction, water and nutrient transport, and the central plant operations of photosynthesis mechanism.

Conduct research on fundamental plant processes, responses to stress, or other physiological processes by reviewing relevant literature.

Present findings of literature surveys on topics in plant anatomy and physiology, individually or as part of a group

Explain the plant’s response towards different kind of abiotic stresses

BIOE355.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE355 Animal Anatomy and Physiology
BIOE355.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE355
This course aims at covering the interplay and communication that coordinates cells into organ systems and organisms as whole, with especial emphasis on form and function in animal groups. Different organ systems including nervous system, hormonal system, cardiovascular system, respiratory system, immune system and urinary system will be discussed emphasizing how these systems are integrated and how homeostatic is maintained during health or challenged under conditions of disease and stress.
Animal Anatomy and Physiology (BIOE355) > Credit Hours : 3

Animal Anatomy and Physiology (BIOE355) > Prerequisites
BIOC160
Animal Anatomy and Physiology (BIOE355) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the functions of the organs of the animal body

Describe the basic physical-chemical mechanisms responsible for each organ system function.

Relate the integrative interaction between different organ systems to achieve body homeostasis.

Recognize and analyze pathophysiological states (disease) as consequences of altered cell and organ function

Deliver presentations and produce reports on selected topics on animal anatomy and physiology.

BIOE360.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE360 Principles of Oceanography
BIOE360.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE360
The course is a multidisciplinary one that focuses on the main Oceanographic topics, including the principals of the different oceanic studies such as, Physical Oceanography, Geological Oceanography, Chemical Oceanography, Biological Oceanography, and Marine pollution as well as the law of the sea.
Principles of Oceanography (BIOE360) > Credit Hours : 3

Principles of Oceanography (BIOE360) > Prerequisites
BIOC160
Principles of Oceanography (BIOE360) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Outline the basic concepts, processes, and analytical tools in the science of oceanography.

Communicate orally and in writing concepts in oceanography.

Evaluate and articulate the application and relevance of specific oceanographic topics to the world around them at a personal, community, and global level.

Analyze and evaluate scientific data to create a conclusion about oceanographic processes.

Explain interrelationships of oceans to other earth systems

BIOE370.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE370 Botany
BIOE370.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE370
A study of the basic principles of plant life. Topics of study include: Plant Essential to Human Life, structures and functions of flowering plants and their cells, tissues, flowers, fruits, and seeds, growth and development of plants from seed to maturity, pollination and fertilization. Related investigations take place during three hours of lab each week. Laboratory topics include: a microscopic study of tissues, and study the diversity of plant parts (flowers, fruits and seeds). A greenhouse is available for class use.
Botany (BIOE370) > Credit Hours : 3

Botany (BIOE370) > Prerequisites
BIOC165
Botany (BIOE370) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Illustrate the benefits of plants to the environment and to the human.

Explain flower structure, embryo development, seed structure and types of fruits

Research scientific literature and produce reports on topics in plant biology

Design and conduct experiments in plant growth and development, collect data, analyze and interpret results

Present findings of guided research in plant biology, including anatomy, physiology and evolution individually or as part of a group.

BIOE380.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE380 Desert Ecology
BIOE380.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE380
This course aims at covering the general history and evolution of desert ecosystems. Topics covered include the biological and physical factors that shaped unique adaptations of desert organisms, the interactions dominating and influencing food webs, biodiversity, human impact, and future of deserts.
Desert Ecology (BIOE380) > Credit Hours : 3

Desert Ecology (BIOE380) > Prerequisites
BIOC250
Desert Ecology (BIOE380) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe The Concepts Of Relationships Within Desert Ecosystems Through Group Discussions And Reporting Case Studies From The Region.

Describe The Concepts Relating To Deserts And The Interactions Ofbiotic As Well As Abiotic Components.

Highlight The Role Of Humans In Desert Ecosystems Within The Uae And Around The Globe.

Recognize The Various Desert Plants And Animals And Their Living Adaptations.

BIOE391.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE391 Field Ecology
BIOE391.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE391
This course introduces students to survey methods in ecology using a hands-on approach. Through lectures, problem-solving exercises, and a major field/laboratory component, students will develop the ability to study organisms and communities in the field and utilize them in assessing environmental health.
Field Ecology (BIOE391) > Credit Hours : 3

Field Ecology (BIOE391) > Prerequisites
BIOC160 with a minimum grade D
Field Ecology (BIOE391) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

‎Recognize principal tools of field surveys involving different organismal groups.

Identify different major organismal groups using a combination of resources.

Conduct field surveys using appropriate study design, sampling techniques and analyze data.

Interpret, discuss and present results in reports and presentations both individually or as ‎part of a group.

BIOE435.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE435 Bacteriology
BIOE435.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE435
This course aims at studying the bacterial cell, and the criteria used in the differentiation and identification of bacteria. It includes the classification of bacteria into different groups with examples of the most common genera and species in each group, and the economic and medical importance of bacteria to man and the environment.
Bacteriology (BIOE435) > Credit Hours : 3

Bacteriology (BIOE435) > Prerequisites
BIOE230
Bacteriology (BIOE435) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the different groups of bacteria in nature and to demonstrate familiarly with these bacteria.

Discuss and evaluate the impact of bacteria on human affairs.

Demonstrate the relationship between bacteria and the environment.

Evaluate all factors affecting bacterial growth, nutrition and metabolism.

Apply the recent novel techniques in the field of water and wastewater analysis.

Explain the role of bacteria in the engineering applications and the treatment systems.

Relate the theoretical science with the practical applied science.

BIOE436.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE436 Molecular Ecology
BIOE436.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE436
This course provides an overview of molecular tools used in the study of ecological and evolutionary processes in natural populations and their impact on biodiversity. A hierarchical approach is used to examine ecological processes from studies involving individuals, parentage, kinship, population structure, species identity, community genomics using molecular markers. Students will become familiar with methods, their strengths and limitations as well as data analytical techniques. Discussions will include conservation genetics, applications to plant breeding and surveillance of genetically modified organisms.
Molecular Ecology (BIOE436) > Credit Hours : 3

Molecular Ecology (BIOE436) > Prerequisites
BIOC250 with a minimum grade D

BIOC270 with a minimum grade D
Molecular Ecology (BIOE436) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe basic concepts relating to molecular aspects of ecology.

Explain molecular aspects of population biology, phylogeography and conservation genetics using appropriate terminology

Analyze complex interactions through case studies and focused literature reviews.

Recognize scientific approaches to the study of molecular aspects of ecology through examples of manipulative experiments.

BIOE450.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE450 Biology and Diversity of Birds
BIOE450.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE450
This course is an advanced undergraduate survey of the biology and diversity of birds. The course focuses on evolutionary biology, functional morphology, physiology, systematics, ecology and behavior. The course will explain concepts leading to understanding of evolutionary hypotheses, ecological processes, physiological and neurobiological mechanisms, and behavioral characteristics using birds as examples. It will emphasize on methods of conducting scientific research, from collecting data on birds to reading, writing, and interpreting the scientific literature, using birds as model organisms. A three-hour laboratory is included in this course that will examine diversity, functional morphology and adaptations in birds.
Biology and Diversity of Birds (BIOE450) > Credit Hours : 3

Biology and Diversity of Birds (BIOE450) > Prerequisites
BIOC100 with a minimum grade D
Biology and Diversity of Birds (BIOE450) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Interpret classification of all major chordates.

Describe morphological characteristics of different avian groups and explain their functions.

Analyze the relationship between form and function and explain their interaction with adaptation and constraint.

Discuss evolution of vertebrates through scientific studies.

Critically evaluate biological literature and interpret case studies in avian biology, through discussions, presentations and reports.

BIOE453.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE453 Environmental Toxicology
BIOE453.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE453
The course aims at introducing a profound knowledge of the fundamental concepts of toxicity and its ecological implications. It includes a detailed study of the classification of toxicants and pollutants, the principal physiological mechanisms governing the action of these pollutants and some general aspects of pollution stress on individuals, populations and ecosystems.
Environmental Toxicology (BIOE453) > Credit Hours : 3

Environmental Toxicology (BIOE453) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Classify toxicants and pollutants and their impact on the environment.

Describe the environmental toxicology and its ecological implications.

Describe the role of pesticides (insecticides, fungicides, herbicides, acaricides, and rodenticides) as major environmental pollutants.

Discuss the effects of toxins as major stress factors on individuals, populations and ecosystems.

Identify environment crises arising from toxins in ecosystems.

Interpret the modes of action of toxins on physiology

BIOE454.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE454 Marine Biology
BIOE454.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE454
This course aims at developing a clear understanding of the basic concepts in marine biology as an integrated part of the student's overall curriculum. It includes physico-chemical properties of the water, marine biodiversity, plankton, nekton, benthos, seaweeds, kelp forest, coral reefs, marine reptiles, birds, marine mammals and mariculture.
Marine Biology (BIOE454) > Credit Hours : 3

Marine Biology (BIOE454) > Prerequisites
BIOC250 with a minimum grade D
Marine Biology (BIOE454) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the diversity of marine organisms, their evolutionary history, biogeography, interactions with other organisms, and adaptations to their environments.

Formulate hypotheses about marine-related scientific questions and design and execute experiments to test those hypotheses.

Synthesize knowledge of physical and chemical processes of oceans and the biology of organisms to ask questions about natural history and ecology.

Summarize the impact of habitat perturbation on marine organisms, and subsequent ecosystem-level consequences and feedbacks.

BIOE457.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE457 Animal Behavior
BIOE457.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE457
This course is an advanced level survey of modern approaches to the study of animal behavior, emphasizing the integration of ecological, evolutionary, ethological, and physiological approaches.
Animal Behavior (BIOE457) > Credit Hours : 3

Animal Behavior (BIOE457) > Prerequisites
BIOE250 with a minimum grade D
Animal Behavior (BIOE457) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the basic elements of the study of animal behavior and the general terminology associated with experimental approaches.

Describe the basic principles of genetics as it relates to animal behavior, evolution, and traits.

Critique theories on homing, migration, communication, foraging, timekeeping, and others.

Explain animal intelligence and how it relates to the processes of individual and phylogenetic learning.

BIOE459.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE459 Conservation Biology
BIOE459.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE459
The course explores the diversity of life, how that diversity has changed over Earth history, and how human disturbance now threatens that diversity. We begin the course with the study of biodiversity globally. We then explore a number of conservation topics, including species conservation, global biodiversity, conservation genetics, community- and ecosystem-level conservation, habitat fragmentation, conservation reserves, and ecological restoration.
Conservation Biology (BIOE459) > Credit Hours : 3

Conservation Biology (BIOE459) > Prerequisites
BIOC160 with a minimum grade D
Conservation Biology (BIOE459) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain biodiversity at different levels.

Outline knowledge in biodiversity within biological management and conservation projects.

Identify the utilitarian and aesthetic values in the field of conservation biology.

Explain how individuals can help to sustain biodiversity.

BIOE599.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE599 Independent Study
BIOE599.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE599
The course is taken only in case the courses offered within the MSc program do not satisfy the student’s academic needs. This course aims at filling-in knowledge gaps in topics closely related to the students’ research work and expected expertise. This course has to be based on the student’s independent learning. Learning may be based on term papers, literature review and presentations on topics closely related to the specific field of study. Depth of the topics covered is a key aspect of this course. The research topic (ie. Thesis title) of the student is to be communicated to the instructor of this course, in order for him/her to efficiently plan for the independent studies to be addressed. The students’ supervisor is responsible to identify and contact the faculty member who will teach this course.
Independent Study (BIOE599) > Credit Hours : 3

BIOE601.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE601 Environmental Sciences
BIOE601.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE601
This course is divided into two parts: First part is Environmental Geology which is designed to teach how geological phenomena such as flooding, earthquakes etc. are strongly related with many environmental issues and understanding of their influences on environmental related problems. The course will include two main sections: the first focusing on internal structure of earth, plate tectonics, mineral resources, and rocks/soils. While the second covers water resources and its management, water pollution, natural hazards, global climate changes and their relationships to the environment. Second part is Environmental Biology which will deal with the biological issues such as, ecological principles, biological resources and its hierarchical structure. In addition, it will cover different environmental biomes as well different phenomenon at the biosphere level, such as, natural disasters and anthropogenic impacts mainly, biodiversity loss, invasive species, and red tides. In addition, biodiversity, water pollution as well as management of aquatic bodies and protected areas will be covered as part of environmental conservation in light of global climate change.
Environmental Sciences (BIOE601) > Credit Hours : 3

Environmental Sciences (BIOE601) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Critically Examine basic environmental information to assess any biologically and geologically related problems.

Critically evaluate the fundamental relationships between natural and Anthropogenic hazards associated with environmental problems.

Critically evaluate interdisciplinary scientific skills to deal with environmental problems.

Improve students’ awareness on environmental problems and solutions with the aim of establishing the sense of environmental citizenship at the student attitude.

Develop the students’ ability in finding proper and ecologically sound solutions to the existing environmental problems on both local and global levels.

BIOE602.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE602 Applied Ecology
BIOE602.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE602
This course aims at studying ecological theory and how it can be applied to environmental problems. It reviews the principles that underlie ecological processes and the extent to which these are used in environmental management. monitoring and assessment of natural resources play an important component of the applications in ecology. Applied Ecology starts with an analysis of our planet’s basic natural resources – energy, water and soil; it moves on to the management of biological resources – fish, grazing lands and forests, and then to exploiting variability, pest control and measuring the effects of pollution. Finally, the course tackles conservation and management of wild species, modeling ecosystems and the restoration of ecological communities. The use of RS/GIS in monitoring and adopting proper management and conservation outcomes will be the focus of the second part of the course.
Applied Ecology (BIOE602) > Credit Hours : 2

Applied Ecology (BIOE602) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Summarize ecological principles and solve UAE and world related ecological and environmental problems.

Recognize methodologies used to solve challenges facing our world such as land degradation, deforestation, loss of biodiversity and pollution.

Develop practical plans to tackle ecological and environmental challenges.

Solve practical environmental and ecological problems using Geospatial technologies such as: Remote Sensing and GIS.

BIOE603.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE603 Field Survey and Environmental Assessment
BIOE603.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE603
This course introduces students to several of the major tools to address issues relating to field surveys and environmental assessment. Through lectures, problem-solving exercises, group assignments, the students will develop a good idea on best approaches to survey field related resources and assess evironmental indicators. The course covers scientific investigation and sampling, environmental assessment, laws and regulations, and elements of environmental assessment techniques and methods.
Field Survey and Environmental Assessment (BIOE603) > Credit Hours : 2

Field Survey and Environmental Assessment (BIOE603) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Summarize principal tools of field surveys and environmental impact assessment.

Apply generalized scientific approaches in field surveying and environmental assessment, experimental designs and data preparation and analysis.

Recognize environmental assessment methods and apply them to field surveys and environmental impact assessment.

Analyze and interpret environmental data in varied ways to solve environmental challenges.

BIOE604.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE604 Complementary Alternative Medicine
BIOE604.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE604
According to NIH “complementary” refers to an unorthodox practice used together with conventional medicine. For example, acupuncture to help with side effects of cancer treatment. The term “Alternative” however refers to a practice that used to replace a conventional medicine. The global use of non-traditional therapeutic modalities, herbal medicines, and supplements has grown exponentially. Thus, this Master program recognizes the need to develop and incorporate CAM into the education of its environmental students and into graduate programs in general. This graduate course focuses on principles of complementary and alternative therapies including but not limited to dynamic phytotherapy and herbal medicine.
Complementary Alternative Medicine (BIOE604) > Credit Hours : 2

Complementary Alternative Medicine (BIOE604) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Summarize underlying principles of CAM.

Distinguish, compare, and contrast various CAM modalities.

Differentiate between the currently popular targeted medicine versus broad‐spectrum approach.

Explain underlying principles of CAM.

BIOE615.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE615 Coastal and Marine Management
BIOE615.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE615
This course is an intensive introduction to the principles and practices of coastal zone management, with specific reference to coastal zone issues. It is pitched at immediate postgraduate / Masters student level, but is also intended as a continuing professional development course suitable for professional environmental managers and consultants. It will also be suitable as a continuing education course for others with relevant interests.
Coastal and Marine Management (BIOE615) > Credit Hours : 2

Coastal and Marine Management (BIOE615) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Summarize ecological, geological, chemical and biological concepts as they relate to the coastal zone environment.

Analyze the interests of stakeholders from a multidisciplinary and integrated perspective.

Recognize current and future human-driven problems that impact the marine environment and propose solutions using scientific principles.

Describe and analyze interactive policy development and decision-making in coastal zone management problems.

Evaluate projects focused at sustainable development of commercial activities in the coastal zone.

BIOE616.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE616 Genetically Modified Organisms
BIOE616.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE616
In the past few decades, our understanding of molecular biology and genetics has enabled us to transform the face of food production and to drastically increase access to human therapies, and in the near future, it may help us mitigate the looming energy crisis. This course will explore the ways in which genetically modified organisms (GMOs) have already influenced our society, examine their potential to confront the challenges that lie ahead, and delve into the biological details of what GMOs are and how they are made. Completion of Molecular Biology course is strongly recommended but not mandatory.
Genetically Modified Organisms (BIOE616) > Credit Hours : 2

Genetically Modified Organisms (BIOE616) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain major biological concepts.

Solve and criticize practical and theoretical problems in biology.

Conduct safe and ethical biological lab experiments, data analysis, and interpretation of results.

Demonstrate research competence including analysis of scientific literature and adherence to research ethics.

BIOE620.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE620 Environmental Awareness and Education
BIOE620.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE620
Environmental education is a process that allows individuals to explore environmental issues, engage in problem solving, and take action to improve the environment. As a result, individuals develop a deeper understanding of environmental issues and have the skills to make informed and responsible decisions.
Environmental Awareness and Education (BIOE620) > Credit Hours : 2

Environmental Awareness and Education (BIOE620) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe of the impact of human activity on the environment.

Explain how environmental awareness and education impact daily changes in societal approaches.

Define modern ways to improve environmental awareness and education and address faced challenges.

Communicate proper environmental awareness and education strategies to ensure adoption by the wider community.

BIOE623.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE623 Environmental Microbiology
BIOE623.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE623
Functional aspects of microorganisms in nature. Diversity of microbial habitats. Inter-and extra microbial relationships. Transformation in geochemical cycles. Microbial toxins in the environment.
Environmental Microbiology (BIOE623) > Credit Hours : 2

Environmental Microbiology (BIOE623) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Appraise The Role Of Microbes In The Applied And Environmental Applications.

Investigate The Advantages And Limitations Of Current Tools For Investigation Of Environmental Microbiology.

Investigate The Important Role Of Microorganisms In Both The Natural And Man-Made Environment.

Present Scientific Papers In Environmental Microbiology.

Relate The Relationship Between Microorganisms And The Environment.

Value The Occurrence, Abundance And Distribution Of Microorganism In The Environment.

BIOE624.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE624 Sustainable Development
BIOE624.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE624
This course is designed to serve as a foundation course for graduate studies in Sustainable Development. It will introduce to students the core concepts, principles and practices of sustainable development (SD). It examines the environmental, economic, and social dimensions of SD by focusing on changing patterns of consumption, production, and distribution of resources. This course includes an international focus and examines the impact of globalization, the role of the private sector, and NGOs. This course also considers the evolving models of the economic evaluation of SD initiatives and programs.
Sustainable Development (BIOE624) > Credit Hours : 2

Sustainable Development (BIOE624) > Prerequisites
BIOE602
Sustainable Development (BIOE624) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Critically evaluate the sustainability of ‘infrastructure’, projects and other human activities on the environment.

Characterize conceptual and practical issues relating to sustainable development.

Describe modern ways to address sustainable management challenges using sustainable technologies and interdisciplinary principles.

Critically examine strategies to ensure sustainable development of current and future resources in our environment.

BIOE625.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE625 Coastal Management
BIOE625.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE625
Characteristics of the marine environment and primary productivity. Marine resources and organisms of economic importance. Management of resources and hazards of pollution. Conservation laws and legal aspects.
Coastal Management (BIOE625) > Credit Hours : 2

Coastal Management (BIOE625) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze The Interests Of Stakeholders From A Multidisciplinary And Integrated Perspective.

Gain Knowledge In Ecological, Geological, Chemical And Biological Concepts As They Relate To The Coastal Zone Environment.

Participate In Projects Focused At Sustainable Development Of Commercial Activities In The Coastal Zone

Participate In The Implementation Of Interactive Policy Development And Decision-Making In Coastal Zone Management Problems.

Understand The Natural And Human-Driven Problems Currently, And Anticipated To, Impact The Marine Environment

BIOE626.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE626 Air Quality and Climate Change
BIOE626.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE626
This is an introductory course to air pollution.
