Students will gain an understanding of the types, sources and effect of air pollutants as well as the general knowledge of the legislative and regulatory approaches to air quality management. Students will also gain insight into the dispersion of air pollution in the atmosphere as well as an understanding of physical and chemical behavior of gaseous pollutants, air quality modeling and meteorological factors that contribute to air quality degradation. The course will also expose students to analytical techniques for air quality monitoring and a wide range of air pollution control technologies and legislation.
Air Quality and Climate Change (BIOE626) > Credit Hours : 2

Air Quality and Climate Change (BIOE626) > Prerequisites
BIOE601
Air Quality and Climate Change (BIOE626) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify major global environmental changes affecting air quality and climate change.

Explain key components of climate change and its potential human health impacts.

Evaluate global environmental changes and characterize their specific health outcomes.

Characterize biological mechanisms involved in environmental exposure as a result of air quality and climate change.

BIOE627.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE627 Desert Ecology
BIOE627.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE627
Course material will be a collection of book chapters and review articles. This course focuses on studying the ecology of deserts, their environments, formation and diagnostic features. It covers the desert ecology, population and community ecology, physiology and behavior. It concentrates on the principles that underline environmental adaptations and their underlying /morphological/physiological mechanisms.
Desert Ecology (BIOE627) > Credit Hours : 2

Desert Ecology (BIOE627) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co BIOE601
Desert Ecology (BIOE627) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognize species interactions and adaptations of organisms in desert environments.

Evaluate components of deserts and recognize deserts as complex biomes.

Outline issues relating to desert conservation.

Solve problems relating to desert conservation.

Analyze and interpret data relating to scientific investigations in desert ecosystems.

BIOE636.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE636 Seminar in Environmental Science
BIOE636.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE636
Analysis of current and prospective issues in specified subject areas related to the students field of research interest. The students will present results and finding from their research or will present a review articles or recent journal publications of related topics, and also the exploration of unsolved scientific problems and opportunities in the field, especially which related the country and to the gulf region.
Seminar in Environmental Science (BIOE636) > Credit Hours : 1

Seminar in Environmental Science (BIOE636) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate current research of selected topics and their impact on scientific findings.

Evaluate methods and results within the field of specialization critically and ethically.

Demonstrate strong written and oral presentation skills both individually and as part of a team.

BIOE700.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE700 Lab Rotations
BIOE700.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE700
Ph.D. students are required to take a lab rotation-based course during their first year of graduate study. Typically, students will be required to rotate through 3 to 4 laboratories (minimum of 2 in exceptionally trained students), covering the whole semester. During each laboratory rotation, the student will be exposed to methods, equipment, and experimental procedures currently in use in a particular departmental research laboratory selected by the student and through arrangement with the professor in charge of that laboratory. At the end of each rotation, students will receive a written evaluation from the rotation supervisor. These evaluations are then submitted to the program chair to become part of the student’s permanent file. It is important to note that these evaluation letters will be considered during the comprehensive examination evaluation.
Lab Rotations (BIOE700) > Credit Hours : 3

Lab Rotations (BIOE700) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Examine different scientific methods use in ecology and environmental sciences.

Interpret scientific information from published literature to address ecological and environmental challenges.

Synthesize scientific information and address challenges through experimentation.

Propose different solutions to an environmental problem facing our society.

BIOE703.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE703 Applied Biostatistics
BIOE703.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE703
In this applied biostatistics course we will explore the use of statistical methodology in designing, analyzing, interpreting, and presenting biological experiments and observations. This course covers the basic applied statistics tools for the collection, analysis, and presentation of data. Central to these skills is assessing the impact of chance and variability on the interpretation of research findings and subsequent recommendations for experimental studies in biology. Topics covered include: general principles of study design; hypothesis testing; elements of experimental design; review of methods for comparison of discrete and continuous data including ANOVA, t-test, correlation, and regression as they relate to biological data.
Applied Biostatistics (BIOE703) > Credit Hours : 3

Applied Biostatistics (BIOE703) > Prerequisites
STAT235 with a minimum grade D
Applied Biostatistics (BIOE703) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss statistical inference using confidence intervals and tests of significance.

Explain the differences among various statistical techniques and identify an appropriate technique for a given set of variables and research questions.

Tabulate, summarize and interpret data visually through appropriate statistical graphs.

Perform a T-Test, ANOVA, Regression and Correlation analyses using practical data.

Interpret output data relating to T-Test, ANOVA, Regression and Correlation from statistical packages (eg. SPSS and RStudio).

BIOE710.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE710 Field Ecology
BIOE710.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE710
The course surveys the quantitative field methods in ecology. Lectures and field applications focus on research design and hypothesis testing, with an emphasis on sampling design, measurement, and statistical comparison of environmental variables, plant and animal abundance, diversity, spatial pattern, and species composition. Students will build skills in statistical analysis, scientific rigor, and critical thinking, and in the practical application of quantitative field methods in ecology. Prerequisites: At least minor in biology including ecology course(s), concurrent with Biostatistics or consent of Ph.D. committee.
Field Ecology (BIOE710) > Credit Hours : 3

Field Ecology (BIOE710) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Design studies and test hypotheses in field ecology.

Demonstrate competence in field techniques in a wide range of ecological studies.

Demonstrate skills in recording observations of ecological interactions in natural settings.

Perform statistical analyses on data collected from ecological studies.

Present results and write scientific reports on collected/analysed data.

BIOE720.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE720 Ecosystem Management & Sustainability
BIOE720.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE720
This course will introduce students to the advanced concepts and principles of natural resource management with an emphasis on sustainable ecosystems. Students will learn selected important ecosystem management issues, including genetic diversity in ecosystem management, landscape-level conservation, single-species land management, and the skill and art of keeping fragile ecosystems in balance. Highly complex ecosystem management approaches will be assessed by the students. Additionally, different case studies will be presented to demonstrate how ecological concepts and principles can be applied to the sustainable management of ecosystems. Students will also have a chance to critique and suggest innovative solutions to challenges faced by various ecosystems.
Ecosystem Management & Sustainability (BIOE720) > Credit Hours : 3

Ecosystem Management & Sustainability (BIOE720) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Investigate the concept of "ecosystem" and the advantages and constraints of using ecosystems as a management unit.

Appraise characteristics that might indicate a healthy ecosystem.

Design some environmental management approaches and their strengths and weaknesses.

Develop management goals and objectives that consider sustainability as the core objective of ecosystem management.

Investigate natural resource management knowledge and analytical tools to address environmental issues.

BIOE730.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE730 Topics In Ecology and Environmental Sciences
BIOE730.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE730
This course focuses on exposing students to current topics relating to ecology and environmental sciences. Up-to-date weekly readings will be the core of this course. Students will be required to present and critique publications and their importance to the field. Such course is primarily intended to develop in the students’ ability to use the published literature as the primary source of information. Integration of such information into a cohesive body of knowledge will be assessed. The ability of the student to report, present and review published work will be also tested. The ultimate aim for this course is for the student to develop a research problem(s) and ways to address it through proper scientific methodologies.
Topics In Ecology and Environmental Sciences (BIOE730) > Credit Hours : 3

Topics In Ecology and Environmental Sciences (BIOE730) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate up to date topics relating to ecology and environmental studies with emphasis on innovative techniques and technologies such as remote sensing and GIS, GPS, etc.

Integrate scientific information from published literature to address ecological and environmental challenges.

Develop scientific reports and defend them in front of expert panels.

Compile published work into a cohesive body of knowledge and present findings.

BIOE731.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE731 Aquatic Ecology
BIOE731.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE731
This course will cover the fundamentals of aquatic science bringing together the physical, chemical, and biotic aspects of lake, river, and estuary systems including how humans are changing aquatic ecosystems and management techniques for the use and conservation of these resources. Topics covered during the class will include the structures and function of aquatic systems; the dynamics of the pelagic and littoral zones, human impacts and environmental change, and monitoring and management of aquatic ecosystems.
Aquatic Ecology (BIOE731) > Credit Hours : 3

Aquatic Ecology (BIOE731) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Understand and explain how physical and chemical features in marine and freshwater ecosystems interact and influence plants, animals and ecological processes such as organic matter dynamics.

Demonstrate an understanding of the significance of the need for and correct use of appropriate equipment and methods to sample water quality and biota from a range of aquatic ecosystems.

Predict and appreciate the likely outcomes of changes to land-water linkages and gradients of salinity on plants, animals and ecological processes in aquatic ecosystems.

Apply this knowledge and understanding to manage marine and freshwater ecosystems in an ecologically sustainable manner.

BIOE740.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE740 Wildlife Disease Ecology
BIOE740.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE740
This course will provide an introduction to the field of wildlife disease ecology. Emphasis will be placed on the diversity of parasites and pathogens of wildlife, with an examination of ecological interactions between hosts and parasites from an individual and population-level perspective. This course will also examine strategies used by parasites to exploit hosts, strategies used by hosts to evade parasites, host-parasite coevolution, community ecology of disease, drivers of emerging infectious diseases and the role of disease in wildlife conservation. Prerequisites: Topics in Ecology and Environmental Sciences or consent of Ph.D. committee.
Wildlife Disease Ecology (BIOE740) > Credit Hours : 3

Wildlife Disease Ecology (BIOE740) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe different levels host-parasite or pathogen interactions and their roles in ecosystem.

Explain how host-parasite disease systems evolve.

Identify how wildlife and human interactions facilitate parasite or pathogen evolution and disease emergence.

Review the scientific literature on host-parasite or host-pathogen systems and communicate views orally and in writing.

BIOE759.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE759 Conservation Biology
BIOE759.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE759
It examines patterns of species diversity on earth, comparing past and present extinction of species and assemblages, and identifies the major threats to flora and fauna in the Anthropocene. The course then takes a closer look at selected major threats such as overexploitation, habitat fragmentation and destruction, impact of invasive species etc. The course also examines areas in conservation biology like restoration ecology, conservation genetics, demographic analyses to guide wildlife management and conservation policy. Students will be required to read, understand and discuss research articles covering all aspects of conservation biology.
Conservation Biology (BIOE759) > Credit Hours : 3

Conservation Biology (BIOE759) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Assess different levels of biodiversity and explain their complexity, using contemporary scientific literature.

State and analyze the major threats to biodiversity and explain how the threats may be reduced.

Identify organizations at the international, national, and local levels, as well as laws and policies that are working to sustain biodiversity.

Discuss how education and communication programs are vital components in sustaining biodiversity and offer examples of educational programs.

Review the scientific literature on conservation practices and communicate views orally and in writing.

BIOE765.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE765 Global Environmental Changes
BIOE765.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE765
The course covers both the physiochemical and biological nature of change and the effects and consequences of natural and human-induced change on ecosystems, humans, and human infrastructures. The unifying theme of this course is consideration of both natural and human-induced environmental change, with emphasis on the latter.
Global Environmental Changes (BIOE765) > Credit Hours : 3

Global Environmental Changes (BIOE765) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the major ways in which our global environment is changing.

Explain the physical and biological basis of these changes, and the role which human beings have played in causing them.

Assess and explain the impact of these changes on natural ecosystems, on human beings, and on the infrastructure upon which human beings rely.

BIOE782.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOE782 Desert Ecology
BIOE782.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOE782
The course material will cover book chapters. This course focuses on studying the ecology of deserts, their environments, formation and diagnostic features. It covers the desert ecology, population and community ecology, physiology and behavior. It concentrates on the principles that underlie environmental adaptations and their underlying /morphological/physiological mechanisms.
Desert Ecology (BIOE782) > Credit Hours : 3

Desert Ecology (BIOE782) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognizing the critical importance of the components making deserts as a complex biome within our planet.

Linking the principles of adaptation in desert with data and publication relating to scientific investigations in desert ecosystems.

Learning about the biodiversity issues in desert ecosystems.

Identifying factors contributing to desert sustainability.

Identifying the different adaptations in deset community.

BIOL105.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOL105 Basic Biology II
BIOL105.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOL105
This course aims at covering diverse topics including evolution, speciation, systematic, diversity of plants and animals, plant form and function, animal form and function, and conservation biology. The course is intended to complement Basic Biology (which covers cellular and biochemical basis of life) by covering the basic concepts relating to whole-organism topics.
Basic Biology II (BIOL105) > Credit Hours : 3

Basic Biology II (BIOL105) > Prerequisites
BIOC100 with a minimum grade D
Basic Biology II (BIOL105) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Differentiate plant and animal life cycles in relation to complexity and mode of life.

Discuss the fundamentals of evolution and how it affects the biological thinking

Discuss the major homeostatic mechanism operating in animals.

Explain and list the criteria used in the science of systematic.

Integrate the relationship between animals’ structure and function and their habitats.

Integrate the relationship between plants’ structure and function and their habitats.

Recognize the importance of the diversity of life with emphasis on plants and animals.

BIOL114.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOL114 General Biology Lab
BIOL114.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOL114
This laboratory course aims at introducing the students to the basic laboratory knowledge, skills and measurements in common use in life sciences; applying these knowledge and skills in writing of laboratory reports, using of light microscope, pipetting, diluting and preparing of molar solutions. The major theme will be devoted to describe and analyze the molecules of life, cell structure and function, and plants/animals diversity, structure and function. The latter includes important physiological concepts e.g. photosynthesis in plants and homeostasis in animals.
General Biology Lab (BIOL114) > Credit Hours : 1

General Biology Lab (BIOL114) > Corequisites
BIOL105
General Biology Lab (BIOL114) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Appreciate the importance of writing and data analysis skills independently and in a team.

Define and understand terms relating to form, function and life diversity.

Differentiate major groups of plants and animals and knowing their taxonomy, structures and adaptations in relation to the habitats.

Identify macromolecules properties and detecting them in unknown samples.

Justify knowledge common to contemporary biologists.

Use various techniques in biology experiments.

BIOM229.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM229 Cell Biology I
BIOM229.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM229
This course aims at studying the cell compartments, starting from the nucleus to the cell membrane. It includes description of the structure and function of organelles and the cytoskeleton as well as the genetic diseases affecting the cell functions.
Cell Biology I (BIOM229) > Credit Hours : 2

Cell Biology I (BIOM229) > Prerequisites
BIOC100 with a minimum grade D
Cell Biology I (BIOM229) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Compare and contrast between structures and biogenesis of different cellular rganelles.

Correlate cytoskeletal structures to different cellular functions.

Differentiate between prokaryotes and eukaryotes.

Discriminate between respiration and photosynthesis as tools for energy conservation.

Recognize various structures of the cell and differentiate between them.

BIOM310.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM310 Introduction to Neurosciences
BIOM310.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM310
The course is an introduction to neuroscience. It introduces students to the anatomy and biology of the brain and nervous system. Core topics covered include brain anatomy, mechanisms of neurotransmission and synaptic communication, structure and function of sensory and motor systems, and brain development and plasticity. The course also explores the neural basis of some complex brain processes like language development and learning and memory.
Introduction to Neurosciences (BIOM310) > Credit Hours : 3

Introduction to Neurosciences (BIOM310) > Prerequisites
BIOC290 with a minimum grade D
Introduction to Neurosciences (BIOM310) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the mechanisms underlying neuronal transmission and processing

Illustrate the neuronal basis of neurodegenerative diseases

Describe the hardwiring of the brain and brain plasticity

Critically evaluate the relationship between neural circuitry and behavior

BIOM335.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM335 Molecular Biology of Genes
BIOM335.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM335
This course aims at developing a deeper understanding of gene regulation in eukaryotes and prokaryotes. This course will describe how the genetic information is decoded by transcription and translation to form proteins and how organisms control these processes to ensure that the correct proteins are produced in the correct cells at the correct times and in the correct amounts. This course will examine the mechanisms of transcription initiation, RNA splicing and processing, protein synthesis, activators and attenuators. This course will also examine the effects of catalytic and regulatory RNA in gene regulation. Finally, lectures will also cover the following topics: eukaryotic chromosome structure and its modifications, mechanisms of chromatin-mediated regulation of gene expression, and epigenetics. Research methods that have been applied to achieve our current understanding of these processes will be discussed.
Molecular Biology of Genes (BIOM335) > Credit Hours : 3

Molecular Biology of Genes (BIOM335) > Prerequisites
BIOC290 with a minimum grade D
Molecular Biology of Genes (BIOM335) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the basic concept of molecular interaction that provide the essential cellular function.

Identify major component that are required for molecular interaction.

Identify elements that are necessary for experiment to investigate molecular biology. 4. Read and write specialized reports in molecular biology.

Read and write specialized reports in molecular biology.

BIOM339.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM339 Virology
BIOM339.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM339
This course aims at understanding the basics of virus definition, structure, nomenclature and classification. It includes mode of infection, replication, lysogenic, virus-host interaction, common viral diseases and viral vaccines.
Virology (BIOM339) > Credit Hours : 2

Virology (BIOM339) > Prerequisites
BIOC160 with a minimum grade D
Virology (BIOM339) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the different groups of viruses in nature.

Explain the basic concepts of viral Structures.

Describe the different methods of viral Replication.

Understand and discuss the different methods of virus cultivation, purification, and assay.

Demonstrate and evaluate the impact of viruses on our view of life (on the environment, research and diseases).

Evaluate all laboratory diagnoses of viral diseases.

Explain the role of viruses in the recent novel applications of viruses (water and sewage treatment), treatment of human, animal, plant, and insect diseases.

Relate the theoretical science with the practical applied science.

Solve and criticize practical and theoretical problems related to Virology.

BIOM350.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM350 Developmental Biology
BIOM350.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM350
This course aims at integrating the knowledge of different fields in order to understand the cellular and molecular mechanisms of the processes of the embryonic development in vertebrates and invertebrates. This course will focus on the description of a certain number of modes of development and, on the analysis of the expression and regulation of genes controlling the morphogenesis of the embryo. The students will discuss and interpret the key classical experiments on which the principles of developmental biology are founded. The models of animal developmental biology will be introduced with all the fundamental notions of this discipline. The principle stages of embryogenesis will be illustrated and the classical experiments proving the existence of organizer centers of morphogenesis will be analyzed. The mechanisms by which the layers of embryonic tissues move will be discussed. A certain number of molecules responsible of development will be described and examples of their roles in the cascades of genetic interactions during organogenesis and cellular differentiation will be detailed.
Developmental Biology (BIOM350) > Credit Hours : 3

Developmental Biology (BIOM350) > Prerequisites
BIOC290
Developmental Biology (BIOM350) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate factual and conceptual knowledge of how cells, organs, and organisms work.

Describe scientific hypothesis testing and critical-thinking skills.

Explain arguments orally and in writing, in a standard scientific format.

Manipulate and observe animal embryos and record the timing of early events development and recognize when development has been adversely affected.

Describe developmental processes in animal model systems and recognize the importance of cell-cell interactions.

Work in small groups to look for topics relating several aspects of developmental biology.

BIOM370.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM370 Introductory Bioinformatics
BIOM370.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM370
Bioinformatics is an interdisciplinary topic that encompasses biology, computer science, mathematics and statistics. With the advent of high throughput technologies, large amount of biological data is being generated that provides us rich information about life around us. This course will introduce students to the basic concepts and methods in this field. Topics covered will include sequence databases, sequence searching, sequence alignment, phylogenetics and genome assembly. Each topic will be accompanied by a hand-on computer laboratory session. Furthermore, students will be briefly introduced to how bioinformatics can be used to study human disease.
Introductory Bioinformatics (BIOM370) > Credit Hours : 3

Introductory Bioinformatics (BIOM370) > Prerequisites
BIOC290
Introductory Bioinformatics (BIOM370) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe major bioinformatics tools and algorithms applicable to sequence alignment, phylogenetics and sequence assembly.

Analyze macromolecular sequence and structure using multiple bioinformatics tools.

Interpret research articles and communicate these through individual or group presentations and reports.

BIOM380.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM380 Genomics
BIOM380.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM380
This course provides a comprehensive overview of the fundamental principles and applications of genomics. It introduces the structure and function of genomes and builds an understanding of large-scale genomic analysis. Students will explore workflows of next-generation sequencing (NGS) technologies and computational strategies for genome assembly, annotation, and comparative analysis, enabling the interpretation of genomic information across diverse organisms. The course also examines emerging omics approaches such as metagenomics and transcriptomics, highlighting their roles in studying microbial communities and gene expression. In addition, it discusses the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning in genomic research. Finally, the course addresses the impact of genomics on human and environmental health, emphasizing its applications in personalized medicine, disease understanding, and ecosystem management.
Genomics (BIOM380) > Credit Hours : 3

Genomics (BIOM380) > Prerequisites
BIOC290 with a minimum grade D
Genomics (BIOM380) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the fundamental principles of genomics, including genome structure, organization, and large-scale analysis techniques.

Demonstrate proficiency in next-generation sequencing (NGS) workflows and data processing methods.

Analyze metagenomic and transcriptomic datasets to interpret microbial diversity and gene expression patterns.

Evaluate the applications of artificial intelligence (AI) in genomics and assess their implications for human and environmental health.

BIOM390.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM390 Introduction to Epigenetics
BIOM390.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM390
Chromosomes are always subject to changes in structure and organization which can affect gene expression. These epigenetic modifications can be results of DNA methylation, histone modifications (acetylation, methylation…), chromatin remodeling complexes, and the binding of non-coding RNA (Xist). Epigenetic modifications are either inherited or accumulated throughout a life of an organism. This course is intended to introduce students to the molecular mechanisms underlying epigenetic inheritance. The role of epigenetics in biological processes such as imprinting, X-inactivation, cellular identity and cellular memory will be discussed. The relationship between epigenetic alteration and disease will be reviewed.
Introduction to Epigenetics (BIOM390) > Credit Hours : 2

Introduction to Epigenetics (BIOM390) > Prerequisites
BIOM335 with a minimum grade D
Introduction to Epigenetics (BIOM390) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Understand how chromatin modifications and remodeling regulate gene expression.

Understand how DNA methylation regulates gene expression.

Understand the role of non-coding RNAs in epigenetic regulation.

Understand how epigenetic modifications are propagated and transmitted.

Understand the relationship between epigenetic alterations and diseases including cancer.

BIOM420.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM420 Molecular Basis of Cell and Tissue Development
BIOM420.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM420
The aim of this course is to bring to students the knowledge of fundamental aspects of the Extracellular Matrix (ECM) and its importance for tissue function, wound healing and tissue repair. The students will also acquire basic knowledge on tissue-tissue interactions, and overlapping cellular and molecular pathways that exist in multiple tissues. Understand the concept of a cell cycle, and how it plays an important role in different types of organisms. Evaluate the relative contribution of mutations in tumor suppressor genes and proto-oncogenes in the development of cancer.
Molecular Basis of Cell and Tissue Development (BIOM420) > Credit Hours : 3

Molecular Basis of Cell and Tissue Development (BIOM420) > Prerequisites
BIOM335 with a minimum grade D
Molecular Basis of Cell and Tissue Development (BIOM420) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Gain solid foundation on how cells use pathways to communicate, develop, differentiate and die.

Comprehend how cells use different pathways to relay information or to respond to different stimuli.

Develop general concepts on multidisciplinary natures of the field and how to synthesize different information.

Read and understand original research articles dealing with various signaling transduction pathways and cell development and regeneration.

BIOM430.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM430 Cellular Biochemistry
BIOM430.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM430
This course is designed to provide students with essential and fundamental aspects of the composition and function of bioorganic macromolecules in living systems. The course is divided into five sections: (i) chemical building blocks of cells (carbohydrates, lipids, amino acids, and nucleic acids) and their functional integration into macromolecules with particular emphasis on (ii) protein structure and function will be focused in this course. We will also focus on (iii) how cells obtain energy from nutrients (e.g. carbohydrates and lipids) and how these processes are regulated. On the fourth (vi) part of the course biomembrane structure will be studied in details and (v) an overview of membrane transport will be covered at the end of this course. Throughout the course, cellular and biochemical techniques that enable the study of cellular macromolecules in biomedical research will be discussed.
Cellular Biochemistry (BIOM430) > Credit Hours : 3

Cellular Biochemistry (BIOM430) > Prerequisites
BIOC290 with a minimum grade D
Cellular Biochemistry (BIOM430) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Relate the structure and the physiological function of major biomolecules.

Explain the concept of the structure-function relationship of major biomolecules.

Classify the major biomolecules metabolism and the factors that regulate them.

Describe various techniques used in the field of cellular biochemistry.

BIOM433.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM433 Biotechnology & Genetic Engineering
BIOM433.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM433
This course aims at providing the student with the wealth of knowledge developed in the field of genetic engineering. This course introduces the student to a series of logical ordered recombinant genetic principles. Furthermore, the course is specifically formatted to allow the student the flexibility to follow any one of numerous and interlinking paths through molecular biology concepts, principles and key recombinant genetic methods or approaches toward numerous defined destinations and horizons. The topics include enzymes for molecular cloning, visualization of nucleic acids, and construction of vectors (plasmid, bacteriophage, YAC, etc.). These topics are followed by DNA sequencing, probe construction for gene identification or labeling specific regions of the genomes, construction of genomic and cDNA libraries. Expression of foreign genes in various systems is described. PCR amplification is introduced with its potential applications in research, molecular diagnostic and forensic sciences.
Biotechnology & Genetic Engineering (BIOM433) > Credit Hours : 3

Biotechnology & Genetic Engineering (BIOM433) > Prerequisites
BIOM335 with a minimum grade D
Biotechnology & Genetic Engineering (BIOM433) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognize knowledge and comprehension of core concepts of genetics, microbiology and cellular and molecular biology.

Discuss ethical principles regarding the use of biotechnology.

Solve problems associated with genetic engineering individually and/or collaboratively

BIOM445.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM445 Macromolecules Structure Function and Bioinformatics
BIOM445.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM445
This course will introduce the students to bioinformatics database and bioinformatics tools that can be used to study macromolecular sequence, structure and function. Additionally, students will also be introduced to the concepts of microarrays and microarray data analysis. Furthermore, students will be briefly introduced to how bioinformatics can be used to study human disease.
Macromolecules Structure Function and Bioinformatics (BIOM445) > Credit Hours : 3

Macromolecules Structure Function and Bioinformatics (BIOM445) > Prerequisites
BIOC290
Macromolecules Structure Function and Bioinformatics (BIOM445) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Assimilate Scientific Literature Related To Macromolecular Structure And Function Through Presentations And Reports

Construct Sequence Alignments And Visualize Strucutures Of Macromolecules Using Bioinformatics Tools

Define The Structural Components Of Macromolecules

Describe The Basis Of Macromolecular Sequence And Structure

Examine Dna, Rna & Protein Sequence And Structure Available In Public Databases

BIOM461.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM461 Tissue Culture
BIOM461.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM461
This course aims at understanding the fundamentals of plant and animal tissue culture. It includes sterilization techniques, media preparation and culture of plant tissues, protoplasts, anthers, preparation of animal primary culture, cell line, DNA transfection and cell fusion.
Tissue Culture (BIOM461) > Credit Hours : 3

Tissue Culture (BIOM461) > Prerequisites
BIOC290 with a minimum grade D
Tissue Culture (BIOM461) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain and present ideas on the basic knowledge and skills essential to successful cultivation of plant cells and tissue

Describe laboratory techniques and applications of tissue culture; and the use in genetically modified plants/animals

Analyze and evaluate original research literature and communicate using appropriate technology.

BIOM462.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM462 Immunology
BIOM462.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM462
This course mainly covers the fundamental principle of immunology including hematopoiesis; tissues and cells of the immune system; complement, cytokines; innate immunity; humoral and cell-mediated immune responses; immunoglobulin structure, function and biosynthesis; genetics and generation of diversity in antibody and T cell receptors, lymphocyte activation, major histocompatibility complex and antigen presentation. The course deals briefly with the role of the immune system in controlling diseases, including how the immune system deals with infection; inflammation; allergy and hypersensitivity; tissue graft rejection, clinical tissue matching; the immune system vs. cancer; autoimmune diseases; AIDS. Also, this course briefly covers topics on some common immunological experimental approaches that are used in research and diagnostic laboratories.
Immunology (BIOM462) > Credit Hours : 3

Immunology (BIOM462) > Prerequisites
BIOC290 with a minimum grade D
Immunology (BIOM462) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate the complex cellular and molecular interrelationships between the various components of the immune system and their roles in health and disease.

Assess immunological article reporting a contemporary issue.

Prepare a literature review about an important area of immunology.

Identify molecular or cellular targets for treatment of diseases

BIOM470.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM470 Molecular Physiology
BIOM470.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM470
This topical course deals with the physiological processes at molecular level that are peculiar to higher plants and animals. The course consists of two parts: First part will include the molecular basis of the (i) structure of plants and plant cells, (ii) energy dynamics in plant cells, (iii) water and nutrient transport, (iv) growth and development (v) responses to environmental stresses and (vi) metabolic engineering of natural products. The second part will cover molecular and cellular mechanisms of cell communication within the major integrated systems and their physiological processes in human and animal. This will focus on the endocrine, the nerve, the vascular, and the muscular systems by covering two structural and functional aspects. The first aspect is related to the properties of biomembranes with a particular emphasis on signal transduction and transport across membranes. For this, tangible examples of different types of cell membranes (intestinal mucosa, renal tubules, muscle cells, nerve cells, and retinal cells) will be studied. The second aspect will be on the molecular mechanisms of the endocrine system and hormone action addressing the major endocrine components and glands such as pituitary, thyroid, pancreas, adrenal glands and gonads with examples of endocrine dysfunction and diseases including diabetes, thyroid disorders, obesity, and fertility.
Molecular Physiology (BIOM470) > Credit Hours : 3

Molecular Physiology (BIOM470) > Prerequisites
BIOC290 with a minimum grade D
Molecular Physiology (BIOM470) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Summarize the fundamental molecular principles underlying the physiology, regulation of development, reproduction and adaptation of plants.

Elaborate on plant's response towards abiotic stress at the molecular level.

Integrate the cellular and molecular aspects of human health and physiology. This implies that students will learn how cells, organs and higher level systems are integrated and coordinated in the functions of humans and animals.

Analyze the methods used for metabolic engineering in plants and those for studying the cell and molecular aspects of human physiology.

BIOM481.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM481 Molecular Evolution
BIOM481.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM481
The change in the sequence of macromolecules like DNA, RNA and proteins over several generations is termed as molecular evolution. This course will introduce students to principles of such molecular evolutionary processes and how it can be evaluated. It will also provide knowledge and skills in phylogenetic analysis and how this can be used to study molecular evolution.
Molecular Evolution (BIOM481) > Credit Hours : 3

Molecular Evolution (BIOM481) > Prerequisites
BIOC290 with a minimum grade D
Molecular Evolution (BIOM481) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe evolutionary process at the molecular level.

Explain and justify different models of sequence evolution.

Apply molecular methods to study genetic variation within and between species.

Evaluate different phylogenetic optimality criteria, and select adequate criterion to solve a given problem.

BIOM489.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM489 Molecular Biology Techniques
BIOM489.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM489
This course aims at developing the basics of gene cloning as well as introducing the recent development in molecular biology and bio-computing. It includes introduction to general molecular biology techniques, gene cloning, and bio-computing.
Molecular Biology Techniques (BIOM489) > Credit Hours : 1

Molecular Biology Techniques (BIOM489) > Prerequisites
( BIOC290 or BIOL270)

BIOC275 with a minimum grade D
Molecular Biology Techniques (BIOM489) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Communicate arguments orally and in writing, in a standard scientific format.

Demonstrate basic knowledge of laboratory safety.

Perform various methods for gene cloning.

Prepare independently reagents required and perform the experiments.

Use literature retrieval and reference management techniques and packages

BIOM490.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM490 Biology of Diseases
BIOM490.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM490
This course is designed to introduce students in the “Cellular and Molecular Biology” track to the molecular basis of disease and provide them with in-depth knowledge of the basic molecular mechanisms underlying human diseases such genetic, infectious and metabolic diseases. Examples of diseases highlighted will include cancer, diabetes and obesity, Alzheimer’s disease among others. Overall, this course aims to provide students with knowledge and critical-thinking skills to understand human health and diseases. Experimental approaches utilized to study those diseases will also be discussed.
Biology of Diseases (BIOM490) > Credit Hours : 3

Biology of Diseases (BIOM490) > Prerequisites
BIOC290 with a minimum grade D
Biology of Diseases (BIOM490) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Understand the molecular processes that lead to the development of human diseases and demonstrate how this knowledge contribute to the development of potential therapeutic strategies.

Be able to integrate different fields (physiology, molecular biology, cell biology, etc..) to gain a better understanding of the regulatory mechanism employed by the human body to maintain its health.

Be able to critically evaluate and discuss current research centered on current molecular understanding of disease.

BIOM508.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM508 Advanced Gene Expression
BIOM508.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM508
The objective of this course is to tackle the basic principles and advanced aspects of prokaryotic and eukaryotic molecular biology with topics such as DNA structure, transcriptional and translational mechanisms, and mechanisms of gene expression, activation and inactivation of whole chromosome.
Advanced Gene Expression (BIOM508) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Gene Expression (BIOM508) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Able To Extract Relevant Information From Literature Databases And To Present It In Written And/Or Oral Form.

Analyze Scientific Research In Gene Expression Data Described In Peer-Reviewed Journals And Develop Critical Thinking And Creativity In Scientific Research.

Master Of The Underlying Conceptual Framework Regarding The Molecular Mechanisms In Eukaryotic And Prokaryotic Gene Expression And Regulation At The Transcriptional, Posttranscriptional And Chromatin Levels.

BIOM512.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM512 Advanced Genetic Engineering
BIOM512.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM512
Course content covers nucleic acids and protein detection methodologies, multifunctional vectors and gateway cloning system, protein production in eukaryotes and prokaryotes, Construction and screening of genomic and cDNA expression library, differential and substractifs screening, applications of the PCR: RACE-PCR, Q-PCR, reverse PCR, differential display, in vitro and in vivo footprinting, site directed mutagenesis. In vivo transgenesis strategies (gene over-expression and gene Knock out), conditional knock out, inducible expression system, applications in gene therapy and in biotechnology.
Advanced Genetic Engineering (BIOM512) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Genetic Engineering (BIOM512) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Acquire a great knowledge of the different methodologies in genetic ngineering.

Autonomously design and generate construct of nterest.

Perfectly master the basics and advanced concepts of genetic engineering.

BIOM516.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM516 Advanced Molecular Biology Techniques I
BIOM516.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM516
This is mainly a laboratory exercise course designed to help students become more familiar with common molecular techniques. Lectures will cover basic principles and applied aspects of molecular studies, and recent advances in genomics and proteomic techniques. Practical classes will include DNA/RNA isolation, hybridization, sequence analysis, various PCR reactions, library construction and screening, protein isolation, and plant transformation.
Advanced Molecular Biology Techniques I (BIOM516) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Molecular Biology Techniques I (BIOM516) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze Biological Data Including Genomic And Proteomic Sequences And Structures

Evaluate The Principles Of Rna Extraction

Explain The Purpose Of Rt-Pcr And Its Main Components And Know How Rt-Pcr Differs From Other Available Types

Explain What “Gene Expression” Refers To

Identify And Use Major Bioinformatics Databases Available At Ncbi, Ebi And Elsewhere

Synthesize A Report And Presentation Encompassing Data Obtained And Analyzed From Bioinformatics Database And Analysis Tools Through A Mini-Project.

BIOM525.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM525 Applications of Bioinformatics
BIOM525.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM525
Techniques commonly used to depict biological implications from molecular sequence data. This course will start with introduction to sequence retrieval and identification using databases (e.g., Genbank and EMBO), pairwise sequence comparisons and multiple sequence alignments and conserved sequence pattern, recognition (e.g., gene identification in genomic data, RNA secondary structure prediction). Phylogenetic analysis will be presented in detail (e.g., distance, parsimony, maximum likelihood, and Bayesian methods). tools, phylogenetic analysis.
Applications of Bioinformatics (BIOM525) > Credit Hours : 3

Applications of Bioinformatics (BIOM525) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze biological data including genomic and proteomic sequences and structures.

Compare the advantages and disadvantages of various bioinformatics algorithms and tools.

Identify and use major bioinformatics databases available at Ncbi, Ebi and Elsewhere.

Synthesize a report and presentation encompassing data obtained and analyzed from bioinformatics database and analysis tools through a mini-project.

BIOM541.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM541 Environmental Biotechnology
BIOM541.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM541
This course focuses on fundamentals of molecular biology and biotechnology for environmental applications. The major topics include activated sludge processes, stoichiometry, bioenergetics, anaerobic digestion, biological nitrogen and phosphorus removal, molecular microbiology tools, biofouling, antibiotic resistance, and biofuels.
Environmental Biotechnology (BIOM541) > Credit Hours : 3

Environmental Biotechnology (BIOM541) > Prerequisites
BIOM512 with a minimum grade D

BIOM516 with a minimum grade D
Environmental Biotechnology (BIOM541) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the fundamentals of environmental microbiology.

Demonstrate the new applications of plants and microorganisms in biotechnological applications, including bioremediation and biodegradation.

Explain the new technologies in waste water management and biofuel production.

Distinguish the use of specific bacterial enzymes to protect plants against environmental stresses.

BIOM544.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM544 Epigenetics & Cell Different
BIOM544.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM544
Epigenetic control genome expression in eukaryotes (plants, yeast and mammals). Histone code, histone variants, chromatin remodeling complexes, microRNA , DNA methylation, spatial and functional compartmentation of the genome in the nucleus
Epigenetics & Cell Different (BIOM544) > Credit Hours : 3

Epigenetics & Cell Different (BIOM544) > Prerequisites
BIOM508 with a minimum grade D
Epigenetics & Cell Different (BIOM544) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Criticize The Scientific Research In Epigenetic And Stem Cell Differentiation Described In Research Papers And Effectively Communicate And Discuss Data

Distinguish The Different Types Of Stem Cells, How They Are Derived And The Extent Of Their Plasticity And Understand How Epigenetic Mechanisms Regulate The Potentiality And Differentiation Of Stem Cells.

Compare The Epigenetic Influences On Gene Expression And The Range Of Epigenetic Mechanisms Used By Several Eukaryotic Organisms

BIOM552.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM552 Molecular & Genetic Aspects of Plant Responses to Pathogens
BIOM552.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM552
This course discusses the aspects of the nature of disease resistance and response mechanisms in plants. Special emphasis is placed on emerging concepts and paradigms that underlie a wide variety of plant-pathogen interactions, and how the knowledge gained from these studies is being used to devise effective and environmentally safe strategies of plant protection. Topics include history, breeding, and genetics of disease resistance, physiology, biochemistry, and molecular genetics of disease resistance and response mechanisms and emerging concepts in this rapidly advancing area and its contribution to plant biotechnology.
Molecular & Genetic Aspects of Plant Responses to Pathogens (BIOM552) > Credit Hours : 3

Molecular & Genetic Aspects of Plant Responses to Pathogens (BIOM552) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze primary research papers (scientific presentation and writing Skills)

Translate biotechnology aimed at Improving crop plants for better adaptations to environment.

Understand how plants cope with biotic stress in their environments.

Understand the genetic, molecular and physiological mechanisms that underlie plant responses to the environment.

BIOM555.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM555 Biotechnology Applications in Forensic Science
BIOM555.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM555
This course is designed to give a student a thorough knowledge and understanding of modern biology, together with an insight into forensic science. The course provides a firm foundation in biochemistry, molecular biology, cell biology and human biology, together with an introduction to the role of the forensic scientist and the analytical investigations carried out in forensic laboratories.
Biotechnology Applications in Forensic Science (BIOM555) > Credit Hours : 3

Biotechnology Applications in Forensic Science (BIOM555) > Prerequisites
BIOM600 with a minimum grade D
Biotechnology Applications in Forensic Science (BIOM555) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply different molecular techniques in understanding basics of forensic science.

Assess the ethical and cultural guidelines of forensic science.

Collaborate with peers to introduce concepts of forensic science in a public setting.

Identify different applications of forensic science of environmental microbiology.

BIOM571.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM571 Seminar in Biotechnology & Molecular Biology
BIOM571.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM571
This course will be delivered through discussion of current research and development findings emphasizing the myriad of applications of the fields of Biotechnology and Molecular Biology. Seminars will be delivered by faculty members, guest speakers, visiting scientists and industry professionals.
Seminar in Biotechnology & Molecular Biology (BIOM571) > Credit Hours : 1

Seminar in Biotechnology & Molecular Biology (BIOM571) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate Current Research Of Selected Molecular And Biotechnological Techniques And Their Impact On Scientific Findings.

Demonstrate Strong Team Work, Written And Oral Presentation Skills.

Evaluate Methods And Results Within The Field Of Specialization Critically And Ethically.

BIOM600.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM600 Advanced Molecular Biology Techniques II
BIOM600.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM600
This course will present a variety of molecular biology techniques that are frequently used in the field of biotechnology. It focuses on how to apply these technologies to a specific research question. In addition to hand on experience in techniques such as real-time PCR, Westerns, cell analysis, sequencing, reporter gene analysis, cDNA synthesis and proteomic gel analysis; the students should be able to record and analyze scientific data, write scientific report and appreciate and design solution to scientific problems.
Advanced Molecular Biology Techniques II (BIOM600) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Molecular Biology Techniques II (BIOM600) > Prerequisites
BIOM516 with a minimum grade D
Advanced Molecular Biology Techniques II (BIOM600) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Conduct Several Molecular Based Methods Such As Dna/Rna/Protein Extraction, Pcr, Western Blotting, And Dna Sequencing And Understand The Purpose, Principle And Methodology Of Each

Record And Analyze Scientific Data, Write Scientific Report And Appreciate And Design Solution To Scientific Problems

Use Bioinformatics Tools Such As The Basic Local Alignment Search Tool (Blast) To Identify Sequences In Databases.

Use Dna Barcodes To Identify And Classify Living Organisms.

BIOM700.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM700 Laboratory Rotations
BIOM700.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM700
Ph.D. students are required to take a lab rotation-based course during their first year of graduate study. Typically, students will be required to rotate through three to 4 laboratories (minimum of 2 in exceptionally trained students), each of which lasts about three months. During each laboratory rotation, the student will be exposed to methods, equipment, and experimental procedures currently in use in a particular departmental research laboratory selected by the student and through arrangement with the professor in charge of that laboratory. At the end of each rotation, students will receive a written evaluation from by the rotation supervisor. These evaluations are then submitted to the program chair to become a part of the student's permanent file. It is important to note that these evaluation letters will be considered during the comprehensive examination evaluation.
Laboratory Rotations (BIOM700) > Credit Hours : 3

Laboratory Rotations (BIOM700) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Able to design and execute an original research project

Demonstrate independent scientific thinking.

Master of use cutting edge research tools in Molecular Biology and biotechnology.

Able to work as a part of a team.

BIOM720.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM720 Advanced Genetics
BIOM720.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM720
This course tackles advanced principles and recent findings in genetics including: cell, molecular and direct approaches to genetic analysis and genetic interactions; chromosomal organization and aberrations; transposable elements; mutations, paramutation and epigenetics; extranuclear inheritance; genetic manipulations; gene discovery; ESTs and global gene expression analysis, proteomics, metabolic profiling, comparative genomics and genome evolution.
Advanced Genetics (BIOM720) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Genetics (BIOM720) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognize knowledge and comprehension of core concepts, including cellular biology, biochemistry, genetics, molecular biology, and microbiology.

Describe laboratory techniques essential to genetics and biotechnology.

Analyze and evaluate original research literature and communicate using appropriate technology.

Define questions or problems and develop comprehensive solutions individually and/or collaboratively.

BIOM730.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM730 Molecular Basis of Diseases
BIOM730.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM730
The course provides the students with a fundamental understanding of the molecular mechanisms and pathways underlying various pathological conditions in humans and plants. Attention will be given to the molecular mechanisms and processes at the level of the cell and tissue characterizing and/or leading to the most important human diseases (cancer, diabetes, neurodegenerative diseases) and plant diseases. This includes the signaling pathways, cellular/subcellular changes, gene expression pattern, identification of mutations, and chromosome abnormalities and other genetic alterations as well as cytogenetics, preimplantation genetic diagnostics, prenatal molecular diagnosis. For plants, various other aspects of disease resistance and response mechanisms in plants may also be covered. Finally, recent advances in the therapeutic approaches and strategies will also be covered.
Molecular Basis of Diseases (BIOM730) > Credit Hours : 3

Molecular Basis of Diseases (BIOM730) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe how plants cope with biotic stress in their environments.

Translate scientific techniques employed for studying responses to the environment.

Identify molecular mechanisms of physiological and pathophysiological processes.

BIOM735.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM735 Applied Immunobiology
BIOM735.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM735
Students will be exposed to applied aspects of immunology. Students will be given concept of fundamental principles of immunology including hematopoiesis; tissues and cells of the immune system; complement, cytokines. Major Topics covered include: Innate and adaptive immunity, how immune system is coordinated to combat infections, actors, Important aspects of cell receptors, VDJ recombination and DNA repair structure of the antigenic receptors, superantigen, as well as variability of the antigenic receptors. Dysfunction and pathologies: Immune subversion by malignant tumors, immune subversion by viruses, inherited immune deficiency, control of autoimmunity.
Applied Immunobiology (BIOM735) > Credit Hours : 3

Applied Immunobiology (BIOM735) > Prerequisites
BIOM462 with a minimum grade D

BIOM793 with a minimum grade D
Applied Immunobiology (BIOM735) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Understand the complex cellular and molecular interrelationships between the various components of the immune system and their roles in health and disease.

Critically appraise and interpret data from various immunological studies, and communicate these to a research audience.

Develop skills to discuss and present the recent developments in key selected areas of applied immunobiology to both lay and specialist audiences.

Acquire up to date knowledge of current clinical approaches in Immunology field for the treatment of various diseases.

BIOM740.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM740 Molecular Physiology
BIOM740.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM740
This course will tackle signal transduction mechanisms used by membrane ion channels and receptors that detect the microenvironmental cues and transmit the signals to downstream effectors. Integrated molecular approach will be used so that the students gain a better and more fundamental understanding of the molecular signaling cascades employed under physiological conditions. Attention may be given to signaling in pathophysiology as well. Modern molecular/structural techniques (patch clamp, protein crystallization, molecular genetics, and expression cloning and protein purification) will be introduced along with each topic.
Molecular Physiology (BIOM740) > Credit Hours : 3

Molecular Physiology (BIOM740) > Prerequisites
BIOM462 with a minimum grade D

BIOM793 with a minimum grade D
Molecular Physiology (BIOM740) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

To address major principles of how the various physiological systems of the body function, both individually and as an integrated unit to achieve body homeostasis.

To address, at the molecular level, several signaling pathways starting from gene, to system, to the whole organism body in both normal physiologic resting and stimulated as well as diseased conditions.

To be able to discuss the recent literature focused at the molecular basis of human diseases as well as to study useful and related genetically engineered animal models.

BIOM745.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM745 Selected Topics in Biotechnology
BIOM745.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM745
Through student’s presentations, group discussion and assignments, selected biotechnological biological topics, such as immunotherapy, applications of CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing in human disease and plant/crop genome editing and microbial biotechnology will be explored. For each topics, the material will be presented in form of assignment, presentation and group discussion. In addition, ethical issues in animal and plant biotechnology will be discussed. The major goal for this course is for the PhD student to develop a research issues and ways to address them through adequate scientific methodologies.
Selected Topics in Biotechnology (BIOM745) > Credit Hours : 3

Selected Topics in Biotechnology (BIOM745) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Define core concepts, including cellular biology, biochemistry, genetics, molecular biology, and microbiology.

Analyze and evaluate original research literature related to different areas of advanced biotechnology.

Discuss and communicate using appropriate technology.

Describe advanced laboratory techniques essential to biotechnology.

Assess ethical principles regarding the use of biotechnology.

BIOM787.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM787 Developmental Biology
BIOM787.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM787
A survey of molecular and cellular mechanisms involved in growth and development of organisms is explored. Topics to be covered include fertilization and early cell lineage, body axis formation, gastrulation, neural induction and patterning, segmentation, and other aspects of pattern formation including organogenesis of branching organs, limb development and regeneration.
Developmental Biology (BIOM787) > Credit Hours : 3

Developmental Biology (BIOM787) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate a broad understanding of the key cellular and molecular mechanisms and signal transduction pathways that control key embryonic development process including, fertilization, implantation, cleavage, gastrulation and organogenesis.

Describe the most important mechanisms of cell–cell communication and cell-matrix (ECM) interaction in cell migration and morphogenesis during early development.

Consolidate and extend the knowledge about the difference between specification and determination in early development.

Describe the cortical rotation in the frog sets up the dorsal-ventral and anterior-posterior axes and understand the role of the Nieukoop center and the Spemann-Mangold organizer in development of the frog.

Identify the major molecular and morphological events related to limb formation of vertebrates during development

Demonstrate the ability to conduct literature-based research, to identify key knowledge and concepts in the field of developmental biology.

Demonstrate the ability to critically interpret and discuss modern developmental biology research using effective written and oral communication skills including the ability to retrieve relevant information from the literature and online resources

BIOM793.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM793 Advanced topics in Cellular and Molecular Biology: A literature review
BIOM793.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM793
Topics will be chosen by the instructors’ along with the registered students. The main aim of this course is to give a chance to students to analyze, present and discuss the most recent and significant findings, through research manuscripts, in the field of cellular and molecular biology. Topics might be subject to a yearly change. Such course is primarily intended to develop in the students their ability to use the literature review as the primary source of information, evaluating it critically, and integrating it in to a cohesive body of knowledge. The ability of the student to present and review work will be tested.
Advanced topics in Cellular and Molecular Biology: A literature review (BIOM793) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced topics in Cellular and Molecular Biology: A literature review (BIOM793) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Present published results in the most effective way

Utilize and search different databases to find relevant information

Analyze and discuss the presented results with his/her class.

Critically evaluate the selected literature.

Propose possible extension of his/her presented study.

Integrate the knowledge acquired from this course to his/her theses.

BIOM794.title: UAEU Catalog — BIOM794 Genomics
BIOM794.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BIOM794
This course primarily covers prokaryotic and eukaryotic genomes. Experimental strategies and analytical challenges of modern genomics research, theory and mechanics of data analysis are thoroughly discussed. Structural, functional, and comparative genomics are also explored.
Genomics (BIOM794) > Credit Hours : 3

Genomics (BIOM794) > Prerequisites
BIOM793 with a minimum grade D
Genomics (BIOM794) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the underlying principles, strategies and methodologies involved in genomics.

Evaluate the strengths and limitations of different methodologies and tools employed in the field.

Demonstrate the use of these methods for real-life problem-solving and hypothesis testing.

Distinguish between trait-based genetics and gene-based genomics.

BION210.title: UAEU Catalog — BION210 Animal Biology for Non-Majors
BION210.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BION210
This course aims at studying the biology and taxonomy of invertebrates and vertebrates of the animal kingdom. It includes the phyla: Porifera, Cnidaria, Platyhelminthes, Nematoda, Mollusca, Annelida, Arthropoda, Echinodermata and Chordata which includes lower chordates, fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals with specific examples from each group selected for a detailed study.
Animal Biology for Non-Majors (BION210) > Credit Hours : 3

Animal Biology for Non-Majors (BION210) > Prerequisites
BIOC100
Animal Biology for Non-Majors (BION210) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe how animals cells function

Differentiate different functions of animal cells.

Discuss the major homeostatic mechanism used by animals

Identify animal mechanisms to adapt to their surroundings.

BION215.title: UAEU Catalog — BION215 Plant Biology for Non-Majors
BION215.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BION215
This course aims at introducing plant classification and the morphological and anatomical characteristics of different plant parts. It includes kingdoms Monera, viruses, Protista, Fungi, Bryophytes, Pteridophytes, Conifers and flowering plants; cell structure and tissue types; morphology and anatomy of root, stem, and leaf and secondary growth of root and stem.
Plant Biology for Non-Majors (BION215) > Credit Hours : 3

Plant Biology for Non-Majors (BION215) > Prerequisites
BIOC100
Plant Biology for Non-Majors (BION215) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss the fundamentals of plant cells

Explain and list the criteria for prokaryotic and eukaryotic Cells

Integrate the relationship between plants’ structure and function and their habitats.

Recognize the importance of the diversity of life with emphasis on plants

BION225.title: UAEU Catalog — BION225 Practical Plant Biology for Non-Majors
BION225.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BION225
This practical course aims at developing a clear understanding of plant kingdom components such as prokaryotes, fungi, algae, bryophytes, pteridophytes, gymnosperms and flowering plants. It includes cell structure, function and diversity, morphological and anatomical structure of roots, stems and leaves.
Practical Plant Biology for Non-Majors (BION225) > Credit Hours : 1

Practical Plant Biology for Non-Majors (BION225) > Corequisites
BION215
Practical Plant Biology for Non-Majors (BION225) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Differentiate major groups of plants with their taxonomy, structures and adaptations in relation to the habitats.

Identify plant parts under different growth patterns.

State differences between different functions of plant parts.

Use various techniques to differentiate between plant cells.

BION230.title: UAEU Catalog — BION230 Microbiology for Non-Majors
BION230.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BION230
This course focuses on the examination of prokaryotic and eukaryotic cell structures, microbial nutrition, classifications of microbial growth, microbial metabolism, microbial regulation through physical and chemical agents, foundational principles of bacterial taxonomy, as well as an overview of the general characteristics of diverse microorganism groups, including bacteria, fungi, viruses, protozoa, and microalgae. This course includes a laboratory component of three hours per week.
Microbiology for Non-Majors (BION230) > Credit Hours : 3

Microbiology for Non-Majors (BION230) > Prerequisites
BIOC100 with a minimum grade D
Microbiology for Non-Majors (BION230) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Classify the various categories of microorganisms found in nature.

Examine the influence of microorganisms on human activities.

Assess variables influencing microbial growth, feeding, and metabolism.

Connect theoretical concepts with practical applied microbiology.

Conduct microbiological laboratory experiments, encompassing statistical analysis and interpretation of data.

BION270.title: UAEU Catalog — BION270 General Genetics for Non-Majors
BION270.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BION270
This course aims at developing a clear understanding of genetics. It includes Mendelian genetics, molecular basis of genetics, genetic variation, and mutations. The course also aims at introducing the application of genetics in various fields.
General Genetics for Non-Majors (BION270) > Credit Hours : 2

General Genetics for Non-Majors (BION270) > Prerequisites
BIOC100
General Genetics for Non-Majors (BION270) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the basic concept of genetic inheritance and variation.

Identify terminologies associated with genetics.

Interpret and solve genetics problems.

Perform tasks relating to reading and writing capabilities in genetics.

BION275.title: UAEU Catalog — BION275 Genetics Laboratory for Non-Majors
BION275.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=BION275
This course provides non-major students with an introduction to genetics. It focuses on observing patterns of heredity and understanding how genes influence visible traits. Students participate in laboratory activities such as studying cell division, fruit fly characteristics, blood group variation, and simple DNA experiments. The course maintains a practical approach with clear, concise discussions that connect genetics to everyday life.
Genetics Laboratory for Non-Majors (BION275) > Credit Hours : 1

Genetics Laboratory for Non-Majors (BION275) > Prerequisites
BIOC165 with a minimum grade D or BIOL114 with a minimum grade D
Genetics Laboratory for Non-Majors (BION275) > Corequisites
BIOC270 with a minimum grade D
Genetics Laboratory for Non-Majors (BION275) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the concept of heredity using accessible, real-world examples.

Demonstrate safe and organized work habits in the laboratory.

Recognize and identify patterns in traits using visual and numerical tools.

Relate genetics to real-world applications and issues.

Accurately record observations and summarize results.

FORS600.title: UAEU Catalog — FORS600 Fundamentals of Forensic Science
FORS600.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=FORS600
