The course will provide students with broad introductions to the fundamental concepts, techniques and processes used in the collection, processing, analysis and storage of forensic evidence and data. Students will also develop a rigorous approach to the acquisition of a broad knowledge base within forensic science. Students will employ a range of specialized skills; evaluate observed and acquired information using it to plan and develop investigative strategies and to determine solutions to a variety of unpredictable problems. This course will also focus on human tissue analysis, biological trace evidence, hair and fiber analysis, fingerprints and the ethical considerations involved when dealing with forensic evidence. In addition, students will develop an understanding of the basic laboratory skills including microscopy, undertaking appropriate anti-contamination procedures, note taking and report writing.
Fundamentals of Forensic Science (FORS600) > Credit Hours : 3

Fundamentals of Forensic Science (FORS600) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate competence in retrieving, analyzing, and documenting evidence within a laboratory environment to produce sound forensic laboratory reports.

Explain the foundational theoretical concepts of forensic science and their application in investigations.

Show how diatoms can be used in Forensic investigations.

Classify vegetation for the purposes of forensic work.

Identify and utilize appropriate standard techniques for the retrieval and analysis of evidence in alignment with ethical, legal, and scientific standards

Critically evaluate different biological procedures and methodologies used in forensic investigations.

FORS601.title: UAEU Catalog — FORS601 Forensic DNA Analysis
FORS601.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=FORS601
This course provides a scientific foundation for understanding DNA's role in forensic investigations. It covers the significance of genome polymorphism, natural variations in DNA sequences that distinguish individuals, and forensic genetic markers such as STRs and SNPs, essential for genetic profiling. Additionally, it highlights advancements in DNA analysis technologies, including PCR and next-generation sequencing. These tools empower modern forensic science to solve crimes, identify individuals, and analyze complex evidence with enhanced precision and accuracy.
Forensic DNA Analysis (FORS601) > Credit Hours : 3

Forensic DNA Analysis (FORS601) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze genomic markers to enhance their application in forensic investigations.

Explain the critical role of DNA in forensic science.

Perform next-generation sequencing experiments and interpret the resulting data effectively.

Evaluate genomic variations within the human population and apply them to improve profiling and forensic identification techniques.

FORS602.title: UAEU Catalog — FORS602 Forensic Chemistry and Toxicology
FORS602.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=FORS602
This Course develops a science-based, objective approach to evidence identification, examination, analysis, interpretation and presentation. It examines the application of forensic science and its limitations in investigations. It evaluates the scope, concepts, complementary nature of both physical evidence examination and analysis. This course will introduce the concepts, theories and principles used in forensic identification of biological evidence. The course will cover the characterization of blood and other body fluids including the determination of whether a stain is blood and if it is human blood. The techniques applied in forensic identification of blood and other body fluids will be covered. Additionally, the blood spatter pattern analysis will be introduced. The analysis of blood spatter patterns will be studied with an emphasis on determining the type of spatter and the direction and angle from which the spatter was made.
Forensic Chemistry and Toxicology (FORS602) > Credit Hours : 3

Forensic Chemistry and Toxicology (FORS602) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Predict and explain the structure-property relationships of selected trace evidence types. Locate and obtain information from blood and other biological evidence.

Assess the significance and characterization of a range of trace evidence types.

Evaluate the physical and chemical procedures and principles used for the enhancement of surface transfer marks.

Evaluate forensic firearm and ballistic examinations and the motion and directionality of blood spatter pattern.

Research, contextualize, implement, manage and reflect on a range of analytical procedures appropriate to trace evidence analysis.

Formulate and communicate the results of forensic investigations

FORS603.title: UAEU Catalog — FORS603 Crime Scene Investigation
FORS603.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=FORS603
This course examines the management, control, techniques methodology and recording of crime scene investigation, searching and examination. Documentation of evidence, chain of custody, mapping, photography, roles of various personnel, additional techniques available, and recovery techniques for fingerprints. This course will also focus on Casting techniques for tool marks and footprints, footwear comparison and cast identification. The course will emphasis on evidence collection, packaging, labeling and preservation. The students will also get extensive training as an expert witness and writing court worthy witness statements.
Crime Scene Investigation (FORS603) > Credit Hours : 3

Crime Scene Investigation (FORS603) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Select forensic techniques that are appropriate for a particular study or investigation.

Evaluate evidence from a forensic-based investigation

Construct a legal statement based on forensic evidence and demonstrate communication skills in a simulated courtroom scenario

Analyze critically the tools and approaches used to secure process and interpret crime scenes, and judge the strengths, limits and biases of current professional practice.

Assess the implications of cultural and social contexts in crime interpretation, investigation, prevention, prosecution, and punishment

Explain the objectives and aims of the criminal justice response to crime, the forensic processes, and the limitations and cultural origins of the forensic narrative.

Describe good practice in securing, processing, and interpreting crime scenes, acting with initiative and within professional guidelines.

FORS604.title: UAEU Catalog — FORS604 Forensic Biology
FORS604.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=FORS604
Forensic Biology is a comprehensive course designed to explore the application of biological sciences in forensic analysis. The course begins by introducing students to the role and scope of forensic biology, highlighting the critical importance of biological evidence in investigations. Students will examine the role of biological evidence in forensic investigations along with appropriate methods for evidence collection and handling. A central theme of the course will be the role of molecular biology in forensic analysis, which includes DNA extraction, analysis, polymorphisms, short tandem repeat profiling and next generation sequencing. Forensic serology and immunology will also be covered in this course focusing on the identification of blood, saliva and other biological fluids as well as antibody-antigen interaction with forensic applications. Students will also explore the role of microbiology and microbial communities in forensic evaluations. Emerging topics like forensic microbiomics, genetic geology will also be covered briefly. Theoretical understanding of the topic will be complemented with detailed case studies that demonstrates the real-world application of forensic biology.
Forensic Biology (FORS604) > Credit Hours : 3

Forensic Biology (FORS604) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the key skills expected of a forensic biologist

Determine procedures for handling samples and providing evidence from biological analysis

Determine techniques involved in the analysis of various types of forensic biological samples

Evaluate molecular biology techniques and its application to forensic sciences

FORS605.title: UAEU Catalog — FORS605 Forensic Analytical Chemistry and Instrumentation
FORS605.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=FORS605
Forensic chemistry involves the application of analytical chemistry to physical evidence in the practice of forensic science. This course is designed to introduce forensic chemistry that applies chemical principles, methods, and instrumentation in the analysis of physical evidence for forensics. In addition, the course may cover major topics that are most commonly applicable to the everyday functions of a crime laboratory professional. The combined lecture/lab course applies the principles of analytical chemistry and instrumental analysis to forensic chemistry. Students learn the principles of classical, electrochemical, spectrochemical, and chromatographic analysis. The laboratory component provides hands-on training. Topics include instrumentation, sample preparation, data analysis, and recent developments in analytical techniques.
Forensic Analytical Chemistry and Instrumentation (FORS605) > Credit Hours : 3

Forensic Analytical Chemistry and Instrumentation (FORS605) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate if a set of measurements or data is accurate and statistically significant;

Explain the principles of operation of selected modern analytical instrumentation and methods.

Choose a proper instrumental technique for a given analytical problem.

Design experiments using instruments and techniques in forensic analytical chemistry .

Judge the effectiveness of the techniques of some recent methods in selected application.

Retrieve and present information relevant to instrumental analysis from scientific literature.

FORS607.title: UAEU Catalog — FORS607 Application in Forensic Geosciences
FORS607.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=FORS607
The course will provide students with the most significant theories, techniques, and forensic geosciences applications. Forensic sedimentology, petrography, pedology and geophysics are some of the topics covered in the study units, as well as an introduction and overview of some of the fundamental geoscience principles and how these may be applied to policing and law enforcement. Furthermore, also included are some of the operational and ethical issues facing forensic geologists working at crime scenes. It describes physical principles, campaign procedures and processing, as well as interpretation techniques, while also highlighting new acquisition and data analysis procedures. A large section of the study unit is centered on the applications, from measurements to the interpretation of data. Further, the study unit aims to instruct student on how to design and offer guidance on selecting the best method for the problem at hand, and on selecting the best type of data acquisition and processing. Overall, it will give students a thorough understanding of relevant aspects of applied geosciences in the context of forensic sciences.
Application in Forensic Geosciences (FORS607) > Credit Hours : 3

Application in Forensic Geosciences (FORS607) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the application of geologic/geochemical evidence in forensic science including soils, rocks, fossils, spores and pollen, and the geochemistry of cosmetics.

Demonstrate knowledge of environmental pollutants and in identifying their sources.

Critically evaluate different geophysical procedures for forensic investigations.

Contribute to the knowledge relevant legislation in relation to collection of evidence

Read and draft reports drafted by others on different case studies

FORS610.title: UAEU Catalog — FORS610 Digital Forensics
FORS610.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=FORS610
This course presents an overview of the principles and practices of digital investigation. The students will be aware of different types of digital evidence, how to seize electronics devices on crime scene and the way to secure mobile devices from electromagnetic radiations. Students will also learn how to acquire digital evidence from different types of evidence like different types of HDDs, USBs, cloud, etc. Different techniques to make copies off evidence without modifying the original data will also be studied. The students will learn about write blockers, data acquisition, analysis and investigation. Students will learn different techniques and procedures that enable them to perform digital investigation. The course focuses mainly on the phases of digital investigation such as preservation, acquisition, analysis and reporting. The objective of this class also prepares the students to conduct full digital investigation and understand the basics of investigation by implementing theoretical and practical exercises. Upon the completion of the course, the students can apply full digital forensic investigation process from stage one of preserving the evidence tell the presentation of the report in front of the court.
Digital Forensics (FORS610) > Credit Hours : 3

Digital Forensics (FORS610) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply Forensic techniques and tools used to acquire digital evidence.

Develop proficiency in the case management process.

Implement various types of forensic tools to perform rudimentary investigations

Discover the evidences related to digital media devices

Implement the knowledge of digital forensics in different case studies.

FORS636.title: UAEU Catalog — FORS636 Graduate Seminar
FORS636.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=FORS636
This module aims to provide an integrative view of forensic science and its underlying disciplines. Students will be expected to peruse relevant scientific literature and case reports related to forensics and provide a summarised discourse. It will sharpen a student’s skills to both assimilate information from written literature and to communicate it effectively to an audience.
Graduate Seminar (FORS636) > Credit Hours : 1

Graduate Seminar (FORS636) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate critically current scientific research and their application in the field of forensic science

Develop and communicate scientific literature in written and oral form both individually and in teams

GESU121.title: UAEU Catalog — GESU121 Sustainability
GESU121.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2902.shtml?id=GESU121
Today, the world we live in is facing challenges from numerous facets: food scarcity, energy demands, climate change and a population that is projected to increase. This course, therefore, focuses on sustainability as one of the dominant global concerns from an environmental, economic and social point of view. It is an urgent issue that is facing the world not only in our current century, but beyond. The course will introduce the major components of sustainability: definition, monitoring and assessment. Furthermore, the course will assist students in developing the core concepts of sustainable management from local to regional to global view points. Finally, case studies from the UAE, the region and the world will be used as real-world examples for students’ reports and presentations.
Sustainability (GESU121) > Credit Hours : 3

Sustainability (GESU121) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the basics of sustainability as it relates to the issues, processes and practices.

Recognize the importance of sustainable use of the natural resources globally regionally and locally.

Understand the ethical and social issues related to sustainable use of natural resources.

Translate the understanding of the sustainability challenges into solutions both in writing and verbally.

CHME300.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME300 Introduction to Chemical Engineering
CHME300.text:
This course introduces the students to the chemical engineering profession and basic calculations in mass and energy balance; phase equilibria; and process flow sheeting. It includes applications on reactive and non-reactive chemical processes. Computer programs are used to implement these topics.
Introduction to Chemical Engineering (CHME300) > Credit Hours : 3

Introduction to Chemical Engineering (CHME300) > Prerequisites
CHEM111 with a minimum grade D

CHEM175 with a minimum grade D
Introduction to Chemical Engineering (CHME300) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply basic principle of chemical engineering calculations

Perform a degree-of-freedom analysis for the overall system and each possible subsystem

Solve material and energy balance equations for non-reactive systems

Solve material and energy balance equations for reactive systems

Develop effective communication skills via group works

Identify current topics in chemical engineering

CHME320.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME320 Aspen Hysys Lab
CHME320.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME320
This laboratory course introduces students to the practical use of Aspen HYSYS for chemical engineering process simulation. Students will gain hands-on experience in modeling, simulating, and analyzing steady-state chemical processes and common unit operations. The course develops skills in selecting thermodynamic models, building process flow diagrams, performing material and energy balances, and evaluating process performance. Through guided exercises and case studies, students will apply Aspen HYSYS to process design, optimization, and integration tasks relevant to industrial chemical and petrochemical applications.
Aspen Hysys Lab (CHME320) > Credit Hours : 1

Aspen Hysys Lab (CHME320) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co CHME300 with a minimum grade D
Aspen Hysys Lab (CHME320) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Simulate chemical engineering processes using Aspen HYSYS

Evaluate process performance and operating conditions

Function effectively in a team to complete a simulation-based design project

CHME322.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME322 Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics
CHME322.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME322
Review of the basic laws in thermodynamics. Theory and applications of solution thermodynamics, vapor-liquid and liquid-liquid equilibrium for ideal and non-ideal systems, and chemical reaction equilibrium.
Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics (CHME322) > Credit Hours : 3

Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics (CHME322) > Prerequisites
GENG220 with a minimum grade D
Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics (CHME322) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Relate the P-V-T properties of real gases at high pressure and liquids using EOS [1]

Calculate changes in U, H, and S for ideal and non-ideal gases [1]

Apply the criteria for chemical reaction equilibria and calculate compositions at equilibrium for single or multiple reactions in a single or multiple phase [1]

Solve phase equilibrium problems for pure substances and mixtures utilizing chemical potential and fugacity [1]

Present (P-T, P-x-y, T-x-y and x-y) curves for binary mixtures and utilize Raoult’s law [1]

Calculate the bubble point and dew point and perform flash calculations. [1]

Explain the azeotrope phenomenon and determine ways of overcoming azeotrope [1]

CHME330.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME330 Chemical Engineering Fluid Mechanics
CHME330.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME330
Principles of fluid mechanics and physical separation processes are introduced. Topics include flow and pressure measurement for Newtonian and non-Newtonian fluids, dimensional analysis and pressure drop, and flow through porous media and packed beds. Applications to filtration, fluidization, sedimentation, and biosystems.
Chemical Engineering Fluid Mechanics (CHME330) > Credit Hours : 3

Chemical Engineering Fluid Mechanics (CHME330) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co PETE290 with a minimum grade D or Pre/Co CHME300 with a minimum grade D

PHYS105 with a minimum grade D
PHYS135 with a minimum grade D)
Chemical Engineering Fluid Mechanics (CHME330) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Distinguish between different types of fluids and flow behaviours

Calculate basic properties of fluids such as viscosity.

Apply principles of energy, momentum and mass balances to solve engineering problems involving fluid flow

Calculate fluid friction and pressure drop in fluid flow and porous media systems.

Design common fluid flow devices with emphasis on pumps and compressors.

Solve fluid mechanics problems collectively.

CHME357.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME357 Fundamentals of Biochemical Engineering
CHME357.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME357
The course covers basic aspects of biochemical engineering and bioprocesses. Topics covered include: Microbial structure, growth kinetics and product formation in cell cultures. Applied enzyme catalysis and kinetics of enzymatic reactions, continuous fermentation, agitation, mass transfer, and design and analysis of bioreactors
Fundamentals of Biochemical Engineering (CHME357) > Credit Hours : 3

Fundamentals of Biochemical Engineering (CHME357) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co CHEM282 with a minimum grade D
Fundamentals of Biochemical Engineering (CHME357) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply material and energy balance on biochemical problems [PLO1]

Derive kinetic equations for various types of enzyme reactions [PLO1, PLO6]

Determine microbial growth kinetics and stoichiometry [PLO1, PLO6]

Design enzymatic bioreactor [PLO1, PLO2]

Analyze fermentation systems and design fermenters [PLO1, PLO2]

CHME360.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME360 Numerical Methods in Chemical Engineering
CHME360.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME360
The objective of this course is to learn basic computational techniques for solving a variety of mathematical problems that cannot be solved analytically, and to improve students' confidence in using computational tools to solve problems in chemical engineering. The methods will be applied to many problems in chemical engineering.
Numerical Methods in Chemical Engineering (CHME360) > Credit Hours : 2

Numerical Methods in Chemical Engineering (CHME360) > Prerequisites
MATH140 with a minimum grade D
Numerical Methods in Chemical Engineering (CHME360) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Solve mathematical problems with a computer [PLO1]

Write structured code using relevant software such as MATLAB [PLO1]

Solve sets of linear and nonlinear equations using numerical methods [PLO1]

Apply explicit and implicit numerical methods [PLO1]

Solve boundary value problems using shooting and finite difference methods as a teamwork [PLO 1,5]

CHME390.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME390 Engineering and Strength of Materials
CHME390.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME390
This course introduces the students to the concepts and fundamentals of engineering and strength of materials. Topics covered include structure and imperfection of solid material, types of materials, mechanical properties and deformation, failures, corrosion, vector force and moment, objects in equilibrium, centroids and center of mass, moments of inertia, and internal forces and moments, and torsion
Engineering and Strength of Materials (CHME390) > Credit Hours : 3

Engineering and Strength of Materials (CHME390) > Prerequisites
CHEM111 with a minimum grade D
Engineering and Strength of Materials (CHME390) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Differentiate between crystalline and non-crystalline materials and their defects, applications involving metals, ceramics, polymers and composite materials and their manufacturing method [1]

Identify the different types of material tests such as stress-strain, fatigue, and creep and to derive mechanical properties from different types of material testing [2]

Apply material mechanics to chemical and petroleum engineering calculations [1]

Design mechanical component based on strength of material [6]

Formulate and solve engineering problems related to engineering and strength of materials [1]

CHME411.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME411 Reactor Design
CHME411.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME411
This course covers kinetics of homogeneous and heterogeneous reactions, design of isothermal reactors such as Batch, CSTR and PFR, introduction to bioreactors, catalysis and catalytic reactions; non-isothermal reactor design; multiple reactions.
Reactor Design (CHME411) > Credit Hours : 3

Reactor Design (CHME411) > Corequisites
CHEM351 with a minimum grade D
Reactor Design (CHME411) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Solve the reactor design equations without catalyst decay for isothermal and without pressure drop [1].

Design reactor including the effect of pressure [1,2]

Apply the effect of temperature on the reactor design equations [1]

Design catalytic reactor systems [1,2]

Use the available software packages for design of the complex reactor problems. [1,2]

CHME413.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME413 Heat Transfer
CHME413.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME413
This course covers the three modes of heat transfer: conduction, convection, radiation, and their applications in steady- and unsteady-state heat transfer. Integrated analogy between fluid and heat transfer operations. Condensation, boiling, and evaporation. Energy applications in biosystems. Heat exchangers: types, design, and rating.
Heat Transfer (CHME413) > Credit Hours : 3

Heat Transfer (CHME413) > Prerequisites
CHME330 with a minimum grade D
Heat Transfer (CHME413) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain various modes of heat transfer. [1]

Analyse conduction in various coordinates and in composite systems [1,2]

Determine free and forced convection heat transfer coefficient [1]

Design heat exchangers of various types [1,2,3,5]

CHME415.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME415 Fluid Mechanics and Heat Transfer lab
CHME415.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME415
This is an experimentation course introducing concepts of experimentation data analysis to emphasize the relationship between predictive theories and actual experimental results and to enhance oral and written communication skills. A number of experiments are selected to cover topics related to fluid mechanics and heat transfer, such as fluid friction, filtration, fixed and fluidized bed, centrifugal pump, concentric tube heat exchanger, radiation etc.
Fluid Mechanics and Heat Transfer lab (CHME415) > Credit Hours : 1

Fluid Mechanics and Heat Transfer lab (CHME415) > Prerequisites
GENG215 with a minimum grade D
Fluid Mechanics and Heat Transfer lab (CHME415) > Corequisites
CHME413 with a minimum grade D
Fluid Mechanics and Heat Transfer lab (CHME415) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze and interpret experimental data

Communicate effectively orally and in writing

CHME417.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME417 Mass Transfer and Reactor Design Lab
CHME417.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME417
This is an experimentation course introducing concepts of experimentation data analysis to emphasize the relationship between predictive theories and actual experimental results and to enhance oral and written communication skills. A number of experiments are selected to cover topics related to mass transfer and reactor design, such as molecular diffusion, mass transfer in wetted wall column, batch reactor, CSTR, plug flow reactor, etc.
Mass Transfer and Reactor Design Lab (CHME417) > Credit Hours : 1

Mass Transfer and Reactor Design Lab (CHME417) > Corequisites
CHME411 with a minimum grade D
Mass Transfer and Reactor Design Lab (CHME417) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Design and conduct experiments

Communicate in teams to write laboratory reports

CHME421.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME421 Mass Transfer
CHME421.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME421
This course covers molecular and convective steady-state and unsteady-state mass transfer. Integrated analogy between fluid, heat, and mass transfer operations. Interfacial mass transfer, continuous and stage-wise contact operations, with applications in absorption and distillation.
Mass Transfer (CHME421) > Credit Hours : 3

Mass Transfer (CHME421) > Prerequisites
CHME330 with a minimum grade D
Mass Transfer (CHME421) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify mass transfer mechanisms by molecular diffusion and convection.

Estimate the diffusion coefficient in gas, liquid and solid phases at specified conditions using standard models and correlations.

Identify the different boundary conditions involved in modeling a mass transfer process.

Solve steady-state and unsteady-state mass transfer problems.

Compute convective mass transfer coefficients for specified values of the Reynolds and Schmidt number.

CHME455.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME455 Data Science and AI for Chemical Engineers
CHME455.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME455
This course introduces fundamental data science and introductory artificial intelligence (AI) concepts with a focus on chemical engineering applications. Students develop practical skills in analyzing, visualizing, and modeling process data using appropriate computational tools. The course covers regression techniques, basic machine learning methods, and interpretation of data-driven models for engineering decision-making. Emphasis is placed on applying AI and data analytics to real chemical engineering problems such as process optimization, predictive maintenance, and smart manufacturing. The course prioritizes practical understanding and application over advanced mathematical theory.
Data Science and AI for Chemical Engineers (CHME455) > Credit Hours : 3

Data Science and AI for Chemical Engineers (CHME455) > Prerequisites
GENG230 with a minimum grade D

STAT210 with a minimum grade D
Data Science and AI for Chemical Engineers (CHME455) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Interpret data-driven model results for engineering decision-making

Perform data preprocessing and visualization for process data

Analyze chemical engineering datasets using statistical methods

Develop basic regression and classification models for process prediction

Explain fundamental artificial intelligence concepts for chemical engineering applications

CHME485.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME485 Internship I
CHME485.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME485
Students spend 8 weeks on a full-time basis in an engineering or consulting office in the UAE or abroad to earn practical skills. This course aims at offering career exploration opportunities for students.
Internship I (CHME485) > Credit Hours : 1

Internship I (CHME485) > Prerequisites
MATH135 with a minimum grade D or MATH110 with a minimum grade D

STAT210 with a minimum grade D

MATH275 with a minimum grade D

MATH140 with a minimum grade D

PHYS105 with a minimum grade D

PHYS135 with a minimum grade D

GENG215 with a minimum grade D

GENG220 with a minimum grade D

GENG230 with a minimum grade D

CHEM111 with a minimum grade D

CHEM175 with a minimum grade D

CHME300 with a minimum grade D

CHME330 with a minimum grade D
Internship I (CHME485) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Function effectively in multi-disciplinary teams and individually to achieve the planned tasks and goals.

Develop communication skills through oral and written presentations.

Evaluate different engineering situations and judgments based on ethical codes and professional responsibilities.

CHME490.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME490 Internship II
CHME490.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME490
Students spend 8 weeks on a full-time basis in an engineering or consulting office in the UAE or abroad to earn practical skills. This course aims at offering career exploration opportunities for students as well as opportunities to correlate their academic preparation to the reality of conducting professional practice, to interact effectively with others in practice, to develop professional skills and communicate effectively in the workplace and to gain true practical experience that is necessary for their future practice as engineers in their respective discipline after graduation.
Internship II (CHME490) > Credit Hours : 1

Internship II (CHME490) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co CHME485 with a minimum grade P

PHYS110 with a minimum grade D

PHYS140 with a minimum grade D

GENG315 with a minimum grade D

CHME421 with a minimum grade D

CHME413 with a minimum grade D
Internship II (CHME490) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Function effectively in multi-disciplinary teams and individually to achieve the planned tasks and goals.

Develop communication skills through oral and written presentations

Evaluate different engineering situations and judgments based on ethical codes and professional responsibilities

Propose ideas/solutions for real-life problems based on the learned knowledge.

CHME506.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME506 Process Modeling & Simulation
CHME506.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME506
This course aims at introducing principles of process modeling using general-purpose software packages to solve model equations of various unit operations. Topics covered include multi-component phase equilibria, fluid flow reaction kinetics and separation processes. Applications are performed using MATLAB/SIMULINK and polymath in solving model equations.
Process Modeling & Simulation (CHME506) > Credit Hours : 3

Process Modeling & Simulation (CHME506) > Prerequisites
MATH275 with a minimum grade D
Process Modeling & Simulation (CHME506) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop mathematical models to represent physical lumped and distributed systems.

Apply the various numerical computational techniques; Euler method, Rung Kutta.

Implement the computational technique in the form of a computer program

Compute numerically initial and boundary value problems

Solve mathematical models of lumped and distributed system using MATLAB/SIMULINK software package

CHME508.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME508 Process Control
CHME508.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME508
This course aims at introducing process dynamics and principles of control for chemical processes. Topics covered include block diagrams, Laplace transforms, transient response of feed-back systems, stability analysis, gain and phase margins.
Process Control (CHME508) > Credit Hours : 3

Process Control (CHME508) > Prerequisites
MATH275 with a minimum grade D
Process Control (CHME508) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop mathematical models of chemical processes for control purposes. [1,2]

Analyse the dynamic behaviour of First and Second order systems [1]

Use computer software packages for the simulation and control of chemical processes. [1,2]

Design of feedback/feedforward/cascade control systems. [1,2]

Examine the stability of feedback systems [1]

CHME510.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME510 Process and Plant Design
CHME510.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME510
This course exposes the student to design strategies and interrelationships between process and design variables. There is an emphasis on cost analysis, environment, and rational use of energy and raw materials. Design of processes related to the petroleum and petrochemical industries.
Process and Plant Design (CHME510) > Credit Hours : 3

Process and Plant Design (CHME510) > Prerequisites
CHME421 with a minimum grade D
Process and Plant Design (CHME510) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze a chemical process in terms of the logic behind selecting its operating conditions and conditions of particular concern.

Design the leading equipment involved in a chemical process using the short-cut techniques

Estimate the capital and manufacturing cost of a chemical process as a prerequisite to judging its economic profitability.

CHME517.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME517 Mass Transfer Operations
CHME517.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME517
This course starts with a review of phase equilibria, and then covers binary and multi-component distillation, leaching, and liquid-liquid extraction, with applications in design of a multi-column distillation process.
Mass Transfer Operations (CHME517) > Credit Hours : 3

Mass Transfer Operations (CHME517) > Prerequisites
CHME421 with a minimum grade D
Mass Transfer Operations (CHME517) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the suitability of different types of separation techniques.

Formulate material and energy balances over separation equipment (i.e., distillation tower, absorption/stripping towers, leaching process, liquid-liquid extraction cascades).

Develop operating line, feed line and equilibrium equations to determine NTP & NAP.

Illustrate separation problems graphically.

Solve governing equations to find the design specifications for a separation problem (i.e. multicomponent distillation process).

Optimize separation processes for solvent flow rate and reflux ratio.

CHME528.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME528 Unit Operation and Process Control Lab
CHME528.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME528
This is an experimentation course introducing concepts of experimentation data analysis to emphasize the relationship between predictive theories and actual experimental results and to enhance oral and written communication skills. A number of experiments are selected to cover topics related to unit operations, separation processes and process control, such as drying, cooling tower, gas absorption, distillation, liquid-liquid extraction, level control, dynamics of step input to CSTR in Series, etc.
Unit Operation and Process Control Lab (CHME528) > Credit Hours : 1

Unit Operation and Process Control Lab (CHME528) > Corequisites
CHME508 with a minimum grade D
Unit Operation and Process Control Lab (CHME528) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze and interpret experimental data.

Communicate effectively orally and in writing

CHME533.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME533 Water Desalination
CHME533.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME533
This course aims at studying industrial desalination processes. Topics covered include global and local water resources, water quality and analysis, technical and economic analysis of major desalination processes such as multi-stage flash, reverse osmosis, multiple-effect distillation and electrodialysis.
Water Desalination (CHME533) > Credit Hours : 3

Water Desalination (CHME533) > Prerequisites
CHME413 with a minimum grade D
Water Desalination (CHME533) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognize water shortage problem and importance of desalination technologies

Demonstrate chemistry and analysis of saline water

Explain problems associated with scale formation and its preventive tools

Evaluate mathematically various desalination operations currently used worldwide

Examine economic consideration in reverse osmosis

CHME541.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME541 Industrial & Wastewater Treatment
CHME541.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME541
Definitions, characteristics, survey and monitoring of industrial wastewater. Legislation, guidelines, and standards. Treatment processes: volume and strength reduction, neutralization and equalization, removal of suspended and colloidal solids, removal of dissolved organics. Combined treatment of industrial and domestic wastewaters. Treatment economics. New trends in treatment processes.
Industrial & Wastewater Treatment (CHME541) > Credit Hours : 3

Industrial & Wastewater Treatment (CHME541) > Prerequisites
CHEM111 with a minimum grade D
Industrial & Wastewater Treatment (CHME541) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the characteristics of industrial wastewater

Classify various processes in wastewater treatments

Develop models for industrial wastewater treatment operations

Identify current topics in industrial wastewater treatment.

CHME542.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME542 Corrosion
CHME542.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME542
This course introduces electrochemical principles and their application to corrosion. Topics covered include different corrosion mechanisms, corrosion inhibition and different methods for electrochemical metal protection. Case studies from oil and petroleum refining industries are also included.
Corrosion (CHME542) > Credit Hours : 3

Corrosion (CHME542) > Prerequisites
CHME390 with a minimum grade D
Corrosion (CHME542) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify various types of corrosion. [1]

Describe corrosion control methods. [1]

Describe corrosion characteristics of metals, alloys, plastics, and nonmetallic. [1]

Demonstrate the ability to select treatments for various corrosion problems. [1,2]

Identify various metals. [1,2]

Demonstrate knowledge of cathodic protection terminology and identify cathodic protection equipment. [1,4]

Practice effectively in groups/teams by engaging in independent learning to develop effective oral, written, and interpersonal communication skills. [3,5,7]

CHME544.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME544 Renewable Energy Sources
CHME544.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME544
The objective of this course is to assess current and potential future energy systems, including resources, extraction, conversion, and end-use, with emphasis on meeting regional and global energy needs. Different renewable and conventional energy technologies will be presented, including bio-fuels, fuel cells, solar energy, wind energy and nuclear energy. Topics include basic principles of reactor design and operation at commercial nuclear electrical generating facilities, including an examination of nuclear waste issues. The photovoltaic solar energy systems will be presented, focusing on the behavior and design of "stand-alone" photovoltaic systems.
Renewable Energy Sources (CHME544) > Credit Hours : 3

Renewable Energy Sources (CHME544) > Prerequisites
PHYS105 with a minimum grade D
Renewable Energy Sources (CHME544) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify various non-renewable and renewable energy sources

Develop fundamental background required for examining various energy sources

Illustrate the importance of renewable energy sources

Illustrate mathematical principles behind important renewable energy sources

Practice effectively in groups/teams by engaging in independent learning to develop effective oral, written, and interpersonal communication skills.

CHME555.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME555 Molecular Modeling and Simulation
CHME555.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME555
This course introduces the fundamental principles and practical techniques of molecular modeling and simulation for chemical engineering applications. Students gain knowledge of molecular level interactions and their influence on material properties and process behavior. The course develops skills in applying computational methods such as Molecular Dynamics (MD) and Monte Carlo (MC) simulations to predict structural, thermodynamic, and transport properties. Through theory supported hands on exercises using modern simulation software, students analyze simple fluids, polymers, and nanoporous materials. Emphasis is placed on linking molecular scale insights to macroscopic design, analysis, and decision making in chemical engineering practice.
Molecular Modeling and Simulation (CHME555) > Credit Hours : 3

Molecular Modeling and Simulation (CHME555) > Prerequisites
CHME360 with a minimum grade D
Molecular Modeling and Simulation (CHME555) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain how molecular interactions determine material properties.

Set up molecular systems with appropriate force fields and boundary conditions.

Perform Molecular Dynamics and Monte Carlo simulations to compute material properties.

Analyze simulation data to obtain structural and transport properties.

Relate molecular predictions to macroscopic engineering behavior.

Communicate simulation results using reproducible and ethical practices.

CHME560.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME560 Pharmaceutical Process Engineering
CHME560.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME560
This course introduces the principles and practice of pharmaceutical product and process development from a chemical engineering perspective. Students gain knowledge of active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) manufacturing, pharmaceutical unit operations, and formulation of major dosage forms. The course develops skills in applying engineering concepts to drug product design, process selection, and scale‑up. Emphasis is placed on modern pharmaceutical manufacturing approaches, including controlled drug delivery systems, continuous manufacturing, and emerging technologies. Through applied examples and case studies, students learn how chemical engineering principles are used to design, optimize, and improve pharmaceutical products and processes in industrial practice.
Pharmaceutical Process Engineering (CHME560) > Credit Hours : 3

Pharmaceutical Process Engineering (CHME560) > Prerequisites
CHME421 with a minimum grade D
Pharmaceutical Process Engineering (CHME560) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the structure of the pharmaceutical industry and the role of chemical engineers.

Apply transport and mechanical operations principles to pharmaceutical unit operations.

Perform basic design and performance calculations for pharmaceutical operations.

Relate drug and excipient properties to formulation and process choices.

Develop conceptual process flowsheets for dosage forms and identify critical parameters.

CHME561.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME561 Natural Gas Processing
CHME561.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME561
This course introduces different techniques for processing natural gas. Topics include properties and behavior of natural gas using equations of state, hydrate formation, field treatment including dehydration, sour gas sweetening, sulfur recovery, and liquefaction. Design of main processing equipment will be studied.
Natural Gas Processing (CHME561) > Credit Hours : 3

Natural Gas Processing (CHME561) > Prerequisites
CHME322 with a minimum grade D
Natural Gas Processing (CHME561) > Corequisites
CHME421 with a minimum grade D
Natural Gas Processing (CHME561) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply thermodynamic knowledge to understand phase behaviour and calculations of natural gas properties

Design system components such as dehydration and sweetening of natural gas

Survey recent issues related to the natural gas processing via internet and periodical journals

Practice engineering techniques, including computer-based tools, in solving engineering problems, such as Hysys

CHME562.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME562 Petroleum Refining Engineering
CHME562.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME562
This course aims at introducing different techniques for petroleum refining. Topics include refinery feed stocks and products, field processes, crude distillation, coking and thermal processes, catalytic reforming and cracking, hydro-processing, and solvent treating processes. Students will do a case study of a typical refinery.
Petroleum Refining Engineering (CHME562) > Credit Hours : 3

Petroleum Refining Engineering (CHME562) > Prerequisites
CHME300 with a minimum grade D

CHEM282 with a minimum grade D
Petroleum Refining Engineering (CHME562) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the characteristic properties of crude oils [1,2]

Identify the specifications of various petroleum products and their utilizations [1]

Classify the various refinery processes with their principle of operation, process flow diagram and operating conditions, and how they are interrelated [1,2]

Evaluate problems pertaining to crude oil refinery engineering [1, 4]

CHME564.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME564 Polymer Engineering
CHME564.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME564
Introduction to polymer science and synthesis: condensation polymerization, addition polymerization, bulk polymerization, solution polymerization, suspension polymerization, and emulsion polymerization. Industrial polymer processing: extrusion, injection molding, blow molding, calendaring, sheet forming and fiber spinning. Review of the design and manufacture of polymer products, with particular emphasis on material selection and processing technology. Engineering properties of elastomers, thermoplastics, blends and specialty polymers in terms of processing characteristics and end-use performance.
Polymer Engineering (CHME564) > Credit Hours : 3

Polymer Engineering (CHME564) > Prerequisites
CHME330 with a minimum grade D
Polymer Engineering (CHME564) > Corequisites
CHME390 with a minimum grade D
Polymer Engineering (CHME564) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Define various terminologies associated with polymer science and engineering

Illustrate polymerization mechanisms and processes, and processing of polymers for product manufacturing

Demonstrate fundamental understanding of molecular weight distribution, and the relationships between chemical structure and physical properties of polymers

Evaluate important engineering concepts in polymer science such as dynamic mechanical and rheological properties

Work and interact effectively in groups/teams by engaging in independent learning to develop effective oral, written, and interpersonal communication skills.

CHME565.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME565 Hydrogen Technology
CHME565.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME565
This course introduces the fundamental principles of hydrogen technology with an engineering focus on sustainable energy systems. Students develop knowledge of hydrogen production methods, storage technologies, and integration with renewable energy sources. The course builds skills in understanding electrolysis, electrochemical energy conversion, and the operation of batteries and fuel cells as key hydrogen applications. Emphasis is placed on evaluating the technical and economic performance of hydrogen systems. Students also gain practical insights into applying artificial intelligence and data‑driven methods for system optimization, performance prediction, and techno‑economic analysis of hydrogen energy technologies.
Hydrogen Technology (CHME565) > Credit Hours : 3

Hydrogen Technology (CHME565) > Prerequisites
GENG220 with a minimum grade D
Hydrogen Technology (CHME565) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the fundamentals of hydrogen technologies.

Analyze hydrogen technologies for efficiency and sustainability.

Design hydrogen energy systems with fuel cells and AI tools.

Evaluate the economic feasibility of hydrogen technologies.

Assess blue hydrogen’s role in energy transition and decarbonization.

Present technical information in written and oral formats.

CHME585.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME585 Design and Critical Thinking in Chemical Engineering
CHME585.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME585
This course concentrates on the rigors of communication, design, and critical thinking in an engineering context including problem identification, feasibility study of alternative solutions, preliminary design, technical writing, teamwork, and formal presentations. A team of students will apply the knowledge gained throughout their study and from industrial training to an engineering design project, emphasizing critical thinking, creativity, and originality. The selected alternatives will be the foundation of the capstone design project. A final report is required.
Design and Critical Thinking in Chemical Engineering (CHME585) > Credit Hours : 3

Design and Critical Thinking in Chemical Engineering (CHME585) > Prerequisites
MATH110 with a minimum grade D or MATH135 with a minimum grade D

PHYS110 with a minimum grade D

PHYS140 with a minimum grade D

MATH140 with a minimum grade D

MATH275 with a minimum grade D

GENG215 with a minimum grade D

GENG230 with a minimum grade D

GENG220 with a minimum grade D

GENG315 with a minimum grade D

STAT210 with a minimum grade D
Design and Critical Thinking in Chemical Engineering (CHME585) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the relevant theoretical background of a contemporary engineering problem. [PLO1]

Apply the fundamentals of engineering-design and critical thinking, including the assessment and evaluation of alternative engineering solutions. [PLO2]

Develop and conduct appropriate experimentation, modeling, simulation, and/or data analysis using engineering tools. [PLO6]

Communicate effectively through oral and written presentations. [PLO3]

Outline the principles of engineering ethics, and social and environmental responsibilities. [PLO4]

Recognize the need for ongoing additional knowledge, and the potential of integration and/or application of this knowledge effectively. [PLO7]

Develop leadership skills and project management techniques to independently and/or collaboratively handle complex professional tasks in a team-work context. [PLO5]

CHME590.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME590 Capstone Engineering Design Project
CHME590.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME590
This course builds on the outcomes of CHME 585 course to perform detailed design and cost estimate of the selected alternative solutions to a well-defined engineering problem. Student teams are expected to apply knowledge gained throughout their studies to an engineering design project, emphasizing creativity and originality. A final report is required.
Capstone Engineering Design Project (CHME590) > Credit Hours : 3

Capstone Engineering Design Project (CHME590) > Prerequisites
CHME585 with a minimum grade D
Capstone Engineering Design Project (CHME590) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the theoretical background of a contemporary engineering problem. [PLO1]

Apply the fundamentals of engineering-design, including the assessment and evaluation of alternative engineering solutions. [PLO2]

Develop and conduct appropriate experimentation, modelling, simulation, and/or data analysis using modern engineering tools. [PLO6]

Communicate effectively through oral and written presentations. [PLO3]

Recognize the principles of engineering ethics, and social and environmental responsibilities. [PLO4]

Recognize the need for ongoing additional knowledge, and the potential of integration and/or application of this knowledge effectively. [PLO7]

Develop leadership skills and project management techniques to independently and/or collaboratively handle complex professional tasks in a team-work context. [PLO5]

CHME611.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME611 Transport Phenomena
CHME611.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME611
Prediction of velocity, temperature, and concentration profiles for flowing fluids; unifying concepts and analogies in momentum, heat, and mass transport; streamline flow and turbulence, molecular and eddy conduction and diffusion, boundary layers, smooth and rough conduits and other boundaries.
Transport Phenomena (CHME611) > Credit Hours : 3

Transport Phenomena (CHME611) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate The Differences In Transport Processes Occurring In Newtonian And Non-Newtonian Fluids.

Practice Effectively Both Independent And Team Work On Research Projects And Presentations.

Solve The Differential Momentum, Heat, And Mass Balances For One And Multi-Dimensional Steady State Problems.

Solve The Shell Momentum, Heat, And Mass Balances For One Dimensional Steady State Problems.

Undersand The Molecular Transport Of Momentum (Newton’S Law Of Viscosity), Heat (Fourier’S Law), And Mass (Fick’S Law).

CHME612.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME612 Advanced Reaction Engineering
CHME612.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME612
Kinetics of fluid-solid reactions in single particles, Mechanisms and kinetics of catalytic reactions; Reactor design: Fixed, fluidized and transport bed reactors for homo/heterogeneous systems; Novel reactors; Applications in petroleum and chemical industries.
Advanced Reaction Engineering (CHME612) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Reaction Engineering (CHME612) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply The Concept Of Effectiveness Factor For Analysis Of Non-Isothermal Reactions With Simultaneous Diffusion And Reaction In Catalysts

Classify The Mechanism Of Heterogeneous Reactions For The Design Equations Of Adsorption-Based Reactive Systems Without Phase Change

Classify The Types Of Chemical Reactors, Especially Heterogeneous Reactors.

Solve The Reactor Design Equations (Chemical As Well As Biochemical Reactors) With Catalyst Decay, Both Analytically And Numerically

Using The Available Software Packages Of Reaction Engineering To Solve Complex Reaction Engineering Design/Research Problems

CHME621.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME621 Advanced Mass Transfer
CHME621.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME621
A study of fundamental mass transfer; theories of interphase mass transfer; gas-liquid and liquid-liquid systems; characterization; selection and design of equilibrium and rate-governed separation processes; capacity and efficiency of mass transfer equipment.
Advanced Mass Transfer (CHME621) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Mass Transfer (CHME621) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze Experimental Diffusion Coefficient Data

Analyze Mass Transfer Between Phases And Boundary Layer

Analyze The Mass Transfer Theories

Create Micro- And Macro-Models For Processes Involving Mass Transfer

Demonstrate The Fundamentals Of Diffusion And Convective Mass Transfer

Develop And Analyze Mass Transfer Operations By Membranes

CHME622.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME622 Biochemical Engineering
CHME622.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME622
An integrated approach to the application of engineering principles to biochemical processes. Topics include: cellular biology, polymeric cell compounds, enzyme and microbial kinetics, design and scale-up of bioreactors, sterilization, and bioseparation processes.
Biochemical Engineering (CHME622) > Credit Hours : 3

Biochemical Engineering (CHME622) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Define the importance of enzymes in modern industry.

Describe the structure of enzymes and their action.

Explain the key structural and energetic factors which give rise to increased enzyme stability.

Describe the industrial enzyme production and immobilizations techniques.

Design a bioreactor packed with immobilized enzyme.

CHME623.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME623 Advanced Polymer Engineering
CHME623.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME623
Polymer reaction engineering, characterization and processing for chemical engineers; polymerization mechanisms, kinetics and industrial equipment; thermodynamics of polymer solutions, morphology; crystallization and mechanical properties; polymer processing equipment and technology.
Advanced Polymer Engineering (CHME623) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Polymer Engineering (CHME623) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze Polymerization Mechanisms And Processes, And Processing Of Polymers For Product Manufacturing

Function Effectively In Groups/Teams By Engaging In Independent Learning To Develop Effective Oral, Written, And Interpersonal Communication Skills

Interpret Advanced Polymer Engineering Concepts Such As Dynamic Mechanical And Rheological Properties

Interpret Molecular Weight Distribution; And Physical Properties Of Polymers In Solid, Melt, And Solution

Recognize Various Terminologies Associated With Polymer Science And Engineering

CHME624.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME624 Advanced Process Dynamics & Controls
CHME624.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME624
Open-loop system dynamics, closed-loop systems, systems with difficult dynamics, non-linear systems, discrete-time systems, model-based control, adaptive systems and artificial intelligence. application to the chemical industry.
Advanced Process Dynamics & Controls (CHME624) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Process Dynamics & Controls (CHME624) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply The Computational Technique In The Form Of A Computer Program.

Demonstrate Of Physical Systems Into An Appropriate Mathematical Model.

Develop A Detailed Mathematical Model Of Lumped And Distributed System And Solving Emerged Model Equations Using Matlab/Simulink Software Package Compared With Analytical Solution.

Employ Of Computer Software Packages For The Simulation And Control Of Chemical Processes.

Explain Controlling Dynamic System.

Select A Suitable Computational Technique.

CHME625.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME625 Selected Topics in Chemical Engineering
CHME625.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME625
Different selected topics in chemical engineering were selected to complement the student's program and approved by the Program Committee.
Selected Topics in Chemical Engineering (CHME625) > Credit Hours : 3

Selected Topics in Chemical Engineering (CHME625) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Utilize advanced chemical engineering principles to a relevant area of the topic

Evaluate critically recent relevant research articles

Analyze the environmental, safety, economic, and technical dimensions of a chemical engineering case study

Communicate effectively through oral presentations and written reports

CHME626.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME626 Waste Management
CHME626.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME626
This course aims at presenting the characteristics of different types of solid waste, their generation rate, and associated regulations and legislation. Several waste management issues are covered including collection, transfer and transport, processing techniques, resource recovery, incineration, and landfilling. Control measures, reduction strategies, recycling and reuse industries are explored and their relevance to UAE and the region are discussed.
Waste Management (CHME626) > Credit Hours : 2

Waste Management (CHME626) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain waste processing and recovery techniques with particular emphasis on the UAE.

Establish plans for waste management programs.

Differentiate between different recycling options.

Determine the requirements of a composting facility.

Determine the requirements of a sanitary landfill facility.

Write technical reports and conduct professional presentations.

CHME710.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME710 Advanced Mathematical Modeling
CHME710.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME710
Formulation of mathematical modeling in chemical/petroleum engineering; Vectors and Matrices; Solution of algebraic sets of equations. Solution of Ordinary Differential Equations: Analytical and Approximate Methods, Qualitative Analysis, Numerical Methods; Initial Value Problems, Boundary Value Problems; Numerical Methods and Parameter Estimation. Solution of Partial Differential Equation: Analytical Methods, Numerical Methods, Finite Difference Methods, Finite Element Methods. Applications in chemical/petroleum engineering including problem assignments, term projects and course exams.
Advanced Mathematical Modeling (CHME710) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Mathematical Modeling (CHME710) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Formulate mathematical models for physical systems related to chemical/petroleum engineering applications

Solve the mathematical model by selecting and applying suitable mathematical methods

Solve ordinary and partial differential equations resulted from the mathematical modeling part

Interpret the mathematical solution resulting and make sensitivity analysis on the original problem

CHME720.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME720 Rheology and Rheometry
CHME720.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME720
A systematic development of the principles and applications of the science of rheology. Reviews vector and tensor mathematics and Newtonian fluid dynamics. Develops the physical and mathematical nature of stress and deformations in materials. Covers the use of theory and application of rheological equations of state. Describes and predicts non-linear viscous behavior as well as linear viscoelasticity. Covers the use of rheometry to determine rheological parameters in shear and extensional flow, and the rheology of interfaces
Rheology and Rheometry (CHME720) > Credit Hours : 3

Rheology and Rheometry (CHME720) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Relate the variety of flow phenomena that can occur in rheologically complex materials to the corresponding rheological concepts

Explain the concepts of viscoelasticity and other rheological parameters

Calculate material functions from an appropriate constitutive equation and using this information to model rheological behavior

Analyze rheological data of specific material classes to extract its structure information

Apply technical and theoretical knowledge about experimental rheometry techniques to select the appropriate techniques and measurement protocols depending on the material and application

CHME731.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME731 Nanoscience and Nanotechnology
CHME731.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME731
This course will cover range of fundamental topics in the fields of nanoscience and nanotechnology, including properties of nanomaterials (role of size; mechanical, optical, thermal, etc. properties(, classification of nanomaterials, structure-property relationship, synthesis of nanomaterials (Chemical vapor deposition, Arc discharge, RF-plasma, Ion sputtering, Laser ablation, Laser pyrolysis, Electro-deposition, etc.), characterization of nanomaterials (XRD, SEM, TEM, Optical, AFM, etc.), applications of nanomaterials (solar cells, nanocomposites, drug delivery, etc.), and the major challenges in nanotechnology in terms of nanomaterials dispersion, purity and mass production.
Nanoscience and Nanotechnology (CHME731) > Credit Hours : 3

Nanoscience and Nanotechnology (CHME731) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the influence of structure/geometry/size on nanomaterials properties

Identify the synthesis methods and the characterization techniques of nanomaterials.

Identify the key applications of nanotechnology and the major challenges in terms of nanomaterials dispersion, purity and mass production.

Explain the environmental, health and safety implications of nanomaterials.

Communicate effectively with the peers and faculty member(s) on the topics related to of nanoscience and nanomaterials.

CHME742.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME742 Advanced Catalysis
CHME742.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME742
The course introduces catalysis and fundamental catalytic phenomena. These phenomena are discussed in light of different catalyst properties and catalyst preparation techniques. Physical and chemical properties of the catalyst are used to demonstrate the principles of the catalyst selection process. Reactors and reactor design for activity testing are described as well as catalyst deactivation mechanism and treatment. Industrial catalytic processes are discussed such as synthesis gas reactions (ammonia synthesis and Fischer-Tropsch synthesis), petroleum refining and processing, and environmental catalysis
Advanced Catalysis (CHME742) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Catalysis (CHME742) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the concepts of catalysis and fundamental catalytic phenomena

Relate catalyst properties and preparation techniques to catalyst activity and selectivity

Utilize the physical and chemical properties of the catalyst for catalyst selection

Analyze activity data of a catalyst to describe catalyst deactivation mechanism and treatment

Apply technical and theoretical knowledge of catalysis to industrial catalytic processes

CHME750.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME750 Enzyme Technology
CHME750.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME750
This course provides information on enzyme technology, with emphasise on kinetics of enzymatic reactions. Immobilization processes, kinetics of immobilized enzymes and the design of packed bed enzymatic bioreactors are also discussed. The course starts with a general introduction to enzymes, their role and advantages over chemical catalysts, and genetics and protein synthesis. The course also covers enzyme production and purification techniques
Enzyme Technology (CHME750) > Credit Hours : 3

Enzyme Technology (CHME750) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the processes of industrial enzymes synthesis and production

Describe the Kinetics of enzymatic reaction, both free and immobilized.

Model systems with simultaneous diffusion-reaction.

Design bioreactors packed with immobilized enzyme and/or simultaneous product separation.

Communicate findings effectively, orally and in writing, with their peers and the engineering community.

CHME760.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME760 Advanced Membrane Technology
CHME760.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME760
The course goal is to introduce students to a comprehensive understanding of membrane technology with reference to the transport mechanisms through different types of membranes. The course will cover various topics such as transport through polymeric, inorganic and hybrid membranes; the influence of sorption, diffusion, adsorption, pore size and pore size distribution to the membrane separation. Separation in various systems at varying conditions. The importance of the materials chemical structure, the physical properties of the gases and liquids, interaction between gases/liquids and membrane material, and possible degradation. This course will enable students to understand the design of membrane-based separation/reaction processes by acquiring in-depth knowledge in the area of membrane separation mechanisms, transport models, membrane permeability computations, membrane types and modules, membrane reactors
Advanced Membrane Technology (CHME760) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Membrane Technology (CHME760) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Classify separation processes and membrane technology

Evaluate which membrane materials and morphologies are most suitable for a membrane separation/purification system

Select the types of membrane separation processes which are suitable for various gas or liquid separations

Explain the principles of how the membranes are prepared (ceramics, polymers, hybrids) and of the up-scaling of the membrane modules and processes

Solve problems related to membrane reactors and/or the membrane-based separation/reaction plants

CHME850.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME850 Candidacy Exam
CHME850.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME850
The Candidacy Exam for the PhD in Chemical Engineering is a non-credit Pass/Fail exam. Students have up to two trials to pass the exam; upon passing it, the student becomes a PhD candidate. The Candidacy Exam is structured to evaluate the student’s breadth and depth of fundamental knowledge in the area(s) closely related to the thesis work. The Candidacy Exam committee, in consultation with the advisor, decides on the topic(s) of the Candidacy Exam. The PhD student prepares a concise and comprehensive research proposal that clearly defines the research problem and objectives and outlines the research methodology that he/she plans to follow. The concerned PhD student should present and defend his/her proposal in front of the Candidacy Exam committee.
Candidacy Exam (CHME850) > Credit Hours : 0

Candidacy Exam (CHME850) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate the depth and breadth of their knowledge in the field of chemical engineering relevant to student’s research topic.

Propose a well-structured research project that outlines clear objectives, a detailed plan, and an appropriate methodology.

Demonstrate sufficient communication skills relevant to field of study and the research topic.

CHME900.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME900 Dissertation Doctoral Research
CHME900.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME900
Open to students who have successfully completed the comprehensive exam. PhD student conducts original research under the direction of a supervisory committee. Credits are determined in consultation with the dissertation supervisor. Prerequisite: Student must pass
Dissertation Doctoral Research (CHME900) > Credit Hours : 30

Dissertation Doctoral Research (CHME900) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explore novel ideas of engineering significance.

Carry out rigorous and original experimental and/or theoretical work.

Comprehend the merits, limitations, and possibilities for new developments of the topic under investigation.

Apply sound research methodologies in addressing the topic under investigation.

Draw appropriate conclusions; and write and successfully defend research thesis.

CHME901.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME901 Dissertation Doctoral Research
CHME901.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME901
The PhD student conducts original research under the direction of an advisory committee. Credits registered in each semester are determined in consultation with the dissertation advisor.
Dissertation Doctoral Research (CHME901) > Credit Hours : 42

Dissertation Doctoral Research (CHME901) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Conduct independent research in a specific research area.

Produce a dissertation of publishable academic quality.

CHME910.title: UAEU Catalog — CHME910 Dissertation Defense
CHME910.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CHME910
Two part exam, open and close, to defend the results of PhD research work
Dissertation Defense (CHME910) > Credit Hours : 0

Dissertation Defense (CHME910) > Prerequisites
CHME850
Dissertation Defense (CHME910) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Assess primary literature and explain areas of active research in the chosen field

Discuss research design, including results, recommendations, and conclusions

Communicate research outcomes logically and persuasively both in writing and orally

Evaluate the study results in line with the research design, including ethical and professional considerations

CPSE600.title: UAEU Catalog — CPSE600 Graduate Seminar
CPSE600.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CPSE600
Research preparation
Graduate Seminar (CPSE600) > Credit Hours : 0

Graduate Seminar (CPSE600) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :
