Criticize others’ presentations objectively.

Demonstrate the ability to be a good listener

Demonstrate the ability to be a good presenter

Prepare an effective presentation (seminar)

CPSE610.title: UAEU Catalog — CPSE610 Fluid Phase Equilibria
CPSE610.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CPSE610
Review of energy and reversibility concepts; single-phase systems of pure materials and mixtures; equilibrium and stability of PVT systems; phase behavior of multicomponent, multiphase systems; applications using equations of state.
Fluid Phase Equilibria (CPSE610) > Credit Hours : 3

Fluid Phase Equilibria (CPSE610) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Determine Chemical Potential, Fugacity, Activity, Residual Properties And Excess Properties Of Real Mixtures.

Present Results Orally And In Written Assay.

Solve Vapor-Liquid Equilibria Problems Involving Real Mixtures.

Use Equations Of State To Determine Properties Of Real Fluids (Pure And Mixtures).

CPSE624.title: UAEU Catalog — CPSE624 Well Stimulation
CPSE624.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CPSE624
In-situ stress determinations, effects of stress and strain gradients, time-dependent effects, Griffith's theory, crack phenomena, fracture toughness of rocks, pore-elasticity concepts. Hydraulic proppant fracturing. Formation damage and modeling damage. Acid treatment of carbonates. Geochemistry of acid-rock interactions. Matrix acidizing of sandstone and carbonates. Sand Control.
Well Stimulation (CPSE624) > Credit Hours : 3

Well Stimulation (CPSE624) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Design of an acidizing and sand control jobs.

Designing and interpreting hydraulic fracturing treatments.

Evaluate and select an appropriate engineering action to near well bore damage accused by drilling and completion operations.

Selecting appropriate stimulation method for sandstone and carbonate oil eservoirs.

Understand mechanical properties of rocks, fracture models, rheology of the fracture fluid, proppant, etc. required to design a fracturing job.

CPSE695.title: UAEU Catalog — CPSE695 Technical Project
CPSE695.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CPSE695
This course involves independent work on a design, simulation, modeling, development or experiments-related technical project. All projects must be supervised by a faculty member and the student is responsible for finding his/her project supervisor. Project topics may be faculty initiated, student initiated, or suggested by industrial contacts. The student is expected to submit a brief description of a work plan by the end of the second week of the semester and a comprehensive final report by the last week of lectures of the semester. The student is also required to give an oral presentation during that week.
Technical Project (CPSE695) > Credit Hours : 6

Technical Project (CPSE695) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop a work plan for a technical project in the field of Chemical or Petroleum Engineering.

Apply advanced research and/or design skills to a specific problem related to chemical or petroleum engineering.

Report findings in a well written technical report.

Present results at a high level of proficiency to a technical and non-technical audience.

CPSE699.title: UAEU Catalog — CPSE699 Thesis Research
CPSE699.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=CPSE699
A directed research study on a specialized topic under the supervision of faculty advisor(s). The research is carried out during two or more terms. A written report is submitted at the end of the study and defended in front of a panel.
Thesis Research (CPSE699) > Credit Hours : 9

Thesis Research (CPSE699) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply advanced concepts of fundamental sciences and engineering to solve complex chemical and petroleum engineering problems.

Conduct advanced research to develop innovative solutions for complex chemical and petroleum engineering problems through the use of selected research methodology and modern computing tools.

Search, evaluate and acquire information and data from relevant chemical and petroleum engineering literature.

Design advanced approaches to conduct chemical and petroleum engineering experiments.

Use advanced quantitative and qualitative methods to interpret research experimental results.

Disseminate and discuss their professional and scientific work to the general public, as well as to experts in both writing and oral formats.

Observe and apply ethical and professional codes and responsibilities.

PETE290.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE290 Introduction to Petroleum Engineering
PETE290.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE290
This course introduces the general activities of the upstream sector of the petroleum industry including origin of petroleum, petroleum traps, exploration for oil and gas, drilling and completion practices, and production operations, corrosion, pollution, oil storage, transportation, refining, and marketing.
Introduction to Petroleum Engineering (PETE290) > Credit Hours : 1

Introduction to Petroleum Engineering (PETE290) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Understand the history of oil and gas origin, generation and migration, the concepts behind a range of exploration, drilling, production and refining techniques , the petroleum engineer`s roles and petroleum engineering terminology.

Describe the early history of petroleum inducstry, the origins of major national oil companies, the technological challenges facing the industry in an increasingly environmentally coscious world.

PETE305.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE305 Reservoir Rock & Fluid Properties
PETE305.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE305
This course introduces fundamental properties of reservoir rocks and fluids (oil, natural gas, formation water). Rock properties include porosity, fluid saturation, rock compressibility, permeability, capillary pressure, and effective and relative permeability. Fluid properties include composition of hydrocarbons, phase behavior of hydrocarbon systems, types of reservoir fluids, properties of oil-phase, gas-phase, and water-phase at reservoir pressures and temperatures, gas-liquid equilibrium (flash and differential vaporization), and gas-liquid equilibrium calculations using K values.
Reservoir Rock & Fluid Properties (PETE305) > Credit Hours : 3

Reservoir Rock & Fluid Properties (PETE305) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co GENG220 with a minimum grade D GEOL100 PETE290 with a minimum grade D
Reservoir Rock & Fluid Properties (PETE305) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recall the physical meaning and uses of various reservoir rock and fluid properties.

Use Darcy’s law to compute fluid flow rate for single -phase flow and multi-phase flow in linear and radial flow geometries.

Examine fluid phase behavior at reservoir pressure and temperature to predict phases present, amount, and composition for multi-component fluids.

Evaluate oil, natural gas, and water properties at reservoir pressure and temperature.

PETE308.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE308 Drilling Engineering I
PETE308.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE308
This course introduces basic drilling techniques and drilling fluid properties. Topics include components of rotary drilling rig: rig, power transmission, hoisting, rotary table, bottom hole assembly, drilling bits; prediction of formation pressure, fracture pressure, and casing setting depths; mud properties and mud weight calculations; drilling hydraulics and nozzle sizing; factors affecting rate of penetration; cementing operations; and lab measurements of mud properties.
Drilling Engineering I (PETE308) > Credit Hours : 3

Drilling Engineering I (PETE308) > Corequisites
CHME330 with a minimum grade D

CHME390 with a minimum grade D
Drilling Engineering I (PETE308) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate basic rig components and decide on their operating parameters.

Evaluate drilling hydraulics and pressure losses in a well and decide on nozzle sizes for a bit.

Predict formation pressure,, mud pressure,, and formation fracture pressure.

Design laboratory experiments to measure drilling mud properties and generate lab reports.

PETE315.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE315 Reservoir Rock & Fluid Properties lab
PETE315.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE315
This course deals with the measurement of fundamental properties of reservoir rocks and fluids. Rock properties include porosity, irreducible water saturation, residual oil saturation, absolute permeability. Fluid properties include oil distillation, oil composition of one of oil fractions, oil density at room conditions and at high pressure and temperature conditions, oil viscosity at high pressure and temperature, surface and interfacial tensions, flash liberation process, estimation of bubble-point pressure at reservoir temperature, and oil-formation-volume factor and solution gas/oil ratio at pressures below the bubble-point pressure.
Reservoir Rock & Fluid Properties lab (PETE315) > Credit Hours : 2

Reservoir Rock & Fluid Properties lab (PETE315) > Prerequisites
PETE305 with a minimum grade D
Reservoir Rock & Fluid Properties lab (PETE315) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply specific procedures as a group to carry out experiments that comply both safety and environmental regulations.

Analyze the experimental data to obtain rock and fluid properties and submit reports using MS word.

PETE320.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE320 Reservoir Mechanics
PETE320.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE320
This course deals with material balance (MB) techniques to estimate oil and gas reserves. Topics include generalized MB equations for oil and gas reservoirs, fluid drive mechanisms, selection of PVT data, water influx, analysis of production history data and performance prediction of oil and gas reservoirs.
Reservoir Mechanics (PETE320) > Credit Hours : 3

Reservoir Mechanics (PETE320) > Prerequisites
PETE305 with a minimum grade D
Reservoir Mechanics (PETE320) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Compare various hydrocarbon recovery mechanisms in oil and gas reservoirs combined with volumetric estimation to calculate recovery factors (A).

Apply the concept of material balance in petroleum reservoirs by including the various hydrocarbon production mechanisms to derive the general material balance equation and driving indices and to solve engineering problems (A, E).

Analyze reservoir pressure and production history for oil and gas reservoirs in order to determine reservoir parameters such as oil-in-place, gas-in place, size of gas cap, and type and strength of water aquifer (B, E, K).

Predict reservoir performance of depletion-drive and water-drive gas reservoirs; and depletion-drive, gas cap-drive, and water-drive oil reservoirs (E, K).

PETE362.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE362 Data Analysis in Petroleum Engineering
PETE362.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE362
This course concentrates on the application of probability theory to analyze data in petroleum engineering processes. This includes data analysis of heterogeneous reservoir rock properties to estimate the most probable values of porosity, water saturation, permeability, and volumetric hydrocarbon reserves; use of permeability distribution as a descriptor of reservoir heterogeneity; probabilistic analysis of new hydrocarbon discoveries; and estimation of reservoir performance using probabilistic procedures and regression analysis.
Data Analysis in Petroleum Engineering (PETE362) > Credit Hours : 1

Data Analysis in Petroleum Engineering (PETE362) > Prerequisites
STAT210 with a minimum grade D

PETE305 with a minimum grade D
Data Analysis in Petroleum Engineering (PETE362) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Familiar with the data and their sources normally engaged in drilling, production, reservoir engineering.

Organize and evaluate these engineering data using statistical tools.

Draw conclusions under uncertainty using statistical analysis methods.

Design controlled experiments

Apply statistical method in solving engineering problems.

PETE403.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE403 Well Logging
PETE403.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE403
This course covers analysis of various well measurements of reservoir properties. Topics include effect of the bore hole environment on logging operations interpretation of self potential, resistivity induction, neutron, sonic, density gamma ray, and dipmeter logs to determine hydrocarbon saturation, porosity, permeability, and facies. Also this course covers fundamental geophysical concepts including wellbore seismic and stratigraphic information from dipmeter.
Well Logging (PETE403) > Credit Hours : 3

Well Logging (PETE403) > Prerequisites
PETE305 with a minimum grade D

GEOL372 with a minimum grade D
Well Logging (PETE403) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Understand the principles and practices of wireline logs and their importance in formation and reservoir evaluation

Identify the differences between various logging tools: advantages and limitations, read and comprehend different log responses

Apply integrated log interpretation techniques in formation evaluation

Identify petrophysical properties of reservoir rocks, differentiate between reservoir and non-reservoir rocks, and design optimum logging programs

PETE407.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE407 Drilling Engineering ll
PETE407.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE407
This course deals with additional topics in drilling engineering, namely design of directional and horizontal wells, survey analysis methods, tie point and collision, casing specifications and strengths, casing sizing, prediction of casing loads and resistances, and design of different casing strings.
Drilling Engineering ll (PETE407) > Credit Hours : 3

Drilling Engineering ll (PETE407) > Prerequisites
PETE308 with a minimum grade D
Drilling Engineering ll (PETE407) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Summarize the types and uses of directional wells, kick off methods, and bottom-hole-assemblies used to control bottom-hole angle [A, C].

Analyze well survey data obtained during drilling a well utilizing manual and computer programs [1, 3]

Design a directional well in vertical plane utilizing manual and computer programs [1, 2, 5]

Design casing for vertical and directional wells using basic principles as well as available computer programs [C, E, F, K]

PETE410.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE410 Independent Studies
PETE410.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE410
An independent investigation by each student of a certain problem in the core areas of Petroleum Engineering. The investigation may require theoretical, numerical, and/or experimental work. Grades are based on solving the assigned problem, giving oral presentation, and a written report. There are no formal lectures. The choice of problem requires arrangement with a faculty member and the approval of the department.
Independent Studies (PETE410) > Credit Hours : 3

Independent Studies (PETE410) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Choose the techniques, skills, and petroleum engineering tools necessary for engineering practice. (1, 2, 6)

Demonstrate the impact of engineering solutions in a global, economic, environmental, and societal context. (1, 3, 4, 5,)

Identify, formulate, and solve engineering problems. (1, 3, 4, 5,)

Ability to communicate effectively in writing and orally. (3)

Explore into advanced literature and contemporary issues. (7)

PETE413.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE413 Applied Reservoir Geology
PETE413.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE413
Oil distribution in the world and in the United Arab Emirates; geology of reservoirs, which includes the formation of reservoir rocks, cap rocks, source rocks and the environments of deposition; petrophysical parameters of reservoir rocks, porosity and permeability; reservoir fluids: oil field waters, crude oil and natural gas; reservoir conditions: pressure, temperature and their effects on oil maturation, migration and accumulation; oil generation; oil migration; types of oil traps; and methods of exploration.
Applied Reservoir Geology (PETE413) > Credit Hours : 3

Applied Reservoir Geology (PETE413) > Prerequisites
GEOL100 with a minimum grade D
Applied Reservoir Geology (PETE413) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Gain knowledge on the role of depositional environment and textural parameters influencing reservoir rock [1];

Develop an understanding of the effect of heat and pressure on oil migration and entrapment [1];

Develop the ability to use formation water to identify the source of formation water [1, 6];

Develop the ability to use RFT to define zonation of the reservoir [1, 6].

PETE419.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE419 Well Performance
PETE419.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE419
This course covers basic well performance calculations necessary for the design and analysis of naturally flowing and artificially lifted wells. Topics include Inflow Performance Relationship (IPR), Tubing Performance Relationship (TPR), Flowline Performance Relationship (FPR), Choke Performance Relationship (CPR), Gas-Lift, Electric Submersible Pumps (ESP), and production forecasting.
Well Performance (PETE419) > Credit Hours : 3

Well Performance (PETE419) > Prerequisites
CHME330 with a minimum grade D

PETE320 with a minimum grade D
Well Performance (PETE419) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply surface production data to estimate PVT and physical properties of produced fluids.

Evaluate the performance of individual components making up production systems (IPR, TPR, FPR, and CPR).

Apply NODAL System Analysis and the resulting total system analysis to optimize simple and complex production systems.

Design gas-lift installation and size ESPs.

PETE422.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE422 Reservoir Simulation
PETE422.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE422
This course covers fundamental concepts of reservoir simulation to model single-phase flow in petroleum reservoirs. Topics include reservoir engineering concepts, mathematical concepts, derivation of reservoir flow equations, finite difference equations and their solutions, and applications to predict reservoir performance.
Reservoir Simulation (PETE422) > Credit Hours : 3

Reservoir Simulation (PETE422) > Prerequisites
PETE320 with a minimum grade D
Reservoir Simulation (PETE422) > Corequisites
MATH140 with a minimum grade D
Reservoir Simulation (PETE422) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Define the steps involved in developing a reservoir simulator for single- as well as multi-phase-reservoirs (A).

Outline the physics of flow for single-phase reservoir and rephrase it in terms of mathematical equations (A).

Write and solve the algebraic flow equation for single-phase (oil, water, or gas) for all reservoir blocks (C, E).

Build a computer model to represent a reservoir by preparing data for reservoir blocks, run the single-phase simulator, and interpret results of simulator. (B, E, K)

PETE424.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE424 Safety & Environment Impact
PETE424.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE424
This course introduces students to safety and environmental issues in petroleum operations. Topics include sources of pollutants and hazards, management of safety and loss prevention, safety programs and safety rules, and environmental protection, rules and regulations.
Safety & Environment Impact (PETE424) > Credit Hours : 3

Safety & Environment Impact (PETE424) > Prerequisites
MATH110 with a minimum grade D

CHEM111 with a minimum grade D

CHEM175 with a minimum grade D
Safety & Environment Impact (PETE424) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analysis of steady state, unsteady state, conservative and non-conservative environmental systems (1).

Apply basic chemistry principles to different environmental problems (1).

Apply Petroleum and Petrochemical industries safety standards and regulation (2, 5, and 6).

Conduct qualitative and quantities risk assessment (1, 2, 4, 6, and 7).

PETE443.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE443 Transport & Storage of Petroleum
PETE443.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE443
This course deals with analysis and design of surface piping and storage facilities of crude oil and natural gas. Topics include fluid flow and pressure losses in pipes, pipeline design, selection and sizing of liquid pumps and gas compressors, corrosion in pipes, other transportation methods, and storage of petroleum and its products.
Transport & Storage of Petroleum (PETE443) > Credit Hours : 3

Transport & Storage of Petroleum (PETE443) > Prerequisites
PETE419 with a minimum grade D
Transport & Storage of Petroleum (PETE443) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop the understanding of different types of flow, calculate fluid friction and apply Bernoulli Eq. to calculate pressure drop and pipe diameter

Identify and apply the fundamental principle governing equations such as continuity and mechanical energy equation

Design a piping compression and pumping system and understand the factor controlling the performance of pumps, gas compressor and efficiencies

Design gas and oil storage tanks and gathering points

PETE485.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE485 Internship I
PETE485.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE485
Students spend 8 weeks on a full-time basis in an engineering or consulting office in the UAE or abroad to earn practical skills. This course aims at offering career exploration opportunities for students.
Internship I (PETE485) > Credit Hours : 1

Internship I (PETE485) > Prerequisites
STAT210 with a minimum grade D

MATH135 with a minimum grade D or MATH110 with a minimum grade D

MATH140 with a minimum grade D

MATH275 with a minimum grade D

PHYS105 with a minimum grade D

PHYS135 with a minimum grade D

GENG215 with a minimum grade D

GENG220 with a minimum grade D

GENG230 with a minimum grade D

CHEM111 with a minimum grade D

CHEM175 with a minimum grade D

PETE290 with a minimum grade D

CHME330 with a minimum grade D
Internship I (PETE485) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Function effectively in multi-disciplinary teams and individually to achieve the planned tasks and goals.

Develop communication skills through oral and written presentations.

Evaluate different engineering situations and judgments based on ethical codes and professional responsibilities.

PETE490.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE490 Internship II
PETE490.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE490
Students spend 8 weeks on a full-time basis in an engineering or consulting office in the UAE or abroad to earn practical skills. This course aims at offering career exploration opportunities for students as well as opportunities to correlate their academic preparation to the reality of conducting professional practice, to interact effectively with others in practice, to develop professional skills and communicate effectively in the workplace and to gain true practical experience that is necessary for their future practice as engineers in their respective discipline after graduation.
Internship II (PETE490) > Credit Hours : 1

Internship II (PETE490) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co PETE485 with a minimum grade P

PHYS110 with a minimum grade D

PHYS140 with a minimum grade D

PETE308 with a minimum grade D

PETE320 with a minimum grade D
Internship II (PETE490) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Function effectively in multi-disciplinary teams and individually to achieve the planed tasks and goals.

Develop communication skills through oral and written presentations.

Evaluate different engineering situations and judgments based on ethical codes and professional responsibilities.

Propose ideas/solutions for real-life problems based on the learned knowledge.

PETE507.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE507 Well Testing
PETE507.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE507
This course covers reservoir characterization by pressure test analysis. Topics include fluid flow equations in porous media under transient and pseudo-steady state flow conditions, pressure buildup and pressure drawdown tests, average reservoir pressure, type curve matching, well testing of heterogeneous reservoirs, pressure derivatives analysis technique, multiple well testing, and test design and instrumentation
Well Testing (PETE507) > Credit Hours : 3

Well Testing (PETE507) > Prerequisites
MATH275 with a minimum grade D

PETE320 with a minimum grade D
Well Testing (PETE507) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply the CTR and other approximate solutions of the diffusivity equation to solve well testing problems.

Identify test objectives and understand the role of well test analysis in reservoir planning and management.

Use straight line, type-curve matching, and pressure derivative techniques to analyze pressure transient tests’ data.

Design well tests to meet test objectives.

PETE512.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE512 Petroleum Production Operations
PETE512.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE512
Well completions, perforations, Chemical and mechanical properties of reservoir rocks/fluids and treatment fluids, formation damage sources, detection, and modeling. Hydraulic fracturing, and fracturing fluids. Acid/rock interactions and acid treatment of oil reservoirs. Sand control methods. Evaluation of various skin factors.
Petroleum Production Operations (PETE512) > Credit Hours : 3

Petroleum Production Operations (PETE512) > Corequisites
PETE419 with a minimum grade D
Petroleum Production Operations (PETE512) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate and design well completions including optimum perforating.

Assess formation damage and other wellbore restrictions and recommend appropriate solutions.

Evaluate and assess well problems with production logs and make decisions to rectify the situation.

Design matrix acidizing treatments and hydraulic fracturing treatments.

PETE519.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE519 Secondary Recovery Methods
PETE519.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE519
This course covers analysis and design of the secondary (water and gas injection) recovery technique to recover oil. Topics include flood patterns, mobility ratio, sweep efficiency, displacement mechanisms, injection rates and pressures, reservoir heterogeneity, performance prediction, and sources and treatment of water for water flooding.
Secondary Recovery Methods (PETE519) > Credit Hours : 3

Secondary Recovery Methods (PETE519) > Prerequisites
PETE320 with a minimum grade D
Secondary Recovery Methods (PETE519) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply the petrophysical principles governing both static and dynamic of fluid -rock interactions (1).

Apply the physics of multiphase fluid flow in oil reservoirs (1).

Predictive the performance of water flooding using CGM model (1, 2).

Design water flooding project for homogeneous and heterogeneous oil reservoirs (1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7).

PETE520.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE520 Fluid Flow in Porous Media Lab
PETE520.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE520
This course deals with the design aspects of oil displacement by another fluid in rock samples. It builds on the experiences of students obtained in lab measurements of individual reservoir rock and fluid properties in PETE 315 to create an integrated lab measurement of all properties needed to analyze oil displacement by a displacing fluid. The displacing fluid can be chosen to study the relative permeability, capillary pressures, and displacement efficiency of water flooding, gas flooding, or any enhanced oil recovery fluids (acidic water, microbial water, polymer solution, or steam) using cores, fractured cores (sand packs and glass beads may be considered as alternatives) in one-dimensional geometry or packed layers in two-dimensional geometry.
Fluid Flow in Porous Media Lab (PETE520) > Credit Hours : 1

Fluid Flow in Porous Media Lab (PETE520) > Prerequisites
PETE315 with a minimum grade D
Fluid Flow in Porous Media Lab (PETE520) > Corequisites
PETE519 with a minimum grade D
Fluid Flow in Porous Media Lab (PETE520) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply specific procedures as a group to carry out experiments that comply both safety and environmental regulations.

Analyze the experimental data to obtain rock and fluid properties that affecting fluid flow through porous media and submit reports using MS word.

PETE526.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE526 Separation & Treatment Petrol Fluid
PETE526.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE526
This course deals with design of separation and treatment facilities for crude oil. Topics covered include phase behavior of water-hydrocarbon systems, flash calculations, 2 and 3- phase oil and gas separators sizing and design, oil-water emulsions and heater-treater design, treatment of oil field waters, and oil skimmers selection and design.
Separation & Treatment Petrol Fluid (PETE526) > Credit Hours : 3

Separation & Treatment Petrol Fluid (PETE526) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the basic component of the separator. (1, 2, 3, 4, 6)

Design two-phase and three-phase separators. (1, 2, 3, 4, 6)

Design waste water treatment process. (1, 2, 3, 4, 6)

Design oil and emulsion treater. (1, 2, 3, 4, 6)

PETE542.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE542 Petroleum Property Evaluation
PETE542.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE542
This course deals with economic evaluation of exploration and producing properties. It combines reservoir-engineering techniques such as reserve calculations and decline curve analysis with rate of return calculations for assured and risky ventures to project economic values for petroleum properties.
Petroleum Property Evaluation (PETE542) > Credit Hours : 3

Petroleum Property Evaluation (PETE542) > Prerequisites
GENG315 with a minimum grade D
Petroleum Property Evaluation (PETE542) > Corequisites
PETE419 with a minimum grade D
Petroleum Property Evaluation (PETE542) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Compare the definition of reserves, reserves estimation, material balance analysis, decline curve analysis. [1, 3, 4, 5, 6]

Demonstrate of cash-flow for petroleum properties: income, expenditures, taxes, and tax allowances: depreciation, depletion. [1, 3, 4, 5, 6]

Outline the basis for evaluating economic projects and different techniques for measuring return on investments. [1, 3, 4, 5, 6]

Explain the time value of money, the concepts of economic interest, interest relations, and nominal/effective interest. [1, 3, 4, 5, 6]

Illustrate the economic indicators: NPV, ROR, MCO, TCS, cash-flow, profit-to-investment ratio and payout time. [1, 3, 4, 5, 6]

Apply of statistical analysis and the applications of probability distributions and decision-making analysis. [1, 3, 4]

PETE547.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE547 Applied Reservoir Simulation
PETE547.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE547
This course covers advanced topics in reservoir simulation. These include reservoir fluid flow equations in multiphase, multidimensional flow, up-scaling of rock properties, pseudo functions, vertical equilibrium, analysis of data for for consistency, history matching, and applications to field cases.
Applied Reservoir Simulation (PETE547) > Credit Hours : 3

Applied Reservoir Simulation (PETE547) > Prerequisites
PETE422 with a minimum grade D
Applied Reservoir Simulation (PETE547) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Define achievable objectives and available sources of data, company resources, and time constraint for the simulation study (A, D, G).

Analyze data quality and scale for reservoir, fluid, and reservoir-fluid from various sources for consistency; and production data needed for constructing simulation model (B, C, E, K).

Conduct history matching consistent with the objective of history matching using the simulation model created by dividing the reservoir into blocks and assigning block properties (B, D, E, K).

Design prediction runs that maximize oil recovery and achieve the objective of the simulation study (B, C, D, E, G, K).

PETE557.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE557 Enhanced Oil Recovery
PETE557.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE557
This course covers chemical and thermal methods of EOR. Specific topics include interfacial tension, entrapment and mobilization of oil in porous media, residual oil, miscibility, adsorption at solid/liquid interfaces, surfactants and micro-emulsions, miscible gas flooding, polymer flooding, thermal methods, and effect of reservoir heterogeneity.
Enhanced Oil Recovery (PETE557) > Credit Hours : 3

Enhanced Oil Recovery (PETE557) > Prerequisites
PETE519 with a minimum grade D
Enhanced Oil Recovery (PETE557) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the mechanism of different EOR processes (1).

Identify causes of failures and successes of EOR processes (1, 2, 6).

Design of Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR) Technologies (1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7).

PETE570.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE570 Special Topics in Petroleum Engineering
PETE570.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE570
This course may cover any area of petroleum engineering that is not covered by other courses of the program. A topic, approved by the Department, is selected for an in-depth study in the form of a semester course.
Special Topics in Petroleum Engineering (PETE570) > Credit Hours : 3

Special Topics in Petroleum Engineering (PETE570) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Understand the basis of reservoir simulation Eclipse 100 Software (6, 4,7).

Describe a simulation model, what analytical models and numerical models are and what specifically a reservoir simulation model is (6, 4,7).

Learn the difference between a simple or complex reservoir model that required to model reservoir processes (6, 4,7).

Illustrate the meaning of e.g. history matching, black oil model, transmissibility, pseudo relative permeability etc. (6, 4,7).

Develop the ability to Use modern tools of word processing, graphics, presentation and other computational tools of reservoir engineering, Exercise sound engineering judgment and provide physical arguments in support of his/her conclusions and results. (6, 4,7).

Communicate effectively in writing and orally (1,2, 3, 6, 4,7).

PETE585.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE585 Design and Critical Thinking in Petroleum Engineering
PETE585.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE585
This course concentrates on the rigors of communication, design, and critical thinking in an engineering context including problem identification, feasibility study of alternative solutions, preliminary design, technical writing, teamwork, and formal presentations. A team of students will apply the knowledge gained throughout their study and from industrial training to an engineering design project, emphasizing critical thinking, creativity, and originality. The selected alternatives will be the foundation of the capstone design project. A final report is required.
Design and Critical Thinking in Petroleum Engineering (PETE585) > Credit Hours : 3

Design and Critical Thinking in Petroleum Engineering (PETE585) > Prerequisites
PHYS110 with a minimum grade D

PHYS140 with a minimum grade D

MATH275 with a minimum grade D

MATH140 with a minimum grade D

GENG215 with a minimum grade D

GENG220 with a minimum grade D

GENG230 with a minimum grade D

GENG315 with a minimum grade D

STAT210 with a minimum grade D
Design and Critical Thinking in Petroleum Engineering (PETE585) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the relevant theoretical background of a contemporary engineering problem. [PLO1]

Apply the fundamentals of engineering-design and critical thinking, including the assessment and evaluation of alternative engineering solutions. [PLO2]

Develop and conduct appropriate experimentation, modeling, simulation, and/or data analysis using engineering tools. [PLO6]

Communicate effectively through oral and written presentations. [PLO3]

Outline the principles of engineering ethics, and social and environmental responsibilities. [PLO4]

Recognize the need for ongoing additional knowledge, and the potential of integration and/or application of this knowledge effectively. [PLO7]

Develop leadership skills and project management techniques to independently and/or collaboratively handle complex professional tasks in a team-work context. [PLO5]

PETE590.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE590 Capstone Engineering Design Project
PETE590.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE590
This course builds on the outcomes of PETE 585 course to perform detailed design and cost estimate of the selected alternative solutions to a well-defined engineering problem. Student teams are expected to apply knowledge gained throughout their studies to an engineering design project, emphasizing creativity and originality. A final report is required.
Capstone Engineering Design Project (PETE590) > Credit Hours : 3

Capstone Engineering Design Project (PETE590) > Prerequisites
PETE585 with a minimum grade D
Capstone Engineering Design Project (PETE590) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the theoretical background of a contemporary engineering problem. [PLO1]

Apply the fundamentals of engineering-design, including the assessment and evaluation of alternative engineering solutions. [PLO2]

Develop and conduct appropriate experimentation, modelling, simulation, and/or data analysis using modern engineering tools. [PLO6]

Communicate effectively through oral and written presentations. [PLO3]

Recognize the principles of engineering ethics, and social and environmental responsibilities. [PLO4]

Recognize the need for ongoing additional knowledge, and the potential of integration and/or application of this knowledge effectively. [PLO7]

Develop leadership skills and project management techniques to independently and/or collaboratively handle complex professional tasks in a team-work context. [PLO5]

PETE608.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE608 Advanced Drilling Engineering
PETE608.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE608
This course covers advanced drilling topics which is essential in drilling technology environment. These topics were carefully selected to add to the skill of advanced drilling engineer. It is an introduction to advanced drilling topics such as High Pressure High Temperature (HPHT) drilling, modern drilling technologies, special well design, advanced wellbore stability analysis, pore pressure and fracture gradient estimation strategies before and during drilling are highly critical topics for anyone involved in the drilling process, problems and their solutions.
Advanced Drilling Engineering (PETE608) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Drilling Engineering (PETE608) > Prerequisites
PETE308 with a minimum grade C

PETE407 with a minimum grade C
Advanced Drilling Engineering (PETE608) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Classify key aspects of drilling operations, drill rig types and fundamental differences between onshore and offshore drilling (PLO1).

Explain the process of mud preparation, circulation and cleaning, including understanding of mud types, mud chemistry and properties and the calculation of required pump rate and power (PLO1).

Describe the purpose of downhole equipment used in drilling, including calculation of hole, pipe and annulus volumes (PLO1, 2).

Analysis of critical safety parameters associated with drilling, such as safe drilling window, pore pressure, fracture pressure and collapse pressure (PLO1, 2, 3, 6).

Summarize the hydraulics of mud flow through the borehole including calculation and application of hydraulics through the string, across the drill bit and up the annulus (PLO1, 7).

Explain the process and importance of cementing and casing (PLO1).

Utilize knowledge of key safety features in well control procedures (PLO1, 4).

Describe processes associated with directional drilling and its uses in exploration and production (PLO1, 4, 6).

PETE612.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE612 Advanced Natural Gas Engineering
PETE612.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE612
Reserve estimates for gas and gas-condensate reservoirs; gas well performance; gas-well testing, gas flow in transmission lines; gas storage fields; liquefied natural gas.
Advanced Natural Gas Engineering (PETE612) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Natural Gas Engineering (PETE612) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply Modified Material Balance Equation To Treat Unconventional Sources Of Natural Gas.

Design And Interpret Gas Well Deliverability Tests.

Determine The Physical Properties Of Natural Gas Mixtures Adjusted For Contaminants.

Perform Gas Flow Calculations In Reservoirs And Piping Systems Using Advanced Models .

Specify The Data Needs And Carry Out Basic Reservoir Performance Calculations Of Dry, Wet And Retrograde Gas Reservoirs With And Without Water Influx.

Understand The Role Of Phase Behavior In Reservoir Classification, Gas Production And Separation.

Write Relevant Articles And Make A Presentation.

PETE615.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE615 Advanced Reservoir Engineering
PETE615.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE615
This course covers advanced topics in reservoir flow and the use of its initial production data for optimum development and management leading to a forecast of its future production capacity. Topics include fluid and petrophysical properties and measurements; horizontal, radial, and vertical flow, multiphase flow, heterogeneous, multilayered, and inclined reservoirs; up-scaling and averaging properties; diffusivity equation and solutions, aquifer influx reserve estimation; reserve estimates from decline curve analysis; productivity index for vertical, horizontal and multilateral wells, gas and water coning, production forecasting; field development alternatives: infill drilling, secondary recovery using water and gas injection patterns, drainage volumes for various schemes, streamlines, tracer methods; introduction to enhanced oil recovery.
Advanced Reservoir Engineering (PETE615) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Reservoir Engineering (PETE615) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Acquainted With The Laboratory Experiments For Routine Pvt Analysis On An Initially Undersaturated Oil And Able To Modify The Results Of The Differential Vaporization To Cater For The Effect Of Separation Conditions Before Use In All Reservoir Studies.

Correct Laboratory Pvt Results To Match Field Observations After The Appraisal Stage And Start Of Continuous Production And To Make The Necessary Pvt Adjustments Of Volatile Oil Systems For Use In Black Oil Material Balance Equation.

Design The Various Aspects Of Engineered Water-Drive In One And Two Dimensions, Capacities For Various Scenarios Of Water Injection Schemes And Water Cut Development, Calculations Of Water Injection Requirements And Corresponding Oil Recoveries.

Prepare Complete Spread Sheet Calculations For The Various Applications Of Material Balance Equation Including Pore Compaction Drive And To Handle Volatile Oil Systems.

PETE619.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE619 Advanced Petroleum Production Engineering
PETE619.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE619
In this course the function of the production engineering is envisioned in the context of well design, multi-stage separation, and recent advances in hydraulic fracturing. Advanced study of production operations, artificial lift methods, well problems and optimization well deliverability from vertical, horizontal and multilateral wells; multiphase flow modeling in wellbores and pipes.
Advanced Petroleum Production Engineering (PETE619) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Petroleum Production Engineering (PETE619) > Prerequisites
PETE419 with a minimum grade D
Advanced Petroleum Production Engineering (PETE619) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify two-phase-flow phenomena.

Design two-phase flow systems or conducting research in this area.

Apply mechanistic models to predict multi-phase flow in pipes.

Analyze deliverability of vertical, horizontal, and multilateral well trajectory.

Design multi-stage separation.

Create unified fracture design approach.

Prepare specialized working spread sheet to achieve specific tasks and present their research-oriented tasks.

PETE621.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE621 Non-Thermal EOR Methods
PETE621.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE621
New principles of recovery of oil and gas fields including use of polymer, gas-miscible, surfactant, and microbial processes with emphasis on the miscible flooding process. Phase behavior, first contact miscibility, multiple contact miscibility processes, predictive models and economic analysis, selection of candidate reservoirs; design and performance prediction of improved recovery floods.
Non-Thermal EOR Methods (PETE621) > Credit Hours : 3

Non-Thermal EOR Methods (PETE621) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Characterize The Reservoir, Identify The Appropriate Non-Thermal Eor Process, Determine Engineering Design Parameters, Conduct Pilot Or Field Tests As Needed And Finish With A Plan To Manage The Project.

Communicate Effectively In Writing And Orally.

Explore Into Advanced Literature And Contemporary Issues.

Identify And Understand The Fundamentals And Theory Of Non-Thermal Enhanced Oil Recovery Methods Such As; Polymer Flooding, Surfactant Flooding And Miscible Gas Flooding….Etc. And Application Of Fractional Flow Theory; Strategies And Displacement Performance Calculations.

Used Industrial-Standers Software Packages.

Work In Teams.

PETE625.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE625 Selected Topics in Petroleum Engineering
PETE625.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE625
Different selected topics in petroleum engineering selected to complement the student's program and approved by the Program Committee.
Selected Topics in Petroleum Engineering (PETE625) > Credit Hours : 3

Selected Topics in Petroleum Engineering (PETE625) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Individual Or Group Studies Of Advanced Topics At The Msc. Level. Selected Study Is Performed By Appointment With The Faculty.

PETE626.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE626 Advanced formation evaluation
PETE626.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE626
This course provides the student with a working knowledge of the current methodologies used in Geological description/analysis, Formation evaluation (the analysis/interpretation of well log data), and the analysis of well performance data (the design/analysis/interpretation of well test and production data).
Advanced formation evaluation (PETE626) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced formation evaluation (PETE626) > Prerequisites
PETE507 with a minimum grade C

PETE403 with a minimum grade C
Advanced formation evaluation (PETE626) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify components of a petroleum system, the organic sources of hydrocarbons processes of thermal maturation, primary and secondary migration, and hydrocarbon trapping; and types of self-sourcing reservoirs.

Explain the origin of structural features and stratigraphic traps, including folds, fractures, and traps; describe unconformities, the methods and tools used for structural evaluations and modeling.

Describe porosity-permeability relations in clastic and carbonate reservoirs; give examples of scalar effects on permeability determination, Logging operation surface, downhole equipment, Logging operation procedure, principles of operation and interpretation of the following logs: Density Spontaneous Potential, Sonic, Neutron, Gamma Ray and resistivity with the determination of saturation.

Establish the capability to integrate, analyze, and interpret well test and production data to characterize a reservoir in terms of reservoir properties and performance potential (field study project), methodologies for pressure drawdown and pressure buildup tests — for liquid, gas, and multiphase flow systems (i.e., "conventional" plots and type curve analysis. Production data analysis (rate-time or pressure-rate-time data) to obtain reservoir volume and estimates of reservoir properties for gas and liquid reservoir systems.

PETE627.title: UAEU Catalog — PETE627 Advanced Reservoir Simulation
PETE627.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2904.shtml?id=PETE627
This course provides advance numerical simulation of multiphase flow in heterogeneous porous media, with emphasis on advanced techniques based on numerical methods to develop flow equations, finite difference approximations their solution and applications to predict reservoir performance. Formulate discretization of partial differential equations combined with state-of-the-art linear and nonlinear solvers and well modeling and enhance students ability for self-learning through solving practical problems using a compositional oil reservoir simulator
Advanced Reservoir Simulation (PETE627) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Reservoir Simulation (PETE627) > Prerequisites
( PETE422 with a minimum grade C and ELEC600 with a minimum grade C)
Advanced Reservoir Simulation (PETE627) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop an in-depth understanding of current approaches to building models of flow in porous media and their numerical simulation (PLO1).

Describe the various difference methods which are used to solve the transport equations applied in reservoir simulation (PLO1, 2).

Recognize the limitations of traditional petroleum engineering numerical methods, their advantages and understand the methodology used to solve engineering problems using reservoir simulation (PLO1).

Describe the different linear equation solvers solution methods used in reservoir simulators (PLO1, 3, 7).

Argue for the consequence for stability and dispersion when applying reservoir simulation software (PLO1, 2, 4).

Acquire hands on experience with the industry-standard software package (Eclipse) (PLO1).

BCHM361.title: UAEU Catalog — BCHM361 Biochemistry I
BCHM361.text:
This course will cover the structure and function of different biological molecules, including proteins, carbohydrates, lipids and nucleic acids. Topics covered include living cells; chemical and physical properties of water and buffers; amino acids; sugars; nucleotides; levels of protein structure and stability; protein purification; introduction to steady-state kinetics; enzyme mechanism; controlling enzymatic activity and inhibition; glycolysis; pyruvate metabolism; the TCA cycle; electron flow and oxidative phosphorylation; fatty acid catabolism; structure of nucleic acids; DNA replication and DNA polymerase; transcription; translation and the genetic code. The experimental part provides students with a range of techniques and methodology including sequential configuration, chromatography and electrophoresis for the isolation, separation and characterization of biomolecules; protein determination and enzyme activity assays
Biochemistry I (BCHM361) > Credit Hours : 4

Biochemistry I (BCHM361) > Prerequisites
CHEM115 with a minimum grade D

CHEM241 with a minimum grade D
Biochemistry I (BCHM361) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the major biochemical molecules found in living cells.

Explain the four levels of protein structure.

Describe the kinetics, mechanism and role of enzymes in living systems.

Develop a strategy to purify specific proteins from bio-samples.

Predict the amount of energy (ATP) produced from the complete oxidative metabolism of lipids and carbohydrates.

Appreciate the relationship between biochemistry and genomics and proteomics.

Do literature search then perform electrophoresis and kinetics experiments independently or as a team in a safe manner and report and results using scientific writing.

BCHM362.title: UAEU Catalog — BCHM362 Biochemistry II
BCHM362.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=BCHM362
The aim of this course is to apply the basic knowledge gained in Biochemistry (CHEM 361) course to specific metabolic reactions and certain physiologically important biomolecules. The course covers bioenergetics, photosynthesis, regulation of carbohydrate metabolism, biosynthesis of glycoproteins, mechanisms of transport through membranes, immunoglobulins and immunity, blood clotting proteins, and biochemical communications.
Biochemistry II (BCHM362) > Credit Hours : 3

Biochemistry II (BCHM362) > Prerequisites
CHEM361
Biochemistry II (BCHM362) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Categorize Biological Membranes And Various Mechanisms Of Transport Of Molecules Through Membranes.

Compare Between Different Types Viruses And How They May Contribute To Some Forms Of Cancers.

Demonstrate An Understanding Of Various Aspects Of Cellular Signaling, Including Hormones And Second Messengers.

Draw And Explain The Reactions Involved In Photosynthesis And The Nitrogen Cycle Including Amino Acid Anabolism.

Explain The Basics Of Gene Cloning And Pcr.

Explain The Various Ways That Enzymes Can Be Regulated, Including Post-Translational Modifications Of Proteins And Their Degradation.

BCHM418.title: UAEU Catalog — BCHM418 Research Project
BCHM418.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=BCHM418
In this course, a student carries out a research project under the academic supervision of a faculty member in the Department. The aim of the course is to provide students with an opportunity (after a successful review of the chemical literature) to apply their biochemical knowledge and skills to an area of research without the restrictions of a planned practical. The course is offered to students who have a solid chemistry background, good laboratory skills and have an interest in scientific research. The student is expected to devote a set number of hours per week to research as discussed with his/her academic supervisor. At the end of the project, the student is required to submit a report on his/her research results, present a poster and give a short oral poster presentation based on his/her project.
Research Project (BCHM418) > Credit Hours : 3

Research Project (BCHM418) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Access chemical abstracts and other databases in order to review and carry out searches of the chemical literature.

Use a range of advanced research methods and/or analytical techniques using modern instrumentation or sophisticated computer programs.

Handle chemicals in the laboratory following strict safety codes of practice.

Analyze scientific data and interpret the overall findings of the project.

Produce a research report of high quality, conforming to the Department of Chemistry, UAE University guidelines for undergraduate research projects.

Present a short oral presentation on the research findings, using a range of computer packages.

BCHM462.title: UAEU Catalog — BCHM462 Clinical Biochemistry
BCHM462.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=BCHM462
The aim of this course is to enable students to understand and critically evaluate the pathophysiology and investigation of human disease by studying selected topics across the fields of Clinical Chemistry and Haematology. This course evaluates the contribution of laboratory investigations to the diagnosis, treatment and prevention of disease in key areas such as renal disease, diabetes, anaemia, and haematological malignancies.
Clinical Biochemistry (BCHM462) > Credit Hours : 3

Clinical Biochemistry (BCHM462) > Prerequisites
BCHM362 with a minimum grade D
Clinical Biochemistry (BCHM462) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify and evaluate critically the diagnostically useful changes which occur in normal body chemistry in selected examples of disease/trauma.

Demonstrate an in-depth understanding of the regulation of haemopoesis and haemoglobin production, and the interrelationships of the processes involved.

Determine the classification and investigation of haematological malignancy.

Retrieve literature and assess, select and apply the practical skills involved in the investigation of biochemical and haematological disease.

Interpret and evaluate the investigations that can aid the management of key examples of disease.

Evaluate the processes involved in the investigation of blood groups, and describe the techniques used in blood transfusion.

BCHM472.title: UAEU Catalog — BCHM472 Protein Structure and Function
BCHM472.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=BCHM472
The aim of this course is to study three principal aspects of proteins - physical properties, interaction with other biomolecules, and biochemical function - with an emphasis on levels of protein structure, folding conformation, biosynthesis, ribosome assembly, targeting, protein degradation, protein/DNA interactions and gene expression, membrane proteins and receptors, signal transduction, muscle action proteins.
Protein Structure and Function (BCHM472) > Credit Hours : 3

Protein Structure and Function (BCHM472) > Prerequisites
BCHM362 with a minimum grade D
Protein Structure and Function (BCHM472) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain primary, secondary and higher orders of protein structure and how sequence leads to structure (PLOs 1,4,5,6,7).

Describe how structure provides the basis for protein function (PLOs 1,2,4,5,6,7) .

Explain multiple strategies for cellular control of globular proteins (PLOs 1,2,4,5,6,7).

Describe functional and structural genomics strategies and applications (PLOs 1,4,5,6,7).

Investigate protein structure problems using visualization software and modeling tools (PLOs 1,3,5,6,7).

BCHM483.title: UAEU Catalog — BCHM483 Special Topics in Biochemistry I
BCHM483.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=BCHM483
This course aims to cover selected topics dealing with the recent advances in the field of genomics (genes related issues) and proteomics (protein related issues). The course will also discuss the current knowledge on cellular signal transduction, and link it with the actions of hormones, clinical biochemistry, as well as some types of cancer. Special attention will be paid to nuclear hormone receptor and G-protein coupled receptor signaling pathways. Students will be required to read up on primary literature and make an oral presentation to the whole class on a chosen topic.
Special Topics in Biochemistry I (BCHM483) > Credit Hours : 3

Special Topics in Biochemistry I (BCHM483) > Prerequisites
BCHM362 with a minimum grade D
Special Topics in Biochemistry I (BCHM483) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain topics in genomics-based research.

Explain topics in proteomics-based research.

Retrieve information relevant to genomics and proteomics from scientific literature.

Write scientific content in a clear and concise manner in the form of an abstract.

Prepare and deliver a PowerPoint presentation on a chosen course topic.

Evaluate oral presentations made by their colleagues in a critical manner.

BCHM484.title: UAEU Catalog — BCHM484 Special Topics in Biochemistry II
BCHM484.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=BCHM484
This course aims to cover selected topics that are not discussed in other courses but are of current importance such as effects of environmental pollutant on biochemical metabolism, drug and antibiotic metabolism, antibodies and immunochemistry, biotransformation and detoxification.
Special Topics in Biochemistry II (BCHM484) > Credit Hours : 3

Special Topics in Biochemistry II (BCHM484) > Prerequisites
BCHM362 with a minimum grade D
Special Topics in Biochemistry II (BCHM484) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognize the basis of 3D structures of proteins and how they relate to their biological functions.

Describe how reactive oxygen species can intracellular biological molecules

Explain and summarize basics of environmental and biochemical toxicology.

Explain the various modes of cellular signaling that is used in biological systems.

Research, organize and prepare professional PowerPoint presentation on a chosen topic.

CHEM111.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM111 General Chemistry I
CHEM111.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM111
Matter and measurement. Atoms, molecules and ions. Chemical stoichiometry. Acids-Bases and oxidation-reduction reactions. Oxidation numbers and the balancing of equations. The electronic structure of atoms and the periodic table of elements. Periodic properties of the elements. Basic concepts of chemical bonding and molecular geometry. Gases. Intermolecular forces. Solubility and Concentration units.
General Chemistry I (CHEM111) > Credit Hours : 3

General Chemistry I (CHEM111) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe matter, its properties and naming of compounds.

Perform stoichiometric calculations including those related to gases, and solution concentrations.

Describe the atomic structure of elements and their properties based on their position in the Periodic Table.

Describe the basic types of chemical bonding, ionic and covalent.

Predict some chemical and physical properties using the Periodic Table, molecular geometry and/or intermolecular forces.

Understand the ideal gas law and its application.

CHEM112.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM112 General Chemistry II for Non Major
CHEM112.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM112
Thermochemistry. Reactions in aqueous solutions. Gaseous equilibrium. Acids and bases. Ionic equilibria. Qualitative analysis. Electrochemistry. Rates of reactions.
General Chemistry II for Non Major (CHEM112) > Credit Hours : 2

General Chemistry II for Non Major (CHEM112) > Prerequisites
CHEM111 with a minimum grade D
General Chemistry II for Non Major (CHEM112) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply The Theories And Concepts Introduced In The Course To Solve Problems, Perform Calculations, And Improve Critical Thinking Skills

Explain The Fundamental Concepts Of Equilibria And Apply These To Gases, And Solutions, To Deduce Various Properties Such As Equilibrium Constant, Dissociation Of Weak Acids, Buffering Action And Solubility Of Sparingly Soluble Salts.

Explain The Principles Of Thermochemistry And Its Application To Various Systems

Integrate The Various Concepts Developed In This Course To Evaluate Solutions To Chemical Problems In A Logical And Coherent Way

Recognize The Concepts Of Spontaneity And Reversibility Of Reaction, Entropy, Free Energy And Be Able To Calculate These Using Tabulated Values

Recognize The Various Terms Used In Chemical Kinetics , Such As Order Of Reaction, Rate Constant And Activation Energy And The Mathematical Relationships Between Them

CHEM113.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM113 General Chemistry II
CHEM113.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM113
The main concepts covered in this course include the thermochemistry and thermodynamics of chemical reactions, the kinetics of chemical reactions, and the principles of chemical equilibrium, the equilibrium involving acids and bases, and additional aspects of aqueous equilibria with emphasis on solubility equilibrium. This course also covers principles of electrochemistry and a brief discussion of colligative properties.
General Chemistry II (CHEM113) > Credit Hours : 3

General Chemistry II (CHEM113) > Prerequisites
CHEM111 with a minimum grade D
General Chemistry II (CHEM113) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the principles of thermochemistry, and thermodynamics and solve their relevant problems.

Recognize the various terms used in chemical kinetics, such as order of reaction, rate constant and activation energy, and the mathematical relationships between them.

Explain and describe the concepts of equilibria, acid-base equilibria, solubility equilibria and buffer solutions and to be able to solve problems relevant to these concepts.

Outline the principles of colligative properties and electrochemistry and solve their relevant problems.

CHEM115.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM115 General Chemistry Lab
CHEM115.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM115
Introduction to the elementary laboratory techniques. It includes principles of chemical calculations, techniques of qualitative analysis with special emphasis on applications of chemical equilibria.
General Chemistry Lab (CHEM115) > Credit Hours : 1

General Chemistry Lab (CHEM115) > Prerequisites
CHEM113 with a minimum grade D or CHEM112 with a minimum grade D
General Chemistry Lab (CHEM115) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Find and interpret information regarding chemical hazards (MSDS) and handle chemicals appropriately.

Conduct experiments using basic chemistry laboratory glassware and equipment.

Analyze data from experiments using spreadsheets and graphical approaches.

Apply basic chemical knowledge to predict and explain experimental observations.

Write reports summarizing experimental findings.

CHEM175.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM175 Chemistry Lab I for Engineering
CHEM175.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM175
Chemistry Lab 1 for Engineering is an introduction to elementary laboratory techniques. It includes the principles of chemistry calculations, techniques of quantitative and qualitative analysis.
Chemistry Lab I for Engineering (CHEM175) > Credit Hours : 1

Chemistry Lab I for Engineering (CHEM175) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co CHEM111
Chemistry Lab I for Engineering (CHEM175) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze Data From Experiments Using Spreadsheets And Graphical Approaches

Apply Basic Chemical Knowledge To Predict And Explain Experimental Observations

Conduct Experiments Properly And Safely Using Basic Chemistry Laboratory Glassware And Equipment

Handle Properly The Basic Laboratory Tools And Glassware

Write Reports Summarizing Experimental Findings

CHEM181.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM181 Chemistry in the Modern World
CHEM181.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM181
The role of chemistry in important issues of modern life is examined including the economic, social, health and ecological impact of chemistry. Chemical concepts are presented through examining various topics such as environment, ecology, nutrition and health.
Chemistry in the Modern World (CHEM181) > Credit Hours : 3

Chemistry in the Modern World (CHEM181) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe contemporary scientific issues.

Describe the relationship between chemistry and other disciplines.

Explain the role of this chemistry in natural and technological phenomena observed in everyday life.

Identify the role of scientific inquiry and scientific research in solving problem and providing better life.

CHEM222.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM222 Analytical Chemistry
CHEM222.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM222
The course introduces to students the fundamental aspects of analytical chemistry. It deals with various classical analytical chemistry methods that include volumetric and gravimetric analysis. Volumetric methods cover acid-base reactions, complexmetric, redox and precipitation reactions. The course also introduces students to various types of errors in chemical analysis and methods of their evaluations. Kinetic methods of analysis, non-chromatographic separation, and sample preparation will be also discussed. Applications to selected real analytical problems such as pharmaceutical analysis will be discussed. The associated laboratory experiments provide experience in applying these methods in chemical determinations
Analytical Chemistry (CHEM222) > Credit Hours : 4

Analytical Chemistry (CHEM222) > Prerequisites
CHEM113 with a minimum grade D

CHEM115 with a minimum grade D
Analytical Chemistry (CHEM222) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Differentiate between qualitative and quantitative analysis and between classical and instrumental analysis.

Describe the principles of classical and instrumental methods of analysis.

Apply statistics to analytical data and use excel in chemical analysis

Solve problems related to volumetric, gravimetric, spectrophotometric and chromatographic methods of analysis.

Analyze real samples using classical and instrumental methods.

Complete assigned tasks by self-reliance, discipline and responsibility

CHEM231.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM231 Inorganic Chemistry I
CHEM231.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM231
This course involves topics in basic inorganic chemistry which cover the structure and bonding in molecules, the chemistry of the oxoanions and oxoacids, solvents, solutions, acids and bases and the chemistry of selected main group elements and their associated compounds. The course covers the following areas explicitly: the structure of atoms, atomic orbitals in wave mechanics; periodic properties of the elements; structure and bonding in molecules: introduction, molecular orbital theory: homo and heteronuclear diatomics, polyatomics, multicentre MO, electron-deficient molecules, ?-donor and acceptor ligands; elements of symmetry, symmetry operations and point group symmetry determination; ionic solids: lattice and close-packing concepts, ionic radii, lattice energy calculations and correlation to properties solubility, hardness etc.; metallic substances: metallic bonding, band theory, conductivity, semiconductors, insulators, defects, preparation of new materials through doping, metallurgy; solvents, solutions, acids and bases; chemistry of the main-group elements.
Inorganic Chemistry I (CHEM231) > Credit Hours : 3

Inorganic Chemistry I (CHEM231) > Prerequisites
CHEM113 with a minimum grade D or CHEM112 with a minimum grade D
Inorganic Chemistry I (CHEM231) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Construct Mo Energy Level Diagrams And Be Able To Extract Bonding Information Characteristics Of Molecules From Them.

Define And Explain Different Models Of Acid-Base Theory In Aqueous And Non-Aqueous Media.

Describe Bonding In Inorganic Solids Such As Ionic Compounds, Metals And Semiconductors.

Explain The Atomic Structure Based On Quantum Mechanics And Explain Periodic Properties Of The Atoms.

Use The Group Theory To Recognize And Assign Symmetry Characteristics Of Molecules, And To Predict The Appearance Of A Molecule’S Spectra As A Function Of Symmetry And Chirality.

CHEM241.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM241 Organic Chemistry I
CHEM241.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM241
Introduction to organic chemistry. Nomenclature, isomerism, sources, methods of preparation, physical properties, reactions and mechanisms of: alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, alicyclic hydrocarbons, alkyl halides, alcohols and ethers. Stereochemistry and optical activity. IR and UV-Vis spectroscopy.
Organic Chemistry I (CHEM241) > Credit Hours : 3

Organic Chemistry I (CHEM241) > Prerequisites
CHEM111 with a minimum grade D
Organic Chemistry I (CHEM241) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Classify Organic Compounds

Deduce Functional Groups Of Compounds Based On Their Spectroscopic Data

Describe The Fundamentals Of Carbon Chemistry

Draw And Interpret 3D Structures Of Stereoisomers

Explain Reactions Of Simple Organic Compounds And Their Reaction Mechanism Based On The Fundamental Concepts Of Acid-Base Chemistry Nucleophiles And Electrophiles

Name Properly Different Organic Compounds

CHEM242.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM242 Organic Chemistry II
CHEM242.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM242
Nomenclature, methods of preparation. Physical properties. Reactions and mechanisms of the following organic compounds: aldehydes, ketones, carboxylic acids, esters, amides, anhydrides and other acid derivatives and aromatic compounds. Introduction to carbohydrates, proteins and lipids. Introduction to NMR spectroscopy and mass spectrometry.
Organic Chemistry II (CHEM242) > Credit Hours : 3

Organic Chemistry II (CHEM242) > Prerequisites
CHEM241 with a minimum grade D
Organic Chemistry II (CHEM242) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze Reactions/Compounds Using Different Spectroscopic Techniques.

Apply The Mechanistic Theory To Propose Reaction Mechanisms.

Design Syntheses Of Simple Organic Compounds.

Distinguish And Explain The Physical Property Differences Of Organic Compounds.

Identify The Structural Formulas And Iupac Names Of Organic Compounds.

Predict Products For Most Important Organic Reactions.

CHEM245.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM245 Organic Chemistry Lab I
CHEM245.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM245
Characterization of some organic compounds using physical and spectroscopic techniques, study of the chemical properties of some aliphatic and aromatic compounds containing functional groups.
Organic Chemistry Lab I (CHEM245) > Credit Hours : 1

Organic Chemistry Lab I (CHEM245) > Prerequisites
CHEM115 with a minimum grade D
Organic Chemistry Lab I (CHEM245) > Corequisites
CHEM241
Organic Chemistry Lab I (CHEM245) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Characterize Organic Substances By Physical And Spectroscopic Methods.

Engage In Safe Laboratory Practices While Handling Laboratory Glassware, Equipment And Chemical Reagents.

Practice Simple Techniques Such As Distillation, Separation, And Crystallization.

Prepare Experimental Reports Using Notational And Descriptive Content Including Msds Information On Relevant Chemical Reactions.

CHEM251.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM251 Physical Chemistry I
CHEM251.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM251
The First law of thermodynamics. Thermo-chemistry, Second law of thermodynamics. Entropy and free energy. Third law of thermodynamics. Absolute zero. Chemical potential. Phase equilibria. Statistical thermodynamics.
Physical Chemistry I (CHEM251) > Credit Hours : 3

Physical Chemistry I (CHEM251) > Prerequisites
MATH105 with a minimum grade D

( CHEM113 with a minimum grade D or CHEM112 with a minimum grade D)
Physical Chemistry I (CHEM251) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe The Laws Of Thermodynamics, And The Relationships Between Them, And Apply Thermodynamics Equations In Describing And Analyzing A Particular System And Binary Solutions.

Explain The Difference Between Ideal And Real Behavior Of Gasses And Solutions, And The Principles Of Heat Transfer Between Systems And Surroundings, And The Conservation Of Energy.

Extend The Principles Of Thermodynamics And Free Energies To Predict And Determine The Direction Of A Spontaneous Process.

Interpret The Formation Of Simple Mixtures Using Thermodynamcs.

Utilize Thermodynamic Relations To Study Simple Phase Diagrams, Phase Stability, And Phase Boundary.

CHEM270.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM270 Materials Science
CHEM270.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM270
