This course aims at studying basic concepts and fundamentals of material science and engineering in order to develop the understanding that how structure, properties, and processing relationships are established and used for different types of materials. Topics covered are bonding, internal micro-and macro structure, crystallography, material defect; mechanical, thermal, electrical, magnetic, and optical properties of materials; strengthening mechanisms and failure analysis; micro-structural design of materials. An application module is introduced where a software (JMatPro®) is used for calculations related to phase diagrams and anticipated Materials Properties.
Materials Science (CHEM270) > Credit Hours : 3

Materials Science (CHEM270) > Prerequisites
CHEM111 with a minimum grade D

CHEM175 with a minimum grade D
Materials Science (CHEM270) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the structure of various types of materials.

Describe sources of defects and imperfections in materials.

Relate phase transformations to processing of materials.

Describe types of processing techniques as related to the structure and application of materials.

Explain different properties of materials and establish structure-property relationships in various types of materials.

CHEM282.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM282 Organic Chemistry for Non-Majors
CHEM282.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM282
Introduction to structure. Nomenclature. Physical properties. Preparation, reactions of hydrocarbons and functional groups containing organic compounds. The laboratory component includes the purification, isolation, characterization and study of the properties of typical organic compounds.
Organic Chemistry for Non-Majors (CHEM282) > Credit Hours : 3

Organic Chemistry for Non-Majors (CHEM282) > Prerequisites
CHEM111 with a minimum grade D

CHEM115 with a minimum grade D
Organic Chemistry for Non-Majors (CHEM282) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss Some Of Organic Reactions With Describing Its Industrial Applications

Engage In Laboratory Safety Practices, Handling Glassware, Equipment And Chemical Reagents.

Identify Organic Compounds According To Their Functional Groups

Name Organic Compounds Of Intermediate Complexity According To Iupac Nomenclature

Practice Simple Techniques And Prepare Experimental Reports With Complete Characterization By Physical And Spectroscopic Methods.

Understand Basic Bonding Principles In Organic Chemistry

CHEM283.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM283 Biochemistry for Non-Majors
CHEM283.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM283
The chemical and physical properties of biological compounds. Theories of enzyme action and the factors affecting them. The practical component includes the isolation and study of biological properties of some biological compounds.
Biochemistry for Non-Majors (CHEM283) > Credit Hours : 3

Biochemistry for Non-Majors (CHEM283) > Prerequisites
CHEM282 with a minimum grade D
Biochemistry for Non-Majors (CHEM283) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Appreciate the amount of energy (ATP) produced from the metabolism of lipids and carbohydrates

Describe the major biochemical molecules of living cells

Describe the mechanism and role of enzymes in living systems

Design and execute biochemical experiments and express observations and results using scientific writing

Explain the four levels of protein structure

Use laboratory tools, equipment and chemicals in a safe and ethical way

CHEM321.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM321 Instrumental Analysis I
CHEM321.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM321
This course aims primarily at developing the fundamental understanding of theory and applications of instrumental analytical techniques. The topics covered include spectrochemical, electrochemical and chromatographic techniques. The associated laboratory practical component provides extensive experience in applying these techniques to the chemical analysis of different samples.
Instrumental Analysis I (CHEM321) > Credit Hours : 4

Instrumental Analysis I (CHEM321) > Prerequisites
CHEM221 with a minimum grade D
Instrumental Analysis I (CHEM321) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Complete Assigned Tasks By Self-Reliance, Discipline And Responsibility

Determine A Proper Instrumental Technique For A Given Analytical Problem

Explain The Operating Principles Of The Basic Atomic, Molecular And Electro Analytical Instrumentations

Perform Standard Instrumental Laboratory Procedures

Recognize The Performance Characteristics Of Different Analytical Techniques And Their Potentials And Limitations

Retrieve Information Relevant To Instrumental Analysis From Scientific Literature

CHEM331.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM331 Inorganic Chemistry II
CHEM331.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM331
This course introduces the basic principles of coordination chemistry involving the following areas: introduction, chemical nomenclature, stereochemistry and isomerism of coordination compounds; theories of bonding in coordination compounds; the Jahn-Teller Effect; magnetic properties of transition metal complexes; electronic spectroscopy, term symbols and the spectrochemical series; thermodynamic aspects: formation constants, hydration enthalpies, ligand field stabilization energies, chelate effects; tautomerism, stereochemical nonrigidity and fluxionality; synthesis and types of reactions of complexes; lanthanides and actinides; mechanisms of inorganic reactions.
Inorganic Chemistry II (CHEM331) > Credit Hours : 3

Inorganic Chemistry II (CHEM331) > Prerequisites
CHEM231 with a minimum grade D
Inorganic Chemistry II (CHEM331) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply Nomenclature Rules To Name Coordination Compound.

Describe Bonding In Coordination Compounds Using Modern And Classical Theories Of Bonding Including Valence Bond Theory, Crystal Field Theory And Molecular Orbital Theory.

Describe The Geometries And Different Possible Types Of Isomerism In Complexes.

Explain And Interpret Electronic Spectra Of Complexes.

Outline Common Reactions Of Coordination Compounds.

Predict Magnet Properties Of Complexes.

CHEM332.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM332 Chemistry of Elements
CHEM332.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM332
This course covers fundamental properties of main group elements and their compounds. Concepts related to main group elements discussed in this course include extraction methods, structures, properties, and reactivity. The course also briefly covers the coordination and organometallic chemistry of s- and p-block elements. Selected inorganic materials of the d-block elements and their technological applications will be also discussed with emphasis on nanomaterials.
Chemistry of Elements (CHEM332) > Credit Hours : 3

Chemistry of Elements (CHEM332) > Prerequisites
CHEM231 with a minimum grade D
Chemistry of Elements (CHEM332) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the occurrence and extraction’s methods of the main group elements.

Compare the physical and chemical properties of the elements in Groups 1, 2 and 13-18.

Identify the structures and reactivity’s trends of the main group elements compounds including organometallic complexes.

Outline the main industrial and technological applications of the main group elements and their compounds including organometallic complexes.

CHEM337.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM337 Practical Inorganic Chemistry
CHEM337.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM337
This practical course covers the preparation and identification of a variety of main group and transition metallic compounds. The experiments include important inorganic synthetic techniques and methods of spectroscopic characterization.
Practical Inorganic Chemistry (CHEM337) > Credit Hours : 1

Practical Inorganic Chemistry (CHEM337) > Prerequisites
CHEM321 with a minimum grade D

CHEM331 with a minimum grade D
Practical Inorganic Chemistry (CHEM337) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply Theoretical Principles To Perform And Interpret Experiments In Inorganic Chemistry.

Carry Out Practical Or Project Work Effectively And Safely, Working Both Independently Or As Part Of A Team, Using Proper Safety Procedures Throughout.

Demonstrate Skills In Preparing, Handling, Purifying, And Analyzing Inorganic Compounds. (Suggest To Prephrase: Prepare, Handle, Purify, And Analyze Inorganiz Compounds)

Perform Accurate Characterization For Metal Complexes By Combining The Data Collected From Analytical, Spectroscopic, Thermal And Magnetic Techniques.

Write Reports Describing Experimental Methods And Discussing Results In An Appropriate Format And Style.

CHEM345.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM345 Organic Chemistry Lab II
CHEM345.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM345
This experimental course covers multiple step syntheses of selected organic compounds and the characterization of their functional groups by spectroscopic analysis.
Organic Chemistry Lab II (CHEM345) > Credit Hours : 1

Organic Chemistry Lab II (CHEM345) > Prerequisites
CHEM245 with a minimum grade D
Organic Chemistry Lab II (CHEM345) > Corequisites
CHEM242
Organic Chemistry Lab II (CHEM345) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Characterize Prepared Samples By Physical And Spectroscopic Methods

Engage In Safe Laboratory Practices While Handling Laboratory Glassware, Equipment And Chemical Reagents

Perform Standard Synthesis Techniques Including Purification

Prepare Experimental Reports Using Notational And Descriptive Content Including Msds Information On Relevant Chemical Reactions

CHEM351.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM351 Physical Chemistry II
CHEM351.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM351
This course covers two areas of physical chemistry, namely kinetics and quantum mechanics. The first part deals with chemical kinetics and the topics include the study of rate of chemical reactions and of the molecular processes by which the reaction occurs, differential and integral expressions with emphasis on multi-step as well as single-step first-order phenomena, expressing mechanisms in rate laws, consecutive elementary reactions, steady state approximation, and reactions approaching equilibrium, The second part deals quantum mechanics and the topics included are fundamental principles of quantum theory, such as Schrodinger equation, wave functions, quantum mechanical operators, quantum mechanics of a particle-in-a-box model, vibrational motion, rotational motion, and hydrogenic atoms.
Physical Chemistry II (CHEM351) > Credit Hours : 3

Physical Chemistry II (CHEM351) > Prerequisites
CHEM251 with a minimum grade D
Physical Chemistry II (CHEM351) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply the concepts of chemical kinetics to calculate reaction rates, temperature dependence of rate constants and relate that to activation energy in addition to emphasis on collision theory activation rate theory.

Illustrate the mathematical formulation of reactions approaching equilibrium and the variety of complex reactions and their mechanisms

Explain the origin of quantum mechanics: energy quantization, uncertainty principle, and wave-particle duality.

Explain various models to represent translational, vibrational, rotational, and electronic transitions in one- and many-electron atoms

CHEM355.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM355 Physical Chemistry Lab I
CHEM355.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM355
The main objective of this course is to provide students with the necessary training on the use of modern techniques and instrumentation in thermodynamics, electrochemistry, kinetics and surface chemistry.
Physical Chemistry Lab I (CHEM355) > Credit Hours : 1

Physical Chemistry Lab I (CHEM355) > Prerequisites
CHEM115 with a minimum grade D

( CHEM251 with a minimum grade D or ( CHME322 with a minimum grade D and GENG220 with a minimum grade D)
Physical Chemistry Lab I (CHEM355) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze Statistical Data Using Software’S Such As Excel, Prosim, Etc.

Comply With The Safety And Hygiene Precautions.

Describe The Behavior Of Bulk Materials At The Most Fundamental Level

Identify Some Physical Phenomena In Nature And Industry Through Performing Relevant Experiments And Using Laboratory Chemical Models And Instruments.

Relate Theoretical Concepts To Real Experiments Such As Ideality, Partial Molar Volume, And Physical Changes Such As To Construct Phase Diagram.

CHEM356.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM356 Physical Chemistry Lab II
CHEM356.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM356
This course involves experimental and computational techniques in physical chemistry. The course contents include: infrared and visible-ultraviolet spectroscopic experiments for chemical analysis, identification of molecular structure, determination of molecular geometry, and chemical kinetics; molecular modeling and simulations; computational chemistry, which includes quantum mechanical and semi-empirical methods.
Physical Chemistry Lab II (CHEM356) > Credit Hours : 1

Physical Chemistry Lab II (CHEM356) > Prerequisites
CHEM355 with a minimum grade D

Pre/Co CHEM351 with a minimum grade D
Physical Chemistry Lab II (CHEM356) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply Basic Principles And Methodologies Of Kinetics, Thermodynamics, Thermochemistry, Spectroscopy And Surface Chemistry

Measure Physical Quantities To Predict The Behavior Of Chemical Systems Based On Physical Laws, And To Select And Evaluate Appropriate Techniques And Instrumentation

Practice The Proper Procedures And Regulations For Safe Handling And Use Of Chemicals.

Use Computers In Data Acquisition And Processing And Use Available Software As A Tool In Data Analysis

CHEM377.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM377 Instrumental Analysis for Chemical Engineering
CHEM377.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM377
The course deals with the fundamental concepts and applications of instrumental techniques in chemical analysis. The course covers some atomic and molecular spectroscopic tecniques as well as chromatographic methods of analysis.
Instrumental Analysis for Chemical Engineering (CHEM377) > Credit Hours : 1

Instrumental Analysis for Chemical Engineering (CHEM377) > Prerequisites
CHEM112 with a minimum grade D or CHEM113 with a minimum grade D
Instrumental Analysis for Chemical Engineering (CHEM377) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the basic concepts and working principles of some modern analytical instruments.

Identify the potentials and limitations of different instrumental analytical techniques.

Select s proper instrumental analytical technique for solving a given analytical problem.

Solve problems through using Instrumental analysis.

CHEM418.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM418 Research Project
CHEM418.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM418
In this course, a student carries out a short research project under the academic supervision of a faculty member in the Department. The aim of the course is to provide students with an opportunity after a successful review of the chemical literature to apply their chemical knowledge and skills to an area of research without the restrictions of a planned practical. The student is expected to devote a set number of hours per week to research as discussed with his or her academic supervisor. At the end of the project, the student must submit a report on his/her research results, present a poster and give a short oral presentation based on the work.
Research Project (CHEM418) > Credit Hours : 3

Research Project (CHEM418) > Prerequisites
CHEM337 with a minimum grade D

CHEM345 with a minimum grade D

BCHM361 with a minimum grade D

Pre/Co CHEM356
Research Project (CHEM418) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Access Chemical Abstracts And Other Databases In Order To Review And Carry Out Searches Of The Chemical Literature

Be Capable Of Using A Range Of Advanced Methods Of Synthesis, Analytical Techniques Using Modern Instrumentation Or Sophisticated Computer Programs

Handle Chemicals In The Laboratory Following Strict Safety Codes Of Practice

Present A Short Oral Presentation On The Research Findings, Using A Range Of Computer Packages, E.G. Powerpoint, Molecular Graphics, Two-Dimensional Chemical Drawing Programs, The Internet, Excel Etc And Present A Poster On The Project And Interpret The Findings Of The Research Project, To Faculty And Fellow Students Working In The Field

Produce A Research Report Of High Quality, Conforming To The Department Of Chemistry, Uae University Guidelines For Undergraduate Research Projects

Statistically Analyze Scientific Data And Interpret The Overall Findings Of The Project

CHEM419.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM419 Internship
CHEM419.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM419
The student spends 8 weeks of training in an approved training site. (This course is conducted over half a semester (8 weeks) during the third year of study. Offered condensed courses should be taken during the other half of the semester).
Internship (CHEM419) > Credit Hours : 6

Internship (CHEM419) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Appreciate The Central Role Of Chemistry In Different Disciplines.

Complete Assigned Tasks Assigned By Site Supervisor By Self-Reliance, Discipline And Responsibility.

Explain And Summarize Chemical Analysis Procedures Followed At The Internship Place.

Interpret Different Types Of Laboratory Data Such As Spectra, Chromatograms, And Thermograms.

Write Clear And Concise Weekly And Final Reports And Prepare And Present Professional Presentation On Their Training Experience.

CHEM422.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM422 Instrumental Analysis II
CHEM422.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM422
This is a theoretical course aims to introduce students to the fundamentals aspects, general principles and analytical applications of atomic and molecular mass spectrometry, infrared spectroscopy, nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, atomic X-ray spectrometry and hyphenated techniques. Moreover, an introduction to surface analytical techniques as well as automation in analytical laboratories will be discussed.
Instrumental Analysis II (CHEM422) > Credit Hours : 3

Instrumental Analysis II (CHEM422) > Prerequisites
CHEM321 with a minimum grade D
Instrumental Analysis II (CHEM422) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the basic principles and theories of instrumental methods covered in this course.

Choose and Justify the utilization of adequate technique in addressing a particular analytical problem.

Assess the quality of results of chemical analyses and Interpret different types of output signals

Retrieve information relevant to instrumental analysis from scientific literature.

Plan systematic approaches to apply instrumental analysis in solving real world analytical problems using complex matrices.

Complete assigned tasks by self-reliance, discipline and responsibility.

CHEM423.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM423 Environmental Chemistry
CHEM423.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM423
Environmental chemistry is the chemistry of the natural processes in air, water, and soil. It is concerned principally with the chemical aspects of problems created by human beings in the natural environment. Environmental analytical chemistry deals with separation and identification of countless complex biological, environmental and industrial samples. The two topics are highly important for the conservation of the earth's environment and makes it suitable for the coexistence of all living organisms. This course introduces students to the concepts of environmental chemistry and environmental analytical chemistry. The course deals with topics like toxic chemicals, pollution prevention, properties of water and waters bodies, fundamentals of aquatic acid base chemistry, atmospheric chemistry, atmosphere and hazardous substances, hazardous wastes and their effects on living organisms, stratospheric chemistry, ozone layer, air analysis, water analysis and speciation analysis. The course will also discuss different methods used for analyzing environmental samples.
Environmental Chemistry (CHEM423) > Credit Hours : 3

Environmental Chemistry (CHEM423) > Prerequisites
CHEM321 with a minimum grade D
Environmental Chemistry (CHEM423) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate knowledge about the chemistry of natural and industrial processes affecting the environment.

Integrate information from different disciplines to assess the effects of human’s development on environment.

Describe the physical and chemical principles underlying environmental phenomena.

Describe how pollutants are transported, accumulated and affects the environment.

Identify the proper approach for developing analytical protocols to quantify environmental pollutants and solving problems in environment.

Use writing and presentation skills to express environmental information.

CHEM441.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM441 Polymer and Petroleum Chemistry
CHEM441.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM441
This course introduces students to polymer chemistry, polymerization reaction mechanisms (step-growth polymerization and chain-growth polymerization via radical and ionic intermediates), methods for molecular weight determinations and characterization of polymers. It will also briefly introduce students to petroleum chemistry, refining operation, and petrochemicals as the raw material for all petro-plastics and its future impact on the polymer manufacturing industry.
Polymer and Petroleum Chemistry (CHEM441) > Credit Hours : 3

Polymer and Petroleum Chemistry (CHEM441) > Prerequisites
CHEM242 with a minimum grade D or BCHM362 with a minimum grade D
Polymer and Petroleum Chemistry (CHEM441) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the relationships between polymer chemistry and petroleum chemistry

Recognize the basic concepts of polymer chain architecture, classifications, structure and morphology.

Describe various methods for the synthesis, molecular weight, and characterization of polymers.

Identify petrochemicals that are related to the polymer industry.

Describe the refining, reforming, cracking, alkylation, polymerization, and separation processes of products and petrochemicals

Apply the general quality control testing and characterization procedures on some petroleum and petrochemical products used as monomers in polymers’ synthesis and manufacturing.

CHEM442.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM442 Introduction to Medicinal Chemistry
CHEM442.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM442
This course introduces students to the field of medicinal chemistry, as a highly interdisciplinary science which combines organic chemistry, biochemistry, pharmacology, molecular, and cellular biology, along with aspects of computational chemistry to design, and develop useful chemical agents with therapeutic utility against disease. It will focus on introducing the foundations of medicinal chemistry, the process of drug design, discovery, and clinical development, along with teaching students core concepts such as pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics (ADMET), drug metabolism (phase I, II), pro-drugs, and target classes. The course introduces the role of AI and machine learning in modern drug discovery, including applications in hit identification, SAR prediction, and lead optimization (e.g., AlphaFold, Boltz, SwissADME, DeepChem, Chemistry42). The importance of synthetic organic chemistry to drug discovery also represents an overarching theme across the course, and students will develop an understanding of organic functional groups, and their role in the clinical success of a drug candidate along with an ability to analyse/summarize current medicinal chemistry literature.
Introduction to Medicinal Chemistry (CHEM442) > Credit Hours : 3

Introduction to Medicinal Chemistry (CHEM442) > Prerequisites
CHEM242 with a minimum grade D

BCHM361 with a minimum grade D
Introduction to Medicinal Chemistry (CHEM442) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate the basic concepts of medicinal chemistry.

Classify drugs based on their physical concepts.

Recognize the difference between prodrugs, drugs and drug toxicity.

Recognize the importance of organic chemistry in the drug's design and its applications in the field of medicinal chemistry.

Understand the process of drug synthesis

CHEM446.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM446 Spectroscopic Identification of Compounds
CHEM446.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM446
This course is designed to equip student with the basic knowledge and techniques for elucidating structures of organic compounds. Modern spectroscopic techniques such as ultraviolet/visible spectrometry, mass spectrometry, infrared spectroscopy, nuclear magnetic resonance spectrometry will be discussed for the identification and quantification of organic compounds. The course also teaches students proper sample handling, instrument use and interpretation of spectra. On successful completion of this course, students will be able to deduce structures of unknown simple organic molecules.
Spectroscopic Identification of Compounds (CHEM446) > Credit Hours : 3

Spectroscopic Identification of Compounds (CHEM446) > Prerequisites
CHEM242 with a minimum grade D

CHEM321 with a minimum grade D
Spectroscopic Identification of Compounds (CHEM446) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the basic principles and ideas for modern spectroscopic techniques their use in structural determinations of organic compounds.

Apply the principles of spectroscopic methods for the identification of simple organic compounds.

Write independent reports.

Comply to safety rules in handling chemicals and operate instruments.

CHEM453.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM453 Electrochemistry
CHEM453.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM453
The course is intended to cover the principles of electrochemistry and its applications; topics such as ionic interaction, conducting properties of electrolytes, interfacial phenomena and double layer, thermodynamics and kinetics of electrochemical reactions and electrode processes (kinetics), and applications. Applications include Pourbaix diagrams and their constructions, fuel cells, re-chargeable batteries, and corrosion.
Electrochemistry (CHEM453) > Credit Hours : 3

Electrochemistry (CHEM453) > Prerequisites
CHEM251 with a minimum grade D or ( CHEM113 with a minimum grade D and CHME322 with a minimum grade D)
Electrochemistry (CHEM453) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain concepts and terms related to electrochemical reactions and cells

Demonstrate basic knowledge of ionic interaction, conductivity, interface, thermodynamics, and kinetics of electrochemical reactions.

Derive basic equations related to electrolytes and electrochemical systems, including salt activity, conductivity, Nernst equation, and the Butler-Volmer equation.

Apply basic laws and equations to electrochemical systems.

Calculate quantities related to activity, activity coefficient, molar conductivity, solubility, equilibrium constant, surface tension, Ecell, and reaction rates.

CHEM454.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM454 Nuclear and Radiation Chemistry
CHEM454.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM454
This course covers topics like radioactivity, nuclear structure, stability and properties, radioactive decay, nuclear transformations, nuclear reactions, sources of ionizing radiation, detection and measurement of nuclear radiation, nuclear reactors, application of radioactive substances in various fields, nuclear waste disposal, fundamentals of radiation chemistry, radiation chemical yield, chemical dosimetry and effects of radiation on matters such as gases, water, aqueous solutions, organic liquids and solids.
Nuclear and Radiation Chemistry (CHEM454) > Credit Hours : 3

Nuclear and Radiation Chemistry (CHEM454) > Prerequisites
CHEM321 with a minimum grade D

CHEM113 with a minimum grade D
Nuclear and Radiation Chemistry (CHEM454) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the properties of the nucleus and its stability and properties

Recognize various of types of radiations emitted by the nuclei and their method of detection and write balanced nuclear reactions

Demonstrate the working principle of instruments used to monitor nuclear radiation and calculate the radiation dose absorbed by matter

Recognize the various methods by which radioactive substances can be disposed

Explain the working principles of nuclear reactors and the useful effects of radiation in research and other disciplines

Recognize the effects of various types of nuclear radiations on matter (gases, liquids and solids)

CHEM480.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM480 Research Project II
CHEM480.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM480
CHEM 480 is an experimental based elective research project course for undergraduate chemistry and biochemistry students. The course provides students the opportunity to develop their skills of project planning, methodology development, data analysis and results dissemination as well as employability skills required for labour market. In this course, students will run research projects under academic supervisions from faculty members in the department. Research work could be an advancement of their work started in their research project I course (CHEM 418 or BCHEM 418), or a new more advanced research topic. Students enrolled in this course are required to develop their research proposals independently or with help of their supervisors. At the end of the project, students are required to submit reports, present posters and give oral presentations on the results of their research projects.
Research Project II (CHEM480) > Credit Hours : 3

Research Project II (CHEM480) > Prerequisites
CHEM418 with a minimum grade D or BCHM418 with a minimum grade D
Research Project II (CHEM480) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Suggest, plan and develop a research proposal in discussion with the project’s supervisor.

Review and update related literature from chemical data bases and other relevant sources.

Use relevant library resources competently and use appropriate software for chemical drawing, molecular modelling and data processing.

Prepare a structured, critically evaluated written report for the research topic and experimental data collected.

Present and disseminate the results to appropriate scientific community through written and oral presentations, conforming to the guidelines for undergraduate research projects set by the department of chemistry and UAE University

Demonstrate an ability to work independently and to make informed decisions on the progress of the project

CHEM522.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM522 Analytical Spectroscopy
CHEM522.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM522
Advanced treatment of spectroscopic techniques and instrumentation. Atomic and molecular absorption, emission, and scattering processes and their application to quantitative chemical analysis are outlined.
Analytical Spectroscopy (CHEM522) > Credit Hours : 3

Analytical Spectroscopy (CHEM522) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the basic theory/fundamental aspects of atomic and molecular spectroscopic techniques.

Describe components of spectroscopic instruments and explain their functions.

Understand signals’ generation and its correlation with analytes’ compositions and concentrations.

Recognize the analytical capabilities, limitations and performance characteristics of different spectroscopic techniques; e.g. UV-Vis, fluorescence, IR spectroscopy, NMR, X-ray, ..etc).

Select a proper instrumental technique for solving problems in different life endeavors.

Use analytical literature to retrieve information related to spectroscopic methods of analysis.

CHEM523.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM523 Separation & Chromatographic Techniques
CHEM523.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM523
Theoretical and practical aspects of gas and high performance liquid chromatographic methods; supercritical fluid chromatography and capillary electrophoresis. Related instrumentation and selected applications are discussed.
Separation & Chromatographic Techniques (CHEM523) > Credit Hours : 3

Separation & Chromatographic Techniques (CHEM523) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Appreciate the role of separation science and the hyphenated instrumental techniques in the field of chemical analysis.

Comprehend and present literature that utilizes chromatography and other separation techniques in qualitative/quantitative analysis of known/unknown samples.

Define The Potential And Limitations Of Different Separation Techniques.

Describe The Role Of Different Components And The Fundamental Concepts Common To Instrumental Separation Techniques.

Explain How Various Instrumental Separation Techniques Achieve Good Separation Of Mixture Components Based On Different Principles.

Suggest A Proper Separation Technique For A Given Real World Analytical Problem.

CHEM524.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM524 Electroanalytical Techniques
CHEM524.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM524
Review of the relevant thermodynamic, kinetic, and electronic principles of electrochemical techniques used for analysis and for the characterization of inorganic and organic systems.
Electroanalytical Techniques (CHEM524) > Credit Hours : 3

Electroanalytical Techniques (CHEM524) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the theoretical and experimental aspects of common elector analytical techniques.

Derive some fundamental equations such as Butler-Volmer Equation.

Explain the potential and limitations of some selected electroanalytical techniques

Evaluate the applications of electroanalytical techniques in solving analytical problems.

Retrieve and present information relevant to electroanalytical techniques

CHEM526.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM526 Chemical Instrumentation
CHEM526.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM526
Electronics as applied to chemical instrumentation; design and construction of instruments used in chemical research, analysis, recording, and control
Chemical Instrumentation (CHEM526) > Credit Hours : 3

Chemical Instrumentation (CHEM526) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the fundamental concepts common to analytical instrumental techniques.

Explain how various instrumental techniques achieve selectivity based on different principles.

Recognize various instrumental outputs.

Solve problems related electrical circuits and data acquisition.

Correlate sensor construction to its selectivity.

Retrieve information relevant to instrumental analysis from scientific literature.

CHEM531.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM531 Advanced Organic Synthesis
CHEM531.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM531
The course is an intensive integrated course of study to introduce students to advanced concepts, reactions, and techniques in contemporary organic chemistry. Focus on multi-step synthesis of diverse target molecules.
Advanced Organic Synthesis (CHEM531) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Organic Synthesis (CHEM531) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Understand concepts in organic chemistry such as ureactivity, electronic and steric factors.

Describe chemical reactions, especially aromatic substitution, addition reactions and oxidation/reductions

Identify and manipulate stereo centers in chemical transformations

Retrieve information relevant to organic chemistry from the scientific literature

CHEM533.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM533 Organic Reaction Mechanisms
CHEM533.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM533
A mechanistic view of free-radical reactions, polar reactions, dipolar reactions, pericyclic reactions, frontier molecular orbital theory.
Organic Reaction Mechanisms (CHEM533) > Credit Hours : 3

Organic Reaction Mechanisms (CHEM533) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Understand reaction mechanisms based on frontier molecular orbital theory.

Describe tools used for the elucidation of organic reaction mechanisms

Describe major reaction mechanisms.

Propose reaction mechanisms to explain organic product formation.

CHEM534.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM534 Catalysis in Organic Chemistry
CHEM534.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM534
The course deals with basic catalysis, metal-mediated reactions, enzyme catalysis and organocatalysis. Applications of transition metal organometallic compounds in catalysis and organic synthesis will also be discussed.
Catalysis in Organic Chemistry (CHEM534) > Credit Hours : 3

Catalysis in Organic Chemistry (CHEM534) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate a good knowledge of a variety of metal-catalyzed reactions.

Outline the mechanism of common catalytic C-C bond forming reactions.

Demonstrate knowledge of the principles of organocatalysis/organocatalysts

Describe main catalytic reactions in organic synthesis in an industrial setting.

CHEM535.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM535 Polymer Chemistry
CHEM535.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM535
An introduction to the chemistry of polymers, including synthetic methods, mechanisms and kinetics of macromolecule formation, and polymer characterization techniques.
Polymer Chemistry (CHEM535) > Credit Hours : 3

Polymer Chemistry (CHEM535) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the basic principles of polymerization such as physical and chemical properties of polymers and polymer solutions.

Write polymer reaction synthesis mechanisms (addition, step growth, and other polymerizations).

Describe and calculate all types of polymer molecular weights

Classify polymers structures and morphologies and distinguish between polymers properties in bulk and solutions.

Recognize various instrumental techniques used for polymer characterization.

Search, review, and write scientific report in some selected special topics in polymer chemistry.

CHEM541.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM541 Advanced Biochemistry I
CHEM541.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM541
The course will build on the basics of biochemistry the students should already be familiar with and cover in detail various biochemical topics that are of current interest. Specifically the course will be comprised of three separate modules – advanced protein structure and function (including protein purification & enzymology), metabolism of pollutants (including oxidative stress and reactive oxygen species), and cellular signaling. The students will also be exposed to primary literature in the above mentioned areas of biochemistry and they will be asked to make a class presentation reviewing, presenting, and critiquing a published paper on environmental toxicology.
Advanced Biochemistry I (CHEM541) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Biochemistry I (CHEM541) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze And Research A Chosen Topic And Produce A Report On A Topic Related To Biochemical Toxicology.

Describe The Different Ways Of Carrying Out Protein Purification.

Evaluate The Oral Presentations Made By Their Colleagues For The Soundness Of Their Understanding And Organization Of Their Presentation.

Explain And Summarize Basics Of Environmental And Biochemical Toxicology.

Explain The Various Modes Of Cellular Signaling That Is Used In Biological Systems.

Recognize Primary, Secondary And Higher Orders Of Protein Structure And Correlate The Relationship Between Sequence And Structure.

CHEM551.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM551 Advanced Inorganic Chemistry I
CHEM551.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM551
Advanced course in inorganic chemistry focusing on one of the following topics: Transition metal organometallic chemistry, bioinorganic chemistry, inorganic cluster chemistry, solid state inorganic chemistry.
Advanced Inorganic Chemistry I (CHEM551) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Inorganic Chemistry I (CHEM551) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the coordination of different types of ligands to transition metals.

Apply bonding theories to bonding in transition metal complexes.

Propose Appropriate Routes For Preparation Of Organometallic Compounds.

Correlate between structures, properties, and reactivity of complexes and predict reaction products.

Propose appropriate mechanisms for catalytic reactions of organometallic compounds in advanced applications.

Evaluate recent literature reports on advanced topics in organometallic chemistry.

CHEM561.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM561 Advanced Physical Chemistry I
CHEM561.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM561
Advanced course in physical chemistry focusing on one of the following topics: Chemical Thermodynamics, Statistical Thermodynamics, Molecular Spectroscopy, Chemical Dynamics, Quantum Chemistry, Materials Surface Characterization
Advanced Physical Chemistry I (CHEM561) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Physical Chemistry I (CHEM561) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze spectroscopic data of simple molecules to determine molecular structural properties.

Build up electronic transitions in selected chromophores or fluorophores: intrinsic pathways, intra-molecular or inter-molecular photo-physical processes.

Plan appropriate experimental measurements to understand the molecular structure and dynamic of selected fluorescent probes.

Predict changes in absorption and emission peak position and intensity as a function of certain local environmental factors: Ph, temperature, polarity and viscosity.

CHEM598.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM598 Selected Topics
CHEM598.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM598
This course is designed for students, who want to gain a better understanding and more comprehensive knowledge in a study area for which a course does not exist in the curriculum. The course is offered in a standard lecture format. While there are quizzes, a midterm and a final examination for the course, there is also one term paper that the students will write and orally present. The term paper can be designed as a joint project paper among students taking the class.
Selected Topics (CHEM598) > Credit Hours : 3

Selected Topics (CHEM598) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain fundamental concepts of the topic studied.

Give a well-informed oral presentation of chosen subtopics of the general area of study.

Write a short overview of aspects of the material of the topic studied.

Evaluate the interactions of the studied topic with other related areas of science to assess the impact and application of the topic.

CHEM636.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM636 Seminar
CHEM636.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM636
This is a course in oral communication for graduate students in Chemistry. It is intended to provide graduate students with experience in the presentation of scientific data and help the student in the later defense of a proposal or a thesis. Presentations may be based on published peer reviewed publications or on original research, conducted by the student or within the student's laboratory. In addition, students will attend lectures of guest speakers both from within the chemistry department as well from other departments.
Seminar (CHEM636) > Credit Hours : 2

Seminar (CHEM636) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate the ability to present scientific material in a presentation of a peer-reviewed research article or their graduate research project.

Demonstrate the ability to critically evaluate the research presented in a peer reviewed article and to answer questions posed by the audience on this research at the end of the presentation.

Demonstrate an ability to listen to a scientific presentation and to ask pertinent questions regarding the material presented.

Actively participate in a discussion of strengths and weaknesses of a speaker's presentation and/or the scientific merit of the research presented.

CHEM641.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM641 Advanced Biochemistry II
CHEM641.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM641
Chemical composition of living matter and the chemistry of life processes. Characterization of amino acids, proteins, carbohydrates and lipids; enzymology and co-enzymes; metabolism of carbohydrates; biological oxidations. Metabolism of lipids, amino acids, and nucleotides; membrane biochemistry; biosynthesis of DNA, RNA, and proteins; gene regulation.
Advanced Biochemistry II (CHEM641) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Biochemistry II (CHEM641) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the structure and function of the major biomolecules: proteins, carbohydrates, lipids and nucleic acids.

Describe the catabolic and anabolic pathways of carbohydrate and lipid metabolism.

Understand and describe the basics of membrane biochemistry.

Communicate effectively through oral presentation based on a scientific publication.

Retrieve information from published literature and write a detailed scientific report on an advanced biochemistry topic.

CHEM651.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM651 Advanced Inorganic Chemistry II
CHEM651.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM651
Advanced course in inorganic chemistry focusing on one of the following topics: Chemical Applications of Group Theory, Chemistry of f-block elements, Identification and Characterization of Inorganic Compounds, Nanoscale Materials.
Advanced Inorganic Chemistry II (CHEM651) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Inorganic Chemistry II (CHEM651) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Define the properties of a point group and its symmetry elements.

Expressing the symmetry transformation of a point or the collection of points using matrix notation.

Generate irreducible representations form the reducible representation of a specific point group.

Use the projection operator method to generate symmetry adapted linear combinations SALCs of a molecule.

Determine vibration modes the molecule have using group theory.

CHEM661.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM661 Advanced Physical Chemistry II
CHEM661.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM661
Advanced course in physical chemistry focusing on one of the following topics: Chemical Bonding and Spectra, Nuclear and Radiation Chemistry, Heterogeneous Catalysis and Colloid Chemistry.
Advanced Physical Chemistry II (CHEM661) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Physical Chemistry II (CHEM661) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop the capability to use normal mode theory for describing vibrational structure of polyatomic Molecules.

Employ molecular orbital theory to account for chemical Bonding.

Use Hartree-Fock method to solve schrodinger equation of molecules.

Use rotational and vibrational spectra to extract important structural nformation.

Use semi-empirical methods, e.g. Huckel’s and Extended Huckel’s) to treat conjugated molecules.

Utilize Franck-Condon Principle to account for electronic transitions and the pathways of irradiative ransitions

CHEM701.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM701 Advanced Analytical Chemistry
CHEM701.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM701
This course will introduce students to the advances in methods used for chemical analysis of different substances. The course will cover advances in spectroscopic, electro analytical and/or chromatographic techniques. Applications related to analyses of chemical, biological and environmental samples will be considered
Advanced Analytical Chemistry (CHEM701) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Analytical Chemistry (CHEM701) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Conceptualize the operation principles of selected modern analytical instrumentation and methods.

Correlate the principle of instrument operation to the nature of the measured analytical signal, and source of intrinsic selectivity.

Assess different measurements methods, e.g., absolute, relative, ratiometric, differential, scanning, averaging, background subtraction, etc.

Select a proper instrumental technique for a given analytical problem.

Criticize the effectiveness of the application of some recent techniques in selected application.

Evaluate information relevant to instrumental analysis from scientific literature.

CHEM712.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM712 Selected Topics in Analytical Chemistry
CHEM712.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM712
This course is offered into two modules cover subjects related surface and interface analyses and chemical sensors and biosensors. Module A: The course will cover the methods used for surface and interface analyses and characterizing their properties, composition and structure. Techniques based on interactions of light beams, electron beams and ion beams with matter will be discussed in terms of its theoretical background, components, applications as well as limitations and advantages. Samples’ preparation for measurement by each technique as well as examples of problem’s solving using surface analyses will be provided in different fields. Module B: This course aims to introduce graduate students to the area of chemical sensors and biosensors. Topics to be covered include structure and properties of various recognition materials, and reagents, physicochemical basis of various transduction methods, auxiliary materials used in the construction of chemical sensors and biosensors, advanced manufacturing methods and versatility of sensors’ constructions. Selected applications of some electrochemical, optical, mass and thermometric sensors in biochemical, industrial and environmental fields are to be discussed.
Selected Topics in Analytical Chemistry (CHEM712) > Credit Hours : 3

Selected Topics in Analytical Chemistry (CHEM712) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain structural and properties’ differences between surface, interface and bulk of materials.

Describe the mechanisms of interactions of light, electrons and ions beams with matter surface.

Demonstrate the theoretical bases and type of information generated using different types of surface and interface analytical techniques.

Describe different methods for sample’s preparation and the effect of matrix on measurements.

Evaluate different techniques in terms of sensitivity, resolution, information gained and data acquisition procedures.

Use surface methods for determining the elemental and molecular compositions of surfaces characterize morphologies and solve real life problems.

Demonstrate the exciting world of chemical sensors and its applications in life and science.

Outline different types of chemical sensors (potentiometric, voltammetric, optical, solid electrolyte, mass and …).

Know theoretical bases for sensors’ signal generation, quantitation, and techniques used for their fabrications.

Evaluate different sensors in terms of sensitivity, resolution, information gained and data acquisition procedures.

Explain the applications of sensors in solving problems in various fields, e.g health, environment, industry, ..etc. .

CHEM722.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM722 Advanced Organic Chemistry and Biocatalysis
CHEM722.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM722
The course is an intensive course of study to introduce students to advanced concepts, reactions, and techniques in contemporary organic and bioorganic chemistry. Focus will be on name reac¬tions, and on multi-step synthesis of diverse target molecules. Aside from traditional chemistry, biotechnological approaches will also be covered. The physical and kinetic properties of enzymes that permit their use for the synthesis of chemicals will be discussed, along with state-of-the-art examples of how enzyme-based systems have been successfully applied for the synthesis of commercially relevant molecules.
Advanced Organic Chemistry and Biocatalysis (CHEM722) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Organic Chemistry and Biocatalysis (CHEM722) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate selective named reactions and how they apply to contemporary synthetic methodology.

Predict and elucidate the stereochemical outcome of reactions.

Evaluate which properties of enzymes are important for biocatalysis and how these properties impact biocatalysis.

Solve problems related to enzyme kinetics and present recent state-of-the-art examples of how enzymes can be applied as biocatalysts within the chemical sector.

Apply retrosynthetic analysis to a molecule of average complexity.

Plan multistep sequences to molecules of average complexity.

CHEM723.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM723 Selected Topics in Organic Chemistry
CHEM723.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM723
Module A: The course gives a mechanistic view of free-radical reactions, polar reactions, and pericyclic reactions with an insight to Frontier Molecular Orbital theory. It provides an overview of bonding theories. Energetics of reactions are discussed, also.
Selected Topics in Organic Chemistry (CHEM723) > Credit Hours : 3

Selected Topics in Organic Chemistry (CHEM723) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Use theories of bonding to explain reaction mechanisms.

Predict independently the stereochemical outcome of reactions.

Retrieve and evaluate relevant information on the subject from the scientific literature.

Apply the learnt knowledge in industrial processes.

Transfer the knowledge to new reactions.

CHEM724.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM724 Selected Topics in Biochemistry
CHEM724.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM724
The chemical industry is currently exploring alternative approaches to chemical synthesis, which are renewable, sustainable and environment-friendly. Industrial biotechnology, in particular, holds great promise for solving societal challenges and meeting the global demands for food, fuel, and materials, while reducing the environmental impact. This course will cover the increasingly important role of the biochemical sciences for the synthesis of chemicals. In particular, we will look at various aspects of this fast-growing technology which encompasses techniques from several research areas including genetic engineering, metabolic engineering, protein engineering and synthetic biology. We will look at the biochemical principles that underpin them, along with recent case studies that demonstrate the production of industrially relevant target chemicals including biofuels, bioplastics, and specialty chemicals.
Selected Topics in Biochemistry (CHEM724) > Credit Hours : 3

Selected Topics in Biochemistry (CHEM724) > Prerequisites
CHEM283 with a minimum grade D
Selected Topics in Biochemistry (CHEM724) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate and formulate strategies for the genetic modification of biological hosts.

Evaluate and design biological pathways for the production of target chemicals.

Evaluate and design assays for improving traits of enzymes involved in chemical production.

Evaluate and design assays for chemical screening.

Communicate effectively through oral presentation based on a course-related scientific publication as well as a peer-review.

Retrieve information from published literature and write a scientific report on topics relating to the course.

CHEM733.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM733 Molecular Structure and Bonding
CHEM733.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM733
This course describes modern theories of chemical bonding, with an emphasis on molecular quantum mechanics, and their application in the prediction and interpretation of molecular properties. Topics include applications of group theory, valence bond theory, and molecular orbital theory in the study of structure, reactivity, electronic spectra, vibrational spectra, rotational transitions and electrochemical properties of main group and transition metal compounds.
Molecular Structure and Bonding (CHEM733) > Credit Hours : 3

Molecular Structure and Bonding (CHEM733) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the terms that arise from the ground state configuration of an atom.

Find the positions of the corresponding spectral lines in many-electron atoms.

Account for vibronically allowed transitions.

Construct the molecular orbitals of polyatomic molecules.

Estimate the electric properties of molecules.

CHEM734.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM734 Selected Topics in Inorganic Chemistry
CHEM734.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM734
This course studies subjects related to synthesis, structure, properties and applications of solid materials. The topics that are discussed in this course include: structure and bonding in solids, crystals and crystalline solids, preparative methods, characterization and physical properties of solids. The course also discusses selected solid materials and their applications with emphasis on nano-materials in advanced applications such as electronic and catalysis.
Selected Topics in Inorganic Chemistry (CHEM734) > Credit Hours : 3

Selected Topics in Inorganic Chemistry (CHEM734) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Provide bonding model and describe structures of different inorganic solids.

Develop the ability to discriminate between different types of defects and non-stoichiometry in solid structures.

Demonstrate an ability to compare different preparative methods of inorganic solids with emphasis on preparation of nano-structured materials.

Demonstrate a broad foundational knowledge of advanced methods of solid materials’ characterization with emphasis on diffraction techniques.

Evaluate the relationships between structure/bonding and electronic, electrical, magnetic and optical properties of solids.

Demonstrate in-depth knowledge of advanced applications of solid materials with emphasis on nanomaterials in advanced technologies related to electronics, medicine, and catalysis.

CHEM735.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM735 Selected Topics in Physical Chemistry
CHEM735.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM735
This course is offered into two modules cover subjects related to electrochemistry and interface kinetics, advanced corrosion and inhibition theories and mechanisms and photochemistry. Module A covers advanced electrochemistry and interface kinetics, advanced theories of corrosion and inhibition as well as mechanisms of corrosion and inhibition. Module B covers the concepts of photochemistry in terms of the experimental and theoretical aspects of chemical reactions induced by visible and Ultraviolet radiation. Fluorescence and chemiluminescence.
Selected Topics in Physical Chemistry (CHEM735) > Credit Hours : 3

Selected Topics in Physical Chemistry (CHEM735) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Module A - Course Learning Outcomes:

Analyze the electrode-electrolyte interface and the nature of the double layer.

Conceptualize and utilize the Bulter-Volmer equation, the Tafel equation, and the Stern Geary equation.

Criticize the kinetics of electrode processes, polarization techniques, and analyse the corrosion rates.

Self-evaluate the different forms of corrosion.

Conceptualize corrosion mechanisms.

Analyze and criticize the Mixed-Potential theory.

Self-evaluate and manage inhibition and protection theories and techniques.

Module B - Course Learning Outcomes:

Criticize the role of photochemistry in our everyday living

Conceptualize the Frontier molecular orbital theory.

Analyze fundamental photophysical and photochemical processes qualitatively and quantitatively.

Manage the type of photonic materials for a specific application.

Self-evaluate photochemical process in what goes on in your environment.

CHEM740.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM740 Advanced Spectroscopic Methods
CHEM740.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM740
Elucidation of molecular structure utilizing IR, UV, and NMR spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, and other methods.
Advanced Spectroscopic Methods (CHEM740) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Spectroscopic Methods (CHEM740) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Utilize the basic principles of modern NMR (1H and 13C NMR), IR spectroscopic and mass spectrometric techniques in their own research work.

Apply modern multi-dimensional NMR techniques such as COSY, HETCOR, HMQC, HMBC, INADEQUATE, TOCSY, NOESY.

Use these techniques to determine the structure of complex unknown organic compound.

Design their own experiments for specific purposes.

Critically evaluate techniques used in structure determination of organic compounds in the literature.

CHEM741.title: UAEU Catalog — CHEM741 NanoChemistry
CHEM741.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2905.shtml?id=CHEM741
The course is interdisciplinary covers the chemistry of materials at the nanoscale. It provides detailed background on the preparation, characterization, and applications of selected strategic nanomaterials.
NanoChemistry (CHEM741) > Credit Hours : 3

NanoChemistry (CHEM741) > Prerequisites
CHEM111 with a minimum grade D

CHEM112 with a minimum grade D
NanoChemistry (CHEM741) > Corequisites
CHEM241 with a minimum grade D
NanoChemistry (CHEM741) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze the chemistry of preparation of nanoparticles and nanofibers showing an advanced level of understanding of the subject.

Identify and evaluate the methods of nanomaterials surface chemical modification.

Critique different characterization data and properties of nanomaterials.

Construct a thorough knowledge of the instruments used for the characterization of nanomaterials.

Establish structure-property relationships in various types of nanomaterials based on their characterization.

Manage advanced applications of various types of nanomaterials.

CIVL200.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL200 Computer Aided Drafting
CIVL200.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL200
This course introduces the basic principles of computer-aided drawings, including: geometric construction, dimensioning, drawing scales, layouts, and line convention. It includes two-dimensional sketching, orthographic projections, principal views, isometric, and sectional views. Students will gain an understanding of the essential techniques required to create precise and detailed technical drawings. The course also enhances students’ visualization skills for interpreting the geometrical features of three-dimensional objects, and equips them with the ability to create layouts for various civil engineering projects.
Computer Aided Drafting (CIVL200) > Credit Hours : 1

Computer Aided Drafting (CIVL200) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the fundamental geometric concepts in engineering drawings.

Apply standard conventions of scales, line types, dimensioning, and lettering using CAD software.

Produce multi-view orthographic projection of 3D objects.

Create three-dimensional objects (isometric) drawings

Integrate drafting techniques in the preparation of civil engineering drawings.

CIVL201.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL201 Engineering Materials for Art
CIVL201.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL201
The course focuses on providing non-engineering students with a fundamental understanding of basic engineering materials technology to bridge the gap between engineering knowledge and non-engineering applications. The course takes a general approach that includes: the role and importance of materials in history and modern society, introduction to materials resources and availability, material cost, principles for systematic materials selection, principles of material properties. The course also provides the students with a basic understanding of the nature of materials. It covers materials such as steel, aluminum, concrete and its ingredients, gypsum, timber, and composites (polymers and fibers). The course includes basic laboratory tests to evaluate the engineering properties of materials and other possible applications.
Engineering Materials for Art (CIVL201) > Credit Hours : 3

Engineering Materials for Art (CIVL201) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify basic engineering materials, technology, nature, and general properties.

Describe basic engineering materials resources and availability, and material cost.

Identify principles of material properties for selection

Identify various properties of steel, aluminum, concrete and its ingredients, gypsum, timber, and composites (polymers and fibers).

Conduct various laboratory tests to evaluate the different properties of steel, aluminum, concrete and its ingredients, gypsum, timber, and composites (polymers and fibers), and interpret test results.

CIVL220.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL220 Computer Aided Drawing (CIVL)
CIVL220.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL220
This course gives an introduction to computer graphics, geometric construction and line convention. It includes orthographic projections, isometric, dimensioning, sectional views, and preparation of drawings for different civil engineering projects including concrete and steel structures.
Computer Aided Drawing (CIVL) (CIVL220) > Credit Hours : 2

Computer Aided Drawing (CIVL) (CIVL220) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply fundamental geometric constructions.

Draw isometric of an object by AutoCAD.

Prepare shape and size descriptions of an object in a multi-view orthographic projection by AutoCAD with the application of the conventions of scales, line symbols, dimensioning and engineering lettering.

Identify the different basic components in any reinforced concrete (RC) or steel structures.

Represent different structures (RC or Steel) in multi-view orthographic projection.

Use modern tools (e.g., computer aided software) in constructing engineering drawings.

Communicate effectively in class.

CIVL240.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL240 Statics
CIVL240.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL240
This course aims at introducing the students to the mechanics of rigid, non-accelerating bodies with applications to machinery and structures. Topics covered include scalar and vector quantities; two-dimensional force systems: forces, moments, couples and resultants; free body diagrams; equilibrium conditions; three-dimensional force systems; analysis of structures: method of joints, method of sections; distributed forces: introduction to shear forces and bending moments in beams; center of mass and centroid; properties of areas; and friction.
Statics (CIVL240) > Credit Hours : 3

Statics (CIVL240) > Prerequisites
PHYS105 with a minimum grade D

PHYS135 with a minimum grade D
Statics (CIVL240) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply fundamental vector mechanics concepts to determine the resultant In 2-D and 3-D force systems.

Draw free-body diagrams and utilize equations of Equilibrium to solve particle and rigid-body equilibrium problems.

Analyze forces acting on pin-connected members of trusses and frames.

Resolve the internal forces (normal forces, shear forces, and bending moments) in a structural or mechanical member.

Determine the location of the center of mass of a body and centroid of an area.

Determine the moment of inertia of an area.

Formulate and solve simple statics problems collectively using engineering software packages.

CIVL260.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL260 Introduction to Environmental Data and Mapping
CIVL260.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL260
This course provides an accessible introduction to the concepts and tools used to collect, visualize, and analyze geospatial environmental data, with a focus on digital mapping. Designed for students from all academic backgrounds, the course requires no prior experience with coding, mapping, or environmental science. Students will learn how to work with open-source data and visualize remote sensing data through software packages, explore real-world environmental datasets, and create effective maps to communicate environmental issues. Through hands-on exercises, students will develop practical skills in spatial thinking, environmental data mapping, and data visualization—essential tools for addressing climate change and sustainability challenges.
Introduction to Environmental Data and Mapping (CIVL260) > Credit Hours : 3

Introduction to Environmental Data and Mapping (CIVL260) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe basic concepts of environmental data.

Employ geospatial software packages in hands-on exercises.

Visualize spatial and environmental data by creating simple maps.

Associate visual maps with efforts in mitigating climate change and achieving sustainable development goals.

CIVL270.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL270 Introduction to Environmental Engineering
CIVL270.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL270
This course aims at introducing the different topics related to the field of environmental engineering. It includes the role of environmental engineers; fundamentals of environmental chemistry; fundamentals of environmental microbiology; mass balance; mathematics of growth; risk assessment; water pollution; water quality control; solid and hazardous waste management; and air pollution. The course includes hands-on training experience including life cycle analysis, environmental chemistry, water, solid waste, hazardous waste, risk assessment and air pollution.
Introduction to Environmental Engineering (CIVL270) > Credit Hours : 3

Introduction to Environmental Engineering (CIVL270) > Prerequisites
CHEM111

CHEM175
Introduction to Environmental Engineering (CIVL270) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop a mass balance expression for contaminants under different case scenarios and design a simple system to meet desired needs

Forecast population using different models and calculate risk associated with exposure to a certain level of a contaminant

Apply the basic fundamentals of environmental chemistry and environmental microbiology to environmental engineering problems

Determine water quality parameters and select appropriate treatment method for water and wastewater

Characterize air quality and calculate the air pollution standard index

Determine needed resources for the management of solid and hazardous waste and design a sanitary landfill

Write technical reports and conduct professional presentations related to national, regional, and global environmental issues

Utilize computer software packages related to environmental engineering and conduct relevant experiments

CIVL290.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL290 Sustainable Engineering Principles
CIVL290.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL290
This course focuses on fundamental knowledge of sustainability within global and local contexts. The course will cover major areas of sustainable engineering theory and practice. Topics include sustainability monitoring and assessment, green systems assessment, sustainable building process, sustainable natural resources management, sustainable material selection, climate change, and carbon footprint. Case studies on real-world sustainable engineering principles will be furnished
Sustainable Engineering Principles (CIVL290) > Credit Hours : 3

Sustainable Engineering Principles (CIVL290) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the environmental, economic, health, social, and safety impacts of engineering practices on the sustainable engineering design process

Identify strategies for mitigating climate change in sustainable engineering projects.

Compare material options, considering sustainability criteria, for informed selections.

Assess the relative sustainability of engineering designs using international and local rating systems.

Communicate appropriate engineering solutions in addressing sustainability challenges both in writing and verbally.

CIVL305.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL305 Air Quality Engineering
CIVL305.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL305
The course provides the students the opportunity to use engineering- and science-based approaches to describe, quantify, and assess sources, transport mechanisms, and environmental impacts of atmospheric and indoor air pollutants. Moreover, the course aims to develop an understanding of regulatory approaches to address the health and welfare impacts of air pollution. In addition, it explores the application of air quality models for the evaluation and design of air quality control equipment.
Air Quality Engineering (CIVL305) > Credit Hours : 3

Air Quality Engineering (CIVL305) > Prerequisites
CIVL270
Air Quality Engineering (CIVL305) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the sources, effects, history, and regulation of the major air pollutants

Interpret experimental laboratory data and use engineering judgment to draw conclusions

Explain the causes, consequences, and possible solutions for major air quality issues

Design air quality control equipment by applying knowledge of math, science, and engineering

Describe the major types of health and welfare effects and how they are used in the regulatory process

Communicate results both written and orally

CIVL310.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL310 Structural Analysis
CIVL310.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL310
This course aims at providing students with the skills and techniques required for the analysis of statically determinate structures. It includes the discussion and review of basic statics; stability and determinacy; analysis of determinant structures (trusses, beams, and frames); cables and arches; influence lines of moving loads; deflection analysis (geometric and energy approach); introduction to indeterminate structures (slope deflection method and moment distribution method).
Structural Analysis (CIVL310) > Credit Hours : 3

Structural Analysis (CIVL310) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co MECH305 with a minimum grade D
Structural Analysis (CIVL310) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Distinguish between stable and unstable and statically determinate and indeterminate structures.

Apply equations of equilibrium to different types of structures to compute the support reactions.

Analyze simple, compound and complex trusses.

Derive the internal shear and bending moment equations and draw the internal shearing force and bending moment diagrams.

Evaluate and draw the influence lines for reactions, shears, and bending moments in beams and for the axial force in truss members due to moving loads.

Compute deflection of structures using different methods (methods of double integration and conjugate beam, and beam tables).

Communicate and express their ideas effectively during classroom discussions.

CIVL330.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL330 Transportation Engineering
CIVL330.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL330
This course aims at introducing the notions of transportation systems, organizations, and management.
