The course covers in details the elements of the transportation planning process; namely trip generation, trip attraction, trip distribution, modal split and trip assignment models. The course also covers aspects of forecasting travel demand and evaluating transportation alternatives using both economical and effectiveness approaches.
Transportation Engineering (CIVL330) > Credit Hours : 3

Transportation Engineering (CIVL330) > Prerequisites
STAT210
Transportation Engineering (CIVL330) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Calibrate zonal demand generation/attraction regression models.

Calibrate demand distribution models (gravity models).

Calibrate modal split models for mode choice analysis.

Calculate the traffic flow of network links using user equilibrium and system optimum assignment techniques.

Estimate the traffic impact of new developments using the four-stage sequential models.

Make final decisions among planning alternatives that best integrate multiple objectives such as technical feasibility, environmental impact and cost minimization.

Communicate effectively via class technical discussions and presentations.

CIVL335.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL335 Surveying
CIVL335.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL335
This course aims at studying fundamentals of plain surveying for civil engineers. It includes fundamentals of surveying measurements, including using classical and electronic measuring devices. Topics cover vertical distance measurements, topography representation, and horizontal distance measurements. Computation and determination of point coordinates are covered including measurements of angles and directions, and establishing of the horizontal control by Traverses, including field procedures and computations. Computation of earthwork volumes is also included in the course.
Surveying (CIVL335) > Credit Hours : 3

Surveying (CIVL335) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co CIVL200 with a minimum grade D or Pre/Co CIVL220 with a minimum grade D
Surveying (CIVL335) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze and solve basic mathematical and geometric problems related to surveying activities.

Conduct measurement campaigns and analyze results for ground distances using various methods and instruments.

Measure and layout the elevations using various leveling techniques and instruments.

Design leveling framework for civil engineering projects.

Measure and layout horizontal and vertical angles using various angle measurement techniques and instruments.

Solve control surveying traverses computing closure errors, their adjustments and assess the order of accuracy.

Compute areas and volumes of earthworks using various techniques and methods.

CIVL340.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL340 Soil Mechanics
CIVL340.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL340
This course aims at introducing the engineering properties of soils to the students. Topics cover soil formation and classification; soil water interaction; soil plasticity; permeability of soils; stress distribution in soils; soil compaction; shear strength of soils; the principle of effective stress.
Soil Mechanics (CIVL340) > Credit Hours : 3

Soil Mechanics (CIVL340) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co MECH305 with a minimum grade D
Soil Mechanics (CIVL340) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply the first principles and phase diagram to calculate soil properties.

Evaluate the total stress, effective stress and pore water pressure in soil.

Conduct and analyze grain size distribution tests and Atterberg Limits tests, and classify the soil accordingly.

Conduct and analyze compaction of soils, standard and modified, as well as sand cone test, and use the interpreted data in geotechnical design.

Apply the principles of water flow in soil and conduct and analyze permeability tests.

Estimate consolidation settlement of structures due to externally applied loads, and conduct and analyze consolidation test.

Evaluate the shear strength of a given soil under given loading conditions and conduct and analyze shear test data.

CIVL345.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL345 Fluid Mechanics for Civil and Architectural Engineering
CIVL345.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL345
This course aims at presenting basic principles of fluid mechanics. It includes definitions and fundamental concepts, dimensions and units, properties of fluids, flow regimes, pressure and force calculations under hydrostatic conditions, manometers, buoyancy and stability of floating and submerged bodies, elementary fluid dynamics, conservation equations: mass, energy and momentum, continuity and Bernoulli equations, hydraulic gradient line and total energy line, linear momentum equation, Angular momentum equation, applications on conservation equations, Navier-Stockes equation, dimensional analysis, Rayleigh Method, Pi theorem, Geometric, kinematic and dynamic hydraulic similarities, undistorted and distorted hydraulic models, and Lab experiments on the above topics.
Fluid Mechanics for Civil and Architectural Engineering (CIVL345) > Credit Hours : 3

Fluid Mechanics for Civil and Architectural Engineering (CIVL345) > Prerequisites
CIVL240 with a minimum grade D
Fluid Mechanics for Civil and Architectural Engineering (CIVL345) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify important fluid properties.

Calculate the pressure in fluids at rest.

Calculate the hydrostatic force on totally/partially submerged surfaces.

Calculate the forces exerted by a moving fluid using the continuity and momentum equations.

Calculate the pressure and velocity heads under different flow conditions and draw the hydraulic gradient and total energy lines.

Formulate equations using dimensional analysis to assess prototype behavior using hydraulic similarity.

Conduct physical experiments to simulate different types of flow, analyze the data to obtain the required information, and provide scientific interpretation of experimental results.

CIVL358.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL358 Surveying for Architectural Engineering
CIVL358.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL358
This course aims at learning fundamentals of measurements of horizontal and vertical distances, measuring angles, using classical and electronic measuring equipment, computing areas and volumes of earthwork, staking-out of buildings and sewers, staking-out of hardscapes, setting out verticality of columns and buildings, and measuring settlement of buildings.
Surveying for Architectural Engineering (CIVL358) > Credit Hours : 2

Surveying for Architectural Engineering (CIVL358) > Prerequisites
STAT210 with a minimum grade D
Surveying for Architectural Engineering (CIVL358) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Measure and layout horizontal distances and horizontal angles.

Measure and layout elevations and vertical angles.

Conduct grid leveling for preparation of contour maps.

Prepare land profiles and cross-sections from contour maps.

Compute earthwork using profiles, cross-sections, and contour maps.

Operate or use surveying equipment.

Apply Surveying in Construction.

Function in teams during field data gathering, analysis, and reporting.

CIVL360.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL360 Concrete Technology
CIVL360.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL360
This course aims at introducing concrete and its constituents to the students. Topics include properties and specification of different types of cements; properties of aggregates; properties of fresh concrete; mixing, placing, and compaction of concrete; strength and durability of hardened concrete; concrete mix design; types of admixtures for concrete; special concretes and their applications; introduction to hot weather concreting; introduction to masonry materials.
Concrete Technology (CIVL360) > Credit Hours : 3

Concrete Technology (CIVL360) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co CHEM270
Concrete Technology (CIVL360) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify types, evaluate properties and select concrete ingredients; aggregates, Portland cements, mixing water and concrete admixtures suitable for use in concrete production and apply acceptance criteria.

Conduct various laboratory tests to evaluate concrete ingredients, aggregate and cement, and interpret test results and conformity with relevant code provisions.

Evaluate various properties of fresh and hardened concrete, and different factors which affect these propertie

Conduct various laboratory tests to evaluate the different properties of fresh and hardened concrete and interpret test results.

Design concrete mixtures to meet specific criteria and specifications.

Identify and choose among concrete construction methods (i.e. mixing, transporting, casting and consolidation) and different types of concretes and its applications.

CIVL361.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL361 Construction Materials
CIVL361.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL361
This course aims to introduce materials engineering concepts, principles for systematic materials selection, and material properties for civil engineering design. It covers different construction materials, including steel, aluminum, and composites. The course also introduces specifications of concrete and its constituents, including aggregates, cement, water, and admixtures, and evaluates its fresh and hardened properties. Concrete mix design procedures are also studied.
Construction Materials (CIVL361) > Credit Hours : 3

Construction Materials (CIVL361) > Prerequisites
CHEM111 with a minimum grade D

CHEM175 with a minimum grade D

Pre/Co MECH305 with a minimum grade D
Construction Materials (CIVL361) > Corequisites
CIVL362 with a minimum grade D
Construction Materials (CIVL361) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe basic engineering materials concepts, nature, properties, and selection criteria.

Identify the properties of different construction materials, including steel, aluminum, and composites.

Identify types and properties of concrete ingredients suitable for use in concrete production and apply acceptance criteria.

Evaluate different construction methods and properties of fresh and hardened concrete.

Design concrete mixtures to meet specific criteria and specifications.

CIVL362.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL362 Construction Materials Lab
CIVL362.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL362
The course evaluates the characteristics and properties of various construction materials using standardized tests, including steel, aluminum, composites, aggregates, and cement. It focuses on specimen preparation, safe laboratory practices, use of international standards, experimental data acquisition, and interpretation of results. The fresh and hardened concrete properties are evaluated following standardized tests. Technical report writing, teamwork, and professional laboratory conduct are integral components of the course.
Construction Materials Lab (CIVL362) > Credit Hours : 1

Construction Materials Lab (CIVL362) > Corequisites
CIVL361 with a minimum grade D
Construction Materials Lab (CIVL362) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Conduct various laboratory tests to assess the characteristics of different construction materials, including steel, aluminum, and composites.

Perform various laboratory tests to evaluate properties of concrete ingredients and interpret test results and conformity with relevant code provisions.

Carry out various laboratory tests to assess the properties of fresh and hardened concrete and interpret test results.

Communicate effectively with a range of audiences through written reports.

CIVL365.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL365 Reinforced Concrete Design I
CIVL365.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL365
This course introduces students to the engineering design process for reinforced concrete (RC) structural members. Topics include introduction to concrete building systems and structural safety; determination and distribution of gravity loads; analysis and design of statically determinate RC beams of various cross-sectional shapes for flexure and shear; design of short RC columns subjected to axial loads and bending moments; and principles of bond, anchorage, and development length. The design process introduced in this course is complemented by the application of industry-standard computer software to support RC design and verification.
Reinforced Concrete Design I (CIVL365) > Credit Hours : 3

Reinforced Concrete Design I (CIVL365) > Prerequisites
CIVL310 with a minimum grade D

Pre/Co CIVL360 with a minimum grade D or Pre/Co CIVL361 with a minimum grade D

Pre/Co CIVL362 with a minimum grade D
Reinforced Concrete Design I (CIVL365) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Determine service loads on reinforced concrete beams and columns.

Design reinforced concrete beam sections of various shapes for flexure.

Design reinforced concrete beam sections for shear.

Design of short reinforced concrete columns subjected to axial loads and combined axial load and bending.

Apply principles of bond, anchorage, and development length.

Utilize industry-standard software and communicate findings effectively.

CIVL375.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL375 Water & Wastewater Technology
CIVL375.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL375
This course aims at presenting the analysis and design aspects of main technologies employed in water and wastewater treatment. It includes physical treatment processes like screening, grit removal, aeration, sedimentation, and filtration, chemical treatment processes like coagulation, flocculation, softening, iron and manganese removal, disinfection, ion exchange and adsorption, and biological treatment processes like activated sludge and anaerobic treatment units. The course addresses the reuse of wastewater and the treatment and disposal techniques of generated sludge. It also includes a number of laboratory experiments illustrating selected water and wastewater treatment technologies.
Water & Wastewater Technology (CIVL375) > Credit Hours : 3

Water & Wastewater Technology (CIVL375) > Prerequisites
CIVL270 with a minimum grade D
Water & Wastewater Technology (CIVL375) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop mass balance expressions for contaminants under different case scenarios and design a simple system to meet desired needs.

Construct an appropriate treatment scheme to remove certain pollutants present in water or wastewater.

Design a water or wastewater treatment component.

Conduct bench-scale water and wastewater treatment processes.

Conduct an independent study related to water and wastewater treatment.

CIVL380.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL380 Engineering Principles of Climate Change
CIVL380.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL380
In this course, students will learn about the fundamental principles of engineering as they relate to climate change. The course will begin with an introduction to the science of climate change and its causes, including the role of greenhouse gases and the impacts of global warming. Students will then explore the different engineering approaches to mitigating climate change, including renewable energy technologies, energy efficiency improvements, and carbon capture and storage. In the second part of the course, students will focus on engineering solutions for adapting to the impacts of climate change, including infrastructure improvements for flood and drought management and sustainable urban drainage systems. Throughout the course, students will analyze case studies of successful engineering projects and gain hands-on experience through exercises.
Engineering Principles of Climate Change (CIVL380) > Credit Hours : 3

Engineering Principles of Climate Change (CIVL380) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the scientific principles underlying climate change and its causes

Evaluate engineering approaches for mitigating climate change

Select sustainable engineering solutions for climate change adaptation

Communicate effectively about climate change and engineering solutions

CIVL400.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL400 Water Resources
CIVL400.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL400
This course aims at presenting the different aspects of water resources and hydraulic applications. It includes introduction to, and significance of, water resources, rainfall, evaporation, infiltration, and surface runoff, mass curves, steady flow in closed conduit, friction losses in pipelines, pipe networks, types, selection and operation of pumps, open channel flow, normal and critical depths, specific energy concept, rapidly and gradually varied flow, water surface profile analysis and computation, introduction to groundwater hydraulics, and flow calculation in 2-D and 3-D wells. It also includes a number of laboratory experiments.
Water Resources (CIVL400) > Credit Hours : 3

Water Resources (CIVL400) > Prerequisites
CIVL345
Water Resources (CIVL400) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Characterize head losses in pipeline flow and design pipelines in serial, parallel, and network configurations to deliver a specified flow and meet pressure constraints.

Analyze hydraulic systems to develop system curves and effectively use pump curves to select single or multiple pumps that satisfy discharge and head requirements.

Apply a computer software to analyze and design pipeline systems and effectively present results and findings both orally and in written form.

Analyze data for and relate between components of the hydrologic cycle, including: precipitation, evapotranspiration, infiltration, runoff, and stream flow.

Calculate aquifer properties and determine soil hydraulic conductivity to characterize two and three dimensional groundwater flow under both gravity and pumping conditions.

Design open channel sections and characterize uniform, gradually varied, and rapidly varied flow using the specific energy principle and the momentum principle.

Take laboratory measurements of volumetric flow rates, manometer pressures, slopes, and water levels; and prepare well written technical reports.

CIVL412.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL412 Reinforced Concrete Design II
CIVL412.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL412
The course aims at the design of complex reinforced concrete structural systems. It includes the analysis and design of continuous beams; two-way slabs; design of reinforced concrete slender columns; and shear walls. It also includes an introduction to the seismic design of reinforced concrete structures and application of computer software for analysis and design of reinforced concrete elements.
Reinforced Concrete Design II (CIVL412) > Credit Hours : 3

Reinforced Concrete Design II (CIVL412) > Prerequisites
CIVL365 with a minimum grade D
Reinforced Concrete Design II (CIVL412) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze and design continuous reinforced concrete elements and produce drawings of reinforcement detailing.

Analyze, design, and produce drawings for the detailing of reinforcement of two-way floor slab systems.

Design reinforced concrete slender columns.

Design reinforced concrete shear walls under gravity and lateral loads.

Apply computer software to analyze and design reinforced concrete elements.

Communicate results and findings effectively.

CIVL417.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL417 Structural Steel Design
CIVL417.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL417
This course aims at studying the properties of structural steel, steel sections and design concepts. In addition, the course discusses in details the design of main structural elements such as tension and compression members, as well as the design of beams. The course also covers the design of bolted and welded connections for tension members, and sheds the light on the design of simple beam connections.
Structural Steel Design (CIVL417) > Credit Hours : 3

Structural Steel Design (CIVL417) > Prerequisites
CIVL310 with a minimum grade D

Pre/Co CIVL365 with a minimum grade D
Structural Steel Design (CIVL417) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Determine the design loads on typical steel buildings including steel roof trusses or steel floor systems.

Evaluate the design strength of tension members resulting from different failure modes and design the optimal section.

Compute the design strength of compression members considering all possible failure modes and design the optimal section.

Compute the design strength of beams resulting from different failure modes and design the optimal section.

Analyze and design steel connections for axially-loaded steel members.

Develop computer-based design tools for steel members.

CIVL433.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL433 Highway Engineering
CIVL433.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL433
The course aims at covering aspects of geometric and structural design of highways. Aspects of geometric design include capacity calculations, sight distance, horizontal and vertical alignment, design of at-grade and grade- separated intersections. Aspects of structural design include loading analysis, design of asphalt layers, and design of hot asphalt mixes.
Highway Engineering (CIVL433) > Credit Hours : 3

Highway Engineering (CIVL433) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co CIVL335 with a minimum grade D
Highway Engineering (CIVL433) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Design geometric elements of highways.

Apply AASHTO standards for the design of highway elements

Design of asphalt mixes

Calculate design traffic loading

Design structural elements of pavements

CIVL442.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL442 Foundation Engineering
CIVL442.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL442
This course aims at developing an understanding of the application of soil mechanics to design of foundations. It includes subsurface exploration; bearing capacity and settlement calculations for shallow foundations, structural design of shallow foundations; capacity and settlement calculations for deep foundations; lateral earth pressure and retaining walls.
Foundation Engineering (CIVL442) > Credit Hours : 3

Foundation Engineering (CIVL442) > Prerequisites
CIVL340 with a minimum grade D

Pre/Co CIVL365 with a minimum grade D
Foundation Engineering (CIVL442) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognize the different subsurface exploration methods and field tests.

Differentiate between the different types of foundations and identify the function of each type.

Estimate settlement of shallow foundations.

Calculate the ultimate and allowable soil bearing capacity for shallow foundations.

Design isolated and combined footings.

Estimate the capacity of piles (side friction and end bearing).

Calculate the earth pressure on retaining walls and check the stability.

CIVL445.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL445 Construction Management
CIVL445.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL445
This course aims at introducing students to the different types and functions of management, project delivery methods, and types of contracts. It also includes the critical path method (CPM) and its application and the program evaluation and review technique (PERT) method of scheduling. In this course, students will also learn resource leveling and allocation, cost estimation and bidding, and overall project management using CPM. The course also includes several computer applications.
Construction Management (CIVL445) > Credit Hours : 3

Construction Management (CIVL445) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co GENG315 with a minimum grade D
Construction Management (CIVL445) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the basic concepts of construction management including types and functions of management, project delivery methods, and types of contracts.

Prepare early and detailed cost estimates for construction projects and estimate activity durations.

Plan and schedule construction projects using different planning and scheduling techniques, and use specialized scheduling software.

Manage construction projects, resources, and use specialized software for resource management

Perform cash flow analysis and overdraft calculations for construction projects considering various project-financing options.

Use specialized software for data management and formulate models of construction problems to find an optimum solution

Interpret construction project drawings, express ideas during classroom discussions, function effectively on teams, and communicate effectively while working in the term project.

CIVL485.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL485 Internship I
CIVL485.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL485
Students spend 8 weeks on a full-time basis in an engineering or consulting office in the UAE or abroad to earn practical skills. This course aims at offering career exploration opportunities for students.
Internship I (CIVL485) > Credit Hours : 1

Internship I (CIVL485) > Prerequisites
GENG215 with a minimum grade D

GENG230 with a minimum grade D

GENG315 with a minimum grade D

MATH135 with a minimum grade D or MATH210 with a minimum grade D

MATH275 with a minimum grade D

STAT210 with a minimum grade D

CIVL200 with a minimum grade D or CIVL220 with a minimum grade D

CIVL270 with a minimum grade D

CIVL310 with a minimum grade D

CIVL305 with a minimum grade D
Internship I (CIVL485) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Function effectively in multi-disciplinary teams and individually to achieve the planned tasks and goals

Develop communication skills through oral and written presentations

Evaluate different engineering situations and judgments based on ethical codes and professional responsibilities

CIVL490.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL490 Internship II
CIVL490.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL490
Students spend 8 weeks on a full-time basis in an engineering or consulting office in the UAE or abroad to earn practical skills. This course aims at offering career exploration opportunities for students as well as opportunities to correlate their academic preparation to the reality of conducting professional practice, to interact effectively with others in practice, to develop professional skills and communicate effectively in the workplace and to gain true practical experience that is necessary for their future practice as engineers in their respective discipline after graduation.
Internship II (CIVL490) > Credit Hours : 1

Internship II (CIVL490) > Prerequisites
PHYS110 with a minimum grade D

PHYS140 with a minimum grade D

CIVL330 with a minimum grade D

CIVL335 with a minimum grade D

CIVL340 with a minimum grade D

CIVL345 with a minimum grade D

CIVL360 with a minimum grade D or CIVL361 with a minimum grade D

CIVL362 with a minimum grade D

CIVL365 with a minimum grade D

Pre/Co CIVL485 with a minimum grade P
Internship II (CIVL490) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Function effectively in multi-disciplinary teams and individually to achieve the planed tasks and goals

Develop communication skills through oral and written presentations

Evaluate different engineering situations and judgments based on ethical codes and professional responsibilities

Propose ideas/solutions for real-life problems based on the learned knowledge

CIVL510.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL510 Special Topics in Structural Engineering
CIVL510.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL510
This course aims at introducing topics based on the recent developments and advances in structural engineering. It includes topics that are selected by the department based on the needs of students. The choice of the topics will be limited to the academic and financial resources of the department.
Special Topics in Structural Engineering (CIVL510) > Credit Hours : 3

Special Topics in Structural Engineering (CIVL510) > Prerequisites
CIVL365 with a minimum grade D
Special Topics in Structural Engineering (CIVL510) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply the principles of earthquake engineering in the design process of RC structures.

Determine earthquake loads using latest seismic provisions.

Evaluate wind loads using modern design codes.

Compute earthquake and wind loads of multi-story buildings using modern analysis tools.

Employ the underlying principles of prestressed concrete in the design of prestressed members.

Analyze and design prestressed concrete beams for flexure.

Perform analysis and design of prestressed concrete slabs.

CIVL515.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL515 Advances in Concrete Technology
CIVL515.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL515
This course provides an in-depth study of advanced materials, technologies, and performance-based approaches in modern concrete technology. The course covers concrete behaviour under different environmental conditions, supplementary cementing materials, reaction kinetics, microstructure development, and valorization of industrial wastes in concrete production. Emphasis is placed on special, innovative, and sustainable types of concrete with the incorporation of techno-economic analysis to evaluate their technical feasibility and cost-effectiveness. The course also introduces artificial intelligence techniques to predict the properties of concrete.
Advances in Concrete Technology (CIVL515) > Credit Hours : 3

Advances in Concrete Technology (CIVL515) > Prerequisites
CIVL360 with a minimum grade D or CIVL361 with a minimum grade D

CIVL362 with a minimum grade D
Advances in Concrete Technology (CIVL515) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the methods and performance of concrete under different environmental conditions.

Explain the chemical, physical, and microstructural mechanisms governing cementitious and alkali-activated systems.

Evaluate the effect of incorporating different supplementary cementing materials in concrete mixtures on its properties and reaction kinetics.

Evaluate the properties and techno-economics of special types of concrete.

Conduct various laboratory tests to evaluate concrete properties and interpret test results using AI-based tools, where applicable.

Communicate technical findings effectively through written reports, oral discussions, and professional presentations.

CIVL517.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL517 Matrix Structural Analysis
CIVL517.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL517
The course aims at the analysis of structural systems. It includes the review of structural mechanics and matrix algebra, formulation of stiffness matrices of linear elements, displacement method and introduction to finite element analysis. It sheds light on the use of software packages for structural analysis.
Matrix Structural Analysis (CIVL517) > Credit Hours : 3

Matrix Structural Analysis (CIVL517) > Prerequisites
CIVL310 with a minimum grade D
Matrix Structural Analysis (CIVL517) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop MS-Excel macros to formulate matrices and solve linear system of equations and to analyze 2D beam, frame, and truss structures.

Draw a line-model of any real structure and define joints, elements, supports, and degrees of freedom of a structure.

Formulate the global and local stiffness matrix for the beam, truss and frame elements and assemble the element stiffness matrices into the global stiffness matrix.

Formulate the local and global fixed-end reaction vectors for the beam and frame element.

Solve the structural stiffness equations and interpret the element end-force vectors for beam, truss, and frames structures.

Incorporate member end releases, intermediate hinge, temperature and support settlement loads into the matrix analysis of structures.

Use commercial structural analysis software, SAP2000, in solving assignment problems.

Express their ideas more effectively during classroom discussions.

CIVL520.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL520 Special Topics in Water Resources & Environmental Engineering
CIVL520.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL520
Topics will be decided by the department based on the recent developments in water resources and the environmental engineering field, and the needs of students. The choice of the topics will be limited to the academic and financial resources of the department.
Special Topics in Water Resources & Environmental Engineering (CIVL520) > Credit Hours : 3

Special Topics in Water Resources & Environmental Engineering (CIVL520) > Prerequisites
CIVL270 with a minimum grade D

CIVL400 with a minimum grade D
Special Topics in Water Resources & Environmental Engineering (CIVL520) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe and characterize contemporary water and/or environmental engineering problems.

Identify and describe modern solutions to water and/or environmental engineering problems.

Analyze and/or design water and/or environmental engineering solution elements.

Conduct an independent study pertaining to contemporary water and/or environmental engineering problems.

CIVL522.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL522 Advanced Environmental Engineering
CIVL522.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL522
This course aims to provide students the opportunity to learn about the different tools and techniques used to evaluate the environmental impact of human activities and the various strategies to mitigate negative effects. The course covers a broad range of topics, including environmental impact assessment, environmental policies, and environmental justice. The course will also focus on design components for unconventional water treatment, tertiary wastewater treatment, direct and indirect carbon capture, and/or bioremediation. In addition, the course will have a module on pollution prevention, which will cover strategies and sustainable practices for reducing pollution at the source.
Advanced Environmental Engineering (CIVL522) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Environmental Engineering (CIVL522) > Prerequisites
CIVL270
Advanced Environmental Engineering (CIVL522) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply the principles of environmental impact assessment of human activities.

Describe the major environmental policies and regulations that govern environmental engineering practice.

Analyze the social and ethical dimensions of environmental engineering, including issues of environmental justice and equity.

Design environmental engineering systems using appropriate modeling and simulation tools.

Evaluate the sustainability of environmental engineering designs and recommend strategies for reducing their environmental impact.

CIVL525.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL525 Hydrology
CIVL525.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL525
The course aims at introducing basic concepts of hydrology. It includes introduction to hydrology, hydrologic budget, hydrologic measurements and data, statistical methods in hydrology, point and areal precipitation, evaporation, infiltration, characteristics of drainage basins, stream flow measurements: stage, velocity, discharge, stream flow hydrograph, surface water runoff, base flow separation, estimation of surface runoff volume, unit hydrograph, types of aquifers and wells, physical properties of aquifers, hydraulic gradient, specific yield and specific storage, Darcy's law, groundwater flow nets, governing equations for flow in confined and phreatic aquifers, pumping and recovery tests, groundwater recharge, groundwater exploration and well construction.
Hydrology (CIVL525) > Credit Hours : 3

Hydrology (CIVL525) > Prerequisites
CIVL400
Hydrology (CIVL525) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Define and compute the components of the Hydrologic Cycle including Precipitation, Evapotranspiration, Infiltration, and Runoff, and relate them through Hydrological Budget.

Estimate Surface Water Runoff and derive Unit Hydrograph, Instantaneous Unit Hydrograph, and Synthetic Unit Hydrograph with their applications.

Calculate stream flow, derive the stage-discharge-rating curve, and apply it with the benefit-to-cost ratio curve.

Derive Stream Flow and Reservoir Flow routing curves.

Calculate the aquifer’s properties using Darcy’s rule applied to steady and unsteady flow systems.

Calculate aquifer’s properties using numerical modeling and present results in the form of technical reports.

CIVL526.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL526 Sustainable Solid Waste Engineering
CIVL526.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL526
This course provides an in-depth study of the solid waste engineering problem. It covers waste composition, characterization, collection and transfer, and the design of municipal solid waste handling processes, including: waste separation and recovery processes, composting, landfill disposal, incineration and energy recovery.
Sustainable Solid Waste Engineering (CIVL526) > Credit Hours : 3

Sustainable Solid Waste Engineering (CIVL526) > Prerequisites
CIVL270
Sustainable Solid Waste Engineering (CIVL526) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss the composition of solid waste and the factors that influence the solid waste management system

Evaluate different methods for the collection and separation of solid and hazardous waste

Design solid waste handling processes

Communicate results both written and orally

CIVL529.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL529 Coastal Engineering
CIVL529.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL529
The course provides knowledge of the fundamental theories of coastal waves including wave deformation in water, wave energy and transport potential, and wave-structure interaction. Additionally, students will apply the primary steps of design of coastal defense structures with reference to the relevant manuals such as the Coastal Engineering Manual.
Coastal Engineering (CIVL529) > Credit Hours : 3

Coastal Engineering (CIVL529) > Prerequisites
CIVL345

MATH275
Coastal Engineering (CIVL529) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Classify waves based on their characteristics

Calculate the parameters to define waves in motion and assess their energy

Calculate the spatial evolution of wave height and length along its path

Calculate the characteristic wave from time-series analysis

Calculate the potential sediment transport rate against wave conditions

Apply design steps of coastal defense structures

CIVL530.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL530 Special Topics in Transportation Engineering
CIVL530.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL530
Topics will be decided by the department based on the recent developments in transportation engineering and the needs of students. The choice of the topics will be limited to the academic and financial resources of the department.
Special Topics in Transportation Engineering (CIVL530) > Credit Hours : 3

Special Topics in Transportation Engineering (CIVL530) > Prerequisites
CIVL330
Special Topics in Transportation Engineering (CIVL530) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply the principles of traffic flow theory and modeling.

Apply the queueing theory principles to solve engineering problems.

Utilize modern software tools for network representation and traffic simulation.

Design pre-timed and actuated signalized intersections, and determine the signal splits.

Conduct traffic impact studies to assess the impacts of new developments.

Select among various traffic design alternatives that best integrate multiple objectives.

CIVL531.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL531 Topographic Surveying
CIVL531.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL531
This course aims at studying essential topics in topographic surveying. It includes establishment and calculations of circular compound and reverse curves, spirals, and vertical curves. Topics also cover precise leveling, establishment of horizontal control in the form of triangulation networks, and methods for monitoring stability of structures. An introduction to photogrammetry will be included. In addition, the course sheds light on the GPS satellite based measurements and positioning.
Topographic Surveying (CIVL531) > Credit Hours : 3

Topographic Surveying (CIVL531) > Prerequisites
CIVL335 with a minimum grade D or CIVL358 with a minimum grade D
Topographic Surveying (CIVL531) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Design and layout circular compound curves and reverse curves, spirals, and vertical curves.

Solve and design vertical control networks using precise leveling through advanced usage of level instruments.

Solve and design horizontal control networks in the form of triangulation, trilateration, and traverse networks.

Apply basic photogrammetric mapping principles for flight planning and determining ground point coordinates.

Describe the concept of the global positioning system, its satellites, and signal structures used in the GPS system.

Analyze and interpret data acquired using laser scanners for various derivatives.

Describe the common methods for monitoring stability of structures including geodetic and geotechnical methods.

CIVL534.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL534 Computer Aided Mapping
CIVL534.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL534
This course aims at studying the up-to-date techniques used in map generation aided by computer usage. Topics include Digital mapping and applications, and Digital terrain modeling. The course discusses different types of coordinate systems and their transformation. It introduces use of satellite positioning techniques in mapping and land information systems. The course also includes map projections methods and their applications.
Computer Aided Mapping (CIVL534) > Credit Hours : 3

Computer Aided Mapping (CIVL534) > Prerequisites
CIVL335 with a minimum grade D
Computer Aided Mapping (CIVL534) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the concept of computer-based Geographic Information Systems, digital maps, and data sources.

Apply digital mapping principles in the design, creation, interpretation, and analysis of digital maps from multiple data sources.

Design and apply the methods of producing digital terrain modeling, data sources and structures, calculation and use of topographic attributes, digital terrain analysis methods.

Analyze global and local geodetic and Cartesian datums, its transformation from/to other datums. Also analyze geodetic and Cartesian coordinate systems and their transformation.

Describe the concept of GNSS systems, its satellites, signal structures and its applications in mapping and land information systems.

Apply the concept of map projection methods and analyze the distortions induced by its usage including Universal Transverse Mercator UTM system.

Integrate acquired concepts and skills in the design and production of maps with the aid of computers using ArcGIS and AutoCAD software.

CIVL538.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL538 Advanced Highway Engineering
CIVL538.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL538
This course provides students an advanced knowledge about the elements of highway systems including human factors and vehicle characteristics. In addition, this course will cover highway capacity analysis methods. Since there have been remarkable advancements in highway design tools, some software tools such as Civil 3D and MX Road / Open Road will be introduced to students. Technical improvements in flexible and rigid pavement designs will also be discussed.
Advanced Highway Engineering (CIVL538) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Highway Engineering (CIVL538) > Prerequisites
CIVL433
Advanced Highway Engineering (CIVL538) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Relate vehicular movements and characteristics to the highway designs.

Recognize highway design elements related to human factors.

Conduct highway capacity analyses.

Examine newly developed highway design tools.

Investigate the advancement in flexible and rigid pavements.

CIVL539.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL539 Traffic Engineering
CIVL539.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL539
The course aims at studying the basics of traffic engineering and modeling of highway networks. Topics to cover include traffic capacity analysis, levels of service, delay calculations, fundamentals of signal design and timing, analysis and design of pre-timed signalized intersections, and actuated signals and detection. It also introduces traffic network simulation models for traffic modeling, evaluation, and assessment of effectiveness of design alternatives.
Traffic Engineering (CIVL539) > Credit Hours : 3

Traffic Engineering (CIVL539) > Prerequisites
CIVL330
Traffic Engineering (CIVL539) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the purpose of traffic engineering analyses and studies.

Classify and allocate traffic control devices.

Estimate traffic models based on traffic data.

Estimate and interpret traffic stream characteristics and parameters.

Conduct traffic-engineering studies such as speed, volume, accident, parking, travel-time, and delay studies.

Apply a number of statistical techniques in traffic engineering applications.

Assess highway operational quality by conducting highway capacity and level of service analyses.

Identify proper intersection control and signalization.

Design signal timing and conduct operational assessment of signalized intersections.

CIVL540.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL540 Special Topics in Construction Management
CIVL540.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL540
This course aims at studying topics that are decided by the department based on the recent developments in construction management and the needs of students. The choice of the topics will be limited to the academic and financial resources of the department.
Special Topics in Construction Management (CIVL540) > Credit Hours : 3

Special Topics in Construction Management (CIVL540) > Prerequisites
CIVL445
Special Topics in Construction Management (CIVL540) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the basic theories and techniques underpinning 3D, 4D and 5D Building Information Modeling.

Apply the basic theories and techniques underpinning Critical Path Method, line of balance, and flowline scheduling.

Select appropriate 3D model-surfaces to take off location-based quantities for a building construction project.

Develop an appropriate location break-down structure with a look-ahead consideration of schedule efficiency.

Make informed decisions about linking construction tasks and activities through layeredlogic dependencies for a building construction project.

Optimize construction schedules as per time, cost and risk constraints for a building construction project.

Determine optimized BIM level-of-detail (LOD) needed for construction planning purposes.

CIVL541.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL541 Special Topics in Soil Mechanics & Foundation Engineering
CIVL541.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL541
Topics will be decided by the department based on the recent developments in soil mechanics and foundation engineering, and the needs of students. The choice of the topics will be limited to the academic and financial resources of the departments.
Special Topics in Soil Mechanics & Foundation Engineering (CIVL541) > Credit Hours : 3

Special Topics in Soil Mechanics & Foundation Engineering (CIVL541) > Prerequisites
CIVL340 with a minimum grade D
Special Topics in Soil Mechanics & Foundation Engineering (CIVL541) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Estimate the factor of safety for slopes in cohesive soil using the moment area method.

Calculate the factor of safety for slopes in c-phi soils using the method of slices and Taylor method.

Calculate the factor of safety for infinite slopes.

Calculate the lateral earth pressure using Rankin theory and evaluate the sliding and overturning stability of gravity retaining walls.

Explain the soil stabilization techniques and identify the suitable techniques for given soil conditions.

CIVL547.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL547 Advanced Construction Management
CIVL547.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL547
This course aims at studying the advanced techniques used for the scheduling of construction project operations. This includes scheduling of repetitive and linear projects using the line of balance technique. It also includes project financing and progress control, time-cost tradeoff analysis, and optimum markup estimation. This course also includes application of computer project management packages to construction and case studies.
Advanced Construction Management (CIVL547) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Construction Management (CIVL547) > Prerequisites
CIVL445
Advanced Construction Management (CIVL547) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe various professional concepts of construction management including total quality management, project organization structures, value engineering, and claims and disputes.

Apply the linear scheduling method (LSM) and the line of balance (LOB) technique for scheduling linear and repetitive construction operations.

Identify the different scenarios related to schedule compression using time-cost tradeoff analysis.

Identify the information needed and approaches used to perform schedule updating.

Describe the issues related to project financing and project control including measuring schedule and cost progress using the earned value technique.

Analyze the different bidding strategies and the behavior of key bidding competitors to estimate an optimum markup.

CIVL548.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL548 Advanced Geotechnical Engineering
CIVL548.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL548
Topics include soil structures; primary and secondary clay minerals; diffuse double layer; soil water potential (soil suction); saturated and unsaturated water flow; heat flow in soils; soil stabilization; and slope stability analysis.
Advanced Geotechnical Engineering (CIVL548) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Geotechnical Engineering (CIVL548) > Prerequisites
CIVL340 with a minimum grade D
Advanced Geotechnical Engineering (CIVL548) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Differentiate between the different clay minerals, and soil structures.

Calculate the quantity of water flowing through single and multi-layer soils.

Design and draw flow nets for two-dimensional seepage problems and use them to calculate quantity of seepage and water pressure.

Identify suitable stabilization technique/s for a given soil.

Analyze the safety of a given soil slope.

CIVL552.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL552 Advanced Steel Design
CIVL552.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL552
This course aims at studying the design of built-up beams and plate girders. It also includes details of the design of composite beams. In addition, the course discusses the design and detailing of common building connections, rigid frames, roof trusses and structural steel building systems.
Advanced Steel Design (CIVL552) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Steel Design (CIVL552) > Prerequisites
CIVL417
Advanced Steel Design (CIVL552) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate the design strength of welded steel plate girders resulting from different failure modes and design the optimal section.

Compute the design strength of composite beams (steel beams with reinforced concrete slabs) considering all possible failure modes and design the optimal composite beam section.

Calculate the design strength of welded steel connections with axially-loaded steel members resulting from different welded connection failure modes.

Examine the design strength of bolted steel connections under i) shear and tension and ii) shear and torsion and of bolted steel base plate connections.

Probe the design strength of steel beam-column elements subjected to combined action of axial load and bending moment subsequent to different failure modes and design the optimal section.

Develop computer-based design and analysis tools for steel members and connections.

CIVL585.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL585 Design and Critical Thinking in Civil Engineering
CIVL585.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL585
This course concentrates on the rigors of communication, design, and critical thinking in an engineering context including problem identification, feasibility study of alternative solutions, preliminary design, technical writing, teamwork, and formal presentations. A team of students will apply the knowledge gained throughout their study to an engineering design project, emphasizing critical thinking, creativity, and originality. The selected alternatives will be the foundation of the capstone design project. A final report is required.
Design and Critical Thinking in Civil Engineering (CIVL585) > Credit Hours : 3

Design and Critical Thinking in Civil Engineering (CIVL585) > Prerequisites
PHYS110 with a minimum grade D

PHYS140 with a minimum grade D

MATH135 with a minimum grade D or MATH210 with a minimum grade D

MATH275 with a minimum grade D

GENG215 with a minimum grade D

GENG230 with a minimum grade D

GENG315 with a minimum grade D

CIVL305 with a minimum grade D

CIVL310 with a minimum grade D

CIVL330 with a minimum grade D

CIVL335 with a minimum grade D

CIVL340 with a minimum grade D

CIVL345 with a minimum grade D

CHEM270 with a minimum grade D or CIVL361 with a minimum grade D

CIVL360 with a minimum grade D or CIVL362 with a minimum grade D

Pre/Co CIVL365 with a minimum grade D

Pre/Co CIVL375 with a minimum grade D
Design and Critical Thinking in Civil Engineering (CIVL585) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the relevant theoretical background of a contemporary engineering problem

Apply the fundamentals of engineering-design and critical thinking, including the assessment and evaluation of alternative engineering solutions

Develop and conduct appropriate experimentation, modeling, simulation, and/or data analysis using engineering tools.

Communicate effectively through oral and written presentations.

Outline the principles of engineering ethics, and social and environmental responsibilities.

Recognize the need for ongoing additional knowledge, and the potential of integration and/or application of this knowledge effectively.

Develop leadership skills and project management techniques to independently and/or collaboratively handle complex professional tasks in a team-work context.

CIVL590.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL590 Capstone Engineering Design Project
CIVL590.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL590
This course builds on the outcomes of CIVL 585 course to perform detailed design and cost estimate of the selected alternative solutions to a well-defined engineering problem. Student teams are expected to apply knowledge gained throughout their studies to an engineering design project, emphasizing creativity and originality. A final report is required.
Capstone Engineering Design Project (CIVL590) > Credit Hours : 3

Capstone Engineering Design Project (CIVL590) > Prerequisites
CIVL585 with a minimum grade D
Capstone Engineering Design Project (CIVL590) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the theoretical background of a contemporary engineering problem.

Apply the fundamentals of engineering-design, including the assessment and evaluation of alternative engineering solutions.

Develop and conduct appropriate experimentation, modelling, simulation, and/or data analysis using modern engineering tools.

Communicate effectively through oral and written presentations.

Recognize the principles of engineering ethics, and social and environmental responsibilities.

Recognize the need for ongoing additional knowledge, and the potential of integration and/or application of this knowledge effectively.

Develop leadership skills and project management techniques to independently and/or collaboratively handle complex professional tasks in a team-work context.

CIVL600.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL600 Graduate Seminar
CIVL600.text:
Current research topics in Civil Engineering will be presented and discussed. Seminars will be delivered by faculty, staff and industry experts and professionals in the field. This is a pass or fail core course. Plan A students should present a research proposal to pass the course while Plan B students (non-thesis option) should present a summary report of the presented talks.
Graduate Seminar (CIVL600) > Credit Hours : 0

Graduate Seminar (CIVL600) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognize state-of-the-art research topics in Civil Engineering

Identify potential msc thesis research topic for students with the Thesis-Option

Recognize different research approaches in Civil Engineering

Communicate effectively in oral, written and express ideas with confidence

CIVL602.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL602 Environmental Impact Assessment Principles & Applications
CIVL602.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL602
Basic concepts; environmental policies; framework of environmental assessment; impact assessment methodologies; preparation of impact statements; air, water and soil qualities; noise; energy; vegetation; wildlife, marine life, and socioeconomic factors. Case studies.
Environmental Impact Assessment Principles & Applications (CIVL602) > Credit Hours : 3

Environmental Impact Assessment Principles & Applications (CIVL602) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify and apply laws, policies and institutional arrangements for conducting an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) of a proposed activity or project

Identify and apply local, regional and international guidelines for EIA studies (e.g. Environment Agency Abu Dhabi EIA guideline)

Identify the different steps of an EIA study (screening, scoping, baseline study, impact analysis and mitigation & monitoring)

Identify stakeholders and apply methods for public participation in the different steps of an EIA study

Effectively communicate and apply their knowledge in a multi-disciplinary EIA study team

Prepare an EIA study report on a proposed or existing project

Conduct professional presentations of EIA studies

Express their ideas more effectively during classroom discussion

CIVL605.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL605 Experimental Methods in Civil Engineering
CIVL605.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL605
Introduction to experimental methods, instrumentation, data acquisition, data processing, static and dynamic testing, overview of laboratory work with several hands-on applications in the laboratory, physical models in Structural Engineering, Physical models in Water Resources, Physical models in Geotechnical Engineering, Physical models in Highway Engineering, experimental project.
Experimental Methods in Civil Engineering (CIVL605) > Credit Hours : 3

Experimental Methods in Civil Engineering (CIVL605) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the advantages and limitations of experimental testing

Apply various instrumentations' principals to collect and analyze data and compute results

Design laboratory experiments to model real life situations and with respect to identifying required quantities to be measured and selecting suitable measuring instrumentations

Describe advanced tests for concrete characterization

Identify different geotechnical instrumentations principals to measure field quantities

Conduct geotechnical field test and collect and interpret data and results

Critically present and discuss advanced Civil Engineering monitoring techniques

CIVL610.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL610 Advanced Mechanics of Materials
CIVL610.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL610
Analysis and design of load-carrying members, shear center, unsymmetrical bending, curved beams, beams on elastic foundations, energy methods, theories of failure, thick-walled cylinders, stress concentrations, design to prevent failure by excessive elastic deformation, plastic deformation and fracture, buckling of bars.
Advanced Mechanics of Materials (CIVL610) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Mechanics of Materials (CIVL610) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply knowledge of mathematics and engineering to formulate engineering problems

Derive constitutive relations for the response of materials and understand their deformations under applied forces

Use the appropriate failure criteria for yield of brittle and ductile materials

Demonstrate the use of energy methods to calculate the displacement of indeterminate structures

Determine the stress and deformation of noncircular and open-sections in torsion

Determine the stresses in nonsymmetrical straight beams and the shear center for thin-walled cylinders

Identify stresses of curved beams when subjected to shear forces and bending moments

Give firm basis for advanced design topics while providing the foundation to handle more complex engineering problems

Provide the necessary foundation for plastic analysis to properly deal with steel structures

Communicate effectively in oral and written teamwork and express their ideas more effectively during classroom discussion

CIVL611.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL611 Structural Dynamics
CIVL611.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL611
Damped and undamped natural vibration, response of single- and multiple-degrees-of-freedom systems to steady-state and transient excitations, modal analysis, nonproportional damping and complex modes, variation formulation of equations of motion, discretization of structural systems for vibrational analysis, applications for earthquake and machinery loadings.
Structural Dynamics (CIVL611) > Credit Hours : 3

Structural Dynamics (CIVL611) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Comprehend the concepts related to structural dynamics

Apply the concepts related to structural dynamics in the design process

Determine the dynamic response under free and forced vibration, including harmonic and periodic excitations

Compute the dynamic response of generalized SDOF and MDOF systems

Evaluate the earthquake dynamics of elastic and inelastic SDOF and MDOF systems

Apply the principles of structural dynamics in analysis as per building codes

Perform analysis using structural dynamics and earthquake engineering software

CIVL612.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL612 Prestressed Concrete Structures
CIVL612.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL612
Basic concepts of prestressing, materials and systems for prestressing, partial losses of prestressing, behavior and design of simple span and continuous span prestressed concrete members in flexure and shear, application of prestressed concrete to columns, composite sections, and circular storage tanks.
Prestressed Concrete Structures (CIVL612) > Credit Hours : 3

Prestressed Concrete Structures (CIVL612) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate the instantaneous and time-dependent losses in prestressed concrete structures

Evaluate the internal stresses in a prestressed concrete element considering the critical loading stages

Perform analysis and design of prestressed concrete beams and slabs for flexure and shear using the ACI provisions

Compute and evaluate the short-term and long-term deflections of prestressed concrete beams using the ACI provisions

Identify the most appropriate structural system for complex prestressed concrete problems

Present and critique recent research related to prestressed concrete structures

Communicate effectively and express ideas with confidence

CIVL614.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL614 Design of Advanced Steel Systems
CIVL614.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL614
Review of the design of tension and compression members. Compression plates: stability, analysis, and design. Lateral torsional buckling of Beams. Design for torsion. Plate girders: stability, strength, and stiffener design. Design of different types of connections. Continuous beams and rigid frames: failure mechanisms and elastic/plastic design criteria. Braced and unbraced frames: stability and bracing requirements.
Design of Advanced Steel Systems (CIVL614) > Credit Hours : 3

Design of Advanced Steel Systems (CIVL614) > Prerequisites
CIVL417
Design of Advanced Steel Systems (CIVL614) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Design of tension and compression members

Analyze and design compression plates

Design structural elements for torsion

Design beams and plate girders including calculation for stability, strength, and stiffener design

Design of different types of connections

Analyze and design continuous beams and rigid frames

Identify stability and bracing requirements of braced and unbraced frames

Develop computer simple programs/Excel sheets that facilitate the design of steel structures

Communicate effectively; verbal and written

CIVL615.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL615 Bridge Engineering
CIVL615.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL615
History and development of bridges. Construction materials for Bridges. Bridge components. Bridge design philosophies. Loads on bridges. Slab-on-steel beam bridges (composite and non-composite construction). Plate-girder bridges. Box-girder bridges (straight and curved). General overview of special bridge types (arch and truss bridges, cable-supported bridges). Substructure design (piers and abutments). Bridge evaluation procedures - bridge rating.
Bridge Engineering (CIVL615) > Credit Hours : 3

Bridge Engineering (CIVL615) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Determine the self-weight of all the bridge components and estimate their resulting moments and shears. [PLO2]

Predict the live load effects on the various members of the bridge according to AASHTO LRFD Specifications. [PLO1, PLO2]

Develop computer models to design concrete and steel bridges. [PLO1, PLO2, PLO7]

Criticize available bridge issues. [PLO5]

CIVL616.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL616 Rehabilitation of Structures
CIVL616.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL616
Damage mechanisms, instrumentation and non-destructive test methods, conventional repair techniques, innovative repair and strengthening techniques with composites, case studies.
Rehabilitation of Structures (CIVL616) > Credit Hours : 3

Rehabilitation of Structures (CIVL616) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe damage mechanisms and principles of structural strengthening

Identify causes of defects, cracks, damage and deterioration of concrete structures

Develop an appropriate repair strategy for a deficient structure taking into consideration the social, economic and commercial aspects

Perform analysis and design of reinforced concrete elements strengthened with advanced composites using appropriate problem-solving approaches and international code provisions

Conduct experiments for condition assessment, corrosion monitoring, and strengthening of columns using advanced techniques

Report findings and critique recent research on assessment and rehabilitation of structures

Communicate effectively with peers and clients at a high level of proficiency

CIVL618.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL618 Construction Equipment & Methods
CIVL618.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL618
Major construction equipment and operations. Selection of construction equipment including scrapers, dozers, cranes, etc., based on applications, methods, and production requirements. Power generation, transmission, and output capacity of equipment. Calculation of transport cycle times. Concreting methods including mixing, delivery, and placement. Design of forms for concrete walls and supported slabs.
Construction Equipment & Methods (CIVL618) > Credit Hours : 3

Construction Equipment & Methods (CIVL618) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Select the most appropriate equipment/method for carrying out a construction process

Estimate the time and cost incurred by a construction process when using a particular equipment/method

Optimize construction operations and eliminate poor efficiency

Propose incremental productivity improvements based on highly sophisticated equipment/method analyses

Express their ideas and share their professional insights more effectively during classroom discussions

Trace recent technological developments of construction equipment and methods

Communicate effectively in oral, written and express ideas with confidence

CIVL620.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL620 Construction Cost Estimating
CIVL620.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL620
Conceptual and detailed cost estimating. Cost of different construction operations including handling and transporting materials, excavation, concrete structures, floor finishes, floor systems, masonry, carpentry, interior finishes, roofing and flashing, plumbing, steel structures. Estimation of profit and project budgeting.
Construction Cost Estimating (CIVL620) > Credit Hours : 3

Construction Cost Estimating (CIVL620) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Convert contract document information, using the masterformat specifications, to construction process cost elements

Evaluate the various types of contracts, bonds and insurances and their effect on cost estimation and bidding procedures

Perform detailed takeoffs and cost estimates to an acceptable level of reliability for various construction items including construction overheads, labor, equipment, excavation, concrete, steel and masonry

Perform semi-automatic takeoffs and cost estimates using specialized construction software

Express their ideas and share their professional insights more effectively during classroom discussions

Trace recent research trends and directions in the field of construction takeoff and cost estimation, while critically evaluating current techniques and practices

CIVL621.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL621 Advanced Foundation Design
CIVL621.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL621
Design of shallow foundations, bearing capacity and settlement, combined footings and rafts; eccentric and inclined loads, footings in slopes, machine foundations. Deep foundations; caissons and piers, piles, pile groups, tension piles. Tunnels and tunnel linings, flexible culverts. Earth pressures, retaining walls, sheeting and bracing, cofferdams. Case records of foundation performance including failures.
Advanced Foundation Design (CIVL621) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Foundation Design (CIVL621) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Use results of subsurface exploration techniques to evaluate the soil parameters

Evaluate the bearing capacity and settlement for shallow foundations (different BC theories and different loading and ground conditions), analyze settlement profiles and estimate associated problems for structures and cracking patterns, design combined footing and raft foundation

Estimate the bearing resistance of piles in soils, intermediate materials and rocks, interpret pile load test results using different techniques, evaluate the negative skin friction and its effect on the capacity of piles.

Recognize design considerations for foundations in difficult ground conditions (collapsible soils, swelling soil)

Evaluate ground surface settlement due to bored tunnels and assess the stability of bored tunnels during construction

CIVL622.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL622 Stability of Earth Supported Structures
CIVL622.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL622
Introduction, lateral earth pressure, gravity and cantilever walls, mechanically stabilized retaining walls, sheet pile walls, braced cuts, drilled shafts, caissons.
Stability of Earth Supported Structures (CIVL622) > Credit Hours : 3

Stability of Earth Supported Structures (CIVL622) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Calculate active and passive earth pressure on retaining walls using different theories

Evaluate stability of retaining walls

Evaluate straining actions in elements of different embedded wall systems (SPW, Soldier piles, Contiguous piles, Secant piles, Diaphragm walls)

Calculate earth pressure envelopes on braced cuts and evaluate the stability

Design mechanically stabilized walls and soil nails

CIVL623.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL623 Foundation Dynamics
CIVL623.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL623
Design of foundations subjected to vibratory and impulsive loadings, evaluation of dynamic soil properties, lumped mass analogies, earthquake effects in slope stability and earthwork structures.
Foundation Dynamics (CIVL623) > Credit Hours : 3

Foundation Dynamics (CIVL623) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognize the nature and different types of dynamic loading on soil

Describe the different modes of vibrations of a foundation-soil system, conduct lumped mass analogy, and evaluate the requirements for safe design

Explain the fundamentals of wave propagation in soil necessary to characterize the dynamic load

Estimate dynamic soil properties from results of laboratory and field tests

Evaluate the earth pressure values acting on retaining walls during an earthquake

CIVL624.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL624 Theory & Design of Pavement Structures
CIVL624.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL624
Theories of pavement behavior and concepts of pavement design, Pavement design considerations, Calculations of ESAL, Design reliability concept, AASHTO method for flexible pavement design, PCI method for flexible pavement design, AASHTO method for rigid pavement design, Economic Considerations.
Theory & Design of Pavement Structures (CIVL624) > Credit Hours : 3

Theory & Design of Pavement Structures (CIVL624) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe how material properties impact pavement design and performance

Describe the role of each layer forming a pavement structure

Evaluate pavement durability and reliability

Conduct analysis of flexible and rigid pavements in regards to stresses, strains, and deflections

Describe testing procedures to evaluate soil, as well as granular and bituminous materials used in pavement construction

Design flexible and rigid pavements based on mechanistic-empirical procedures

Identify various types of distresses occurring in different pavement layers and types

CIVL625.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL625 Pavement Management Systems
CIVL625.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL625
Stresses in flexible pavements, Stresses in rigid pavements, Pavement materials, distress survey and rating procedures, Non-destructive testing, Roughness measurements, Skid resistance measurements, Pavement serviceability index calculation, Pavement condition index calculations, Pavement condition prediction models, Network-level management, Project-level management, Computer applications in PMS.
Pavement Management Systems (CIVL625) > Credit Hours : 3

Pavement Management Systems (CIVL625) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Relate pavement stresses with pavement conditions

Identify data needs and formulate pavement performance models

Calibrate and evaluate pavement performance models

Use the models to predict pavement conditions

Identify and select maintenance and rehabilitation strategies to apply

Prioritize maintenance and rehabilitation projects

Use software output to make sound decisions

CIVL626.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL626 Advanced Traffic Engineering & Management
CIVL626.text:
