Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL626
Introduction to traffic flow theory, Traffic capacity analysis concepts, Highway capacity analysis of multilane uninterrupted flow facilities, Calibrating relationships for freeway analysis, Traffic control devices, Principles of intersection signalization, Signal design and timing, Analysis of signalized intersections, Actuated signals and detection, Signal coordination, Computer traffic control systems, Arterial design and management, Traffic simulation tools.
Advanced Traffic Engineering & Management (CIVL626) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Traffic Engineering & Management (CIVL626) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the principles of traffic flow theory and different traffic flow conditions

Code different traffic flow scenarios using microscopic and macroscopic simulation models

Identify the methodology defined in Highway Capacity Manual (HCM) to conduct different traffic studies

Design different types of traffic controllers for signalized intersection

Interact and communicate effectively via class technical discussions and presentations

Utilize modern traffic software tools for network representation and traffic simulation

Define multiple criteria and select the optimal solution among various alternatives to improve traffic flow conditions

CIVL627.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL627 Design of Transportation Systems
CIVL627.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL627
Characteristics of Urban travel and transportation systems, Transportation planning and decision making, Data management and diagnosis, Analysis and evaluation of transportation systems, Demand analysis, Supply analysis, Transportation systems evaluation, Program and project implementation, Intelligent transportation systems: introduction.
Design of Transportation Systems (CIVL627) > Credit Hours : 3

Design of Transportation Systems (CIVL627) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply the 4-step urban travel demand forecasting process

Plan, design, and conduct surveys related to transportation planning and design

Assign trips to network links using a number of traffic assignment techniques

Evaluate transportation systems applying advanced mathematical and statistical tools

Perform traffic analyses of transportation networks

Interact and communicate effectively via class technical discussions and term project presentations

Evaluate transportation alternatives and propose measures to mitigate traffic congestion and delay

CIVL628.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL628 Map Projections and Geometric Geodesy
CIVL628.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL628
Coordinate frames used in geodesy, Photogrammetry, Surveying and mapping, Cartesian, spherical, and ellipsoidal coordinates, Earth-fixed geocentric and topocentric frames, Fundamentals of mapping, Curvilinear coordinate systems, Mapping projections, Projection aspects, Distortion, Conformal mapping, State plane coordinate systems, Applications, Datums: global and local, horizontal and vertical, and three-dimensional, Geodetic reference systems.
Map Projections and Geometric Geodesy (CIVL628) > Credit Hours : 3

Map Projections and Geometric Geodesy (CIVL628) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the concepts of Mapping, Cartography, and Geodesy as related to map scale, geometrical transformations, map generalization and symbolism

Apply principles of geodesy in the analysis and computations of spherical earth modeling

Analyze and design ellipsoidal earth models and its relevant computations

Solve modeling problems using least-squares optimization

Identify the principles of geodetic datums, its transformations and applications

Apply and design map projection methods and analyze the distortions induced by its usage

Design and construct UTM map projections taking in to account aspect and distortion distributions

CIVL629.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL629 Digital Terrain Modeling & Applications
CIVL629.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL629
Global and local modelling strategies for topography, Elements of spatial topology and geomorphology, Breaklines, trends, periodicities and related features, Sampling techniques and accuracy considerations, Triangulation, tessellations and other partitions, Contouring shading and other graphical representations, Network modeling approaches of Werner and Warntz, Graph theoretic approach of Pfaltz, Contour trees and generalizations, Surface patchwork intelligent approach, Fractals and applications, Overview of data structures.
Digital Terrain Modeling & Applications (CIVL629) > Credit Hours : 3

Digital Terrain Modeling & Applications (CIVL629) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the terminology, importance, and need for dtms and its elements and models

Analyze surfaces and solid models through various interpolation methods

Apply geostatistics through variograms and kriging to analyze spatial DTM data

Identify DTM various data collection methods including ground surveys, photogrammetry, and LIDAR

Manipulate dtms to produce various derivatives including volume computations, contours, orthophotos, and drainage networks

Choose the appropriate data structure that represents DTM data including raster and TIN models

CIVL630.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL630 Special Topics in Civil Engineering
CIVL630.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL630
Different selected topics in Civil Engineering to complement the student's program. The executive committee of the program should decide the topics to be offered each semester based on the needs.
Special Topics in Civil Engineering (CIVL630) > Credit Hours : 3

Special Topics in Civil Engineering (CIVL630) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify selected topics in civil engineering to complement the student's study program

Improve skills on how to properly write scientific reports

Communicate effectively via class technical discussions and presentations

CIVL632.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL632 Structural Health Monitoring with AI Applications
CIVL632.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL632
This course introduces the principles and practical applications of Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) and smart infrastructure systems. Emphasis is placed on real-world monitoring, signal interpretation, and basic data-driven reasoning inspired by modern artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) concepts such as pattern recognition and trend analysis. Students will learn how sensors, data acquisition, and analytical tools can be used to assess the performance and safety of civil structures. The course provides introductory exposure to AI/ML algorithms commonly used in SHM, including basic supervised learning for damage detection and unsupervised techniques for anomaly identification. Targeted hands-on sessions will provide practical experience with low-cost sensors, data collection, interpretation of structural response, and application of artificial intelligence tools.
Structural Health Monitoring with AI Applications (CIVL632) > Credit Hours : 3

Structural Health Monitoring with AI Applications (CIVL632) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain principles of smart structural health monitoring in infrastructure systems.

Identify smart sensors and data acquisition systems used in structural health monitoring and their roles in maintenance and decision-making.

3. Apply artificial intelligence/machine learning and soft computing techniques for signal processing and structural damage detection.

Interpret monitored data to support maintenance and decision-making.

Communicate technical findings and solutions effectively through written reports and presentations.

CIVL633.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL633 Digital Twins Modeling for Integrated Infrastructure Systems
CIVL633.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL633
This course introduces the principles and applications of Digital Twins in the planning, design, construction, and operation of integrated infrastructure systems, including transportation and urban assets. Students will learn how to build dynamic digital representations of civil infrastructure using Building Information Modeling (BIM), Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Internet of Things devices, and artificial intelligence (AI) techniques. Emphasis is placed on integrating data from multiple sources across the infrastructure lifecycle to enable real-time monitoring, predictive analytics, automated maintenance, and data-driven decision-making that promote sustainability, efficiency, and resilience in infrastructure management. Students will learn how to use multi-source data throughout the infrastructure lifecycle to enable efficient and sustainable infrastructure management and improve construction productivity.
Digital Twins Modeling for Integrated Infrastructure Systems (CIVL633) > Credit Hours : 3

Digital Twins Modeling for Integrated Infrastructure Systems (CIVL633) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the principles, frameworks, and architectures of digital twins for integrated infrastructure systems.

Collect data from sensing, imaging, and other digital technologies to support digital twin development.

Develop BIM- and GIS-based digital models incorporating AI and analytics for system monitoring and prediction.

Apply digital twin technologies across the design, construction, and operational phases to improve infrastructure performance, construction productivity, and decision-making.

Evaluate the sustainability, efficiency, and resilience outcomes of infrastructure systems using data-driven and AI-supported approaches.

Communicate technical findings and solutions effectively through written reports and presentations.

CIVL634.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL634 Environmental Risk and Finance with AI Applications
CIVL634.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL634
This course introduces principles of environmental risk assessment and environmental finance in engineering systems. It covers climatic and health risks, uncertainty analysis, and probabilistic modeling, alongside techno-economic evaluation, carbon markets, and risk financing. Emphasis is placed on decision-making under risk and financial trade-offs. Artificial intelligence and machine learning are applied as advanced tools to support modeling, prediction, and risk-informed environmental and financial assessments.
Environmental Risk and Finance with AI Applications (CIVL634) > Credit Hours : 3

Environmental Risk and Finance with AI Applications (CIVL634) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate environmental and health risks using quantitative and probabilistic methods.

Design risk mitigation and resilience strategies for environmental engineering systems.

Analyze financial and techno-economic aspects of environmental engineering projects for decision-making.

Apply AI and machine learning techniques to support risk and financial assessment in environmental engineering.

CIVL650.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL650 Research Thesis
CIVL650.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL650
A directed research study on a topic relevant to the main specialization under the supervision of faculty advisor(s). The research should be conducted during two or more terms. A research thesis will be submitted upon advisor(s) approval at the end of the study and defended orally to a committee as stipulated by the University’s Graduate Studies regulations.
Research Thesis (CIVL650) > Credit Hours : 9

Research Thesis (CIVL650) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe highly specialized civil engineering principles, concepts, and methodologies

Evaluate the performance of advanced civil engineering systems and components through the use of applicable research principles, analytical methods or modeling techniques

Conduct advanced research to develop innovative solutions for highly complex civil engineering problems through the use of appropriately selected research methodologies and modern engineering tools

Apply advanced multidisciplinary problem-solving approaches to critically analyze contemporary, sophisticated, and highly complex civil engineering problems

Present and critique highly complex civil engineering issues and communicate effectively at a high level of proficiency

Lead professional activities and manage ethical issues in highly complex civil engineering projects

Implement the social, environmental, ethical, economic and commercial aspects to develop valid decisions affecting highly complex civil engineering projects

CIVL695.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL695 Technical Project
CIVL695.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL695
This course involves independent work on a design, simulation, modelling, or lab-based technical project. All projects must be supervised by a faculty member and the student is responsible for selecting his/her project supervisor. Project topics may be faculty-initiated, student-initiated, or suggested by industrial contacts. The student is expected to submit a brief description of a work plan by the end of the second week of the semester. The student is also required to submit a comprehensive final report and give an oral presentation during the last week of lectures of the semester.
Technical Project (CIVL695) > Credit Hours : 6

Technical Project (CIVL695) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop a work plan for a technical project in the field of Civil Engineering.

Apply advanced design, simulation, modelling, or experimental skills to a specific problem related to civil engineering.

Report findings in a well-written technical report.

Present results and findings at a high level of proficiency.

CIVL732.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL732 Sustainable Civil Infrastructure Engineering
CIVL732.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL732
This course provides the background required for modelling the interconnected nature of infrastructure systems and understanding the different types of interdependencies that exist between them. It also introduces the application of the three dimensions of sustainability, economic, environmental and social, towards the planning, design and operation of sustainable infrastructure systems. The course provides also the background necessary for performance-based design and durability analysis of civil engineering infrastructure. It provides an advanced knowledge on the use of recycled waste materials in sustainable civil engineering infrastructures. It introduces the concept of civil engineering infrastructure life cycle cost analysis and assessment
Sustainable Civil Infrastructure Engineering (CIVL732) > Credit Hours : 3

Sustainable Civil Infrastructure Engineering (CIVL732) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the different types of interdependencies that exist within and across different infrastructure sectors

Evaluate the impacts of infrastructure systems on sustainable economic, environmental and social dimensions and appreciate their interdisciplinary nature

Evaluate the impact of using alternative materials and methods on sustainability of civil engineering infrastructure.

Evaluate the durability performance and service life of concrete infrastructure

Apply concepts of life cycle cost analysis and assessment to civil engineering infrastructure

Report findings and communicate effectively with peers and clients

CIVL734.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL734 Earthquake Engineering
CIVL734.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL734
This course aims at introducing the central concepts in structural earthquake engineering. The topics covered include causes and measuring of earthquakes; lessons learned from previous earthquakes; structural response characteristics; key aspects of seismic design; structural configurations and systems for earthquake resistance; principles of seismic hazard assessment; earthquake input motion; and seismic response evaluation.
Earthquake Engineering (CIVL734) > Credit Hours : 3

Earthquake Engineering (CIVL734) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the earthquake causes and effects based on lessons learned from previous earthquakes.

Apply the principles of earthquake engineering to characterize structural response and deal with key aspects of seismic design.

Choose structural configurations and systems for effective earthquake resistance.

Determine the main features and representations of earthquake ground motion for assessment and design.

Evaluate actions and deformations of structural systems under the effect of earthquake loads.

CIVL737.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL737 Design of Concrete Structures with Fiber Reinforced Polymers
CIVL737.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL737
This course aims at developing an in-depth understanding of the performance and design of concrete structures internally-reinforced with fiber reinforced polymers (FRP) bars. The course introduces the students to the strut-and-tie modeling approach used for the design of FRP-reinforced concrete structures with discontinuity/disturbed regions (D-regions). Students will use modern software to simulate the behavior of complex FRP-reinforced concrete members. The course introduces the students to the Arrhenius concept used for service life prediction of FRP composites in harsh environments.
Design of Concrete Structures with Fiber Reinforced Polymers (CIVL737) > Credit Hours : 3

Design of Concrete Structures with Fiber Reinforced Polymers (CIVL737) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply advanced theories and modern software to develop innovative solutions for the design of complex of FRP-reinforced concrete members.

Apply Arrhenius concept to evaluate the long-term performance of FRP composite bars in harsh environments.

Discuss and critique recent research findings on FRP-reinforced concrete structures.

Communicate findings effectively, orally and in writing, with their peers and the engineering community.

CIVL738.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL738 Tunneling and Deep Excavation
CIVL738.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL738
History of tunneling; functions, types of tunnels; Geotechnical aspects in tunneling; Excavation methods and construction techniques; Prediction of ground deformation due to tunneling; Effect of ground deformation on existing structures; Types of tunnel lining; Design methods for tunnel lining; Instrumentation and monitoring. Braced excavations; straining actions in support elements of deep excavations
Tunneling and Deep Excavation (CIVL738) > Credit Hours : 3

Tunneling and Deep Excavation (CIVL738) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the evolution of construction methods of tunnels over time, recommend and justify the use of a construction method suitable for a given geotechnical condition, and assess the stability of tunnels during construction.

Estimate the ground settlement due to tunneling and its effect on nearby structures or utilities and explain and justify the assumptions used in the analysis.

Apply principles of soil-structure interaction to estimate straining actions in tunnel lining and justify the assumptions incorporated in these design principles.

Assess the stability of supported excavations, calculate the straining actions in support elements of an excavation, and explain the limitations of the currently used methods of analysis.

Present findings of a term project and communicate effectively with peers.

CIVL739.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL739 Contaminant Subsurface Hydrology
CIVL739.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL739
Description and quantification of solute transport processes (diffusion, dispersion, advection, sorption, transformations, etc.) in porous media. Physical-chemical-biological concepts of retention and transport of water and solutes in unsaturated and saturated media. Formulation and solution of solute transport equations, modeling of water flow and solute transport equations. Applications: Groundwater contamination and site remediation
Contaminant Subsurface Hydrology (CIVL739) > Credit Hours : 3

Contaminant Subsurface Hydrology (CIVL739) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify advanced concepts of water and solute transport in groundwater.

Apply the theoretical aspects of water and solute transport in porous media.

Recognize the inter-relationships among various physical, chemical, and biological processes that influence solute transport in porous media.

Apply analytical and numerical modeling approaches to solve contaminant transport problems.

Compare different techniques to remediate contaminated groundwater sites.

Report findings and communicate effectively with peers.

CIVL742.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL742 Sustainable Water Treatment Systems
CIVL742.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL742
This course covers sustainability issues as they apply to water treatment systems. Topics will cover two broad issues related to sustainable water treatment technologies and management of water treatment systems. Sustainable water treatment technologies will focus on wastewater reclamation, grey water utilization, and use of nanomaterial and green technologies for water treatment. Management of water treatment systems will include risk assessment, economic assessment and asset management. Throughout the course, case studies, application examples and numerical problems will be presented
Sustainable Water Treatment Systems (CIVL742) > Credit Hours : 3

Sustainable Water Treatment Systems (CIVL742) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Critically review emerging issues pertaining to sustainable water treatment technologies.

Describe current and potential applications of nano and green technologies for water treatment.

Assess the impact and risk emanating from emerging contaminants in water.

Compare between greywater treatment alternative processes.

Discuss issues pertaining to the economic and environmental sustainability of water treatment systems.

Report findings and communicate effectively with peers.

CIVL743.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL743 Urban Traffic Control Systems
CIVL743.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL743
This course introduces the students to various topics of relevance to the design, operation, and management of traffic flow over complex urban traffic networks. It covers mainly the traffic flow modeling and traffic flow operations. Sub-topics include dynamic traffic assignment, network optimization techniques, advanced queuing theory, transit systems preemption, incident management, and integrated control systems
Urban Traffic Control Systems (CIVL743) > Credit Hours : 3

Urban Traffic Control Systems (CIVL743) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop network models using dynamic traffic assignment concepts.

Apply optimization techniques for the network models.

Apply queuing theory principles for various transportation systems applications.

Explain the basics of incident detection in urban traffic networks.

Evaluate transit signal preemption control methodologies.

Conceptualize advanced integrated control of traffic signals.

Communicate the findings of term project effectively with peers.

CIVL746.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL746 Transport Economics and Transit Systems Operation Management
CIVL746.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL746
This course is aimed at covering relevant topics related to applied transport economics, including transport demand, supply, and costs, as well as applications of cost-benefit analyses in the transportation context. The course is also aimed at exposing students to transport pricing practices and transport financing alternatives. This course also entails introducing data needs for evaluating and managing transit systems and developing the skills of using various analytical methods. Methods entail the use of Simulators, Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA), and Technique of Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS). Several issues concerning the efficiency and effectiveness of transit systems as well as accessibility are discussed through real-life examples and data.
Transport Economics and Transit Systems Operation Management (CIVL746) > Credit Hours : 3

Transport Economics and Transit Systems Operation Management (CIVL746) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply principles related to Transport Economics.

Explain aspects related to transport demand, supply, and costs.

Propose transport pricing schemes and financing alternatives.

Conduct cost-benefit analyses in the transportation context.

Explain the transit systems operation aspects, as well as data needs for operation assessment and management.

Apply simulation models for traffic network and transit systems evaluation.

Apply Data Envelopment Analysis for assessment of transit systems efficiency and effectiveness.

Apply TOPSIS models for assessment of transit systems accessibility.

CIVL748.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL748 Durability of Concrete
CIVL748.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL748
This course provides students with an advanced understanding of durability of concrete as a construction material, transport phenomena, physicochemical, and electrochemical deterioration mechanisms in concrete, and service life modelling and prediction. The course covers long-term design approaches for concrete and AI-driven predictive models for durability-related properties and service life of concrete. It also examines the synergy of engineering and costs aspects of concrete subjected to various exposure and operational environments.
Durability of Concrete (CIVL748) > Credit Hours : 3

Durability of Concrete (CIVL748) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze physicochemical and electromechanical mechanisms governing durability of concrete.

Explain advanced transport phenomena in concrete.

Apply durability-based design principles to enhance the long-term performance and service life of concrete.

Assess long-term behavior and develop prediction models for concrete, including empirical and AI-driven approaches.

Report findings and communicate effectively with peers and clients.

CIVL751.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL751 Engineering Risk Assessment and Management
CIVL751.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL751
This course will provide students with a thorough understanding of effective planning for risk management. Students will learn how to identify project risks, prioritize identified risks, analyze and evaluate these risks, and develop responses for high priority risks. The course will also introduce students to risk response planning, risk monitoring, and risk control. The course will focus on the PMI Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK) process of risk management. Students will also learn how to identify and analyze risks related to a project’s scope, schedule, and resources. The course will introduce students to advanced tools and techniques used for risk management. Applications to case studies will be covered
Engineering Risk Assessment and Management (CIVL751) > Credit Hours : 3

Engineering Risk Assessment and Management (CIVL751) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify project risk events and the priorities of identified risks

Analyze and evaluate project risks

Develop responses for high priority project risks

Develop a plan to monitor and control project risks

Report findings and communicate effectively with peers and clients.

CIVL753.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL753 Intelligent Geospatial Observation Systems and Analytics
CIVL753.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL753
This course provides an advanced exploration of spatial data acquisition, multi-sensor geomatics technologies, and analytical methods used in civil and environmental engineering systems. Emphasis is placed on engineering decision-making, environmental processes, sustainability-driven applications, and research-grade analytics. Students will study recent advancements in GNSS, LiDAR, UAV photogrammetry, and SAR/optical remote sensing with explicit applications in water resources, environmental monitoring, climate resilience, land subsidence, infrastructure deformation, and sustainable engineering systems. The course integrates advanced spatial datasets using stochastic modelling and AI-driven spatio-temporal analytics, and introduces techno-economic to assess cost–performance–risk trade-offs, value of information, in support of informed engineering and sustainability decisions.
Intelligent Geospatial Observation Systems and Analytics (CIVL753) > Credit Hours : 3

Intelligent Geospatial Observation Systems and Analytics (CIVL753) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate advanced geodetic and spatial reference frameworks.

Evaluate advanced remote sensing and geomatics observation systems.

Analyze uncertainty, error propagation, and system reliability.

Integrate large-scale, multi-source geospatial datasets within Big Data environments using AI-driven techniques to support cost-effective and sustainable engineering solutions.

Communicate assessment results through professional reports and presentations.

CIVL850.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL850 Candidacy Exam
CIVL850.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL850
The Candidacy Exam for the PhD in Civil Engineering is a non-credit Pass/Fail exam. Students have up to two trials to pass the exam; upon passing it, the student becomes a PhD candidate. The Candidacy Exam is structured to evaluate the student’s breadth and depth of fundamental knowledge in the area(s) closely related to the thesis work. The Candidacy Exam committee, in consultation with the advisor, decides on the topic(s) of the Candidacy Exam. The PhD student prepares a concise and comprehensive research proposal that clearly defines the research problem and objectives and outlines the research methodology that he/she plans to follow. The concerned PhD student should present and defend his/her proposal in front of the Candidacy Exam committee.
Candidacy Exam (CIVL850) > Credit Hours : 0

Candidacy Exam (CIVL850) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate the depth and breadth of their knowledge in the field of civil engineering relevant to student’s research topic.

Propose a well-structured research project that outlines clear objectives, a detailed plan, and an appropriate methodology.

Exhibit sufficient communication skills relevant to field of study and the research topic.

CIVL900.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL900 Dissertation Doctoral Research
CIVL900.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL900
Open to students who have successfully completed the comprehensive exam. PhD student conducts original research under the direction of a supervisory committee. Credits are determined in consultation with the dissertation supervisor.
Dissertation Doctoral Research (CIVL900) > Credit Hours : 30

CIVL910.title: UAEU Catalog — CIVL910 Dissertation Defense
CIVL910.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=CIVL910
Two part exam, open and close, to defend the results of PhD research work
Dissertation Defense (CIVL910) > Credit Hours : 0

Dissertation Defense (CIVL910) > Prerequisites
CIVL850
Dissertation Defense (CIVL910) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Assess primary literature and explain areas of active research in the chosen field

Discuss research design, including results, recommendations, and conclusions

Communicate research outcomes logically and persuasively both in writing and orally

Evaluate the study results in line with the research design, including ethical and professional considerations

ENVE700.title: UAEU Catalog — ENVE700 Aquatic Chemistry
ENVE700.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=ENVE700
The goal of this course is to introduce students to the concepts and models used in aquatic chemistry while providing a foundation in the basic principles used in the chemical aspects of environmental science. The course content is centered on the chemical equilibrium and kinetic analysis of the speciation, transformation and partitioning of (primarily) inorganic chemical species in aqueous systems; including the aqueous components of surface and groundwater systems, soils, and the atmosphere. Emphasis is on the study of acid-base chemistry, complexation, precipitation-dissolution and reduction-oxidation reactions.
Aquatic Chemistry (ENVE700) > Credit Hours : 3

Aquatic Chemistry (ENVE700) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Formulate appropriate solutions for aqueous speciation.

Characterize speciation involved in carbonate chemistry.

Determine the state of aqueous metals.

Solve complex solutions with heterogeneous chemistry.

Identify gaps in the current state of knowledge.

ENVE710.title: UAEU Catalog — ENVE710 Contaminant Fate and Transport
ENVE710.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=ENVE710
This course aims at introducing students to the fundamental processes controlling the fate and transport of chemicals in natural and engineered settings, and how these processes are described, modeled, monitored, and quantified.
Contaminant Fate and Transport (ENVE710) > Credit Hours : 3

Contaminant Fate and Transport (ENVE710) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Assess the significance and uncertainty of individual processes controlling the fate and transport of chemicals mathematically.

Estimate the fate of chemicals in surface waters (streams, rivers, lakes, estuaries, wetlands).

Formulate chemical fate and transport to subsurface environment (groundwater) mathematically.

Characterize the fate of pollutants in the atmosphere.

Communicate findings on the current state of knowledge.

ENVE720.title: UAEU Catalog — ENVE720 Biological Treatment of Waste Streams
ENVE720.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=ENVE720
This course aims at evaluating microorganisms, their metabolism, nutrient requirements, substrate requirements, environmental conditions for growth and control, and other interactions that are important in biological treatment processes in water, air, and soil. Different biological processes for the removal of organic matter and nutrients will also be investigated. In addition, key factors governing waste treatment kinetics and their applications to the analysis of the biological processes will be discussed.
Biological Treatment of Waste Streams (ENVE720) > Credit Hours : 3

Biological Treatment of Waste Streams (ENVE720) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the fundamentals of biological treatment.

Evaluate the effectiveness of aerobic processes for the treatment of organics.

Calculate the effectiveness of nutrient treatment processes.

Formulate appropriate solutions for different unit operations and advanced treatment processes.

Identify gaps in the current state of knowledge.

ENVE730.title: UAEU Catalog — ENVE730 Physical and Biochemical Treatment Processes
ENVE730.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=ENVE730
This course aims to cover various advanced treatment mechanisms and processes. The focus is on physical, chemical, and biochemical processes. Each process is described in terms of its typical function, theoretical fundamentals, reaction kinetics involved, design considerations, factors influencing its efficiency, and advances in its implementation.
Physical and Biochemical Treatment Processes (ENVE730) > Credit Hours : 3

Physical and Biochemical Treatment Processes (ENVE730) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Characterize aqueous and environmental contaminants or pollutants.

Design carbon adsorption beds to purify water.

Determine optimal design parameters used for air stripping towers.

Identify the essential factors involved in a successful membrane treatment process.

Design advanced oxidation treatment options for wastewater treatment.

Outline the advances in the field of bioremediation.

ENVE740.title: UAEU Catalog — ENVE740 Advanced Topics in Environmental Engineering
ENVE740.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=ENVE740
The goal of this course is to introduce students to an advanced topic in environmental engineering focused on the one of the following environmental engineering fields: a) solid waste management, b) air pollution, or c) hazardous waste management. One choice out of these three fields will be made each class offering. The content will be designed every offering to cater for the interest of the exiting PhD students with emphasis on new frontiers.
Advanced Topics in Environmental Engineering (ENVE740) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Topics in Environmental Engineering (ENVE740) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate the effectiveness of a treatment solution for an environmental problem.

Review the literature of a current environmental challenge.

Identify gaps in the current state of knowledge.

Propose a solution for the current environmental challenge.

ENVE750.title: UAEU Catalog — ENVE750 Environmental Systems Analysis
ENVE750.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=ENVE750
This course introduces an integrated framework for environmental systems analysis to evaluate and improve the climate neutrality and sustainability of engineering systems and processes. It covers analytical tools for quantifying climate impacts, including global warming potential and carbon footprint analysis, and examines sustainability across environmental, economic, and social dimensions. Core methods include Environmental Life Cycle Assessment, Life Cycle Costing Assessment (including technoeconomic analysis), Social Life Cycle Assessment, and material and substance flow analysis. The course incorporates AI-enabled approaches and apply software tools for LCA modeling, uncertainty analysis, and perturbation analysis, and applies multi-criteria decision analysis to support SDG-aligned engineering decisions.
Environmental Systems Analysis (ENVE750) > Credit Hours : 3

Environmental Systems Analysis (ENVE750) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate climate neutrality of engineering interventions through relevant impact metrics.

Analyze material and substance flows contribution to sustainability performance.

Evaluate life cycle sustainability using appropriate software tools and AI-enabled methods.

Communicate assessment results through professional reports and presentations.

ENVE800.title: UAEU Catalog — ENVE800 Comprehensive Exam
ENVE800.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=ENVE800
Every PhD student must pass a Comprehensive Examination (CE) designed to evaluate the breadth and depth of the student’s knowledge of his or her discipline. The CE consists of a written and an oral part and will be prepared, administered, and evaluated by an examination committee from the student’s concerned department. It must be taken before the start of the student’s fifth semester in the program. Students taking the CE must be in good academic standing after completion of the required coursework. The CE may be repeated only once, no later than the end of the student’s fifth semester. A second unsuccessful attempt leads to immediate termination of the student’s enrollment in the PhD program. The CE course is non-credit rated, while a Pass or Fail result for each attempt will be recorded on the student’s academic transcript.
Comprehensive Exam (ENVE800) > Credit Hours : 0

Comprehensive Exam (ENVE800) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate the depth and breadth of their knowledge in the designated engineering discipline.

Demonstrate sufficient communication skills relevant to the specific field.

ENVE810.title: UAEU Catalog — ENVE810 Prospectus Exam
ENVE810.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=ENVE810
The Prospectus Examination is a non-credit rated Pass/Fail exam. A PhD student should prepare a concise and complete Research Proposal that clearly defines the research problem and objectives and outlines the research methodology that the student plans to follow. The content and format of the Research Proposal must follow the PhD Research Proposal Preparation Guidelines issued by the CGS. The concerned PhD student should present and defend his/her Research Proposal in front of the Prospectus Examination Committee and Advisory Committee members. The Prospectus Examination results will be recorded on the student’s academic transcript.
Prospectus Exam (ENVE810) > Credit Hours : 0

Prospectus Exam (ENVE810) > Prerequisites
ENVE800
Prospectus Exam (ENVE810) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Prepare a concise and complete Research Proposal that outlines the research questions and objectives, as well as the proposed methodology to conduct the work.

Present and defend the Research Proposal to the Prospectus Examination Committee and Advisory Committee members.

ENVE850.title: UAEU Catalog — ENVE850 Candidacy Exam
ENVE850.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=ENVE850
Candidacy Exam (ENVE850) > Credit Hours : 0

Candidacy Exam (ENVE850) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate the depth and breadth of their knowledge in the field of environmental engineering relevant to student’s research topic.

Propose a well-structured research project that outlines clear objectives, a detailed plan, and an appropriate methodology.

Exhibit sufficient communication skills relevant to field of study and the research topic.

ENVE900.title: UAEU Catalog — ENVE900 Dissertation Doctoral Research
ENVE900.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=ENVE900
Student conducts high quality academic research under the direction of his/her supervisor. Student and supervisor shall meet on regular basis and discuss progress and issues related to the student’s dissertation research. Furthermore, the student writes an annual report based on a meeting with supervisor and Advisory Committee, in which a review is conducted to determine progress, identify problems, and project dates for completion of various tasks. The research shall represent original contribution to human knowledge in the particular academic field and is presented in a written research dissertation of a publishable standard. The document shall also demonstrate the candidate’s acquaintance with the literature in the field and the proper selection and execution of research methodology. The physical form of the dissertation must comply with the regulations stated in the Thesis and Dissertation Preparation Guidelines, issued by the College of Graduate Studies
Dissertation Doctoral Research (ENVE900) > Credit Hours : 30

Dissertation Doctoral Research (ENVE900) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Conduct independent research in a specific research area.

Produce a dissertation of publishable academic quality.

ENVE901.title: UAEU Catalog — ENVE901 Dissertation Doctoral Research
ENVE901.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=ENVE901
Student conducts high quality academic research under the direction of his/her supervisor. Student and supervisor shall meet on regular basis and discuss progress and issues related to the student’s dissertation research. Furthermore, the student writes an annual report based on a meeting with supervisor and Advisory Committee, in which a review is conducted to determine progress, identify problems, and project dates for completion of various tasks. The research shall represent original contribution to human knowledge in the particular academic field and is presented in a written research dissertation of a publishable standard. The document shall also demonstrate the candidate’s acquaintance with the literature in the field and the proper selection and execution of research methodology. The physical form of the dissertation must comply with the regulations stated in the Thesis and Dissertation Preparation Guidelines, issued by the College of Graduate Studies.
Dissertation Doctoral Research (ENVE901) > Credit Hours : 42

Dissertation Doctoral Research (ENVE901) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Conduct independent research in a specific research area.

Produce a dissertation of publishable academic quality.

ENVE910.title: UAEU Catalog — ENVE910 Dissertation Defense
ENVE910.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=ENVE910
Student defends his/her research dissertation in the form of an oral presentation in a public session, followed by a closed session, before a dissertation examination committee, which includes internal and external examiners. The Dissertation Defense course is non-credit rated, while a Pass or Fail result for each attempt will be recorded on the student’s academic transcript.
Dissertation Defense (ENVE910) > Credit Hours : 0

Dissertation Defense (ENVE910) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Define and articulate research gaps in the current state of knowledge, as well as knowledge advancement in the research area. [PLO1, 2]

Apply research methodologies and analyze research results in light of the proposed research questions. [PLO2]

Respond appropriately to technical questions posed by members of the dissertation examination committee members and the public. [PLO1, 3]

Effectively present the dissertation in public and in front of the dissertation examination committee. [PLO3]

Present and discuss the implications of various findings, including their impact and limitations. [PLO3, 4]

WATR601.title: UAEU Catalog — WATR601 Fluid Mechanics for Non Eng.
WATR601.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=WATR601
Definitions, Dimensions and units, dimensional homogeneity, characteristics of fluids, Fluid Statics: Hydrostatic Pressure and manometers, Types of Flow, Forces and Motion, Basic Laws: Continuity equation, momentum equation, and energy equation, Applications to the basic laws, Uniform, Rapid and Gradually Varied flow in Open Channels, dimensional analysis, physical models.
Fluid Mechanics for Non Eng. (WATR601) > Credit Hours : 3

Fluid Mechanics for Non Eng. (WATR601) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Define and calculate important fluid properties using the force/mass systems and Si/Bg units

Calculate the hydrostatic pressure at any point in fluids at rest

Calculate the hydrostatic force on submerged surfaces

Calculate forces in flow fields using the momentum equation

Calculate the pressure and velocity heads under different flow conditions and draw the hydraulic grade line and the total energy line

Formulate equations using dimensional analysis and determine prototype behavior using hydraulic similarity

WATR602.title: UAEU Catalog — WATR602 Water Resources Management
WATR602.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=WATR602
Availability of water resources, demands, supplies, reservoirs operation, planning and development, re-use and disposal of re-used water, economic valuation techniques and impact analysis, human resources development, social aspects of water resources development.
Water Resources Management (WATR602) > Credit Hours : 3

Water Resources Management (WATR602) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify institutions of the water sector and recognize the important parts of water infrastructure projects.

Identify the different steps in the planning and decision making process in the water sector.

Analyze water systems

Evaluate water projects using economic tools.

Identify social impacts of water resources management.

Conduct projects on contemporary issues related to water resources management.

WATR603.title: UAEU Catalog — WATR603 Surface Water Hydrology
WATR603.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=WATR603
Hydrologic measurements and data, Statistical methods in hydrology, Precipitation, Evaporation and Transpiration, Water Budget, Infiltration, stream flow measurements, Watersheds and drainage basins, Rainfall-runoff, Hydrographs, an introduction to hydrological modeling.
Surface Water Hydrology (WATR603) > Credit Hours : 3

Surface Water Hydrology (WATR603) > Prerequisites
WATR601 with a minimum grade C or CIVL345 with a minimum grade D
Surface Water Hydrology (WATR603) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Quantify the different surface hydrological processes (precipitation, infiltration, evapotranspiration, runoff, and streamflow), and describe how they are affected by land surface conditions.

Describe hydrological processes by means of conservation equations.

Solve (analytically as well as numerically) conservation equations in order to quantify the hydrological fluxes.

Apply hydrological models to estimate hydrological fluxes or relate between land surface conditions and hydrological processes.

Analyze scientific literature on surface water hydrology and discuss the approach and main conclusions of the papers with fellow hydrologists.

Express their ideas more effectively in their submitted assignments and during classroom discussions.

WATR605.title: UAEU Catalog — WATR605 Introduction to Water Science and Technology
WATR605.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=WATR605
This course introduces the students to surface and ground water resources, non-conventional water resources, types of desalination, new technologies in water reuse and recycling in different sectors. It examines current and future plight of water shortages and water quality issues. It also introduces aspects of water and wastewater quality assessment and treatment.
Introduction to Water Science and Technology (WATR605) > Credit Hours : 3

Introduction to Water Science and Technology (WATR605) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe and use scientific and technical terms and concepts related to surface and ground water, water quality, water usage, water treatment, sewage treatment, and water supply and collection

Analyze, interpret and write about water quality and quantity data

Describe basic physical, chemical, and microbiological processes within different water contexts

Apply the basic principles and equations for water and wastewater storage and treatment

Manage their own water resources study

WATR606.title: UAEU Catalog — WATR606 Water Quality
WATR606.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=WATR606
Sources and uses of water. Water characteristics. Water pollution, physical, chemical, biological and radiological pollutants. Risk and hazard index. Water quality standards. Sampling, measurement and analysis of water. Pollution control.
Water Quality (WATR606) > Credit Hours : 3

Water Quality (WATR606) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze and evaluate physical, chemical and biological water quality parameters

Assess the risk of water contamination and quantify the hazard index

Interpret contaminant mobility in terms of influencing transport mechanisms.

Differentiate between various water and wastewater treatment techniques and their intended uses.

Conduct an independent study related to water quality.

WATR608.title: UAEU Catalog — WATR608 Graduate Seminar
WATR608.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=WATR608
Presentations by faculty and professionals on different topics related to Water Resources, Presentations by students on their research interest, Thesis Proposal (Thesis option).
Graduate Seminar (WATR608) > Credit Hours : 0

Graduate Seminar (WATR608) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognize contemporary research topics in Water Resources.

Identify potential master thesis research topics.

Recognize different research approaches in Water Resources.

Communicate effectively by oral means.

WATR611.title: UAEU Catalog — WATR611 Hydraulics of Closed Conduits
WATR611.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=WATR611
Pipe transmission design. Flow control and measurement. Selection of pumps. Forces in pipelines. Hydraulics of valves, transients and cavitation. Computer applications in water supply systems, extended period simulation in pipe networks.
Hydraulics of Closed Conduits (WATR611) > Credit Hours : 3

Hydraulics of Closed Conduits (WATR611) > Prerequisites
WATR601 with a minimum grade C or CIVL345 with a minimum grade D
Hydraulics of Closed Conduits (WATR611) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Determine the water capacity/demand of a public water supply system.

Design key components of a water transmission line.

Analyze and design water distribution networks.

Describe and calculate common pipe flow perturbations and provide technical options to improve any shortcomings identified.

Describe pipe networks components, material, construction, operation and maintenance.

Apply computer software to analyze and design water pipe networks.

WATR615.title: UAEU Catalog — WATR615 Groundwater Hydrology
WATR615.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=WATR615
Types of Aquifers, Darcy equation, Aquifer characterization. Types of Models, Governing equations, initial and boundary conditions, closed form solutions, numerical techniques, development of a conceptual model, Flow and transport models, data requirement, verification, calibration and validation of numerical models, MODFLOW, Applications and study cases. Groundwater contamination and transport processes.
Groundwater Hydrology (WATR615) > Credit Hours : 3

Groundwater Hydrology (WATR615) > Prerequisites
WATR601 with a minimum grade C or CIVL345 with a minimum grade D
Groundwater Hydrology (WATR615) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify important physical properties of aquifers.

Derive Darcy equation and use it in different applications.

Derive the basic groundwater flow equation and calculate groundwater velocity at any point in an aquifer.

Apply the finite difference method to develop numerical solution for simple groundwater flow systems.

Simulate simple flow systems, conduct model calibration, and assess model results.

WATR616.title: UAEU Catalog — WATR616 Advanced Hydrochemistry
WATR616.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=WATR616
Groundwater origin and quality, types and causes of contamination, contaminant transport in porous media, Basic concepts in hydrogeochemistry, Chemical equilibrium and kinetics, Acid-base reaction and carbonate system, Mineral weathering, Mineral surface processes, Redox reaction processes, Sorption reactions, Applications of isotopes in hydrogeology and hydrogeochemistry, Alternative approaches in hydrogeochemisty. Groundwater remediation.
Advanced Hydrochemistry (WATR616) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Hydrochemistry (WATR616) > Prerequisites
WATR605 with a minimum grade C
Advanced Hydrochemistry (WATR616) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Calculate the equilibrium constant and reaction rates of different chemical reactions in the aquatic medium.

Analyze carbonate systems by calculating concentrations of constituents, dissolved carbon dioxide, total alkalinity, and calcite dissolution.

Evaluate the ion exchange in salt/fresh water intrusions.

Differentiate between the various redox reactions in the groundwater and surface water.

Determine and evaluate the effect of organic compounds and their transformation due to aerobic and anaerobic reactions in groundwater and surface water.

WATR617.title: UAEU Catalog — WATR617 Water and Wastewater Treatment
WATR617.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=WATR617
Wastewater sources and characteristics. Wastewater treatment methods: pretreatment, primary (physical), secondary (biological), and tertiary (advanced) treatment. Primary treatment: (screening, coagulation, flocculation, sedimentation, filtration, aeration), Biological systems of treatment (activated sludge processes, biological filtration, sludge handling). Tertiary treatment (adsorption, ion exchange, disinfection).
Water and Wastewater Treatment (WATR617) > Credit Hours : 3

Water and Wastewater Treatment (WATR617) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognize environmental issues, laws and regulations related to water characteristics, sources and usage.

Identify the different types of process units used or required in water and wastewater treatment.

Design different types of water and wastewater treatment process units.

WATR618.title: UAEU Catalog — WATR618 Sustainable Water Desalination
WATR618.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=WATR618
This course provides an in-depth exploration of desalination technologies, focusing on both thermal and membrane-based processes. It covers source water quality characterization, desalination system design, bio-fouling and scale formation and control, brine management, and pre-and post-treatment operations. Students analyze case studies, evaluate desalination plant performance, and engage in practical design projects. Special emphasis is placed on sustainability, energy efficiency, and environmental impact mitigation.
Sustainable Water Desalination (WATR618) > Credit Hours : 3

Sustainable Water Desalination (WATR618) > Prerequisites
WATR601 with a minimum grade C or CIVL345 with a minimum grade D
Sustainable Water Desalination (WATR618) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Assess source water quality and its impact on desalination system design and performance.

Design desalination plant components, including intakes, pretreatment systems, membrane systems, and post-treatment processes.

Differentiate between the various pretreatment and post-treatment processes.

Describe problems and solutions associated with energy consumption, brine management, biofouling, and scale formation.

Evaluate cost and environmental impacts in desalination plant operations.

WATR620.title: UAEU Catalog — WATR620 Membrane Desalination
WATR620.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=WATR620
Overview of water quality characterization; introduction to desalination engineering; Membrane transport theory; membrane types and modules; Concentration polarization; Fundamentals of reverse osmosis desalination: membrane structure and materials, membrane types, water and salt transport, performance factors for the membrane desalination, desalination plant components; Plant consideration; Pre- and Post-treatments of the source water; and environmental effects of membrane desalination plant.
Membrane Desalination (WATR620) > Credit Hours : 3

Membrane Desalination (WATR620) > Prerequisites
WATR618
Membrane Desalination (WATR620) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Understand water chemistry and its quality measurements.

Model transport of small molecules through various membrane modules.

Understand material and processes for membrane design.

Analyze performance of an existing reverse osmosis membrane plant.

Understand optimization factors for plan location considerations.

Formulate simplified analytical equations for membrane performance analysis using transport theory.

WATR622.title: UAEU Catalog — WATR622 Coastal Hydrodynamics
WATR622.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=WATR622
Basics of coastal hydraulics and physical oceanography. Linear wave theory and determination of significant wave heights. Hydraulics of tides and harmonic analysis. Coastal and oceanographic currents and circulation. Ekman currents and Geostrophic flow. Transport modes. Heat and turbulence transfer. Physical measurements and field observations. Introduction to hydrodynamic modeling.
Coastal Hydrodynamics (WATR622) > Credit Hours : 3

Coastal Hydrodynamics (WATR622) > Prerequisites
WATR601 with a minimum grade C
Coastal Hydrodynamics (WATR622) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze data obtained by field measurement methods to model beach and shoreline profile changes.

Characterize and compute basic coastal sediment transport processes and rates.

Characterize and quantify tidal and wave processes including wave generation, propagation, refraction, shoaling, diffraction, and breaking.

Compute wave properties important to coastal engineering, including wave heights, speeds, induced water velocities, pressures, making appropriate approximations for deep and shallow waters.

Differentiate between coastal and oceanographic currents and circulation.

Use an open source coastal hydrodynamics model.

WATR631.title: UAEU Catalog — WATR631 Special Topics in Water Resources
WATR631.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=WATR631
Different courses will be offered based on the needs and Theses requirements. Examples of the courses to be offered include: Coastal hydraulics, Groundwater contamination, Mathematical methods in Water Resources, Water recycle and wastewater minimization, Industrial Wastewater Treatment, Small-scale Desalination Techniques, and others.
Special Topics in Water Resources (WATR631) > Credit Hours : 3

Special Topics in Water Resources (WATR631) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe and characterize contemporary water resources problems.

Identify and describe modern solutions to water resources problems.

Analyze and/or design solution elements to water resources issues.

Conduct an independent study pertaining to a water resources problem.

WATR632.title: UAEU Catalog — WATR632 Directed Studies in Water Resources
WATR632.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=WATR632
The student can select a topic under the guidance of his supervisor and approval of the executive committee. Selected topics should not be part of Theses. The student should submit a report about the studied topic.
Directed Studies in Water Resources (WATR632) > Credit Hours : 3

Directed Studies in Water Resources (WATR632) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe a major scientific advancement in a water resources research area.

Discuss and critique original and recent journal articles of relevance to the research area.

Apply research principles to evaluate the performance of an advanced water resources system or component.

Report findings and make presentations at a high level of proficiency.

WATR640.title: UAEU Catalog — WATR640 Research Thesis
WATR640.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=WATR640
Supervision of research work is made towards the completion of M.Sc. requirements for Thesis option students.
Research Thesis (WATR640) > Credit Hours : 9

Research Thesis (WATR640) > Prerequisites
WATR608
Research Thesis (WATR640) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Formulate research questions or a hypothesis

Critically review previous work of relevance to the selected research area

Construct a sound approach to address a water resources issue

Apply research principles to analyze a proposed water resources issue

Report the implications and limitations of study findings

Describe the achieved advancement of knowledge

Report findings in a written thesis

Present results at a high level of proficiency

WATR695.title: UAEU Catalog — WATR695 Technical Project
WATR695.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=WATR695
This course involves independent work on a design, simulation, modeling, or lab-based technical project. All projects must be supervised by a faculty member and the student is responsible for finding his/her supervisor. Project topics may be faculty-initiated, student-initiated, or suggested by industrial contacts. The student is expected to submit a brief description of a work plan by the end of the second week of the semester. The student is also required to submit a comprehensive final report and give an oral presentation during the last week of lectures of the semester.
Technical Project (WATR695) > Credit Hours : 6

Technical Project (WATR695) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop a work plan for a technical project in the field of Water Resources

Apply advanced design, simulation, modelling, or experimental skills to a specific water resources problem

Report findings in a well-written technical report

Present results at a high level of proficiency

WATR700.title: UAEU Catalog — WATR700 Sustainable Water Resources Management
WATR700.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=WATR700
This course aims to discuss the integrities of economics principles, ethics, and governance for sustainable water management. The course will largely cover topics including fundamental concepts of sustainable and ethical water uses, water rights, valuing and pricing water with various pricing models, water governance including water policies and water acts, water disputes management, and global water diplomacy. Attention will be given to policy aspects of service delivery, the multiple roles for government intervention, causes and consequences of government policy responses in the water sector, including water system regulations.
Sustainable Water Resources Management (WATR700) > Credit Hours : 3

Sustainable Water Resources Management (WATR700) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss major water policy issues and concepts including water regulation, ethics, governance, and the water-energy-food nexus.

Discuss theoretical and substantive areas of water management for different human and natural uses, focusing on aspects of ethics and rights.

Apply methods used in evaluating sustainable water systems such as water footprint and pricing.

Employ tools to evaluate real world case studies.

Report findings and communicate effectively with audience.

WATR710.title: UAEU Catalog — WATR710 Water Resources Systems Analysis
WATR710.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=WATR710
The course explores the systems view of water resources where modeling, optimization, risk and uncertainty analysis come together to provide a more sustainable and holistic management of this important resource. This course will introduce methods used in risk analysis, reliability, and decision-support with applications to water resources systems. Focus is on applied optimization and risk analysis methods such as linear programming, fault tree analysis, failure mode and effects analysis. Attention will be given to multi-objective and multi-criteria analysis.
Water Resources Systems Analysis (WATR710) > Credit Hours : 3

Water Resources Systems Analysis (WATR710) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply the systems approach for analyzing water resources problems.

Formulate and apply optimization models for water resources systems.

Apply risk and uncertainty analysis techniques to water resources problems.

Apply multi-criteria decision analysis techniques to water resources problems.

Report findings and communicate effectively with audience.

WATR720.title: UAEU Catalog — WATR720 Advances in Urban Water Management
WATR720.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=WATR720
The course explores the issues of urban development related to water quantity and quality control and their impact on design of urban water management systems using sustainable best management practices. It also aims to provide an appreciation of the interdisciplinary nature of pollution control of the different urban water streams and provide an insight into the design and modeling of urban water management systems.
Advances in Urban Water Management (WATR720) > Credit Hours : 3

Advances in Urban Water Management (WATR720) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Assess urban water quantity and quality issues.

Discuss best management practices and advances in urban water management.

Select suitable and sustainable urban water management systems.

Assess the impact of urban water control on pollutant loading.

Report findings and communicate effectively with audience.

WATR730.title: UAEU Catalog — WATR730 Subsurface Hydrology
WATR730.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=WATR730
This course covers fundamentals of subsurface flow, emphasizing the role of groundwater in the hydrologic cycle, the relation of groundwater flow to geologic structure, Types of Aquifers, Darcy equation, Aquifer characterization, flow nets, mass conservation, the aquifer flow equation, heterogeneity and anisotropy, storage properties, regional circulation, unsaturated flow, recharge, stream-aquifer interaction, well hydraulics, flow through fractured rock.
Subsurface Hydrology (WATR730) > Credit Hours : 3

Subsurface Hydrology (WATR730) > Corequisites
WATR615
Subsurface Hydrology (WATR730) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify important physical properties of aquifers.

Apply Darcy’s equation to various groundwater flow problems.

Derive complex groundwater flow equations.

Calculate groundwater velocity at any point in an aquifer.

Identify different methods to solve different versions of the flow equation.

Draw flow nets for complex groundwater flow scenarios.

WATR750.title: UAEU Catalog — WATR750 Sediment Transport
WATR750.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=WATR750
The course focuses on aspects of fluid dynamics relevant to transport and deposition of particulate sedimentary materials. Emphasis is on the structure of turbulent shear flows and the forces exerted by fluid motions on bed of loosed sediment. Modes of transport and resulting bed evolution are described and algorithms for predicting sediment transport are defined. The implications of biology and engineering interventions are addressed.
Sediment Transport (WATR750) > Credit Hours : 3

Sediment Transport (WATR750) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Measure thresholds and modes of transport for sediment.

Apply empirical/theoretical equations to estimate sediment transport rates and directions.

Estimate bed shear stress using theoretical approaches and field data.

Describe sediment transport by unidirectional wave and wave-induced currents, alone and in combination.

Report findings and communicate effectively with audience.

WATR760.title: UAEU Catalog — WATR760 Water Resources Modeling
WATR760.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=WATR760
This course focuses on the general theory of mathematical, numerical, and/or stochastic modelling. Emphasis is on the integration of basic water processes (e.g. flow) in models, the fundamentals of model calibration, parameter optimization, and validation. It also introduces the different approach to deal with inherent model uncertainty and the application of water resources models.
Water Resources Modeling (WATR760) > Credit Hours : 3

Water Resources Modeling (WATR760) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the application of different types of models in water resources, including model calibration, validation and uncertainty.

Apply models for forecasting, water resources assessment, and impact assessment.

Evaluate models with respect to their applications on gauged and ungauged water resources.

Apply models to heterogeneous systems by different approaches and the estimation of uncertainties.

Report findings and communicate effectively with audience.

WATR770.title: UAEU Catalog — WATR770 Hydrometeorology
WATR770.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=WATR770
This course aims to explore and link the theories and observations of hydrological processes on the land surface with those in the atmosphere. The focus will be on topics related to precipitation processes, radiation and cloud formation, atmospheric boundary layer dynamics, and hydroclimatology. Emphasis will be given on recent research and modern methods for data analysis and modeling.
Hydrometeorology (WATR770) > Credit Hours : 3

Hydrometeorology (WATR770) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze meteorological processes involving precipitation, lifting, atmospheric stability, radiation.

Estimate radiation budget at a given location and time of the year.

Apply mathematical modeling techniques to surface hydrologic processes.

Communicate findings on the current state of knowledge.

WATR800.title: UAEU Catalog — WATR800 Comprehensive Exam
WATR800.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=WATR800
Every PhD student must pass a Comprehensive Examination (CE) designed to evaluate the breadth and depth of the student’s knowledge of his or her discipline. The CE consists of a written and an oral part and will be prepared, administered, and evaluated by an examination committee from the student’s concerned department. It must be taken before the start of the student’s fifth semester in the program. Students taking the CE must be in good academic standing after completion of the required coursework. The CE may be repeated only once, no later than the end of the student’s fifth semester. A second unsuccessful attempt leads to immediate termination of the student’s enrollment in the PhD program. The CE course is non-credit rated, while a Pass or Fail result for each attempt will be recorded on the student’s academic transcript.
Comprehensive Exam (WATR800) > Credit Hours : 0

Comprehensive Exam (WATR800) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate the depth and breadth of their knowledge in the designated engineering discipline.

Demonstrate sufficient communication skills relevant to the specific field

WATR850.title: UAEU Catalog — WATR850 Candidacy Exam
WATR850.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=WATR850
The Candidacy Exam for the PhD in Water Resources is a non-credit Pass/Fail exam. Students have up to two trials to pass the exam; upon passing it, the student becomes a PhD candidate. The Candidacy Exam is structured to evaluate the student’s breadth and depth of fundamental knowledge in the area(s) closely related to the thesis work. The Candidacy Exam committee, in consultation with the advisor, decides on the topic(s) of the Candidacy Exam. The PhD student prepares a concise and comprehensive research proposal that clearly defines the research problem and objectives and outlines the research methodology that he/she plans to follow. The concerned PhD student should present and defend his/her proposal in front of the Candidacy Exam committee.
Candidacy Exam (WATR850) > Credit Hours : 0

Candidacy Exam (WATR850) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

1Demonstrate the depth and breadth of their knowledge in the field of water resources relevant to student’s research topic

Propose a well-structured research project that outlines clear objectives, a detailed plan, and an appropriate methodology.

Exhibit sufficient communication skills relevant to field of study and the research topic

WATR900.title: UAEU Catalog — WATR900 Dissertation Doctoral Research
WATR900.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2906.shtml?id=WATR900
Student conducts high quality academic research under the direction of his/her supervisor.
