Distinguish between short and long run horizons and assess their consequences.

Appraise how government intervention affects efficiency and welfare as well as differentiate between its positive and normative implications.

ECON212.title: UAEU Catalog — ECON212 Intermediate Theory of Macroeconomics
ECON212.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=ECON212
This is a course on intermediate macroeconomic theory, where students will be introduced to concepts and analytical tools frequently used by economists to tackle a range of macroeconomic issues that are relevant to businesses, governments, and households. It examines issues relating to long-term growth as well as business cycles. Significant attention is paid to macroeconomic stabilization (fiscal and monetary policies). The course also introduces open macro economy issues such as balance of payments, exchange rates and currency crises. The course is not just a descriptive survey of issues. The aim will be to provide coherent analytical frameworks and theoretical foundations to understanding cotemporary global macroeconomic policies.
Intermediate Theory of Macroeconomics (ECON212) > Credit Hours : 3

Intermediate Theory of Macroeconomics (ECON212) > Prerequisites
ECON125 with a minimum grade D
Intermediate Theory of Macroeconomics (ECON212) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Examine the different approaches to and problems in measuring key macroeconomic variables such as GDP, inflation, and unemployment.

Explain macroeconomic theories as well as various schools of thought and how they apply to real world policy issues.

Explain the origins, evolution, sources, and mechanisms of economic growth.

Apply simple analytical models like the IS-MP/AD-AS to conduct macroeconomic analysis.

Examine the impact of exchange rate fluctuations on the macroeconomy

Produce data-driven policy briefs on contemporary macroeconomic policy issues.

ECON215.title: UAEU Catalog — ECON215 Money and Banking
ECON215.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=ECON215
This course focuses on understanding money, the banking and financial systems, and the role of monetary policy in the economy. The course emphasizes concepts that are fundamental to understand financial instruments, institutions and markets, and the tools and techniques employed throughout the financial system. The course objectives include an understanding of 1) the origins and nature of money; 2) the determination of interest rates; 3) how to apply basic knowledge of financial markets and instruments; 4) how money and capital market’s function; and 5) the role of central banks and formulation of monetary policy.
Money and Banking (ECON215) > Credit Hours : 3

Money and Banking (ECON215) > Prerequisites
ECON125 with a minimum grade D
Money and Banking (ECON215) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss the structure of the Financial System and the role of money in the economy.

Explain the significance of the Financial System in the economy

Identify the determinants of interest rate in the Financial Markets and Financial Institutions.

Recognize the role of the Financial System in the money creation.

Produce professional quality reports on Money and Financial System.

ECON231.title: UAEU Catalog — ECON231 Introduction to Econometrics
ECON231.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=ECON231
The objective of this course is to provide the basic knowledge of econometrics that is an essential tool for any serious economist or social scientist. This course emphasizes both the theoretical and the practical aspects of econometric analysis. It aims at developing an intuitive understanding of the material that allow students to utilize these skills effectively and creatively. Throughout the course, students will be offered practical exercises that give them opportunity to use statistical software in conducting econometric analyses. After accomplishing the goals of this course, students are expected to have a solid foundation for the elementary concepts, which enable them to acquire further specialized and advanced econometric skills by self-learning.
Introduction to Econometrics (ECON231) > Credit Hours : 3

Introduction to Econometrics (ECON231) > Prerequisites
MATH115 with a minimum grade D

STAT102 with a minimum grade D

STAT202 with a minimum grade D
Introduction to Econometrics (ECON231) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss the assumptions, concepts, and methods in regressions

Interpret the results of multivariate regressions

Conduct hypothesis testing on the coefficients of regression equations

Apply econometric techniques to investigate economic or financial relationships using economic data and statistical software.

ECON236.title: UAEU Catalog — ECON236 Public Projects Economics
ECON236.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=ECON236
This course practically introduces the students to the foundations of cost-benefit analysis (CBA) techniques in public projects. It applies the concepts of social surplus and allocative efficiency, costs and benefits in primary and secondary markets, discounting, market distortions and the various approaches to shadow pricing in developing countries to public projects appraisal. Various related public policy issues, e.g., monetization, the identification and valuation of social impacts, and the tradeoff between efficiency and equity are addressed; that leads to considering the rationale for, and reviewing the methods of, distributional weighting in CBA (DWCBA), cost-effectiveness analysis (CEA), multi- criteria analysis (MCA), and the qualitative (non-economic) techniques of project assessment.
Public Projects Economics (ECON236) > Credit Hours : 3

Public Projects Economics (ECON236) > Prerequisites
ECON211 with a minimum grade D
Public Projects Economics (ECON236) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Distinguish between primary and secondary benefits and costs in a simple cost benefit analysis framework.

Apply discounting techniques in a simple public project or policy appraisal.

Use shadow pricing methods in a simple Social Benefit-Cost analysis framework.

Write simple appraisal conclusions and qualitative environmental and distributional impact reports.

Evaluate the advantages and disadvantage of different methods of appraisal for various types of projects.

ECON311.title: UAEU Catalog — ECON311 Microeconomics of Competitiveness
ECON311.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=ECON311
The course explores the social welfare implications of different market structures, as they affect the behaviour and strategies of firms in terms of price, output, or R&D. Part of the course will focus on the theory of oligopoly and how it fits within the overall structure-conduct-performance (SCP) paradigm. The lessons obtained from the theory will then be applied to the analysis of mergers, price-fixing, or abuse of dominant position, among other topics. Real-life case studies will be discussed in class, and they appear in all forms of assessment.
Microeconomics of Competitiveness (ECON311) > Credit Hours : 3

Microeconomics of Competitiveness (ECON311) > Prerequisites
ECON211 with a minimum grade D
Microeconomics of Competitiveness (ECON311) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Critically discuss what determines inter-industry differences in the structure of markets.

Identify how firms interact with each other in their price, output and R & D decisions.

Analyze how firms may act strategically to retain profits by deterring entry, and what motivates firms to merge or collude.

Evaluate how the structure of industries affects the pricing, output, R&D and their economic performance.

Analyse why and how existing regulations protect competition.

ECON320.title: UAEU Catalog — ECON320 Climate Change Economics and Policy
ECON320.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=ECON320
The aim of the course is to apply key concepts and fundamentals of economic analysis to study the environmental, economic, social, and economic policy (either mitigation or adaptation) issues related to climate change. The objective is to enable students to understand the drivers of climate change, the methods to analyze them, and the ways used in order to design climate change policies in theory and practice. The introductory part of the course will discuss why climate change represents a main issue for our societies – i.e., the economic challenge raised by climate change with the notion of global externality, with specific attention to how reducing GHG emissions to lower the negative impacts of present activities on future welfare. The second part of the course will discuss how to design effective policy instruments in order to limit climate change, the costs and benefits of such policies, and the international architecture and political economy issues in implementing these policies. This part of the course also discusses UAE's mitigation and adaptation policies. Lastly, the course will briefly discuss the role of energy prices and renewable energy in global climate change and addresses the issues of climate change from developing country perspectives.
Climate Change Economics and Policy (ECON320) > Credit Hours : 3

Climate Change Economics and Policy (ECON320) > Prerequisites
ECON211 with a minimum grade D

ECON212 with a minimum grade D
Climate Change Economics and Policy (ECON320) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify key issues relating to climate change.

Analyze how economics can offer public policies aimed at mitigating the effects of climate change.

Apply economic instruments in designing appropriate climate change policies.

Evaluate the role of energy prices in mitigating the effects of climate change.

Undertake independent research in the area of the economics of climate change mitigation.

ECON321.title: UAEU Catalog — ECON321 Energy Economics and Policy
ECON321.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=ECON321
The course applies key economics and political economy concepts and theories to address contemporary trends in global energy markets and their implications from national and global perspectives. Topics of interest to the UAE long-term energy strategy (2050) are emphasized. That includes, the Energy-Economy-Environment nexus, Energy Indicators for Sustainable Development, the economics of renewable and non-renewable energy, the role of markets and international policies in the global energy transition, oil and natural gas markets and prices, unconventional sources such as shale gas, the impact of globalization on energy performance and productivity.
Energy Economics and Policy (ECON321) > Credit Hours : 3

Energy Economics and Policy (ECON321) > Prerequisites
ECON211 with a minimum grade D
Energy Economics and Policy (ECON321) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain how energy demand and supply factors influence oil prices in the short and the long run.

Critically assess how shale gas advancements have changed the way the oil and natural gas markets operate.

Apply economic methods and analysis to assess energy efficiency policies and effects on energy sustainability.

Analyze how energy transition polices affect climate change and the attainment of the relevant Sustainable Development Goals.

Effectively communicate the highlights and conclusions of articles addressing recent energy markets developments.

ECON330.title: UAEU Catalog — ECON330 International Trade
ECON330.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=ECON330
This course focuses on both international trade theory and trade policy analysis. Emphasis will be placed on using trade theories to understand the reasons for and processes of international trade in goods and services. The course is not just a descriptive survey of trade policy issues but will aim to provide theoretical frameworks to examine topics such as comparative advantage, factor mobility, new trade theories, and political economy of trade policy.
International Trade (ECON330) > Credit Hours : 3

International Trade (ECON330) > Prerequisites
ECON211 with a minimum grade D
International Trade (ECON330) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the importance of international trade in a globalized economy.

Debate the role played by trade policy in promoting economic growth.

Explain the difference between comparative and competitive advantage

Use theoretical models to understand why countries engage in international trade.

Apply general equilibrium reasoning to understand the political economy of trade and trade policy analysis.

Communicate, orally and in writing, the salience of contemporary international trade policy issues.

ECON331.title: UAEU Catalog — ECON331 International Finance and Policy
ECON331.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=ECON331
This course focuses on selected analytical and policy issues relating to international financial markets and policies. Emphasis will be placed on developing simple analytical tools to understand international macroeconomic policy issues confronting the world economy. The course is not just a descriptive survey of issues but will aim to provide analytical frameworks to examine topics such as international financial crises, exchange rates and its impact on trade and investment, the role of international agencies such as the International Monetary Fund, as well as cutting-edge issues in financial globalization.
International Finance and Policy (ECON331) > Credit Hours : 3

International Finance and Policy (ECON331) > Prerequisites
ECON212 with a minimum grade D
International Finance and Policy (ECON331) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the core concepts and theories in international finance and open-economy macroeconomics.

Apply simple analytical frameworks to study important issues in international finance such as exchange rates and financial crises.

Evaluate the nature, evolution, and impacts of financial globalization on emerging markets.

Debate the empirical evidence on the benefits and trade-offs associated with international financial integration.

Communicate, orally and in writing, the significance of contemporary international financial policy issues.

ECON344.title: UAEU Catalog — ECON344 Public Economics
ECON344.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=ECON344
The aim of this course is to provide the tools to analyze the role of the role of the government and the public sector in mixed economies. The course discusses the ideal situation of perfectly competitive markets and how market structure relates to economic efficiency. Market failures result in inefficiency. The government can not only improve efficiency but resource distribution in society. Topics covered in the course include market efficiency, market failure, externalities, equity, public goods, public expenditure, taxation, and fiscal federalism.
Public Economics (ECON344) > Credit Hours : 3

Public Economics (ECON344) > Prerequisites
ECON211 with a minimum grade D
Public Economics (ECON344) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain how markets and governments affect economic efficiency.

Distinguish market failure sources and the role of government in correcting them.

Compare between the different public goods.

Analyze the alternative means and impact of government finance.

Compare income, consumption, and wealth taxes.

Examine the impact of the different taxes on saving, investment, and labor.

ECON350.title: UAEU Catalog — ECON350 Sustainable Development
ECON350.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=ECON350
This course aims to provide a holistic view of economic issues pertaining to sustainable development. It begins with an overview of economic development and its distinction from economic growth. Topics include: poverty, inequality, unemployment, population growth, competitiveness, human capital, technology, the IV industrial revolution, and urbanization. Additionally, the course assesses how institutions affect economic outcomes and why some nations fail while others succeed. Next, this course considers the impediments to development and how they can potentially be implemented through sustainable development policies at the micro and macro level. It covers topics such as definitions and intellectual background of sustainable development, measurement of sustainable development, sustainable management of cities and communities, and sustainable industry and infrastructure. Theoretical issues are illustrated by case studies with a special emphasis on the UAE.
Sustainable Development (ECON350) > Credit Hours : 3

Sustainable Development (ECON350) > Prerequisites
ECON211 with a minimum grade D

ECON212 with a minimum grade D
Sustainable Development (ECON350) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe central themes and issues of sustainable economic development.

Debate sustainable economic development goals, challenges, and opportunities.

Analyze sustainable development paths through a range of sustainability indicators.

Analyze empirical evidence on the policies of sustainable economic development.

Evaluate policy actions and discussions related to the areas covered in the course

ECON360.title: UAEU Catalog — ECON360 Economic Policy Analysis
ECON360.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=ECON360
This course is intended to equip students with the needed techniques to conduct applied economic analysis of public policies. In its first part, the course introduces the foundations, basic concepts and goals of public policy and the role of the policy analyst. Relevant microeconomics, public choice foundations, and quantitative methods and tools for public policy analysis will be reviewed, including theories on the rationale of government intervention in the economy. The second part of the course is devoted to the study of the principles of impact evaluations and its application in economic policy cases, e.g., healthcare, urban transportation, pollution control, Emiratization, Value Added taxes etc. Students will work in teams towards a common project.
Economic Policy Analysis (ECON360) > Credit Hours : 3

Economic Policy Analysis (ECON360) > Prerequisites
ECON231 with a minimum grade D

ECON236 with a minimum grade D
Economic Policy Analysis (ECON360) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply appropriate techniques and economic frameworks to the analysis of a range of public policies.

Assess economic policies, using impact evaluation or econometrics methods.

Integrate identified social and sustainability aspects in economic policy proposals.

Write effective policy briefs, in teams and individually, advising public officials on a particular economic policy.

Communicate, orally, in teams and individually, public policy proposals and discussions.

ECON420.title: UAEU Catalog — ECON420 Resource Economics and Policy
ECON420.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=ECON420
This course aims to apply key concepts and fundamentals of economic analysis to the study of natural resources use and management. In its first part, the students are introduced to the microeconomic theories and techniques relevant to understanding issues related to the depletion and degradation of natural resources as a result of human behavior, e.g., common pool resources. The second part is devoted to the study of public policy and issues of governance of natural resources. It introduces an analysis of market-based and regulatory solutions to achieving economic efficiency and sustainability that help inform policies related to effective natural resource management. Finally, the course will address some applied natural resource problems of relevance to the UAE economy, such as water resources, fisheries, land and biodiversity.
Resource Economics and Policy (ECON420) > Credit Hours : 3

Resource Economics and Policy (ECON420) > Prerequisites
ECON236 with a minimum grade D
Resource Economics and Policy (ECON420) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify market failures related to natural resources and their implications on resources sustainability.

Assess the tradeoffs of different resource efficiency and sustainability policies.

Apply relevant economic concepts and frameworks to analyze natural resources’ demand and supply sides.

Reflect on the role of firms and individuals’ social responsibility in natural resources sustainability.

Effectively communicate conclusions or findings of recent articles on natural resources policies.

ECON432.title: UAEU Catalog — ECON432 Research Methods in Economics
ECON432.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=ECON432
The aim of this course is to supply students with an understanding of the issues and problems of conducting research in economics and the tools available to them. The course will enable students to develop skills necessary to conduct applied research in economics or an allied field. During the course students will develop original research question/s and hypotheses, conduct a literature review and use bibliographic software to manage their citations and references, analyze the problem/s using appropriate research methods (quantitative/qualitative) according to ethical standards, test their analysis or model of the problem, interpret their results, and write up the findings using appropriate academic language.
Research Methods in Economics (ECON432) > Credit Hours : 3

Research Methods in Economics (ECON432) > Prerequisites
ECON211 with a minimum grade D

ECON212 with a minimum grade D

ECON231 with a minimum grade D
Research Methods in Economics (ECON432) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze, Criticize And Research Contemporary Economic Issues In Relation To The Uae'S Economic Development

Communicate Their Research Results Effectively In A Written Format Understandable To An Expert And Layperson Using Appropriate Academic Writing Skills

Develop A Well-Articulated Research Question/S And Abstract, Based On A Comprehensive Review Of The Existing Academic Literature

Present Their Research Findings To A Technically Minded Audience

Understand Different Research Methodologies And Carry Out Primary And/Or Secondary Research

Understand The Ethical Implications Of Research Including How To Avoid Plagiarism And Demonstrate Use Of Technical Software For Referencing And Citation Purposes

ECON433.title: UAEU Catalog — ECON433 Applied Economics of the Middle East
ECON433.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=ECON433
This course aims to provide students with an understanding of the socio-economic and structural characteristics of the Middle East and North African economies. The course analyses the contemporary opportunities and challenges facing these economies, with a specific focus on the Gulf region. Learning methods require students to analyze academic articles on the region and utilize econometric techniques. Among the topics covered are developments in the oil and gas sector, labor markets and migration, the implications of changing demographics such as declining birth rates, the role of inter-regional and international trade, capital flows, the role of government policy, economic reforms and diversification, and finally the significance of banks and financial markets in the region’s economic development.
Applied Economics of the Middle East (ECON433) > Credit Hours : 3

Applied Economics of the Middle East (ECON433) > Prerequisites
ECON105 with a minimum grade D

ECON212 with a minimum grade D

ECON231 with a minimum grade D
Applied Economics of the Middle East (ECON433) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Assess The Applicability Of Development Theories To The Economies In The Middle East

Discuss The Economic Teachings Of Islam

Evaluate The Role Of International And Intra-National Trade In The Economic Development Of The Middle East

Explain Structural Transformation And Growth In The Middle East

Express The Role Of Oil And Gas Production In Development Of The Middle East

Identify Demographic Changes In The Middle East And Their Economic Consequences

ECON441.title: UAEU Catalog — ECON441 Labor and HR Economics
ECON441.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=ECON441
This course introduces students to the key aspects of labor economics and human resource development theory: demand and supply; market equilibrium; productivity; and incentive structures. It introduces the main tools used to analyze, evaluate and understand labor market dynamics. In addition, it concentrates on the labor markets of the UAE and the Arabian Gulf. It introduces UAE specific case studies and labor market data for empirical applications.
Labor and HR Economics (ECON441) > Credit Hours : 3

Labor and HR Economics (ECON441) > Prerequisites
ECON211 with a minimum grade D
Labor and HR Economics (ECON441) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Illustrate how workers make labor supply, occupation choice, and human capital investment decisions.

Relate training costs to employees’ wages.

Analyze how wages and employment are determined in the alternative labor and product markets.

Compare the alternative pay schemes and their effect on labor efficiency.

Dissect the government impact on the GCC labor market.

ECON455.title: UAEU Catalog — ECON455 Selected Topics In Economics
ECON455.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=ECON455
This course introduces students to the art of applying different economic theories and concepts to specific “real world” topics in economics. The course topics may vary to reflect changing interests and state of the art topics. Depending on faculty interest and availability, the course may cover a wide range of special topics in economics with an applied orientation. For instance, it may cover topics that belong to Health Economics, Public Economics or Sustainable Development Economics. The present course topics are related to sustainable development. This course is aimed at giving an introduction to the basic concepts of “sustainable development” and how these concepts have been implemented through “sustainable development policies” at the micro and macro level. The theoretical contents of the course is based on the concepts of environmental and resource economics and macroeconomics. Theoretical issues are illustrated by case studies with a special emphasize on the UAE and/or GCC cases. It covers topics such as: definitions and intellectual backgrounds of sustainable development, measurement of sustainable development, sustainable urban management, sustainable management of resources, sustainable development and firms environmental strategies.
Selected Topics In Economics (ECON455) > Credit Hours : 3

Selected Topics In Economics (ECON455) > Prerequisites
ECON211 with a minimum grade D

ECON212 with a minimum grade D
Selected Topics In Economics (ECON455) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply The Appropriate Technique Of Economic Evaluation To Resource Allocation Decisions

Apply The Fundamental Principles Of Health Economics To Decision Making In Health Care

Critically Appraise A Health Economics Article

Describe And Critically Appraise And Compare The Role Of The Government And The Private Market As Health Insurance Providers

Describe The Different Methods That Can Be Used To Assist Health Care Priority Setting Development.

Describe The Fundamental Principles Of Health Economics

Discuss Different Methods For Eliciting Preferences And The Strengths And Weaknesses Of Each Method

Discuss The Different Methods For Measuring Costs And Benefits In Economic Evaluation

Discuss The Role Of Institutions And Health Care Systems

Discuss The Role Of Markets And Incentives In The Demand And Supply Of Health Care

Interpret Basic Regression Coefficients From A Dce

ECON460.title: UAEU Catalog — ECON460 Seminar in Economic Policy Research
ECON460.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=ECON460
This course is a culmination of students’ exposure to the various areas and techniques of economics and is intended to provide an integrative experience to the study of economic policy analysis. Students will be coached on one-on-one basis to develop their own research interests, choose their research topics in economic policy, work individually to write their own research paper, and present their results. In the individual project, students are expected to shape their research questions, review relevant literature, formulate research hypotheses, collect economic data, implement appropriate econometric models, analyze the results, draw conclusions, and provide policy recommendations. Students will practice how to write an economic policy brief and make oral presentations on their findings and conclusions.
Seminar in Economic Policy Research (ECON460) > Credit Hours : 3

Seminar in Economic Policy Research (ECON460) > Prerequisites
ECON212 with a minimum grade D

ECON344 with a minimum grade D

ECON360 with a minimum grade D
Seminar in Economic Policy Research (ECON460) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Formulate a proper economic research question and the related hypotheses.

Identify possible econometric techniques and their requirements for a given research question.

Interpret the results from using a statistical software to draw findings.

Write an effective literature review corresponding to the research problem under investigation.

Effectively communicate, orally and in writing, the research findings and implications for policy.

ECON541.title: UAEU Catalog — ECON541 Economics for Policy Analysis
ECON541.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=ECON541
The course will focus on the principles and techniques of economics important for analyzing economic aspects of public policy. First, the course will focus on the working on the aggregate economy highlighting topics like employment, productivity, trade and fiscal deficits, inflation, interest rate and exchange rates and their impacts on public policy. Then the course will focus on micro issues like the models of economic behavior, the price system, market failure and interventions, and related policy instruments. The course will examine Islamic principles and theories of the above topics, as appropriate
Economics for Policy Analysis (ECON541) > Credit Hours : 3

Economics for Policy Analysis (ECON541) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain how a system of perfectly competitive markets can achieve efficient outcomes.

Explain why and how positive and negative externalities constitute a failure of the market system.

Describe the taxonomy of public goods and explain how they can be produced and financed.

Describe alternative means of financing government activities and compare the economic impacts of a different tax structures.

Explain the differences between criteria used to evaluate different methods of government finance and the impact of government taxes on private agents’ income, consumption and wealth.

Explain how cost/benefit analysis can be used to assess public policies.

ECON544.title: UAEU Catalog — ECON544 Financial Management and Public Budgeting
ECON544.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=ECON544
This course will examine the major aspects of financial planning and public budgeting focusing on topics like the philosophy of public finance, financial analysis and planning techniques, theories of budgeting and budget as a mechanism for planning and control, accounting and auditing in the public sector, government responsibility for capital facilities planning, etc. The course will also look at the contemporary issues in public budgeting and financial management, and how they interface with public management drawing on comparative regional and international experiences, as available and appropriate.
Financial Management and Public Budgeting (ECON544) > Credit Hours : 3

Financial Management and Public Budgeting (ECON544) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Understand the principles of public finance and budgeting.

Compare different theories and approaches of budgeting in the public sector.

Recognize the ethical dimensions of public finance and budget issues.

Evaluate the theoretical and practical implications of the government's budgeting in a fast changing world.

ECON651.title: UAEU Catalog — ECON651 Managerial Economics
ECON651.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=ECON651
This course covers the essential principles and tools of Managerial Economics. The course examines the principles of microeconomics, and illustrates how they apply to managerial decision-making. Students who master this material will be better prepared for leadership positions in business, not-for-profit, and government entities. The first part of the course discusses basic economic concepts such as supply, demand and costs. We move from these basic concepts to studying how firms behave when they have market power. Topics include differences between perfectly and imperfectly competitive markets, optimal pricing for firms with monopoly power, and the use of advanced pricing such as bundling and versioning to capture value. The final section of the course focuses on advanced topics in market analysis. These include the role of externalities and imperfect or asymmetric information.
Managerial Economics (ECON651) > Credit Hours : 3

Managerial Economics (ECON651) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Use graphical tools to analyze economic interactions and outcomes.

Apply mathematical skills to provide solutions and recommendations to managerial economic problems.

Demonstrate managerial economics knowledge in the areas of consumer and firm behavior analysis, competitive market structure, and macroeconomic activity.

Analyze management related ethical issues through case studies.

Demonstrate presentation skills using case study analysis.

Construct policy recommendations at the microeconomic and the macroeconomic level.

ECON655.title: UAEU Catalog — ECON655 Economics for Management
ECON655.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=ECON655
This course focuses on managerial applications of key macroeconomic and microeconomic principles pertaining to market competition, the national economy, and global markets. The course examines how an understanding of micro and macroeconomic fundamentals can help enhance managerial decision making. It aims to foster an economic way of thinking in making complex managerial decisions, especially in situations of incomplete information. The first part of the course discusses concepts related to microeconomics, such as supply, demand, and production costs. The course then moves to studying how firms behave when they have market power. Topics include differences between perfectly and imperfectly competitive markets, optimal pricing for firms with market power, and the use of advanced pricing strategies to capture value. The second part of the course focuses on macroeconomic concepts, specifically related to open economies, providing a clear framework for understanding the process of economic and financial globalization and their significance for multinational businesses.
Economics for Management (ECON655) > Credit Hours : 3

Economics for Management (ECON655) > Prerequisites
STAT511 or STAT202
Economics for Management (ECON655) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze the market structure and the business environment in which a manager operates for the purpose of making informed business decisions.

Assess consumer and firm behavior, in a complex global and domestic market environment, as input for the development of business strategies

Apply economic tools and concepts to a wide range of strategic business decisions in response to changing macroeconomic policies and global supply and demand conditions.

Evaluate the importance of Globalization and regional integration, and its potential impact on the UAE and its organizations using business analytical frameworks.

FINC110.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC110 Fundamentals of Financial Derivatives
FINC110.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC110
This course introduces financial derivatives and their role in modern financial markets. It examines the fundamental derivative instruments, including futures, forwards, swaps, and options, and explores their applications in hedging, speculation, and financial risk management. The course covers the structure and operation of derivative markets, pricing principles, trading mechanisms, and the role of market participants. Topics include futures markets, hedging strategies, determination of forward and futures prices, interest rate futures, swap contracts, and the fundamentals of options markets. Emphasis is placed on the practical use of derivative securities to manage financial risk and support investment and corporate financial decisions. Ethical considerations in derivative trading are also discussed, while real-world examples and case studies are used to enhance students’ understanding of derivative markets and their applications.
Fundamentals of Financial Derivatives (FINC110) > Credit Hours : 3

Fundamentals of Financial Derivatives (FINC110) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate knowledge of derivative securities, including futures, forwards, swaps, and options, and their role in financial markets.

Analyze the use of derivative instruments for hedging, speculation, and financial risk management.

Apply basic pricing principles used in the valuation of derivative securities.

Interpret financial market information and evaluate derivative-based strategies using appropriate financial tools and technologies.

Demonstrate ethical awareness and professional responsibility in derivative trading and financial decision-making.

FINC120.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC120 Financial Engineering
FINC120.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC120
This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the fundamental concepts and applications of financial engineering. It examines the major derivative instruments, including forwards, futures, options, and swaps, and explores the role of market participants such as hedgers, speculators, arbitrageurs, market makers, and high-frequency traders in modern financial markets. The course covers the structure and operation of futures markets, hedging strategies, basis risk, interest rates, yield curves, and the principles of forward and futures pricing. Particular emphasis is placed on derivative valuation and risk management. Students will develop an understanding of option pricing theory, including binomial tree models, risk-neutral valuation, and the Black-Scholes-Merton framework. The course also examines the use of derivatives for hedging and managing financial risk, as well as the applications of interest rate and credit derivatives. Throughout the course, theoretical concepts are reinforced through practical examples, case studies, and real-world financial market applications, enabling students to develop the analytical skills required for effective decision-making in financial markets.
Financial Engineering (FINC120) > Credit Hours : 3

Financial Engineering (FINC120) > Prerequisites
FINC110
Financial Engineering (FINC120) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze the structure and applications of derivative securities and financial engineering products.

Compute options and derivatives prices using explicit simple models and Monte-Carlo methods.

Construct hedging portfolios and measure options’ greeks.

Learn the basics of high-frequency trading and market making.

Communicate effectively with market participants, using the fundamental terminology and concepts of derivative securities in professional financial contexts.

FINC210.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC210 Business Finance
FINC210.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC210
This course introduces the fundamental principles of finance, with a focus on corporate finance and financial decision-making in real-world contexts. It examines how firms and investors interact within money and capital markets. The course develops students’ understanding of key financial concepts and analytical tools, including the time value of money, valuation of bonds and stocks, and financial statement analysis. It also covers risk and return, capital budgeting, cash flow analysis, and financial planning. Emphasis is placed on applying quantitative techniques and critical thinking skills to evaluate investment and financing decisions. The course provides a strong foundation for advanced study in finance, banking, and related fields while supporting the development of professional competencies.
Business Finance (FINC210) > Credit Hours : 3

Business Finance (FINC210) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co ACCT111 with a minimum grade D
Business Finance (FINC210) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply the basic principles of finance in analyzing financial situations and making informed decisions.

Analyze financial performance using financial statements and ratio analysis techniques

Evaluate business decisions using time value of money techniques (e.g., NPV, IRR) and risk–return analysis.

Calculate and interpret risk and return measures for investment decisions.

Compare and evaluate sources of finance and apply appropriate valuation techniques for each.

Apply capital budgeting techniques such as NPV, IRR, Payback Period to evaluate long-term investment projects.

FINC340.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC340 Finance Analytics
FINC340.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC340
This course introduces students to the application of data science in finance and shows how data analytics can help with financial decision-making. Throughout this course, students will use the statistical language R to develop analytical programs in finance and apply them for time series analysis, forecasting, portfolio selection. The course also highlights how big data and data analytics shape the way finance is practiced by emphasizing problems currently confronting finance professionals.
Finance Analytics (FINC340) > Credit Hours : 3

Finance Analytics (FINC340) > Prerequisites
FINC210

ECON231
Finance Analytics (FINC340) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Use appropriate software/programming language to solve empirical finance problems.

Apply analytics tools to analyze finance time series data, build forecasting models and interpret results.

Communicate finance analytics methodologies and findings orally and in written form.

Utilize statistical and algorithmic knowledge to extract useful insights for financial decision-making.

FINC341.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC341 Corporate Finance
FINC341.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC341
The course reviews and reinforces the basic concepts covered in Business Finance and builds on them. Building on students’ knowledge of ratio analysis, financial statements, the time value of money, stock and bond valuation, and capital budgeting, the primary objective of this course is to expand this knowledge by introducing students to real-world examples of how these concepts are used in day-to-day corporate strategic planning and decision-making. Topics covered include financial analysis using both quantitative and qualitative data; theories of capital structure and dividends; long-term financing decisions and the appropriate use of debt and equity; calculation of the optimal capital structure; sources and uses of short-term financing; mergers and acquisitions; bankruptcy and financial restructuring; and corporate governance. A wide range of applications and case studies are used to support the practical aspects of the course.
Corporate Finance (FINC341) > Credit Hours : 3

Corporate Finance (FINC341) > Prerequisites
FINC210 with a minimum grade D
Corporate Finance (FINC341) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply financial principles to present and analyze agency problems.

Evaluate investment projects using capital budgeting criteria.

Evaluate and justify firms’ financing decisions

Calculate and critically analyze firms’ cost of capital

Compare and evaluate alternative dividend policies

FINC344.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC344 Islamic Finance and Banking
FINC344.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC344
This course aims to provide the essential understanding of Islamic economics and Islamic finance, including the setting up of traditional Islamic financial tools and practices and the development of modern Islamic banking and financial instruments and institutions. The course examines and relates the theory of Islamic finance to recent development in Islamic banking and financial industry. Topic covered include money policy, profit sharing, Islamic financial and banking institutions and their operations, Islamic banking model and alternative models of financing and structuring of Islamic investment funds.
Islamic Finance and Banking (FINC344) > Credit Hours : 3

Islamic Finance and Banking (FINC344) > Prerequisites
FINC210 with a minimum grade D
Islamic Finance and Banking (FINC344) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate Comprehensive Understanding Of The Islamic Finance Theoretical Framework

Demonstrate Awareness Of The Ethical Issues Associated With The Islamic Financial Framework

Design Basic Islamic Finance Products

Assess The Risk-Return Profiles Of Basic Islamic Finance Products

Analyze The State Of Islamic Finance And Make Predictions Regarding Its Future Directions

FINC348.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC348 International Finance
FINC348.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC348
This course provides a foundational knowledge of the international business environment as well as introduces ideas on how financial management helps multinational firms operate optimally in that environment. The course focuses on international financial management within the multinational firm and provides an understanding of international regulatory and environment differences, the different foreign exchange regimes, balance of payments, access to money and capital markets, use of derivatives to hedge exchange rate risk, measurement and management of exposure to exchange rate and interest rate fluctuations, and international diversification. Emphasis is on international financial decision-making through the extensive use of cases and real-world examples.
International Finance (FINC348) > Credit Hours : 3

International Finance (FINC348) > Prerequisites
ECON215

FINC210
International Finance (FINC348) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze multinational corporations (MNCs) by applying international business theories and explaining international trade and capital flows.

Interpret international financial information by using appropriate methods, data sources, and IT tools.

Use appropriate quantitative and analytical techniques to solve a problem related to international financial management.

Use the appropriate technology to deliver an effective presentation and to produce professional quality reports on international financial issues.

Contribute to team-based projects by preparing professional reports and presentations that effectively communicate analyses and recommendations.

Evaluate international financial decisions within ethical frameworks.

FINC351.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC351 Insurance and Regulation
FINC351.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC351
This course introduces students to the fundamentals of insurance and its essential role in modern financial systems. It focuses on the nature of risk, the structure and operations of insurance markets, legal principles governing insurance contracts, major insurance products, and the regulatory and ethical environment of the insurance industry. The course builds progressively from basic insurance concepts to applied understanding of different types of insurance policies such as life, health, property, and retirement-related insurance products. Practical applications will be provided and the determination of the fair premium of pertinent insurance policies in the market will be rigorously dealt with.
Insurance and Regulation (FINC351) > Credit Hours : 3

Insurance and Regulation (FINC351) > Prerequisites
FINC341
Insurance and Regulation (FINC351) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the basic concepts of risk, insurability, and insurance.

Describe the structure and operations of insurance companies and insurance markets.

Apply legal principles and contractual foundations relevant to insurance.

Differentiate between major insurance products and their applications.

Explain the regulatory framework and ethical standards governing insurance practices.

FINC370.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC370 Financial Technologies I
FINC370.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC370
FinTech is a disruptive force in the financial sector, revolutionizing current business models, navigating regulatory and legal challenges, and prompting traditional financial institutions to quickly adopt, adapt and strategically engage with financial technology. This course introduces the FinTech discipline with a structured focus on how emerging technologies are transforming financial services, business models, and financial intermediation. This course introduces the Fintech discipline and investigates how it is changing the financial ecosystem by investigating transformations happening to financial services across industries and giving a broad understanding of the current and emerging technologies, including blockchain, cryptocurrencies, Distributed Ledger Technologies (DLTs). The course emphasizes practical understanding of digital finance applications, including digital payments, lending platforms, artificial intelligence, and data-driven financial services. Other topics include the regulation of fintech and the opportunities it provides for inclusive growth and transparent funding and investments. Overall, the course's aim is to introduce the fintech industry and establish a knowledge base that enables students to critically assess this rapidly growing and highly competitive industry.
Financial Technologies I (FINC370) > Credit Hours : 3

Financial Technologies I (FINC370) > Prerequisites
FINC210

ECON215
Financial Technologies I (FINC370) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate knowledge of the overall fundamentals of the Fintech industry.

Analyze digital payments, digital currencies, and distributed ledger technologies (DLTs).

Examine digital lending and crowdfunding.

Utilize big data, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Internet of Things (IoT) in finance.

Demonstrate knowledge of cybersecurity, and Regtech, as well as their ethical implications.

FINC378.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC378 Investment and Portfolio Analysis
FINC378.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC378
The course builds upon the concepts covered in the principles of financial management course (FINC 240). This course introduces the students to the analysis of investment information, evaluation of risks and returns, and principles of portfolio selection in investment decisions. This course focuses on securities markets, investment risk-return tradeoff, asset pricing models, and stock price behavior in relation to capital market efficiency hypotheses. Particular emphasis is placed on stocks, bonds, mutual funds and financial futures and options contracts. Special prominence is given on the study of the operations of securities markets, investment policies, valuation of individual securities, and techniques of investing in securities. Topics covered include investment instruments and their characteristics, introduction to portfolio and capital market theory, theory of valuation of stocks, bonds and the term structure of interest rates, options, commodity and financial futures, investment companies and mutual funds, and international investments.
Investment and Portfolio Analysis (FINC378) > Credit Hours : 3

Investment and Portfolio Analysis (FINC378) > Prerequisites
FINC210 with a minimum grade D
Investment and Portfolio Analysis (FINC378) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate a clear knowledge of the risks and rewards, asset allocation and diversification.

Apply various valuation models to estimate stock and bond prices.

Demonstrate internet and computer competencies by navigating to outside practitioner readings and data sources to interpret financial data and information.

Use appropriate quantitative and analytical techniques using software components to compare investment choices and implement trading strategies.

Produce a concise report on investment analysis, portfolio diversification, and their impact on wealth.

Demonstrate awareness about ethical issues related to financial decisions.

FINC380.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC380 Financial Institutions & Risk Management
FINC380.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC380
This course takes a risk management approach to the analysis of financial institutions operations and is designed to develop an understanding of the challenges in the management and regulation of financial intermediaries. As such, this course is designed to provide students with a conceptual framework necessary for analyzing and comprehending the current problems confronting managers of depository institutions and other intermediaries. It begins with a description of the institutional structure of financial institutions and the current global initiatives to regulate the risk management of banks (Basel accords on capital adequacy). It then characterizes the primary risks financial institutions confront. This is followed by development and use of risk management tools by financial institutions. The emphasis will be on the risk structure, operations and regulation of depository institutions.
Financial Institutions & Risk Management (FINC380) > Credit Hours : 3

Financial Institutions & Risk Management (FINC380) > Prerequisites
FINC341 with a minimum grade D

ECON215 with a minimum grade D
Financial Institutions & Risk Management (FINC380) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the special roles financial intermediaries play and functions they provide.

Contrast the structure and management of depository and other selected intermediary institutions.

Identify the various financial risks facing financial institutions.

4.Analyze the most common and important risk management tools and techniques in financial markets.

Explain the role of derivatives in financial risk management.

FINC422.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC422 Sustainability in Finance
FINC422.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC422
This course explores the principles and practices of sustainable finance, emphasizing the role of finance in addressing environmental, social, and governance (ESG) challenges. Students will learn about the integration of sustainability into investment decisions, the development of green financial instruments, and regulatory initiatives aimed at fostering sustainable financial systems. The course focuses on global trends, challenges, and opportunities in sustainable finance, with a particular emphasis on the financial sector's role in achieving the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
Sustainability in Finance (FINC422) > Credit Hours : 3

Sustainability in Finance (FINC422) > Prerequisites
FINC341

FINC377
Sustainability in Finance (FINC422) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the key concepts and principles of sustainable finance.

Analyze the role of financial institutions and markets in promoting sustainability.

Evaluate environmental, social, and governance risks and opportunities in financial decision-making.

Develop strategies for integrating sustainability into financial products and services.

Examine the regulatory frameworks and global initiatives driving sustainable finance.

FINC434.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC434 Financial Statement Analysis and Business Valuation
FINC434.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC434
The course covers core and applied topics in financial statement analysis and business valuation, with a strong focus on using financial information for investment, credit, and managerial decision-making. Building on knowledge gained in earlier accounting and finance courses, the course equips students with analytical tools to interpret financial statements, assess firm performance, and evaluate financial health in both domestic and multinational contexts. The course is specifically focused on developing a structured approach to business analysis through strategy analysis, accounting analysis, and financial analysis, followed by prospective analysis including forecasting and valuation techniques. The course emphasizes the systematic analysis of firms through strategy analysis, accounting analysis, and financial ratio analysis, followed by prospective analysis techniques such as forecasting and valuation. Students learn how to estimate firm and equity value using fundamental valuation approaches and how financial statement information supports equity security analysis and credit risk assessment. The course further develops practical skills in applying valuation models to real-world scenarios, including equity analysis, credit risk assessment, and financial distress prediction. Particular attention is given to identifying financial distress, evaluating creditworthiness, and understanding the implications of accounting choices on valuation outcomes. In addition, the course develops students’ ability to communicate financial analysis effectively and to understand the role of corporate governance in financial reporting and valuation. By combining theoretical foundations with practical applications, the course prepares students to apply financial statement analysis and valuation techniques in banking, investment, and corporate finance roles.
Financial Statement Analysis and Business Valuation (FINC434) > Credit Hours : 3

Financial Statement Analysis and Business Valuation (FINC434) > Prerequisites
FINC341
Financial Statement Analysis and Business Valuation (FINC434) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the framework of business analysis and valuation using financial statements.

Analyze financial statements to assess the performance of a business entity in various decision-making contexts.

Conduct business forecasting and valuations on the basis of accounting data by applying various quantitative and analytical techniques.

Apply prospective analysis including forecasting and valuation techniques to various contexts such as equity analysis, credit analysis, distress prediction and mergers and acquisitions.

Demonstrate hands-on modeling skills using spreadsheet software to prepare a financial planning model for a business entity, covering financial statement forecasts, ratio analysis and business valuation calculations.

Develop capabilities to work effectively in a group to produce a professional quality report related and to deliver a professional quality presentation.

FINC440.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC440 Financial Econometrics
FINC440.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC440
The underlying course builds upon the notions contained in the Introduction to Econometrics course (ECON 231). The current course deals with the regression model and the assumptions for a good regression model that each needs to be tested. If any assumption is not fulfilled remedies are presented to the students. The course also introduces different volatility models that are crucial for financial applications. Next, multivariate dynamic models are presented and used to test for both symmetric and asymmetric causality and generating impulses response functions as well as variance decomposition. Since financial data is usually non- normally distributed with time-varying volatility, bootstrap simulations are implemented for conducting more accurate empirical inference. In addition, tests for unit roots and cointegration are conducted. Forecasting by using time series data is also an integral part of the course.
Financial Econometrics (FINC440) > Credit Hours : 3

Financial Econometrics (FINC440) > Prerequisites
FINC341

ECON231
Financial Econometrics (FINC440) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate knowledge of financial econometric techniques needed to investigate financial concepts and relationships using appropriate statistical software.

Interpret the results of multivariate regressions and conduct hypothesis testing.

Estimate statistical tests to differentiate between stationary and non-stationary time series.

Utilize statistical tests to determine the presence of long-run relationships with short-run adjustments.

Apply appropriately financial time series models that display significant time variation in conditional variance.

Develop applied financial econometrics research projects.

FINC463.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC463 Case Studies in Finance
FINC463.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC463
This course emphasizes the case study approach to intermediate financial management (corporate finance and security analysis). The course focuses on the application of financial theories and analytical techniques to real-world business situations through structured case study analysis. It is designed to deepen students’ understanding of key corporate finance and investment concepts by engaging them in critical evaluation and decision-making processes based on real financial data and scenarios. The course deals with the applications of principles and techniques of corporate finance to real-world situations through the intensive use of case studies. Topics covered include advanced capital budgeting, corporate governance, mergers and acquisitions, capital structure, dividend policy, short-term financial management and advanced security analysis techniques.
Case Studies in Finance (FINC463) > Credit Hours : 3

Case Studies in Finance (FINC463) > Prerequisites
FINC341

FINC378
Case Studies in Finance (FINC463) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply Theories And Concepts To Practical Problems And Real World Cases In Finance.

Evaluate Investments.

Explain The Macro Implications Of The Financial Management Process.

Produce Professional Quality Reports On Financial Issues.

Analyze financial case studies and communicate findings effectively in written and/or oral form.

Evaluate Financial Decisions Within An Ethical Framework.

FINC470.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC470 Financial Technologies II
FINC470.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC470
The course builds on foundational knowledge from Financial Technologies I and focuses on advanced applications of financial technologies in modern financial systems. It examines cryptoassets, decentralized finance (DeFi), blockchain-based financial innovations, central bank digital currencies (CBDCs), and emerging digital financial ecosystems. The course emphasizes analytical evaluation, portfolio applications, financial innovation strategies, and regulatory challenges in fintech. Students will develop the ability to critically assess fintech solutions and their implications for financial markets, institutions, and policy frameworks.
Financial Technologies II (FINC470) > Credit Hours : 3

Financial Technologies II (FINC470) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate knowledge of financial econometric techniques needed to investigate financial concepts and relationships using appropriate statistical software.

Interpret the results of multivariate regressions and conduct hypothesis testing.

Estimate statistical tests to differentiate between stationary and non-stationary time series.

Utilize statistical tests to determine the presence of long-run relationships with short-run adjustments.

Apply appropriately financial time series models that display significant time variation in conditional variance.

Develop applied financial econometrics research projects.

FINC472.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC472 Portfolio Management
FINC472.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC472
The course deals with the theoretical and operative framework of advanced investment management using modern portfolio theories and money management techniques. It builds and expands on the knowledge the students gained in FINC 377 (Investments). It studies how optimal portfolios are constructed, the relation between risk tolerance and asset allocation, the use of hedging instruments to manage risk or/and enhance expected returns, and performance evaluation given the investor's objectives and constraints. In this course, students will apply portfolio models and concepts to actual market data to perform analytical skills and evaluate equities, fixed income securities and other investments. Asset pricing, diversification and other financial models are covered in detail. Active versus passive investment strategies, trading practices and the role of derivatives in managing securities risk, through case study and simulation approach, will be highlighted throughout the course.
Portfolio Management (FINC472) > Credit Hours : 3

Portfolio Management (FINC472) > Prerequisites
FINC377 with a minimum grade D
Portfolio Management (FINC472) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply various valuation models to estimate stock and bond prices.

Construct optimal portfolios using the mean-variance efficient frontier.

Demonstrate internet and computer competencies by navigating to outside practitioner readings and data sources to collect financial data and information.

Describe active and passive management strategies for stock and bond portfolios and related performance.

Explain the concepts of risk/return tradeoff, asset allocation and Diversification.

Produce a short report related to a portfolio diversification project summarizing their investment choices and trading strategies and explaining how they affected their wealth.

FINC474.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC474 Selected Topics in Finance
FINC474.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC474
This course examines selected advanced and contemporary topics in finance, with emphasis on strategic issues relevant to modern financial practice. Building on prior finance coursework, it develops students’ ability to analyze specialized topics such as mergers and acquisitions, corporate restructuring, valuation, financial distress, venture capital and private equity, behavioral finance, and real estate finance. The specific topic focus for a given offering will be determined by the instructor and communicated to students in the detailed course plan during the first week of the semester. Through this course, students broaden and deepen their understanding of advanced finance issues and their practical applications in industry.
Selected Topics in Finance (FINC474) > Credit Hours : 3

Selected Topics in Finance (FINC474) > Prerequisites
FINC341

FINC377
Selected Topics in Finance (FINC474) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze selected advanced topics related to financial theory, financial markets, financial instruments, and financial institutions.

Interpret financial data and information by using appropriate methods and it applications.

Use appropriate quantitative and analytical techniques to identify a financial problem, analyze and compare alternatives and propose a solution.

Use appropriate technology to deliver effective presentations and produce professional-quality written reports on financial issues.

Collaborate effectively in team-based finance tasks and presentations to achieve agreed objectives.

Evaluate financial decisions within ethical frameworks.

FINC475.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC475 Derivatives Securities
FINC475.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC475
This course covers derivatives products theories and its applications in financial markets. The course covers the conceptual and practical aspects of the use of derivative products for speculation and hedging purposes. It comprehensively studies equity and debt-based options, futures and other derivative instruments. It discusses the functioning of options and futures markets and the role of the market participants. Derivative instruments are analyzed with a focus on pricing, hedging techniques and arbitrage applications. Topics covered include derivatives products theories and applications, derivatives exchanges, valuation of derivatives (futures, forward, swaps and options contracts on different underlying assets), trading practices and regulations and the corporate management of financial risks. Case work and analysis is emphasized throughout the course.
Derivatives Securities (FINC475) > Credit Hours : 3

Derivatives Securities (FINC475) > Prerequisites
FINC377 with a minimum grade D
Derivatives Securities (FINC475) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Acquire and demonstrate necessary knowledge of different derivatives instruments in financial markets, and hedging techniques for reducing risk.

2.Interpret financial data and information by using appropriate methods and IT applications, such as the application of Financial Trading System (FTS) to derivative securities.

Use of appropriate quantitative and analytical techniques to analyze Options Contracts.

Demonstrate proficiency in computer applications relevant to financial analysis and problem solving of Options contracts and Delta-Hedging.

5.Produce professional quality reports that deal with issues pertinent to financial derivatives securities by using appropriate technology to deliver an effective group presentation.

Demonstrate ethical awareness in financial decision making as related to derivative securities and trading of derivative products.

FINC477.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC477 Alternative Finance
FINC477.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC477
This course provides comprehensive theoretical and practical knowledge of alternative investment vehicles, emphasizing their application in modern financial markets. It covers key topics in venture capital, private equity, and hedge funds, focusing on investment strategies, risk-return dynamics, and valuation techniques. Students will develop a working knowledge of the characteristics of alternative assets, including hedge funds and private equity, and explore their historical performance and main strategies. The course delves into security valuation, requiring students to apply these skills to valuing private firms, startups, financially distressed companies, and leveraged buyouts. By the end of the course, students will have a nuanced understanding of alternative investments, their valuation, and their role in enhancing portfolio performance and managing financial risk.
Alternative Finance (FINC477) > Credit Hours : 3

Alternative Finance (FINC477) > Prerequisites
FINC378
Alternative Finance (FINC477) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of the characteristics and investment strategies of alternative securities, including hedge funds, and private equity, and venture capital.

Apply valuation techniques to assess alternative assets, including private firms, startups, distressed companies, and leveraged buyouts.

Apply analytical and quantitative techniques to evaluate theoretical and empirical evidence on risk–return dynamics of alternative investments and their role in portfolio management.

Create professional reports and presentations that effectively communicate analyses and recommendations for alternative investment opportunities.

Exhibit ethical awareness and professional judgment in evaluating and recommending alternative investment decisions in financial markets.

FINC480.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC480 Research in Finance and Banking
FINC480.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC480
This course is a culmination of students’ exposure to the various areas and techniques of banking and finance. The course is intended to provide an integrative experience to studying financial policy analysis. Students will be coached on a one-on-one basis to develop their research interests, choose their research topics in finance and banking, work in groups to write their research papers, and present their results. In the group project, students are expected to shape their research questions, review relevant literature, formulate research hypotheses, collect economic data, implement appropriate econometric models, analyze the results, draw conclusions, and provide policy recommendations. Students will practice how to write a financial policy brief and make oral presentations on their findings and conclusions.
Research in Finance and Banking (FINC480) > Credit Hours : 3

Research in Finance and Banking (FINC480) > Prerequisites
ECON231

FINC434
Research in Finance and Banking (FINC480) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Formulate a proper finance research question and the related research hypotheses.

Identify possible econometric techniques and their requirements for a given research question.

Interpret the results from using a statistical software to draw findings.

Write an effective literature review corresponding to the research problem under consideration.

Effectively communicate, orally and in writing, the research findings and implications for policy makers.

FINC481.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC481 Research in FinTech
FINC481.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC481
This seminar-style course integrates advanced concepts from previous FinTech coursework (FinTech-I and FinTech-II) and Financial Econometrics. Students will independently explore specialized research topics in FinTech, such as blockchain, cryptoassets, digital lending, decentralized finance (DeFi), central bank digital currencies (CBDCs), RegTech, and WealthTech. Emphasis is placed on the use of advanced econometric techniques to analyze financial technology trends, develop research hypotheses, conduct empirical analyses, and critically evaluate policy implications of emerging FinTech innovations. Students will complete original research papers, deliver oral presentations, and critically engage with peers through seminar discussions.
Research in FinTech (FINC481) > Credit Hours : 3

Research in FinTech (FINC481) > Prerequisites
FINC440

FINC470
Research in FinTech (FINC481) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop original research questions related to FinTech innovations.

2)Apply econometric and statistical models to analyze FinTech data.

Evaluate the implications of blockchain, cryptocurrencies, and decentralized finance.

4)Critically assess regulatory, ethical, and cybersecurity challenges in FinTech.

Synthesize research findings and communicate clearly in professional written and oral formats.

FINC600.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC600 Accounting and Finance for Decision Making
FINC600.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC600
This course aims to introduce students to the essentials of financial accounting and business finance. It provides the framework, concepts and tools needed to analyze financial decisions under uncertainty. After getting exposed to the concepts and theoretical foundations underlying financial statements and their use for financial analysis and diagnosis, students will understand the key financial issues facing managers, investors and entrepreneurs. Key topics and concepts include an overview of financial statement analysis, different financing instruments and how corporations issue securities, valuation of bonds and stocks, cost of capital, capital budgeting, and short-term financial planning.
Accounting and Finance for Decision Making (FINC600) > Credit Hours : 3

Accounting and Finance for Decision Making (FINC600) > Prerequisites
ACCT520 or ACCT111
Accounting and Finance for Decision Making (FINC600) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :
