Use appropriate accounting numbers and ratios when diagnosing the financial health and results of a business.

Differentiate the sources of long-term capital (specifically bonds, preferred stock, and common stock) and their use to support business growth.

Evaluate investment decisions using discounted cash flow and risk/return concepts.

Propose short term financial planning and working capital management.

FINC610.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC610 Financial Management
FINC610.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC610
This course aims at introducing MBA students to the essentials of modern corporate finance, financial management, and the process of financial decision-making at the corporate level. It focuses on the role of financial management in maximizing the value of the firm. It provides a framework for understanding the financial dimensions of implementing a competitive strategy in an unpredictable global economy. Throughout this course, students will examine the three responsibilities of a financial manager: (i) Making good investment decisions; (ii) Making good financing decisions; and (iii) implementing appropriate payout policies. Emphasis is on financial decision-making through the extensive use of cases and real-world examples.
Financial Management (FINC610) > Credit Hours : 3

Financial Management (FINC610) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Compare Different Valuation Techniques Used In Practice And Apply Them To Various Decision Making Contexts Such As Investment Decisions, Mergers And Acquisitions, Security And Portfolio Analysis,…

Demonstrate Hands-On Modeling Skills Using Spreadsheet Software To Implement Time Value Of Money, Cost Of Capital And Valuation Calculations And Make Appropriate Financial Decisions In Complex Practical/Real Case Settings.

Describe The Strengths And Pitfalls Of The Value Maximization Objective In Financial Decision Making And Discuss Its Ethical And Social Responsibility Dimensions.

Develop Capabilities To Work Effectively In A Group And/Or Demonstrate Autonomy And Responsibility To Produce A Professional Quality Report Related To A Relevant Financial Management Project, And/Or Deliver A Professional Quality Presentation.

Identify Corporate Financing Alternatives And The Design Of A Company’S Capital Structure And Discuss How Capital Structure And Payout Policies Affect Firm Value.

Make Capital Budgeting Decisions And Compare Alternative Investment Opportunities On The Basis Of Real Accounting And Financial Data By Applying Various Quantitative And Analytical Techniques.

FINC645.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC645 Financial Markets and Trading
FINC645.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC645
This course is designed to provide students with an overview of the organization, structure and mechanisms of securities markets. Students will be exposed to various financial instruments and trading strategies and to the principles of valuation of financial instruments traded in financial markets. In this course, students will also acquire an in-depth understanding of the concepts of efficient markets, fundamental and technical analysis, and will be introduced to derivative securities.
Financial Markets and Trading (FINC645) > Credit Hours : 3

Financial Markets and Trading (FINC645) > Prerequisites
FINC600
Financial Markets and Trading (FINC645) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss the differences between the different financial markets, instruments, and related mechanisms.

Apply various stock, bond valuation models.

Assess the performance of the designed trading strategies using portfolio selection mechanisms.

Explain major financial market failures and related regulations.

FINC650.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC650 International Finance & Banking
FINC650.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC650
The course focuses on the unique problems encountered by the international treasurer or chief financial officer of multinational corporations. It is the international sequel of a corporate finance course and as such it revisits the same funding/financing and investment questions within a multi-currency setting. This course is designed to provide a foundational knowledge of the international business environment and to introduce ideas on how financial management helps multinational firms operate optimally in that environment. Emphasis is on international financial decision-making through the extensive use of cases and real-world examples.
International Finance & Banking (FINC650) > Credit Hours : 3

International Finance & Banking (FINC650) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply Theories And Concepts Related To International Economic Environment In A Multinational Firm Context.

Appreciate Various Appropriate Financial Contracts (Securities) And Their Use In The Efficient Management Of International Business Risks (Particularly The Risk Of Changing Currency Values).

Demonstrate An Understanding Of The Nature And Roles Of The International Monetary System And Of Private Financial Institutions And Markets.

Learn To Identify Ways Of Using The Knowledge Of Uae Business Environment In Optimally Financing International Business.

Learn To Plan And Implement International Financial Decisions In Ways That Optimize The Objectives Of The Firm.

Recognize The Ramifications Of Exchange Rate Fluctuation On The Operation And Profitability Of Multinational And Domestic Firms.

FINC655.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC655 Fintech and Blockchains
FINC655.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC655
This course is designed to help students understand the role of Fintech and Disruptive tools at the intersection of Finance and Technology, called FinTech. It comprises two distinct but related components: (1) Financial Technology and (2) Blockchains. Technology is taking parts in Financial services faster than ever. We have already witnessed how technology is shaping the recent developments in payment systems, insurance, risk management, P2P lending, crowdfunding, money transfers and regulation. For the first part of the course, students will be exposed to issues on Financial Innovation from a theoretical and historical perspective. Here, the role of big data, and artificial intelligence will be examined with several case studies. The second part of the course, i.e., Blockchain and Cryptocurrencies, will introduce students to blockchains, cryptocurrency infrastructure, institutions, cryptoassets, cryptocurrency regulation and the role of blockchains in financial innovation.
Fintech and Blockchains (FINC655) > Credit Hours : 3

Fintech and Blockchains (FINC655) > Prerequisites
FINC600
Fintech and Blockchains (FINC655) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss the significance and limitations of classical financial services in payments, lending, funding and cross-country investments.

Discuss the role of technology and automation with Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning for financial transactions and events.

Evaluate the potential use of Blockchain and Cryptocurrencies in financial services.

Select the most effective Fintech solution in analyzing insurance, risk management, P2P lending, crowdfunding, money transfers and payments.

Propose potential solutions related to recent Blockchain applications in financial transaction considering regulatory aspects.

FINC665.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC665 Applied Corporate Finance
FINC665.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC665
This course aims to consolidate students’ understanding of the fundamental concepts and decision-making tools of modern corporate finance with significant emphasis on application. The course critically examines financial policies relating broadly to the appraisal of investment opportunities, the design of optimal capital structures, the implementation of appropriate dividend payout policy, and the valuation of start-ups, mergers and private equity buyouts. Throughout the course, students will be exposed to real-world applications of a wide range of finance tools to address common issues faced by corporate managers, investors, and entrepreneurs. Extensive and revealing cases will be used to help enhance students’ understanding.
Applied Corporate Finance (FINC665) > Credit Hours : 3

Applied Corporate Finance (FINC665) > Prerequisites
FINC600
Applied Corporate Finance (FINC665) > Corequisites
MGMT666
Applied Corporate Finance (FINC665) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate the value maximization objectives of financial decision-making from organizational and ethical perspectives.

Appraise capital investment decisions by applying various analytical techniques to make informed investment decisions.

Design optimal capital structures and payout policies and evaluate their implications.

Apply different firm/business valuation techniques in real-world financial settings and under various scenarios.

FINC675.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC675 Entrepreneurial Finance
FINC675.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC675
This course aims at providing students with a broad view of the financing landscape for start-ups and during the early stages of company development. Young firms face high degrees of uncertainty and their financing decisions are crucial as they may have implications for their future opportunities and choices. Throughout the course, we emphasize financial opportunities and decisions from both the perspective of entrepreneurs and VC/PE potential investors. Financing decisions and associated valuation tools and techniques are considered for the start-up, then the on-going company in operation to finally cover possible exit routes.
Entrepreneurial Finance (FINC675) > Credit Hours : 3

Entrepreneurial Finance (FINC675) > Prerequisites
FINC600
Entrepreneurial Finance (FINC675) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Appraise relevant financial statements and other firm financial information in the context of an entrepreneurial firm seeking funding.

Apply different methods to value entrepreneurial firms.

Compare possible sources of financing for an entrepreneurial firm including various types of private equity, debt financing and non-traditional sources.

Analyze the investment harvesting process and different exit strategies.

FINC680.title: UAEU Catalog — FINC680 Islamic Finance & Financial Institutions
FINC680.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2911.shtml?id=FINC680
This course is designed to introduce students to the basic concepts of Islamic Finance and the functioning of Islamic financial institutions, applied locally and globally. Topics covered include Islamic banking, bonds (Sukuk), insurance (Takaful), and investment funds. After reviewing the basic concepts of economics from an Islamic perspective, the course introduces and analyzes the financial instruments and techniques developed and used by Islamic financial institutions in the process of collecting savings and making investments. This course also covers special topics such as the worldwide development of the Islamic finance industry, its challenges and opportunities and the regulation and governance of Islamic financial institutions.
Islamic Finance & Financial Institutions (FINC680) > Credit Hours : 3

Islamic Finance & Financial Institutions (FINC680) > Prerequisites
FINC600
Islamic Finance & Financial Institutions (FINC680) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate comprehensive understanding of the Islamic finance theoretical framework.

Demonstrate awareness of the ethical issues associated with the financial services sector.

Design basic Islamic finance products

Assess the risk-return profiles of basic Islamic finance products.

Discuss the state of Islamic finance and its future directions.

ECOM320.title: UAEU Catalog — ECOM320 Probability and Random Processes
ECOM320.text:
An overview of sets, events, single random variables and probability theory; Multiple Random variables, joined density and distribution functions, operations on multiple random variables, moments and characteristic functions, dependence and correlation; multi-variant Gaussian distribution; Random processes, stationarity, ergodicity, correlation functions, temporal and spectral characteristics.
Probability and Random Processes (ECOM320) > Credit Hours : 3

Probability and Random Processes (ECOM320) > Prerequisites
STAT210 with a minimum grade D

MATH135 with a minimum grade D or MATH110 with a minimum grade D
Probability and Random Processes (ECOM320) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Characterize probability models by employing counting methods and basic probability mass function and probability density function canonical models for discrete and continuous random variables. [PLO 1]

Describe conditional and independent events and conditional random variables. [PLO 1]

Characterize jointly multiple discrete and continuous random variables by joint density and distribution functions. [PLO 1]

Evaluate first and second moments and cumulative distribution functions for both discrete and continuous single and multiple random variables. [PLO 1]

Perform operations on single and multiple random variables of expectation and transformation of a single and multiple random variables. [PLO 1]

Characterize stochastic processes with an emphasis on stationary random processes. [PLO 1]

Compute the correlation function and power density spectrums. [PLO 1]

ECOM360.title: UAEU Catalog — ECOM360 Fundamentals of Communication Systems
ECOM360.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ECOM360
Background and overview of communication systems. Analysis and transmission of signals. Analog modulation techniques: amplitude modulation/demodulation, DSB, DSB-SC, SSB, and Phase and frequency Modulation/Demodulation. Analog communication Systems: Super heterodyne receiver, Multiplexing systems, Phase-locked loops, and Television and broadcast systems. Sampling theory and Pulse Modulation: PAM, PPM and PWM.
Fundamentals of Communication Systems (ECOM360) > Credit Hours : 3

Fundamentals of Communication Systems (ECOM360) > Prerequisites
ELEC360 with a minimum grade D
Fundamentals of Communication Systems (ECOM360) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify typical communication channels, effects of channel attenuation and distortion, and noise on transmitted signals using Fourier transform and/or Fourier series. This includes identifying white noise and the effect of the signal-to-noise ratio and its improvement on a communication system.

Analyze ideal and practical filters, distortion (linear and nonlinear), spectral density, and correlation.

Determine the mathematical expressions for amplitude, double sideband, single sideband, and vestigial sideband modulated signals.

Determine the mathematical expressions for phase and frequency modulated signals.

Analyze phase and frequency modulated signals spectrum and derive mathematical expressions for the transmission bandwidth.

Identify different circuits and block diagrams for AM and FM modulation and demodulation.

ECOM402.title: UAEU Catalog — ECOM402 Communication Systems Lab
ECOM402.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ECOM402
Filter design and characteristics. ,AM Modulation/Demodulation Circuits, FM Modulation/Demodulation Circuits.PCM, Delta Modulation, and Delta-Sigma Modulation Circuits. Bandpass digital Modulation/Demodulation techniques ASK ,FSK BPSK QPSK. Spread Spectrum –DSSS mod/dem.,Fiber Optics – basics .
Communication Systems Lab (ECOM402) > Credit Hours : 1

Communication Systems Lab (ECOM402) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co ECOM422 with a minimum grade D
Communication Systems Lab (ECOM402) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Investigate AM/FM modulation/demodulation characteristics and circuits.

Investigate sampling / reconstruction characteristics and PCM techniques and circuits.

Investigate digital modulation/demodulation techniques such as ASK, FSK, BPSK, QPSK.

Investigate spread spectrum – DSSS mod/dem.

ECOM412.title: UAEU Catalog — ECOM412 Electromagnetic Waves
ECOM412.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ECOM412
Time varying fields and Maxwell's equations. Plane wave propagation in perfect dielectric, lossy dielectric and good conducting materials. Power flow and power losses. Standing wave ratio and skin effect. Reflection and refraction of plane waves for normal and oblique wave incidence. Transmission lines (TL), power flow on lossless lines, transient signal analysis on TL. Smith chart, input impedance and matching with single stubs. Rectangular waveguides and resonators.
Electromagnetic Waves (ECOM412) > Credit Hours : 3

Electromagnetic Waves (ECOM412) > Prerequisites
ELEC325 with a minimum grade D
Electromagnetic Waves (ECOM412) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Solve Maxwell’s equations in phasor and time domain to yield the wave equation and compute plane wave propagation properties in conducting, lossless and lossy material and estimate the skin effect and attenuation factor.

Apply EM boundary conditions and solve for normal wave incidence at boundary interface between two and three different dielectric media.

Use the circuit-parameter (RLCG) model of transmission lines (TL) to solve for TL voltages and currents, and compute TL input impedance, standing wave ratio (SWR), and power.

Use the Smith Chart graphical tool in TL analysis, and apply TL concepts and Smith chart in the design and analysis of some TL applications (TL transformer, single stub, and impedance matching circuits).

Analyze transients on a transmission line and their application to some electrical engineering problems.

Define waveguides and solve for Maxwell’s equations in a rectangular waveguide, and understand waveguide propagation modes and compute the properties of TM and TE modes.

Apply the concept of waveguide to the solution of rectangular cavities and resonators.

ECOM422.title: UAEU Catalog — ECOM422 Digital Communication Systems
ECOM422.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ECOM422
Introduction: sampling theorem, quantizing & PCM, the maximum-likelihood (ML) receiver, error probability in ML receivers. Digital modulations: phase-shift keying (PSK), amplitude-shift keying (ASK), & frequency-shift keying (FSK). Pulse shaped modulations. Some advanced topics: differential PSK & offset PSK schemes. Generation of coherent references: phase-locked loops, linear & nonlinear models of PLL in the presence of additive noise.
Digital Communication Systems (ECOM422) > Credit Hours : 3

Digital Communication Systems (ECOM422) > Prerequisites
ECOM320 with a minimum grade D

ECOM360 with a minimum grade D
Digital Communication Systems (ECOM422) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply the theory of Random variables and Random Processes to the digital communication systems.

Employ Sampling Theory and Nyquist criteria for Perfect Reconstruction.

Analyze Binary PCM systems and design binary waveforms, and TDM.

Apply the matched-filter theory for the design and analysis of optimum coherent receiver in AWGN channel.

Distinguish Intersymbol interference and Nyquist Criterion for distortionless baseband data transmission.

Identify signal bases functions for signal analysis and reconstruction.

Use the maximum likelihood (ML) and maximum a-posteriori (MAP) criteria to design and analyze coherent receivers of AWGN channel.

ECOM432.title: UAEU Catalog — ECOM432 Data Communications & Networks
ECOM432.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ECOM432
Principles of data communications; information transfer, computer networks and their applications. Open systems and the OSI reference model. Physical layer, transmission media, multiplexing, analog and digital transmissions. Data Link Layer: media access control, error detection and correction, multiple access, circuit switching: PSTN, packet switching: and Ethernet and gigabit networking. Local Area Networks (LANS), and Wide area Networks, (WANs), Network layer addressing and TCP/IP protocol stack.
Data Communications & Networks (ECOM432) > Credit Hours : 3

Data Communications & Networks (ECOM432) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co ECOM360 with a minimum grade D
Data Communications & Networks (ECOM432) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe data communication system fundamentals, open systems interconnection (OSI) model, and Internet model.

Identify different transmission media, the fundamental limits of digital transmission, and multiplexing techniques.

Apply the coding techniques that can be used to detect and correct errors that may occur during digital transmission.

Demonstrate the operation of transport layer protocols; namely, user datagram protocol (UDP) and transport control protocol (TCP).

Demonstrate the operation of different data link layer point-to-point and multiple access protocols and devices such as switches and bridges.

Design Internet Protocol (IP) sub-networks with static routing tables and general router architecture.

Demonstrate the functionalities of different application layer protocols.

ECOM442.title: UAEU Catalog — ECOM442 Data Communications & Networks Lab
ECOM442.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ECOM442
Network Cabling and Testing, Building a Network, Testing and Troubleshooting a Network, Switching Basics and Intermediate Routing, Routing and Routing Basics, WAN Technologies, Network Monitoring and security, and Wireless LAN.
Data Communications & Networks Lab (ECOM442) > Credit Hours : 1

Data Communications & Networks Lab (ECOM442) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co ECOM432 with a minimum grade D
Data Communications & Networks Lab (ECOM442) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Investigate communication basics and basic functions and types of network devices, media, and protocols.

Investigate OSI model and its layers, their roles and functions, standards, and protocols

Explore the concepts of routing packets related to addressing, path determination, data packets, and IP

Investigate network addressing and how to use the address mask, or prefix length, to determine the number of subnetworks and hosts in a network.

Explore the basic concepts of encapsulation processes that occur as data travels across a lan and a wan.

Utilize simulation tools using packet tracer and wireshark software to practice IP subnetting, building planning and configuring a complex network

ECOM451.title: UAEU Catalog — ECOM451 Digital Signal Processing
ECOM451.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ECOM451
Overview of discrete-time signals and systems, representation of discrete-time systems by means of difference equations. Analysis of discrete-time signals and systems using Fourier and z-transforms. The sampling theory of continuous-time signals, digital processing of continuous-time signals using A/D and D/A conversion. Transform-based analysis of linear time-invariant (LTI) FIR and IIR systems and their structures. Discrete Fourier transform (DFT) and fast algorithms for its computation. FIR and IIR digital filter design.
Digital Signal Processing (ECOM451) > Credit Hours : 3

Digital Signal Processing (ECOM451) > Prerequisites
ECOM360 with a minimum grade D
Digital Signal Processing (ECOM451) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe discrete-time signals and systems as mathematical functions and transformation, respectively.

Apply z-Transform for the analysis and design of DSP systems.

Apply discrete-Time Fourier transform (DTFT) in the analysis of discrete-time signals and systems.

Apply discrete Fourier transform (DFT) in the analysis of discrete-time signals and systems.

Identify basic filters' design and their structures.

Design FIR and IIR digital filters using various techniques, and realization using various structures.

ECOM461.title: UAEU Catalog — ECOM461 Digital Signal Processing Lab
ECOM461.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ECOM461
Fundamentals of applied digital signal processing (DSP) by implementing a wide range of DSP applications on general-purpose DSP development kits. Experiments cover fundamental concepts of digital signal processing like sampling and aliasing, quantization in A/D conversion, digital filter design and implementation, signal generation, spectrum estimation and fast transforms, sampling-rate conversion and multi-rate processing. Application experiments address a selection of multi-media and digital communications problems.
Digital Signal Processing Lab (ECOM461) > Credit Hours : 1

Digital Signal Processing Lab (ECOM461) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co ECOM451 with a minimum grade D
Digital Signal Processing Lab (ECOM461) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply Analog to digital and digital to analog conversion to signals.

Analyze sampling and Aliasing.

Apply Z-transform, and discrete-time Fourier Transform in real time systems.

Design Basic Digital Filter Design and Applications.

Apply Frequency Analysis for Discrete-Time Signals.

Implement Real-Time signal acquisition, processing and DSP Applications.

ECOM530.title: UAEU Catalog — ECOM530 Microwave Circuit Design
ECOM530.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ECOM530
Design and analysis of passive microwave circuits. Topics include transmission lines, electromagnetic field theory, waveguides, microwave network analysis and signal flow graphs, impedance matching and tuning, resonators, power dividers and directional couplers, and microwave filters and components
Microwave Circuit Design (ECOM530) > Credit Hours : 3

Microwave Circuit Design (ECOM530) > Prerequisites
ECOM412 with a minimum grade D
Microwave Circuit Design (ECOM530) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify important Fundamentals of the theory of Transmission lines.

Design Microstrip lines.

Obtain Scattering Parameters and ABCD matrix for multi-port network.

Perform Impedance matching techniques.

Design Power Dividers, Couplers and Filters.

ECOM532.title: UAEU Catalog — ECOM532 Antenna Engineering
ECOM532.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ECOM532
Fields and power radiation of different thin linear antennas (e.g. ideal dipole, electrically short dipole, half wave dipole and dipole over perfect ground plane). Antenna parameters in the far zone: radiation pattern, beam width, side lobe level, radiation resistance, power loss, efficiency, directivity, gain and polarization. Antennas in communication links and radar (Friis formula, radar cross-section, effective aperture). Antenna arrays: array factor, radiation pattern, beam width and directivity of isotropic arrays and short dipole arrays, case of uniformly excited, equally spaced linear arrays. Descriptive study of wire antennas (e.g. Yagi-Uda) and broadband antennas (e.g. helical, biconical).
Antenna Engineering (ECOM532) > Credit Hours : 3

Antenna Engineering (ECOM532) > Prerequisites
ECOM412 with a minimum grade D
Antenna Engineering (ECOM532) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Determine antenna specifications and parameters, and determine the far-zone radiated fields and polarization

Evaluate the receiving characteristics (field strength, antenna effective aperture, received power, etc) in simple communication links using the Friis transmission formula

Calculate the radiation properties of arbitrarily oriented wire antennas in the presence of a perfectly conducting ground plane

Evaluate the analytical expression of the array factor and the radiation properties of uniform array. .

Design linear arrays with phase steering using the concept of pattern multiplication to obtain the radiation pattern of non-uniformly excited linear arrays and 2-D arrays.

Design Smart antenna for communication system

ECOM542.title: UAEU Catalog — ECOM542 Wireless Communications
ECOM542.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ECOM542
Introduction to wireless communication systems. The cellular concept and system design fundamentals: frequency reuse, interference and system capacity. Radio propagation and large-scale path loss. Small-scale fading and multipath propagation: Doppler shift, mobile multipath channel parameters such as coherence bandwidth and coherence time. Diversity techniques and diversity combining. Spread spectrum communication techniques. Multiple access techniques: TDMA, FDMA, CDMA, SDMA. Current and future wireless systems and standards.
Wireless Communications (ECOM542) > Credit Hours : 3

Wireless Communications (ECOM542) > Prerequisites
ECOM360 with a minimum grade D

ECOM412 with a minimum grade D
Wireless Communications (ECOM542) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Characterize of mobile communication channel and apply analytical and empirical propagation models in the design of wireless links

Use of the basics of traffic and queuing theory in the design a cellular communication system.

Apply capacity and coverage enhancement techniques.

Analyze the performance of digital wireless systems in terms of BER and outage probability.

Distinguish multiple radio access and division techniques.

Recognize the need of diversity, equalization, coding, interleaving and data link control techniques for wireless communications.

ECOM560.title: UAEU Catalog — ECOM560 Radar System Fundamentals and Applications
ECOM560.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ECOM560
This course introduces the fundamental principles of radar systems and their applications. Topics include radar equations, types of radar, pulse and Doppler radar, radar cross-section, signal processing techniques, tracking radars, and radar applications in remote sensing, military, and automotive systems.
Radar System Fundamentals and Applications (ECOM560) > Credit Hours : 3

Radar System Fundamentals and Applications (ECOM560) > Prerequisites
ECOM412 with a minimum grade D

ECOM451 with a minimum grade D
Radar System Fundamentals and Applications (ECOM560) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the fundamental radar equation and performance factors.

Explain different radar types and their applications.

Analyze Doppler radar and pulse compression techniques.

Evaluate radar signal processing methods.

Design tracking radars and phased arrays.

ECOM561.title: UAEU Catalog — ECOM561 Information Theory & Coding
ECOM561.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ECOM561
The concept of amount of information; average information; entropy and information rate; Shannon's theorem; channel capacity. Coding: mathematics of coding, groups, rings, fields and Galois fields. Block codes: parity and generator matrix, syndrome, and minimum distance. Cyclic and BCH codes; Convolutional codes and Viterbi decoding algorithm.
Information Theory & Coding (ECOM561) > Credit Hours : 3

Information Theory & Coding (ECOM561) > Prerequisites
ECOM360 with a minimum grade D
Information Theory & Coding (ECOM561) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Calculate the amount of information & uncertainty

Apply source coding theorem such as Huffman & Lempel-Ziv coding techniques

Apply information capacity and coding theorem

Determine parity-check matrix for linear block codes

Design a convolutional encoder and implement Viterbi algorithm to decode convolutional codes

Evaluate the performance of selected coding algorithms on some error-correction and coding techniques using Matlab

ECOM562.title: UAEU Catalog — ECOM562 Satellite Communications Systems
ECOM562.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ECOM562
Introduction to Satellite Communication Systems. Link Analysis. Satellite Communication Techniques. Multiple Access Techniques. Multibeam Satellite Systems. Regenerative Satellite Systems. Broadcasting by Satellites. Inter Satellite Links. Satellite Communication Payload, Earth Station Technology, Project Work
Satellite Communications Systems (ECOM562) > Credit Hours : 3

Satellite Communications Systems (ECOM562) > Prerequisites
ECOM412 with a minimum grade D
Satellite Communications Systems (ECOM562) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Understand Satellites Spacecraft subsystems.

Identify satellite different payload and applications. [

Be familiar with the satellite Communication Systems and the future needs and challenges.

Be familiar with satellite link budget.

Identify Earth Station antenna and equipment.

Design satellite communication systems and to do a systems tradeoff design.

ECOM571.title: UAEU Catalog — ECOM571 Communication Circuits
ECOM571.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ECOM571
RF signals in analog and digital modulations. RF circuits including linear amplifiers, mixers, oscillators, detectors, limiters, and power amplifiers; Transmitter and receiver structures; Phase locked loops; Design of RF integrated circuits; Circuit concepts like stability, noise, distortion, intermodulation, and dynamic range. Design problems of RF communication circuits or subsystems based on component, circuit, and system data and specifications.
Communication Circuits (ECOM571) > Credit Hours : 3

Communication Circuits (ECOM571) > Prerequisites
ELEC370 with a minimum grade D

ECOM360 with a minimum grade D
Communication Circuits (ECOM571) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain principles of the most common radio transmitter and receiver systems

Use narrow band approximations and series-to-parallel conversions to design frequency selective networks

Construct RF impedance matching and transformation circuits using discrete components

Analysis and Design of RF circuits amplifiers

Analysis and Design of analog filters

Calculate signal-to-noise ratio noise-figure of amplifiers

Understand the theory and applications of phase-locked loops

ECOM580.title: UAEU Catalog — ECOM580 Special Topics in Communications
ECOM580.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ECOM580
Topics in communications engineering are chosen by the course instructor at the beginning of the term and approved by the department council.
Special Topics in Communications (ECOM580) > Credit Hours : 3

Special Topics in Communications (ECOM580) > Prerequisites
ECOM412 with a minimum grade D or ECOM360 with a minimum grade D
Special Topics in Communications (ECOM580) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify different implementation requirements of communication systems by applying communication engineering principles.

Identify design methodologies related to communication systems in the contexts of environmental, economic and social standards.

Examine solutions to the state-of-the-art communication engineering problems, and communicate findings.

ELEC290.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC290 Artificial Intelligence for Engineering
ELEC290.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC290
This course covers the fundamentals and importance of Artificial Intelligence (AI) with a focus on both theoretical concepts and engineering applications with ethical considerations. Students will learn the importance of Artificial Intelligence in engineering, understand its basics and apply algorithms such as Decision Trees, Regression and Classification of engineering data. Students will also be able to train, and test data models to understand underfitting, overfitting, and cross-validation. Students will be exposed to different evaluation methodologies for supervised and unsupervised learning, including deep learning techniques as applied to engineering disciplines with examples.
Artificial Intelligence for Engineering (ELEC290) > Credit Hours : 3

Artificial Intelligence for Engineering (ELEC290) > Prerequisites
MATH140 with a minimum grade D

STAT210 with a minimum grade D
Artificial Intelligence for Engineering (ELEC290) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the artificial intelligence concept as applied to engineering with examples

Explain Regression and Classification concepts with examples of engineering

Employ supervised, unsupervised, and deep learning concepts

Use artificial intelligence models for engineering applications

Recognize Ethics of Artificial Intelligence

ELEC305.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC305 Electric Circuits I
ELEC305.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC305
Circuit Analysis Techniques: Nodal Analysis, Mesh Analysis, Source Transformation, Superposition, Thevenin?s and Norton Theorems. Transient Response: First Order RC & RL Circuits, Step Response & Time Constants, Second Order RLC Circuits, Resonance & Quality Factor. Sinusoids and Phasors: Phasor Representation of Sinusoids, Impedance & Admittance, Circuit Analysis using Phasors. Average Power and RMS values. Operational Amplifiers (Op Amp): Ideal Op Amp Operation, Circuit Analysis of Op Amp Inverting Configuration, Applications of Inverting Configuration, Circuit Analysis of Op Amp Non-Inverting Configuration.
Electric Circuits I (ELEC305) > Credit Hours : 3

Electric Circuits I (ELEC305) > Prerequisites
MATH135 with a minimum grade D or MATH110 with a minimum grade D
Electric Circuits I (ELEC305) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze DC electric circuits using nodal and loop analysis.

Analyze the current and voltage using network theorems such as Superposition, and Source-transformation, Thevenin’s, Norton’s, and Maximum-Power-Transfer.

Investigate the ideal Op-Amp characteristics and applications.

Identify the voltage–current relationship and compute energy stored ion inductors and capacitors circuits.

Analyze the transient response of first order RL and RC circuits as well as second order RLC circuits.

Analyze the AC steady-state and transient of RLC circuits’ w.r.t the impedance, admittance and AC-power.

ELEC310.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC310 Electric Circuits I lab
ELEC310.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC310
Introduction to Circuit Simulators. Circuit Analysis Techniques I (Nodal & Mesh Analysis). Circuit Analysis Techniques II (Thevenin?s & Norton & Superposition). Transient Analysis of RC & RL circuits. Resonance & Quality Factor of RLC Circuits. Circuit Analysis using Phasors. Networks DC & Transient Analysis. Op Amp Circuits I (Configurations & Circuit Analysis). Op Amp Circuits II (Op Amp Applications). Op Amp Limitations.
Electric Circuits I lab (ELEC310) > Credit Hours : 1

Electric Circuits I lab (ELEC310) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co ELEC305 with a minimum grade D
Electric Circuits I lab (ELEC310) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Conduct experiments to analyze circuits using nodal and super position techniques.

Conduct experiments to verify Thevenin’ theorems.

Design, analyze and implement Op-Amp circuits.

Conduct experiments to study the transient behavior of first- and second-order circuits.

Conduct experiments to study the steady state response, resonance, and complex power of circuits excited by AC sources.

Effectively use Multisim tools to design, model and simulate circuits.

ELEC315.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC315 Fundamentals of Microelec Devices
ELEC315.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC315
Semiconductors: energy bands, carrier concentration, carrier transport phenomena: drift, diffusion. P-N Junction: current-voltage characteristics. Diode models. Diode circuit applications: Rectifiers, Clippers, Clamper, Zener diode (Regulators). Metal-Semiconductor Contacts: equilibrium, idealized metal semiconductor junctions, non-rectifying (Ohmic) contacts, Schottky diodes. Metal Oxide Semiconductor (MOS) capacitance. MOS Field-Effect Transistor: structure, current-voltage characteristics, DC biasing., the MOSFET as an amplifier and as a switch. Bipolar junction transistor (BJT): structure, current-voltage characteristics, DC biasing, charge control switching model, Ebers-Moll model.
Fundamentals of Microelec Devices (ELEC315) > Credit Hours : 3

Fundamentals of Microelec Devices (ELEC315) > Prerequisites
ELEC305 with a minimum grade D
Fundamentals of Microelec Devices (ELEC315) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explore basics of semiconductor materials and electrical characteristics.

Investigate diode characteristics and diode-based circuits.

Examine MOSFET structure, electrical characteristics, DC biasing and the use of MOSFET as switch and amplifier.

Examine BJT structure, electrical characteristics, DC biasing and the use of BJT as switch and amplifier.

Use simulation tools to analyze bias point, DC sweep and perform transient analysis.

ELEC320.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC320 Electric Circuits II
ELEC320.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC320
Review of Instantaneous Power, Average power and RMS values, Active and Reactive Power. Three Phase Circuits and Power Distribution systems: Configuration of Different Three phase Systems, Three phase Power, Power factor Correction. Magnetically Coupled Circuits: Mutual Inductance, Dot Convention, Energy stored, Ideal Transformers, Three Phase Transformers. Frequency Response: Network Functions, Bode Plot, Resonance Circuits. Two port networks: Admittance Parameters, Impedance Parameters and Hybrid Parameters.
Electric Circuits II (ELEC320) > Credit Hours : 3

Electric Circuits II (ELEC320) > Prerequisites
ELEC305 with a minimum grade D
Electric Circuits II (ELEC320) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze instantaneous power, average power, complex power and power factor in AC networks at steady-state conditions.

Analyze three-phase circuits and three-phase source/load connections.

Analyze self and mutual inductances, energy stored in magnetically coupled networks and ideal transformers.

Interpret Bode plots for electrical circuits.

Analyze filters and resonant circuits.

Analyze admittance, impedance, hybrid and transmission parameters in linear two-port networks.

ELEC325.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC325 Engineering Electromagnetics
ELEC325.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC325
The course covers field theory topics related to stationary and moving charges. Coulomb’s law, Electric flux and Gauss’s law, Divergence theorem and capacitance. Electric boundary conditions. Magnetostatics: steady magnetic field, Biot-Savart Law, Ampere’s Law, Stokes’ theorem and magnetic flux. Magnetic force and inductance. Magnetic boundary conditions. Faraday’s law and Maxwell’s equations. Introduction to transmission line theory.
Engineering Electromagnetics (ELEC325) > Credit Hours : 3

Engineering Electromagnetics (ELEC325) > Prerequisites
PHYS110 with a minimum grade D

PHYS140 with a minimum grade D

MATH135 with a minimum grade D or MATH210
Engineering Electromagnetics (ELEC325) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Compute electric field intensity and electric potential due to different charge distributions using Coulomb’s law and Gauss’s law. [PLO-1].

Compute the electric field inside an electric material space (dielectric, conductors) with application to resistance and capacitance. [PLO-1, 2]

Compute magnetic field and energy using Ampere’s circuital law and Biot-Savart law. [PLO-1]

Apply magnetic field fundamentals to the analysis and design of magnetic circuits. [PLO-1, 2]

Apply Faraday’s law to solve for time varying electromagnetic field. [PLO-1, 7]

Solve the transmission line equations in lossless medium. [PLO-1, 7]

ELEC335.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC335 Digital Logic Design
ELEC335.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC335
Data representation, number systems, codes, arithmetic operations, Boolean algebra, logic gate, combinational logic circuits, minimization techniques, MSI modules: adder, decoders, multiplexers, programmable logic arrays. Flip Flops, sequential circuits, registers, counters, and memory. Design of synchronous and asynchronous sequential circuits, state diagrams, state minimization and assignment. Memories.
Digital Logic Design (ELEC335) > Credit Hours : 3

Digital Logic Design (ELEC335) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Manipulate number system, binary codes, and computer arithmetic.

Apply Boolean algebra and Karnaugh map minimization techniques to simplify Boolean expressions.

Design binary adders, decoders, encoders, multiplexers, and de-multiplexers to implement combinational logic circuits.

Design with flip-flops, synchronous and asynchronous sequential circuits, state diagrams, and state tables.

Design registers (serial, parallel, and shift) ripple counters, and synchronous counters.

Design digital circuits with memory devices of ROMs, PLAs, & PALs.

ELEC345.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC345 Digital Logic Design Lab
ELEC345.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC345
Hands-on experimentation with primitive logic gates, decoders, multiplexers, adders, flip-flops, counters, registers, LEDs, and seven-segment displays.
Digital Logic Design Lab (ELEC345) > Credit Hours : 1

Digital Logic Design Lab (ELEC345) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co ELEC335 with a minimum grade D
Digital Logic Design Lab (ELEC345) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Construct digital circuits using primitive logic gates.

Design digital combinational circuits using Medium Scale Integrated Circuits such as decoders, multiplexers and comparators.

Construct combinational circuits using adders, seven-segment decoders and seven-segment displays.

Construct sequential circuits using several types of flip-flops.

Construct sequential circuits using counters and seven-segment displays.

ELEC360.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC360 Signals & Systems
ELEC360.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC360
Continuous-time and discrete-time signals and systems. Linear time-invariant (LTI) systems: system properties, convolution sum and the convolution integral representation, system properties, LTI systems described by differential and difference equations. Fourier series: properties and applications, Fourier transform: properties and applications. Laplace Transform: properties and applications.
Signals & Systems (ELEC360) > Credit Hours : 3

Signals & Systems (ELEC360) > Prerequisites
MATH275 with a minimum grade D
Signals & Systems (ELEC360) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Understand the basics of signals and Systems: including signals’ operation, classifications, operation and conditioning, systems properties, classifications, and modeling.

Solve first and second order systems using system impulse responses and convolution, find the zero-input and zero-state responses).

Derive the generalized Fourier Series (FS) expansion of a signal, sketch and interpret the Frequency Line Spectra of periodic signals.

Find Fourier Transform (FT) and understand its properties, sketch and interpret the Frequency Spectra of signals.

Apply Fourier transform techniques in applications of system analysis such as basic ideal filters and AM modulation.

Use computing tools such as Matlab to signal and systems analysis problems.

ELEC365.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC365 Principles and Practice of Systems Engineering
ELEC365.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC365
This course provides the foundational principles and methods of systems engineering, emphasizing a structured, interdisciplinary approach to the development of complex systems. It covers the full system life cycle—from concept to retirement—while presenting techniques such as requirements definition, functional analysis, system architecture, modeling, risk assessment, and trade off analysis.
Principles and Practice of Systems Engineering (ELEC365) > Credit Hours : 3

Principles and Practice of Systems Engineering (ELEC365) > Prerequisites
ELEC360 with a minimum grade D or MECH350 with a minimum grade D
Principles and Practice of Systems Engineering (ELEC365) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the principles, scope, and life cycle of systems engineering.

Analyze stakeholder needs and system requirements

Apply systems thinking for decomposition, interface definition, and integration

Evaluate design alternatives using trade-offs and risk analysis.

Communicate systems engineering documentation and design rationale

ELEC370.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC370 Electronic Circuits
ELEC370.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC370
Low and high frequency models for transistors. Small-signal analysis and design of single-stage MOSFET amplifiers. Small-signal analysis and design of single-stage BJT amplifiers. Frequency response characteristics of amplifiers. Multistage amplifiers: Small signal analysis and Frequency response characteristics of multistage amplifiers. Negative feedback: Properties and the four basic feedback topologies. Wave shaping: Basic principles of Sinusoidal Oscillators, Op Amp-RC Oscillator circuits, LC and crystal Oscillators, Multi-vibrators, and Voltage controlled oscillators (VCO). Output stages and power amplifiers: Classification.
Electronic Circuits (ELEC370) > Credit Hours : 3

Electronic Circuits (ELEC370) > Prerequisites
ELEC315 with a minimum grade D or MECH350 with a minimum grade D
Electronic Circuits (ELEC370) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe classification of electronic signals, understand signal amplification process, and explore circuit models for amplifiers.

Analyze and design the different configurations of single stage and multistage amplifiers based on small signal ac-model and discuss the gain, input and output resistances.

Determine the frequency response of an amplifier and understand the role of coupling and bypass capacitors.

Evaluate the effect of negative and positive feedback on the amplifier and wave-shaping circuits.

Explore different classes of power amplifier circuits.

ELEC372.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC372 Electro-Mechanical Devices
ELEC372.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC372
AC circuit analysis: phasors steady state power analysis, polyphase circuits; basics of electrical machines construction, theory of operation, equivalent circuit and its governing equations of DC machines, 3-phase synchronous generations, single phase transformers, and 3-phase induction motors, semiconductor devices and transducers.
Electro-Mechanical Devices (ELEC372) > Credit Hours : 2

Electro-Mechanical Devices (ELEC372) > Prerequisites
MECH350 with a minimum grade D
Electro-Mechanical Devices (ELEC372) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the main components, of the electric circuits the basic theories, and the power sign convention

Apply analysis techniques (mesh, node, superposition and Thevenin) to solve DC&AC circuits.

Determine the instantaneous power, average power, complex power, and power factor in single-phase and three-phase AC networks

Realize the basic principles of single-phase transformer, its equivalent circuit, and the efficiency and regulation concepts

Identify the construction, operation, and basic characteristics of the 3-phase Synchronous Generator

Identify the construction, operation, and basic characteristics of the 3-phase Induction Motors

ELEC375.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC375 Electronic Circuits Lab
ELEC375.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC375
Diode Characteristics & Circuit Applications, Zener Diode Characteristics & Circuit Applications. FET Characteristics, FET Amplifiers and frequency response characteristics. BJT DC Characteristics, BJT Amplifiers and frequency response characteristics. RC Coupled Amplifier characteristics and frequency response, Feedback amplifier operation and characteristics, Hartley and Colpitts oscillators and multivibrators, Complementary Power Amplifier DC Operation, AC Voltage and Power Gain.
Electronic Circuits Lab (ELEC375) > Credit Hours : 1

Electronic Circuits Lab (ELEC375) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co ELEC370 with a minimum grade D

ELEC310 with a minimum grade D
Electronic Circuits Lab (ELEC375) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explore the characteristics, operation and circuits of Diodes and Zeners.

Investigate the operation, characteristics and design of single stage and multistage amplifiers.

Investigate the operation and characteristics of feedback amplifiers.

Investigate the operation, characteristics and design of wave generators.

Explore the operation and characteristics of Power amplifiers and Regulated Power supplies.

ELEC380.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC380 Analytical Methods for Electrical Engineering
ELEC380.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC380
Complex analysis: complex numbers, complex functions, complex integration, and series representations of complex functions. Ordinary differential equations: first order, second order, power series and Frobenius methods, boundary-value problems, Fourier series, and Strum-Liouville problem. Partial differential equations: the wave equation, the heat equation, and the Laplace equation. Applications include circuit theory, digital signal processing, control theory, and electromagnetics.
Analytical Methods for Electrical Engineering (ELEC380) > Credit Hours : 3

Analytical Methods for Electrical Engineering (ELEC380) > Prerequisites
MATH275 with a minimum grade D
Analytical Methods for Electrical Engineering (ELEC380) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain Complex variables and functions

Apply complex differentiation and integration to complex functions.

Solve initial value problems and boundary value problems

Identify Sturm-Liouville Boundary value problems and orthogonal functions

Solve Partial differential equations.

Develop Solutions involving physical systems and applications

ELEC395.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC395 Artificial Intelligence Applications in Engineering Laboratory
ELEC395.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC395
Introduction to AI and machine learning, hands-on in data acquisition and sensor interface. Computer experiments to cover applications in IoT and smart systems, including smart homes, smart health, autonomous driving, and robotics.
Artificial Intelligence Applications in Engineering Laboratory (ELEC395) > Credit Hours : 1

Artificial Intelligence Applications in Engineering Laboratory (ELEC395) > Prerequisites
ELEC345 with a minimum grade D

GENG230 with a minimum grade D

Pre/Co ELEC375 with a minimum grade D
Artificial Intelligence Applications in Engineering Laboratory (ELEC395) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Understand the basics of machine learning, artificial intelligence and IoT

Analyze datasets using machine learning methods for regression and classification

Explore data acquisition and sensor interface platforms.

Develop AI skills for machine learning in IoT based applications such as home-automation, smart health, robotics, autonomous driving etc.

Demonstrate ability to work with a group and communicate findings effectively.

ELEC411.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC411 Electric Energy Conversion
ELEC411.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC411
Faraday's Law and applications, Magnetic circuits and introduction to the machinery principles. Single phase transformer, Ideal and Real Transformers theory of operation, Modeling and derivation of equivalent circuit parameters, experimental determination of equivalent circuit parameters. Theory of operation of AC Machines. 3-phase synchronous Generators, theory of operation, Machine modeling, experimental determination of the equivalent circuit parameters and parallel operation. Induction motors, theory of operation, Equivalent circuit development, experimental determination of equivalent circuit parameters, torque speed curve characteristics.
Electric Energy Conversion (ELEC411) > Credit Hours : 3

Electric Energy Conversion (ELEC411) > Prerequisites
ELEC320 with a minimum grade D

ELEC325 with a minimum grade D
Electric Energy Conversion (ELEC411) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze magnetic circuit and its relationship to transformers and electric machines.

Apply the theory of operation of ideal and real transformers.

Explain the basic working principle of DC and AC machines.

Describe the operation of synchronous machines.

Describe the operation of induction machines.

ELEC431.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC431 Control Systems
ELEC431.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC431
Control Systems in the Real World, Feedback Concept, Modeling of Dynamic Systems, Block Diagrams, Sensitivity and Disturbance Analysis, Steady State Error Analysis, Stability Analysis, Time Domain Analysis of Control Systems, Frequency Domain Analysis of Control Systems, Control system design in frequency domain (Nyquist and Nichols Charts), Control System Design in time domain (Proportional-Integral-Derivative Control and lead-lag compensator).
Control Systems (ELEC431) > Credit Hours : 3

Control Systems (ELEC431) > Prerequisites
ELEC360 with a minimum grade D

MATH140 with a minimum grade D
Control Systems (ELEC431) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Formulate the mathematical models of systems.

Analyze time response of the first order systems, second order systems, and higher order systems.

Use reduction techniques of block diagrams with multiple subsystems.

Evaluate the stability and steady-state error of the closed loop systems.

Apply frequency response techniques.

Design controllers for closed-loop systems.

ELEC433.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC433 Instrument & Control Lab
ELEC433.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC433
Practical analysis and design of feedback control systems and components: control design of second-order systems, PID control design, Programmable Logic Controllers.
Instrument & Control Lab (ELEC433) > Credit Hours : 1

Instrument & Control Lab (ELEC433) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co ELEC431 with a minimum grade D
Instrument & Control Lab (ELEC433) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the main components of dynamical systems (plant, actuators, sensors...)

Differentiate between the performance of open-loop and closed-loop systems

Identify the parameters of the PID controller for real setups based on its open loop step response.

Use the data acquisition boards and the modern engineering tools such as MATLAB and LABVIEW in control systems

Implement different types of PLC controllers for specific tasks in real systems.

ELEC451.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC451 Microprocessors
ELEC451.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC451
Architecture of a Microcomputer System, Evolution of the Microprocessors, Software Architecture of the 8088/8086 Microprocessors, Software Development Tools, Instruction Set, Assembly Language Programming Techniques, Interfacing and Applications, Interrupts.
Microprocessors (ELEC451) > Credit Hours : 3

Microprocessors (ELEC451) > Prerequisites
ELEC335 with a minimum grade D

GENG230 with a minimum grade D
Microprocessors (ELEC451) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain internal architecture of CISC microprocessors and its comparison to RISC family processors.

Illustrate the different addressing modes of the microprocessor using assembly instructions.

Analyze the instruction set of the microprocessor, including data transfer, arithmetic and logic, and control instructions.

Compose procedures for assembly programs.

Show hardware organization of the microprocessor, I/O and memory interfaces.

Construct assembly programs to solve engineering problems.

ELEC461.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC461 Microprocessors Lab
ELEC461.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC461
Software debugging and development tools, Instruction set, Assembly language programming techniques with applications.
Microprocessors Lab (ELEC461) > Credit Hours : 1

Microprocessors Lab (ELEC461) > Prerequisites
ELEC451 with a minimum grade D

ELEC345 with a minimum grade D
Microprocessors Lab (ELEC461) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze instructions using a debugger or a similar tool.

Write assembly programs, procedures including interrupt service routines using a assembler tool.

Develop assembly programs to access memory and peripheral devices for data operations.

Test assembly programs to configure and control peripheral devices using a microprocessor toolkit.

ELEC462.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC462 Computer Architecture & Organization
ELEC462.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC462
Basic structure of computers, machine programs sequencing, addressing modes, micro-programmed control, CISC & RISC CPUs, instruction architecture, data path and control, computer arithmetic, input-output organizations, I/O channels computer communications, memory organizations.
Computer Architecture & Organization (ELEC462) > Credit Hours : 3

Computer Architecture & Organization (ELEC462) > Prerequisites
ELEC451 with a minimum grade D
Computer Architecture & Organization (ELEC462) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain functional units, fetch-execute cycle, and internal structure of a CPU

Apply various I/O techniques for serial and parallel connections

Use computer arithmetic circuits to solve computing problems

Analyze various memory organization techniques in solving storage problems

Examine techniques to increase instruction throughput like pipelining & parallel processing

Employ digital-design tools to simulate hardware functions

ELEC472.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC472 Power Systems
ELEC472.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC472
Power Systems Concept and Components, The UAE Power Network, Review of Phasors and Complex Power, Balanced Three-phase Circuits, Per Unit Notation, Transmission Line Parameters, Modeling of Transmission Lines in the Steady State Mode, Introduction to Power Flow, Fundamentals of Symmetrical faults calculation, Computer applications.
Power Systems (ELEC472) > Credit Hours : 3

Power Systems (ELEC472) > Prerequisites
ELEC320 with a minimum grade D

ELEC325 with a minimum grade D
Power Systems (ELEC472) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze steady-state performance of single phase and balanced three-phase systems.

Use one-line diagram and per unit notations for modelling power system elements, including generators, transmission lines, transformers, and loads.

Explain the equivalent circuits of short, medium, and long overhead transmission lines.

Describe multi-node power systems using admittance matrix or impedance matrix for power flow study.

Solve power flow problem using Gauss-Seidel method and Newton-Raphson approach.

Analyze electric power systems during symmetrical faults.

ELEC481.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC481 Electric Energy Conversion Lab
ELEC481.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC481
Transformer basics including turns ratio test, open-circuit test and short circuit test to determine the equivalent circuit parameters, in addition to exploring the concept of the voltage regulation and efficiency. DC machines (motors and generators) operation and basic characteristics. Basic tests and modeling of 3-phase synchronous generator in addition to the load characteristics. Torque-speed, efficiency, starting and other main characteristics of the Induction Motors.
Electric Energy Conversion Lab (ELEC481) > Credit Hours : 1

Electric Energy Conversion Lab (ELEC481) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co ELEC411 with a minimum grade D
Electric Energy Conversion Lab (ELEC481) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze data for the equivalent circuit, losses, voltage regulation, and efficiency of the single-phase transformer.

Differentiate between the different types of connections and vector groups of the three-phase transformers.

Examine the main characteristics of the DC machines (motors and generators).

Examine the main characteristics of the synchronous generator, its parameters, and its regulation under R, L and C loads.

Examine the main characteristics of the induction machine, its parameters, and the types of losses in this machine.

ELEC485.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC485 Internship I
ELEC485.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC485
Students spend 8 weeks on a full-time basis in an engineering or consulting office in the UAE or abroad to earn practical skills. This course aims at offering career exploration opportunities for students.
Internship I (ELEC485) > Credit Hours : 1

Internship I (ELEC485) > Prerequisites
STAT210 with a minimum grade D

GENG230 with a minimum grade D

MATH275 with a minimum grade D

MATH140 with a minimum grade D

PHYS110 with a minimum grade D

PHYS140 with a minimum grade D

CHEM111 with a minimum grade D

CHEM175 with a minimum grade D

ELEC305 with a minimum grade D

ELEC315 with a minimum grade D

ELEC325 with a minimum grade D

ELEC335 with a minimum grade D

ELEC360 with a minimum grade D

ELEC310 with a minimum grade D

ELEC345 with a minimum grade D
Internship I (ELEC485) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Function effectively in multi-disciplinary teams and individually to achieve the planed tasks and goals.

Develop communication skills through oral and written presentations.

Evaluate different engineering situations and judgments based on ethical codes and professional responsibilities.

ELEC490.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC490 Internship II
ELEC490.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC490
Students spend 8 weeks on a full-time basis in an engineering or consulting office in the UAE or abroad to earn practical skills. This course aims at offering career exploration opportunities for students as well as opportunities to correlate their academic preparation to the reality of conducting professional practice, to interact effectively with others in practice, to develop professional skills and communicate effectively in the workplace and to gain true practical experience that is necessary for their future practice as engineers in their respective discipline after graduation.
Internship II (ELEC490) > Credit Hours : 1

Internship II (ELEC490) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co ELEC485 with a minimum grade P

CHEM270 with a minimum grade D

GENG215 with a minimum grade D

GENG315 with a minimum grade D

ELEC370 with a minimum grade D

ECOM360 with a minimum grade D

ELEC380 with a minimum grade D

ELEC375 with a minimum grade D

ELEC451 with a minimum grade D

ELEC320 with a minimum grade D or ( ECOM320 with a minimum grade D and ECOM412 with a minimum grade D)
Internship II (ELEC490) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Function effectively in multi-disciplinary teams and individually to achieve the planed tasks and goals.

Develop communication skills through oral and written presentations.

Evaluate different engineering situations and judgments based on ethical codes and professional responsibilities.

Propose innovative ideas/solutions for real-life problems based on the learned knowledge.

ELEC512.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC512 Digital Electronics
ELEC512.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC512
MOS Digital Circuits: Digital Circuit Design Overview, the MOSFET as a Digital Circuit Element Design and performance Analysis of the CMOS Inverter, CMOS Logic Circuits Pseudo-NMOS Circuits, Pass-Transistor Logic Circuits, Dynamic Logic Circuits, Latches and Flip-Flops, Multivibrators, Semiconductor Memories: Types and Architectures, Random-Access Memory (RAM) Cells, Read-Only Memory (ROM). Bipolar Digital Circuits: The BJT as a Digital Circuit Element, Transistor-Transistor Logic (TTL or T?L) 3. Characteristics of Standard TTL; TTL Families with Improved Performance; Emitter-Coupled Logic (ECL), Timing Circuits (Astable, Bistable, Monostable). Advanced Technology Digital Circuits: BiCMOS Digital Circuits, Overview of Silicon Germanium (SiGe) and Gallium-Arsenid.
Digital Electronics (ELEC512) > Credit Hours : 3

Digital Electronics (ELEC512) > Prerequisites
ELEC370 with a minimum grade D
Digital Electronics (ELEC512) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain Moore’s law and its impact in IC’s design.

Understand nMOSFET & pMOSFET structure and operation in deep submicron technology.

Investigate CMOS inverter & digital logic circuits.

Explore advanced logic circuits.

Analyze semiconductor memories.

ELEC521.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC521 Advanced Control Systems
ELEC521.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC521
Controllability and Observability, State and Output Feedback Controller Design, Observer Design, Linear Quadratic Regulator, Introduction to Robust Control Design, Fundamentals of Nonlinear Control.
Advanced Control Systems (ELEC521) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Control Systems (ELEC521) > Prerequisites
ELEC431 with a minimum grade D
Advanced Control Systems (ELEC521) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply state-space modeling techniques for systems.

Apply signal-flow diagrams techniques for systems.

Analyze open-loop aspects of state-space models including controllability, observability, and canonical forms.

Design full state feedback controllers and full-state observers.

Design controllers using optimal control theory.

Apply the theory of nonlinear systems.

ELEC522.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC522 Industrial Automation
ELEC522.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC522
Graphical symbols in Control Systems, Data acquisition, Implementation of digital PID controllers, Cascade Control, Feedforward control, Smith predictor controller, Programmable Logic Controller (PLC), Ladder diagrams, SCADA systems.
Industrial Automation (ELEC522) > Credit Hours : 3

Industrial Automation (ELEC522) > Prerequisites
ELEC431 with a minimum grade D
Industrial Automation (ELEC522) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe piping and instrumentation diagram.

Design industrial controller using cascade, feedforward, and Smith predictor controllers.

Implement digital controller.

Implement ladder diagram programming for PLCs.

Discuss various topics in industrial automation such as industrial sensors, signal conditioning, etc.

ELEC523.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC523 Intelligent Systems
ELEC523.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC523
This course provides a mathematical framework for various data-driven techniques in soft computing, focusing on intelligent system design for modeling, optimization, and control. It explores the theory and applications of neural network paradigms, fuzzy logic, machine learning, and optimization strategies, emphasizing approaches that rely on data rather than explicit physical models. The course also includes MATLAB simulation examples considering different areas to illustrate key concepts and facilitate understanding
Intelligent Systems (ELEC523) > Credit Hours : 3

Intelligent Systems (ELEC523) > Prerequisites
ELEC431 with a minimum grade D or MECH409 with a minimum grade D
Intelligent Systems (ELEC523) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Understand the general principles of soft computing components

Apply fuzzy logic and artificial neural networks for intelligent modeling.

Employ evolutionary and swarm intelligence algorithms for intelligent optimization

Design of intelligent controllers using fuzzy logic and neural network.

Use MATLAB software for the assessment of intelligent systems

ELEC530.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC530 Special Topics in Power & Control Engineering
ELEC530.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC530
Topics in power and control engineering are chosen by the course instructor at the beginning of the term and approved by the department council.
Special Topics in Power & Control Engineering (ELEC530) > Credit Hours : 3

Special Topics in Power & Control Engineering (ELEC530) > Prerequisites
ELEC431 with a minimum grade D or ELEC472 with a minimum grade D
Special Topics in Power & Control Engineering (ELEC530) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply various theories and methodologies related to selected power and control systems.

Design using selected contemporary techniques for power and control systems.

Communicate the major findings in the topics of power and control systems engineering orally and in writing.

Discuss contemporary topics in the area of power and control systems engineering.

ELEC531.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC531 Power Systems Analysis
ELEC531.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC531
Power Systems in the Real World, Sources of Faults in Power Systems, Symmetrical Components, Sequence Networks, Unsymmetrical Short Circuits, Advanced load flow analysis, Power System Stability, Power System Protection.
Power Systems Analysis (ELEC531) > Credit Hours : 3

Power Systems Analysis (ELEC531) > Prerequisites
ELEC472 with a minimum grade D
Power Systems Analysis (ELEC531) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply Newton Raphson and Fast Decoupled techniques for power flow analysis.

Apply symmetrical component for unbalanced fault analysis.

Perform balanced and unbalanced fault analyses.

Apply equal area criterion method for steady state stability analysis.

Understand principles and requirements for the protection schemes.

ELEC533.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC533 Very Large Scale Integrated Circuits (VLSI)
ELEC533.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC533
Historical perspective and future trend of CMOS technology; Basics of CMOS process; Design methodologies: custom, semicustom, automatic. The focus is on CMOS technology, using custom and standard cell-based design flows. Issues covered at the introductory level include deep sub-micron design, Global design issues: clocking, interconnect, physical design, sub-system design, power, testing as well as CAD tools. The course includes a project component in which students design and layout a small circuit (Chip).
Very Large Scale Integrated Circuits (VLSI) (ELEC533) > Credit Hours : 3

Very Large Scale Integrated Circuits (VLSI) (ELEC533) > Prerequisites
ELEC370 with a minimum grade D
Very Large Scale Integrated Circuits (VLSI) (ELEC533) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the IC design flow.

Demonstrate a thorough knowledge of the ideal and non-ideal I-V characteristics of MOS transistor.

Explore CMOS technology and layout design rules.

Analyze delay, power dissipation in circuits and the impact of technology scaling.

Investigate various CMOS combinational logic and sequential circuit.

Use available software VLSI design tools.

ELEC534.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC534 Power System Distribution
ELEC534.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC534
Generation, Transmission and distribution, Load characteristics, load estimation, Subtransmission lines and distribution substation, Primary systems, Secondary systems, Voltage drop, power loss, Application of capacitor banks, Distribution systems voltage regulation, Distribution System faults, Distribution System protection, Earthing systems, Power quality assessment, system reliability and Distribution automation.
Power System Distribution (ELEC534) > Credit Hours : 3

Power System Distribution (ELEC534) > Prerequisites
ELEC472 with a minimum grade D
Power System Distribution (ELEC534) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify different load demand parameters required for rating main equipment in distribution systems.

Analyze different distribution systems to limit voltage drop under different configurations.

Design proper capacitors bank to enhance system voltage and system losses.
