Apply distribution voltage regulators for controlling customer’s voltage.

Identify the main components required for an overcurrent protection system.

Design an overcurrent protection system for radial feeders.

ELEC551.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC551 Digital Image Processing
ELEC551.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC551
An introduction to basic techniques of analysis and manipulation of pictorial data by computer, image /output devices, Image processing software, Enhancement, Segmentation, Property measurement, Hough transform, Fourier analysis, Computer encoding, processing, and analysis of curves.
Digital Image Processing (ELEC551) > Credit Hours : 3

Digital Image Processing (ELEC551) > Prerequisites
ELEC360 with a minimum grade D

MATH140 with a minimum grade D
Digital Image Processing (ELEC551) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Learn the basics of Image Processing, Computer vision, and Analysis.

Apply image representation, preprocessing and geometry.

Analyze digital images.

Implement various basic image operations like gradient operators, segmentation, etc.

Apply various discrete transforms to images for purpose of edge and line detection, Hough transforms, resolution, filtering, etc.

Demonstrate ability in using imaging software for various image operations, transformations, and analysis.

ELEC561.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC561 Java Programming Applications
ELEC561.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC561
Introduction to Java applications & applets, Control structures, Methods, Arrays, Object-oriented programming, Strings & characters, Files and streams, GUIs, Term project.
Java Programming Applications (ELEC561) > Credit Hours : 3

Java Programming Applications (ELEC561) > Prerequisites
GENG230 with a minimum grade D
Java Programming Applications (ELEC561) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply selection and repetition control structures to execute statements.

Examine object oriented design techniques.

Use arrays to store, sort, search list, and tables of values.

Apply text processing on Characters and String Objects.

Develop a Graphical User Interface (GUI).

ELEC562.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC562 Embedded System Design
ELEC562.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC562
An investigation of current microcomputer structures with emphasis on design of control software, hardware implementation of I/O, analogy to digital (A/D) converter, serial communication, direct memory access, interrupts, interfacing external memory device, and microprogramming.
Embedded System Design (ELEC562) > Credit Hours : 3

Embedded System Design (ELEC562) > Prerequisites
ELEC451 with a minimum grade D
Embedded System Design (ELEC562) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply fundamental embedded system knowledge

Use sensors in a stand-alone system.

Design an Interrupt Handler software for a specific micro-controller.

Design software to control digital I/O interfaced with external hardware.

Design software to handle analog inputs.

Construct an embedded system.

ELEC570.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC570 Special Topics in Computer Engineering
ELEC570.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC570
Topics in computer engineering are chosen by the course instructor at the beginning of the term and approved by the department council.
Special Topics in Computer Engineering (ELEC570) > Credit Hours : 3

Special Topics in Computer Engineering (ELEC570) > Prerequisites
GENG230 with a minimum grade D

ELEC451 with a minimum grade D
Special Topics in Computer Engineering (ELEC570) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Investigate a set of techniques and tools used in the design/analysis of computer components/systems.

Assess appropriate tools for developing computer hardware/software components/systems.

Design a computer component/system that achieves a specific task individually and in a team environment.

ELEC580.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC580 Special Topics in Electronic Engineering
ELEC580.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC580
Topics in electronic engineering are chosen by the course instructor at the beginning of the term and approved by the department council
Special Topics in Electronic Engineering (ELEC580) > Credit Hours : 3

Special Topics in Electronic Engineering (ELEC580) > Prerequisites
ELEC370 with a minimum grade D
Special Topics in Electronic Engineering (ELEC580) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Investigate the state-of-the-art of the selected special topics in electronic Engineering.

Examine the devices, circuits and/or systems, which are relevant to the selected topics

Evaluate the frontier emerging technologies for the selected topics.

ELEC582.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC582 Analog Integrated Circuit Design
ELEC582.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC582
Integrated-circuits devices and modeling. Design of basic analog circuits, such as current sources and mirrors, differential amplifiers. Basic amplifier circuits, CMOS opamps, opamp compensation. Comparators. Noise. Reference circuits.
Analog Integrated Circuit Design (ELEC582) > Credit Hours : 3

Analog Integrated Circuit Design (ELEC582) > Prerequisites
ELEC370 with a minimum grade D
Analog Integrated Circuit Design (ELEC582) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Depict the operation and ability to use the comparators circuits

Describe and illustrate the models for active devices in MOS Based I Technologies

Design and analyze the differential amplifiers & basic operational amplifiers

Design and analyze the single stage amplifiers and C current sources and current mirrors

Explain the operation and employ the bandgap reference in real biasing application

Illustrate the noise sources and models applicable in Opamp Design

ELEC585.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC585 Design and Critical Thinking in Electrical Engineering
ELEC585.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC585
This course concentrates on the rigors of communication, design, and critical thinking in an engineering context including problem identification, feasibility study of alternative solutions, preliminary design, technical writing, teamwork, and formal presentations. A team of students will apply the knowledge gained throughout their study and from industrial training to an engineering design project, emphasizing critical thinking, creativity, and originality. The selected alternatives will be the foundation of the capstone design project. A final report is required.
Design and Critical Thinking in Electrical Engineering (ELEC585) > Credit Hours : 3

Design and Critical Thinking in Electrical Engineering (ELEC585) > Prerequisites
GENG215 with a minimum grade D

GENG315 with a minimum grade D

CHEM270 with a minimum grade D

( ECOM320 with a minimum grade D and ECOM412 with a minimum grade D or ELEC320 with a minimum grade D or ECOM360 with a minimum grade D)

ELEC325 with a minimum grade D

ELEC370 with a minimum grade D

ELEC375 with a minimum grade D

ELEC451 with a minimum grade D

ELEC380 with a minimum grade D

MATH140 with a minimum grade D

ELEC335 with a minimum grade D

ELEC345 with a minimum grade D
Design and Critical Thinking in Electrical Engineering (ELEC585) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the relevant theoretical background of a contemporary engineering problem. [PLO1]

Apply the fundamentals of engineering-design and critical thinking, including the assessment and evaluation of alternative engineering solutions. [PLO2]

Develop and conduct appropriate experimentation, modeling, simulation, and/or data analysis using engineering tools. [PLO6]

Communicate effectively through oral and written presentations. [PLO3]

Outline the principles of engineering ethics, and social and environmental responsibilities. [PLO4]

Recognize the need for ongoing additional knowledge, and the potential of integration and/or application of this knowledge effectively. [PLO7]

Develop leadership skills and project management techniques to independently and/or collaboratively handle complex professional tasks in a team-work context. [PLO5]

ELEC590.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC590 Capstone Engineering Design Project
ELEC590.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC590
This course builds on the outcomes of ELEC 585 course to perform detailed design and cost estimate of the selected alternative solutions to a well-defined engineering problem. Student teams are expected to apply knowledge gained throughout their studies to an engineering design project, emphasizing creativity and originality. A final report is required.
Capstone Engineering Design Project (ELEC590) > Credit Hours : 3

Capstone Engineering Design Project (ELEC590) > Prerequisites
ELEC585 with a minimum grade D
Capstone Engineering Design Project (ELEC590) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the theoretical background of a contemporary engineering problem. [PLO1]

Apply the fundamentals of engineering-design, including the assessment and evaluation of alternative engineering solutions. [PLO2]

Develop and conduct appropriate experimentation, modelling, simulation, and/or data analysis using modern engineering tools. [PLO6]

Communicate effectively through oral and written presentations. [PLO3]

Recognize the principles of engineering ethics, and social and environmental responsibilities. [PLO4]

Recognize the need for ongoing additional knowledge, and the potential of integration and/or application of this knowledge effectively. [PLO7]

Develop leadership skills and project management techniques to independently and/or collaboratively handle complex professional tasks in a team-work context. [PLO5]

ELEC592.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC592 Power Electronics
ELEC592.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC592
The Thyristor, AC and DC diode circuits, Thyristor commutation techniques, Single and three-phase converters, Controlled rectifiers, different static switches, AC voltage controllers, inverters and cycloconverters, DC Choppers. Thyristor data sheets, Protection of diodes and circuits.
Power Electronics (ELEC592) > Credit Hours : 3

Power Electronics (ELEC592) > Prerequisites
ELEC320 with a minimum grade D

ELEC370 with a minimum grade D
Power Electronics (ELEC592) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Understand power electronics, power semiconductor switches characteristics, switch selection, data sheet, and diode circuits.

Analyze uncontrolled single phase and three-phase rectifiers.

Analyze controlled single phase and three-phase rectifiers.

Examine the operation of DC-DC converters, including buck converter, boost converter, buck-boost converter, and Cuk converter.

Investigate the operation of single phase and three phase inverters

ELEC600.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC600 Numerical Methods in Engineering
ELEC600.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC600
This course focuses on numerical methods for the analysis and design of engineering processes and systems. The course will include approximation and interpolation, root-finding, solution of linear and nonlinear equations, curve fitting, numerical differentiation and integration, numerical optimization, solution of ordinary and partial differential equations, finite difference and introduction to finite element techniques.
Numerical Methods in Engineering (ELEC600) > Credit Hours : 3

Numerical Methods in Engineering (ELEC600) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the difference between analytical and numerical olutions

Compute roots of linear and non-linear equations

Examine stable and accurate numerical methods to solve linear systems of equations

Solve basic linear and nonlinear optimization problems related to engineering

Apply numerical integration and differentiation

Evaluate stable methods to solve ordinary and partial differential equations

ELEC602.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC602 Linear Systems
ELEC602.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC602
Mathematical description of systems, fundamental of matrix algebra and quadratic forms, state space solution and realization of linear systems, stability of linear and nonlinear systems, controllability and observability, minimal realization and coprime fractions state feedback and state estimators.
Linear Systems (ELEC602) > Credit Hours : 3

Linear Systems (ELEC602) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze aspects of linear time-invariant systems including controllability, observability, canonical forms and stability.

Construct dynamical systems using linear time-invariant state space realizations and transfer functions.

Demonstrate knowledge of fundamental concepts in linear algebra, systems analysis and matrix theory.

Design state feedback.

Design state observers for state estimation.

ELEC604.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC604 Advanced Digital Signal Processing
ELEC604.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC604
Review important concepts in digital signal processing and introduce a number of advanced topics and applications in one-dimensional digital signal processing. Review the basic discrete time transforms including discrete time Fourier transform (DTFT), discrete Fourier transform (DFT), and Z-transform. Introduce selected topics from IIR and FIR filter design, short-time Fourier analysis, modern spectral estimation, linear prediction, adaptive filtering, and array processing. Applications from speech / music analysis and synthesis would also be included.
Advanced Digital Signal Processing (ELEC604) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Digital Signal Processing (ELEC604) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Solve difference equations representing a linear time-invariant Discrete-Time System

Analyze LTI systems in the frequency domain.

Apply the Z-Transform and its application to the analysis of Linear Time Invariant Systems.

Determine the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) of signals and its properties and applications.

Implement Discrete-Time Systems.

Design FIR and IIR Digital Filters.

ELEC612.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC612 Communications Networks
ELEC612.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC612
Fundamental concepts of communication networks, architecture for access and internetworking, packet switching; protocols and throughput optimization, routing; error and flow control, TCP/IP and other internet protocols, topological design algorithms, queuing theory and its applications, multiple access schemes.
Communications Networks (ELEC612) > Credit Hours : 3

Communications Networks (ELEC612) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recall the basic principles of computer networking, the operation of the TCP/IP protocol and local area networks.

Analyze packet switching throughput and delay performance using queuing models.

Outline the operation of different routing and internetworking techniques in packet switching networks such as link state routing and distance vector routing.

Identify and compare between Internet routing protocols such as routing information protocol (RIP), open shortest path first (OSPF) and border gateway protocol (BGP).

Describe and analyze the different congestion control techniques at the network layer level.

Describe the research outcomes and the technical analysis of a research paper and make a technical presentation about it.

ELEC613.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC613 Advanced Wireless Communications
ELEC613.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC613
Evolution of radio communications and broadcast systems, new trends, economics of radio communications, spectrum usage; Cellular concept, coverage, frequency reuse, interference; Broadcast concepts; Radio propagation; Large scale path loss, small scale fading and multi-path; Wireless modulation techniques; Multiple access techniques; Networking and planning; Case studies.
Advanced Wireless Communications (ELEC613) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Wireless Communications (ELEC613) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Understand the new trends in wireless communication.

Describe the characteristics of wireless communication channels.

Apply the basics of traffic and queuing theory.

Design a cellular communication system using frequency reuse, cell splitting, sectoring, and capacity and coverage enhancement techniques.

Analyze the performance of digital wireless systems in terms of BER and outage probability.

Apply performance enhancement techniques such as diversity, equalization, coding, interleaving, and data link control techniques.

Work out a complete research-based project related to wireless communications.

ELEC615.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC615 Adaptive Signal Processing
ELEC615.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC615
Basic concepts and applications of adaptive signal processing; adaptive filters, beam-formers, optimum space/time processors and their adaptive implementation, adaptive algorithms.
Adaptive Signal Processing (ELEC615) > Credit Hours : 3

Adaptive Signal Processing (ELEC615) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Use basic probability theory to model random signals in terms of Random Processes.

Derive the Wiener filter for signals with known second order statistics.

Formulate the Wiener filter as a constrained optimization problem.

Solve the Wiener filter weights for the prediction filter using the Levinson-Durbin algorithm

Use the LMS algorithm and its variants for iteratively estimating the Wiener filter weights.

Determine suitable LMS step size to trade off convergence time and misadjustment.

Implement the RLS algorithm for iteratively estimating the Wiener filter weights.

ELEC617.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC617 Antenna Design & Applications
ELEC617.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC617
Review of antennas basic theory: radiation pattern antenna impedance, gain, directivity, bandwidth, beam width, and frequency dependence. Advanced level treatment of antenna design and analysis. Analysis and synthesis of phased arrays. Reflector antennas. Micro strip antennas. Single and dual reflector systems. New concepts of primary radiator design. Primary feeds for monopulse radar. Antennas for navigation aids. Adaptive phased arrays and their application to radar.
Antenna Design & Applications (ELEC617) > Credit Hours : 3

Antenna Design & Applications (ELEC617) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify And Define Important Antenna Parameters Such As Antenna Impedance, Directivity, Efficiency, Gain.

Determine Analytical Expression Of The Far-Zone Radiated Electric Field And Antenna State Of Polarization. Evaluate The Antenna Receiving Characteristics.

Describe and calculate the radiation properties of arbitrarily oriented wire antennas in the presence of a perfectly conducting ground plane.

Determine the analytical expression of the array factor for linear array antennas and Evaluate radiation properties.

Design array factor for 2-D arrays rectangular and circular, and compute radiation properties.

Explain the operational principles and use of a Yagi-Uda array antenna, and compute its radiation properties using available software.

Contemporary issues of antennas in modern mobile communication: Smart antenna system and MIMO antenna; definition and design, Beam scanning and directive antenna systems.

ELEC619.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC619 Advanced Topics in Communication Engineering
ELEC619.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC619
The course aims at developing students’ abilities and enriching their background in order to effectively conduct research in very specialized topics in communication engineering. The course topics are to be selected by the course instructor.
Advanced Topics in Communication Engineering (ELEC619) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Topics in Communication Engineering (ELEC619) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain how network capacity planning is performed for distributed and infrastructure-based wireless networks.

Apply traffic engineering basics for distributed and infrastructure-based wireless networks.

Apply the analytical fundamentals of radio resource management and mobility management in wireless networks

Explain the different medium access control techniques that are used in wireless networks.

5.Identify the main design issues of ad hoc networks from medium access control (MAC) and routing layers’ perspective.

6.Describe the architecture and the operation of 2G/3G/4G cellular networks including high speed data link packet access

Describe the research outcomes and the technical analysis of a research paper and make a technical presentation about it.

ELEC620.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC620 Analytical Techniques in Engineering
ELEC620.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC620
Ordinary differential equations: first-order and second-order ordinary differential equations, initial-value and boundary-value problems, Green’s function, systems of differential equations, power series method and Frobenius method, special functions, orthogonal functions and Strum-Liouville problems. Partial differential equations: the diffusion (heat) equation, the wave equation, Laplace equation, nonhomogeneous partial differential equations, and partial differential equations in curvilinear coordinates. Complex analysis: complex numbers, complex functions, complex differentiation and integration, series representations of complex functions, residue integration, and application of residue integration in evaluating real integrals.
Analytical Techniques in Engineering (ELEC620) > Credit Hours : 3

Analytical Techniques in Engineering (ELEC620) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze complex system using complex integration and differentiation

Determine stable point and phase plane analysis for systems of differential Equations

Develop solution of Sturm Loiuvel system using mathematical Fourier Series solution

Develop solutions to special differential equations: Bessel’s Equation and Bessel Functions, Legendre’s Equation, Orthogonality of Legendre Polynomials

Solve partial differential equations; separation of variables, heat equation, wave Equation

Solve 1st & 2nd order ordinary differential equations

ELEC622.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC622 Power Systems Protection
ELEC622.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC622
Review of power system symmetrical components & fault analysis, protective device operating principles, instrument transformers, over current protection, distance and pilot protection, equipment protection: machines, transformers, buses, protection aspects of power system phenomena.
Power Systems Protection (ELEC622) > Credit Hours : 3

Power Systems Protection (ELEC622) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze short-circuit current using symmetrical components

Apply the basic principles of electrical systems and requirements for the protection schemes

Evaluate various components of the protection systems and their duties

Perform relay coordination for overcurrent protection relays

Analyze distance and unit protection systems for the power systems Equipment.

ELEC625.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC625 Power Systems Quality
ELEC625.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC625
Power quality disturbances, power quality standards, CBEMA and ITIC curves, power quality indices, power interruption, faults as a sources of sags and swells, motor starting sags, mitigation of sag and swell disturbances, waveform distortion, voltage fluctuation, power frequency variation, harmonic sources, power system responses to harmonics, resonance, harmonic analysis methods, harmonic mitigation, transients, capacitor-switching transients, interaction of capacitor banks, circuit analysis of cap-switching transients, mitigation of transients, power quality monitoring, detection classification and measurement, power quality and deregulation. Solving power quality problems, power conditioning devices, static circuit breaker, static shunt and series compensator, passive and active harmonic filters.
Power Systems Quality (ELEC625) > Credit Hours : 3

Power Systems Quality (ELEC625) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe and understand the concept of power quality disturbances on the power system and power quality standards.

Perform an analysis of short-duration power quality problems and their impact on power system equipment.

Perform an analysis of harmonics problems and apply suitable mitigation techniques

Evaluate the practical power quality data and propose solutions to the problems.

Design an experiment through measurement/monitoring using the power quality analyzer.

ELEC629.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC629 Advanced Topics in Power Engineering
ELEC629.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC629
This course deals with advanced power / power electronics topics as per instructor area of expertise.
Advanced Topics in Power Engineering (ELEC629) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Topics in Power Engineering (ELEC629) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Design ideal stand-alone and grid-connected photovoltaic systems.

Design ideal stand-alone and grid-connected wind systems.

Develop analytical techniques for analyzing the steady-state and dynamic characteristics of PV inverters.

Evaluate the power quality issues of RE resources integration and apply mitigation techniques.

Plan DG resources in power distribution systems considering sizing and placement.

ELEC637.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC637 Sensors Design and Applications
ELEC637.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC637
Design, analysis and application of sensors used to measure physical quantities such as flow, level, temperature, pressure and density.
Sensors Design and Applications (ELEC637) > Credit Hours : 3

Sensors Design and Applications (ELEC637) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analysis different electronics interface circuits for sensor applications.

Explore the use of piezoelectric materials for sensor design and applications.

Explore the use of resistive, inductive and capacitive concepts in sensor design.

Explore the use of sensors to measure physical quantities such as displacement, flow, level, temperature, pressure and density.

Investigate the fabrication technologies for sensor fabrications.

ELEC639.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC639 Advanced Topics in Electrical Engineering
ELEC639.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC639
This course focuses on the in-depth study of a selected advanced or emerging topic in electrical engineering, with an emphasis on integrating knowledge across multiple subfields. It addresses the analysis, design, and evaluation of complex engineering systems using state-of-the-art methods, including modeling, simulation, and optimization. The specific topic varies based on current research trends, allowing students to engage with cutting-edge developments while applying multidisciplinary approaches to solve open-ended problems. The course also promotes critical thinking, innovation, and practical problem-solving skills.
Advanced Topics in Electrical Engineering (ELEC639) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Topics in Electrical Engineering (ELEC639) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze highly complex electrical engineering problems using advanced theoretical and multidisciplinary approaches.

Design innovative solutions for complex engineering systems using appropriate methodologies and tools.

Evaluate the functioning of advanced engineering systems using various types of analysis techniques.

Conduct practical research to solve difficult problems in electrical engineering.

Communicate complex ideas about engineering systems professionally and clearly.

ELEC641.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC641 Contemporary Digital Systems
ELEC641.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC641
Introduction to combinational & sequential logic, finite state machines, high performance digital systems: theory and application of modern design, alternative implementation forms and introduction to HDL, sequential logic technologies.
Contemporary Digital Systems (ELEC641) > Credit Hours : 3

Contemporary Digital Systems (ELEC641) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate the use of 5/6 variable k-maps and quine McKusick method for function minimization, and function implementation by using nand/nor logic

Design counters, counter design procedures, reversed-engineered counters, and cascaded counters to build finite state machines

Develop alternative implementations and incomplete specified functions of combinational logic systems, and function minimization by using hypercube

Formulate logic techniques for multiplexers, decoders, Rom, Pla, & Pal

Introduction to a Hdl (Verilog) programming language with logical simulation

Mastery of logic elements, state diagrams, state tables, flip-flops, master-slave flip-flops, and registers

ELEC644.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC644 Artificial Neural Networks
ELEC644.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC644
Overview of neuro-engineering technology, basic neural network architectures, single layer perception classifiers and multi-layer feed forward networks, single-layer feedback networks, and associative memories, Kohonen models and counter propagation networks, adaptive resonance theory and Boltzmann machines, Simulated annealing, temporal modeling, supervised and unsupervised learning, Implementation, basic applications to pattern recognition.
Artificial Neural Networks (ELEC644) > Credit Hours : 3

Artificial Neural Networks (ELEC644) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Interpret basis of neuron and brain model

Classify different neural network architectures

Demonstrate supervised learning; Perceptron and its relation to Bayes Classifier

Investigate Hebbian-based learning and apply principles of Self-Organization

Analyze Self-organized maps and Kohonen Networks

Examine recurrent networks and support vector machines concept

ELEC646.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC646 Computational Vision
ELEC646.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC646
The fundamentals of computer vision and techniques for image understanding and high-level image processing. Includes computational techniques, image segmentation, geometric structures, relational structures, inference, matching, stereo vision, sequence of images, shape, color and texture, three dimensional scene analysis, vision systems, and applications.
Computational Vision (ELEC646) > Credit Hours : 3

Computational Vision (ELEC646) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Learn human eye and basics of computer imaging

Understand image geometry and different image transformation techniques

Demonstrate understanding of image enhancement and restoration techniques

Investigate image segmentation techniques and morphological operations

Analyze image transforms

Investigate lossless and lossy image compression

ELEC649.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC649 Advanced Topics in Computer Engineering
ELEC649.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC649
Topics to be chosen every year according to specific interests.
Advanced Topics in Computer Engineering (ELEC649) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Topics in Computer Engineering (ELEC649) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze operating system architecture, system calls, process concept, interprocess communication, and threads concept.

Build various CPU-scheduling algorithms and solutions for process synchronization including critical section and semaphores.

Compose various ways of organizing memory hardware and memory management techniques including paging and segmentation.

Develop the concept of virtual memory, demand paging, page-replacement algorithms, and allocation of page frames.

Determine details of layered file system structure, file allocation methods, and free space management.

Analyze physical structure of mass storage systems including the secondary and tertiary storage devices.

ELEC652.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC652 Nonlinear Control
ELEC652.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC652
Analysis of nonlinear control systems; Lyapunov stability, numerical methods, phase-plane techniques, describing functions, and linearization via feedback.
Nonlinear Control (ELEC652) > Credit Hours : 3

Nonlinear Control (ELEC652) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate knowledge of fundamental mathematics for nonlinear systems

Design nonlinear observers

Design using backstepping method

Design using feedback linearization method

Evaluate stability of autonmous Systems

Evaluate stability of non autonomous systems

ELEC656.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC656 Optimal Control
ELEC656.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC656
Optimal control by dynamic programming. Pontryagins maximum principle, and variational methods; minimum time, energy, and fuel problems for linear continuous and discrete systems.
Optimal Control (ELEC656) > Credit Hours : 3

Optimal Control (ELEC656) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate knowledge of fundamental concepts in optimization and calculus of variation.

Design using linear quadratic gaussian.

Design using quadratic regulator.

Solve control problems using model predictive control.

ELEC659.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC659 Advanced Topics in Control Systems
ELEC659.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC659
Topics are to be chosen every year according to specific interests.
Advanced Topics in Control Systems (ELEC659) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Topics in Control Systems (ELEC659) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze and design using conventional PID control techniques.

Analyze and design using fuzzy Logic control techniques.

Analyze and design using robust control techniques.

Analyze and design using nonlinear control techniques.

Analyze and design using optimal control techniques.

Model systems using system identification techniques.

ELEC665.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC665 Embedded AI and Edge Computing
ELEC665.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC665
This course focuses on the deployment and optimization of Artificial Intelligence models on embedded and edge platforms operating under power, memory, and latency constraints. It addresses the architectural and computational challenges of executing AI workloads on resource-limited systems. Topics include model compression techniques (quantization and pruning), TinyML, neural accelerator architectures, hardware–software co-design, memory hierarchy optimization, energy-aware inference, and secure embedded AI deployment. The course emphasizes mapping neural network models onto specific hardware platforms and optimizing performance in terms of energy efficiency and real-time execution. By the end of the course, students will be able to analyze, optimize, and deploy AI models on embedded systems while balancing computational performance, energy consumption, and reliability requirements.
Embedded AI and Edge Computing (ELEC665) > Credit Hours : 3

Embedded AI and Edge Computing (ELEC665) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the architecture and constraints (power, memory, latency) of embedded and edge AI systems.

Analyze hardware–software trade-offs for AI workloads in edge computing environments.

Implement optimized AI models on embedded hardware using compression techniques and deployment tools (e.g., TensorFlow Lite Micro, Edge Impulse, uTensor)

Evaluate performance metrics such as latency, energy consumption, and computational efficiency in embedded AI systems.

Present technical solutions for embedded AI deployment effectively through written reports and presentations.

ELEC667.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC667 AI for Cyber-Physical and Engineering Systems
ELEC667.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC667
This course examines the integration of Artificial Intelligence into cyber-physical and engineering systems where computation interacts with physical processes through sensing, communication, and control. It focuses on applying AI techniques to dynamic systems governed by differential equations and operating under stability, reliability, and safety constraints. Topics include system modeling and identification, reinforcement learning for control, physics-informed neural networks, predictive maintenance, and the development of AI-enabled digital twins for real-time monitoring and optimization of cyber-physical systems. By the end of the course, students will be able to design and evaluate AI-based controllers and monitoring systems that maintain stability, efficiency, and resilience in complex engineering infrastructures.
AI for Cyber-Physical and Engineering Systems (ELEC667) > Credit Hours : 3

AI for Cyber-Physical and Engineering Systems (ELEC667) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze the architecture and operational principles of cyber-physical systems and the role of artificial intelligence in their monitoring and control

Analyze dynamic engineering systems using system identification and AI-based modeling techniques

Design AI-enabled control and monitoring systems using techniques such as reinforcement learning and physics-informed neural networks

Evaluate the performance, safety, and reliability of AI-enabled cyber-physical systems in real-world engineering applications

5.Present technical findings and system designs effectively in written and oral formats

ELEC691.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC691 Graduate Seminar I
ELEC691.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC691
Thesis option students should present a research proposal in front of a panel appointed by the EE Graduate Studies committee. Research projects are discussed to decide on the Master's Thesis.
Graduate Seminar I (ELEC691) > Credit Hours : 0

Graduate Seminar I (ELEC691) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify potential research topic in Electrical Engineering.

Apply research skills formulations to address selected research topic.

Develop a technical proposal for selected research topic.

Present a research proposal at a high level of proficiency.

ELEC693.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC693 Master's Research Thesis
ELEC693.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC693
Supervision of research work is made towards the completion of M.Sc. requirements for Thesis option students.
Master's Research Thesis (ELEC693) > Credit Hours : 9

Master's Research Thesis (ELEC693) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrates good knowledge of methodology and gives a justification for methods used.

Discusses the implications of findings from the study and describes its impact on future research as well as its limitations.

Expresses ideas clearly and logically with a good writing style that is easy to follow and understand.

Identifies relevant research and literature and provides a summary and appropriate citation of major work in the field.

Includes a definition and articulation of the research question with a justification for the current research.

Presents and interprets results in light of the research question and includes explanations for tables and graphs.

Presents evidence that the research has resulted in the advancement of new knowledge in the research field.

ELEC694.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC694 Research / Design Paper
ELEC694.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC694
Supervision of research/design paper is made towards the completion of M.Sc requirements for Non-Thesis option students.
Research / Design Paper (ELEC694) > Credit Hours : 3

Research / Design Paper (ELEC694) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrates good knowledge of methodology and gives a justification for methods used.

Discusses the implications of findings from the study and describes its impact on future research as well as its limitations.

Expresses ideas clearly and logically with a good writing style that is easy to follow and understand.

Identifies relevant research and literature and provides a summary and appropriate citation of major work in the field.

Includes a definition and articulation of the research question with a justification for the current research.

Presents and interprets results in light of the research question and includes explanations for tables and graphs.

Presents evidence that the research has resulted in the advancement of new knowledge in the research field.

ELEC695.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC695 Technical project
ELEC695.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC695
This course involves independent work on a design, simulation, modeling, or lab-based technical project. All projects must be supervised by a faculty member and the student is responsible for finding his/her supervisor. Project topics may be faculty-initiated, student-initiated, or suggested by industrial contacts. The student is expected to submit a brief description of a work plan by the end of the second week of the semester. The student is also required to submit a comprehensive final report and give an oral presentation during the last week of lectures of the semester.
Technical project (ELEC695) > Credit Hours : 6

Technical project (ELEC695) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop a work plan for a technical project in the field of Electrical Engineering.

Apply advanced research and/or design skills to a specific problem related to the Electrical Engineering area.

Report findings in a well written technical report.

Present results at a high level of proficiency.

ELEC709.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC709 Machine Learning in Engineering
ELEC709.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC709
This course provides a comprehensive introduction to machine learning. The course covers learning theory, supervised learning, unsupervised learning, ensemble and graphical models, generative and reinforcement learning, and various learning networks like convolutional networks and recurrent networks.
Machine Learning in Engineering (ELEC709) > Credit Hours : 3

Machine Learning in Engineering (ELEC709) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Interpret machine learning concept as applied to engineering

Demonstrate supervised learning, unsupervised learning and algorithms

Analyze linear, tree-based, ensemble and graphical models

Investigate Generative and reinforcement learning

Examine different machine learning structures and algorithms

ELEC711.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC711 Micro and Nano Systems
ELEC711.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC711
The objectives of this course are to provide a deep insight of the materials used in the fabrication of micro and nano based electronic devices and sensors. Advancement in integration and packaging processes and techniques to be covered. The course also presents the applications of micro and nanosystems. Multiphysics tools will be utilized for simulations and modelling. Also, this course should address the fundamental and frontier of modern nanoelectronics
Micro and Nano Systems (ELEC711) > Credit Hours : 3

Micro and Nano Systems (ELEC711) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Investigate the materials used in the fabrication of micro and nano-based systems

Make qualified choices for suitable fabrication process for sensors and electronic devices

Evaluate the integration, packaging processes and techniques

Explore the applications of micro and nano systems

Utilize multiphysics design tools and commercial modeling programs for micro and nano systems simulations and modeling

Assess and update the fundamentals and frontiers of modern nanoelectronics

ELEC712.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC712 Advanced Circuits and Systems
ELEC712.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC712
The course is intended to cover the current technology and interest in Circuits and Systems. The topics include energy harvesting, biomedical, RF and biotechnology. It also cover the circuit/system characterizations and modeling along with testing and reliability measurements. It also involves the utilization of signal processing for circuits and systems
Advanced Circuits and Systems (ELEC712) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Circuits and Systems (ELEC712) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Acquire the current technology for circuits and systems

Assimilate the possible applications in different areas: energy harvesting, biomedical, RF, and biotechnology

Analyze and assess the characterization, modeling and reliability measurements of circuits and systems

Utilize signal processing for circuits and systems

ELEC731.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC731 Power System Planning
ELEC731.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC731
Economic dispatch, unit commitment, dynamic programming, power system planning and operation, control, generation modeling, AGC, and power protection
Power System Planning (ELEC731) > Credit Hours : 3

Power System Planning (ELEC731) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate deep understanding on power system planning principles

Apply economic principles in power dispatch and unit commitment

Analyze historical data and apply load forecasting methodologies in generation expansion planning

Formulate, and solve constraint generation, substation, network expansion and reactive power planning problems

Illustrate configurations of power system protection schemes and generation control methods.

ELEC733.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC733 Multivariable Feedback Control
ELEC733.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC733
Introduction to multivariable control; limitation on performance in multi-input-multi-output (MIMO) systems; robust stability and performance analysis for MIMO systems; controller design and structure for MIMO systems; model reduction; linear matrix inequalities (LMI)
Multivariable Feedback Control (ELEC733) > Credit Hours : 3

Multivariable Feedback Control (ELEC733) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the fundamentals of MIMO systems and its performance limitations

Analyze robust stability and performance for MIMO Systems

Design controller for MIMO systems

Apply model reduction techniques for MIMO systems

Design controller using LMI techniques

ELEC735.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC735 Advanced Topics in Electrical Eng I
ELEC735.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC735
To be designed to the specific interest of the exiting PhD students with emphasis on new frontiers in Electrical Engineering
Advanced Topics in Electrical Eng I (ELEC735) > Credit Hours : 3

ELEC742.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC742 Detection and Estimation Theory
ELEC742.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC742
Random processes; detection and estimation theory, with applications to communication systems and statistical signal processing; decision-theory concepts and optimum-receiver principles; parameter estimation; linear and nonlinear estimation; Application in spectral estimation, filtering, and array signal processing
Detection and Estimation Theory (ELEC742) > Credit Hours : 3

Detection and Estimation Theory (ELEC742) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Construct a hypothesis testing problem; specify the probability distributions of the observations under each hypothesis; formulate optimal decision rules according to various criteria

Apply the Bayesian, minimax or Neyman-Pearson approaches to design optimal decision rules; assess the Bayes risk, detection probability, and false-alarm probability

Apply detection theory for signal detection in discrete time; design optimal receiver structures

Construct a parameter estimation problem; specify the likelihood function; formulate optimal estimators according to various criteria

Design Bayesian estimator in presence of prior information; design minimum variance unbiased estimator or maximum likelihood estimation in absence of prior information

Apply detection theory and estimation algorithms learned to real-world application examples

ELEC743.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC743 Information Transmission Systems
ELEC743.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC743
Random processes and mathematical models of communication; Modulation schemes and principles; Multicarrier and multiples access systems; Transmission over fading channels; Multiple antenna and multiple users systems; Principles of Communication network modeling , Modeling error control, flow control and medium access control protocols
Information Transmission Systems (ELEC743) > Credit Hours : 3

Information Transmission Systems (ELEC743) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Model random processes and signals that characterize the operation of different communication systems

Compare between the current state-of-the-art modulation schemes

Analyze the performance of multiple carrier and multiple access systems

Formulate the outcome of signal transmission over fading channel

Construct multiple and smart antenna systems

Analyze the performance of flow control, error control, and medium access control protocols currently used in communication networks

ELEC850.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC850 Candidacy Exam
ELEC850.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC850
The Candidacy Exam for the PhD in electrical engineering is a non-credit Pass/Fail exam. Students have up to two trials to pass the course; upon passing the exam, the student becomes a PhD candidate. The course is structured to evaluate the student’s breadth and depth of fundamental knowledge in the area(s) closely related to the thesis work. The course committee, in consultation with the advisor, decides on the topic(s) of the course. The PhD student prepares a concise and comprehensive research proposal that clearly defines the research problem and objectives and outlines the research methodology that he/she plans to follow. The concerned PhD student should present and defend his/her proposal in front of the course committee.
Candidacy Exam (ELEC850) > Credit Hours : 0

Candidacy Exam (ELEC850) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the depth and breadth of their knowledge in the electrical engineering discipline.

Prepare a well-structured research proposal, including objectives, plans and methods.

Demonstrate sufficient communication skills relevant to electrical engineering.

ELEC900.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC900 Dissertation Doctoral Research
ELEC900.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC900
Open to students who have successfully completed the comprehensive exam. PhD student conducts original research under the direction of a supervisory committee. Credits are determined in consultation with the dissertation supervisor.
Dissertation Doctoral Research (ELEC900) > Credit Hours : 30

Dissertation Doctoral Research (ELEC900) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify gaps in the current state of knowledge and outline directions to produce new knowledge at the frontier of the electrical engineering discipline.

Apply advanced theories and research methodologies to critically analyze open research problems in electrical engineering and develop innovative solutions.

Produce and defend an original research work that advances the state of the art in the electrical engineering discipline.

Communicate research findings, orally and in writing, at a high level of proficiency to faculty, peers, and the lay public.

Evaluate and manage complex professional engineering activities and diverse ethical issues within the work context.

ELEC901.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC901 Dissertation Doctoral Research
ELEC901.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC901
This course provides students with the opportunity to conduct and complete original doctoral research leading to a dissertation. Under the guidance of their supervisor and Advisory Committee, students develop advanced research, critical analysis, problem-solving, and scholarly communication skills while addressing significant research problems in electrical engineering. Regular meetings and annual progress reviews support the achievement of research milestones. Students apply advanced research methodologies to generate original knowledge, disseminate research findings, and prepare a dissertation of publishable quality. The dissertation must comply with the College of Graduate Studies’ Thesis and Dissertation Preparation Guidelines.
Dissertation Doctoral Research (ELEC901) > Credit Hours : 42

Dissertation Doctoral Research (ELEC901) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify gaps in the current state of knowledge that can lead to the generation of new knowledge at the frontier of the electrical engineering discipline

Analyze open research problems in electrical engineering and develop innovative solutions

Develop original research work advances state of the art in the electrical engineering discipline

Communicate research findings, orally and in writing, at a high level of proficiency to faculty, peers, and the lay public

Evaluate complex professional engineering activities and diverse ethical issues within the work context

ELEC910.title: UAEU Catalog — ELEC910 Dissertation Defense
ELEC910.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2912.shtml?id=ELEC910
Two part exam, open and close, to defend the results of PhD research work
Dissertation Defense (ELEC910) > Credit Hours : 0

Dissertation Defense (ELEC910) > Prerequisites
ELEC850
Dissertation Defense (ELEC910) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Assess primary literature and explain areas of active research in the chosen field

Discuss research design, including results, recommendations, and conclusions

Communicate research outcomes logically and persuasively both in writing and orally

Evaluate the study results in line with the research design, including ethical and professional considerations

GENG215.title: UAEU Catalog — GENG215 Engineering Ethics
GENG215.text:
This course introduces students to Engineering Ethics, as a set of moral principles that relate to Engineering projects and designs. The course explores creative ways of reconciling conflicting moral claims. It outlines the responsibilities of Engineers towards public safety and the environment, within economic constraints and governing laws. A systematic Engineering Design process is introduced. Each design stage explores relevant methods and their ethical implications. The course critically examines litigations that involve the engineering profession in relation to product liability.
Engineering Ethics (GENG215) > Credit Hours : 2

Engineering Ethics (GENG215) > Prerequisites
GEAE101 with a minimum grade D
Engineering Ethics (GENG215) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify ethical and professional issues pertaining to personal integrity, and professional conduct pertaining to the society and the environment.

Recognize an engineering ethical dilemma and apply a systematic process of moral and ethical reasoning to resolve it.

Analyze several moral theories and principles (e.g., utilitarianism, duty ethics, virtue ethics, and religious ethics) and apply them to the examination of ethical issues in engineering.

Analyze case studies of conflict in Engineering and make choices based on engineering ethics codes and apply one to the resolution of an ethical dilemma.

Identify the value of teamwork and multi-discipline work in relation to types and scales of projects, through assignments and group projects.

Apply the design process using systematic design methods, and identify the related professional responsibilities and ethical issues.

GENG220.title: UAEU Catalog — GENG220 Engineering Thermodynamics
GENG220.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2914.shtml?id=GENG220
Thermo-physical properties of pure substances and gases. 1st law of thermodynamics, conservation of energy, and closed and open systems. Limitations and efficiencies of energy conversion processes. Introduction to the 2nd law of thermodynamics and entropy. Applications in Engineering.
Engineering Thermodynamics (GENG220) > Credit Hours : 3

Engineering Thermodynamics (GENG220) > Prerequisites
PHYS105 with a minimum grade D

Pre/Co PHYS135 with a minimum grade D
Engineering Thermodynamics (GENG220) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the basic concepts of macroscopic thermodynamics

Explain the properties of pure substances

Explain the heat transfer and work interaction between a system and its surroundings

Apply the first law of thermodynamics for closed and open systems

Explain and apply the Second law concepts

Analyze thermodynamic processes and cycles within the conceptual frameworks of the First and Second laws

Use the “Engineering Equation Solver (EES)” learning tool to solve thermodynamics problems

GENG230.title: UAEU Catalog — GENG230 Computer Programming
GENG230.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2914.shtml?id=GENG230
Introduction to computing, data types and variables, expressions, selection and repetition control structures, library and user-defined functions, files and streams, arrays, library and user-defined classes, and Artificial Intelligence applications.
Computer Programming (GENG230) > Credit Hours : 3

Computer Programming (GENG230) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Use variables to store, retrieve and calculate information

Write programs by using decision structures, Boolean logic, and repetition structures.

Construct programs modularly by using functions.

Use lists to store, search, and sort elements of an array.

Save and retrieve information from files with exceptions.

Apply object-oriented programming to describe classes, instances, and inheritance.

Apply programming tools to solve one of the Artificial Intelligence related problems in different engineering disciplines.

GENG315.title: UAEU Catalog — GENG315 Engineering Economics
GENG315.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2914.shtml?id=GENG315
Introduction to the basic concepts and principles of engineering economics. Familiarization of the different cost components, cost estimation techniques, cash flow analysis, time value of money, and measures of project performance. Comparing alternatives. Application of engineering practice and entrepreneurship to engineering design and projects.
Engineering Economics (GENG315) > Credit Hours : 3

Engineering Economics (GENG315) > Prerequisites
MATH110 with a minimum grade D
Engineering Economics (GENG315) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the principles of engineering economy and the engineering economic analysis procedure

Describe some of the basic cost terminology and concepts used in engineering practice

Explain the concept of price-demand relationship

Describe the different techniques used for cost estimation

Explain the concept of the time value of money

Evaluate a single project and select among alternative project options

Explain the concepts of entrepreneurship and discuss different elements of a business plan

GENG701.title: UAEU Catalog — GENG701 PhD Research Seminar
GENG701.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2914.shtml?id=GENG701
This course offers the students the opportunity to integrate their knowledge, skills, and practical experience with their peers and the course instructor. The course will contribute to the student’s professional development focusing on skills and professional experience. It consists of presentations on current research or applied projects in engineering, informatics, or related fields. The presentations are delivered by the course instructor, registered PhD students, faculty members, or invited speakers.
PhD Research Seminar (GENG701) > Credit Hours : 1

PhD Research Seminar (GENG701) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Prepare and deliver effective presentations describing a recent advancement in engineering, informatics, or related fields.

Explain knowledge to others through effective presentations and discussions.

Critique presentations of their peers objectively.

GENG702.title: UAEU Catalog — GENG702 Research Methods
GENG702.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2914.shtml?id=GENG702
This course provides students with a comprehensive understanding of research methodologies. It will cover the fundamental concepts of theory and scientific research, literature search and referencing, design and analysis of experiments, problem identification and formulation, research design including experimentation, measurements and sampling, data analysis, and paper and thesis organization. The course also includes proposal presentation, ethical issues in research and the importance of time management and multi-disciplinary research.
Research Methods (GENG702) > Credit Hours : 2

Research Methods (GENG702) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify relevant literature and produce reports using standard referencing methods.

Identify research problems and develop appropriate research design.

Design and carry out experimentation, sampling and measurement procedures to collect data.

Evaluate and choose research methodologies applicable to problems in a specific field of research.

Present and discuss research issues, approaches and findings.

Organize the research and its findings in a paper format.

GENG710.title: UAEU Catalog — GENG710 Optimization Methods for Engineering
GENG710.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2914.shtml?id=GENG710
This course focuses on the use of numerical search and optimization tools for purposes of conducting advanced technical decision-making. It will provide students with the fundamentals of the theory of optimization. The topics to be covered in this course include: formulation of optimization problems, mathematical modelling, non-gradient and stochastic search techniques, gradient-based optimization algorithms for unconstrained and constrained problems, numerical methods for sensitivity analysis, global optimization and surrogate modelling. A series of practical examples and case studies will complement the course material
Optimization Methods for Engineering (GENG710) > Credit Hours : 3

Optimization Methods for Engineering (GENG710) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Formulate engineering design problems with various requirements and constraints into optimization problems

Interpret the results of an optimization calculation in terms of the original practical problem

Evaluate optimization results by conducting sensitivity analyses, and exploring cost functions, and figures of merit

Differentiate between different optimization techniques and assess their pros and cons

Identify multi-objective optimization problems including the conditions for optimality

HSR140.title: UAEU Catalog — HSR140 Introduction to Society & Behavior
HSR140.text:
This course covers the basic concepts and purposes of Psychology, Sociology, Social Work, and Human Services and Counseling. This course will provide definitions of these four areas, their fields of inquiry, and their roles in studying and addressing behavioral and societal issues. The primary goal of this course is to enable students to recognize the uniqueness of each of the four areas and to appreciate how they interrelate and complement each other in approaching and resolving behavioral and societal problems.
Introduction to Society & Behavior (HSR140) > Credit Hours : 3

Introduction to Society & Behavior (HSR140) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Choose one discipline from the four disciplines

Describe sociology, psychology, human services and counseling, and social work

Evaluate the major perspectives, specialization areas, of sociology, psychology, human services and counseling, and social work

Understand the types and the nature of the careers in each of the four disciplines

HSR150.title: UAEU Catalog — HSR150 Introduction to Government Policy & Urban Structures
HSR150.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2924.shtml?id=HSR150
This interdisciplinary course combines concepts, ideas, and theories from Geography, Political Science, and Urban Planning. The course interactively addresses a series of topics relevant to the above mentioned disciplines, and aims to help students comprehend the intricacies and essentials of some contemporary human phenomena. The selected topics include government, leadership, human environment interaction and urban planning.
Introduction to Government Policy & Urban Structures (HSR150) > Credit Hours : 3

Introduction to Government Policy & Urban Structures (HSR150) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify and describe basic concepts and definitions related to political science, geography and urban planning

Demonstrate a basic understanding of concepts and issues related to political science, geography, and urban planning

Analyze basic concepts and issues related to political science, geography and urban planning

Interpret issues related to political science, geography and urban planning

Determine problems, challenges and solutions related to political science, geography and urban planning

GEOL100.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL100 Physical Geology
GEOL100.text:
This course aims to provide the students with fundamental knowledge about the Earth’s origin, composition, structures and history. Information about the different geological processes and plate tectonics are also introduced.
Physical Geology (GEOL100) > Credit Hours : 3

Physical Geology (GEOL100) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain Earth origin, processes and evolution during geological time.

Recognize the internal and external geological processes and rock types.

Discuss Plate Tectonics and its relation to geological events.

Describe formation processes and distribution of oceans, mountains, rivers, and deserts.

Describe effects of earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, and other geologic hazards.

GEOL110.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL110 Planet Earth
GEOL110.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL110
The course is designed to all university students in order to provide them with general education knowledge about our planet; its past, present and future changes. The course will include three main sections; the first focusing on Earth evolution in time and space, the second covers the Earth materials and Earth shaping processes and the third deals with natural hazards and the future of earth sciences. The course will be based on lectures, computer assisted exercises, multimedia presentations and seminars.
Planet Earth (GEOL110) > Credit Hours : 3

Planet Earth (GEOL110) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Use basic geological theories and models to explain the history of planet earth.

Explain fundamental geological concepts used to identify and classify minerals, rocks, and fossils.

Identify the Earth's natural resources, natural hazards and paleo-climatic changes.

Explain the basic processes intrinsic to diverse geological events ranging from the transportation of a sand grain to the formation of a mountain.

Define and characterize various modern geosciences and identify some of their applications.

GEOL215.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL215 Mineralogy
GEOL215.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL215
This course aims to develop a clear understanding and basic concepts of crystallography and mineralogy. Crystal system, symmetry, lattice, defect, twining, mineral groups, and mineral optical properties are well discussed. Petrographic microscope parts and uses, thin-section, opaques, isotropic and anisotropic minerals and related characteristics are included. Uniaxial and biaxial minerals are also defined with their different appearance. The course is associated with a laboratory part that forms the main practical application of the course items.
Mineralogy (GEOL215) > Credit Hours : 3

Mineralogy (GEOL215) > Prerequisites
GEOL100 with a minimum grade D

PHYS105 with a minimum grade D

CHEM111 with a minimum grade D
Mineralogy (GEOL215) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the basic concepts of crystallography and mineralogy.

Distinguish between different crystal systems and different mineral groups.

Discuss the basic hypothesis of light and its application in optical mineralogy.

Define the basic terminology of the petrography and optical mineralogy.

Identify some rock-forming minerals by using their physical and optical characteristics

Apply simple research activities related to the general mineralogy such mineral separation techniques.

GEOL220.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL220 Structure Geology
GEOL220.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL220
This course introduces the students to the principles of Structural geology, including the essential types of structural data, and how to measure and record them. It briefly treats primary structures before proceeding to explain the evolution of the important deformation (secondary) structures. The analysis of data to reveal the form and time relations of the largest crustal structures is then presented. The significance of plate tectonics for resource exploration will also be mentioned.
Structure Geology (GEOL220) > Credit Hours : 3

Structure Geology (GEOL220) > Prerequisites
GEOL100 with a minimum grade D

MATH105 with a minimum grade D
Structure Geology (GEOL220) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Interpret concepts used in structural geology and tectonics.

Recognize different parameters used in recording and constructing structural maps and tectonic elements.

Apply simple methods of structural data analysis in the solution of basic geological problems.

Prepare Structural Maps And Present Structural Data Using Basic Methods.

Communicate professionally through oral presentation and/or writing of scientific documents, such as reports and papers.

GEOL260.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL260 Paleontology
GEOL260.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL260
This Paleontology course is divided into two parts: the first deals with Micropaleontology and concentrates on selected forams, ostracods, nannofossils and etc…. The second part instructs students in the essentials of Invertebrate Macropaleontology, with emphasis on sponges, corals, bryozoa, brachiopods, molluscs, echinoids and arthropods. Students are trained to identify and describe key fossils to genus level using microscope and hand lens and to determine their relative age. Additional skills include fossil sketching and literature search. Some applications of Paleontology to hydrocarbon exploration are presented. Invertebrate Paleontology is the study of ancient invertebrates, typically defined as any organisms without backbones and divided into Micropaleontology (is the study of microscopic fossils) and Macropaleontology (fossils which can be studied with naked eye and using hand lens).
Paleontology (GEOL260) > Credit Hours : 3

Paleontology (GEOL260) > Prerequisites
GEOL100 with a minimum grade D

BIOC100 with a minimum grade D
Paleontology (GEOL260) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the key events in the evolution of life on the Earth.

Identify geologic time boundaries using index fossils.

Describe the main fossil phyla and important examples of classes, families and genera from the UAE

Apply the principles of fossils to relatively date sedimentary strata.

Apply the basic concepts of paleontology in the petroleum exploration.

GEOL300.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL300 Igneous and Metamorphic Rocks
GEOL300.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL300
This course presents a broad review of igneous rocks, emphasising their tectonic associations, interrelationships and petrogenesis as well as an introduction to the principles that govern mineralogical mineral assemblages and reactions in metamorphic rocks. After successful completion of this course you will have an integrated understanding of the range, composition and petrogenesis of the major igneous and metamorphic rock groups and will be able to identify them in thin section and deduce their tectonic association and mode of origin. You will review metamorphic facies, facies series and their distribution, as well as the thermal and tectonic controls on metamorphism. You will become familiar with the key skills used to aid the interpretation of metamorphic rocks: AKF, AFM diagrams and Thompson projections (for pelites) and petrogenetic grids and you will learn how to interpret these.
Igneous and Metamorphic Rocks (GEOL300) > Credit Hours : 3

Igneous and Metamorphic Rocks (GEOL300) > Prerequisites
GEOL215 with a minimum grade D

GEOL220 with a minimum grade D

( STAT210 with a minimum grade D or ( STAT235 with a minimum grade D)
Igneous and Metamorphic Rocks (GEOL300) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify igneous and metamorphic rocks in hand sample and thin section

Evaluate minerals and textures to unravel the history of igneous and metamorphic rocks

Explain how magma is generated, evolves, and crystallizes and fundamental principles controlling metamorphism

Interpret geochemical data of igneous and metamorphic rocks

Compile a coherent scientific report for a specific problem related

GEOL340.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL340 Sedimentation and sedimentary rocks
GEOL340.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL340
The course aims to develop the skills of students with a firm understanding of the basic principles and concepts of sedimentation and sedimentary rocks in relation to depositional and post-depositional processes and products. It includes studying both modern and ancient sedimentary environments on continents and in marine systems. The course provides introduction to the environments, processes and classification of sediments and sedimentary rocks. The topics cover information about weathering, erosion, sedimentation and formation of rocks. Field and laboratory techniques used in the analyses of sediments and sedimentary rocks are presented. Description of all varieties of sedimentary rocks and their economic uses are discussed with examples from the UAE region.
Sedimentation and sedimentary rocks (GEOL340) > Credit Hours : 3

Sedimentation and sedimentary rocks (GEOL340) > Prerequisites
GEOL220 GEOL215 with a minimum grade D
Sedimentation and sedimentary rocks (GEOL340) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the theoretical concepts of sedimentary environments and formation processes of sedimentary rocks.

Examine types of sedimentary rocks and their components through laboratory methods.

Identify sediments and sedimentary rocks in the field and their composition and depositional environment.
