Communicate professionally through both oral presentation and in writing of scientific documents.

Explain the economic benefits of sediments and sedimentary rocks in exploration of natural resources

GEOL345.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL345 Engineering Geology
GEOL345.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL345
This course is aimed to acquaint students with the fundamental concepts of engineering geoscience and applications in engineering constructions and infrastructure planning such as tunnels, dams, bridges etc. In addition, the course will provide methods and techniques commonly used in collecting and testing geological units and classify the data for engineering applications.
Engineering Geology (GEOL345) > Credit Hours : 3

Engineering Geology (GEOL345) > Prerequisites
GEOL340 with a minimum grade D
Engineering Geology (GEOL345) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognize the principles of engineering geoscience.

Discuss the importance of geological information in engineering applications

Identify the required geological information to overcome engineering problems

Describe the way of implementations to solve such problems before, during and after any engineering applications.

GEOL350.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL350 Economic Geology
GEOL350.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL350
Economic geology: Study the genesis and geology of ore deposits including base- and precious-metals, gems and other materials of commercial value, such as salt, gypsum, and building stone. This course concerned with the distribution of mineral deposits, factors controlling the formation of these deposits, the economic considerations involved in their recovery, and an assessment of the reserves available.. It applies the principles and methods of various other fields of the geologic sciences, most notably geophysics, structural geology, and stratigraphy. Its chief objective is to guide the exploration for mineral resources and help determine which deposits are economically worthwhile to mine. . Discuss how society uses each material, the environmental implications of doing so, and the remediation steps necessary to minimize the associated environmental impact.
Economic Geology (GEOL350) > Credit Hours : 3

Economic Geology (GEOL350) > Prerequisites
GEOL300 with a minimum grade D
Economic Geology (GEOL350) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognize common ore minerals in hand samples and under the microscope

Classify the common ore types, apply relevant research methods to study their properties and geological setting.

Explain the processes and mechanisms of their genesis and devise strategies for exploration for them.

Describe the applicability of different ore exploration methods and are able to utilize them in practice.

Apply how the mining process can take place with minimal negative consequences for the environment.

GEOL370.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL370 Geophysics
GEOL370.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL370
This course is designed to give a comprehensive knowledge of geophysics focusing mainly on the theory of potential field methods and their applications. The course covers the gravity and magnetic methods as well as the electric and electromagnetic methods. The course subject will focus on the application of these methods in subsurface structure studies, groundwater prospecting, mineral prospecting, engineering and environmental studies.
Geophysics (GEOL370) > Credit Hours : 3

Geophysics (GEOL370) > Prerequisites
MATH110 with a minimum grade D

PHYS110 with a minimum grade D

GEOL340 with a minimum grade D
Geophysics (GEOL370) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the basics of geophysics.

Recognize the theory of the different potential field surveys

Illustrate the relation between the various geophysical properties of rocks and the different potential field surveys.

Manipulate instrumentation during field procedures.

Interpret procedure of potential field surveys

GEOL390.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL390 Stratigraphy
GEOL390.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL390
Stratigraphy is the study of all rock strata, and their organization into mappable units based on their properties. Students will be instructed in elementary lithostratigraphy and biostratigraphy, and introduced to other stratigraphic method (chronostratigraphy, magnetostratigraphy, sequence stratigraphy, seismic stratigraphy, etc.). Practical aspects of this course include stratigraphic section measurement, correlation, lithofacies and biofacies analysis. Applications of stratigraphy to hydrocarbon exploration are discussed.
Stratigraphy (GEOL390) > Credit Hours : 3

Stratigraphy (GEOL390) > Prerequisites
GEOL215 with a minimum grade D

GEOL260 with a minimum grade D
Stratigraphy (GEOL390) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe theoretical concepts of stratigraphy.

Explain the hierarchy of lithostratigraphic systems, and concepts of biostratigraphy, chrono- stratigraphy, magnetostratigraphy and geochronology, etc.

Construct stratigraphic sections and sedimentary logs in the field and laboratory.

Explain the impact of stratigraphy on the exploration and exploitation of natural resources.

GEOL395.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL395 Seismic Methods
GEOL395.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL395
This course introduces the students to the theory and applications of Exploration Seismology. The course is concentrated on the reflection and refraction techniques. The course focuses on the field survey and data acquisition, data processing and interpretation in terms of structural and stratigraphic features. The course introduces the students to processing of seismic data on computer with emphasis on exploring and characterizing petroleum reservoirs using seismic reflection methods.
Seismic Methods (GEOL395) > Credit Hours : 3

Seismic Methods (GEOL395) > Prerequisites
GEOL370 with a minimum grade D
Seismic Methods (GEOL395) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the theory of exploration seismology.

Recognize the principles of seismic reflection and refraction

Interpret the basic data processing and gain experience in certain commercial processing software

Apply the seismic techniques for petroleum exploration, groundwater prospecting, environmental and engineering studies.

Identifying different structures and depositional environment on seismic sections.

GEOL398.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL398 Seismology and Plate Tectonics
GEOL398.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL398
This course covers the theory of plate tectonics and examines the geology of earthquakes, the global pattern of seismicity and seismicity associated with the tectonic settings. It focuses on the regional seismicity and the seismicity of UAE both historical and recent. Special attention will be given on the interpretation of seismic waves, fault mechanism, identification of events from observatory records, and assessing seismic hazards in the region.
Seismology and Plate Tectonics (GEOL398) > Credit Hours : 3

Seismology and Plate Tectonics (GEOL398) > Prerequisites
GEOL370 with a minimum grade D
Seismology and Plate Tectonics (GEOL398) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the Plate Tectonic theory.

Identify the relation between the tectonic movement and the earthquake activities.

Recognize the epicenter and the origin time of an earthquake using actual seismograms.

Identify the seismic wave paths through the Earth.

Explain existing earthquake prediction procedure and seismic hazard map.

GEOL400.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL400 Remote Sensing and GIS
GEOL400.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL400
This course aims at providing students with skills and knowledge to help him extract information, classification, analysis and application of remote sensing data for natural resource exploration and management. Another aim is to introduce spatial data analysis and geomorphological applications of GIS (Geographical Information Systems). It is expected that at the end of the course students will be able to develop methodologies and implement geospatial projects to solve spatial problems about Earth and its resources, using data extracted from RS data in a GIS environment. Case studies from the United Arab Emirates.
Remote Sensing and GIS (GEOL400) > Credit Hours : 3

Remote Sensing and GIS (GEOL400) > Prerequisites
GEOL340 with a minimum grade D

( STAT210 with a minimum grade D or ( STAT235 with a minimum grade D)
Remote Sensing and GIS (GEOL400) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the basic concepts and theories of EM radiation propagation and interaction with the atmosphere and the targets on the surface of the earth

Discuss the different Earth surface’s features that are discerned on B/W and color images

Describe the classification processes and algorithms of satellite imagery

Analyze and evaluate classified imagery to produce meaningful thematic maps as GIS layers

Interpret output GIS analysis results to be used for geologic and geomorphological applications.

GEOL410.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL410 Geochemistry
GEOL410.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL410
This course presents an exposition of the impact of chemistry and its laws on the spatial distribution of elements in the various spheres of the Earth. It introduces theories on the origin of the elements which compose the Earth, and the Solar System. The geochemistry of isotopes and radionucleides. Geochemistry of the three types of rocks on the Earth’s crust. Thermodynamics of elements. Geochemical exploration. Geochemical balance, and finally environmental geochemistry as a modern discipline.
Geochemistry (GEOL410) > Credit Hours : 3

Geochemistry (GEOL410) > Prerequisites
GEOL300 with a minimum grade D

GEOL340 with a minimum grade D
Geochemistry (GEOL410) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze effects of chemical weathering processes.

Explain basic principles of geochemistry and geo-applications

Demonstrate methods to analyses the chemical and mineralogical composition of rocks and minerals.

Describe distribution, behavior and substitution of elements in major rocks.

GEOL415.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL415 Petrophysics
GEOL415.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL415
This course covers the importance of the petrophysical properties of reservoir rocks, such as porosity, permeability, resistivity, and water saturation. It provides the basic background to well logging and reservoir characterization. The course aims at the achievement of profound understanding of the major petrophysical properties of reservoirs, and provides the theoretical knowledge required for log analysis and reservoir characterization. The course leads to bridges the gap between geologic and engineering understanding of reservoir rocks, and give a better understanding of the relation between rocks and fluids.
Petrophysics (GEOL415) > Credit Hours : 3

Petrophysics (GEOL415) > Prerequisites
GEOL340 with a minimum grade D

GEOL370 with a minimum grade D
Petrophysics (GEOL415) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the basic techniques of core recovery, handling, preservation, and analyses.

Explain basic petrophyscial properties of reservoir rocks such as porosity, permeability, water and oil saturation and wettability.

Analyze the behavior of hydrocarbon reservoirs under variable subsurface conditions.

Describe the correlation of petrophysical parameters obtained in laboratory and with the well logging tools.

Communicate in team work of different disciplines to solve reservoir problems.

GEOL425.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL425 Hydrogeology
GEOL425.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL425
This course is an introduction to the groundwater and the problems associated with it. The course is aimed to provide the students the basic aspects of hydrogeology such as hydrological cycle and properties of aquifer. In this course, principles of groundwater flow and soil moisture and groundwater recharge will be covered. The course covers also water chemistry and water quality and introduces the different field methods used in hydrogeology exploration and groundwater modeling. This course will help prepare students for either a career in hydrogeology or in other areas of environmental science and engineering where a strong background in hydrogeology is needed.
Hydrogeology (GEOL425) > Credit Hours : 3

Hydrogeology (GEOL425) > Prerequisites
GEOL340 with a minimum grade D

GEOL370 with a minimum grade D
Hydrogeology (GEOL425) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the fundamental principles and theories of hydrogeological processes.

Analyze and monitor of different hydrogeological processes.

Determine water chemistry and water quality and develop understanding of aquifer properties.

Evaluate groundwater flow and field hydrogeological methods.

Communicate professionally through both oral presentation and in writing of scientific documents, such as reports and papers.

GEOL428.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL428 Space and Terrestrial Planets
GEOL428.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL428
The course aims at introducing principles of cosmology and the formation of galaxies and planets in space and time as well as components of space in our solar system and planetary composition. Methods used to probe space and atmosphere of terrestrial planet will be presented. Special focus will be given to the composition and landscape features of terrestrial planets (Mars, Mercury and Venus) and comparison with those found on Earth.
Space and Terrestrial Planets (GEOL428) > Credit Hours : 3

Space and Terrestrial Planets (GEOL428) > Prerequisites
GEOL340 with a minimum grade D

GEOL370 with a minimum grade D
Space and Terrestrial Planets (GEOL428) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate knowledge of outer space and perceptions of cosmology

Explain the formation of our galaxy and the different planets

Describe the nature and landscape of terrestrial planets

Comprehend the comparison between Earth environment and the environments of terrestrial planets

GEOL430.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL430 Environmental Geoscience
GEOL430.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL430
This course deals with the principles of environmental geology as an integral part of the students’ curriculum. It includes: renewable and non-renewable resources, minerals, fossil fuels and water, conservation measures. Natural hazards including volcanic activity, earthquakes, floods, regional subsidence and landslides. Mitigative measures, pollution of air, surface and subsurface water, and soil. Waste disposal in a geologic context. Man’s modification of the physical environment. Environmental management and monitoring.
Environmental Geoscience (GEOL430) > Credit Hours : 3

Environmental Geoscience (GEOL430) > Prerequisites
GEOL410 with a minimum grade D
Environmental Geoscience (GEOL430) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain basic concepts and principles of environmental geology.

Discuss problems related to natural hazards and the geological environment.

Analyze the relationships between natural resources and environmental pollution.

Evaluate the basic concepts of environmental management and assessment methods.

Communicate ideas related to environmental monitoring guidelines and their application.

GEOL440.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL440 Nuclear Geoscience
GEOL440.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL440
The course aims at introducing the principles of radioactivity and radioactive isotopes, including modes of occurrence in nature and sources for industrial production. Exploration methods for radioactive isotopes and processes of formation will also be introduced. In addition, methods used in the survey and selection of repository sites for the storage of spent nuclear fuel and nuclear waste will be presented.
Nuclear Geoscience (GEOL440) > Credit Hours : 3

Nuclear Geoscience (GEOL440) > Prerequisites
GEOL410 with a minimum grade D
Nuclear Geoscience (GEOL440) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe theoretical concepts of radioactivity

Explain the formation and accumulation of radioactive elements in the lithosphere

Apply methods for exploration of radioactive natural materials.

Identify the criteria needed for selection of repository sites and the implications

GEOL445.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL445 Geoinformatics

GEOL460.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL460 Petroleum Geoscience
GEOL460.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL460
This course introduces the principles and concept of hydrocarbons formation in sedimentary rocks. The course provides comprehensive integration hydrocarbons from the sources to generation, migration and trapping. The course will introduce methods and techniques used to evaluate hydrocarbons potential of sedimentary basins. Introduction of applications related to hydrocarbons exploration, accumulation and exploitation will also be presented. The course aims at teaching the theories and hypothesis related to the formation of hydrocarbons. At the same time the mechanisms of hydrocarbon generation, migration and trapping are learned. Students will learn also about the different methods used in hydrocarbon exploration. Students will learn about the role of geological condition in the hydrocarbon exploration. At the end of the course non-conventional petroleum resources will be presented.
Petroleum Geoscience (GEOL460) > Credit Hours : 3

Petroleum Geoscience (GEOL460) > Prerequisites
GEOL370 with a minimum grade D

GEOL390 with a minimum grade D

GEOL410 with a minimum grade D
Petroleum Geoscience (GEOL460) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate Competence In Laboratory-Related Analyses And Evaluation Of Source And Reservoir Rocks.

Explain The Concepts Of Hydrocarbons Formation, Maturation, Migration And Accumulation.

Explain The Different Methods (Well Drilling, Well Logging, Geophysical, Mapping Technologies) Used In Hydrocarbon Exploration.

Explain The Petroleum Systems And Nonconventional Petroleum Resources.

Explain The Physical And Chemical Properties Of Hydrocarbons.

GEOL470.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL470 Research Project
GEOL470.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL470
This course is designed to enhance the student research and innovation capability in geosciences. This course may also involve field and laboratory activities as well as literature survey. Report and presentation are required.
Research Project (GEOL470) > Credit Hours : 3

Research Project (GEOL470) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate knowledge of concepts used in research

Analyze different parameters used in planning and conducting research activities.

Interpret data in terms of scientific value and application

Communicate professionally through both oral presentation and in writing.

GEOL475.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL475 Geology Of UAE
GEOL475.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL475
The United Arab Emirates lies between two water bodies, the Arabian Gulf to the north and the Gulf of Oman to the east. Most parts of the coastal plains on the Arabian Gulf are characterized by Sabkhas. Deserts represent the majority of UAE and cover the middle, west and southern part of the UAE. The Oman Mountains occupy the eastern and northeastern part of the UAE. There are gravel plains on the eastern and western parts of the Oman Mountains. The course will focus on the geological features of the Arabian Plate, upon which UAE is situated and an overview of the geological evolution of the exposed and deep (subsurface) geology (stratigraphy, structure, economic importance) and the Quaternary development of the UAE. The highlight of the UAE- Oman Semail Ophiolite one of the best and largest exposed ophiolites in the world and metamorphic sole and its economically important.
Geology Of UAE (GEOL475) > Credit Hours : 3

Geology Of UAE (GEOL475) > Prerequisites
GEOL300 with a minimum grade D

GEOL340 with a minimum grade D

GEOL370 with a minimum grade D

GEOL390 with a minimum grade D
Geology Of UAE (GEOL475) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain geologic features of the UAE including rocks and the main tectonic events.

Identify the geology of the UAE in the regional frame and context of the Arabian Plate.

Describe resources of the UAE including mineral, rock, water and petroleum resources.

Interpret the geologic and landscape development of the UAE.

GEOL486.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL486 Natural Water Systems
GEOL486.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL486
The Natural Water Systems course offers an insightful introduction to the essential water systems on our planet, focusing on surface waters as well as those present in soil and the atmosphere, including both salt and fresh water. It highlights the importance of aquatic ecology and geochemistry, concentrating on the conditions and processes vital for evaluating aquatic environmental risks. This course enriches the knowledge required for environmental management and environmental technology, which are pivotal in meeting the UN sustainability goals.
Natural Water Systems (GEOL486) > Credit Hours : 3

Natural Water Systems (GEOL486) > Prerequisites
GEOL340 with a minimum grade D

GEOL370 with a minimum grade D
Natural Water Systems (GEOL486) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the key concepts about the fundamental processes of the water cycle and characteristics of various natural water systems, including their hydrological and environmental significance.

Analyze water quality data using standard monitoring techniques, identifying key indicators and potential pollution sources and the effects of human activities on natural water systems, including pollution, resource extraction, and habitat alteration.

Apply and evaluate sustainable water management strategies that promote the health and resilience of natural water systems.

Interpret data on local water bodies, demonstrating practical skills in water system assessment and communicate research findings through written reports and presentations.

GEOL488.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL488 Landscape Geomorphic Evolution
GEOL488.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL488
The course describes the principles of landscape development through spatial and temporal scales and processes that changes the geomorphic systems. The course introduces factors controlling landscape evolution like lithology, climate and tectonic movements. The course encompasses small- and large-scale geomorphic features such slope stability, mass movements, drainage basin developments, eolian fields and coastal regions. The course presents methods used in the study of landscape evolution and applications in different sectors (agriculture, urban development and water resources.
Landscape Geomorphic Evolution (GEOL488) > Credit Hours : 3

Landscape Geomorphic Evolution (GEOL488) > Prerequisites
GEOL400 with a minimum grade D
Landscape Geomorphic Evolution (GEOL488) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the key concepts about the fundamental processes of landscape geomorphic cycle.

Identify the characteristics of various natural processes affecting the evolution of landscape significance.

Apply different methods, visual and digital, for the construction of landscape geomorphic development on spatial and temporal scales and impacts on societal development.

Communicate the course educational findings effectively through written reports and presentations.

GEOL499.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL499 Field Geology
GEOL499.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL499
This course provides basic training for students in field geological and some survey methods, geological data collection and analysis, map preparation, Quaternary landscapes and report writing. The course covers the various stages of preparation for field work (including aerial photograph & RS image interpretation) and actual geological mapping of a selected local area. A key outcome of the course is learning how to prepare stratigraphic sections, structural profiles, and how to create an informative and accurate geological map, accompanied by an individually written report on the geology of the study area.
Field Geology (GEOL499) > Credit Hours : 3

Field Geology (GEOL499) > Prerequisites
GEOL400 with a minimum grade D

GEOL430 with a minimum grade D

GEOL470 with a minimum grade D
Field Geology (GEOL499) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Operate geological and surveying field instruments.

Collect samples and identify different rock units and systematically analyze them.

Use specified software and digital images to process data.

Prepare geological maps including field, structural and petrographical data.

Solve problems related to geological setting for different rock units.

Write, organize and assemble data for a scientific report.

GEOL500.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL500 Internship
GEOL500.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL500
The training programme is coordinated by both the Department, academic supervisor and the faculty training committee. The programme is continuously monitored and reviewed by a field supervisor staff member at one of the various geological organizations in the United Arab Emirates. (This course is conducted over half a semester (8 weeks) during the third year of study. Offered condensed courses should be taken during the other half of the semester).
Internship (GEOL500) > Credit Hours : 6

Internship (GEOL500) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co GEOL499 with a minimum grade D
Internship (GEOL500) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply basic scientific concepts in real work places.

Develop work experiences and employment skills.

Identify the career path he/she should select.

Evaluate their self-knowledge and their work ethics with the other colleagues.

Discuss the positive and negative relationship between the education institutions and the stockholders' needs.

GEOL521.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL521 Geochemistry for Environment and Mineral Exploration
GEOL521.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL521
The aim of this course is to understand and apply the fundamentals of geochemistry in evaluating methods for mineral exploration and the associated environmental impact (K1, K2). Several analytical techniques such as XRD, XRF, SEM, ICPMS and interpretation and modelling software including Matlab and IGPET will be used to promote application of IA (S1-S6). The course will cover lectures and laboratory and field experiences. By the end of this course students will be able to define the basic principles and methods used in geochemical exploration and survey and environmental impact (S2) Students will also be familiar with the different types of geochemical distribution aureoles, including primary, secondary and flow dispersions, and their relation to ore deposits and environment. mineralogical/geochemical data to determine and interpret the areas of anomalies (S4) and/or a possible association of an environmental effect (S1). Part of the course assessment includes oral presentation and report (S6).
Geochemistry for Environment and Mineral Exploration (GEOL521) > Credit Hours : 3

Geochemistry for Environment and Mineral Exploration (GEOL521) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the behavior and method of geochemical dispersions of elements at different environments.

Define the basic principles and methods used in the geochemical survey and exploration.

Recognize different types of guides (e.g. mineralogical, lithological, stratigraphic guides) and their use in the geological exploration.

Statistically interpret mineralogical/geochemical data used to determine the areas of anomalies.

Measure and/or calculate some geochemical parameters used in exploration and/or environmental study.

GEOL526.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL526 Groundwater Environmental Assessment
GEOL526.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL526
This course aims at introducing ‎the principle used for the ‎evaluation of groundwater ‎potentials and the impact on the ‎environment (K1, S1). The course ‎provides techniques used for ‎the identification and ‎assessment of groundwater ‎during strategic planning for ‎natural resources. Spatially ‎distributed hydrological ‎modelling using ‎Geoinformatics techniques will ‎be introduced (K2, K3, S1, S2). Case studies ‎from arid to semi-arid on ‎groundwater environmental ‎assessment procedures and ‎practices will be addressed. ‎Students finishing the course ‎will gain experience in ‎assessment strategies and ‎approaches commonly applied ‎in groundwater policies and in writing scientific reports (S6).‎
Groundwater Environmental Assessment (GEOL526) > Credit Hours : 3

Groundwater Environmental Assessment (GEOL526) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluating the ‎quality of ‎groundwater in ‎terms of hydro-‎geochemistry, ‎isotopes ‎hydrology and ‎physical ‎parameters. ‎

Mapping and ‎monitoring ‎groundwater ‎chemical ‎parameters ‎through ‎Geoinformatics ‎tools.‎

Modelling the ‎groundwater ‎distribution and ‎recharge ‎sources.‎

Communicating ‎professionally ‎to defense ‎assessment ‎conclusions and ‎recommendations through case ‎studies. ‎

GEOL532.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL532 Non-Seismic Methods
GEOL532.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL532
This course aims to present advanced applications in non-seismic methods (potential field, electrical, electromagnetic) for the purposes of subsurface imaging (K1, K2, S1) and resource exploration (S2). The students will develop skills in the methods of measurement techniques and data acquisition (S3) and data correction/processing and modeling (S4). Particular attention is paid to inversion and modeling of the geophysical data in 2D and 3D, including reference to the application of Artificial Intelligence in geophysical data analysis. Part of the course assessment includes oral presentation and report (S6).
Non-Seismic Methods (GEOL532) > Credit Hours : 3

Non-Seismic Methods (GEOL532) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the principles of the different Non-Seismic Methods.

Investigate the know-how in data acquisition, survey layout, and field procedures.

Evaluate the capacity in advanced data interpretation procedures and modelling.

Relate the importance of non-seismic methods in the following fields: Oil, Mineral and Water exploration as well as the environmental, civil engineering and archaeological studies.

GEOL541.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL541 Geology of Petroleum Plays
GEOL541.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL541
An integral approach to petroleum plays and a review of worldwide petroleum provinces is proposed (K1). This course aims at introducing properties and processes associated with development of hydrocarbon reservoir and seal (cap) rocks (K1). Particular focus will be given to tools and methods that are used to evaluate and define characteristics of reservoirs and seal formation (S1, S2). Students finishing the course will develop skills in recognition of potential reservoir and seal rocks as well as in identifying most suitable methods to be used for fingerprinting rock properties which form an essential component in exploration and production of hydrocarbons (S1, S3). Part of the course assessment includes oral presentation and report (S6).
Geology of Petroleum Plays (GEOL541) > Credit Hours : 3

Geology of Petroleum Plays (GEOL541) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the particularity of petroleum plays combining a multidisciplinary approach. (CLO1)

Determine the applicability of outcrop analogues for subsurface reservoirs. (CLO2)

Compare sediment-body geometry and heterogeneities from recent depositional systems and outcrop analogues with subsurface reservoirs. (CLO3)

Evaluate the appositeness of variable exploration techniques in conventional and unconventional hydrocarbon systems. (CLO4)

Communicate professionally through both oral presentation and in writing. (CLO5)

GEOL574.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL574 Energy Resources
GEOL574.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL574
This course is prepared to help students maximize learning and understanding the subjects in energy and its resources. The major concepts of this course cover the basic relationship between geology and Earth resources, conventional energy sources such as coal, oil and natural gas, sustainable energy such as solar, biomass, fuel cells and etc., minimizing the environmental degradation while extracting, usage of earth natural resources as energy sources, and possible future energy resources.
Energy Resources (GEOL574) > Credit Hours : 2

Energy Resources (GEOL574) > Prerequisites
BIOE601 with a minimum grade D
Energy Resources (GEOL574) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe different types of energy resources and their historical background.

Assess sustainable way to protect environment in case of any environmental problems caused energy resources.

Evaluate the importance of environmental friendly sustainable renewable energy sources.

Discuss future energy resources and their possible efficiencies.

GEOL581.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL581 Applied Paleontology in Hydrocarbon Exploration
GEOL581.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL581
This course builds on the students’ knowledge of the main micro and macrofossil groups, particularly foraminifera, ostracods, calcareous nannofossils and pollen grains and spores (palynomorphs), siliceous microfossils (Radiolaria), sponges, coelenterates, bryozoan, brachiopods, molluscs, echinoids, trilobites, graptolites and trace fossils (S2). The course will further develop the students’ ability to recognize the essential characteristics of the general and apply that knowledge to petroleum exploration through integrated field, laboratory and case study exercises (K1, S1, S2,). The students will also be taught the significance of paleontology in biostratigraphic, paleoenvironmental and paleoclimatic research. Specific applications to basin hydrocarbon exploration and reservoir biostratigraphic zonation will be highlighted. Part of the course assessment includes oral presentation and report (S6).
Applied Paleontology in Hydrocarbon Exploration (GEOL581) > Credit Hours : 3

Applied Paleontology in Hydrocarbon Exploration (GEOL581) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the significance of fossils in hydrocarbon exploration

Demonstrate students’ ability in recognizing relevant fossil genera and species based on their morphological characteristics.

Examine the principles and methods of stratigraphic correlation between surface and subsurface sections.

Evaluate knowledge of the main hydrocarbon source rocks, reservoir rocks and cap rocks in the UAE and their paleontological characteristics.

GEOL585.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL585 Spatial Analysis using GIS and Remote Sensing
GEOL585.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL585
This course explores methods of analyzing spatial data in the interactive and graphical environment of a GIS and remote sensing (K3). The course draws on related theory in spatial statistics, geo-statistics, geographical analysis and cartographic modeling as well as teaching students how to enhance and process satellite images (S1, S2)). It is expected that at the end of the course students will be able to extract the necessary information and integrate Geo-data types related to land forms, environment, water, and hydrocarbon exploration. Part of the course assessment includes oral presentation and report (S6).
Spatial Analysis using GIS and Remote Sensing (GEOL585) > Credit Hours : 3

Spatial Analysis using GIS and Remote Sensing (GEOL585) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain theoretical basis of different spatial analysis methods used in GIS. (PLO1)

Identify data formats and spatial techniques used in Digital Terrain Modeling. (PLO1&PLO2)

Describe the development of a GIS model and its components. (PLO2&PLO3)

Solve problems using spatial analysis and modeling in GIS. (PLO2&PLO4)

Apply spatial analysis techniques using GIS in a practical project (PLO4&PLO5)

GEOL618.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL618 Exploration Geophysics
GEOL618.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL618
The aim of the course is to acquaint the students with the advanced theoretical and interpretation techniques of the different exploration geophysical methods and the problem recognition in exploration mainly in Petroleum Exploration (K1, K2). The course concentrates mainly on the explanation and functioning of the different methods (S2, S3, S4). The course also covers the data acquisition and processing. In addition to the comparison and correlation with other geophysical and geological data. Part of the course assessment includes oral presentation and report (S6).
Exploration Geophysics (GEOL618) > Credit Hours : 3

Exploration Geophysics (GEOL618) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the theoretical aspects of the different geophysical methods.

Explain the principles of the data acquisition.

Illustrate basics of the technique and the physical phenomena of the ground (e.g. contrasts in densities, structure variations, etc..)

Determine with the different processing tools from data reduction to advanced analysis.

Create 2D and 3D interpretation models of the geophysical data.

GEOL620.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL620 Carbonate and Evaporite Depositional Systems
GEOL620.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL620
This course aims to provide advanced methods for the characterization of carbonate and evaporate depositional systems and the techniques used in interpreting and understanding primary and secondary modifications (K1, K2, S1, S2). A special focus will be given to features of depositional environments and in particular to the sabkha system of the UAE (K1). Part of the course assessment includes oral presentation and report (S6).
Carbonate and Evaporite Depositional Systems (GEOL620) > Credit Hours : 3

Carbonate and Evaporite Depositional Systems (GEOL620) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the environmental conditions controlling the carbonate-evaporite system.

Analyze post sedimentation modifications and impact on the carbonate-evaporite system.

Recognize the economic potential of the carbonate-evaporite system.

GEOL631.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL631 Engineering Rock Mechanics
GEOL631.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL631
This course introduces the principles of engineering rock mechanics including data collection and assessment. The course stipulates how structures such as dams, tunnels, caverns, etc. built on or in rock masses critically depend on the rock mass properties and interaction between the rock mass and the engineered structure (K4). This course also focuses on description and representation of a rock mass, stress and strain in a rock mass and deformation and failure of a rock mass. These principles are simply applied to rock engineering applications such as rock slope stability analysis, design of underground structures in rocks (S3). Part of the course assessment includes oral presentation and report (S6).
Engineering Rock Mechanics (GEOL631) > Credit Hours : 3

Engineering Rock Mechanics (GEOL631) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the basic concepts of rock mass properties in rock engineering applications.

Justify appropriate laboratory and field tests to the geological environment in relation to the rock engineering structures.

Identify likely rock mass behaviors under different excavation and loading conditions.

Develop mitigation and sustainable solutions for rock engineering problems.

GEOL632.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL632 Remote Sensing and GIS for Biodiversity Monitoring
GEOL632.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL632
The scope of this course is to use remote sensing and GIS techniques and technologies for mapping, measuring and monitoring biodiversity. The theoretical backgrounds as well as the practical implementation of RS/GIS for biodiversity research and conservation application are taught. The remote sensing data analysis, GIS database building as well as the integration with biodiversity data and the spatial statistics including spatial modelling are introduced and mainly done with Erdas Imagine and ArcGIS softwares.
Remote Sensing and GIS for Biodiversity Monitoring (GEOL632) > Credit Hours : 2

Remote Sensing and GIS for Biodiversity Monitoring (GEOL632) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify major diagnosis of biodiversity issues and the suitable satellite images and procedures

Explain digital Image Processing of satellite images and information extraction

Integrate the use of GIS with remote sensing as a decision making tool for solving biodiversity challenges

Use RS/GIS visualization capabilities to raise awareness and enrich educational knowledge in issues dealing with biodiversity problems and solutions.

GEOL641.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL641 Earthquake Mechanism
GEOL641.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL641
The course covers broad subjects with emphasis on long-lived basic principles of earthquake mechanism. The recent technological progress in instrumentation, computer, and high-quality data has made it very easy to perform seismotectonic research (K1). The course first consolidates students’ knowledge and understanding of the concepts of modern global tectonics (K1, K2). The keys structural elements and seismic characteristics of the tectonic divergent, convergent and transform plate margins are presented. The tectonic evolution of the Arabian Plate is reviewed. The course then explores the dynamics of the solid Earth from theoretical and observational seismology and seismotectonics in relation to earthquake hazard and mitigation (S1, S2). It provides an in-depth study of earthquake seismology and earthquake hazard. Procedures for Interpreting earthquake seismograms and determination of earthquake focal mechanisms are given, with special attention to the seismicity of the UAE via local seismological network data (S3, S4). Part of the course assessment includes oral presentation and report (S6).
Earthquake Mechanism (GEOL641) > Credit Hours : 3

Earthquake Mechanism (GEOL641) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe key concepts in global tectonics.

Analyze competence in extracting critical tectonic and geophysical information from maps and other published resources.

Develop competence in finding and reviewing published material on regional tectonics and seismicity.

Accomplish self-management in selecting, planning and preparing a report for a case study of the earthquakes of a selected area.

Communicate results of analyses of seismic data in the context of tectonic models and seismic hazard assessment, via oral presentations, reports or posters.

GEOL654.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL654 Earth Climate Evolution, Geoinformatics and Environmental Hazards
GEOL654.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL654
This course will focus on Evolution of the Earth’s climate during geological time and factors that cause climatic changes and related environmental hazards (K1, S1). The course will use GeoInformatics techniques and software (S3, S4) for interpretation of geodatabase building (K2, S5) and analysis. Tools commonly used for the identification of climate and paleoclimate changes and associated environmental hazards, such as sea level rise, drought and floods (K2, S3, S4, S5) will be presented. Part of the course assessment includes presentation and report (S6).
Earth Climate Evolution, Geoinformatics and Environmental Hazards (GEOL654) > Credit Hours : 3 - 0

Earth Climate Evolution, Geoinformatics and Environmental Hazards (GEOL654) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the basic variability of the Earth’s climate through geologic time.

Recognize climate-related environmental hazards and appropriate assessment strategies.

Apply GeoInformatics methods and techniques for evaluation and mitigation of climate change and environmental hazards.

Utilize GIS-based spatial analysis and modelling techniques for climate-related environmental hazards.

GEOL671.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL671 Planetary Sciences
GEOL671.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL671
This course deals with the exploration of terrestrial planets in respect to planetary resources and their analogues on Earth. It takes the Earth as a reference to understand development of surface features on terrestrial planets and their related dynamic, physico-chemical, and morphological processes. The course introduces different methods used in the exploration of Earth and terrestrial planets including different specialties of Earth Sciences. The main objective is to introduce students to the geological histories, and geological processes, of other planets and to illustrate how this knowledge has led to our current understanding of the origin and evolution of the solar system. The course is designed to give students the basic introduction to planetary geology, with particular emphasis on the geology of Mars.
Planetary Sciences (GEOL671) > Credit Hours : 3

Planetary Sciences (GEOL671) > Prerequisites
PHYS105 with a minimum grade D

PHYS110 with a minimum grade D

MATH105 with a minimum grade D

MATH110 with a minimum grade D
Planetary Sciences (GEOL671) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the basic geology and geophysics of the planets in the solar system.

Use knowledge gained in the context of the Earth to interpret planetary remote sensing data in investigating other planetary environments.

Compare various techniques used to acquire geological knowledge of other planets.

Appraise the relationship between theories, hypotheses and observations in the planetary science.

GEOL680.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL680 Selected Topics
GEOL680.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL680
This course is designed to meet students’ needs to enhance and support his/her research skills and knowledge. Basic Knowledge competencies and computational skills that may not have been satisfactorily covered by core and elective courses, will be emphasized during this course. K1-K4, S1-S6 will be more emphasized during this course.
Selected Topics (GEOL680) > Credit Hours : 3

Selected Topics (GEOL680) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop specific skills in the subject of the course.

Conduct independent and updated research performance.

Apply scientific concepts and applications.

GEOL710.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL710 Advanced Topics in Plate Tectonics
GEOL710.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL710
This course deals with the details of the essential plate tectonic elements and their evolution and significance in terms of modern Plate tectonic theory. The significance of plate tectonics in terms of geological resources (industrial mineral resources and energy) and in seismic hazards will also be considered.
Advanced Topics in Plate Tectonics (GEOL710) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Topics in Plate Tectonics (GEOL710) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Categorize the characteristics of the tectonic elements from different tectonic settings.

Evaluate the main concepts of plate tectonics including the history of thought in this topic.

Competently analyze tectonic data from a variety of sources.

Examine the significance of tectonics in terms of exploration for industrial mineral and rock resources and energy.

GEOL720.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL720 Modeling and Geoinformatics
GEOL720.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL720
The course aims to enable students to use computer-based innovative techniques for the analysis and modeling of geospatial data. GPS, GIS, Digital Image Processing, and Geo-database building will be explained and used for problem solving and modeling. The course consists of three interrelated parts: a theoretical part which focuses on the concepts, a practical part which aims at developing hands-on skills in using software tools, and an application oriented part in which participants learn how to design and carry out sequential data processing steps for solving typical application problems in Geoscience. It is expected that at the end of the course students will be able to build models integrating various types of Geospatial data related to land forms, environment, water, hydrocarbon exploration, etc.
Modeling and Geoinformatics (GEOL720) > Credit Hours : 3

Modeling and Geoinformatics (GEOL720) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Decide on best practices in building Geo-databases for Geosciences applications

Develop capabilities for creating GeoInformatics-based models

Propose solutions for geosciences-related problems using spatial analysis and GeoInformatics

Originate critical evaluation of research practices in geosciences

Build strong scientific reading and writing skills, presentation and publishing of research papers.

GEOL731.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL731 Geology, Environment and Society
GEOL731.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL731
This course examines the important modern issues of environmental and social dimensions that lie within the geological sphere of study. The main topics covered in this course deal with energy sources and waste products, water for populations and industry, mineral and industrial material resource prospects and challenges, land use, land management, seismic assessment, coastal and sabkha issues, environmental engineering, climate and desertification issues.
Geology, Environment and Society (GEOL731) > Credit Hours : 3

Geology, Environment and Society (GEOL731) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognize the modern issues of environment and its social dimension within the geological study.

Discuss energy sources, efficiencies, renewable and nonrenewable energies and their environmental and social concerns.

Interpret challenges on population growth, limitation of water and mineral resources, waste products and pollution.

Outline the impact of climate change on environment and social life.

GEOL740.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL740 Geophysical Instruments & Data Acquisition
GEOL740.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL740
The aim of the course is to acquaint the PhD students with the different geophysical field techniques and technical problem recognition. The course covers explanation and functioning of the geophysical instruments including magnetometer, gravimeter, geoelectric instruments both electromagnetic and electric, and seismic. The course also covers the data acquisition and first step processing. The course aims at acquainting the students with the principles, data acquisition and processing of gravity, magnetic and geoelectric methods. The roles of these methods in the earth science investigations will be demonstrated.
Geophysical Instruments & Data Acquisition (GEOL740) > Credit Hours : 3

Geophysical Instruments & Data Acquisition (GEOL740) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Summarize the principles of the different geophysical Methods.

Experiment with geophysical data acquisition, survey layout, and field procedures.

Build the capacity in advanced data interpretation procedures and modelling.

Develop the importance of geophysical methods in the following fields: Oil, Mineral and Water exploration as well as the environmental, civil engineering and archaeological studies.

GEOL745.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL745 Seismology & UAE Seismicity
GEOL745.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL745
The course aims to provide an understanding of the dynamics of the solid Earth from theoretical and observational seismology and seismotectonics in relation to earthquake hazard and mitigation. It provides an in-depth study of earthquake seismology and earthquake hazard. The course includes procedures for Interpreting earthquake seismograms and determination of earthquake focal mechanisms. Special attention is given to the seismicity of the UAE by considering the local seismology network data. The keys structural elements and seismic characteristics of the tectonic divergent, convergent and transform plate margins are presented. The tectonic evolution of the Arabian Plate is reviewed. The course then explores the dynamics of the solid Earth from theoretical and observational seismology and seismotectonics in relation to earthquake hazard and mitigation. It provides an in-depth study of earthquake seismology and earthquake hazard. Procedures for Interpreting earthquake seismograms and determination of earthquake focal mechanisms are given, with special attention to the seismicity of the UAE via local seismological network data.
Seismology & UAE Seismicity (GEOL745) > Credit Hours : 3

Seismology & UAE Seismicity (GEOL745) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate knowledge of concepts used in seismology.

Recognize different parameters used in recording and constructing the tectonic elements.

Explain dimensions and factors controlling development of seismicity in the region.

Compile geologic maps, cross sections on local and regional frames in the context of the Arabian Plate seismicity.

Dealing with hazard management and public awareness.

GEOL750.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL750 Diagenesis, Stratigraphy, & Reservoir Evaluation
GEOL750.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL750
This course aims to introduce principles of diagenesis in sedimentary rocks and the effects of diagenetic processes and sequence stratigraphy on petroleum reservoirs with respect to basin architecture, relative sea level change and history. Concepts of stratigraphy, including, litho-bio-chemo-stratigraphy and sedimentology of clastic and nonclastic rocks will be introduced. Diagenetic processes cause changes in the porosity and permeability of sedimentary rocks that are controlled by the sequence stratigraphic secessions order and geometry. These changes impact the development of petroleum reservoirs and systems through changes in the permeability and porosity that directly related to oil migration and exploitation. The course will also introduce the students to sequence stratigraphic correlation on local, regional and global scale.
Diagenesis, Stratigraphy, & Reservoir Evaluation (GEOL750) > Credit Hours : 3

Diagenesis, Stratigraphy, & Reservoir Evaluation (GEOL750) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the theories and principles of diagenesis, stratigraphy to reservoir evaluation.

Recognize applications of diagenetic processes to different problems of geologic environments.

Link diagenesis and stratigraphy to oil exploration and abstraction.

GEOL755.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL755 Formation Evaluation
GEOL755.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL755
This course aims to provide introduction of geological, geophysical, petrophysical and geochemical methods used in the evaluation of petroleum bearing sedimentary rocks. Principles of petroleum systems and elements particularly source, migration, reservoirs, traps and seals will be provided. The course will also include evaluation of geological risk and optimization in exploration prospects through correlation between the different elements of the petroleum system. The course also will provide tools in petrophysics including well logging information and evaluation of petrophysical parameters, covering Porosity, Permeability, Formation evaluation and water and oil saturation, and Capillary pressure curves and wettability. These goals will be achieved by using advanced digital correlation matrices of the different geological, geophysical and geochemical parameters
Formation Evaluation (GEOL755) > Credit Hours : 3

Formation Evaluation (GEOL755) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the theories and principles of formation evaluation.

Evaluate practical aspects of formation evaluation techniques.

Develop capability in applications for oil exploration and abstraction.

GEOL760.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL760 Computer Applications in Geosciences
GEOL760.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL760
The course introduces students to the fundamentals of computing and to their practical applications in geosciences. Students will be trained on how to: define and create thematic layers from remote sensing and field spatial data; classify remote sensing data and extract information about earth surface; build geo-databases in a GIS environment; populate geodatabases, retrieve geo-data from geo-databases; import geo-data from external sources (e. g, existing databases, internet sites, ancillary data, etc.). The software used are ArcGIS from ESRI, Ltd, with Spatial Analyst and 3D analyst extensions for processing vector data models & ERDAS Imagine for raster data models and digital image processing. Students will be trained on using remote sensing data such as: satellite imagery of moderate to high resolutions (examples: Landsat, WV-2 & 3, Pleiades, Sentinel1 & 2, etc.); DEMs (available 15m and 5m for urban areas); GPS data (field survey); old maps (scanned 1: 25,000 topo maps) and other ancillary data. All mentioned data will be integrated in a unified coordinate system in geo-databases. This course is complementary and a co-requisite to the course (GEOL 720: Modelling and GeoInformatics) offered as a core course AND is intended to provide students, who have little to no experience in remote sensing and GIS, with necessary foundations to run smoothly the Modelling and GeoInformatics (GEOL 720) course. Students will acquire more experience and familiarize themselves with more remote sensing and GIS data analysis through hands-on exercises, home assignments and project implementation.
Computer Applications in Geosciences (GEOL760) > Credit Hours : 3

Computer Applications in Geosciences (GEOL760) > Prerequisites
GEOL720
Computer Applications in Geosciences (GEOL760) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discover theoretical basis of different data types and data models used in Geosciences.

Decide data formats and spatial techniques used in GIS, digital image processing and spatial analysis.

Develop skills to build geo-databases.

Build knowledge of applications of computer-based calculations in geosciences.

Create good scientific writing and presentation; create reports and publish research papers.

GEOL767.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL767 Advanced Geochemistry
GEOL767.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL767
The course covers detailed distribution, abundance and behavior of various elements in different parts of the earth. This mean abundance and behavior of trace element and their analysis, mobility and migration. This course focused on trace element geochemistry including a review of partition coefficients and theoretical approaches to understanding trace element partitioning during partial melting and fractional crystallization. Geochemical analyses including varieties of different instrumentation and techniques of different analytical methods. These methods include X-ray Fluorescence (XRD), inductive coupled plasma mass-spectrometer (ICP-MS), thermal ionization mass-spectrometer (TIMS), X-ray diffraction method (XRD), electron microprobe (EPMA) and sensitive resolution mass-spectrometer (SIMS). Throughout the course, lectures are interspersed with papers that are to be read by students and discussed during class. A listing of papers to be discussed is included but unfortunately the interactive class discussions emerging from reading these papers cannot be reproduced in a Web-based course. In addition, part of the course will comprise a seminar format that will require students to use the knowledge gained to evaluate and discuss geochemical topics.
Advanced Geochemistry (GEOL767) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Geochemistry (GEOL767) > Prerequisites
GEOL410 with a minimum grade D
Advanced Geochemistry (GEOL767) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify different types of geochemistry and their historical background.

Explore which rules control distribution of the elements in the lithosphere.

Explain trace element partitioning during partial melting and fractional crystallization.

Use chemical principles and concepts to solve geochemical and environmental problems.

Solve quantitative geochemical problems

GEOL770.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOL770 Environmental Mineralogy
GEOL770.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2929.shtml?id=GEOL770
Minerals are the essential earth solid materials made of chemical elements that occur in almost every environment. Therefore, any environmental impact, protection or treatment is strongly connected directly or indirectly to these materials. This course will explain this connection and reveal how mineralogy is a key of many environmental issues. It is planned to cover more or less following topics: The scope of environmental mineralogy, geochemical distributions of elements, heavy-metals, minerals and soil development, minerals and human health, conservation, landfills and containment control, mineral marine sediments, mine and nuclear wastes mineralogy, and the role of mineralogy in waste management and remediation strategies will be discussed with examples from UAE where possible.. Some geochemical analyses, methods or techniques may also be outlined when necessary. Although textbooks are the main reference of the course, related journal papers or published articles may be added to be presented and discussed during the class time.
Environmental Mineralogy (GEOL770) > Credit Hours : 3

Environmental Mineralogy (GEOL770) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate with examples from UAE the strong connection between minerals and environment.

Use minerals or mineral reactions for healing or remedy of an environmental problem.

Illustrate the role of minerals in changing of many environmental systems.

Judge the proper mineralogical or geochemical technique or analytical method for dealing with or studying a specific geo-environmental impact.

Identify the mineralogical aspects of radioactive and chemical wastes that influence in the environmental protection process and conduct.

ECBP614.title: UAEU Catalog — ECBP614 Mobile Commerce
ECBP614.text:
This course provides a coverage of mobile commerce (m-commerce) including frameworks, applications, requirements, location-based services, group-oriented services, transaction management, content and pricing, business model and emerging m-commerce services. The proposed course brings together challenges and solutions in mobile commerce including multi-layer frameworks, current and emerging mobile commerce services such as mobile financial services and mobile entertainment services. Management of mobile commerce services, business models and revenue management are also included. As m-commerce is going through many advances, many near and long-term issues such as the role of emerging wireless LANs and 3G/4G wireless networks, personalized content management, implementation challenges in m-commerce and futuristic m-commerce services will also be discussed.
Mobile Commerce (ECBP614) > Credit Hours : 3

GEIT112.title: UAEU Catalog — GEIT112 Fourth Industrial Revolution
GEIT112.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=GEIT112
With the rapid technological development and transformation, the world now is amidst the Fourth Industrial Revolution. This revolution is very much driven by intelligence in powering decision-making and processes. This course is designed to offer students an introduction to Fourth Industrial Revolution and provides a coverage of key Fourth Industrial Revolution technologies and trends; the changes it will generate and the benefits of its application; the different provided opportunities and posed challenges; and how organizations can reap Fourth Industrial Revolution benefits.
Fourth Industrial Revolution (GEIT112) > Credit Hours : 3

Fourth Industrial Revolution (GEIT112) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain Fourth Industrial Revolution concepts, components, opportunities, drivers and challenges.

Compare different technologies involved in Fourth Industrial Revolution.

Discuss individuals and societal Fourth Industrial Revolution impacts.

Develop lifelong Fourth Industrial Revolution skills.

GEIT113.title: UAEU Catalog — GEIT113 Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
GEIT113.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=GEIT113
This course offers a comprehensive introduction to Artificial Intelligence (AI), exploring its foundational concepts, societal impacts, and real-world applications. In this course, students will learn about the history and evolution of AI, its role in machine learning, natural language processing, and automation. The course will also examine AI’s influence on various industries, including healthcare, finance, and the creative arts while addressing critical ethical considerations such as bias, privacy, and regulation. Students will gain an understanding of AI’s potential for social good and future advancements, preparing them to engage thoughtfully with AI-driven technologies in their personal and professional lives.
Introduction to Artificial Intelligence (GEIT113) > Credit Hours : 3

Introduction to Artificial Intelligence (GEIT113) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate a basic understanding of core AI concepts.

Recognize the role of AI in shaping societal structures.

Explain how AI technologies are integrated into daily life, such as virtual assistants, smart devices, and creative industries.

Discuss the ethical concerns related to AI, including privacy, surveillance, and regulation.

ISBP631.title: UAEU Catalog — ISBP631 Managing Intelligent Information Systems
ISBP631.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISBP631
Information Technology (IT) broadly encompasses the information that organizations create, manage, and use, as well as a wide spectrum of increasingly convergent and interlinked technologies that process, analyze, and automate information. The course examines the role of IT and Artificial Intelligence (AI) in modern organizations, including how data-driven and intelligent systems support operational efficiency, strategic decision-making, and innovation. Topics include: Information Systems in organizations; organizing and managing data and information; enterprises and their organizational structures; an overview of Electronic Commerce and digital platforms; transaction processing systems, enterprise-wide systems, and AI-enabled enterprise applications; information, decision support, and intelligent systems (including machine learning–based analytics); systems analysis, design, implementation, and maintenance with consideration of AI integration and automation; Database Management Systems and data foundations for AI; current trends in the development of information systems, including AI, automation, and intelligent agents; and creating and sustaining competitive advantage through IT and AI-driven capabilities.
Managing Intelligent Information Systems (ISBP631) > Credit Hours : 3

Managing Intelligent Information Systems (ISBP631) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate IT and AI strategies in an organization.

Synthesize information and technologies used by businesses processes.

Assess information sharing across business departments for efficient operations.

Analyze current trends (including AI) in the development of information systems.

Analyze how IT usage by an organization creates and sustains a competitive advantage.

ISBP632.title: UAEU Catalog — ISBP632 Applied Data Mining
ISBP632.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISBP632
Due to advances in IT, the amount of modern data comprises huge files of diverse types, resulting in data rich but information poor organizations. To facilitate discovery of information patterns and trends, new approaches are required. Data mining techniques can help companies discover information and acquire business intelligence from these massive datasets. This course covers data mining for business intelligence. Data mining refers to extracting or “mining” knowledge from large amounts of data and consists of techniques that aim at discovering patterns that can bring value or “business intelligence” to organizations, for example consumer behavior. The course covers salient data mining techniques including classification, clustering, association rule mining, visualization and prediction.
Applied Data Mining (ISBP632) > Credit Hours : 3

Applied Data Mining (ISBP632) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Perform data pre-processing and exploration.

Apply data mining techniques to extract knowledge from different genres of data.

Develop data mining models for decision making.

Evaluate the performance of different data mining techniques.

Demonstrate teamwork skills.

ISBP633.title: UAEU Catalog — ISBP633 AI Innovations and Entrepreneurship
ISBP633.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISBP633
AI-driven ventures differ from traditional firms in their deep reliance on artificial intelligence technologies to create value, automate processes, and enable new business models. This course explores the unique challenges and opportunities involved in launching and scaling AI-based startups. Students will learn how to identify promising AI venture opportunities, design viable AI-enabled products and services, and navigate the strategic, technical, and ethical considerations that shape today’s AI innovation landscape. Topics include opportunity recognition in emerging AI markets; developing roadmaps for successful AI solutions; evaluating risks, limitations, and returns associated with AI techniques and data-driven systems; and creating robust business and operational plans for AI ventures. The course also addresses organizational development in AI-first companies, talent and data strategy, responsible AI practices, and financing models for technology entrepreneurship. Through practical exercises and case studies, students will gain the knowledge and skills needed to build and lead innovative AI startups in a rapidly evolving digital economy.
AI Innovations and Entrepreneurship (ISBP633) > Credit Hours : 3

AI Innovations and Entrepreneurship (ISBP633) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Investigate the role and skills of an entrepreneur.

Analyze the entrepreneurial process in IT related business.

Evaluate the principles and success factors of IT venture planning.

Assess the viability of functional planning in IT ventures considering key legal and intellectual property issues.

Create a business plan (including financial plan) for an IT venture.

ISBP634.title: UAEU Catalog — ISBP634 AI for Business
ISBP634.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISBP634
AI for Business examines the use of artificial intelligence technologies within enterprise computing environments, focusing on how AI is integrated into business systems, networks, and organizational processes. The course introduces the role of AI in modern enterprises and covers AI-enabled enterprise technologies, including machine learning and natural language processing, intelligent business process modeling, data-driven decision systems, and AI-supported enterprise applications such as ERP, CRM, and intelligent automation platforms. The course also addresses the integration of AI with existing enterprise architectures, data infrastructure, and workflows, highlighting strategic considerations for adoption and deployment. Students will analyze real-world business cases and carry out a project that explores emerging directions, challenges, and opportunities of AI-enabled enterprise applications in contemporary organizations.
AI for Business (ISBP634) > Credit Hours : 3

AI for Business (ISBP634) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Investigate the evolution of enterprise computing and artificial intelligence, including AI-enabled platforms, architectures, and typical business applications.

Apply AI and machine learning techniques within enterprise and business contexts to support decision-making and value creation.

Develop AI-enabled business process models that integrate data, analytics, and intelligent automation.

Construct AI-supported business solutions by integrating AI capabilities with enterprise systems, workflows, and digital platforms.

Conduct research on emerging AI-enabled business applications, challenges, and future directions, including strategic, ethical, and governance considerations.

ISBP635.title: UAEU Catalog — ISBP635 Knowledge Management
ISBP635.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISBP635
Knowledge Management (KM) is a discipline that promotes an integrated approach to identifying, capturing, sharing and evaluating an enterprise's information and knowledge assets. This course reviews and discusses existing technologies in KM and new, emerging KM technologies and practices. The course evaluates the computer representation, access, and utilization of knowledge versus information within a human context. It provides an essential preparation for managerial roles in today's modern knowledge-based economy.
Knowledge Management (ISBP635) > Credit Hours : 3

Knowledge Management (ISBP635) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze Different Approaches To Knowledge Management In Organizational Contexts.

Analyze Knowledge Management Technologies And Practices.

Create A Plan To Leverage Opportunities, Capture, Represent And Share Knowledge Within An Organization.

Demonstrate The Ability To Work In A Team And Communicate Effectively.

Evaluate Current Trends In Knowledge Management And Their Manifestation In Business.

ISBP636.title: UAEU Catalog — ISBP636 IT Legislation
ISBP636.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISBP636
This course provides a broad spectrum and analysis of the legal issues confronted in today’s information technology (IT). It describes the foundation of intellectual property concepts upon which IT activities and transactions are based. The course also explains the licensing issues of software or information resources, the outsourcing or hosting of services or information, the allocation of software or websites development rights. It also addresses existing legislations and regulations impacting the use of IT systems in the UAE, including electronic privacy and security, and commercial laws related to IT
IT Legislation (ISBP636) > Credit Hours : 3

IT Legislation (ISBP636) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Assess The Foundation Of Intellectual Property Concepts.

Discuss The Vital Components And Key Practical Applications Of An Information Security Policy.

Evaluate The Principles And Philosophies Which Underlie Successful Information Security Governance.

Evaluate The Value And Necessity Of Information Security Policies In The Globalizing Business World.

Investigate The Major Social, Legal, And Ethical Issues Present In The Realm Of Computing.
