ISBP637.title: UAEU Catalog — ISBP637 AI Strategy and Governance
ISBP637.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISBP637
This course explores the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in transforming public-sector operations, decision-making, and service delivery. It examines how governments design, deploy, and regulate AI systems to enhance performance, transparency, and societal well-being. The course is structured around three areas: (1) AI strategies and readiness in the public sector, including capabilities, limitations, and adoption frameworks; (2) policy, ethics, and governance issues such as data governance, transparency, accountability, equity, privacy, and regulation; and (3) applied governance through real-world case studies of AI initiatives in government and international organizations. Through discussions and analytical exercises, students develop the skills needed to evaluate and manage AI-driven programs effectively.
AI Strategy and Governance (ISBP637) > Credit Hours : 3

AI Strategy and Governance (ISBP637) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Investigate how governments design, deploy, and regulate AI systems.

Assess AI technologies, their capabilities and limitations, and frameworks for assessing AI readiness and strategic adoption in the public sector.

Analyze key policy challenges including data governance.

Develop a strategic AI Governance project plan for an institution.

ISBP639.title: UAEU Catalog — ISBP639 AI for Digital Transformation
ISBP639.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISBP639
This graduate course examines how artificial intelligence (AI) drives digital transformation across industries, combining AI technical foundations (Machine learning, Natural Language Processing etc.) with strategic frameworks (business models, change management) and sector‑specific applications. In this course students will learn how to effectively implement and manage AI technologies within their organizations. The course prepares graduates to lead AI‑enabled change that improves customer experience, operational efficiency, and competitive advantage. It covers critical topics such as AI technology fundamentals, data-driven decision making, AI application in enhancing customer experience, operational efficiency, and creating competitive advantages. Through case studies and real-world examples, students will learn how to effectively implement and manage AI technologies within their organizations.
AI for Digital Transformation (ISBP639) > Credit Hours : 3

AI for Digital Transformation (ISBP639) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain core AI concepts (ML, DL, NLP) and data infrastructure.

Design AI-enabled business models and transformation roadmaps.

Recognize the key challenges and risks associated with AI for digital transformation

Assess the ethical, legal, and governance implications of AI for digital transformation

ISBP640.title: UAEU Catalog — ISBP640 Cybersecurity for AI and IT Management
ISBP640.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISBP640
This course equips students with cybersecurity knowledge and management practices to protect AI-enabled and data-driven IT systems across their lifecycle. It examines how AI technologies reshape enterprise threat models, introduce new attack vectors (e.g., data poisoning, model extraction, prompt injection), and create governance challenges related to risk, compliance, and resilience. Students learn security-by-design for AI systems, protection of data and model pipelines, identity and access management, cloud and API security, and privacy considerations. The course emphasizes IT management decision-making, including risk assessment, control selection, governance alignment, vendor risk management, and incident response, enabling students to evaluate and manage AI security risks while balancing business and compliance requirements.
Cybersecurity for AI and IT Management (ISBP640) > Credit Hours : 3

Cybersecurity for AI and IT Management (ISBP640) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Assess cybersecurity risks and threat models associated with AI-enabled IT systems.

Evaluate security controls for AI data pipelines, model lifecycles, and deployments.

Design security-by-design and governance practices for secure and compliant AI adoption.

Analyze cybersecurity incidents involving AI systems and propose effective response and mitigation strategies.

Develop an enterprise-level cybersecurity roadmap for AI systems aligned with business, risk, and compliance requirements.

ISBP669.title: UAEU Catalog — ISBP669 Computation and Data Science
ISBP669.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISBP669
This course will introduce the students to the main concepts and tools of computation for data science. There are two main components to this course, namely, conceptual component and practical component. The conceptual part will start with an overview of data, information, and computational techniques that data analysts and data scientists work with. It will follow a description of different types of data analytics, including data extraction, cleaning, statistical inference from data, regression models, and an overview of machine learning. The second part will be a hands on experience with the state-of-the art computational tools for data science, including R, python and java based libraries and tools. This part will also include real case studies. The course will be concluded with relevant contemporary challenges and research problems related to data science.
Computation and Data Science (ISBP669) > Credit Hours : 3

Computation and Data Science (ISBP669) > Prerequisites
PHYS105 with a minimum grade D

PHYS110 with a minimum grade D

MATH105 with a minimum grade D

MATH110 with a minimum grade D
Computation and Data Science (ISBP669) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the conceptual fundamentals of data science

Compare various approaches for data analytics

Design a data analytics solution for a real world problem

Evaluate effectiveness of different data analytics tools on addressing a given problem

ISEC311.title: UAEU Catalog — ISEC311 Network Security I
ISEC311.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISEC311
This course provides the basic fundamental theoretical concepts of network traffic and services filtering. In addition, this course provides concepts of stateless and stateful firewalls. Topics include: TCP/IP protocols, network packet filtering, common Internet services (HTTP, FTP, SMTP, POP3, DNS, etc.) filtering, stateless and stateful firewalls, firewall filtering rules consistency and efficiency verification, VPNs, secure network architectures, network attacks on firewalls.
Network Security I (ISEC311) > Credit Hours : 3

Network Security I (ISEC311) > Prerequisites
ITBP301 with a minimum grade D
Network Security I (ISEC311) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Assess Firewall Filtering Rules Consistency And Efficiency.

Compare Stateless And Stateful Firewalls.

Demonstrate Teamwork Skills.

Describe Tcp/Ip Protocols And Common Network Services.

Discuss Vpn And Secure Network Architectures.

Explain Network Traffic And Service Filtering Concepts.

ISEC312.title: UAEU Catalog — ISEC312 Cryptography
ISEC312.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISEC312
The students in this course will be introduced to various encryption techniques and their applications. The main encryption techniques the students will learn and apply in this course are Symmetric encryption, Public-key encryption, and hash functions. These techniques will be used for digital signatures, certificate generation and verification. The performance of the various encryption techniques used will be analyzed based on certain criteria and design needs.
Cryptography (ISEC312) > Credit Hours : 3

Cryptography (ISEC312) > Prerequisites
ITBP301 with a minimum grade D

CENG202 with a minimum grade D
Cryptography (ISEC312) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze security threats associated with cryptographic algorithms.

Apply hash function Algorithms

Discuss contemporary cryptography and its application.

Evaluate various cryptographic techniques.

Investigate the mathematical concepts required for cryptographic algorithms

ISEC321.title: UAEU Catalog — ISEC321 Network Systems Security
ISEC321.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISEC321
This course provides an in-depth exploration of three core areas of network security: network traffic filtering systems, intrusion detection systems, and penetration testing. It begins by examining the principles and techniques of network traffic and service filtering, with a focus on firewall technologies. Students will gain a detailed understanding of the principles and implementation of common cyberattack techniques. The course then introduces the fundamental concepts and mechanisms behind the development and deployment of network intrusion detection systems, including the design and implementation of cyberattack signature rules. It further explores network vulnerability assessment, auditing, and penetration testing methodologies used to evaluate system security. In addition, the course addresses the security challenges and protection strategies associated with emerging, advanced, and next-generation networks. Finally, it investigates the application of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) techniques in network anomaly detection systems, demonstrating how intelligent algorithms can be used to identify, classify, and mitigate abnormal network behaviours in real time.
Network Systems Security (ISEC321) > Credit Hours : 3

Network Systems Security (ISEC321) > Prerequisites
ITBP301 with a minimum grade D
Network Systems Security (ISEC321) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the principles and techniques of network traffic and service filtering, including the configuration and management of firewall technologies.

Analyze and categorize common network cyberattack techniques, and assess their impact on network infrastructure, performance, and security posture.

Design, implement, and evaluate network intrusion detection systems, and develop and test effective cyberattack signature rules for threat detection.

Conduct network vulnerability assessments and apply penetration testing methodologies to identify and mitigate security risks.

Evaluate the security challenges and protection strategies associated with emerging, advanced, and next-generation networks.

Apply artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques to detect, classify, and mitigate network anomalies in real time.

ISEC322.title: UAEU Catalog — ISEC322 Design and Analysis of Security Protocols
ISEC322.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISEC322
This course provides the students with the necessary knowledge in the design, analysis, and evaluation of various security protocols and mechanisms, including but not limited to: basic symmetric and asymmetric cryptography protocols, SSL/TLS, WEP/WPA, IPSec, S/MIME, PGP, SSH, X.509 and Kerberos. A security protocol may fail in three ways: the protocol design may be flawed, the cryptography may be inadequate, or the implementation may be buggy. This course focuses on discussing the pros and cons of various security trade-offs involved in the design of internet protocols, identifies and describes vulnerabilities associated with such protocols, and describes the mitigations for these vulnerabilities.
Design and Analysis of Security Protocols (ISEC322) > Credit Hours : 3

Design and Analysis of Security Protocols (ISEC322) > Prerequisites
ISEC312 with a minimum grade D
Design and Analysis of Security Protocols (ISEC322) > Corequisites
ISEC324 with a minimum grade D
Design and Analysis of Security Protocols (ISEC322) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze vulnerabilities associated with the insecure internet and E-Commerce Protocols.

Communicate issues relevant to Public-Key Infrastructure (PKI).

Demonstrate how security protocols are used to achieve internet and E-Commerce security.

Describe the internet and E-Commerce Security Protocols.

Explain the concept of trust (and trust models) on the internet using secure internet protocols.

ISEC323.title: UAEU Catalog — ISEC323 Secure Software Design and Engineering
ISEC323.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISEC323
This course takes a close look at software as a mechanism for attack, as a tool for protecting resources, and as a resource to be defended. The course covers how poor software design and engineering can be the root causes of most security vulnerabilities in deployed systems, web technologies and digital rights management. Topics covered include: secure software design and development process, common software and web vulnerabilities such as buffer overflows and cross site scripting, program and code auditing and analysis using static, dynamic, and hybrid analysis, software watermarking and code obfuscation, and software testing for vulnerability.
Secure Software Design and Engineering (ISEC323) > Credit Hours : 3

Secure Software Design and Engineering (ISEC323) > Prerequisites
CSBP219 with a minimum grade D

ITBP301 with a minimum grade D
Secure Software Design and Engineering (ISEC323) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze software vulnerabilities.

Analyze web application security threats and countermeasures.

Compare various software security testing tools and techniques

Discuss common security issues in software.

Explain secure software design & development techniques

ISEC324.title: UAEU Catalog — ISEC324 Cryptography Lab
ISEC324.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISEC324
This laboratory course provides hands-on experience that covers the concepts of symmetric and asymmetric cryptographic algorithms, hash functions, and its real-world security applications. Main topics include: classical cryptography, encryption algorithms including DES, RC4, AES and RSA, Diffie-Hellman key exchange, hash functions, cryptographic-based security protocols including SSL, SSH, PGP, and IPSec.
Cryptography Lab (ISEC324) > Credit Hours : 1

Cryptography Lab (ISEC324) > Corequisites
ISEC322 with a minimum grade D
Cryptography Lab (ISEC324) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze classic cryptographic algorithms.

Compare security properties of well-known cryptographic protocols

Implement an IPSEC VPN solution for a small network.

Implement public-key cryptosystems techniques

Implement symmetric cryptography techniques

ISEC411.title: UAEU Catalog — ISEC411 Privacy and Anonymity
ISEC411.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISEC411
This course prepares students to recognize, analyze, and manage privacy challenges. Students learn concepts and methods for creating technologies and related policies with provable guarantees of privacy protection. Students will draw on work from data mining, information retrieval, web technology, computer security, cryptography, relational databases, statistics and political philosophy. Students are not expected to have these backgrounds; relevant material is introduced as needed. Main topics include: Privacy concepts and challenges, policies, and regulations; identity, anonymity and confidentiality; private data analysis and database sanitization; privacy-preserving data mining techniques including k-anonymity and secure function evaluation, and finally, some case studies from different domains are presented.
Privacy and Anonymity (ISEC411) > Credit Hours : 3

Privacy and Anonymity (ISEC411) > Prerequisites
CSBP320 with a minimum grade D

ITBP301 with a minimum grade D
Privacy and Anonymity (ISEC411) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Use tools to detect when data is mined/shared with false beliefs about privacy and data protection.

Investigate privacy protection technologies that provide formal computational guarantees of privacy.

Discuss challenges to privacy protection.

Analyze privacy legislation, policies, and best practices.

ISEC412.title: UAEU Catalog — ISEC412 Digital Forensics
ISEC412.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISEC412
This course is designed to equip students with the skills needed to safely locate and secure computer evidence at the search site as well as to conduct subsequent off-site analysis. The course aims to equip future Forensics Investigators and Lawful Enforcement Offices with sufficient knowledge on conducting investigation on Internet based or Cyber based crime. It provides knowledge on implementing the right solution for collecting, analyzing, correlating the Internet data and report them as valid and legal evidence in the court. Topics include evidence handling and disk imaging (restore evidence drive, system backup imaging), DOS/Windows forensics utilities (DOS analysis tools, Access Data’s forensics tool kit, Xway’s WinHex Disk Editor), hidden data and encryption, steganography, covert channel, erased file recovery, Internet investigations, Hacker profile analysis, and Email header analysis.
Digital Forensics (ISEC412) > Credit Hours : 3

Digital Forensics (ISEC412) > Prerequisites
CSBP315 with a minimum grade D

ISEC321 with a minimum grade D

ISEC323 with a minimum grade D
Digital Forensics (ISEC412) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze concepts of computer digital forensics.

Assess digital forensics on mobile devices and applications.

Conduct software and hardware based digital forensic analysis.

Discuss laws affecting digital forensics.

Evaluate current computer digital forensics tools.

Evaluate web and cloud based digital forensic tools.

ISEC413.title: UAEU Catalog — ISEC413 Security Architecture and Mechanisms
ISEC413.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISEC413
This course is intended to provide students with an understanding of the OM-AM framework, security architectures and mechanisms, system security infrastructures, access control multilevel security models, and biometric authentication and authorization architecture models. Also, the course provides analysis and evaluation of the security related functions of various systems including: monitoring systems, telecommunication systems, smart grid systems, and physical tamper resistant and proof systems.
Security Architecture and Mechanisms (ISEC413) > Credit Hours : 3

Security Architecture and Mechanisms (ISEC413) > Prerequisites
ISEC321 with a minimum grade D
Security Architecture and Mechanisms (ISEC413) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze security threats associated with information systems and their infrastructures

Apply security access control models

Design a secure information system using the OM-AM framework

Discuss system security architectures concepts and their attributes

Evaluate biometric solutions and authentication protocols

Select security countermeasures solutions

ISEC414.title: UAEU Catalog — ISEC414 Network Security Lab
ISEC414.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISEC414
This lab will be delivered in collaboration with our industry partner, Cisco Academy, to provide students with extensive hands-on learning opportunities. By integrating practical exercises and real-world scenarios, the lab is designed to strengthen students’ technical expertise in network security and support their preparation for professional certification in this field. Main topics include: security features of network devices such as routers and switches; authentication, authorization, and auditing models; best practices of access control security policies; stateful and application firewalls; intrusion detection, prevention, and response systems; network threats and attacks.
Network Security Lab (ISEC414) > Credit Hours : 1

Network Security Lab (ISEC414) > Prerequisites
ISEC321
Network Security Lab (ISEC414) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze common network threats and attack vectors.

Analyze security incidents using intrusion detection and prevention systems.

Apply Attack Mitigation Techniques.

Configure security features of network devices.

Implement packet filters, stateful firewalls, and application layer firewalls.

ISEC416.title: UAEU Catalog — ISEC416 Information Security Management
ISEC416.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISEC416
This course will cover a variety of topics to develop students’ skills in information security management. The course examines the fundamental principles of computer security management as applied to information technology. Course topics include: Security Management Practices: Business Continuity Planning (BCP), Disaster Recovery Planning (DRP), Law, Investigations, and Ethics. Business Needs: Commercial and legal implications. Introduction to ISMS standards: History, development, current situation. Certification: process and maintenance. Accreditation: Current developments, options, designing and implementing a management system. Policy and risk assessment: Statement of applicability, risk management, critical success factors, auditing.
Information Security Management (ISEC416) > Credit Hours : 3

Information Security Management (ISEC416) > Prerequisites
ITBP301 with a minimum grade D

ITBP370 with a minimum grade D
Information Security Management (ISEC416) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze And Implement Business Continuity Planning (Bcp) And Disaster Recovery Planning (Drp)

Analyze Risk Management And Auditing Techniques

Apply Isms Standards.

Apply Risk Evaluation And Mitigation Strategies

Criticize Legal And Ethical Implications On Security Management

Discuss Security Management Policies And Best Practices

ISEC417.title: UAEU Catalog — ISEC417 Database Security
ISEC417.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISEC417
This course is concerned with the study of principles and practices of implementing computer database security. The course discusses the following security features of the database: database security principles, database auditing, security implementation and database reliability, database enumeration (authenticated and unauthenticated), identifying database vulnerabilities, exploiting flaws to gain control, developing an assessment methodology, database assessment flag challenge, and virtual private database. The course provides also suggested architectures for common security problems. Students will learn how to secure their database and how to use the database features that enhance security. The student will be provided with the tools, techniques and industry accepted methodologies so that upon completion of the course the student will be able to describe key concepts of database security and how to apply those concepts to securing database management systems within their organizations.
Database Security (ISEC417) > Credit Hours : 3

Database Security (ISEC417) > Prerequisites
CSBP320 with a minimum grade D

ITBP301 with a minimum grade D
Database Security (ISEC417) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze security vulnerabilities in databases.

Apply database security models and policies on modern databases.

Compare various database security and defense mechanisms.

Describe database security models and architectures.

Discuss data and applications auditing procedures for database security.

ISEC421.title: UAEU Catalog — ISEC421 Risk Analysis and Management
ISEC421.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISEC421
This course provides students with an introduction to the field of information security risk assessment. Students will learn how to design systems that are secure, how to measure risk, and how to ensure that proper levels of security are maintained for individual technology users, businesses, government, and other organizations. This course will cover different approaches for risk assessment and risk mitigation. Students will learn how to apply NIST standards in conducting risk assessments. The course will incorporate cases in risk analysis derived from actual state and law enforcement agencies or private firms. Students will learn how to use a risk analysis matrix for performing both quantitative and qualitative risk analysis. As a part of the course, students learn the different threats that they need to incorporate in their risk analysis matrices. Course topics include: Threat Vulnerability Analysis (TVA), Risk Management Identification and Assessment, Strategies (Avoidance, Transference, Mitigation, Acceptance), Counter-Measures, Cyber Warfare (Technical and People), Vulnerability Testing and Penetration Testing, Contingency Planning (Business Impact Analysis, Disaster Recover, Business Continuity), SETA: Security, Education, Training and Awareness Initiatives, Cost Benefit Analysis of Info Security investments
Risk Analysis and Management (ISEC421) > Credit Hours : 2

Risk Analysis and Management (ISEC421) > Prerequisites
STAT210 with a minimum grade D

ITBP301 with a minimum grade D
Risk Analysis and Management (ISEC421) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Compare risk assessment techniques

Design an information security risk management program for an organization

Implement an information security risk management roadmap

Manage an information security risk assessment consulting contract

ISEC422.title: UAEU Catalog — ISEC422 Security Policy, Laws, and Governance
ISEC422.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISEC422
This course provides students with an introduction to information security policies and standards, as per the ISO/IEC 27001-2013 guidelines. In this course, students will be introduced to sociological and legal issues in policy implementation in general (such as Sarbanes Oxley, HIPAA, Gramm, Leach, Bliley Act, etc.) and will be provided with a focused dialogue on information security specific policies. The course also discusses the entire lifecycle of policy creation and enactment and presents students with issues specific policies in different domains of security. The structure of policy is also discussed to assist the students in the design and modification of policies. Moreover, Students will learn how to allocate the appropriate security techniques needed to satisfy a specific security policy. Several examples from different domains are incorporated in the curriculum to assist students to learn in context of real life situations
Security Policy, Laws, and Governance (ISEC422) > Credit Hours : 3

Security Policy, Laws, and Governance (ISEC422) > Prerequisites
ITBP370 with a minimum grade D

ISEC421 with a minimum grade D
Security Policy, Laws, and Governance (ISEC422) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze Designing Issues Pertaining To Information Security Policies

Apply Principles And Philosophies Which Underlie Successful Information Security Governance

Discuss Interactions Between Information Security Concerns And Business Objectives.

Evaluate Information Security Activities Within The Implementation Of Projects

Investigate Sociological And Legal Issues In Policy Implementations

ISEC423.title: UAEU Catalog — ISEC423 Systems Security Lab
ISEC423.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISEC423
This laboratory course provides practical training and hands-on experience on the basic Computer Systems Security concepts as it pertains to the logical and physical security. It will expose the students to various security principles of trusted computing bases. Main topics include Operating System Security, Access Control Models, Password Cracking, Computer Viruses, Windows Registry Hacks, Computer Viruses, Web Security, Biometrics Solutions, and Digital Forensics.
Systems Security Lab (ISEC423) > Credit Hours : 1

Systems Security Lab (ISEC423) > Corequisites
ISEC413 with a minimum grade D
Systems Security Lab (ISEC423) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Configure biometric security systems.

Design active response security architectures.

Evaluate operating systems security aspects .

Implement lattice-based access control model.

Use digital forensics hardware and software tools

ISEC424.title: UAEU Catalog — ISEC424 Hardware-Oriented Security and Trust
ISEC424.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISEC424
This course will investigate recent technology developments for the design and evaluation of secure and trustworthy hardware. It also teaches the concepts of tamper-proof, tamper-resistance, and trusted platform modules. Topics covered mainly include: Smart cards, RFIDs, cryptographic processor and processing overhead analysis, physical and invasive attacks, side-channel attacks, physically unclonable functions, hardware-based true random number generators, watermarking of Intellectual Property (IP) blocks, FPGA security, passive and active metering for prevention of piracy, access control, hardware Trojan detection and isolation
Hardware-Oriented Security and Trust (ISEC424) > Credit Hours : 3

Hardware-Oriented Security and Trust (ISEC424) > Prerequisites
ISEC413 with a minimum grade D
Hardware-Oriented Security and Trust (ISEC424) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze attacks on hardware systems

Apply detection, prevention and isolation methods against hardware attacks

Assess vulnerabilities of a hardware device or ystem

Evaluate security and trust of hardware systems

Integrate hardware security measures as a design metric

ISEC428.title: UAEU Catalog — ISEC428 Special Topics in Information Security
ISEC428.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISEC428
The course focuses on selected topics pertained to current information security solutions and methodologies. The course represents an in-depth approach to specific areas in information security which are of interest to undergraduate students in the program. It covers topics in computer, network, and systems security and privacy which are not covered as part of required courses. Students will learn to apply existing security techniques and methodologies to emerging systems and networks, derive and enumerate best practices for the selected topics and evaluate chosen security schemes.
Special Topics in Information Security (ISEC428) > Credit Hours : 3

Special Topics in Information Security (ISEC428) > Prerequisites
ITBP301 with a minimum grade D

ISEC322 with a minimum grade D
Special Topics in Information Security (ISEC428) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate options for a needed security solution.

Compare various security mechanisms.

Apply current security solutions to address certain requirements.

Analyze the performance of applied security solutions.

ISEC755.title: UAEU Catalog — ISEC755 Advanced Systems and Data Security.
ISEC755.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ISEC755
The goal of this course is to introduce students to the computational technologies for ensuring systems and data security. The main topics include security architecture, operating systems security, security issues in database systems, privacy preserving data mining, secure computations on distributed data, and secure data outsourcing. The foundations are drawn from a number of sub-disciplines of Computer Science including: database systems, data mining, algorithms, cryptography, and computer security.
Advanced Systems and Data Security. (ISEC755) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Systems and Data Security. (ISEC755) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss policies and best practices in the context of system and data security.

Evaluate system security vulnerabilities and data protection techniques.

Develop secure computing solutions.

Create scientific reports.

ITBP218.title: UAEU Catalog — ITBP218 Entrepreneurship and New Venture Creation in IT
ITBP218.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ITBP218
This course explores key entrepreneurial concepts relevant to starting a new IT venture. Technical students are taught to be business minded in today’s high technology world and guided through how to take ideas to real products. Topics include identifying innovative IT venture opportunities, the entrepreneurial process and perspective, customer discovery, market research, start-up strategies, business idea evaluation, introduction to entrepreneurial finance and venture capital, risks and returns management, and drafting a business plan. Students undertake study of actual business situations through case-studies. The final outcome will be a group report in the form of a business plan, and a presentation.
Entrepreneurship and New Venture Creation in IT (ITBP218) > Credit Hours : 3

Entrepreneurship and New Venture Creation in IT (ITBP218) > Prerequisites
ITBP280 with a minimum grade D
Entrepreneurship and New Venture Creation in IT (ITBP218) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the role and skills of an entrepreneur and cultivate an entrepreneurial mindset.

Outline the process followed by an entrepreneur in selecting a valuable opportunity

Explain the principles and success factors of IT venture planning

Contrast the key legal and intellectual property issues in planning IT ventures

Demonstrate a business model and financial plan for an IT venture

ITBP270.title: UAEU Catalog — ITBP270 Professional Responsibility in Information Technology
ITBP270.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ITBP270
This course delves into the ethics of information technology in the age of artificial intelligence (AI). It addresses crucial topics, including the responsibilities of IT professionals, privacy, security, freedom of expression, and intellectual property. Students will investigate the impact of computing on both employees and organizations within the workplace, as well as its influence on online communities and the digital divide. The course also explores ethical decision-making and emerging technologies, including AI, through case studies.
Professional Responsibility in Information Technology (ITBP270) > Credit Hours : 2

Professional Responsibility in Information Technology (ITBP270) > Prerequisites
GEAE101 with a minimum grade D
Professional Responsibility in Information Technology (ITBP270) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze issues and case studies using ethical decision-making based on a code of ethics and formal methods.

Review privacy, computer and Internet crimes, intellectual property, and software development issues.

Explore the socio-economic implications of online communities and the Digital Divide.

Examine the new ethical issues with emerging technologies, including AI.

ITBP280.title: UAEU Catalog — ITBP280 Information Technology Project Management Exhibition
ITBP280.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ITBP280
This course provides concepts, tools and models built along the IT project management life cycle. It covers detailed topics of IT project management, including project planning, project governance, project procurement management, project time management, project cost management, project risk management, project quality management, leadership and ethics, project closure and evaluation. Application of IT project management skills for an IT project is an important part of this course.
Information Technology Project Management Exhibition (ITBP280) > Credit Hours : 3

Information Technology Project Management Exhibition (ITBP280) > Prerequisites
CSBP219 with a minimum grade D
Information Technology Project Management Exhibition (ITBP280) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply IT project techniques and tools to manage an IT project.

Apply project lifecycle processes to an IT project.

Demonstrate verbal, and written communication skills as part of a team.

Identify internal and external constraints of a given IT project.

Produce documents typically used in the development of an IT Project.

ITBP301.title: UAEU Catalog — ITBP301 Security Principles & Practice
ITBP301.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ITBP301
This course provides an overview of information security. It is designed to help students understand this important priority in society today. The content of the course gives a broad overview of essential concepts and methods for providing and evaluating security in information processing systems (e.g. operating systems and applications, networks, protocols). The course will be organized around a few themes: foundations (security mindset, essential concepts: e.g. policy, CIA), authentication and access control, software security (e.g. vulnerabilities and protections, malware, program analysis), practical cryptography (e.g. encryption, authentication, hashing, symmetric and asymmetric crypto), networks (e.g. wired and wireless networks, protocols, attacks and countermeasures).
Security Principles & Practice (ITBP301) > Credit Hours : 3

Security Principles & Practice (ITBP301) > Prerequisites
CENG210 with a minimum grade D
Security Principles & Practice (ITBP301) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze security threats and vulnerabilities in computer systems.

Define solutions to defend against viruses and other malicious programs.

Describe cryptographic techniques and their applications.

Discuss operating system security models and mechanisms.

Explain security policies, models, and mechanisms.

ITBP321.title: UAEU Catalog — ITBP321 Web Application Development Lab
ITBP321.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ITBP321
The objective of this lab is to provide a hands-on approach to the creation of a Web based application while ensuring the participants are involved in the different stages of a software project lifecycle. The lab formally introduces the fundamentals of using SQL to create a database back-end and tie it to a Web front-end using HTML, JSP and Servlets. The lab also includes a project where students use the acquired Web development knowledge to design and implement a functional Web application. Students work in teams to collaborate in developing the assigned software project
Web Application Development Lab (ITBP321) > Credit Hours : 1

Web Application Development Lab (ITBP321) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co CSBP340 with a minimum grade D
Web Application Development Lab (ITBP321) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply emerging technologies to build web-based applications.

Create database using MYSQL and write SQL quires to add, display, or delete data from database.

Develop internet-based applications using client-side and server-side programming.

Use HTML, servlet and JSP to connect and query databases.

ITBP322.title: UAEU Catalog — ITBP322 Web and Mobile Systems
ITBP322.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ITBP322
This course introduces the concepts, practices, and technologies to design, develop, and manage web and mobile applications. It covers different technologies related to the Web such as HTML5, Cascade Style Sheets (CSS), and Java Script Pages (JSP). The course establishes mobile development foundation, which includes mobile layouts, handlers, and views. It also covers Mobile Development and relevant Internet development approaches and architectures such as Model-View-Controller (MVC), relational databases and restful services. Students develop web/mobile-enabled databases in project-based assignments
Web and Mobile Systems (ITBP322) > Credit Hours : 3

Web and Mobile Systems (ITBP322) > Prerequisites
CSBP219 with a minimum grade D
Web and Mobile Systems (ITBP322) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Design a web site for mobile application (E-learning, E-health, E-Business…) using specific technologies

Design mobile application (M-learning, M-health, M-Business, U-learning.. (U ubiquitous))

Explain the layers based approach to design web and mobile (E, M and U) system.

ITBP323.title: UAEU Catalog — ITBP323 Systems Integration and Administration
ITBP323.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ITBP323
This course will provide students with the knowledge and tools needed to plan, manage and administer network systems hardware and software resources of an enterprise. Topics include, approaches to system integration, performance monitoring and backup strategy, active directories, control users’ access and privileges, troubleshooting for errors and misuse, network services and management, server management, Virtual Machines, user/client administration and services, heterogeneous operating system environment (Linux, Windows ...ect.).
Systems Integration and Administration (ITBP323) > Credit Hours : 3

Systems Integration and Administration (ITBP323) > Prerequisites
CSBP315 with a minimum grade D
Systems Integration and Administration (ITBP323) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss systems integration approaches.

Discuss Virtual Machines in the context of different operating systems.

Configure users, group accounts, and access policies.

Manage servers, files and system resources.

Apply remote access methodologies to manage network devices, servers, and client computers.

Apply troubleshooting of both systems and networks for error, performance and connectivity.

ITBP324.title: UAEU Catalog — ITBP324 Cloud Computing Fundamentals
ITBP324.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ITBP324
This course introduces the concepts, practices and technologies to develop, deploy and manage Cloud computing applications, allows the students to learn and practice the web as the portal to Cloud, including a detailed overview of Web protocols, to learn and practice virtualization and its use and benefits for cloud computing, scheduling of cloud computing loads where issues related to execution time versus bandwidth and load balancing will be examined, distributed data center file systems and technologies, as well as security and privacy issues.
Cloud Computing Fundamentals (ITBP324) > Credit Hours : 3

Cloud Computing Fundamentals (ITBP324) > Prerequisites
CSBP219 with a minimum grade D
Cloud Computing Fundamentals (ITBP324) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop cloud computing application;

Define cloud service in different area ( X as a service);

Design mobile application as a service using cloud computing technology (M-learning, M-health, M-Business, U-learning.. (U ubiquitous));

Specification of cloud computing application using cloudsim.

ITBP410.title: UAEU Catalog — ITBP410 The Internet of Things
ITBP410.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ITBP410
The course covers the significance of Internet of Things (IoT) in society, the common components IoT devices and the future trends. Design considerations for IoT devices and systems and the constraints are also discussed. The interfacing among the IoT devices and the physical world are covered. The course also covers operating systems for IoT. Additionally, the course goes over the major components of networking from the IoT perspective, i.e., Internet-connectivity, mobile adhoc networks, etc. Other topics as they related to IoT are: big data and analytics, edge and cloud computing, and security and privacy. Practical implementation of core IoT concepts is included in the course.
The Internet of Things (ITBP410) > Credit Hours : 3

The Internet of Things (ITBP410) > Prerequisites
CENG530 with a minimum grade D
The Internet of Things (ITBP410) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain IoT, its impact on society and the related technology trends.

Evaluate the components of an IoT embedded system.

Evaluate the interactions of an IoT device with the physical world.

Build an IoT system.

Explain mobile adhoc networks and their relation to IoT devices.

ITBP420.title: UAEU Catalog — ITBP420 Data Analytics
ITBP420.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ITBP420
This course will introduce the students to the main tools and ideas of data analytics. The course will give an overview of the data, questions, and tools that data analysts and data scientists work with. There are two components to this course. The first is a conceptual introduction to the ideas behind turning data into actionable knowledge, which includes exploratory data analysis, statistical inference, regression models, and overview of machine learning. The second is a practical introduction to the tools that will be used in the program like R, and RStudio
Data Analytics (ITBP420) > Credit Hours : 3

Data Analytics (ITBP420) > Prerequisites
CSBP320 with a minimum grade D
Data Analytics (ITBP420) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe different mechanisms of data science

Compare different approaches for data analytics

Design a data analytics solution for a real world problem

Apply different data analytics tools

ITBP421.title: UAEU Catalog — ITBP421 Big Data Analytics
ITBP421.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ITBP421
This course will enrich knowledge of data science by understanding the challenges of Big Data in Analytics. It will introduce the core concepts behind big data problems, applications, and systems. It will provide an introduction to one of the most common frameworks, Hadoop. This course will give an overview architectural components and programming models used for scalable big data analysis. It will also introduce concepts of big data management systems and machine learning with big data.
Big Data Analytics (ITBP421) > Credit Hours : 3

Big Data Analytics (ITBP421) > Prerequisites
ITBP420 with a minimum grade D
Big Data Analytics (ITBP421) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the theory, concepts and challenges in Big Data Analytics.

Analyze different Cloud Computing Techniques for Big Data.

Design efficient and scalable applications for Big Data Analytics.

Compare different Techniques on a given Big Data Analytics problem.

Assess challenges and opportunities of Big Data Analytics for various applications.

ITBP430.title: UAEU Catalog — ITBP430 Mobile Computing
ITBP430.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ITBP430
Mobile computing devices have become omnipresent in our daily activities. This course will introduce students to mobile computing and mobile application development. Mobile computing will be discussed from three perspectives: mobile technology, application development, and user interaction. The course will first overview various mobile computing applications, technologies and wireless communication. Next, students will be introduced to and use mobile application frameworks and development environments. User interface and user experience will be discussed and application development guidelines from various vendors will be discussed and analyzed. Students will be expected to learn at least one mobile application development framework and use it to implement their assignments and course project.
Mobile Computing (ITBP430) > Credit Hours : 3

Mobile Computing (ITBP430) > Prerequisites
ITBP322 with a minimum grade D
Mobile Computing (ITBP430) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain mobile computing concepts and principles.

Design a simple mobile application for hand held devices.

Compare current mobile platforms and their architectures.

Develop applications on a mobile computing system to interact with servers and database systems.

ITBP480.title: UAEU Catalog — ITBP480 Senior Graduation Project I
ITBP480.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ITBP480
Supervised students in small groups undertake full end-to-end development of a substantial project plan, taking it from initial concept through the final delivery. Topics range from applied IT development to assignment on applied research. Students are expected to: complete literature survey; develop a project plan; analyze requirements and acquire the necessary material and steps for their intended project.
Senior Graduation Project I (ITBP480) > Credit Hours : 3

Senior Graduation Project I (ITBP480) > Prerequisites
STAT210 with a minimum grade D
Senior Graduation Project I (ITBP480) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze project requirements

Communicate effectively both orally and in writing

Create an effective project plan

Function effectively, professionally and ethically on teams

Integrate IT technologies/principles into the project design

Undertake a survey of related work and evaluate the project objectives against the findings

ITBP481.title: UAEU Catalog — ITBP481 Senior Graduation Project II
ITBP481.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ITBP481
Students work in teams under the supervision of a faculty member on the implementation, testing and analysis of the results of a project based on the design and schedule completed by the same group of students during the Senior Graduation Project I course
Senior Graduation Project II (ITBP481) > Credit Hours : 3

Senior Graduation Project II (ITBP481) > Prerequisites
ITBP480 with a minimum grade D
Senior Graduation Project II (ITBP481) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze obtained results and make recommendations

Apply enabling technologies/principles to implement the project

Communicate effectively both orally and in writing

Function effectively, professionally and ethically on teams

Recognize the need for continuing professional development

ITBP496.title: UAEU Catalog — ITBP496 Internship
ITBP496.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ITBP496
Students are required to spend one full semester as interns in an approved internship program. The internship provides students with practical experience, which allows them to integrate theory with “real world” situations. ITPG708.text:

ITPG720.title: UAEU Catalog — ITPG720 Numerical Optimization Methods
ITPG720.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ITPG720
This course intends to provide the students with a thorough understanding of numerical optimization methods. This course will cover topics related to unconstrained and constrained optimization, convex optimization and non-convex optimization. The course will also cover derivative-free optimization algorithms and discrete optimization algorithms. Heuristic strategies for optimization will also be covered. Topics include line-search method, trust-region method, conjugate gradient methods, linear programming, the simplex method, duality, interior point methods, quadratic programming, active set methods, gradient projection methods, non-convex stochastic gradient descent, random stochastic gradient descent, discrete optimization algorithms, global search methods and local search methods for derivative-free optimization.
Numerical Optimization Methods (ITPG720) > Credit Hours : 3

Numerical Optimization Methods (ITPG720) > Course Learning Outcomes

Formulate an optimization problem for a problem in their fields of research.

Develop solutions for constrained and non-constrained optimization by applying appropriate algorithms.

Utilize convex and non-convex optimization methods.

Apply gradient-free and discrete optimization algorithms.

Describe the limitations of modern optimization techniques.

ITPG810.text:

Upon passing the comprehensive examination, a PhD student is required to prepare a concise and complete Research Proposal that clearly defines the research problem and objectives, and outlines the research methodology that the student plans to follow. The proposal’s content and format must follow the PhD Research Proposal Preparation Guidelines issued by the College of Graduate Studies. The proposal should be completed under the direction of the student’s supervisor and must be approved by the Advisory Committee. Research Proposals are examined by a committee composed of the student’s advisor, and two other Internal examiners in the field of the student research.

ITPG800

ITPG850.title: UAEU Catalog — ITPG850 Comprehensive Exam and Research Proposal
ITPG850.text:

The Comprehensive Examination and Research Proposal (CERP) for the PhD in Informatics and Computing is a non-credit Pass/Fail exam. Students have up to two trials to pass the CERP; upon passing the exam, the student becomes a PhD candidate. The CERP is structured to evaluate the student’s breadth and depth of fundamental knowledge in the area(s) closely related to the thesis work. The CERP committee, in consultation with the advisor, decides on the topic(s) of the CERP. The PhD student prepares a concise and comprehensive research proposal that clearly defines the research problem and objectives and outlines the research methodology that he/she plans to follow. The concerned PhD student should present and defend his/her proposal in front of the CERP committee.

Demonstrate sufficient communication skills relevant to field of study and the research topic.

ITPG910.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=ITPG910
Student defends his/her research dissertation in the form of an oral presentation in a public session, followed by a closed session, before a Dissertation Examination Committee, which includes internal and external examiners. The outcome of the overall evaluation of the dissertation is based on two main parts: (1) the Committee’s evaluation of the dissertation document and (2) the Committee’s evaluation of the dissertation defense. The final result shall be one of the following: (1) Approve dissertation as presented, (2) Approved with minor revisions, (3) Re-examine after making major revisions, or (4) Rejection of dissertation and dismissal.
Dissertation Defense (ITPG910) > Credit Hours : 0

This course covers the main information security concepts. It provides students with an in-depth-knowledge of the main security issues, and solutions, that face IT Systems today. The course will cover topics that include but not limited to: cryptography and cryptographic protocols, public key infrastructure, operating systems security, authentication and access control technologies and models. Network security and internet security protocols, database security, wireless network vulnerabilities and countermeasures, firewalls, VPN, and intrusion detection/prevention systems.

Analyze Security Policies, Procedures, Models, And Mechanisms.

Evaluate Cryptographic Techniques And Applications.

Evaluate Database Security Issues

Investigate Operating System Security Models And Mechanisms.

SECB622.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=SECB622
This course provides an understanding of advanced network security theoretical concepts, mechanisms, and solutions with emphasis on wired and wireless network architectures, using firewalls, intrusion prevention systems, virtual private networks (VPN), access control lists and protocols. Topics include also anomalies, analysis of network filtering rules, advanced attack signature generation, common attacks mechanisms, covert channels and steganography concepts, operating system fingerprinting, viruses, and malicious codes
Advanced Network Security (SECB622) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Network Security (SECB622) > Course Learning Outcomes

Build network firewall, VPN, and IPS based secure systems.

Develop advanced firewall-filtering rules and attack signatures.

Evaluate appropriate security solutions for different types of network architectures

Investigate system security auditing and Vulnerabilities.

SECB623.title: UAEU Catalog — SECB623 Cryptography and Secure Communications
SECB623.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=SECB623
The students in this course will be introduced to various encryption techniques, their applications and weaknesses. The main encryption techniques the students will learn and apply in this course are Symmetric encryption, Public-key encryption, and hash functions. These techniques will be used for digital signatures, certificate generation and verification. In addition, the required mathematical concepts for information security will be discussed. The performance of the various encryption techniques used will be analyzed based on certain criteria and design needs.
Cryptography and Secure Communications (SECB623) > Credit Hours : 3

Cryptography and Secure Communications (SECB623) > Course Learning Outcomes

Apply Hash Function Algorithms.

Discuss Contemporary Cryptography, Its Application And Weaknesses.

Evaluate Various Cryptographic Techniques.

Investigate The Mathematical Concepts Required For Cryptographic Algorithms.

SECB624.title: UAEU Catalog — SECB624 Software Security
SECB624.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=SECB624
This course provides deep understanding of security vulnerabilities of software, operating systems, and web applications. Common cases of vulnerability exploitations followed by mitigation techniques of these exploitations are discussed. Topics include common security vulnerabilities in software (e.g. buffer overflow, format string bug) and web application (e.g. SQL injection, cross-site scripting), vulnerability databases, malicious code analysis (virus, worm, rootkit), social engineering attacks, and vulnerability detection in software and web applications (security testing, static analysis, penetration testing, web scanner). Additional topics discussed include fundamental security concepts present in operating systems (access control, process, memory), examples of security breach mitigation techniques in operating systems (system log analysis, memory randomization, malicious code monitor).
Software Security (SECB624) > Credit Hours : 3

Software Security (SECB624) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze Security Threats And Vulnerabilities In Software.

Compare Software Security Analysis And Testing Tools And Techniques.

Demonstrate Secure Software Design And Development Techniques To Mitigate Vulnerabilities.

Evaluate Operating Systems Based On Security Risks And Defense Mechanisms.

Investigate Web Application Vulnerabilities And Countermeasures.

SECB626.title: UAEU Catalog — SECB626 Secure Electronic Commerce
SECB626.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=SECB626
This course investigates theoretical security problems related to protocols and applications of the Internet and electronic commerce and provides contemporary solutions to these problems. The focus of this course is on architectures and the implementations of security protocols that are used on the Internet today. Topics include: cryptography techniques; Authentication applications; Public-key Infrastructure and Digital Certificates; Email Security: PGP, S/MIME; Web security: SSL/TLS, SET; IPSec; Digital Cash. The course also includes case studies in application of security technology in electronic commerce.
Secure Electronic Commerce (SECB626) > Credit Hours : 3

Secure Electronic Commerce (SECB626) > Course Learning Outcomes

Demonstrate How Security Protocols Are Used To Achieve Internet And E-Commerce Security.

SECB627.title: UAEU Catalog — SECB627 Ethics, Law and Policy in Cyberspace
SECB627.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=SECB627
This course provides students with the information needed for the creation, selection and implementation of cyber security policies, and audit and control functions to ensure compliance and efficacy. In this course, students will be exposed to the national and international policy and legal considerations related to cybersecurity such as privacy, intellectual property, cybercrime., homeland security and cyberwarfare. Broader technology issues such as system evolution standards (ISO & Common Criteria) also are discussed to ensure compliance and to demonstrate the interdisciplinary influences and concerns that must be addressed in developing or implementing effective national cybersecurity laws and policies.
Ethics, Law and Policy in Cyberspace (SECB627) > Credit Hours : 3

Develop security policies, procedures and guideline.

SECB628.title: UAEU Catalog — SECB628 Computer Crimes and Forensics
SECB628.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2931.shtml?id=SECB628
This course is designed to equip students with the theoretical knowledge and practical skills needed to safely locate and secure computer evidence at the search site as well as to conduct subsequent off-site analysis. The course aims to equip future Forensics Investigators and Lawful Enforcement Officers with sufficient theoretical and practical knowledge on conducting investigation on Internet based or Cyber based crime. It provides knowledge on implementing the right solution for collecting, analyzing, correlating the Internet data and report them as valid and legal evidence in the court. Topics include evidence handling and disk imaging (restore evidence drive, system backup imaging), Windows forensics utilities, Access Data’s forensics tool kit, hidden data and encryption, steganography, covert channel, erased file recovery, Internet investigations, Hacker profile analysis, and Email header analysis.
Computer Crimes and Forensics (SECB628) > Credit Hours : 3

Computer Crimes and Forensics (SECB628) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze Concepts Of Computer Digital Forensics.

Assess Concepts Of Computer Crimes.

Conduct Software And Hardware Based Digital Forensic Investigations.

Evaluate Current Computer Digital Forensics Tools.

Investigate Web And Cloud Based Digital Forensic Tools.
