Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2943.shtml?id=MATH772
Initial Value Problem: Existence and Uniqueness of Solutions; Continuation of Solutions; Continuous and Differential Dependence of Solutions. Linear Systems: Linear Homogeneous And Nonhomogeneous Systems with Constant and Variable Coefficients; Structure of Solutions of Systems with Constant and Periodic Coefficients; Higher Order Linear Differential Equations; Sturmian Theory, Stability: Lyapunov Stability and Instability. Lyapunov Functions; Lyapunov's Second Method; Quasilinear Systems; Linearization; Stability of an Equilibrium and Stable Manifold Theorem for Nonautonomous Differential Equations.
Theory of Ordinary Differential Equations (MATH772) > Credit Hours : 3

Theory of Ordinary Differential Equations (MATH772) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe The Concept Of Stability Of Solutions Of Differential Equations Of Higher Orders And Systems.

Explain The Concepts Of Equilibrium And Stable Manifolds And Their Role In Stability Of Solutions Of Ode’S.

Prove The Existence And Uniqueness Of Solutions Of Certain Class Of Ordinary Differential Equations.

Solve Systems Of Differential Equations Of Different Types.

Use Available Software To Solve Differential Equations And Systems Of Differential Equations.

MATH773.title: UAEU Catalog — MATH773 Dynamical Systems and chaos theory
MATH773.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2943.shtml?id=MATH773
Discrete time dynamical systems. Continuous time dynamical systems. Invariant manifolds, homoclinic orbits, local and global bifurcations. Hamiltonian systems, completely integrable systems, KAM theory. Different mechanisms for chaotic dynamics, symbolic dynamics. Applications in physics, biology and economics.
Dynamical Systems and chaos theory (MATH773) > Credit Hours : 3

Dynamical Systems and chaos theory (MATH773) > Prerequisites
MATH275 with a minimum grade D
Dynamical Systems and chaos theory (MATH773) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Locate and analyse the stability of fixed points and periodic orbits of maps and flows

Identify commonly encountered local and global bifurcations.

Understand the basic notions of chaotic behaviour for maps and flows.

Define integrability of Hamiltonian systems, and give a qualitative and semi-quantitative analysis of perturbed integrable dynamics.

Identify applications of each of the main classes of dynamical systems, stating features of their long time behaviour.

MATH774.title: UAEU Catalog — MATH774 Stochastic Calculus for Finance
MATH774.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2943.shtml?id=MATH774
Stochastic process; Brownian motion; Martingales; Ito's integral; Ito's formula; Stochastic differential equations; Geometric Brownian motion; Arbitrage and SDEs; The diffusion equation; Representation theorems; Risk-neutral measures, Change of measure and Girsanov’s theorem; Arbitrage and martingales; The Feynman-Kac connection.
Stochastic Calculus for Finance (MATH774) > Credit Hours : 3

Stochastic Calculus for Finance (MATH774) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Manipulate continuous stochastic processes such as Brownian motion.

Solve different kinds of stochastic differential equations.

Develop pricing formulas for some financial derivatives using Ito formula and representation and Girsanov theorems.

Construct PDEs for some financial derivatives prices using Feynman-Kac theorem.

MATH777.title: UAEU Catalog — MATH777 Numerical Methods for Finance
MATH777.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2943.shtml?id=MATH777
Numerical differentiation (Forward, Backward, central), Measuring the error, Numerical instability, Finite difference methods, Monte-Carlo methods, the Euler-Maruyama and Milstein's higher order methods for Stochastic Differential Equations. Applications to finance such as the simulation of asset prices, Monte Carlo Evaluation of European options, numerical solution for the Black-Scholes PDE.
Numerical Methods for Finance (MATH777) > Credit Hours : 3

Numerical Methods for Finance (MATH777) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Construct numerical simulations for SDEs.

Evaluate options using the Monte Carlo method.

Solve options pricing PDEs using the finite difference methods.

Develop solutions for derivative price using transform techniques.

Formulate calibration problems to estimate financial asset model parameters.

MATH795.title: UAEU Catalog — MATH795 Independent Studies
MATH795.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2943.shtml?id=MATH795
Graduate students will study topics related to their MSc. thesis independently. The selection of these topics will be with the consent of advisor.
Independent Studies (MATH795) > Credit Hours : 3

Independent Studies (MATH795) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Acquire an understanding of the studied topics.

Demonstrate familiarity with the concepts and tools of the studied topics

Be proficient in expressing clear and accurate mathematical proofs in exploring the properties of the studied Mathematical objects.

AERO215.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO215 Thermofluids
AERO215.text:
This course aims to provide students with essential understanding of the concepts of applied thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, and heat transfer. Topics covered include: Second law of thermodynamics analysis, gas power cycles, basics of compressible flows, momentum equation for finite control volumes, Bernoulli equation, Basic heat transfer by conduction and radiation.
Thermofluids (AERO215) > Credit Hours : 3

Thermofluids (AERO215) > Prerequisites
GENG220 with a minimum grade D
Thermofluids (AERO215) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply the first and second laws of thermodynamics to analyze gas power cycles.

Explain the basics of compressible flows and shock waves.

Describe fluid properties, the conservation of mass, momentum and energy, and Bernoulli equation.

Analyze flow inside a pipe and external flow forces (lift and drag).

Apply steady conduction, convection, and basic radiation heat transfer modes.

Demonstrate ability to communicate effectively.

AERO220.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO220 Aerospace Lab 1
AERO220.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO220
This lab course is an Introduction to lab equipment and safety, an introduction to techniques for engineering measurement, estimation of measurement uncertainty, error analysis, data acquisition, calibration, post processing using computational packages. Basic skills for engineering research are taught, which include: analog electronic circuit analysis, fundamentals of digital data acquisition, measurements of physical quantities related to aerospace engineering: pressure, temperature, flow rate, heat transfer, and static forces and moments.
Aerospace Lab 1 (AERO220) > Credit Hours : 1

Aerospace Lab 1 (AERO220) > Prerequisites
PHYS140 with a minimum grade D
Aerospace Lab 1 (AERO220) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognize measurements uncertainty estimation and error analysis.

Demonstrate the ability to follow experimental procedures.

Utilize transducers to measure physical phenomena such as: velocity, temperature flow rate, pressure drop, forces.

Analyze measured data using computational packages.

Evaluate the validity of experimental results.

AERO280.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO280 Space Mechanics
AERO280.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO280
This course introduces students to the fundamentals of space mechanics, with key topics including the two-body problem, Keplerian orbits, orbital maneuvers, coordinate transformations, interplanetary trajectories, orbital perturbations, ground tracks, and spacecraft mission analysis. Emphasis is placed on both theoretical understanding and practical engineering applications, including simulation and analysis using standard tools such as MATLAB.
Space Mechanics (AERO280) > Credit Hours : 3

Space Mechanics (AERO280) > Prerequisites
MATH275 with a minimum grade D
Space Mechanics (AERO280) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the two-body problem in space.

Discuss various types of orbits and coordinate systems used in aerospace engineering.

Analyze different satellite orbital maneuvers and interplanetary missions.

Identify orbital perturbations, including atmospheric drag and gravitational effects.

Simulate spacecraft orbits using MATLAB.

AERO300.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO300 Aerodynamics 1
AERO300.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO300
Aerodynamic forces & moments; classification of aerodynamic flows, governing equations for aerodynamic flows, elementary potential flows and superposition principle, Aerodynamics of airfoils, introduction to supersonic flows, Boundary layer. Introduction to low speed wind tunnels and testing, and an introduction to CFD methods.
Aerodynamics 1 (AERO300) > Credit Hours : 3

Aerodynamics 1 (AERO300) > Prerequisites
AERO215 with a minimum grade D

MATH210 with a minimum grade D
Aerodynamics 1 (AERO300) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Define the principles of aerodynamic flows, governing equations, potential flows, and the superposition principle.

Evaluate airfoils and finite wings using aerodynamic principles.

Analyze boundary layer behavior in viscous flows.

Identify low-speed wind tunnel types, testing techniques, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) methods.

Demonstrate professional and ethical responsibility and effective teamwork in aerospace engineering.

AERO301.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO301 Aircraft Operations and Flight Mechanics
AERO301.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO301
This course lays down the fundamentals of aeronautical engineering. It introduces a wide range of backgrounds to the basic concepts of aircraft aerodynamics, flight performance theory and practice, aircraft operations, flight mechanics, accelerated flight, and it introduces the concept of stability in particular longitudinal stability.
Aircraft Operations and Flight Mechanics (AERO301) > Credit Hours : 3

Aircraft Operations and Flight Mechanics (AERO301) > Prerequisites
AERO215 with a minimum grade D or ( MECH340 with a minimum grade D and MECH311 with a minimum grade D)
Aircraft Operations and Flight Mechanics (AERO301) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the various aspects associated with aircraft operation.

Apply basic aerodynamic principles to analyze the aerodynamic characteristics of idealized representations of aircraft components and systems.

Analyze the forces and moments acting on the aircraft

Formulate aircraft flight mechanics equations

Analyze the flight performance of aircraft in different situations

Evaluate the static stability of fixed wing aircraft for different flight conditions

Identify the differences between different aircraft configurations and how they impact performance and stability

AERO305.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO305 Aircraft Propulsion
AERO305.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO305
Study of the aero-and thermodynamics of jet and liquid and solid rocket engines. Air-breathing engines as propulsion systems. Turbojets, turbofans, turboprops, ramjets. Aerodynamics of gas-turbine engine components, ideal cycle analysis, component performance, non-ideal cycle analysis. Rocket vehicle performance. Introduction to space propulsion.
Aircraft Propulsion (AERO305) > Credit Hours : 3

Aircraft Propulsion (AERO305) > Prerequisites
AERO215 with a minimum grade D or ( MECH340 with a minimum grade D and MECH311 with a minimum grade D)
Aircraft Propulsion (AERO305) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify air-breathing engines’ components

Analyze ideal and real propulsion engines including ideal ramjet, turbojet, and turbofan at system and component level

Recognize requirements and components of rocket propulsion systems

Demonstrate ability to communicate effectively

Decide professional and ethical responsibility as relevant to propulsion systems

Compose new knowledge in aerospace propulsion

AERO310.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO310 Aircraft Structures 1
AERO310.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO310
Review of concepts of stress (deformation, strain, displacement and equations of elasticity); Aircraft structural components; Airworthiness and airframe loads; Applications to aerospace structural elements. Shear flow in thin walled sections; Design of thin-walled multi-cell sections. Introduction to fracture mechanics and fatigue.
Aircraft Structures 1 (AERO310) > Credit Hours : 3

Aircraft Structures 1 (AERO310) > Prerequisites
MECH305 with a minimum grade D
Aircraft Structures 1 (AERO310) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply the fundamentals of linear elasticity

Explain the principles of stressed skin construction

Compute various airframe loads

Apply the fundamentals of fracture mechanics and fatigue to study cracked aircraft structural components.

Analyze open-section and closed-section thin–walled aircraft structures subject to bending, shear, and torsion loads.

Estimate the properties of laminated composite aircraft structures

Employ experimental stress analysis techniques to analyze aircraft structural components.

Mark the impact of advances in aircraft structures on environment, society and economy

AERO315.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO315 Aerospace Manufacturing Processes
AERO315.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO315
This course introduces students to the principal manufacturing processes using in aerospace engineering (metallic and composites). Furthermore, the fabrication and joining processes widely used in the manufacturing of aerospace engineering components will be covered.
Aerospace Manufacturing Processes (AERO315) > Credit Hours : 3

Aerospace Manufacturing Processes (AERO315) > Prerequisites
MECH390 with a minimum grade D
Aerospace Manufacturing Processes (AERO315) > Corequisites
MECH305 with a minimum grade D
Aerospace Manufacturing Processes (AERO315) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Illustrate different joining and assembly processes

Demonstrate several conventional and non-conventional and additive manufacturing processes.

Practice different composite manufacturing processes.

Solve problems related different manufacturing processes.

Evaluate suitability of a given manufacturing process for a given product or application.

Show the ability of self-study of recent topics in manufacturing processes.

Produce a well-structured report keeping the highest standard of ethics.

AERO350.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO350 Aerospace Lab 2
AERO350.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO350
The lab will include a number of experiments related to propulsion and thermofluids, low speed and high speed aerodynamics. Introducing the fundamental principles and concepts of thermodynamics and fluid dynamic systems. Developing the fundamental concepts of aerodynamics and provides a working knowledge for their application to the design of aircraft.
Aerospace Lab 2 (AERO350) > Credit Hours : 1

Aerospace Lab 2 (AERO350) > Prerequisites
AERO220 with a minimum grade D

AERO305 with a minimum grade D

AERO300 with a minimum grade D
Aerospace Lab 2 (AERO350) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Practice experimental studies in the area of aerodynamics, thermofluids, and propulsion

Analyze experiment results and errors

Operate experimental setups within a team

Demonstrate experimental analysis and results

AERO402.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO402 Aerodynamics 2
AERO402.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO402
Compressible flow, normal shock wave, oblique shock wave, hypersonic flow, linearized supersonic, numerical techniques for nonlinear supersonic flow, supersonic flow over wedges and cones, shock expansion theory, shock wave interactions and reflections, application to supersonic airfoils, introduction to finite element method and CFD.
Aerodynamics 2 (AERO402) > Credit Hours : 3

Aerodynamics 2 (AERO402) > Prerequisites
AERO300 with a minimum grade D
Aerodynamics 2 (AERO402) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Contrast fundamental Principles and formulations related to compressible flow.

Apply the principles to solve problems related to normal shock wave.

Solve problems related to oblique shock wave.

Analyze the formulations related hypersonic flow.

Apply the principles and formulations related Introduction to numerical techniques for nonlinear supersonic flow.

AERO411.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO411 Flight Dynamics, Stability and Control
AERO411.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO411
Introduction to the dynamics and control of atmospheric flight vehicles, aircraft coordinate systems, coordinate system transformations, inertial acceleration, aerodynamic forces and moments (stability derivatives), derivation of aircraft equations of motion EOM, linearization of EOM for a given trimmed flight condition, static stability in longitudinal and lateral-directional, small disturbance equations of unsteady motion, dynamics stability, flying and handling qualities and control of aircraft motions.
Flight Dynamics, Stability and Control (AERO411) > Credit Hours : 3

Flight Dynamics, Stability and Control (AERO411) > Prerequisites
MECH409 with a minimum grade D

AERO301 with a minimum grade D
Flight Dynamics, Stability and Control (AERO411) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe aircraft axes and nomenclature.

Analyze aircraft static longitudinal, lateral, and directional stability.

Formulate aircraft dynamic equations of motion.

Evaluate aircraft dynamic stability.

Interpret how stability and control characteristics influence aircraft flying and handling qualities under various flight conditions.

Apply advanced computational tools (e.g., MATLAB) to model and evaluate aircraft stability and control performance.

AERO450.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO450 Aerospace Lab 3
AERO450.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO450
The lab will include a number of experiments related to flight dynamics, stability, control and structures. It will also serve as a brief introduction to avionics. Laboratory experiments on using autopilots and controlling of multicopters, extracting stability and aerodynamic derivatives of model airplanes using the wind-tunnel, flight simulator, testing of aircraft structural components.
Aerospace Lab 3 (AERO450) > Credit Hours : 1

Aerospace Lab 3 (AERO450) > Prerequisites
AERO411 with a minimum grade D

AERO310 with a minimum grade D

AERO350 with a minimum grade D
Aerospace Lab 3 (AERO450) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognize the role of avionics and state-of-the-art electronics on aircraft

Judge the stability and control aspects of aircraft using the wind-tunnel and flight simulator

Illustrate preliminary structural testing of representative aircraft structures
Internship I (AERO485 )
Students spend 8 weeks on a full-time basis in an engineering or consulting office in the UAE or abroad to earn practical skills. This course aims at offering career exploration opportunities for students.
Internship I (AERO485 ) > Credit Hours : 1

Internship I (AERO485 ) > Prerequisites
CIVL240 with a minimum grade D

MATH275 with a minimum grade D

GENG220 with a minimum grade D

GENG215 with a minimum grade D

GENG230 with a minimum grade D

AERO220 with a minimum grade D

( MECH305 with a minimum grade D or MECH310 with a minimum grade D or AERO315 with a minimum grade D or AERO301 with a minimum grade D or MECH315 with a minimum grade D)
Internship I (AERO485 ) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Function effectively in multi-disciplinary teams and individually to achieve the planned tasks and goals.

Develop communication skills through oral and written presentations.

Evaluate different engineering situations and judgments based on ethical codes and professional responsibilities.

AERO490.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO490 Internship II
AERO490.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO490
Students spend 8 weeks on a full-time basis in an engineering or consulting office in the UAE or abroad to earn practical skills. This course aims at offering career exploration opportunities for students as well as opportunities to correlate their academic preparation to the reality of conducting professional practice, to interact effectively with others in practice, to develop professional skills and communicate effectively in the workplace and to gain true practical experience that is necessary for their future practice as engineers in their respective discipline after graduation.
Internship II (AERO490) > Credit Hours : 1

Internship II (AERO490) > Prerequisites
STAT210 with a minimum grade D

GENG315 with a minimum grade D

MECH305 with a minimum grade D

MECH310 with a minimum grade D

MECH315 with a minimum grade D

MECH350 with a minimum grade D

AERO301 with a minimum grade D

AERO300 with a minimum grade D

AERO315 with a minimum grade D

PHYS200 with a minimum grade D or MATH210 with a minimum grade D Pre/Co AERO485 with a minimum grade P
Internship II (AERO490) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Function effectively in multi-disciplinary teams and individually to achieve the planed tasks and goals.

Develop communication skills through oral and written presentations.

Evaluate different engineering situations and judgments based on ethical codes and professional responsibilities.

Propose ideas/solutions for real-life problems based on the learned knowledge.

AERO496.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO496 Aircraft Design
AERO496.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO496
The course allows student to experience the entire aircraft design process. Examines principles of aircraft configuration and design to meet given performance specifications, taking into account aerodynamic, stability and control, and flying quality considerations, as well as aerospace materials performance and selection. Includes preliminary design of the major elements of an aircraft. The course is complemented with laboratory sessions that involve using appropriate software tools to streamline the design process of the aircraft using the systems engineering approach. Also, the environmental considerations that influence the aircraft design will be discussed.
Aircraft Design (AERO496) > Credit Hours : 3

Aircraft Design (AERO496) > Corequisites
AERO411 with a minimum grade D
Aircraft Design (AERO496) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognize the aircraft design engineering process, as constrained by regulatory and certification requirements.

Analyze alternative aircraft design configurations and design choices.

Apply fundamental engineering analysis knowledge as part of an aircraft design process.

Evaluate conflicting technical objectives and find suitable compromises.

Apply teamwork skills for collaborative efforts to satisfy specifications with the appreciation of the contributions of other team members

Apply Ethical, social, environmental, economical, and sustainability requirements to Aircraft Design

Apply the entire process of aircraft design based on a systems engineering approach

AERO500.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO500 Computational Fluid Dynamics
AERO500.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO500
The course will equip the students with knowledge to use computational techniques to solve problems related to aerospace engineering. Particularly, students will have hands-on experience in using computational fluid dynamics to solve aerospace related problems. Governing equations, discretization schemes, numerical methods, mesh quality and independence test, numerical errors, and boundary conditions as related to solving Navier-Stokes equation and energy equation will be introduced in the course.
Computational Fluid Dynamics (AERO500) > Credit Hours : 3

Computational Fluid Dynamics (AERO500) > Prerequisites
AERO402 with a minimum grade D
Computational Fluid Dynamics (AERO500) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Build the most appropriate CFD model (in terms of boundary conditions, material properties, mesh settings, solution control parameters, grid-convergence, solution monitor, etc.) for the problem in hand

Compute fluid simulations related to steady-state and transient, isothermal and non-isothermal, incompressible and compressible, adiabatic and non-adiabatic multiphase flow, and fluid structure interactions

Use ANSYS Fluent to the standard acceptable for a graduate engineer

Select the required results and plots from the information available at the solution stage

AERO501.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO501 Selected Topics in Aerospace Engineering
AERO501.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO501
Selected topics that meet students' interests, faculty capabilities and available resources in the aerodynamics and flight mechanics area. More than one section of this course may be offered in any semester when different topics need to be covered.
Selected Topics in Aerospace Engineering (AERO501) > Credit Hours : 3

Selected Topics in Aerospace Engineering (AERO501) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate fundamental understanding of selected topics in aerodynamics and flight mechanics

Use engineering tools to solve practical problems arising in aerodynamics and flight mechanics area

Analyze engineering solutions for practical problems in aerodynamics and flight mechanics

AERO505.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO505 Spacecraft Propulsion
AERO505.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO505
This course considers the basic theory and principles of operation of chemical and electric propulsion systems for spacecraft. Both solid and liquid propellant chemical propulsion systems are considered, as is a variety of electric propulsion systems utilizing different propellant acceleration mechanisms. The course addresses propulsion manufacturing, testing, flight operations (orbit-raising and station-keeping), propellant life predictions, and final de-orbiting strategies at spacecraft end-of-life.
Spacecraft Propulsion (AERO505) > Credit Hours : 3

Spacecraft Propulsion (AERO505) > Prerequisites
AERO305 with a minimum grade D
Spacecraft Propulsion (AERO505) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze the design and operational behavior of various types of spacecraft propulsion systems.

Describe types of chemical propulsion systems, and evaluate their use for various different scenarios.

Describe types of electric propulsion systems, and evaluate their advantages and disadvantages.

Design a chemical propulsion system for a particular scenario, and evaluate the design

Explain the different propellant feed system options for both chemical and electric propulsion systems, and their similarities/differences.

Evaluate the factors that limit the performance of these different propellant feed systems

AERO506.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO506 Spacecraft Engineering Design
AERO506.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO506
This course integrates the design elements and fundamental analyses necessary to complete the conceptual design phase of an unmanned spacecraft. It will explore topics such as mission design, propulsion, power, structure, thermal, attitude control, communication, command, and data handling and attitude control systems. It will emphasis the role of project management and systems engineering throughout the design process.
Spacecraft Engineering Design (AERO506) > Credit Hours : 3

Spacecraft Engineering Design (AERO506) > Prerequisites
MATH275 with a minimum grade D
Spacecraft Engineering Design (AERO506) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze spacecraft missions and understand rationales behind design.

Define mission parameters, objectives and requirements.

Explain the functionality of spacecraft different subsystems

Conduct conceptual design and integration studies of an unmanned spacecraft to fulfil specified missions.

Identify key design drivers and critical issues for spacecraft missions.

Explain nature of past spaceflight failures and develop strategies for future missions

AERO511.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO511 Aircraft Structures 2
AERO511.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO511
This course introduces students to structural instability of columns and thin plates. Thin plate theory, Plate subject to pure bending and combined loading. Different analysis methods (Virtual work and energy and matrix methods including FEM) for stress and deflection calculations in determinant and indeterminate structures. Introduction to Composite materials analysis and design. Modelling and analysis of basic aircraft structural components in Ansys. The course includes a project where students design and build a small aircraft wing.
Aircraft Structures 2 (AERO511) > Credit Hours : 3

Aircraft Structures 2 (AERO511) > Prerequisites
AERO310 with a minimum grade D
Aircraft Structures 2 (AERO511) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Determine the effect of different loading and support conditions on the small deflection of columns and rectangular plates

Compute the buckling strength of columns and rectangular

Apply different analysis methods (Energy, Virtual Work, Matrix and FE) to study the behavior of simple structural components

Use finite element matrix analysis for simple bar and beam structures

Determine composite laminates strength and composite sections properties

Design an aircraft structural component

AERO515.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO515 Aviation Regulations and Certifications
AERO515.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO515
This course deals with civil aviation safety and formal processes that assure acceptable levels of flight safety. It provides an overview of the Civil Aviation Regulations (FAR and EASA). It focuses on Airworthiness, Airworthiness Certification Procedures, Aviation System Safety, Engineering Procedures Manuals, Flight Manual, Unmanned Aircraft Regulation, Product Development and Life Cycle Management, Quality Systems and Quality Management and Safety Management Systems.
Aviation Regulations and Certifications (AERO515) > Credit Hours : 3

Aviation Regulations and Certifications (AERO515) > Prerequisites
AERO200 with a minimum grade D
Aviation Regulations and Certifications (AERO515) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognize Civil Aviation regulations and regulatory bodies.

Discuss the importance of airworthiness in maintaining flight safety and the airworthiness. certification procedures.

Illustrate the importance of standards, engineering and flight manuals.

Explain the role of Quality Systems and Reliability Programs.

AERO520.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO520 Spacecraft Dynamics and Attitude Control
AERO520.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO520
This course provides students with a comprehensive introduction to spacecraft attitude dynamics and control, starting with the basic fundamentals of rotational kinematics and dynamics. The course will focus on simplified models of spacecraft attitude dynamics and an overview of attitude control strategies. Topics include theory and applications of spacecraft attitude dynamics; Euler angles; basic introduction to quaternions; attitude sensors; passive control methods like spin stabilization and gravity gradient; introduction to active control strategies with reaction wheels. This course aims to build an understanding that will allow students to analyze and design basic spacecraft attitude control systems.
Spacecraft Dynamics and Attitude Control (AERO520) > Credit Hours : 3

Spacecraft Dynamics and Attitude Control (AERO520) > Prerequisites
MECH409 with a minimum grade D
Spacecraft Dynamics and Attitude Control (AERO520) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze the basic kinematics and dynamics of spacecraft.

Interpret the basic models of orbital and attitude dynamics of spacecraft.

Evaluate different methods for stabilizing spacecraft.

Compare basic methods for attitude control and determination.

Design basic orbital and attitude control systems using MATLAB.

AERO561.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO561 Electric propulsion
AERO561.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO561
Operating principles, performance characteristics, and design features of the state-of-the-art electric propulsion systems. Electrothermal propulsion, Electromagnetic propulsion, Magnetohydrodynamics and pulsed plasma thrusters.
Electric propulsion (AERO561) > Credit Hours : 3

Electric propulsion (AERO561) > Prerequisites
MATH275 with a minimum grade D

MECH311 with a minimum grade D

MECH340 with a minimum grade D or AERO305 with a minimum grade D
Electric propulsion (AERO561) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Use the basics of plasma physics and electrodynamics in propulsion calculations.

Apply kinetic theory of gases to the analysis of standard electric propulsion systems

Analyze electric propulsion systems.

Perform oral and written technical communication

AERO562.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO562 Rocket propulsion
AERO562.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO562
Analysis and design of rocket engines including liquid, solid, hybrid and advanced propulsion systems, monopropellant thrusters, rocket engine thermochemistry, bipropellant engines and components, rocket engine cycle design, solid rocket motors and grain design, hybrid rockets, engineering problems on designing a solid, liquid or hybrid rocket.
Rocket propulsion (AERO562) > Credit Hours : 3

Rocket propulsion (AERO562) > Prerequisites
( MECH311 with a minimum grade D or AERO215 with a minimum grade D and MATH275 with a minimum grade D)
Rocket propulsion (AERO562) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Perform basic performance prediction methods for liquid and solid rocket engines.

Analyze various space vehicle propulsion options and components.

Use Momentum equations in the rocket propulsion thrust force calculations.

Perform needed calculations to design a rocket engine.

Prove effective oral and written technical communication

AERO563.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO563 Kinetics and thermodynamics of gases
AERO563.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO563
Thermodynamics of nonreacting and reacting gas mixtures, Quantum states and energy levels of molecules, Equilibrium population distribution of molecular energy levels, Determination of equilibrium thermodynamics properties of gas mixtures from molecular parameters, Equilibrium kinetic theory of gases, Basic transport properties of gases.
Kinetics and thermodynamics of gases (AERO563) > Credit Hours : 3

Kinetics and thermodynamics of gases (AERO563) > Prerequisites
MECH311 with a minimum grade D or AERO215 with a minimum grade D

MATH275 with a minimum grade D
Kinetics and thermodynamics of gases (AERO563) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply classical thermodynamics on reacting and non-reacting gas mixtures.

Use equilibrium properties of gas mixtures to perform mass and energy balance for reacting / non reacting gases.

Apply concepts of statistical mechanics including quantum states and energy levels in molecules for reacting / non reacting gases.

Apply equilibrium kinetic theory of gases and transport properties to solve engineering problems.

Perform effective technical oral / written communication

AERO564.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO564 Combustion
AERO564.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO564
Modeling of chemical reaction rates and reaction mechanisms, Simplified models for chemical reactors with combined chemical and thermal analysis, Development of the conservation equations for reacting, multispecies flows (including reaction rates and molecular transport), Propagation of laminar premixed combustion waves (detonations and deflagrations), Physical and chemical effects on laminar, premixed flames (e.g., flame speed and thickness), Structure of laminar diffusion flames and burning droplets, Time and spatial scales in turbulent flames, Structure and governing processes in turbulent flames.
Combustion (AERO564) > Credit Hours : 3

Combustion (AERO564) > Prerequisites
MECH311 with a minimum grade D

MECH340 with a minimum grade D or AERO305 with a minimum grade D
Combustion (AERO564) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Model chemical reaction rates and development of reaction mechanisms to reacting flows

Calculate the propagation of laminar premixed combustion waves.

Apply equilibrium kinetic theory of gases and transport properties to flame speed and thickness

Estimate the structure and modeling of non-premixed combustion to solving engineering problems

Show effective technical communication

AERO565.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO565 Experimental Techniques Teaching Lab
AERO565.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO565
The experimental methods teaching laboratory is developed with the following overall objective of providing students with the tools and skills to work in experimental areas focused in propulsion and combustion. The topic areas include – characterizing noise, resolution for imaging sensors, Flow calibration and measurement of associated errors, high frequency DAQ and acoustic characterization, manipulation and usage of pulsed light sources and diagnostics for DC plasma systems
Experimental Techniques Teaching Lab (AERO565) > Credit Hours : 3

Experimental Techniques Teaching Lab (AERO565) > Prerequisites
MECH350 with a minimum grade D

( MECH348 with a minimum grade D or AERO350 with a minimum grade D)
Experimental Techniques Teaching Lab (AERO565) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Use and calibrate of flow sensors and control circuits

Build a complete measurement hardware to perform experimental procedure.

Build an Interface to perform experimental measurement, including the fundamentals of commonly used digital data acquisition systems.

Analyze and interpret measurement data, and perform error analysis and propagation.

Practice team work to achieve experimental goals and analyze data.

Perform effective oral and written technical communication.

AERO566.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO566 High-Temperature Gas Dynamics
AERO566.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO566
Equilibrium properties of high temperature gases, e.g., calorically imperfect gases and reacting gases, Behavior of equilibrium and frozen flows with real gas properties, Nonequilibrium (rate) processes for gas dynamic flows, Behavior of nonequilibrium flows, Radiative energy exchange for gases and impacts on gas dynamic flows, Application of theoretical concepts to solving practical engineering problems in the areas of re-entry dynamics, hypersonic flows and plasma thrusters
High-Temperature Gas Dynamics (AERO566) > Credit Hours : 3

High-Temperature Gas Dynamics (AERO566) > Prerequisites
MECH311 with a minimum grade D

MECH340 with a minimum grade D or ( AERO305 with a minimum grade D)
High-Temperature Gas Dynamics (AERO566) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

At the end of the course students will be able to: Perform equilibrium balance to high-temperature gases, including calorically imperfect and reacting gases.

Apply equilibrium and non-equilibrium principles for real gases

Apply radiative energy exchange for gases.

Apply nonequilibrium flow and kinetics concepts to practical engineering problems

Demonstrate effective technical oral and written communication.

AERO567.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO567 Design of Liquid Rocket Engine
AERO567.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO567
This is a comprehensive course designed for aerospace and mechanical engineering students interested in propulsion systems. This course bridges theoretical knowledge and practical application, focusing on the design, development, and testing of liquid rocket engines (LREs). Students will gain an understanding of LRE components such as combustion chambers, turbopumps, feed systems, and nozzles, while participating in hands-on laboratory work and team-based projects. The course emphasizes collaborative engineering, experimental validation, and safety protocols, preparing students for real-world challenges in aerospace propulsion.
Design of Liquid Rocket Engine (AERO567) > Credit Hours : 3

Design of Liquid Rocket Engine (AERO567) > Prerequisites
AERO562 with a minimum grade D

AERO564 with a minimum grade D

AERO566 with a minimum grade D
Design of Liquid Rocket Engine (AERO567) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Perform basic performance predictions for liquid rocket engines (LREs)

Analyze LRE components and subsystems considering key design and operating parameters

Conduct laboratory experiments related to LREs

Analyze resulting data using engineering judgment to draw conclusions.

Design LRE subsystems covering conceptual design, thermo-structural and fluid-dynamic analyses, and performance optimization

AERO585.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO585 Design and Critical Thinking in Aerospace Engineering
AERO585.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO585
This course concentrates on the rigors of communication, design, and critical thinking in an engineering context including problem identification, feasibility study of alternative solutions, preliminary design, technical writing, teamwork, and formal presentations. A team of students will apply the knowledge gained throughout their study and from industrial training to an engineering design project, emphasizing critical thinking, creativity, and originality. The selected alternatives will be the foundation of the capstone design project. A final report is required.
Design and Critical Thinking in Aerospace Engineering (AERO585) > Credit Hours : 3

Design and Critical Thinking in Aerospace Engineering (AERO585) > Prerequisites
GENG315 with a minimum grade D

MECH305 with a minimum grade D

MECH310 with a minimum grade D

MECH315 with a minimum grade D

MECH350 with a minimum grade D

AERO300 with a minimum grade D

AERO305 with a minimum grade D

AERO310 with a minimum grade D

AERO301 with a minimum grade D or AERO315 with a minimum grade D
Design and Critical Thinking in Aerospace Engineering (AERO585) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the relevant theoretical background of a contemporary engineering problem. [PLO1]

Apply the fundamentals of engineering-design and critical thinking, including the assessment and evaluation of alternative engineering solutions. [PLO2]

Develop and conduct appropriate experimentation, modeling, simulation, and/or data analysis using engineering tools. [PLO6]

Communicate effectively through oral and written presentations. [PLO3]

Outline the principles of engineering ethics, and social and environmental responsibilities. [PLO4]

Recognize the need for ongoing additional knowledge, and the potential of integration and/or application of this knowledge effectively. [PLO7]

Develop leadership skills and project management techniques to independently and/or collaboratively handle complex professional tasks in a team-work context. [PLO5]

AERO590.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO590 Capstone Engineering Design Project
AERO590.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO590
This course builds on the outcomes of AERO 585 course to perform detailed design and cost estimate of the selected alternative solutions to a well-defined engineering problem. Student teams are expected to apply knowledge gained throughout their studies to an engineering design project, emphasizing creativity and originality. A prototype and final report are required.
Capstone Engineering Design Project (AERO590) > Credit Hours : 3

Capstone Engineering Design Project (AERO590) > Prerequisites
AERO585 with a minimum grade D
Capstone Engineering Design Project (AERO590) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the theoretical background of a contemporary engineering problem. [PLO1]

Apply the fundamentals of engineering-design, including the assessment and evaluation of alternative engineering solutions. [PLO2]

Develop and conduct appropriate experimentation, modelling, simulation, and/or data analysis using modern engineering tools. [PLO6]

Communicate effectively through oral and written presentations. [PLO3]

Recognize the principles of engineering ethics, and social and environmental responsibilities. [PLO4]

Recognize the need for ongoing additional knowledge, and the potential of integration and/or application of this knowledge effectively. [PLO7]

Develop leadership skills and project management techniques to independently and/or collaboratively handle complex professional tasks in a team-work context. [PLO5]

AERO601.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO601 Spacecraft Systems
AERO601.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO601
This course deals with the design aspects of spacecraft and launch vehicles. It includes the impacts of the atmosphere and the space environment on the mission selection and on the requirements and configurations of various subsystems. It focuses on the principles and design aspects of structure, material, propulsion, power, thermal, communication, electronic and control subsystems. The course will be complemented by case-studies.
Spacecraft Systems (AERO601) > Credit Hours : 3

Spacecraft Systems (AERO601) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyse spacecraft missions and understand rationales behind design

Compare key design drivers and critical issues for spacecraft missions

Appraise the inter-relations among various subsystems of modern spacecraft

Explain the operating principles of the various spacecraft subsystems

Design concepts of spacecraft to fulfil scientific missions

AERO602.title: UAEU Catalog — AERO602 Spacecraft Dynamics and Attitude Control
AERO602.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=AERO602
This course provides students with a comprehensive treatment of spacecraft attitude dynamics and control, starting with the basic fundamentals of rotational kinematics and dynamics to more advanced topics such as nonlinear attitude control. This includes theory and applications of spacecraft attitude dynamics and control; Euler angles, direction cosines, quaternions; attitude sensors and control actuators; spin, three-axis active, reaction wheel, control moment gyro, and gravity gradient control systems; environmental effects.
Spacecraft Dynamics and Attitude Control (AERO602) > Credit Hours : 3

Spacecraft Dynamics and Attitude Control (AERO602) > Prerequisites
AERO601 with a minimum grade D
Spacecraft Dynamics and Attitude Control (AERO602) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze kinematics and dynamics of 6-degree of freedom rigid body motions

Interpret the models of orbital and attitude dynamics of spacecraft.

Evaluate passive and active methods for spacecraft stabilization

Identify differences between various methods for attitude control and attitude determination.

Simulate Orbital and attitude control systems using Matlab Simulink / STK.

MECH200.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH200 Introduction to Engineering Drawing and Workshop
MECH200.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH200
This lab covers free hand sketching using orthographic and isometric projections, sectional views, dimensioning, surface finishing, materials marking, and working and assembly drawings. The course also introduces the use of basic machines and develop the hand skills and safety in the workshop. This includes basic hand tools, basic machining operations, woodwork, sheet metal work and measuring instruments.
Introduction to Engineering Drawing and Workshop (MECH200) > Credit Hours : 1

Introduction to Engineering Drawing and Workshop (MECH200) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Produce multi-views and isometric views of objects.

Develop sectional and auxiliary views.

Produce detailed working and assembly drawings.

Demonstrate awareness towards workshop safety rules.

Use common workshop tools and equipment.

MECH201.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH201 3D Printing Technologies
MECH201.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH201
This course aims to provide deeper understanding of the 3D printing and additive manufacturing technologies. The course provides both theoretical background about 3D printing as well as hands-on interactive experience on using 3D printers and scanners. Topics include theory of operation, materials used in 3D printing, applications of 3D printing, geometric modeling and 3D design for 3D printing, CAD software used in 3D printing, configuration and calibration of 3D printers, troubleshooting of 3D printers, 3D scanning technology, additive manufacturing technologies and their limitations, future perspectives, several lab exercises on 3D printing and scanning.
3D Printing Technologies (MECH201) > Credit Hours : 3

3D Printing Technologies (MECH201) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Use scientific concepts in designing and printing 3D objects

Ability to troubleshoot and provide proper maintenance for 3D printers

Distinguish between various 3D printing materials and their applications

Demonstrate the ability to use 3D scanners

Interpret professional and ethical responsibility

MECH210.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH210 Measurement and Instrumentation lab
MECH210.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH210
This lab is an introduction to techniques for computer and microcontroller based engineering measurement, data acquisition, calibration, processing, and analysis.
Measurement and Instrumentation lab (MECH210) > Credit Hours : 1

Measurement and Instrumentation lab (MECH210) > Prerequisites
PHYS135 with a minimum grade D
Measurement and Instrumentation lab (MECH210) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Construct basic electrical circuits using breadboard

Measure basic electrical quantities

Examine transducer/sensor characteristics

Practice data acquisition and sensor calibration

Construct microcontroller based measurement system

MECH240.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH240 Introduction to Computing Lab in ME
MECH240.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH240
Fundamental concepts of structured programming and algorithmic problem solving using technical computing commercial packages (e.g., MATLAB). This includes basics of programming, data visualization, software built-in functions, development of efficient codes, testing, and debugging programs. The lab focuses on providing programming practice on mathematical applications relevant to mechanical engineering.
Introduction to Computing Lab in ME (MECH240) > Credit Hours : 1

Introduction to Computing Lab in ME (MECH240) > Prerequisites
GENG230 with a minimum grade D

MATH110 with a minimum grade D
Introduction to Computing Lab in ME (MECH240) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Employ knowledge of basic procedural programming concepts.

Develop basic problem solving skills.

Use software package built-in functions to solve engineering problems.

Write software package scripts to solve engineering problems.

MECH305.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH305 Mechanics of Materials
MECH305.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH305
This course aims at introducing basic concepts and applications of elastic stress analysis. Topics covered include stress, strain, Hooke's law, axial loading, flexural loading. torsional loading, combined loading, Mohr's circle with applications, column buckling.
Mechanics of Materials (MECH305) > Credit Hours : 3

Mechanics of Materials (MECH305) > Prerequisites
CIVL240 with a minimum grade D
Mechanics of Materials (MECH305) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Calculate stresses and / or deformations and apply Hooke’s law in axially loaded members. [1D]

Use the stress concentration factors to find stresses, or allowable loads, on axially loaded members. [1D]

Compute stresses and/or deformations in a circular member subjected to torsion loading. [1D]

Produce shear and bending moment diagrams for beams and calculate bending and shearing stresses and beam deflection. [1D]

Solve problems using the stress transformation equations and Mohr's circle. [1D]

Use Euler's equation to solve buckling problems for various end conditions. [1D]

Analyze experimental data of a material behavior. [5D, 6I]

MECH306.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH306 Manufacturing Processes
MECH306.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH306
This course aims to provide students with basic manufacturing processes such as casting, welding, metal cutting and metal forming. Topics include: Mold design, casting and welding processes, theory of metal cutting, tooling features, mechanics of selected bulk deformation, sheet metalworking processes, and manufacturing process selection for a given product. Ethical issues and entrepreneurial activities are also covered.
Manufacturing Processes (MECH306) > Credit Hours : 3

Manufacturing Processes (MECH306) > Prerequisites
MECH390 with a minimum grade D
Manufacturing Processes (MECH306) > Corequisites
MECH305 with a minimum grade D
Manufacturing Processes (MECH306) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe casting processes.

Identify different welding processes.

Recognize metal removal processes.

Analyze bulk deformation processes.

Analyze sheet metal working.

Demonstrate self-study in recent topics in manufacturing processes.

MECH310.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH310 Dynamics
MECH310.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH310
This course aims to provide students with knowledge of dynamics of particles and rigid bodies. Topics include: plane kinematics and kinetics of particles, rectilinear and curvilinear motion, work and energy, impulse and momentum, plane kinematics and kinetics of rigid bodies, including nonrotating and rotating axes. The course also includes applications using modern engineering tools, such as MATLAB for simulation and analysis of dynamical systems.
Dynamics (MECH310) > Credit Hours : 3

Dynamics (MECH310) > Prerequisites
ELEC325 with a minimum grade D or CIVL240 with a minimum grade D
Dynamics (MECH310) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Solve kinematics of particles in different coordinate systems

Analyze kinetics of particles

Analyze kinematics of rigid bodies

Solve kinetics of rigid bodies

Demonstrate usage of computing packages such as Matlab to simulate dynamics of particles and/or rigid bodies

MECH311.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH311 Applied Thermodynamics
MECH311.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH311
This course aims to provide students with essential understanding of the concepts of applied thermo-dynamics. Topics include: Second law analysis, introduction to exergy, vapor and gas power cycles, ideal gas mixtures and psychrometry, basic air conditioning processes, basic refrigeration cycles, basics of combustion thermodynamics, basic compressible flow.
Applied Thermodynamics (MECH311) > Credit Hours : 3

Applied Thermodynamics (MECH311) > Prerequisites
GENG220 with a minimum grade D
Applied Thermodynamics (MECH311) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply second law of thermodynamics to processes

Analyze gas power, vapor power, and refrigeration cycles using first and second laws

Apply thermodynamics analysis for mixtures and air conditioning processes

Demonstrate a basic understanding of combustion and compressible flows

Communicate effectively in writing

MECH315.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH315 Geometric Modeling
MECH315.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH315
This course aims to introduce students to geometric modeling techniques. Topics include: orthographic and isometric projections, sectional views, and dimensioning. Introduction to geometric modeling and representation, solid modeling, parametric and feature-based modeling will also be covered. Students will use a modern mechanical engineering package (e.g. Pro/E, Solidworks, CATIA) throughout to apply the concepts learnt during this course.
Geometric Modeling (MECH315) > Credit Hours : 2

Geometric Modeling (MECH315) > Prerequisites
MECH200 with a minimum grade D
Geometric Modeling (MECH315) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Use a commercial CAD package to model objects in 3D using Feature Based Modelling

Use the model to produce orthographic projections and section views

Compose the models in Neutral data format for other applications

Apply dimension on Engineering Drawings using accepted standards

Produce a real life object/product into 3D CAD model

Develop computer models ready for rapid prototyping

Recognize the applicability of the knowledge learned in the course in real life applications

MECH340.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH340 Fluid Mechanics
MECH340.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH340
This course aims to provide students with essential concepts of fluid mechanics. Topics include: Fluid properties, similitude, fluid statics, Bernoulli?s equation, applications of the mass, momentum and energy equations, viscous flow in pipes, flow over immersed bodies, and introduction to turbo machinery.
Fluid Mechanics (MECH340) > Credit Hours : 3

Fluid Mechanics (MECH340) > Prerequisites
CIVL240 with a minimum grade D
Fluid Mechanics (MECH340) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognize fluid properties

Analyze hydrostatic forces and buoyancy force and stability of immersed bodies.

Apply momentum equation and Bernoulli equation in different flow settings.

Demonstrate the basic knowledge of Navier-Stokes equations, turbomachinery, and dimensional analysis and similitude.

Analyze lift and drag forces over immersed bodies.

Communicate effectively in writing

MECH348.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH348 Fluid Mechanics Lab
MECH348.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH348
This lab aims to provide students with in-depth understanding of theoretical phenomena studied in the fluid mechanics course. Students are required to use data acquisition system to acquire, analyze, and interpret results. Experiments include: Measurement of pressures, pressure loss in pipes, impact of jet, hydrostatic forces, viscosity, fluid flow rate, lift and drag, boundary layer; flow visualization, shock wave, velocity profiles in laminar and turbulent flows, performance of turbo machines.
Fluid Mechanics Lab (MECH348) > Credit Hours : 1

Fluid Mechanics Lab (MECH348) > Prerequisites
MECH210 with a minimum grade D

Pre/Co MECH340 with a minimum grade D
Fluid Mechanics Lab (MECH348) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Conduct experiments that support the understanding of basic fluid mechanics.

Analyze experimental data

Ability to function effectively on a team

Demonstrate ability to communicate effectively

MECH350.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH350 Introduction to Mechatronics
MECH350.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH350
This course provides students with an introduction to mechatronics. Topics include: characteristics of mechatronics systems, review of measuring fundamental properties; transducers for motion measurements, fluid flow, temperature, pressure and strain, signal conditioning, operational amplifiers, diode circuits and applications, bipolar junction transistors and field-effect transistors theory and applications, analog to digital/digital to analog conversions, and microprocessor applications.
Introduction to Mechatronics (MECH350) > Credit Hours : 3

Introduction to Mechatronics (MECH350) > Prerequisites
( PHYS140 with a minimum grade D and PHYS110 with a minimum grade D and MATH275 with a minimum grade D)

( MECH210 with a minimum grade D or ( AERO220 with a minimum grade D)
Introduction to Mechatronics (MECH350) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe mechatronics systems, components and characteristics

Explain basic electronic circuit models and their applications in mechatronics

Analyze step and frequency responses of dynamic systems analytically and experimentally

Experiment with basic electronic circuits

Explain principles of digital systems in relation to analog systems and signals

Illustrate practically the applications of microcontrollers in mechatronics systems

MECH384.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH384 Mathematics for Mechanical Engineering
MECH384.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH384
This course aims to introduce students to the applied mathematics for engineers. Topics include: Vector Calculus, Ordinary and Partial Differential Equations, Analysis of systems of Linear and Nonlinear Differential Equations, Fourier series, including but not limited to, structural mechanics, dynamic systems, mass, momentum and heat transfer equations.
Mathematics for Mechanical Engineering (MECH384) > Credit Hours : 3

Mathematics for Mechanical Engineering (MECH384) > Prerequisites
MATH275 with a minimum grade D
Mathematics for Mechanical Engineering (MECH384) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Solve systems of linear differential equations.

Demonstrate basic concepts related to vector calculus.

Demonstrate basic understanding of Fourier series.

Analyze the solution of wave/heat equation.

Recognize the basic concepts of nonlinear differential equations.

MECH390.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH390 Engineering Materials
MECH390.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH390
This course aims at studying basic concepts and fundamentals of material science and engineering. Topics covered include atomic structure, arrangements, unit cells, types of engineering materials; metallic alloys, polymers, ceramics, composites, nanocomposites, testing, mechanical and electrical properties, processing, in service behavior, corrosion, deformation, material and process selection.
Engineering Materials (MECH390) > Credit Hours : 3

Engineering Materials (MECH390) > Prerequisites
CHEM111 with a minimum grade D

CHEM175 with a minimum grade D
Engineering Materials (MECH390) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain concepts of crystalline and non-crystalline materials structures and its defects.

Use Fick's first and second laws of diffusion in metals.

Illustrate corrosion of metals.

Illustrate the electrical properties of metals and semiconductors.

Practice different types of material testing to derive mechanical properties.

Produce effective technical reports and presentations.

Identify contemporary issues related to engineering materials.

MECH395.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH395 Materials and Manufacturing lab
MECH395.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH395
This lab covers a variety of experiments to measure the different properties of engineering materials. The experiments include microstructure, Mechanical tests and corrosion experiments. In addition, the lab covers experiments related to manufacturing processes such as casting, welding, machining and metal forming
Materials and Manufacturing lab (MECH395) > Credit Hours : 1

Materials and Manufacturing lab (MECH395) > Corequisites
MECH306 with a minimum grade D
Materials and Manufacturing lab (MECH395) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Conduct different types of material testing to derive mechanical properties

Conduct corrosion and electrical properties tests

Perform different conventional manufacturing processes

Demonstrate ability to present gained technical skills in manufacturing

MECH407.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH407 Machine Design I
MECH407.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH407
This course aims at introducing fundamental skills and concepts of machine design with applications to simple elements. Topics covered include considerations affecting design, fits and tolerances, design of screws, fasteners and connections, welded joints, shafts, and flexible mechanical elements (springs, belts, ropes, flexible shafts, etc). Ethical and Entrepreneurial issues and autonomous learning techniques will be employed throughout the course where relevant.
Machine Design I (MECH407) > Credit Hours : 3

Machine Design I (MECH407) > Prerequisites
MECH305 with a minimum grade D

MECH315 with a minimum grade D
Machine Design I (MECH407) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Use failure theories in component design

Perform buckling analysis of columns

Apply tolerances, fits and stresses involved in machine design

Employ design procedure in shaft design

Employ design procedures in power screw and fastener design

Apply design procedure in flexible mechanical element design

Design mechanical component to meet desired needs

MECH409.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH409 Dynamic Systems & Control
MECH409.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH409
This course aims to introduce students to the fundamental knowledge of control system theories and applications. Topics include: Mathematical modeling, dynamic system responses, feedback control characteristics, stability of feedback systems, feedback control design, design steps of PID controller, and control design using root-locus method. The course also includes applications using modern engineering tools, such as MATLAB for control system design, simulation, and analyzes.
Dynamic Systems & Control (MECH409) > Credit Hours : 3

Dynamic Systems & Control (MECH409) > Prerequisites
MECH310 with a minimum grade D

MATH275 with a minimum grade D

MATH210 with a minimum grade D or MATH135 with a minimum grade D
Dynamic Systems & Control (MECH409) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Formulate differential equations and transfer functions system dynamic models using Laplace transform

Apply block diagram manipulation techniques

Analyze first, second and higher order systems and time response

Evaluate the stability, performance, and disturbance rejection characteristics of closed loop feedback systems

Develop controller design to alter system behavior using PID controllers

Use the graphical method of Root locus for analysis and design of feedback loops

Use Matlab control systems toolbox

MECH411.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH411 Heat Transfer for Mechanical Engineering
MECH411.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH411
This course aims to provide students with essential concepts of Heat Transfer. Topics include: Steady and transient heat conduction, forced and natural convection, internal and external flows, principles of engineering thermal radiation, heat exchanger, boiling and condensation. The course also aims to inspire students as well as enhance their entrepreneurial skills, as related to the heat transfer area.
Heat Transfer for Mechanical Engineering (MECH411) > Credit Hours : 3

Heat Transfer for Mechanical Engineering (MECH411) > Prerequisites
GENG220 with a minimum grade D

MECH340 with a minimum grade D

MECH240 with a minimum grade D

MATH275 with a minimum grade D

MATH135 with a minimum grade D or MATH210 with a minimum grade D
Heat Transfer for Mechanical Engineering (MECH411) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze steady state and transient heat conduction problems.

Apply correlations for natural and forced convection heat transfer.

Compute radiation heat transfer.

Analyze heat exchangers.

Recognize boiling and condensation heat transfer problems.

Demonstrate ability to communicate effectively.

MECH412.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH412 Machine Design II
MECH412.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH412
This course aims at covering the theory and application of design methods for complicated machine components. Computers will be used to help design integrated systems. The course also focuses on gaining skills in self-research, critical thinking and working within design groups. Topics covered include design of journal and rolling-element bearings, gears and gear boxes, clutches, couplings, and brakes. Ethical issues and Entrepreneurial opportunities and case studies will be explored throughout the course.
Machine Design II (MECH412) > Credit Hours : 3

Machine Design II (MECH412) > Prerequisites
MECH407 with a minimum grade D
Machine Design II (MECH412) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop procedures for the design of friction elements

Develop spur and helical gear systems following the design procedures

Develop bevel and worm gear systems following the design procedures

Apply the design procedures for journal bearings

Develop rolling element bearing compensations following the standard procedures

Build a full mechanical system, subsystem, or component

MECH417.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH417 Kinematics Design of Machinery
MECH417.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH417
This course aims to introduce students to the knowledge of kinematics of machinery analysis and synthesis. Topics include: Mobility analysis, kinematics of mechanisms, vector methods of analysis of plane mechanisms, introduction to the synthesis of plane linkages, force analysis of mechanisms, static and dynamic balancing of machines, and analysis and synthesis of cams. The course includes project work where students formed in teams perform analysis and simulation of mechanisms applications. The course also includes applications using modern engineering tools, such as MATLAB or MSC-AdAMS for mechanisms simulation and analysis.
Kinematics Design of Machinery (MECH417) > Credit Hours : 3

Kinematics Design of Machinery (MECH417) > Prerequisites
MECH310 with a minimum grade D
Kinematics Design of Machinery (MECH417) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Illustrate basic kinematics concepts of planar mechanisms

Design of four bar linkage to satisfy certain conditions.

Analyze position, velocity and acceleration of planar mechanisms.

Compute forces and torques under static and dynamic loading for realistic mechanisms.

Examine static and dynamic balance of rotating machinery.

Construct cams for desired output motions.

Develop analysis and simulation of mechanisms using computers.

MECH426.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH426 Thermofluid System Design & Analysis
MECH426.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH426
This course aims to provide students with basic design concepts for thermal-fluid systems. Topics include: Design and analysis of thermal-fluid systems: applications are drawn from power generation, HVAC/R and industrial processes. Introduction to energy management and identification of energy management opportunities. The course also aims to inspire students as well as enhance their entrepreneurial skills. Contemporary issues as well as commitment to standards of ethical practice will be emphasized.
Thermofluid System Design & Analysis (MECH426) > Credit Hours : 3

Thermofluid System Design & Analysis (MECH426) > Prerequisites
MECH311 with a minimum grade D
Thermofluid System Design & Analysis (MECH426) > Corequisites
MECH411 with a minimum grade D
Thermofluid System Design & Analysis (MECH426) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate performance of thermo-fluids components and systems

Develop workable design for the thermo-fluids components and systems.

Demonstrate ability to communicate effectively.

Apply new knowledge in thermo-fluids.

MECH430.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH430 Thermal Engineering Lab
MECH430.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH430
This lab aims to provide students with in-depth understanding of theoretical phenomena studied in the thermodynamics and heat transfer courses. Students are required to use data acquisition system to acquire, analyze, and interpret results. Experiments include: Psychometric processes; performance of refrigeration cycles and components; thermodynamic properties and equations of state; convective heat transfer; combustion engines; heat exchangers. The lab aims to inspire students and enhance their entrepreneurial skills as relevant to the area of thermal engineering.
Thermal Engineering Lab (MECH430) > Credit Hours : 1

Thermal Engineering Lab (MECH430) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co MECH426 with a minimum grade D
Thermal Engineering Lab (MECH430) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Construct experiments that support the understanding of thermo-fluids components and systems.

Analyze experimental data.

Apply design process to thermo-fluids components and systems.

Measure the student ability to work effectively a team.

Interpret professional and ethical responsibility.

Demonstrate ability to communicate effectively.

Apply new knowledge in thermo-fluid.

MECH433.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH433 Introduction to Computer Aided Manufacturing
MECH433.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH433
This course aims to provide students with the fundamentals of computer-aided manufacturing. Topics include: Computer numerical control, application of CAM packages (such as NX-CAM or CATIA-CAM) in machining complex parts, part programming, and introduction to computer integrated manufacturing. Students gain hands-on skills in using a computer aided manufacturing package and computer numerical control machine tools. This course also provides students with the awareness of the entrepreneurial activities in manufacturing.
Introduction to Computer Aided Manufacturing (MECH433) > Credit Hours : 3

Introduction to Computer Aided Manufacturing (MECH433) > Prerequisites
MECH306 with a minimum grade D
Introduction to Computer Aided Manufacturing (MECH433) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain basic components of CNC Systems.

Evaluate a machining sequence in a part drawing

Conduct CNC machining and standard programming.

Generate the CNC code by CAM package.

Use CAM packages to perform feature-based machining.

Produce parts with contours.

MECH440.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH440 Design and Manufacturing Lab
MECH440.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH440
This course aims to integrate theoretical and practical knowledge gained from previous design, materials, manufacturing, dynamics and some aspects of thermofluid courses. Students design and realize typical mechanical engineering systems or components through a series of projects and experiments. Students are required to use conventional and modern engineering tools as well as to develop commitment to ethical, environmental, social and global issues, and to be aware of entrepreneurial opportunities relevant to design and manufacturing.
Design and Manufacturing Lab (MECH440) > Credit Hours : 1

Design and Manufacturing Lab (MECH440) > Prerequisites
MECH407
Design and Manufacturing Lab (MECH440) > Corequisites
MECH433 with a minimum grade D
Design and Manufacturing Lab (MECH440) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop and conduct experiments in the context of design and manufacturing

Design for manufacturing Engineering Systems or components.

Solve problems related to design in consideration to other aspects.
