Demonstrate professional and ethical responsibility through their work in teams.

Demonstrate an appreciation for entrepreneurial opportunities relevant to design and manufacturing.

Develop product that can be manufactured and communicate it both orally and in writing.

MECH450.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH450 Dynamic Systems and Control Lab
MECH450.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH450
The lab provides students with hands-on skills of dynamic systems analysis and control implementation. The lab consists of experiments based on representative thermal, fluid, and mechanical systems. For each experiment the students will model the related process, simulate it, design a controller for it, and implement the final control system on a microcontroller.
Dynamic Systems and Control Lab (MECH450) > Credit Hours : 1

Dynamic Systems and Control Lab (MECH450) > Prerequisites
MECH409 with a minimum grade D

ELEC372 with a minimum grade D
Dynamic Systems and Control Lab (MECH450) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Formulate system dynamics problems mathematically

Analyze uncontrolled dynamic systems in terms of sensor calibration, system order, time response, and stability using Laplace transformation and time domain analysis

Design P, Pi, PD and PID based controllers to meet desired design specifications

Simulate controlled dynamic systems using Matlab

Analyze the performance of controlled dynamic systems

Evaluate the results of control system design

MECH510.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH510 Selected Topics in Thermal Sciences
MECH510.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH510

Selected Topics in Thermal Sciences (MECH510) > Course Learning Outcomes

MECH513.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH513 Air Conditioning Systems
MECH513.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH513
This course aims to introduce air-conditioning theory and applications. Topics covered include air-conditioning systems, cooling load calculations, types of air-conditioning systems, central stations, air-distribution and control systems, cooling water systems design, vibration and noise problems, and selection of optimum air-conditioning system.
Air Conditioning Systems (MECH513) > Credit Hours : 3

Air Conditioning Systems (MECH513) > Prerequisites
MECH311 with a minimum grade D

MECH411 with a minimum grade D
Air Conditioning Systems (MECH513) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Determine the cooling load for central air conditioning systems and cycles.

Compare AC equipment considering the cost and noise of the different component.

Design piping, ducting systems, pumps and fans for the central AC system.

Apply modern tools of reducing the load of AC systems and managing the energy.

MECH514.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH514 Heat Engines
MECH514.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH514
This course aims at explaining internal combustion engines, theory and design. Topics covered include air standard cycles, fuel air, and actual cycles, supercharging, knocking in petrol and diesel engines, fuel rating, engine performance, spark ignition and compression ignition engines, non-conventional engines, and air pollution from I.C. engines.
Heat Engines (MECH514) > Credit Hours : 3

Heat Engines (MECH514) > Prerequisites
MECH311 with a minimum grade D
Heat Engines (MECH514) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Compare between different engine cycles (theoretical and actual)

Compare between different types of flames in diesel and petrol engines

Decide the ethical and professional responsibilities of engine exhaust gases effects

Investigate new trends in engine design and selection of alternative fuels

MECH515.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH515 Optimization Methods in Engineering Systems
MECH515.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH515
This course is an interdisciplinary course for students who seek to apply quantitative methods and analytical techniques to optimize complex systems. The course focuses on the mathematical modeling, analysis, and decision-making processes that are crucial for improving efficiency, performance, and cost-effectiveness in engineering projects. The course covers mathematical modeling, optimization, and decision-making techniques like linear programming and decision trees, helping students solve real-world engineering problems and improve system efficiency across various fields.
Optimization Methods in Engineering Systems (MECH515) > Credit Hours : 3

Optimization Methods in Engineering Systems (MECH515) > Prerequisites
MATH140 with a minimum grade D
Optimization Methods in Engineering Systems (MECH515) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Formulate real-world engineering problems as mathematical models using appropriate Operations Research techniques (e.g., linear programming, decision trees).

Apply analytical techniques (e.g., graphical methods, simplex method, network analysis) to solve the developed mathematical models.

Apply optimal solutions to engineering case studies using appropriate optimization methods.

Practice decision-making techniques (e.g., decision trees, sensitivity analysis) to evaluate and select the best action under uncertainty.

Utilize appropriate software tools (e.g., Excel Solver, specialized optimization software) to solve Operations Research problems.

MECH516.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH516 Energy Management
MECH516.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH516
Energy management principle, energy auditing process, utility rate structures, economic principles and life cycle cost. Energy management applications in buildings, boilers and thermal systems, waste heat recovery, electrical systems, motors and insulation material. Environmental impacts and utilization of renewable energy technologies associated with energy management.
Energy Management (MECH516) > Credit Hours : 3

Energy Management (MECH516) > Prerequisites
MECH311 with a minimum grade D

MECH340 with a minimum grade D
Energy Management (MECH516) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply energy auditing process.

Compute economic and life cycle cost of energy systems.

Examine energy management opportunities for different systems.

Compose contemporary knowledge in energy management.

Recognize professional and ethical responsibilities as relevant to energy management.

MECH517.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH517 Turbomachinery
MECH517.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH517
This course covers a broad treatment of axial and radial turbo machines. Dimensional analysis. Basic laws and equations. Hydraulic pumps, pump and system matching. Centrifugal compressors and fans, pre-whirl, surging, choking. Axial compressors and fans, stage reaction and stage loading, multi-stage performance, axial-flow ducted fans. Axial and radial flow turbines, stator and rotor losses. Efficiencies.
Turbomachinery (MECH517) > Credit Hours : 3

Turbomachinery (MECH517) > Prerequisites
MECH311 with a minimum grade D

MECH340 with a minimum grade D
Turbomachinery (MECH517) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Formulate the dimensionless groups related to turbomachines.

Estimate the effect of blade angles on turbomachines performance.

Compare between different modern turbomachines design and performance.

Determine the professional and ethical solutions related to turbomachine design .

MECH520.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH520 Selected Topics in Bioengineering
MECH520.text:

Selected Topics in Bioengineering (MECH520) > Credit Hours : 3

Selected Topics in Bioengineering (MECH520) > Course Learning Outcomes

MECH522.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH522 Bioinstrumentation
MECH522.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH522

Bioinstrumentation (MECH522) > Credit Hours : 3

Conduct a design project/experiment on medical equipment [4M, 7M]

Engage in activities (research reports) that will contribute to the life-long learning and contemporary issues in biomedical instrumentations [7D]

MECH525.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH525 Introduction to Bioengineering
MECH525.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH525
Physiology of the muscular and cardiovascular systems. Principles of biomechanics, statics and dynamics of human movements. Fundamentals of biomaterials, properties of soft and hard tissue, biocompatibility. Principles of medical instrumentations. Contemporary issues, tissue engineering, genetic engineering, and informatics.
Introduction to Bioengineering (MECH525) > Credit Hours : 3

Introduction to Bioengineering (MECH525) > Prerequisites
MECH305 with a minimum grade D

MECH310 with a minimum grade D

MECH340 with a minimum grade D
Introduction to Bioengineering (MECH525) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Introduce students to the basic concepts and principles of bioengineering applications and topics.

Develop students’ abilities and skills as required in solving engineering problems related to human being health care.

Develop and improve students’ capabilities to conduct experiments properly and safely as well as analyze and interpret results and withdraw a conclusion from the results.

Improve students’ communication and research skills.

Increase students’ appreciation towards team building and long life learning.

Design systems or processes to meet desired bioengineering related needs.

MECH530.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH530 Selected Topics in Mechatronics
MECH530.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH530
Selected topics that meet students' interests, faculty capabilities and available resources in the mechatronics area. More than one section of this course may be offered in any semester when different topics need to be covered.

MECH531.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH531 Introduction to Robotics
MECH531.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH531
Spatial description and transformation. Manipulator kinematics and inverse manipulator kinematics. Jacobians: Velocities and static forces. Manipulator dynamics. Trajectory generation and linear control of manipulators. Introduction to mobile robot. Laboratory applications.
Introduction to Robotics (MECH531) > Credit Hours : 3

Introduction to Robotics (MECH531) > Prerequisites
MECH417 with a minimum grade D
Introduction to Robotics (MECH531) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Formulate spatial descriptions and coordinate transformation [1M]

Solve manipulator direct and inverse kinematics [1D]

Formulate robot Jacobians, velocities and dynamics [1M]

Demonstrate task programming for robotic manipulator [6I]

Produce robot trajectory [1M]

Mark the impact of robotic solutions in a global, economic, environmental, and societal context [4M]

Analyze robot performance using Matlab [7M]

MECH532.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH532 Design of Mechatronics Systems
MECH532.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH532
The course focuses on the design of embedded control systems with applications to electromechanical, electro-fluidic/pneumatic and/or electro-thermal system control. Modeling, simulation and parameter identifications of the designed system are covered. Topics also include real-time embedded system programming using C, representative computer communication protocols, integration of sensors and actuators, design of system/user interface, and applications of ADC and PWM interfaces. A project covering the course topics is used to exemplify the mechatronics system design.
Design of Mechatronics Systems (MECH532) > Credit Hours : 3

Design of Mechatronics Systems (MECH532) > Prerequisites
MECH350 with a minimum grade D or ELEC451 with a minimum grade D
Design of Mechatronics Systems (MECH532) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Model system dynamics using mathematical tools and physics principles

Develop C programming skills

Develop skills and knowledge in building and testing computer communication systems

Develop skills and knowledge in building and testing embedded systems using microcontrollers

Integrate embedded systems, actuators, sensors and computer communication sub-systems to make functioning mechatronics systems.

MECH533.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH533 Mechanical Vibration
MECH533.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH533
This course aims to provide students with knowledge in the area of mechanical vibrations. Topics include: Free and forced vibration of one-degree-of-freedom systems. Free and forced vibrations of multi-degrees-of-freedom systems, natural frequencies and mode shapes, vibration control, vibration measurement methods, and vibration of continuous systems.
Mechanical Vibration (MECH533) > Credit Hours : 3

Mechanical Vibration (MECH533) > Prerequisites
MECH310 with a minimum grade D
Mechanical Vibration (MECH533) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Solve free vibration problems of single-degree-of-freedom systems.

Solve forced vibration problems of single-degree-of-freedom systems associated with rotating unbalance and base excitation.

Analyze transient vibration.

Solve free vibration of multi-degree-of-freedom systems.

Design a mechanical system for vibration suppression.

Use modern computation packages to solve vibration problems.

MECH540.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH540 Selected Topics in Design & Manufacturing
MECH540.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH540
Selected topics that meet students' interests, faculty capabilities and available resources in the design and manufacturing area. More than one section of this course may be offered in any semester when different topics need to be covered.

Selected Topics in Design & Manufacturing (MECH540) > Course Learning Outcomes

Use engineering tools to solve practical problems arising in design and manufacturing

Analyze engineering solutions and their impacts for practical problems in design and manufacturing

MECH541.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH541 Non-conventional Manufacturing
MECH541.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH541
This course aims at studying non- conventional manufacturing processes such as Electro Discharge Machining (EDM), ultrasonic machining and welding. Theory of plasticity for metal forming is covered.
Non-conventional Manufacturing (MECH541) > Credit Hours : 3

Non-conventional Manufacturing (MECH541) > Prerequisites
MECH306 with a minimum grade D
Non-conventional Manufacturing (MECH541) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze mechanical energy techniques.

Examine electrical energy techniques.

Analyze thermos-electrical energy.

Examine thermal energy techniques.

Outline different additive manufacturing processes.

Compare between different non-conventional manufacturing methods.

Produce effective technical reports and presentations.

MECH545.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH545 Maintenance Engineering
MECH545.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH545
This course aims at studying methods and management of engineering maintenance. Topics covered include the role of statistics and probability in failure, types of maintenance, manpower, spare parts and materials, maintenance procedures, planning and organization. Inventory control, work distribution, and administration structure.
Maintenance Engineering (MECH545) > Credit Hours : 3

Maintenance Engineering (MECH545) > Prerequisites
MATH135 with a minimum grade D
Maintenance Engineering (MECH545) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Illustrate the important concepts in reliability and maintainability

Recognize the responsibilities of the engineer working in maintenance

Examine the methods to collect and analyze failure and repair data

Apply the maintenance procedures, planning, and organization

Develop an appropriate reliability and maintainability models

Incorporate cost of reliability and maintainability in the design process in real world examples

Communicate effectively using right reliability, quality and maintainability terminology

MECH547.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH547 Intermediate Mechanics of Material
MECH547.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH547
The course aims at studying 3-D stress and strain analysis, generalised Hooke's law. theories of failure, stress function, applications to selected plane and axi-symmetric problems, linear-elastic fracture mechanics (LEFM), fatigue analysis and experimental stress analysis.
Intermediate Mechanics of Material (MECH547) > Credit Hours : 3

Intermediate Mechanics of Material (MECH547) > Prerequisites
MECH305 with a minimum grade D
Intermediate Mechanics of Material (MECH547) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply the 3-D stress and strain relationships and Generalized Hooke's law.

Apply theories of failure to design components under complex stresses.

Apply the equilibrium and compatibility equations, stress function and boundary conditions to solve plane and axisymmetric problems.

Apply linear elastic fracture mechanics approach.

Apply fracture mechanics based approach to fatigue analysis.

Use modern computation packages to analyze stresses and strains.

Analyze and interpret experimental data and draw conclusions.

MECH550.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH550 Introduction to Aerospace Engineering
MECH550.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH550
Historical perspectives of aerospace engineering, aerospace engineering profession,. Standard atmosphere. Introduction to aircraft performance (steady flight, flight performance, aircraft maneuvers). Introduction airplane aerodynamics and propulsion, introduction to flight controls and stability and introduction aircraft structures.
Introduction to Aerospace Engineering (MECH550) > Credit Hours : 3

Introduction to Aerospace Engineering (MECH550) > Prerequisites
GENG220 with a minimum grade D
Introduction to Aerospace Engineering (MECH550) > Corequisites
MECH340 with a minimum grade D
Introduction to Aerospace Engineering (MECH550) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the history of airplanes and their impact on the global, regional, and national levels.

Analyze the aerodynamics and performance of airplanes.

Describe the basics of propulsion, stability, and structure of aircrafts.

Measure the student ability to work effectively a team.

Apply new knowledge and techniques in the field of aerospace engineering.

Decide the professional and ethical responsibility related to aerospace engineering.

MECH551.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH551 Foundations of Aerodynamics
MECH551.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH551
Aerodynamics forces & moments, non-dimensional coefficients; classification of aerodynamic flows, integral and differential form of governing equations for aerodynamics flows; streamlines, irrotaional and rotational flow, circulation and Kelvin's circulation theorem; low speed wind tunnels, solution for irrotational flows, elementary potential flows and superposition principle, aerodynamics of airfoils, introduction to to supersonic flows, boundary layer.
Foundations of Aerodynamics (MECH551) > Credit Hours : 3

Foundations of Aerodynamics (MECH551) > Prerequisites
MECH340 with a minimum grade D
Foundations of Aerodynamics (MECH551) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the fundamental principles and mathematical formulations related to aerodynamics

Define the principles of inviscid and incompressible flow over airfoils and flow over finite wings.

Recognize the professional and ethical responsibilities related to aerospace engineering.

Apply new knowledge and techniques in the field of aerospace engineering.

Work effectively in a team.

MECH552.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH552 Aircraft Structures
MECH552.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH552
Review of concepts of stress, deformation, strain, displacement and equations of elasticity; Aircraft structural components; Airworthiness and airframe loads; Application aerospace structural elements including general bending and torsion of open and closed thin walled structures, box beams and thin flat curved panels; Shear flow in thin walled sections; Design of thin-walled multi-cell sections; Failure theories and yield criteria and introduction to fracture mechanics and fatigue; Introduction to finite element methods; introduction to stiffness (displacement) method and truss equations
Aircraft Structures (MECH552) > Credit Hours : 3

Aircraft Structures (MECH552) > Prerequisites
MECH305 with a minimum grade D
Aircraft Structures (MECH552) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply the fundamentals of linear elasticity

Explain the principles of stressed skin construction

Compute various airframe loads

Apply the fundamentals of fracture mechanics and fatigue to study cracked aircraft structural components.

Analyze open-section and closed-section thin-walled aircraft structures subject to bending, shear, and torsion loads.

Estimate the properties of laminated composite aircraft structures

Employ experimental stress analysis techniques to analyze aircraft structural components

Identify the impact of advances in aircraft structures on the environment, society, and economy

MECH553.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH553 Flight Dynamics, Stability and Control
MECH553.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH553
Introduction to the dynamics and control of atmospheric flight vehicles, aircraft coordinate systems, coordinate system transformations, inertial acceleration, aerodynamic forces and moments (stability derivatives), derivation of aircraft equations of motion EOM, linearization of EOM for a given trimmed flight condition, static stability in longitudinal and lateral-directional, small disturbance equations of unsteady motion, dynamics stability.
Flight Dynamics, Stability and Control (MECH553) > Credit Hours : 3

Flight Dynamics, Stability and Control (MECH553) > Prerequisites
MECH310 with a minimum grade D
Flight Dynamics, Stability and Control (MECH553) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify aircraft axes and nomenclature

Analyze static longitudinal stability and control

Formulate aircraft dynamic equations of motion

Evaluate aircraft dynamic stability

Identify the impact of flights in a global, economic, environmental, and societal context

Evaluate aircraft stability using advanced computational tools

MECH554.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH554 Aerospace Propulsion
MECH554.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH554
Study of the aero-and thermodynamics of jet and liquid and solid rocket engines. Air-breathing engines as propulsion systems. Turbojets, turbofans, turboprops, ramjets. Aerodynamics of gas-turbine engine components, ideal cycle analysis, component performance, non-ideal cycle analysis. Rocket vehicle performance. Introduction to space propulsion.
Aerospace Propulsion (MECH554) > Credit Hours : 3

Aerospace Propulsion (MECH554) > Prerequisites
MECH311 with a minimum grade D

MECH340 with a minimum grade D
Aerospace Propulsion (MECH554) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify air-breathing engines’ components

Analyze ideal and real propulsion engines including ideal ramjet, turbojet, and turbofan at system and component level

Recognize requirements and components of rocket propulsion systems

Demonstrate ability to communicate effectively

Decide professional and ethical responsibility as relevant to propulsion systems

Compose new knowledge in aerospace propulsion

MECH585.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH585 Design and Critical Thinking in Mechanical Engineering
MECH585.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH585
This course concentrates on the rigors of communication, design, and critical thinking in an engineering context including problem identification, feasibility study of alternative solutions, preliminary design, technical writing, teamwork, and formal presentations. A team of students will apply the knowledge gained throughout their study and from industrial training to an engineering design project, emphasizing critical thinking, creativity, and originality. The selected alternatives will be the foundation of the capstone design project. A final report is required.
Design and Critical Thinking in Mechanical Engineering (MECH585) > Credit Hours : 3

Design and Critical Thinking in Mechanical Engineering (MECH585) > Prerequisites
STAT210 with a minimum grade D

MECH305 with a minimum grade D

MECH310 with a minimum grade D

MECH311 with a minimum grade D

MECH315 with a minimum grade D

MECH340 with a minimum grade D

MECH348 with a minimum grade D

MATH275 with a minimum grade D

PHYS110 with a minimum grade D

PHYS140 with a minimum grade D

CHEM175 with a minimum grade D

MECH350 with a minimum grade D
Design and Critical Thinking in Mechanical Engineering (MECH585) > Corequisites
( MECH306 with a minimum grade D)
Design and Critical Thinking in Mechanical Engineering (MECH585) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the relevant theoretical background of a contemporary engineering problem.

Apply the fundamentals of engineering-design and critical thinking, including the assessment and evaluation of alternative engineering solutions.

Develop and conduct appropriate experimentation, modelling, simulation, and/or data analysis using engineering tools.

Communicate effectively through oral and written presentations.

Outline the principles of engineering ethics, and social and environmental responsibilities.

Recognize the need for ongoing additional knowledge, and the potential of integrating and/or application of this knowledge effectively.

Develop leadership skills and project management techniques to independently and/or collaboratively handle complex professional tasks in a team-work context.

MECH590.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH590 Capstone Engineering Design Project
MECH590.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH590
This course builds on the outcomes of MECH 585 course to perform detailed design and cost estimate of the selected alternative solutions to a well-defined engineering problem. Student teams are expected to apply knowledge gained throughout their studies to an engineering design project, emphasizing creativity and originality. A final report and prototype are required.
Capstone Engineering Design Project (MECH590) > Credit Hours : 3

Capstone Engineering Design Project (MECH590) > Prerequisites
MECH585 with a minimum grade D
Capstone Engineering Design Project (MECH590) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the theoretical background of a contemporary engineering problem

Apply the fundamentals of engineering-design, including the assessment and evaluation of alternative engineering solutions.

Develop and conduct appropriate experimentation, modelling, simulation, and/or data analysis using modern engineering tools.

Communicate effectively through oral and written presentations.

Recognize the principles of engineering ethics, and social and environmental responsibilities.

Recognize the need for ongoing additional knowledge, and the potential of integration and/or application of this knowledge effectively.

Develop leadership skills and project management techniques to independently and/or collaboratively handle complex professional tasks in a team-work context.

MECH612.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH612 Advanced Mechanical Vibrations
MECH612.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH612
Multidegree of freedom discrete systems, continuous systems, approximate methods, finite element method, vibration control, random vibration, and nonlinear vibration.
Advanced Mechanical Vibrations (MECH612) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Mechanical Vibrations (MECH612) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Ability To Critically Review The Literature Including Patents And Synthesize The Information With Calculations To Assess The Feasibility Of Technology Concepts. [Plo3, Plo4]

Understand The Behavior Of A Mechanical System, By Analyzing Nonlinearities In Vibration Behavior. [Plo1]

Understand The Concepts Of Vibration Modes And Natural Frequencies For Multi-Degree-Of-Freedom Systems. [Plo1]

Understand The Fundamentals Of Vibrations Of Continuous Systems Such As Beams And Plates. [Plo1]

Use Modern Computation Packages To Solve Vibration Problems [Plo2]

Use Of Different Numerical Techniques And Its Application To Vibration Design. [Plo2]

MECH614.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH614 Linear Systems Theory
MECH614.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH614
Introduction to state-space representations of continuous systems. State equations' solution. State-feedback. Block diagram, modeling, controllability, and observability. Singular values and model reduction, feedback control, and pole placement. Observers, reduced-order observers, separation principle, and observer design. Optimal control. Linear-quadratic regulator (LQR). Probability and stochastic processes. Optimal estimation. Kalman filter.
Linear Systems Theory (MECH614) > Credit Hours : 3

Linear Systems Theory (MECH614) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze The System Behavior Based On The Mathematical Model Of That System Where The Model May Be Expressed In State-Space Domain. [Plo1]

Apply Linear Algebra To Complex Real World Problems In Order To Obtain Models That Are Expressed Using State Space Equations. [Plo1]

Design Controllers Using The Concept Of State Feedback And Pole Placement Tech. [Plo1]

Design, Build, Simulate, And Test Control Systems And Strategies Using Both Matlab And Simulink. [Plo1, Plo2]

Write A Report That Effectively Communicates The Results Of An Analysis Or Design. [Plo3, Plo4]

MECH615.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH615 Advanced Dynamics
MECH615.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH615
This course covers three-dimensional kinematics and dynamics of particles and rigid bodies using vector (Newton-Euler) and analytical (Lagrange's equations and Hamilton's principle) methods. Study of how kinematic constraints are incorporated into forming the governing equations and their relationship with constraint forces. Holonomic and nonholonomic constraints. Linear and angular momentum, and energy conservation. Using rotating coordinate systems to solve dynamics problems. Two- and three-dimensional rigid body dynamics. Gyroscopic motion. Lagrange multipliers. Kane’s equations. Instruction on advanced topics in analytical dynamics, incorporating D'Alembert's principle, Hamilton's principle and the general Lagrange equations. Reinforcement of concepts through computer analysis using Matlab.
Advanced Dynamics (MECH615) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Dynamics (MECH615) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze The Kinematics Of Particles, Systems Of Particles, And Rigid Bodies. [Plo1]

Choose Different Sets Of Coordinates To Describe The Dynamic Motion. [Plo1]

Combine Computational With Theoretical Analysis Techniques To Solve Advanced Problems In Dynamics. [Plo2]

Derive The Dynamic Equations Of Motion For A Three-Dimensional Rigid Body Using Newtonian/Lagrangian/Hamiltonian/Kane Dynamics. [Plo1]

Derive The Dynamics Equations Using D’Almbert’S Principle, Virtual Displacement And Virtual Work. [Plo1]

Formulate And Solve Kinematics Problems For Multi-Body Mechanical Devices With Holonomic And Non-Holonomic Constraints. [Plo1]

Formulate And Solve Three-Dimensional Kinematics Problems Using Euler Angles. [Plo1]

Interpret The Knowledge Provided In The Course To Model Both Common And Complex Mechanical Systems. [Plo3]

Understand And Apply Linear And Angular Momentum, And Energy Conservation. [Plo1]

MECH616.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH616 Robotic Manipulation and Control
MECH616.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH616
This course covers the principles of robotic manipulation for industrial and service applications. The course covers spatial descriptions and rigid-body transformations, forward and inverse kinematics of serial manipulators, velocity kinematics through Jacobian matrices, singularity and manipulability analysis, dynamic formulations using Newton–Euler and Lagrangian methods, trajectory generation in joint and Cartesian space, and control strategies including computed torque and hybrid force/position control. The course also covers robot programming languages, safety standards, force sensing, and human-robot collaboration. A semester-long term project integrates these methods to model, simulate, and analyze the control of a robotic manipulator selected by the student.
Robotic Manipulation and Control (MECH616) > Credit Hours : 3

Robotic Manipulation and Control (MECH616) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze the architecture, components, classification, and design trade-offs of industrial and service robotic systems.

Apply spatial representation methods and kinematic modeling techniques to analyze robot motion and configuration.

Analyze the dynamic behavior of robotic manipulators

Design trajectory planning and apply control strategies for manipulator operation.

Evaluate robot programming, safety standards, human-robot collaboration, and emerging trends in robotic manipulation.

Critically review recent research in robotic manipulation and communicate technical findings through written reports and oral presentations.

MECH626.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH626 Fatigue & Fracture Mechanics
MECH626.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH626
Analysis of the general state of stress and strain in solids; dynamic fracture tests (FAD, CAT). Linear elastic fracture mechanics (LEFM), Griffith- Irwin analysis, ASTM KIC, KIPCI, KIA, KID. Plane stress, plane strain; yielding fracture mechanics (COD, JIC). Fatigue crack initiation. Goodman diagrams and fatigue crack propagation. Notch sensitivity and stress concentrations. Low-cycle fatigue, corrosion and thermal fatigue.
Fatigue & Fracture Mechanics (MECH626) > Credit Hours : 3

Fatigue & Fracture Mechanics (MECH626) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply Epfm Approach Criteria: Crack Opining Displacement, J Contour Integral, R Curves, Etc. [Plo 1].

Apply The Concept Of Fracture Zone Corrections [Plo1]

Apply The Concepts Of Griffith/Strain Energy Release Rate And Stress Intensity Facto [Plo1].

Apply The Fracture Mechanics Approach To Solve Fatigue Crack Initiation And Propagations Problems [Plo 1, Plo 3].

Apply The Measurement Procedure Of The Fracture Toughness Kic [Plo 1, Plo 3]

Apply The Principles Of Lefm And Epfm In Components Design [Plo1]

Conduct A Presentation On A Relevant Topic To Fatigue And Fracture Mechanics [Plo 4].

Conduct Theoretical And/Or Experimental Work, Analyze The Results And Draw Conclusions In A Scientific/ Applied Research-Based Term Project [Plo3, Plo2]

MECH630.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH630 Advanced Solid Mechanics
MECH630.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH630
The course covers fundamental principles and techniques in stress analysis of trusses, beams, rigid frame, and then-walled structures. State of stress and strain at a point, stress-strain relationships: topics in beam theory such as unsymmetrical bending, curved beams, and elastic foundations: torsion of noncircular cross-sections. Emphasis is placed on energy methods associated with calculus of variations.
Advanced Solid Mechanics (MECH630) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Solid Mechanics (MECH630) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze The Stress At A Point And Apply The Stress Relations [Plo1].

Apply Energy Methods (E.G. Castigliano Theorem) To Solve Problems Of Springs And Beams [Plo 1]

Apply The Principles Of Solid Mechanics To Solve Elasticity Problems [Plo1]

Conduct A Presentation On A Relevant Topic To Advanced Solid Mechanics [Plo3]

Conduct Theoretical And/Or Experimental Work, Analyze The Results And Draw Conclusions In A Scientific Or Applied Research-Based Term Project [Plo4, Plo3, Plo2, Plo1]

Determine The Stresses On Oblique Planes, Principal Stresses, And Octahedral Stresses In 3-D [Plo1].

Measure The Strains At A Point And Obtain The Principle Strains And Stresses [Plo 1, Plo2]

Solve Solid Mechanics Problems (E.G., Thick Walled Tubes, Plates, Shells, Rotating Discs [Plo1]

Use Various Yield Criteria To Explain Material Deformation Mechanisms And Prevent Material From A Catastrophic Failure [Plo1].

MECH632.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH632 Advanced CAD/CAM
MECH632.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH632
Wire frame and other precursors to geometric models. Parametric and Bozier curves; B-splines and NURBS. Boundary representation models. Set theoretic (or CSG) models. Implicit solids and surfaces. Non-manifold geometric models. Feature-based modeling and recognition. Intelligent CAD systems. Numerical accuracy problems in geometric models. Integral properties of geometric models. Procedural shape definition. Types of engineering constraints. Constraint based systems. Techniques for constraint resolution. Rapid prototyping. Part Programming and Machining, NC cutting, path planning and process planning.
Advanced CAD/CAM (MECH632) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced CAD/CAM (MECH632) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Employ the theory on manipulation of vertices.

Use the theory on PC curves, Bezier curves and B-splines in the design and manufacture of components.

Use the theory on PC, Bezier and B spline surfaces.

Practice the fundamentals and advanced theory of solid modeling and Feature Based Modeling.

Create CNC programming

Build CAD model using a CAD/CAM package

MECH633.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH633 Finite Element Methods
MECH633.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH633
This course covers fundamental concepts of the finite element method are presented and developed for one- and two-dimensional problems. Applications in the areas of structural analysis, heat transfer and fluid flow are stressed. Computer implementations of finite element method are emphasized. The course focuses on structural mechanics using spring element, bar elements, 2D trusses elements, beam elements, two-dimensional plane stress/strain elements and axisymmetric elements. Heat transfer, solid mechanics and fluid mechanics problems will also be analyzed.
Finite Element Methods (MECH633) > Credit Hours : 3

Finite Element Methods (MECH633) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply the general steps of finite element methods [PLO1]

Employ the basic finite elements formulation techniques [PLO1]

Formulate equations in finite element methods for 1D and 2D problems [PLO1, PLO3]

Solve basic structural, heat transfer and fluid flow problems [PLO1, PLO3]

Present results of work either orally or in writing [PLO3, PLO4]

Write computer program based on finite element methods [PLO6]

MECH636.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH636 Materials Design, Synthesis, and Processing
MECH636.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH636
This course covers the design, synthesis, and processing of engineering materials with emphasis on structure–property–processing relationships. The course covers powder processing and sintering, thin-film and coating deposition (such as PVD, CVD, sol-gel, and aerosol), crystal growth and solidification control, and surface modification techniques. Case studies drawn from diverse engineering sectors illustrate process selection methodologies that balance performance, cost, manufacturability, and sustainability. A semester-long term project requires the design and evaluation of a synthesis route for a student-selected material system, applying these methods to a research-level problem.
Materials Design, Synthesis, and Processing (MECH636) > Credit Hours : 3

Materials Design, Synthesis, and Processing (MECH636) > Prerequisites
MECH306

MECH311
Materials Design, Synthesis, and Processing (MECH636) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain structure-property-processing relationships governing engineering material behavior.

Apply powder processing, sintering, and thin-film deposition principles to materials design problems.

Analyze crystal growth, solidification control, and surface modification processes.

Evaluate and justify process selection methodologies balancing performance, cost, and sustainability.

Critically review recent research in materials processing and present synthesis route design proposals.

Assess environmental and sustainability dimensions in materials selection and process design decisions.

MECH640.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH640 Directed Studies in Mechanical Engineering
MECH640.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH640
This will require students to discuss and critique original and recent journal articles, describing a major scientific advancement in a research area, which will be chosen in consultation with the student’s supervisor. Students are required to make presentations, submit reports and participate in discussions.
Directed Studies in Mechanical Engineering (MECH640) > Credit Hours : 3

Directed Studies in Mechanical Engineering (MECH640) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Survey most recent journal article/s relevant to scientific advancement in a research topic

Make up presentations on most recent journal article/s relevant to scientific advancement in a research topic

Compose a report on recent journal article/s relevant to scientific advancement in a research topic

MECH645.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH645 Advanced Heat Transfer
MECH645.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH645
This course will cover two major topics in heat transfer: conduction and convection. Specific conduction topics covered will include: methods of solving the (one dimensional & multidimensional) heat conduction equation for various boundary conditions, homogenous vs. nonhomogenous problems, transient versus steady state in rectangular and cylindrical coordinates. The various methods to solve the heat conduction equation involve separation of variables, Duhamel?s Theorem, Laplace Transform technique and integral methods.. Specific topics in convection include: laminar and turbulent heat transfer, thermal boundary layers, ?limiting? condition flows, transpiration cooling, external flows and natural convection.
Advanced Heat Transfer (MECH645) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Heat Transfer (MECH645) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Be Able To Formulate Equations For 1D And 2D Heat Transfer Problems [Plo1, Plo2]

Present Results Of Work Either Orally Or In Writing [Plo3]

Understand And Apply Methods To Solve Steady State And Transient Heat Conduction Equation Problems [Plo1, Plo2]

Understand The Basic Conduction And Convection Heat Transfer Formulation Techniques [Plo1, Plo2]

Understand The General Methods Of Solving Conduction And Convection Heat Transfer [Plo1, Plo2]

Write Computer Program To Solve Heat Transfer Problems Methods [Plo4]

MECH650.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH650 Advanced Fluid Mechanics
MECH650.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH650
Kinematics of fluid motion. Constitutive equations of isotropic viscous compressible fluids. Derivation of Navier-Stokes equations. Lessons from special exact solutions, self-similarity. Admissibility of idealizations and their applications; inviscid, adiabatic, irrotational, incompressible, boundary- layer, quasi one-dimensional, linearized and creeping flows. Vorticity theorems. Unsteady Bernoulli equation. Basic flow solutions. Basic features of turbulent flows.
Advanced Fluid Mechanics (MECH650) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Fluid Mechanics (MECH650) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply Boundary Layer Approximation. [Plo1-Plo2]

Apply Similarity Solution And Non-Dimensional Analysis. [Plo1]

Compute A Numerical Solution For The Bl Approximation And Similarity Solution. [Plo1-Plo2]

Derive Mass And Momentum Conservation Partial Differential Form. [Plo1]

Develop Mathematical Models For Inviscid/Potential Flow. [Plo1-Plo2]

Learn Tensor And Vector Notation Of The Governing Equations. [Plo1]

Properly Apply Mass And Momentum Conservation To Viscous Flow And Produce Exact Analytical Solution. [Plo1]

Understand Fluid Kinematics. [Plo1]

MECH652.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH652 Renewable Energy and Systems
MECH652.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH652
This course covers renewable energy technologies including solar (photovoltaic and thermal), wind, hydropower, biomass and bioenergy, geothermal, and ocean energy (OTEC and tidal). The course covers resource characterization, conversion principles and theoretical performance limits, energy storage requirements, grid integration challenges, and techno-economic and policy assessment. A semester-long techno-economic project applies these methods to a student-selected renewable energy system. The course prepares students for advanced study and applied research in solar, electrochemical, and hybrid energy systems aligned with the UAE Energy Strategy 2050.
Renewable Energy and Systems (MECH652) > Credit Hours : 3

Renewable Energy and Systems (MECH652) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the fundamental principles of renewable energy systems, including renewable vs. non-renewable energy sources, solar energy fundamentals, and photovoltaic (PV) power technology.

Evaluate solar thermal and wind energy systems based on resource characteristics and system performance parameters.

Compare hydropower and bioenergy systems in terms of resource availability, conversion technologies, and operational performance.

Analyze geothermal, energy storage, ocean thermal energy conversion (OTEC), and tidal energy technologies for sustainable energy applications.

Discuss contemporary issues related to renewable energy deployment including grid integration, policy, and techno-economic analysis.

MECH654.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH654 Advanced Thermodynamics
MECH654.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH654
Thermodynamic potentials: Maxwell relations, stability criteria. Barometric formula: applications to clouds, solar chimney, etc. Phase mixtures: chemical potential, osmosis, phase equilibrium, Gibbs phase rule, phase diagrams, fugacity and activity. Reacting mixtures: law of mass action and applications, enthalpy and entropy constants, heat of reaction, combustion, flames, adiabatic flame temperature, reaction rates. Thermodynamics of fuel cells: efficiency, causes of losses, comparison with heat engines.
Advanced Thermodynamics (MECH654) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Thermodynamics (MECH654) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply The Second Law Of Thermodynamics And Exergy Analysis To Advanced Thermodynamics Systems. (Plo1).

Be Able To Understand And Criticize Published Research In Relevant Areas (Plo4)

Be Able To Work On Projects Related To The Thermodynamics Area And To Report The Findings Both Orally And In Writing. (Plo3)

Understand And Be Able To Apply Phase Equilibrium Principles And The Gibbs Phase Rule And To Obtain Relevant Properties For Systems With Different Phases And To Construct Phase Diagrams. (Plo1)

Understand The Chemical Equilibrium Between Species In Reacting Systems And Be Able To Determine Their Stable Concentrations. (Plo1)

Understand The Maxwell Relations And Be Able To Use Them To Obtain Properties And Verify Thermodynamics Quantities. (Plo1)

Understand The Terminology And Be Able To Apply First And Second Law Principles For Reacting Systems. (Plo1)

MECH660.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH660 Mechanical Engineering Seminar
MECH660.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH660
Special topics in Mechanical Engineering presented by post-graduate students, invited speakers from industry and academia.
Mechanical Engineering Seminar (MECH660) > Credit Hours : 0

MECH690.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH690 Thesis
MECH690.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH690
Supervision of research work is made towards the completion of M.Sc. requirements for Thesis option students.
Thesis (MECH690) > Credit Hours : 9

MECH695.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH695 Technical Project
MECH695.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH695
This course involves independent work on design, simulation, modeling, development, or experiments-related technical project in a Mechanical Engineering discipline. Each project must be supervised by a faculty member. Project topics may be faculty-initiated, student-initiated, or suggested by industrial contacts. The student is expected to submit a brief description of a work plan by the end of the second week of the semester and a comprehensive final report by the last week of lectures of the semester. The student is also required to give an oral presentation during that week.
Technical Project (MECH695) > Credit Hours : 6

Technical Project (MECH695) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop a work plan for a technical project.

Apply advanced research and/or design skills to a specific problem related to the mechanical engineering area

Report findings in a well written technical report.

Present results at a high level of proficiency.

MECH711.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH711 Optimal and Robust Control
MECH711.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH711
This course is aimed at an introduction (with rigorous treatment) to the fundamentals of optimal and robust control. It will be divided roughly into two parts. The first will cover aspects of robust control including model reduction, H_2 and H_ infinity control, and feedback control of uncertain systems. The second will delve into optimal control including topics such as the linear quadratic regulator, the calculus of variations, the maximum principle, and the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation
Optimal and Robust Control (MECH711) > Credit Hours : 3

Optimal and Robust Control (MECH711) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Determine robustness through stability margins

Characterize robustness and optimality of H2 and H-infinity controls

Develop skills useful in controlling systems for uncertain systems

Apply optimal control methods to a variety of systems

Propose a robust controller for uncertain systems.

MECH712.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH712 Nonlinear Systems and Control
MECH712.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH712
Introduction to the theory and design methods of non-linear control systems. Application to robotics, vibration and noise control, fluid control, manufacturing processes, and biomedical systems. Mathematical methods based on the theory of differentiable manifolds; non-linear control techniques include feedback linearization, back-stepping, forwarding, and sliding mode control. Additional course topics will include controllability and observability, Lyapunov stability and its applications, limit cycles, input-output stability, zero dynamics, center manifold theory, perturbation theory, and averaging
Nonlinear Systems and Control (MECH712) > Credit Hours : 3

Nonlinear Systems and Control (MECH712) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop fundamental mathematical tools for analysis of nonlinear control systems.

Provide an in-depth treatment of Lyapunov and input-output stability theory for nonlinear systems

Assess the advantages and disadvantages of the different nonlinear methods, and make a qualified choice of method for analysis and design of a dynamical system.

Apply the methods for analysis and design of nonlinear control systems.

Apply this knowledge and proficiency in new areas and complete advanced tasks and projects.

MECH715.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH715 Nonlinear and Optimal Control
MECH715.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH715
This course covers three areas of advanced control theory: nonlinear systems analysis using Lyapunov and input-output stability methods; optimal control including the Linear Quadratic Regulator, Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation, and Linear Quadratic Gaussian design; and nonlinear control design including feedback linearization, sliding mode control, backstepping, and safety-critical control via Control Barrier Functions. Examples are drawn from spacecraft attitude control, UAV guidance, and related engineering systems.
Nonlinear and Optimal Control (MECH715) > Credit Hours : 3

Nonlinear and Optimal Control (MECH715) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Prove stability of nonlinear systems using Lyapunov's direct method, LaSalle's invariance principle, and input-output stability theory.

Design optimal state-feedback and observer-based controllers using the LQR framework, LQG methodology, and the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation.

Design nonlinear controllers using feedback linearization, sliding mode control, and backstepping for engineering systems.

Apply Control Barrier Functions to formulate safety-constrained control laws for engineering systems.

Evaluate control system designs through MATLAB simulation and present findings through a technical report and oral presentation.

MECH720.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH720 Failure Analysis and Prevention
MECH720.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH720
Failure analysis, methodology and procedure. Failure mechanisms: mechanical, corrosion, high temperature. Detection and evaluation of material defects. X-ray radiography, ultrasonic, dye penetrate, magnetic particle and eddy current techniques. Case studies illustrating various causes of failure and prevention techniques: design faults, fabrication, welding, finishing, heat treatment, material selection, service condition
Failure Analysis and Prevention (MECH720) > Credit Hours : 3

Failure Analysis and Prevention (MECH720) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply procedures generally followed when conducting failure analysis

Apply the basic engineering failure mechanisms

Explain the principles behind the choice of instruments and methods of failure analysis

Explain the corrective procedure for failure prevention

Conduct theoretical and/or experimental work, analyze the results and draw conclusions in a scientific or applied research-based term project

MECH730.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH730 Advances in Manufacturing Processes
MECH730.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH730
This course addresses recent advances in manufacturing processes with more focus on non-conventional manufacturing processes. Key areas of research are addressed such as optimization the material removal rate, surface roughness and other output parameters of the nonconventional manufacturing processes, comparing between different nonconventional processes. The course targets graduate student with interest in current trends of manufacturing processes, students who complete the courses successfully will be able it identify the ongoing research in non-conventional manufacturing processes and its real life applications
Advances in Manufacturing Processes (MECH730) > Credit Hours : 3

Advances in Manufacturing Processes (MECH730) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss new trends in manufacturing processes

Describe major scientific advancements in mechanical, electrical, thermal and chemical energy based processes research area

Apply research principles to evaluate the performance of advanced manufacturing processes

Communicate thoughts and ideas in non-conventional manufacturing processes through written reports and oral presentation

Discuss and critique original and recent journal articles of relevance to non-conventional manufacturing processes

MECH731.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH731 Advanced Manufacturing with Smart Technologies
MECH731.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH731
This course focuses on advanced and non-conventional manufacturing processes with emphasis on process mechanisms, performance analysis, and optimization. Topics include electrical, electrochemical, abrasive, laser-based, and hybrid manufacturing processes. Students analyze process parameters and output characteristics such as material removal rate, surface quality, accuracy, and efficiency. Selected smart technologies are introduced to support process monitoring, data acquisition, and performance improvement. The course emphasizes current research trends, real-world industrial applications, and project-based learning.
Advanced Manufacturing with Smart Technologies (MECH731) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Manufacturing with Smart Technologies (MECH731) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze advanced and non-conventional manufacturing processes and trends.

Evaluate process parameters and their impact on performance metrics.

Apply research and modeling techniques to optimize process performance.

Use smart technologies for process monitoring and improvement.

Critically review recent research in advanced manufacturing.

Integrate environmental, economic, and societal considerations in manufacturing applications.

MECH742.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH742 Convective Heat Transfer
MECH742.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH742
This course aims at providing students with essential concepts of Convective Heat Transfer. Topics covered include: Differential and integral formulations of convection Heat Transfer. Parallel and nearly parallel laminar (boundary layer) flows. Similarity solutions. Kinetic and thermal scales. Multiple scale dimensional analysis. Analytical solutions to the momentum and energy conservation equations
Convective Heat Transfer (MECH742) > Credit Hours : 3

Convective Heat Transfer (MECH742) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Derive conservation equations and apply general methods of solving convection heat transfer problems

Explain basic formulation techniques for convection heat transfer

Apply correlations for natural and forced convection heat transfer

Model external and internal convective heat transfer problems

Present results of work either orally or in writing

MECH743.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH743 Energy Storage and Conversion Systems
MECH743.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH743
Fundamentals of electrochemistry applied to energy conversion and storage technologies. Topics include electrochemical thermodynamics, electrode kinetics, and transport phenomena. Energy conversion systems such as fuel cells, solar water-splitting, and CO2 conversion are examined alongside storage technologies including batteries, flow cells, and supercapacitors. The course emphasizes the interplay between materials, electrochemistry, and system design for sustainable energy applications.
Energy Storage and Conversion Systems (MECH743) > Credit Hours : 3

Energy Storage and Conversion Systems (MECH743) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply electrochemical thermodynamics and the Nernst equation to analyze energy conversion device performance.

Evaluate electrode kinetics, Butler-Volmer equation, and transport phenomena in electrochemical systems.

Analyze fuel cell architectures including PEM, SOFC, and their integration in energy systems.

Examine lithium-ion batteries, flow cells, and supercapacitors in terms of materials, mechanisms, and performance.

Design integrated electrochemical systems for sustainable energy storage and conversion applications.

Assess environmental, economic, and societal dimensions of electrochemical energy system deployment.

MECH747.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH747 Solar Energy Systems
MECH747.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH747
Advanced analysis and design of solar-energy systems, covering both photovoltaic and solar-thermal technologies. Topics include device physics and performance of solar cells, solar radiation and collector modeling, concentrating solar-power plants, thermal storage, and integration with buildings and energy-storage systems. The course emphasizes research-driven analysis, critical evaluation of current literature, and development of innovative solar energy solutions aligned with doctoral-level expectations. Students complete design projects for complete solar-energy systems.
Solar Energy Systems (MECH747) > Credit Hours : 3

Solar Energy Systems (MECH747) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze solar radiation geometry, spectrum, and resource characterization methods for system design.

Evaluate photovoltaic device physics, efficiency limits, and system performance modeling.

Assess concentrating solar power (CSP) plants with thermal energy storage systems.

Integrate solar energy systems with buildings and electrical storage for grid-connected and off-grid applications.

Analyze the techno-economic design of solar energy systems.

Evaluate environmental, economic, and policy considerations in solar energy system planning using current research literature.

MECH750.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH750 Advanced Computational Fluid Dynamics
MECH750.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH750
The objectives of this course are to introduce students to general governing equations including Euler equation, Navier-Stokes equation, Diffusion equation and advection equation. Introduce students to Semi-discretization based on finite-difference and finite-volume methods, stability of time-integration methods, and selection of a suitable time-integration method for a given spatial discretization, accuracy and stability of full discretization, development of a CFD code to solve the Euler and Navier-Stokes equations in a simple geometry
Advanced Computational Fluid Dynamics (MECH750) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Computational Fluid Dynamics (MECH750) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze the accuracy of semi-discretization based on finite-difference and finite-volume methods

Analyze the stability of time-integration methods and select a suitable time-integration method for a given spatial discretization

Analyze the accuracy and stability of full discretization

Create a CFD code to solve the Euler or Navier-Stokes equations in a simple geometry

Present results of work either orally or in writing

MECH760.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH760 Advanced Measurement Systems and Data Analysis
MECH760.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH760
Advanced treatment of integrated measurement systems, focusing on uncertainty quantification, stochastic signal processing, and system identification. Topics include time and frequency-domain analysis, parametric modeling, and signal conditioning. The course integrates data-driven methodologies, including machine learning and AI-based approaches, for predictive modeling, classification, and anomaly detection. Emphasis is placed on research-oriented applications such as structural health monitoring and fault diagnosis to support advanced experimental investigation.
Advanced Measurement Systems and Data Analysis (MECH760) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Measurement Systems and Data Analysis (MECH760) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze measurement system principles and instrument characteristics.

Evaluate measurement uncertainty and calibration methods.

Apply stochastic, statistical, and time-frequency-domain signal analysis techniques to interpret measurement data.

Apply data acquisition, signal conditioning, and system identification methods.

Develop data-driven and AI-based methods for measurement applications.

MECH763.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH763 Advanced Spacecraft Relative Motion and Proximity Operations
MECH763.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH763
This course covers spacecraft relative motion and relative-orbit design for rendezvous and docking, proximity operations and inspection, on-orbit servicing and assembly, debris-mitigation missions, and science formations. The course develops nonlinear and linearized relative dynamics about circular, elliptic, and hyperbolic reference orbits. Analytical relative-motion solutions are derived. J2-perturbed relative dynamics and J2-invariant relative orbits are examined. The course concludes with nonlinear feedback control laws for controlled proximity operations.
Advanced Spacecraft Relative Motion and Proximity Operations (MECH763) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Spacecraft Relative Motion and Proximity Operations (MECH763) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Derive nonlinear and linearized relative motion equations for circular, elliptic, and hyperbolic reference orbits.

Formulate relative motion in Cartesian, curvilinear, and orbital‑element‑difference representations.

Design analytically bounded and J2‑invariant relative orbit configurations.

Develop nonlinear Lyapunov‑based feedback control laws for proximity operations.

Evaluate proximity‑mission performance through trajectory design, simulation, and technical reporting.

MECH850.title: UAEU Catalog — MECH850 Candidacy Exam
MECH850.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MECH850
The Candidacy Exam for the PhD in Mechanical Engineering is a non-credit Pass/Fail exam. Students have up to two trials to pass the course; upon passing the exam, the student becomes a PhD candidate. The course is structured to evaluate the student’s breadth and depth of fundamental knowledge in the area(s) closely related to the thesis work. The course committee, in consultation with the advisor, decides on the topic(s) of the course. The PhD student prepares a concise and comprehensive research proposal that clearly defines the research problem and objectives and outlines the research methodology that he/she plans to follow. The concerned PhD student should present and defend his/her proposal in front of the course committee.
Candidacy Exam (MECH850) > Credit Hours : 0

Candidacy Exam (MECH850) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate the depth and breadth of their knowledge in the field of mechanical engineering relevant to student’s research topic.

Propose a well-structured research project that outlines clear objectives, a detailed plan, and an appropriate methodology.

Exhibi sufficient communication skills relevant to field of study and the research topic.

MECH901.text:

MEME621.title: UAEU Catalog — MEME621 Operations Research for Engineers
MEME621.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MEME621
This course introduces a number of models that are efficient and effective in solving certain classes of engineering problems. Students will learn how to apply linear and integer and dynamic programming, forecasting models, simulation, queuing analysis, inventory systems for engineering management decisions.

Operations Research for Engineers (MEME621) > Course Learning Outcomes

Build Models For Real Life Problems Mathematically

MEME635.title: UAEU Catalog — MEME635 Project Management for Engineers
MEME635.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MEME635
This course introduces the life cycle stages of a project and functions of management. Project analysis and evaluation including comparison of alternatives are explored. Project screening and selection. Project organizational structure, work breakdown structures and management of human resources in projects. Conflict management and resolution. Also this course focuses on the basic concepts of project planning including network scheduling techniques including the use of the Gantt Chart and Critical Path Method (CPM). Using PERT for scheduling activities with uncertain durations. Time-Cost Tradeoff analysis. Resource management including resource leveling and allocation. Cost and schedule control. Updating cost and schedule estimates.
Project Management for Engineers (MEME635) > Credit Hours : 3

Project Management for Engineers (MEME635) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze And Apply The Techniques And Tools Used For Project Analysis, Evaluation, Screening And Selection

Apply Project Management Skills, Techniques, And Tools To Meet Project Requirements

Explain Project Management Concepts Including Functions Of Management, Life-Cycle Stages Of A Project, Project Organizational Structures, And Work Breakdown Structure

Use Specialized Software For Project Scheduling And Control

Use The Cpm And Gantt Chart Techniques For Project Scheduling And Evaluate Project Activities With Uncertain Durations Using The Pert Technique

Use Time-Cost-Tradeoff Analysis And Evaluate The Progress Of Projects Using Cost And Schedule Control Techniques

MEME651.title: UAEU Catalog — MEME651 Quality Engineering
MEME651.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MEME651

The course covers techniques of quality control and to utilize reliability consideration in engineering design. This course addresses statistical quality control, quality control charts, ISO 9000, sampling and quality audit, quality control OC curves, Six-Sigma principle.
Quality Engineering (MEME651) > Credit Hours : 3

Quality Engineering (MEME651) > Prerequisites

Quality Engineering (MEME651) > Course Learning Outcomes

Apply The Principles Of Reliability Engineering And Failure Mode And Effect Analysis

Build And Maintain Quality Management Systems For Given Industrial Circumstances

MEME661.title: UAEU Catalog — MEME661 Engineering Process Management
MEME661.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MEME661
The focus of the course is managing engineering processes irrespective of the branch of engineering it belongs to. Topics covered include work systems and how they work, Methods Engineering and Layout planning, integration of Process Information in Manufacturing Systems, Process Safety and Environmental Regulations/Standards (ISO 14001), Occupational Hazards, Ergonomics, Maintenance Procedures and Systems Reliability, Planning for and management of health and safety within a process.

Engineering Process Management (MEME661) > Course Learning Outcomes

Compare And Evaluate Different Work Systems To Choose The Appropriate One And Design A Work System For A Given Work

Comprehend And Apply The Principles Of Work Systems

Design And Develop Facilities Layout For Engineering Works

Design And Develop Health And Safety Systems For Engineering Works

Employ A Systematic Method Study To Facilitate Productivity Improvement

MEME676.title: UAEU Catalog — MEME676 Product Development and Marketing
MEME676.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MEME676
The focus of the course is management of new product development processes, from product definition, design, and ethics through ramp-up of product manufacturing. The Students will be asked to design and develop a product or service by collecting customer and consumers’ needs, analyzing the data, developing a product specification and constructing prototypes. The course will encourage the students to interact with the end users during the product development. The course will introduce the marketing elements to the students in basic forms. This includes, but not limited to, packaging, SWOT analysis, BCG, Positioning, 4Ps. This marketing introductory work will help students to design, develop and construct a product that fulfills customers’ needs and therefore, increase the competitiveness of the firm and the firms’ market share.
Product Development and Marketing (MEME676) > Credit Hours : 3

Product Development and Marketing (MEME676) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe And Apply Systematic Design Process

Explain And Critique Various Design Models And Methods

Analyze, Categorize And Apply The Right Choice Of Design Methods For The Requirements, Specifications, Conceptual Design And Embodiment Design Stages

Synthesize And Execute A Product Development Process

Compose Documents And Make Presentations To Explain The Product Development Processes Of Their Projects

Apply Marketing Tools At The Relevant Stages Of Product Development

MEME685.title: UAEU Catalog — MEME685 Action Project (Capstone)
MEME685.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2945.shtml?id=MEME685

The course explores the impact of marketing, information systems and technology, finance, branding, leadership, Porters factors, SWOT and PESTLE analysis, and innovation on good projects and business plans.
