Topics include ETL/ELT workflows, feature engineering, data modeling, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with vector databases. The course will also focus on real-world case studies in healthcare and smart cities using the DataOps concepts. Students will gain practical experience in building data solutions for AI-driven systems.
AI Data Engineering (CENG500) > Credit Hours : 3

AI Data Engineering (CENG500) > Prerequisites
CENG110 with a minimum grade D

STAT210 with a minimum grade D

CSBP119 with a minimum grade D
AI Data Engineering (CENG500) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the core concepts of data engineering, including data lifecycle, distributed storage, and processing frameworks for AI pipelines

Apply tools for data ingestion, transformation, feature engineering, and real-time analytics to prepare data for AI models.

Evaluate how the integration of DataOps and MLOps practices enhances scalability, automation, and efficiency in AI pipelines.

Design and implement end-to-end data engineering solutions for AI-driven applications in domains like healthcare and smart cities.

CENG510.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG510 AI Systems Deployment
CENG510.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG510
This course provides advanced knowledge of AI systems engineering with a focus on scalable deployment in real-world environments. Students will explore the AI systems life cycle, MLOps principles, and deployment challenges. The course covers parallelism, distributed computing, and hardware acceleration, analyzing CPU bottlenecks, GPU architecture, TPUs, and specialized accelerators. Students will design and implement optimized training and inference pipelines on accelerators using modern frameworks. The course also emphasizes cloud-based deployment using AWS, GCP, and Azure, with hands-on practice in data pipelines, containerization, orchestration, and monitoring.
AI Systems Deployment (CENG510) > Credit Hours : 3

AI Systems Deployment (CENG510) > Prerequisites
CENG310 with a minimum grade D

CENG400 with a minimum grade D
AI Systems Deployment (CENG510) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the principles of AI systems engineering, MLOps foundations, and deployment challenges in scalable AI solutions

Analyze parallelism, distributed computing strategies, and hardware accelerators (CPU, GPU, TPU) for efficient AI model execution

Evaluate optimized AI training and inference pipelines on accelerators and cloud, leveraging modern frameworks and tools

Design and deploy end-to-end AI systems on GPU and Cloud AI platforms

CENG513.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG513 Hardware Testing and Fault Tolerance
CENG513.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG513
The course covers fault tolerance and hardware testing techniques for circuits and systems. The course topics include: reliability, faults and fault models, and metrics such as availability, mean time to failure (MTTF) and mean time between failures (MTBF). The students learn how to derive reliability using reliability block diagrams and Markov chains. The other covered topics are: error detection and correction in digital circuits and systems. The students also learn the techniques for testing digital circuits, for example, built-in self-testing (BIST).
Hardware Testing and Fault Tolerance (CENG513) > Credit Hours : 3

Hardware Testing and Fault Tolerance (CENG513) > Prerequisites
CENG324
Hardware Testing and Fault Tolerance (CENG513) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply Error Detection, Correction, And Redundancy Techniques.

Define Reliability, Availability, Mttf, And Mtbf.

Derive System Reliability Using Reliability Block Diagrams And Markov Chains.

Explain Self-Testing Techniques For Digital Circuits.

Use Different Techniques To Determine Appropriate Test Vectors For Digital Circuits.

CENG521.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG521 Hardware/Software Integration
CENG521.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG521
This course takes the knowledge from a number of prerequisite courses and integrates them into the basis of a hardware and software co-designed embedded systems. The topics covered in this course include: concept of hardware and software, application modeling and analysis, hardware/software communication, performance and trade-offs, state-of-the-art System-on-Chip (SoC), and interfacing and on-chip buses. Hardware implementation techniques using HDL are employed to demonstrate the taught concepts.
Hardware/Software Integration (CENG521) > Credit Hours : 3

Hardware/Software Integration (CENG521) > Prerequisites
CENG324

CENG328

SWEB300
Hardware/Software Integration (CENG521) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze The Data And Control Characteristics Of An Application.

Apply Decision Making Strategies In The Design Process For Optimization.

Design An Embedded Application Employing Taught Techniques, And Analyze The Performance.

Identify The Roles Of Hardware And Software In Embedded Design.

Implement Algorithms And Systems Combinationally In Hdl And Assembly/C.

CENG525.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG525 Generative AI Systems: Models and Prompting
CENG525.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG525
This course introduces undergraduate students to the foundations and applications of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) with a strong emphasis on prompt engineering. Students will explore key concepts such as embeddings, attention, and Transformers, and gain an overview of major generative models, including Transformers, Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), and diffusion models. The course combines theory and hands-on activities, where students will experiment with pre-trained models and apply prompt engineering techniques for generating text and images. A mini-project allows students to demonstrate their understanding by applying generative AI tools to a practical task.
Generative AI Systems: Models and Prompting (CENG525) > Credit Hours : 3

Generative AI Systems: Models and Prompting (CENG525) > Prerequisites
CENG310
Generative AI Systems: Models and Prompting (CENG525) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the fundamental concepts of generative AI, including embeddings, attention, and Transformer architectures.

Describe and compare major generative model families such as Transformers, VAEs, GANs, and diffusion models.

Apply prompt engineering strategies (e.g., zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought) and pre-trained models for text and image generation tasks.

Evaluate generated outputs and present findings through applied experiments and a mini-project.

CENG529.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG529 Networking Lab
CENG529.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG529
This laboratory provides students with a series of hands-on experiments in introductory network topics. It covers the design, configuration and troubleshooting of wired and wireless network as well as implementing basic security mechanisms. Students will gain an understanding of the layered approach to networks and examine the OSI and TCP/IP models to understand their function and services. The lab provides also experimental activities on inter-networking and routing concepts and protocols to develop an understanding on how networks are linked together.
Networking Lab (CENG529) > Credit Hours : 1

Networking Lab (CENG529) > Prerequisites
CENG210 with a minimum grade D
Networking Lab (CENG529) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze IP routing traffic using packet sniffer Software

Build basic wireless communication network

Design and implement a network using various addressing.

Implement network security solutions using various security mechanisms

Perform dynamic and static network configurations and troubleshooting

CENG530.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG530 Computer Network Protocols
CENG530.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG530
This course exposes students to the details of the TCP/IP protocols. Students will learn the IP addressing and sub-netting schemes, data packets delivery and routing techniques. The course covers protocols at various layers with a deep explanation of address resolution protocol (ARP), IP protocol, and transport protocols: UDP and TCP. Students will also learn network troubleshooting using ICMP and routing protocols such as RIP and OSPF. The course also includes an introduction to Internet of Things (IoT), its standards, and protocols.
Computer Network Protocols (CENG530) > Credit Hours : 3

Computer Network Protocols (CENG530) > Prerequisites
CENG210 with a minimum grade D
Computer Network Protocols (CENG530) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the role and functions of each layer in the TCP/IP stack.

Design a network using IP addressing and sub-networking schemes

Explain routing mechanisms and protocols in computer networks

Explain the use and operation of IP and transport protocols

Describe the major IoT concepts and standards

CENG531.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG531 Wireless Communication and Sensor Networks
CENG531.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG531
The objective of this course is to give an introduction to the fundamentals of wireless and mobile communications. The course will cover topics such as RF spectrum, transmission fundamentals, principles of radio communication systems, signal encoding and modulation techniques. It will also cover wireless network architectures, technologies, protocols, and applications. The course will introduce topics related to wireless sensor networks (WSNs) such as WSN architecture and design, routing and transport layer techniques.
Wireless Communication and Sensor Networks (CENG531) > Credit Hours : 3

Wireless Communication and Sensor Networks (CENG531) > Prerequisites
CENG210
Wireless Communication and Sensor Networks (CENG531) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate The Main Concepts Of Medium Access Control, Routing, And Transport Layers In Wsns.

Describe The Key Hardware And Software Architectural Components Of A Sensor Mote.

Discuss Different Modulation/Demodulation Techniques Used In Current Wireless Communication Systems.

Explain Protocols Underlying The Design Of Modern Communication Systems.

Explain The Principles Of Wireless Transmission, Reception, Antennas And Propagation.

CENG532.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG532 Network Security
CENG532.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG532
This course introduces students to the principles of network security with emphasis on network security architectures and mechanisms. Students will learn about network security threats and their countermeasures, types of firewalls, and firewall implementations. The course also covers concepts in Virtual Private Networks and Web security, including IPSEC, L2TP, SSL and SET protocols.
Network Security (CENG532) > Credit Hours : 3

Network Security (CENG532) > Prerequisites
CENG530

ITBP301
Network Security (CENG532) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe The Foundational Concepts Of Vpns

Design Secure Network Solutions Using Various Security Mechanisms

Discuss Network Security Threats And Their Countermeasures

Explain The Operation Of Security Protocols At Various Layers Of The Tcp/Ip Network Model.

Implement Network Security Policies Using Firewalls

CENG533.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG533 Advanced Network Services
CENG533.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG533
Converged network technologies for voice, video and data with emphasis on application layer VoIP protocols (H.323 and SIP); Media gateway controller protocols (MGCP) and the transport of VoIP, and RTP/RTCP; Further topics include:- quality of service (QoS) issues and dimensioning a VoIP network, MPLS, design of VoIP networks, and voice compression standards (G.721, G.729).
Advanced Network Services (CENG533) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Network Services (CENG533) > Prerequisites
CENG530
Advanced Network Services (CENG533) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain converged network architecture, and voice over IP technologies.

Design VoIP based solutions using different network technologies.

Evaluate the performance of a VoIP network.

Identify the benefits and risks of deploying VoIP solutions.

Analyze quality of service requirements for VoIP applications.

Discuss VoIP related protocols such as SIP, MGCP, H.323, and voice compression standards

CENG540.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG540 Embedded and Edge AI
CENG540.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG540
This course introduces techniques and strategies for developing Artificial Intelligence (AI) models on resource-constrained embedded systems and enabling AI-driven computing at the edge level, comprising distributed embedded systems. Topics that are covered include: embedded and edge AI development framework, tiny machine learning and deep learning on edge, edge AI hardware and algorithms, embedded AI accelerators, AI model compression and optimization techniques, and practices of embedded and edge AI in IoT systems and applications. This course also fosters students’ hands-on skills development experience through team-based projects and presentations.
Embedded and Edge AI (CENG540) > Credit Hours : 3

Embedded and Edge AI (CENG540) > Prerequisites
CENG310 with a minimum grade D
Embedded and Edge AI (CENG540) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss the foundations of embedded AI and tiny machine learning models for embedded systems and edge computing.

Collect, preprocess, and manage data on edge devices.

Evaluate the performance of embedded AI and tiny machine learning models in resource-constrained devices.

Design an embedded AI/edge AI system for serving real-time applications.

CENG550.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG550 Selected Topics in AI System Engineering
CENG550.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG550
Selected topics in AI System Engineering is a unique course that covers advanced and emerging topics of special interest to undergraduates. The topics are selected from recent developments and trends in AI System Engineering. The course may introduce new or emerging aspects in the field, contemporary applications and theory in AI System engineering, or assess state-of-the-art through readings, discussions, and critiquing current literature.
Selected Topics in AI System Engineering (CENG550) > Credit Hours : 3

Selected Topics in AI System Engineering (CENG550) > Prerequisites
CENG310
Selected Topics in AI System Engineering (CENG550) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate the feasibility, limitations, and real-world relevance of emerging topics in AI Systems Engineering.

Analyze and compare contemporary methods, techniques, and tools used in advanced AI Systems Engineering applications.

Apply advanced AI system engineering methods and techniques to develop and assess AI-driven solutions or prototypes

CENG560.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG560 Sensor Fusion and Motion Planning
CENG560.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG560
This course provides an in-depth exploration of the essential technologies and techniques used in autonomous systems, focusing on environmental perception, sensor integration, motion planning, and control strategies. Students will engage with various sensor types, including and limited to LIDAR, RADAR, and GPS, to process data in real time and develop environmental representations suitable for autonomous navigation and interaction. The course emphasizes the practical implementation of perception algorithms and their integration into motion planning and control systems for autonomous platforms.
Sensor Fusion and Motion Planning (CENG560) > Credit Hours : 3

Sensor Fusion and Motion Planning (CENG560) > Prerequisites
CENG340
Sensor Fusion and Motion Planning (CENG560) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the core principles of sensor fusion and motion planning in autonomous systems.

Integrate data from multiple sensors and optimize motion planning strategies to solve autonomous navigation problems.

Develop and test software modules for sensor fusion and motion planning to improve autonomous system control and performance.

4. Design and implement efficient sensor fusion and motion planning algorithms for autonomous systems under realistic constraints

CENG570.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG570 Computer Vision and Deep Learning
CENG570.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG570
This undergraduate course provides a comprehensive introduction to computer vision, spanning both classical methods and modern deep learning–based approaches. Topics include image formation, image processing, edge detection, feature extraction and matching, basic multi-view geometry, and 3D reconstruction. The course further covers image classification and object detection using traditional pipelines such as Bag-of-Words and HOG + SVM. In addition, the course places emphasis on deep learning, covering advanced CNN architectures for image classification and segmentation, deep learning–based object detection, and Vision Transformers. Emphasis is placed on fundamental principles, algorithmic understanding, and hands-on implementation using Python, OpenCV, and PyTorch.
Computer Vision and Deep Learning (CENG570) > Credit Hours : 3

Computer Vision and Deep Learning (CENG570) > Prerequisites
MATH140

CENG310
Computer Vision and Deep Learning (CENG570) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain and analyze fundamental imaging concepts, including image formation, basic image processing, and low-level vision.

Implement and evaluate classical computer vision techniques such as feature detection, feature extraction, traditional image classification, and object detection.

Apply convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transfer learning for image classification, object detection and related visual tasks.

Utilize and find-tune transformer-based vision models for advanced tasks and evaluate their effectiveness.

CENG580.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG580 Selected Topics in Computer Engineering
CENG580.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG580
Special topics in computer engineering is a unique course, which covers advanced and emerging topics of special interest to undergraduates. The topics are selected from recent developments and trends in computer engineering. The course may introduce new or emerging aspects in the field, contemporary applications and theory in computer engineering, or assesses the state-of-the-art through readings, discussions, and critiquing current literature. (Pre-requisites: Senior standing)
Selected Topics in Computer Engineering (CENG580) > Credit Hours : 3

Selected Topics in Computer Engineering (CENG580) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply The Specialized Methods, Techniques, And Skills In Computer Engineering Design

Discuss The Methods, Techniques, And Skills Specific To The Topics.

Evaluate The Feasibility And Applications Of The Specialized Topic

CENG585.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG585 AI for Robotics
CENG585.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG585
This course introduces advanced AI techniques for robotics with a strong emphasis on Human–Robot Interaction (HRI). Students will study robot perception, localization, mapping, motion planning, and decision-making, and will apply machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, and learning from demonstration in robotic settings. Using tools such as ROS and Gazebo, students will prototype intelligent robotic behaviors and experiment with emerging approaches, including robotics foundation models and generative AI for simulation. The course examines the cognitive, physical, and social dimensions of HRI, focusing on how humans and robots can collaborate effectively in shared environments. Case studies, coding assignments, and a hands-on group project will prepare students to plan, model, and simulate AI-based robotic systems for real-world applications, particularly in scenarios where full automation is neither feasible nor desirable.
AI for Robotics (CENG585) > Credit Hours : 3

AI for Robotics (CENG585) > Prerequisites
CENG560
AI for Robotics (CENG585) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze state-of-the-art AI methods used in robotics.

Collaborate to design and validate AI-driven robotic solutions using machine learning, reinforcement learning, and simulation tools.

Integrate and analyze AI techniques for localization, mapping, motion planning, and decision making in robotic systems.

Evaluate the accuracy, efficiency, and robustness of AI algorithms and models for robotic tasks under realistic constraints.

CENG590.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG590 Drone System Design and Applications
CENG590.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG590
This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the design and applications of unmanned aerial vehicles (drones). It covers the fundamentals of aerodynamics, propulsion, sensors, control systems, communication protocols, and navigation, along with the use of simulation platforms such as Gazebo, and MATLAB/Simulink. Students will also gain hands-on experience in programming autonomous functions, including path planning, obstacle avoidance, and computer vision based tasks. In addition to technical skills, the course highlights emerging drone applications in agriculture, surveillance, disaster management, and environmental monitoring, while addressing safety, regulatory frameworks, and ethical considerations. By integrating theory, simulation, and project-based learning, students will develop the ability to design, evaluate, and apply drone technologies to real-world challenges.
Drone System Design and Applications (CENG590) > Credit Hours : 3

Drone System Design and Applications (CENG590) > Prerequisites
CENG560
Drone System Design and Applications (CENG590) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the fundamental principles of drone systems, including aerodynamics, propulsion, sensors, and control mechanisms.

Evaluate real-world drone applications (e.g., agriculture, surveillance, disaster management) considering ethical, safety, and regulatory perspectives.

Develop algorithms for autonomous navigation, obstacle avoidance, and computer vision-based drone applications.

Design and simulate drone system components using appropriate software tools and engineering methodologies.

CENG595.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG595 Selected Topics in Robotics and Autonomous Systems
CENG595.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG595
Special topics in Robotics and Autonomous Systems is a unique course, which covers advanced and emerging topics of special interest to undergraduates. The topics are selected from recent developments and trends in Robotics and Autonomous Systems. The course may introduce new or emerging aspects in the field, contemporary applications and theory in Robotics and Autonomous Systems engineering, or assesses the state-of-the-art through readings, discussions, and critiquing current literature.
Selected Topics in Robotics and Autonomous Systems (CENG595) > Credit Hours : 3

Selected Topics in Robotics and Autonomous Systems (CENG595) > Prerequisites
CENG340
Selected Topics in Robotics and Autonomous Systems (CENG595) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate the feasibility, limitations, and real-world relevance of emerging topics in Robotics and Autonomous Systems.

Analyze and compare contemporary methods, techniques, and tools used in advanced Robotics and Autonomous Systems.

Apply advanced methods and techniques in Robotics and Autonomous Systems to develop and assess autonomous or robotic system solutions.

CENG601.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG601 Embedded Systems Design
CENG601.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG601
One of the primary reasons behind the emergence of IoT is the rise of embedded platforms (low cost, small form factor devices with significant processing power) which are powering a number of IoT applications in a wide variety of domains. This course aims to cover trends and challenges in embedded systems design understanding the hardware-software trade-offs, introduce microcontrollers, interfacing these with digital/analog systems and the ability to program these systems. The focus of this course will be on the following topics: Micro-controllers (MCUs) and computer interfacing with analog and digital systems; Real-time control issues; Assembly language programming methods for control; Design of control software; Input/output methods, data interrupts, and general issues in digital signal processors (DSPs); Differences in the architectures, functions, and applications of DSPs.
Embedded Systems Design (CENG601) > Credit Hours : 3

Embedded Systems Design (CENG601) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss the trends and challenges in embedded systems and the different components that make up microcontrollers.

Identify different off-the-shelf microcontroller platforms.

Program microcontrollers and DSPs using suitable Integrated Development Environments (IDEs).

Design microcontroller and DSP systems interfacing with I/O devices and comprehend real-time concepts.

CENG602.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG602 Wireless and Mobile Networks
CENG602.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG602
IoT is multi-disciplinary and broadly involves leveraging sensing and communication technology to solve problems in a wide variety of domains. The objective of this course is to highlight different verticals where IoT has been and continues to be employed. Ubiquitous connectivity is another key reason behind the emergence of the IoT and therefore, this course aims to cover the history, evolution, and developments in wireless and mobile network systems with a particular emphasis on technologies relevant to the IoT (both short-range and long-range). In particular, this course will cover topics on Wireless HART, IEEE 802.15.4, IEEE 802.11ah, Bluetooth Low Energy, Zigbee Smart Energy, HomePlug Low Power Wide Area Networks (focusing on LoRaWAN, SIGFOX, NB-IoT) and 3GPP Machine Type Communications (MTC).
Wireless and Mobile Networks (CENG602) > Credit Hours : 3

Wireless and Mobile Networks (CENG602) > Prerequisites
CENG210 with a minimum grade D
Wireless and Mobile Networks (CENG602) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss the different wireless communication technologies used to build IoT solutions and the role of each one in the IoT ecosystem.

Analyse the different short range and long range wireless connectivity technologies for the IoT.

Evaluate the factors affecting choice of a technology when building a solution.

Build a proof-of-concept prototype IoT application using one of the short range or long range wireless technologies.

CENG603.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG603 Internet of Things (IoT) Systems and Platforms
CENG603.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG603
This course builds on the introductory communication networks course(s) that the students may have taken during their undergraduate education. A brief overview of some of the important topics from the network and transport layer from the undergraduate course is provided followed by treatment of advanced topics, in particular, protocols that have been developed to meet the requirements of the Internet of Things. The specific topics covered will focus on IPv6, network layer protocols such as Routing for Low Power and Lossy Networks (RPL), 6LoWPAN, IPv6 over time slotted channel hopping (6tisch), IPv6 over Bluetooth Low Energy and application layer protocols such as Constrained Application Protocol (CoAP) and Message Queue Telemetry Transport (MQTT). The motivation and overview of different IoT platforms will also be provided in addition to hands-on exercise on how to use the Thingworx platform for building an IoT application.
Internet of Things (IoT) Systems and Platforms (CENG603) > Credit Hours : 3

Internet of Things (IoT) Systems and Platforms (CENG603) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss and analyze the evolution of IoT.

Evaluate the operation of the different protocols for the IoT.

Analyze the different IoT platforms.

Design an application using an IoT platform.

CENG604.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG604 Sensors, Data Acquisition and Interfaces
CENG604.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG604
This course covers a selection of sensors, transducers and the signal conditioning necessary for including these in a data acquisition system such as internet of things. It investigates most common types of sensors, the analogue to digital and digital to analogue conversion principles and their practical applications for data acquisition and control. Examples of a selection of output drivers and devices are also provided. Applications of recording data from sensors (real-time data acquisition and interfaces) in daily life are also provided.
Sensors, Data Acquisition and Interfaces (CENG604) > Credit Hours : 3

Sensors, Data Acquisition and Interfaces (CENG604) > Prerequisites
CENG320 with a minimum grade D

CENG201 with a minimum grade D
Sensors, Data Acquisition and Interfaces (CENG604) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss appropriate techniques and devices for realizing a data acquisition system.

Evaluate sensor, transducer and amplifier characteristics to measure a specific environmental change.

Evaluate the operation of amplifiers, analogue to digital and digital to analogue converters.

Design a data acquisition system utilising smart sensors and transducers.

CENG612.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG612 Generative AI
CENG612.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG612
This course provides a comprehensive introduction to Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI). It explores the foundations of large language models (LLMs), Transformers, and key techniques such as embeddings, attention, and sampling strategies. Students will study major generative modeling approaches, including variational autoencoders (VAEs), generative adversarial networks (GANs), diffusion models, and emerging alternatives such as state space models (SSMs). Through hands-on activities and a project, students will design, fine-tune, and evaluate generative models for text and image tasks. The course concludes with discussions on benchmarking and evaluation metrics, and future directions in generative AI.
Generative AI (CENG612) > Credit Hours : 3

Generative AI (CENG612) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the core principles and architectures of generative AI, including large language models (LLMs), Transformers, and key mechanisms such as embeddings, attention, and sampling strategies.

Compare and apply different generative modeling approaches (VAEs, GANs, diffusion models, and alternative architectures like SSMs) to text, image, and multimodal tasks.

Implement and fine-tune generative models through hands-on activities, culminating in a project to build and evaluate a small Transformer-based model.

4.Evaluate and benchmark generative AI models using established metrics, datasets, and frameworks to critically assess their performance, limitations, and suitability for real-world applications.

CENG613.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG613 AI Systems Engineering and Deployment
CENG613.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG613
This course provides advanced knowledge of AI systems engineering with a focus on scalable deployment in real-world environments. Students will explore the AI systems life cycle, MLOps principles, and deployment challenges. The course covers parallelism, distributed computing, and hardware acceleration, analyzing CPU bottlenecks, GPU architecture, TPUs, and specialized accelerators. Students will design and implement optimized training and inference pipelines on accelerators using modern frameworks. The course also emphasis on cloud-based deployment using AWS, GCP, and Azure, with hands-on practice in data pipelines, containerization, orchestration, and monitoring.
AI Systems Engineering and Deployment (CENG613) > Credit Hours : 3

AI Systems Engineering and Deployment (CENG613) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain and apply the principles of AI systems engineering, MLOps foundations, and deployment challenges in scalable AI solutions

Analyze parallelism, distributed computing strategies, and hardware accelerators (CPU, GPU, TPU) for efficient AI model execution

Evaluate optimized AI training and inference pipelines on accelerators and cloud leveraging modern frameworks and tools

Design and deploy end-to-end AI systems on GPU and Cloud AI platforms

CENG640.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG640 Internet of Things Security
CENG640.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG640
This course will examine the security and ethical issues of the vast implementation of smart devices known as the Internet of Things (IoT). It will discuss IoT technology and market-specific topics, relevant case studies of IoT security vulnerabilities and attacks, and mitigation controls. It will also discuss common security architectures that can be applied to IoT systems and discusses regulations and standards that apply to secure IoT systems.
Internet of Things Security (CENG640) > Credit Hours : 3

Internet of Things Security (CENG640) > Prerequisites
CENG210 with a minimum grade D
Internet of Things Security (CENG640) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss security issues associated with the Internet of Things.

Analyse threats, vulnerabilities and attacks involving the Internet of Things.

Apply security design principles across the IoT stack such as at the device, connectivity, platform/cloud, data and application layers.

Evaluate the use of emerging technologies in addressing security issues in IoT such as machine learning and AI.

CENG655.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG655 Special topics in Computing and IoT
CENG655.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG655
This course covers special topics on various advanced or specialized topics in Computing. Its content is customized on every offering depending on current trends and expression of mutual interest by students and faculty
Special topics in Computing and IoT (CENG655) > Credit Hours : 3

Special topics in Computing and IoT (CENG655) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss emerging trends in computing and IoT.

Analyse new and rapidly evolving computing and IoT technologies and their applications.

Investigate research activities in selected topics of IoT.

CENG709.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG709 Modeling, Simulation and Performance Evaluation
CENG709.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG709
Computer simulation concepts and modeling theory, probability distributions and queuing theory, random number generation, probability distribution generation, data collection and input analysis, discrete modeling and simulation concepts, Monte Carlo" Simulation.
Modeling, Simulation and Performance Evaluation (CENG709) > Credit Hours : 3

Modeling, Simulation and Performance Evaluation (CENG709) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Articulate the significance, similarities, and differences among the modeling, simulation, and performance evaluation techniques

Apply simulation and performance evaluation techniques to develop and evaluate the relative merits of alternative system design models

Analyze simulation and performance evaluation results in a clear and coherent manner

Apply appropriate modeling techniques to real world problems and data sets

CENG742.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG742 Advanced Computer Architecture
CENG742.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG742
This course covers topics essential to modern computing systems including review of current state of computer hardware and architecture; single and multi-core hardware; memory hierarchy and performance; cache hierarchies; cache coherence protocols; pipelining and hazards; quantitative design and analysis; instruction-level parallelism; data-level parallelism; thread-level parallelism; ultra-low power/energy design and optimization; microarchitectures for dependability; microarchitecture modeling and simulation; buses and arbitration; and peripheral devices.
Advanced Computer Architecture (CENG742) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Computer Architecture (CENG742) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate advanced computer architectures including multiprocessor and multicore systems.

Create simulation models of different pipelining architectures.

Create simulation models of different memory hierarchies for performance evaluation.

Evaluate the performance of instruction-level, data-level, and thread-level parallelism.

Synthesize common bus protocol for peripherals.

Create simulation models for improving dependability and power/energy.

CENG750.title: UAEU Catalog — CENG750 Advanced Design and Analysis of Networks
CENG750.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2948.shtml?id=CENG750
This is a course focusing on advanced and emerging research topics in networks. The course topics include advancement of the following; sensor networks such as nanonetworks and IoT, emerging network management methods such as cognitive networks, current and new network paradigms such as fog, dew, cloud computing, state-of-the-art network technologies such 5G broadband networks, Li-Fi, and 802.11ax, and new network services such as information-centric networks and IoT services. The course consists of both a research papers reading/lecture/discussion component and a project component.
Advanced Design and Analysis of Networks (CENG750) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Design and Analysis of Networks (CENG750) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss advancements in network design

Evaluate the performance of the advanced network designs.

Implement advanced network services using network simulators.

Analyze research results related to advanced network designs.

PHTX601.title: UAEU Catalog — PHTX601 General Systemic Pharmacology
PHTX601.text:
This course is designed to teach graduate students the effects of drugs on different organ systems. The drugs acting on major organ systems will be reviewed (the autonomic nervous system and the cardio-vascular, respiratory, kidney, endocrine, gastrointestinal, neuromuscular transmision, antimicrobials and central nervous systems). The course will deal with understanding the molecular basis for the actions of drugs and the characteristics of interactions between drug molecules and those of the substrates of drug action in the cell. This course will be in a seminar format as well as computer based practical programs.
General Systemic Pharmacology (PHTX601) > Credit Hours : 2

General Systemic Pharmacology (PHTX601) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze The Pharmacology Of Histamine, Serotonin And Nitric Oxide, The Eicosanoids Like Prostaglandins, Thromboxanes, Leukotrienes, And Related Compounds.

Categorize The Mechanism Of Action Of Drugs Affecting The Hypothalamic, The Pituitary, The Adrenocortical, The Gonadal, The Thyroid, The Pancreas And The Parathyroid Hormones As Well As Their Clinical Relevance.

Categorize The Molecular Mechanisms And The Clinical Applications Of Drugs Used In Pain (Opioids, Nsaids, Paracetamol, Celecoxib), Movement Disorders, The Uterus, Antimicrobials And Cancer.

Categorize The Molecular Mechanisms Of Action And The Clinical Applications And Side Effects Of Drugs Used In The Cns, Neuromuscular Transmission, Asthma And The Gastrointestinal Tract.

Classify The Mechanism Of Action, Clinical Indications & Contra-Indications Of The Different Sympathomimetics, ? And- ?-Adrenoceptor, And Parasympathomimetics.

Explain The Molecular Mechanisms Of Action And The Clinical Applications And Side Effects Of Drugs Used In Cardiovascular And Blood Disorders.

PHTX602.title: UAEU Catalog — PHTX602 Molecular Mechanism of Drug Action
PHTX602.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2954.shtml?id=PHTX602
This course is designed to teach graduate students general principles of drug actions in the biological systems. The topics are designed to cover most of the major biological mechanisms involved in drug actions. There will also be opportunity to understand current approaches to the principles that dictate interactions of drugs with biological systems.
Molecular Mechanism of Drug Action (PHTX602) > Credit Hours : 2

Molecular Mechanism of Drug Action (PHTX602) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate a broad knowledge of molecular mechanisms of modern pharmacology, from the molecular basis of receptors, to the effects of drugs on whole body systems.

Identify the major classes of drug receptors and sites of drug action within the body.

Explain the principles of pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics and their application in drug development.

PHTX603.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2954.shtml?id=PHTX603
This course is devoted to exploring the biosynthesis, inactivation, receptors, and signaling mechanisms of neurotransmitters and chemical mediators including GABA, glutamate, acetylcholine, catecholamines, purines, peptides, prostaglandins, and histamines. In brief, the molecular and cellular aspects of receptor mechanisms as well as signaling pathways, and effector systems will be discussed. The teaching format includes Seminars and discussions.
Neurotransmitters in Health and Diseases (PHTX603) > Credit Hours : 2

Neurotransmitters in Health and Diseases (PHTX603) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe The Receptors Signalling And Synaptic Transmission

Describe The Cellular And Molecular Foundations Of Neuropharmacology

Describe The Pathophysiological And Pharmacological Relevance Of Amino Acid Transmitters In Neruological Pathologies

Describe The Pathophysiological And Pharmacological Relevance Of Catecholamines, Biogenic Amines And Neuropeptides In Neurological Pathologies

Describe The Pharmaco-Therapeutic Implications Of Neurotransmitters In Psychiatric Diseases

Present The Analytical Techniques Used In The Study Of Neuropharmacology And Biology

PHTX604.title: UAEU Catalog — PHTX604 Molecular Principles of Organ Toxicity
PHTX604.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2954.shtml?id=PHTX604
This course is designed to teach graduate students the mechanisms involved in the actions of drugs and toxins on the target organs. The course will focus on molecular mechanism of chemically-induced toxicity to specific organs in the mammalian species. It describes the principles of cellular and molecular mechanisms of organ system toxicology with emphasis on developmental toxicology, carcinogenesis, immune toxicity, renal toxicity, hepatic toxicity and neurotoxicity.The effects of toxins on respiratory, blood, cardiac, skin and eyes at the cellular level will also be addressed in this course. Various factors affecting toxicity to each particular organ will be studied.
Molecular Principles of Organ Toxicity (PHTX604) > Credit Hours : 2

Molecular Principles of Organ Toxicity (PHTX604) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe The Basic Principles Involved In Toxicokinetics Including Xenobiotics Absorption, Distribution, Metabilism And Elimination

Describe The Mechanims Of Hematological Toxicity, The Approaches To Toxins Hemodialysis And To Delayed Toxins Absorption

Describe The Various Agents That Cause Liver, Kidney, Heart, Lung, Cns, Skin And Endocrine Toxicity And Explain Their Cellular And Molecular Mechanisms Of Action

Explain The Mechanisms Of Toxicity And Principles Of Toxicology Including Impact Of The Dose, The Route And The Duration Of Exposure To A Toxicant And The Animal Models Used In Toxicological Studies

Explain The Molecular Mechanisms Of Developmental Toxicology, Carcinogenesis, Targeted Anti-Cancer Therapies, The Off Target Effects And Principles Of Rna Interference, Oxidative Stress, Cell Cycle And Cell Death

Prepare A Presentation On A Topic Related To The Course

PHTX613.title: UAEU Catalog — PHTX613 Ambulatory Care Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience
PHTX613.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2954.shtml?id=PHTX613
The Advanced pharmacy practice experiences (APPE) are 40 weeks of clinical rotations. The APPEs consist of 10 clinical rotations, 4 weeks each (40 hrs per week, total 160 hours per rotation). The APPEs take place in the second year of the Pharm-D program. APPEs rotations are designed to train students to integrate their didactic knowledge and pharmaceutical care skills into diverse pharmacy practice experiences, with an emphasis on self-learning and increased responsibility. The student will experience a total of 1600 hours in practice areas including hospital pharmacy, internal medicine, general pediatrics, ambulatory care, critical care medicine, oncology, general surgery, and infectious diseases where pharmacists are delivering patient care services to diverse populations. For each rotation, each student is expected to demonstrate knowledge and understanding of pathophysiology, diagnostic and laboratory data interpretation, and commonly used pharmacological agents, and demonstrate the ability to design and monitor’ individualized pharmaceutical care plan utilizing evidence-based treatment guidelines. The students should develop the necessary expressive communication skills and demonstrate the ability to communicate effectively with patients and other healthcare providers. Each APPEs rotations provide students with an opportunity to apply and expand their knowledge and skills, while developing professional attitudes, capacity for self-evaluation and ethical reasoning skills and behaviors.
Ambulatory Care Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience (PHTX613) > Credit Hours : 4

Ambulatory Care Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience (PHTX613) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Integrate didactic knowledge and pharmaceutical care skills of the various disease states commonly found within the ambulatory care setting to assure safe and effective pharmacotherapy and optimize therapeutic outcomes.

Collect, interpret and evaluate patient information to design and optimize patient pharmacotherapy plan that is based on the best available evidence.

Manage the drug regimen by monitoring and assessing the patient and/or patient information, collaborating with other health care professionals, and providing patient education.

Demonstrate effective and appropriate communication with other health care professionals, and patients regarding medication management.

Retrieve, evaluate, and apply evidence-based medical literature related to patient care and problem solving in the ambulatory care setting.

Demonstrate leadership qualities, professional and ethical behavior while working with other health care professionals, and providing patient centered care.

PHTX624.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2954.shtml?id=PHTX624
A broad variety of medicinal chemistry approaches can be used for the identification of hits, generation of leads, as well as to accelerate the development of high quality drug candidates. Structure-based drug design (SBDD) methods are becoming increasingly powerful, versatile and more widely used. This course demonstrates current developments in structure-based virtual screening and receptor-based pharmacophores, highlighting achievements as well as pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetic challenges, along with the value of structure-based lead optimization, with emphasis on recent examples of successful applications for the identification of novel active compounds.
Modern Medicinal Chemistry and Drug Design (PHTX624) > Credit Hours : 1

Modern Medicinal Chemistry and Drug Design (PHTX624) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe Successful Stories In Medicinal Chemistry & Drug Design Related To Countering Drug Resistance & Drug Tolerance And Its Implication In Generics With Focus On The Present And Future Face Of Drug Discovery

Explain The Importance Of Structure-Activity Relationship For Scaffold Selection And Design

Explain The Medicinal Chemistry Rationale Behind Bioisosteric Replacement, Structural Mimicry And Pro-Drug Design For Improved Adme Properties

Explain The Role Of Medicinal Chemistry In Understanding The Rationale Of Drug Design And Lead Compound Optimization

Prepare A Presentation On The Topic Related To Drug Design And Development

PHTX637.title: UAEU Catalog — PHTX637 Pharmacy Practice Research: Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience
PHTX637.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2954.shtml?id=PHTX637
This APPE will guide the student a step by step on how to conduct their research study that was approved at the end of Research project course. The students are expected to collect their research data, enter data into SPSS, analyse data, write study results and discuss their research findings. At the end of this course, the students are expected to submit a final research report in the form of a manuscript.
Pharmacy Practice Research: Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience (PHTX637) > Credit Hours : 4

Pharmacy Practice Research: Advanced Pharmacy Practice Experience (PHTX637) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Collect and document research finding appropriately.

Analyze research data using basic and advanced statistics utilizing statistical software and express findings in the results section of research report.

Discuss research findings and cite literature

Draw appropriate conclusions and speculations from the research results.

Demonstrate scientific writing skills in preparing a final research report in the form of manuscript.

Follow all ethical standards while conducting the research.

PHTX640.title: UAEU Catalog — PHTX640 Advanced Pharmacotherapy 1
PHTX640.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2954.shtml?id=PHTX640
Advanced Pharmacotherapy courses are designed to provide students with advanced knowledge in clinical therapeutics. Students will gain the necessary skills and knowledge required to optimize patients’ treatment and design an evidence-based individualized pharmacotherapeutic plan. The course will discuss treatment of choices, adding and adjusting medications and doses. Goals of treatment and monitoring strategies, drug interactions, and adverse drug reactions will be also discussed for each disease and medications. Pharmacotherapy 1 will focus on cardiovascular diseases (Hypertension, dyslipidaemia, ischemic heart disease, heart failure, venous thromboembolism, Peripheral artery disease, acute coronary syndrome, atrial fibrillation and stroke).
Advanced Pharmacotherapy 1 (PHTX640) > Credit Hours : 4

Advanced Pharmacotherapy 1 (PHTX640) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify aetiology, risk factors, pathophysiology, signs, symptoms and diagnostic criteria of cardiovascular diseases (Hypertension, dyslipidaemia, ischemic heart disease, heart failure, venous thromboembolism, Peripheral artery disease, acute coronary syndrome, atrial fibrillation and stroke).

Contrast the mechanisms of action, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamics properties, indications, side effects, dosage regimens, contraindications and interactions for pharmacotherapeutic options in cardiovascular diseases.

Design an individualized pharmacotherapeutic regimen for patients with cardiovascular diseases

Analyse and monitor patient treatment outcomes for efficacy, safety, adverse drug reactions, and drug interactions and redesign/adjust pharmacotherapeutic regimens accordingly to optimize health outcomes in patients with cardiovascular diseases.

Evaluate patient adherence to medications and counsel patients appropriately on their treatment.

PHTX641.text:

Evaluate patient adherence to medications and counsel patients appropriately on their treatment.

PHTX643.title: UAEU Catalog — PHTX643 Advanced Pharmacotherapy 4
PHTX643.text:

Advanced Pharmacotherapy 4 (PHTX643) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify aetiology, risk factors, pathophysiology, signs, symptoms and diagnostic criteria of Infectious diseases and Critical Care Conditions (CNS infections, upper and lower Respiratory Infections, urinary tract infections, sepsis and septic shock, surgical prophylaxis, invasive fungal infections, skin and soft tissues infections, Clostridium difficile infection).

PHTX644.title: UAEU Catalog — PHTX644 Advanced Pharmacotherapy 5
PHTX644.text:

PHTX645.title: UAEU Catalog — PHTX645 Research Project
PHTX645.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2954.shtml?id=PHTX645
This course is intended to guide the student in the selection, preparation, and the ethical form submission of the research proposal. After the research proposal is prepared, submitted and approved by the ethical committee, the student will continue the project in the (Research project 2). The latter is the actual conduction of the designated research project where the student collects, analyses, and prepare the research report. The student has to conclude the proposal section successfully before moving to conducting the actual research. Research projects suggested by faculty members will be announced to the students at the beginning of each fall semester. Two students will be assigned to each project and supervised by a faculty member. Research project guideline and timeline are attached in the Appendix.
Research Project (PHTX645) > Credit Hours : 2

Research Project (PHTX645) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Search for references in credible and relevant electronic and online search engines.

Analyze data from published literature in preparing a research proposal.

Design appropriate research methodology and statistical analysis

Demonstrate scientific writing skills when preparing the research proposal.

Cite literature in the research proposal appropriately avoiding plagiarism.

Follow all ethical standards in preparing the research protocol and its designed processes.

PHTX650.title: UAEU Catalog — PHTX650 Medication Management and Pharmaceutical Care
PHTX650.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2954.shtml?id=PHTX650
This course introduces the student to their professional and clinical responsibilities as a pharmacist. The course will also provide the students with a systematic approach to patient-centered pharmaceutical care that will be applied and practiced throughout the curriculum and clinical clerkship. Topics covered include pharmaceutical care, medication management services, communication skills, adherence assessment and management, evidence-based medicine, collecting patient history, designing pharmacotherapy care plan, monitoring and adjusting treatment, and communicating recommendations to physicians.
Medication Management and Pharmaceutical Care (PHTX650) > Credit Hours : 2

Medication Management and Pharmaceutical Care (PHTX650) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the sources and collect the essential elements of a patient database.

Analyze patient data to identify and manage medication related problems and medication adherence issues.

Describe the elements of a Medication Therapy Management (MTM) service and how to provide MTM to an individual patient.

Design an individualized pharmacotherapy care and monitoring plan supported by evidence-based literature.

Communicate effectively with patients, physicians, and other health care professionals, including preparing an accurate, concise, and organized written patient care plan.

PHTX651.title: UAEU Catalog — PHTX651 Selected Topics in Pharmacy Practice
PHTX651.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2954.shtml?id=PHTX651
This course will discuss specialized topics that are of relevant importance to the clinical pharmacy practice. This course will focus mainly on clinical pharmacokinetics of selected medications, and social and behavioral aspects of pharmacy practice.
Selected Topics in Pharmacy Practice (PHTX651) > Credit Hours : 4

Selected Topics in Pharmacy Practice (PHTX651) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate understanding of the clinical pharmacokinetic concepts and calculation utilized for therapeutic drug monitoring in clinical settings.

Apply Pharmacogenetics and Pharmacoeconomics concepts and principles to optimize pharmacotherapy and drug dosing for maximal cost effectiveness and benefit risk ratio

Identify ethical issues in pharmacy practice, apply a problem-solving framework to analyze dilemmas, and make decisions regarding appropriate courses of action

Apply social, administrative and behavioral principles in the provision of patient care services

Identify health informatics technologies and patient safety strategies to maintain quality and efficiency in the delivery of patient care.

PHED200.title: UAEU Catalog — PHED200 Foundations of Health and Physical Education
PHED200.text:
This course is designed to provide Health and Physical Education students with a comprehensive overview of the field of health and physical education. Topics cover a range of areas, including health promotion, human wellness, knowledge and skills essential to the development of health and physical education literacy, testing and evaluation of changes. Also, emphasis is placed on career opportunities in this multi-faceted profession.
Foundations of Health and Physical Education (PHED200) > Credit Hours : 3

Foundations of Health and Physical Education (PHED200) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify career opportunities and professional growth in health and sport industry

Demonstrate knowledge of health and physical education literacy

Demonstrate the role of behavioral changes on one’s overall physical activity level and health

Recognize different health promotion models in enhancing human well-being in different societies

PHED201.title: UAEU Catalog — PHED201 Physical Fitness and Wellness
PHED201.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2956.shtml?id=PHED201
This course aims at introducing students to the basic concepts of health and physical education. It covers topics such as health, physical fitness, nutrition, healthy lifestyle, diseases, and drug uses. It also enables students to apply those concepts of personal health in ways that are complementary to each other in various learning settings.
Physical Fitness and Wellness (PHED201) > Credit Hours : 3

Physical Fitness and Wellness (PHED201) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the main components of good health

Differentiate between various effects of drug use on human body

Identify the influences of physical exercise and healthy lifestyle in preventing hypokinetic diseases

Explain the role of nutrition and energy needs

Differentiate between the principles, components and assessment methods of physical fitness with the aid of technology

PHED202.title: UAEU Catalog — PHED202 Invasion Games
PHED202.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2956.shtml?id=PHED202
This lab-based, hands-on course introduces HPE students to the fundamentals of selected invasion games, focusing on skill development, teaching strategies, and game knowledge. Students will actively engage in practice sessions that emphasize skill progressions, offensive and defensive tactics, officiating, and authentic assessment. The course aims to help students gain proficiency in the techniques of various invasion games and model best teaching practices, preparing them to teach and lead these games effectively in educational settings.
Invasion Games (PHED202) > Credit Hours : 2

Invasion Games (PHED202) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate fundamental skills, techniques, and tactics required in selected team games

Design and organize simple defensive and offensive strategies in game situations

Apply the rules and regulations of selected team games in practice and competition settings

Analyze team performance in selected games through field observations and provide constructive feedback

Implement effective teaching methods for instructing team games, including drills and strategy development

PHED203.title: UAEU Catalog — PHED203 Swimming
PHED203.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2956.shtml?id=PHED203
This course introduces the fundamental principles and techniques of swimming, focusing on mastering key strokes such as freestyle, backstroke, and breaststroke. Students will engage in lab-based, hands-on sessions that emphasize practical skill development in the water. Core components include rhythmic breathing, water safety skills (such as floating, treading water, and safe entry/exit methods), and the understanding of aquatic mechanics. Through direct, in-water instruction and guided practice, students will develop both confidence and competency in swimming techniques. By the end of the course, students will have a solid foundation in swimming and essential water safety practices, making it an ideal starting point for beginners or those looking to improve their aquatic skills.
Swimming (PHED203) > Credit Hours : 2

Swimming (PHED203) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate fundamental swimming skills and accurately apply official swimming rules.

Perform a range of swimming strokes, including front crawl, back crawl, breaststroke, sidestroke, elementary backstroke, and butterfly, with correct technique.

Apply proper mechanics to execute essential swimming strokes and movement patterns effectively.

Utilize various swimming equipment and facilities responsibly and appropriately within practice settings.

Analyze swimming stroke techniques performed by peers and provide constructive feedback based on observation and performance principles.

Demonstrate practical water safety and basic lifesaving techniques in aquatic environments.

Explain and apply key mechanical and biomechanical concepts related to aquatic movement and swimming performance.

PHED204.title: UAEU Catalog — PHED204 Human Anatomy and Physiology
PHED204.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2956.shtml?id=PHED204
This is a lecture/lab course with hands-on learning. While lectures introduce the basic structure and function of key human body systems—including the skeletal, muscular, respiratory, circulatory, digestive, and nervous systems—the emphasis is on active, practical engagement. In the lab portion, students will engage in physical activities, body movement analysis, fitness testing, and the use of anatomical models to explore how these systems function during exercise.
Human Anatomy and Physiology (PHED204) > Credit Hours : 4

Human Anatomy and Physiology (PHED204) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze cell structures and fundamental concepts in anatomy and physiology to explain their roles in human body function.

Analyze the structures of the major body systems and their interrelationships within the human body.

Evaluate the functions of the major body systems and their contributions to overall human performance and health

Evaluate the interactions of physiological systems in response to physical activity and environmental factors.

Demonstrate the anatomy and physiological responses of the human body in a holistic context through analysis and application.

PHED205.title: UAEU Catalog — PHED205 Adapted Physical Education
PHED205.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2956.shtml?id=PHED205
This hands-on course is designed to provide an understanding of the methods and practices in teaching physical education to individuals with a variety of disabilities. It is designed to equip future educators with the knowledge and strategies to create inclusive physical education environments.
Adapted Physical Education (PHED205) > Credit Hours : 3

Adapted Physical Education (PHED205) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the field of adapted physical education

Plan and implement appropriate and safe sessions in order demonstrate an understanding of teaching APE principles for children with various disabilities

Design and modify sports settings to meet the needs of individual with a disability

Demonstrate an understanding of the theoretical and practical knowledge of inclusion for all abilities

Analyze and plan effective teaching methods in a variety of settings

PHED206.title: UAEU Catalog — PHED206 School and Community Health
PHED206.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2956.shtml?id=PHED206
This course is designed to introduce fundamental issues related to school and community health. Topics include, but not limited to, environmental influences, health policy, health care system, and students’ unhealthy risk behaviors.
School and Community Health (PHED206) > Credit Hours : 3

School and Community Health (PHED206) > Prerequisites
PHED200
School and Community Health (PHED206) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply school health principles to develop a set of policy and program recommendations that addresses various specific public health problems

Apply skills necessary to make critical decisions regarding health-related issues

Describe the role of schools and their mission, policies, and intervention strategies in promoting health and preventing diseases among school community

Evaluate how each school health program component contributes to the social, health, and academic outcomes of students, schools, families, and communities using both current literature and in-school observations

Understand the relationship of school health programs and their social, health, and academic benefits to schools, families, and ommunities

PHED207.title: UAEU Catalog — PHED207 Exercise Physiology
PHED207.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2956.shtml?id=PHED207
This is a lecture/lab course designed to study the human body under the influence of exercise. The lecture part is developed to provide a comprehensive understanding of body's physiological responses and adaptations to various types of exercises and training conditions. The lab part is designed to allow students to examine the human body under the influence of exercise.
Exercise Physiology (PHED207) > Credit Hours : 3

Exercise Physiology (PHED207) > Prerequisites
PHED204
Exercise Physiology (PHED207) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply physiology concepts to exercise and physical activity

Apply testing methods appropriate to administer fitness assessments

Communicate effectively with students on appropriate exercise issues

Understand and explain the general physiological responses and adaptations that occur in the human body under physical exercise

Understand the role of nutrition in influencing physical exercise

PHED208.title: UAEU Catalog — PHED208 Motor Learning
PHED208.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2956.shtml?id=PHED208
This is an introductory course in motor learning and development. Emphasis is placed on utilizing basic knowledge of the human development and motor learning processes for more effective understanding as to why and how children and adults learn and perform motor skills.
Motor Learning (PHED208) > Credit Hours : 3

Motor Learning (PHED208) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate knowledge of human motor learning and development

Describe the role of memory and attentional processes that influence motor skill acquisition

Design and develop appropriate techniques to practice a motor skill

Develop and design conducive learning environments that help student learn motor skills

Explain the different types of feedback to enhance motor learning

Observe and examine stages related to motor skill acquisition

PHED209.title: UAEU Catalog — PHED209 Track and Field
PHED209.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2956.shtml?id=PHED209
This course aims at introducing the skills and training concepts of track and field. Candidates will learn the mechanics of track and field events (sprints, relays, hurdles, distance, long jump, triple jump, high jump, pole vault, shot put, and discus). Candidates are expected to achieve an intermediate level of skill in the events. Conditioning and rules will also be covered.
Track and Field (PHED209) > Credit Hours : 2

Track and Field (PHED209) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply various running event techniques and skills

Assess peer-performance in selected track and field sports

Become familiar with the appropriate use of tools in track and field

Demonstrate an understanding of rules, regulations, basic mechanics, and training methods in track and field sports

Design and develop strategies to enhance performance

PHED211.title: UAEU Catalog — PHED211 Health and Movement
PHED211.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2956.shtml?id=PHED211
This course introduces students to the concepts of movement education, with a focus on its domains and applications in early childhood education. Students will learn to develop and enhance gross motor, fine motor, and fundamental movement skills while prioritizing personal health and safety. Key topics include locomotor, non-locomotor, and object control skills and the importance of regular physical activity for promoting health. The course will also emphasize the role of family and community involvement, along with addressing the needs of children with special requirements in movement activities. Throughout the course, students will gain practical knowledge for applying these concepts in various learning environments to improve fundamental movement skills in early childhood.
Health and Movement (PHED211) > Credit Hours : 3

Health and Movement (PHED211) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the foundational principles and applications of health and movement in early childhood.

Recognize the role of fundamental movement skills for health in early childhood.

Describe typical growth and development stages in early childhood.

Identify health and safety considerations for early childhood.

Explain methods to enhance fundamental movement skills and physical activity in early childhood.

PHED212.title: UAEU Catalog — PHED212 Early Practicum I
PHED212.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2956.shtml?id=PHED212
Early Practicum 1 is designed to provide students with structured opportunities to observe and practice within supervised, high-quality physical education programs in school settings and sports organizations. This course provides students with field-based experience in learning environments, working under the supervision of qualified educational practitioners. Students will observe the professional roles and responsibilities of physical education teachers, assisting with instruction and working with small groups of students under direct guidance. Students will be accompanied by the UAEU instructor. The course is offered on a pass/fail basis and represents students’ initial field-based training experience within educational settings and sports organisations.
Early Practicum I (PHED212) > Credit Hours : 3

Early Practicum I (PHED212) > Prerequisites
FOED102 with a minimum grade D
Early Practicum I (PHED212) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the teachers’ role in the learning environment

Use observation to gain insight into the key features of the learning environment

Discuss the use of expectations and routines in the learning environment

Describe behavior management techniques used within the learning environment;

Describe differentiation observed within the learning environment

PHED302.title: UAEU Catalog — PHED302 Physical Fitness Conditioning
PHED302.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2956.shtml?id=PHED302
This lab-based course is designed to help candidates develop and assess overall physical fitness through hands-on application of training principles, including cardiovascular endurance, muscular strength, and muscular endurance. Students will actively participate in workout sessions and aerobic exercises, and will be required to design, implement, and evaluate personalized fitness plans. In addition to practical activities, the course includes lectures and discussions aimed at equipping candidates with the knowledge to plan, motivate, and assess school-aged students’ physical fitness. Emphasis is also placed on promoting a positive attitude toward physical activity and healthy living.
Physical Fitness Conditioning (PHED302) > Credit Hours : 3

Physical Fitness Conditioning (PHED302) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate knowledge of physical fitness training principles through practical application and classroom activities.

Utilize technology tools to monitor, track, and enhance exercise performance.

Apply training principles effectively across various exercise environments and workout types.

Implement a variety of structured workout plans targeting different components of physical fitness.

Evaluate physical fitness levels using standardized assessment tools and fitness testing protocols.

Design and develop personalized physical exercise programs based on individual assessment results and fitness goals.

PHED303.title: UAEU Catalog — PHED303 Early Practicum II
PHED303.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2956.shtml?id=PHED303
This course offers students the opportunity to spend time in a learning environment appropriate to their major alongside seminars within the College. Students will have already completed Practicum 1 as a prerequisite to this course. Students will work under the supervision of educational practitioners where they will extend their experience through planning and implementation of sections of lessons and/or small group activities. Students will have the opportunity to engage in reflection and consider differentiation in inclusive practice. This course is a pass/fail course and represents the student’s second training experience within educational settings.
Early Practicum II (PHED303) > Credit Hours : 3

Early Practicum II (PHED303) > Prerequisites
PHED212
Early Practicum II (PHED303) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Plan developmentally appropriate lessons

Deliver microteaching/small-group sessions with effective engagement

Manage classroom dynamics

Design activities for diverse physical abilities

Evaluate teaching effectiveness

PHED304.title: UAEU Catalog — PHED304 Stretching and Body Recovery
PHED304.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2956.shtml?id=PHED304
This course provides an in-depth exploration of stretching techniques and recovery strategies essential for enhancing athletic performance and preventing injuries, including the science of stretching: types, benefits, and best practices, active vs. passive recovery techniques. Students will examine the physiological principles underlying flexibility, muscle recovery, and the role of various recovery modalities, including foam rolling, massage, and other recovery tools, as well as the impact of nutrition on recovery and performance. In addition, candidates will learn to design personalized stretching and recovery programs for different sports and fitness levels.
Stretching and Body Recovery (PHED304) > Credit Hours : 3

Stretching and Body Recovery (PHED304) > Prerequisites
PHED204
Stretching and Body Recovery (PHED304) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate various stretching techniques and understand their applications.

Assess the recovery needs of athletes and design tailored recovery protocols.

Analyze the relationship between flexibility, injury prevention, and performance.
