Work effectively as part of teams or individually while managing ethical and academic responsibility in the execution of a project related to Spacecraft Instruments.

Communicate effectively in written and oral forms the work done related to spacecraft instruments.

PHYS325.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS325 Space Sustainability
PHYS325.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS325
This course addresses the critical challenges of sustaining the space environment amidst rapidly growing governmental and commercial activity. Students will explore orbital debris management, satellite end-of-life protocols, space situational awareness (SSA), and the ethical dimensions of space exploration. Topics include sustainable space mission design, in-situ resource utilization (ISRU), and space traffic management. International policies and agreements, such as the Outer Space Treaty and related UN guidelines, are examined alongside emerging national and commercial practices. Through case studies and a final project, students learn to evaluate risks, navigate legal and governance frameworks, and propose realistic solutions that support long-term, responsible use of outer space. The course incorporates hands-on learning through laboratory sessions, simulations, and design exercises, where students model orbital debris evolution, assess collision risks, evaluate ISRU trade-offs, and develop sustainability metrics for space missions.
Space Sustainability (PHYS325) > Credit Hours : 3

Space Sustainability (PHYS325) > Prerequisites
PHYS310 with a minimum grade D
Space Sustainability (PHYS325) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze the ecological and ethical implications of human activities in outer space to justify the need for sustainable space practices.

Evaluate international policies, treaties, and regulatory frameworks addressing orbital debris and space traffic management, highlighting their strengths and limitations.

Assess near-Earth space hazards related to the increasing population of space objects.

Design effective strategies for orbital debris mitigation, end-of-life satellite management, and responsible use of space resources.

Develop a sustainable space mission plan that aligns with ethical principles, technical feasibility, and existing regulatory frameworks.

PHYS330.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS330 Computational Physics
PHYS330.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS330
This course aims at introducing the basic concepts and principles of numerical methods. It includes: principles of numerical analysis, some important numerical algorithms, mathematical modeling of physical systems, application of numerical techniques to mathematical models, computer simulation of physical systems, the Monte-Carlo method with some applications.
Computational Physics (PHYS330) > Credit Hours : 3

Computational Physics (PHYS330) > Prerequisites
MATH140 with a minimum grade D

PHYS110 with a minimum grade D
Computational Physics (PHYS330) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Create computer codes to problems beyond the reach of mathematical physics.

Evaluate and analyze the difference between simulations and other approximate and analytical methods.

Recognize the basic numerical methods relevant to physics problems.

Use Computers in solving some physical problems numerically.

PHYS333.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS333 Space Communications & Navigation
PHYS333.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS333
This course delves into the principles and technologies enabling communication and navigation in space. Topics include signal transmission, modulation, error correction, and data relay through satellites and deep-space networks. Students will explore navigation techniques, such as GPS, celestial navigation, and autonomous navigation for interplanetary missions. Real-world applications include satellite communication, Mars rover operations, and space-based services. Hands-on projects will involve analyzing signal data and designing basic communication protocols. This course equips students to understand and develop robust systems for efficient communication and navigation in space missions.
Space Communications & Navigation (PHYS333) > Credit Hours : 3

Space Communications & Navigation (PHYS333) > Prerequisites
PHYS310 with a minimum grade D
Space Communications & Navigation (PHYS333) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain key concepts in signal transmission, modulation, error correction, and data relay for satellite and deep-space networks.

Apply various navigation techniques (GPS, celestial, autonomous) to solve real or simulated space mission challenges.

Evaluate communication system design constraints (e.g., power, bandwidth, latency) and navigation architectures for reliability and efficiency.

Design a basic end-to-end communication or navigation solution—integrating modulation, error control, and system constraints—to support a hypothetical space mission.

PHYS335.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS335 Electromagnetic Theory I
PHYS335.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS335
The course aims at establishing the basic knowledge of the static electric and magnetic fields. It includes: electrostatics: Gauss law, electric fields in materials, polarization, boundary-value problems, Laplace and Poisson equations; magnetostatics: Biot-Savart’s law, Ampere’s law, scalar and vector potentials, magnetization of materials, Faraday’s law, and Maxwell's equations.
Electromagnetic Theory I (PHYS335) > Credit Hours : 3

Electromagnetic Theory I (PHYS335) > Prerequisites
PHYS255 with a minimum grade D
Electromagnetic Theory I (PHYS335) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply direct electrostatic laws to determine electric field, potential and energy due to point and continuous charge distributions.

Apply different techniques to solve electrostatic and magnetostatic problems in vacuum and in dielectric media.

Communicate effectively in written and oral form in a subject related to electromagnetic phenomena.

Work effectively on teams or individually while managing ethical and academic responsibility.

PHYS345.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS345 Laser Physics
PHYS345.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS345
The course is intended to develop a clear understanding of the physical foundations of laser operation, laser systems and laser applications. Moreover, the course aims at developing the student's problem solving, skills and creative thought needed to meet modern high technology challenges. The course covers: The basic concepts of laser operation, properties of laser beams, spontaneous and stimulated emission, production of population inversion, optical resonator, pumping process, rate equations with transient & steady state solutions, laser types and applications in science and technology.
Laser Physics (PHYS345) > Credit Hours : 3

Laser Physics (PHYS345) > Prerequisites
PHYS250
Laser Physics (PHYS345) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognize and solve problems related to the laser theory.

Explain the fundamental concepts of laser systems.

Demonstrate the ability to self-learn, work in a team and recognize ethical responsibilities.

Demonstrate skills in oral and written communication.

PHYS355.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS355 Quantum Mechanics I
PHYS355.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS355
This course aims at developing a clear understanding of the fundamentals (concepts, postu-lates, and mathematical structure) of quantum mechanics. It aims also at developing the basic quantitative skills necessary in solving quantum mechanical problems.
Quantum Mechanics I (PHYS355) > Credit Hours : 3

Quantum Mechanics I (PHYS355) > Prerequisites
PHYS250 with a minimum grade D

MATH275 with a minimum grade D or PHYS255 with a minimum grade D
Quantum Mechanics I (PHYS355) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognize the fundamentals of quantum mechanics.

Develop the ability of dealing with the physical concepts quantitatively.

Acquire the basic quantum-mechanical tools necessary in advanced-level physics cours-es.

Demonstrate skills in oral and written communication.

PHYS360.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS360 Space Science Instrumentation
PHYS360.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS360
This course delves into the design, principles, and operation of instruments used in space science research. Students will study key technologies such as cameras, spectrometers, telescopes, etc.. The course covers instrumentation challenges, including the spacecraft environment, spacecraft materials, and spacecraft attitude and orbit control. Also, the course covers spacecraft subsystems and technical instruments, such as for instance spacecraft command and data handling, propulsion, and power management. Students will explore real-world applications through case studies, such as for instance the Hubble Space Telescope and Mars rovers. Hands-on projects will familiarize students with the design and calibration of space science instruments. By integrating scientific knowledge and hands-on projects, the course will equip students to contribute to the development of next-generation space exploration tools.
Space Science Instrumentation (PHYS360) > Credit Hours : 3

Space Science Instrumentation (PHYS360) > Prerequisites
PHYS310 with a minimum grade D
Space Science Instrumentation (PHYS360) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze challenges of the spacecraft environment (launch environment and space environment) and the basic considerations for the materials to be used to build spacecraft and space science instruments.

Evaluate various kinds of space science instruments, such as cameras, spectrometers, telescopes, etc.

Analyze different spacecraft sub-systems, their technical instruments, components, and parameters and how they support space science instruments.

Conduct design work on space science instrumentation in teams or individually, while managing ethical and academic responsibility

Formulate effectively in written and oral forms the work done related to space science instrumentation.

PHYS370.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS370 Space and Atmospheric Physics
PHYS370.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS370
This course provides an understanding of fundamental concepts of physics governing Earth's neutral atmosphere and plasma in the space environment. Students will explore Earth’s middle/upper atmosphere, ionosphere, and magnetosphere. That includes physical properties and processes, such as composition, structure, and dynamics. Also, students will focus on solar-terrestrial interactions, including phenomena like space weather, geomagnetic storms, and aurora. Applications to spacecraft missions, spacecraft operations, and space/atmospheric science will be emphasized. This course lays the groundwork for understanding the complex interactions within Earth’s upper atmosphere and the space environment and their implications for robotic and human activities in space. By integrating scientific knowledge and computer experiments/observational data, this course prepares students to analyze data from spacecraft and ground-based instruments.
Space and Atmospheric Physics (PHYS370) > Credit Hours : 3

Space and Atmospheric Physics (PHYS370) > Prerequisites
PHYS335 with a minimum grade D
Space and Atmospheric Physics (PHYS370) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze fundamental concepts of physics governing Earth’s neutral atmosphere and plasma in the space environment.

Evaluate properties and processes of the Earth middle and upper atmosphere (neutral atmosphere), ionosphere, and magnetosphere, including composition, structure, and dynamics.

Relate the Sun’s activity with space weather near the Earth (solar radiation, solar wind, Earth-Sun-interaction).

Conduct research on space and atmospheric physics in teams or individually, while managing ethical and academic responsibility.

Formulate effectively in written and oral forms the work done related to space and atmospheric physics.

PHYS385.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS385 Radiation Physics
PHYS385.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS385
This course aims at covering topics in radiation and its uses. It includes: types and sources of radiation, radioactive decay processes and energy release involved in decay schemes, interaction of radiation with matter, radiation tracks and stopping power.
Radiation Physics (PHYS385) > Credit Hours : 3

Radiation Physics (PHYS385) > Prerequisites
PHYS250 with a minimum grade D
Radiation Physics (PHYS385) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Differentiate between and classify different types of radiations according to different properties.

Calculate energy quantities involved in nuclear relaxations and draw decay schemes.

Explain in detail the physical processes involved in the interaction of radiation with matter.

Solve for fundamental radiation physics quantities such as attenuation coefficients, stopping power, range, decay times, and yield.

Demonstrate the ability to self-learn, work independently and in teams and to write reports on nuclear technical subjects while managing sensitive ethical issues like originality.

PHYS390.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS390 Introduction to Astrophysics
PHYS390.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS390
The wonders of the Universe and mysteries of the outer space fascinates every human being living on planet Earth. We all find ourselves inherently curious about the objects, events and the related phenomenon, and we strive to know more about it. Astrophysics, as a subject, provides us with the framework to apply laws and theories of Physics to behaviour of various objects and events in the Universe in order build an understanding of their nature, properties and origin. This course is all about how can we best utilize our knowledge of Physics to know more about our Universe in a systematic and scientific way.
Introduction to Astrophysics (PHYS390) > Credit Hours : 3

Introduction to Astrophysics (PHYS390) > Prerequisites
MATH110 with a minimum grade D

PHYS105 with a minimum grade D
Introduction to Astrophysics (PHYS390) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop basic concepts of celestial mechanics and dynamics of the Earth and solar system.

Explain different types of radiation mechanisms in the Universe, the formation of stars, the production and release of stellar energy, radiation mechanisms, distance measurement and stellar dynamics, and the stages of stellar life-cycle.

Analyze and outline galactic dynamics, types, characteristics and the associated astrophysical processes (AGN activity, accretion, jet formation). Identify and describe the elements of Universe at the largest scales: Cosmology.

Analyze Astrophysical information using scientific methods and formulate meaningful research outcomes.

Communicate effectively in written and oral form in a subject related to electromagnetic phenomena..

Work effectively on teams or individually while managing ethical and academic responsibility.

PHYS400.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS400 Planetary Science and Exoplanets
PHYS400.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS400
This course explores the structure, formation, and evolution of planets within and beyond our Solar System. Students will study planetary surfaces, atmospheres, and interiors, focusing on the comparative analysis of terrestrial and Jovian planets. Also, they will study and compare small solar system bodies. The discovery and characterization of exoplanets, including techniques such as transit photometry and radial velocity, will be examined in detail. The course addresses critical questions about planet habitability and the search for life beyond Earth. Students will also analyze selected data/images from space missions (missions related to planetary science and/or exoplanets). By integrating scientific knowledge and observational data, this course equips students with the tools to study planetary systems comprehensively.
Planetary Science and Exoplanets (PHYS400) > Credit Hours : 3

Planetary Science and Exoplanets (PHYS400) > Prerequisites
PHYS225 with a minimum grade D
Planetary Science and Exoplanets (PHYS400) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Judge key factors for the structure, formation, and evolution of solar and planetary systems.

Compare different types of solar system bodies (terrestrial planets, Jovian planets, and small bodies) and how they provide evidence for the history of the solar system.

Evaluate aspects of planetary exploration and exoplanet science, including habitable planetary bodies and the search for extra-terrestrial life.

Conduct research on planetary science and exoplanets in teams or individually, while managing ethical and academic responsibility.

Formulate effectively in written and oral forms the work done related to planetary science and exoplanets.

PHYS410.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS410 Space Applications I
PHYS410.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS410
The Space Applications I course will serve the purpose of introducing the main areas of space science research. An account of remote sensing, earth observation & Geographic Information System will be given followed by the topics of study in space physics. Astronomy & Astrophysics will be outlined as the study of the processes and objects in the Universe. The course will be concluded with the concepts supporting data & image processing and some tools (introduction to Python, IDL and Matlab) and working knowledge of techniques (data analysis & interpretation) will also be developed as an essential skill set to carry out scientific research in the relevant areas of space science introduced in the course.
Space Applications I (PHYS410) > Credit Hours : 3

Space Applications I (PHYS410) > Prerequisites
PHYS200 with a minimum grade D

PHYS235 with a minimum grade D
Space Applications I (PHYS410) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the science done with the remote sensing of Earth and the Geographic Information System.

Illustrate various physical processes discussed within the framework of Space Physics.

Recognize the basic characteristics of objects in the Universe and the associated processes as studied within the framework of Astronomy.

Apply functional skills in some of the computational tools (such as Python, Matlab) to perform data analysis and interpretation for space research.

Work effectively on teams or individually while managing ethical and academic responsibility in executing a project related to space applications.

Communicate effectively in written and oral forms the outcomes derived from space science data analysis.

PHYS415.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS415 Galaxies and Cosmology
PHYS415.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS415
This course provides an introduction to galaxies and cosmology, covering the structure and evolution of galaxies, the principles of cosmic expansion, and the role of dark matter. Students will explore active galactic nuclei, the Big Bang theory, and observational techniques like redshift surveys and gravitational lensing. The course also examines the large-scale structure of the universe and the cosmological models that describe its formation and growth.
Galaxies and Cosmology (PHYS415) > Credit Hours : 3

Galaxies and Cosmology (PHYS415) > Prerequisites
PHYS260 with a minimum grade D
Galaxies and Cosmology (PHYS415) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the structure of our own Galaxy and how it fits into the ‘zoo’ of galaxies distributed through the Universe.

Describe active galactic nuclei such as Seyfert galaxies, quasars, and blazars, and how black holes produce energy through accretion and jets.

Apply cosmological models to analyze the evolution of model universes and examine how this evolution depends on their energy density components.

Evaluate observational evidence to assess and constrain viable cosmological theories.

PHYS420.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS420 Space Applications II
PHYS420.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS420
This course will discuss presenting some more areas of research in space sciences. Firstly, the fundamentals of positioning guidance & navigation using space-based systems will be introduced. Followed by that, an outline of the themes related to atmospheric & ionospheric physics will be given. After that, modern communication achieved with space-based systems will be discussed. The last space applications theme to be outlined will be weather monitoring and prediction using spacecraft. The development of working knowledge of various tools and techniques will continue in this course as well, particularly relevant to the areas covered in this course.
Space Applications II (PHYS420) > Credit Hours : 3

Space Applications II (PHYS420) > Prerequisites
PHYS410 with a minimum grade D
Space Applications II (PHYS420) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the fundamentals space-based positioning, guidance and navigation systems (GPS, GNSS, Galileo, Beidou).

Analyze the behavior of climate, weather patterns, processes in the lower/upper atmosphere determined using space-based systems.

Compare the characteristics of modern space-based telecommunication systems.

Develop skills and expertise in space data analysis and interpretation using various tools and techniques.

Work effectively on teams or individually while managing ethical and academic responsibility in executing a project related to space applications.

Communicate effectively in written and oral forms the outcomes derived from space science data analysis.

PHYS430.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS430 Electromagnetic Theory II
PHYS430.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS430
The course aims at using Maxwell's equations in treating specific problems of wave propagation and their interactions with media and charged particles. It includes wave equation propagation of electromagnetic waves in non-conducting media, polarization. Waves in bounded regions: reflection and refraction at dielectric interface, guided waves. Radiation from a group of moving charges, radiation damping. Electrodynamics and special relativity.
Electromagnetic Theory II (PHYS430) > Credit Hours : 3

Electromagnetic Theory II (PHYS430) > Prerequisites
PHYS335
Electromagnetic Theory II (PHYS430) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply basic principles of electromagnetism to analyze dynamic distributions of charge, systems of conductors, capacitors, dielectrics, and current distributions

Compute the reflected and transmitted amplitudes of electromagnetic waves and the radiated power of moving charges.

Discuss electrodynamics in relativistic form.

Demonstrate proficiency in writing and communicating technical report.

Work effectively on teams or individually while managing ethical and academic responsibility.

PHYS450.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS450 Quantum Mechanics II
PHYS450.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS450
The course aims at developing the student’s fundamental knowledge in Quantum Mechanics. The course introduces several modern concepts in quantum mechanics that include propagators and path integral, symmetries, angular momentum and irreducible tensor operators, approximation methods, and scattering theory.
Quantum Mechanics II (PHYS450) > Credit Hours : 3

Quantum Mechanics II (PHYS450) > Prerequisites
PHYS355
Quantum Mechanics II (PHYS450) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the fundamental concepts of Quantum Mechanics.

Analyze Quantum Mechanics concepts in a quantitative way.

Acquire the necessary physics and mathematics tools to tackle problems of modern Physics.

Communicate effectively a comprehensive term-paper about a topic related to modern quantum physics.

PHYS470.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS470 Solid State Physics
PHYS470.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS470
Students in this course will learn about: crystalline structure and symmetry, Bravais lattice and reciprocal lattice, lattice vibrations and phonons, specific heat, energy band theory of metals, semiconductors and insulators, electric transport in metals and semiconductors, optical, dielectric, and magnetic properties, superconductivity.
Solid State Physics (PHYS470) > Credit Hours : 3

Solid State Physics (PHYS470) > Prerequisites
PHYS220 with a minimum grade D

PHYS250 with a minimum grade D
Solid State Physics (PHYS470) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Compare the different types of crystal structures in terms of Bravais lattices classification

Recognize the basic concepts of the band theory of solids and predict their electronic properties

Construct the theory of lattice vibrations and use it to deduce the thermal properties of solids.

Communicate effectively a scientific report related to modern subject in solid-state physics.

PHYS475.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS475 Semiconductor Physics
PHYS475.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS475
This course will provide students with a solid understanding of the physical principles of basic semiconductor devices. This course will give the students an overview of the development of semiconductor devices. Several important semiconductor physics and prototypical devices will be studied. The course material covers semiconductor properties under thermal equilibrium and under non-equilibrium conditions. Three fundamental device structures will be covered in detail, the p-n junction, the MOSFET and related devices, and the bipolar transistor. The course will focus on aspects of semiconductors such as silicon and gallium arsenide, both of which have commercial relevance. Therefore, fundamental properties of semiconductors will be explored, as well as their device applications.
Semiconductor Physics (PHYS475) > Credit Hours : 3

Semiconductor Physics (PHYS475) > Prerequisites
PHYS231
Semiconductor Physics (PHYS475) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate of the three most basic semiconductor devices, p-n diodes, Field effect transistors (FETs) and Bipolar Junction Transistors (BJTs).

Determine relevant parameters to achieve stated design criteria

Analyze the response of a device given its physical structure.

Communicate effectively an oral presentation about novel semiconductors.

PHYS483.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS483 Introductory Nuclear Physics
PHYS483.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS483
This course covers basic concepts of nuclear physics with emphasis on Rutherford’s nuclear atom model, nuclear properties (nuclear size, mass and abundance of nuclides, nuclear binding energy), nuclear structures and nuclear models (Liquid-drop model and the semi-empirical mass formula, and the shell model). Other topics include nuclear decay and radioactivity, nuclear reactions (fundamental Laws, scattering and reaction cross section, mechanisms of nuclear reactions), nuclear fission (characteristics of fission, energy in fission, fission nuclear reactors), nuclear fusion (basic fusion processes, characteristics of fusion, controlled fusion reactors).
Introductory Nuclear Physics (PHYS483) > Credit Hours : 3

Introductory Nuclear Physics (PHYS483) > Prerequisites
PHYS250 with a minimum grade D
Introductory Nuclear Physics (PHYS483) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the fundamental concepts in nuclear physics and the basic properties of nuclei.

Set balance equations and carefully apply the acquired problem solving skills to solve problems involving production and decay of radionuclides in closed and open systems.

Describe and quantitatively analyze different nuclear reaction mechanisms and apply conservation principles to determine the type of reaction taking place and the possible outcomes.

Describe the role of spin-orbit coupling in the shell structure of atomic nuclei, and predict the properties of nuclear ground and excited states based on the shell model.

Demonstrate critical awareness and insightful understanding of theoretical foundations of nuclear physics topics related to fission and fusion applications.

Demonstrate the ability to self-learn, work independently and in teams and to write reports on nuclear technical subjects while managing sensitive ethical issues like originality.

PHYS494.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS494 Research Project
PHYS494.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS494
This course aims at developing the students’ theoretical and/or experimental research skills necessary for conducting a scientific research project under the guidance of a faculty member. A real-life or active research problem is identified by the instructor and students. Students use their knowledge and get trained on methods to solve the problem. Students will be trained on, literature survey, team work, interpreting their results, implementing the ethics of scientific research, and communicating the whole investigation by means of a written report and an oral presentation.
Research Project (PHYS494) > Credit Hours : 3

Research Project (PHYS494) > Corequisites
PHYS500
Research Project (PHYS494) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Conduct a comprehensive literature review for an identified research problem in physics.

Integrate knowledge of basic physics to analyze and solve a research problem in physics.

Apply theoretical, experimental, and computational methods to address a research problem.

Communicate the results effectively in written and oral forms and recognize ethical concerns in research including academic integrity.

Work effectively in a team.

PHYS495.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS495 Selected Topics
PHYS495.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS495
Physics is a field that is constantly expanding and evolving, with new discoveries and technologies emerging all the time. This course aims to cover selected topics dealing with the recent advances in the field of Physics and Astrophysics. The course will discuss the current knowledge of new emerging topics in modern Physics and related technology. Students will be required to read up on primary literature and make an oral presentation to the whole class on a chosen topic.
Selected Topics (PHYS495) > Credit Hours : 3

Selected Topics (PHYS495) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain fundamental concepts of the topic studied.

Evaluate the relationship of the studied topic with other related areas of physics.

Research and Write a short overview of aspects of the material of the topic studied.

Give a well-informed oral presentation of chosen subtopics of the general area of study.

PHYS500.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS500 Internship
PHYS500.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS500
Students usually choose internship organizations that offer them an opportunity to apply in a supervised manner what they learned in their studies in a practical manner and to apply their rigorous coursework in a professional and industrial setting. In addition to its direct benefits to the student it consolidates the department bonds with the outside world and offers a real opportunity to get feedback about the teaching programs and educational services it offers.
Internship (PHYS500) > Credit Hours : 6

Internship (PHYS500) > Prerequisites
Pre/Co PHYS494 with a minimum grade D
Internship (PHYS500) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Work effectively in a team for a common objective.

Communicate and interact with collaborators and employer.

Commit to regulations, ethical responsibilities and practices set by the work environment.

Demonstrate responsibility and independence in achieving requested tasks.
Introduction to Renewable Energy Technology (PHYS501 )
This course provides a comprehensive introduction to renewable energy systems, integrating fundamental physical principles with engineering applications and economic analysis. Beginning with the basic concepts of energy flow and resource characterization, students explore the major renewable technologies: solar photovoltaics, solar thermal systems, wind energy, hydropower, and bioenergy. The course then addresses cross-cutting themes including energy efficiency in the built environment and industrial processes, as well as energy economics. Through worked examples and a case study (e.g., solar farm with storage), students gain the quantitative skills to evaluate, compare, and design renewable energy systems in real-world contexts.
Introduction to Renewable Energy Technology (PHYS501 ) > Credit Hours : 3

Introduction to Renewable Energy Technology (PHYS501 ) > Prerequisites
PHYS110 with a minimum grade D
Introduction to Renewable Energy Technology (PHYS501 ) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze the physical fundamentals of energy conversion.

Design renewable energy systems

Apply integrated energy efficiency and renewable strategies to improve sector-wide energy systems.

Assess the environmental, economic, and social impacts of renewable technologies.
Fundamentals of Energy Storage Technologies (PHYS502 )
This course introduces undergraduate science and engineering students to the fundamental principles, technologies, and applications of modern energy storage systems. The course focuses on the physical and operational principles of electrochemical and thermal energy storage. Students will gain an understanding of batteries, supercapacitors, thermal storage systems, and the key techniques used to characterize their performance.
Fundamentals of Energy Storage Technologies (PHYS502 ) > Credit Hours : 3

Fundamentals of Energy Storage Technologies (PHYS502 ) > Prerequisites
PHYS110 with a minimum grade D
Fundamentals of Energy Storage Technologies (PHYS502 ) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

1. Explain the fundamental principles of electrochemical and thermal energy storage systems, including batteries and supercapacitors.

PHYS505.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS505 Space Physics
PHYS505.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS505
This course will serve to give an overview of the Physics of near-Earth space. It is intended to build the understanding of physical processes occurring immediately above planet Earth. It will start off with an outline of the characteristics and properties of space plasma including a discussion of various species of particles and their behavior. Followed by that, it will cover the topics related to Earth’s magnetosphere. Then, the aspects of Solar activity along with the elements of Solar-Terrestrial interaction will be highlighted. After that, an account of the characteristics of space weather and its effects on Earth will be given. The students will then be introduced to cosmic radiation, its origins and its interaction with Earth’s atmosphere. Moreover, the dynamics of near-Earth objects such as Asteroids, Meteors and Comets will be discussed including the tracking and mitigation of space debris. In addition, the environment and characteristics of unmagnetized objects (Mars, Venus) and magnetized objects (Mercury, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune) will also be highlighted). Then, a brief history of human space exploration will be given, leading to an outline of the space age we live in today. The course will be concluded with an overview of the methods of space physics research.
Space Physics (PHYS505) > Credit Hours : 3

Space Physics (PHYS505) > Prerequisites
PHYS105 with a minimum grade D

PHYS110 with a minimum grade D

MATH105 with a minimum grade D

MATH110 with a minimum grade D
Space Physics (PHYS505) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain various physical processes in the near-Earth space, fundamental properties of space plasma, species of particles and the aspects of their interactions.

Interpret the underlying concepts of Earth’s Magnetosphere, Solar activity and Solar-Terrestrial interaction.

Examine the characteristics of space weather and its effects on Earth.

Analyze the nature and behavior of cosmic radiation and its interaction with Earth’s atmosphere.

Appraise the dynamics of Asteroids, Meteors and Comets and the distribution of space debris, the potential hazards associated to them and mitigation techniques.

Compare aspects of various methods of space physics research.

PHYS506.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS506 Astronomy & Astrophysics
PHYS506.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS506
This course will develop a good understanding of various astrophysical processes involved in the formation and evolution of astronomical objects such as stars, planets, galaxies. After a brief overwiew about the history of astronomy, we will discuss the fundamentals of celestial and Newtonian mechanics. We will also introduce various types of telescopes, their usability in astronomical observations and how to measure the distances within the solar system and between stars. Students will learn about about fundamental of photometry and spectroscopy. This will enable to them to interpret the stellar spectra and how to mearue brightness and fluxes. Formation of spectral lines in stellar atmospheres and Hertzsprun-Russell Diagram will be discussed in detail. This course will provide a detailed undesrtanding of star formation, stellar evolution and stellar interiors. This course will conclude by giving an overview of galaxy formation and their classification based on the Hubble sequence.
Astronomy & Astrophysics (PHYS506) > Credit Hours : 3

Astronomy & Astrophysics (PHYS506) > Prerequisites
PHYS105 with a minimum grade D

PHYS110 with a minimum grade D

MATH105 with a minimum grade D

MATH110 with a minimum grade D
Astronomy & Astrophysics (PHYS506) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss the underlying astrophysical principles related to various objects and events in the Universe.

Solve problems related to distance measurements, stellar brightness, energetics, relativistic dynamics and mass estimations.

Compare various types of telescopes and various aspects of photometry and spectroscopy.

Interpret models of star formation, evolution and stellar interiors and the associated physical processes.

Examine the properties of the Sun and solar system objects, the solar activity, planetary formation and evolution.

Analyze theories of formation of galaxies, their classification based on the Hubble sequence.

PHYS515.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS515 Methods of Mathematical Physics
PHYS515.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS515
Complex analysis, special functions with applications in Physics, calculus of variations, integral transforms, partial differential equations, boundary-value problems, Green’s functions, operator algebra and tensors.
Methods of Mathematical Physics (PHYS515) > Credit Hours : 3

Methods of Mathematical Physics (PHYS515) > Prerequisites
PHYS255
Methods of Mathematical Physics (PHYS515) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Use of advanced mathematical methods in solving Physics problems

Demonstrate the application of mathematics in different branches of physics.

Develop the learning skills of the students, e.g.: using computers as educational tools, problem solving, and assignments.

Employ computer-related skills to simplify mathematical Physics problems' solutions

PHYS525.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS525 Quantum Physics I
PHYS525.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS525
The course presents the basic concepts and mathematical formalism of quantum mechanics and introduces applications in atomic, molecular, and solid-state Physics. Topics include the mathematics of quantum mechanics, one-dimensional problems, central field problems, the interaction of electromagnetic radiation with atomic systems, the harmonic oscillator, angular momentum, and perturbation theory.
Quantum Physics I (PHYS525) > Credit Hours : 3

Quantum Physics I (PHYS525) > Prerequisites
PHYS355 with a minimum grade D
Quantum Physics I (PHYS525) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply approximation methods to find the spectrum of simple quantum systems.

Describe the fundamental of the quantum angular momentum.

Solve the schrodinger equation for 1-dimensional quantum system such as the harmonic oscillator.

Explain the fundamental notions of state, operator, and a representation of a state.

Demonstrate skills in oral and written communication.

PHYS530.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS530 Electrodynamics I
PHYS530.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS530
Electrostatics and magnetostatics, Electric and magnetic fields in matter, Boundary value problems in electrostatics and magnetostatics, Polarization and magnetization, Multipole expansion and dielectrics, Maxwell’s equations, Conservation laws, Wave guides and resonators.
Electrodynamics I (PHYS530) > Credit Hours : 3

Electrodynamics I (PHYS530) > Prerequisites
PHYS335
Electrodynamics I (PHYS530) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze and solve various electrostatic and magnetostatic problems with green’s function or the method of images.

Analyze the time-varying electromagnetic field as governed by maxwell’s equations.

Demonstrate skills in oral and written communication

Describe all the fundamental aspects of electromagnetism.

Explain and solve problems involving the magnetic properties of a material.

PHYS541.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS541 Atomic Physics
PHYS541.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS541
Electronic structure of one-electron atoms; fine and hyperfine structures, Interaction of one-electron atoms with static external electric and magnetic fields and with electromagnetic radiation. Study of the electronic structure of many-electron atoms using Pauli Exclusion principle, perturbation and variational methods, angular momentum coupling schemes, central field approximation, Thomas-Fermi model, Hartee-Fock method, interactions of many-electron atoms with static and magnetic fields and electromagnetic radiation, Auger effect. Study the structure of molecules and their rotational, vibrational, and electronic structure
Atomic Physics (PHYS541) > Credit Hours : 3

Atomic Physics (PHYS541) > Prerequisites
PHYS250
Atomic Physics (PHYS541) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss the electronic structure of on -electron atom

Analyze the structure of many electron atoms and molecules and their atomic and molecular spectra

Explain the interactions between atoms on one hand and photons and static electromagnetic fields on the other hand

Apply advance mathematical techniques and approximation methods to analyze one- and many-electron atomic and molecular structures

PHYS543.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS543 Advanced Laser Physics
PHYS543.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS543
The course is intended to introduce the fundamental concepts of laser theory and the interaction of electromagnetic waves with matter. The course covers: the concepts of laser operation, absorption, spontaneous and stimulated emission, optical resonator, pumping sources, laser oscillation (gain and threshold), the modulation of optical radiation, Q- switching and mode locking. Moreover, the course aims at developing the student's problem solving, skills and creative thought needed to meet modern high technology challenges.
Advanced Laser Physics (PHYS543) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Laser Physics (PHYS543) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the main physical processes of laser action

Analyze the interaction of radiation with matter

Solve problems related to the laser theory

Illustrate optical resonator design and pumping sources

PHYS545.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS545 Analytical Mechanics
PHYS545.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS545
Elementary principles, variational principles and Lagrange's equations, central force problem, kinematics of rigid body motion, oscillations, Hamilton's principle and Hamilton's equations, Canonical transformations, Hamilton-Jacobi theory, classical chaos, canonical perturbation theory, introduction to Lagrangian and Hamiltonian formulations for continuous systems and fields.
Analytical Mechanics (PHYS545) > Credit Hours : 3

Analytical Mechanics (PHYS545) > Prerequisites
PHYS262 with a minimum grade D
Analytical Mechanics (PHYS545) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognize thoroughly the advanced topics and concepts of classical mechanics.

Apply extensive skills in mathematics and physics to solve problems in classical mechanics.

Develop life-long skills in independent learning and critical thinking.

Communicate findings and scientific results through written & oral presentations while managing ethical issues.

PHYS552.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS552 Nuclear Physics
PHYS552.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS552
Nuclear Properties (Nuclear Radius, Mass and Abundance of Nuclides, Nuclear Binding Energy), Forces between Nucleons (Properties of the Nuclear Force, The Exchange Force Model), Nuclear Structures and Nuclear Models (Liquid-drop Model and the Semi-empirical Mass Formula, Shell Model, More Realistic Nuclear Models), Nuclear Decay and Radioactivity, Nuclear Reactions (Fundamental Laws, Scattering and Reaction Cross Section, The Optical Model, Mechanisms of Nuclear Reactions), Neutron Physics (Neutron Sources, Absorption and Moderation, Neutron Reaction Cross Sections, Neutron Capture, Interference and Diffraction with Neutrons), Nuclear Fission (Characteristics of Fission, Energy in Fission, Fission Reactors, Radioactive Fission Products, Fission Explosives), Nuclear Fusion (Basic Fusion Processes, Characteristics of Fusion, Controlled Fusion Reactors, Thermonuclear Weapons).
Nuclear Physics (PHYS552) > Credit Hours : 3

Nuclear Physics (PHYS552) > Prerequisites
PHYS355
Nuclear Physics (PHYS552) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate well-founded knowledge and understanding of fundamental concepts in nuclear physics, basic properties of nuclei and forces between nucleons.

Describe the role of spin-orbit coupling in the shell structure of atomic nuclei, and predict the properties of nuclear ground and excited states based on the shell model.

Demonstrate critical awareness and insightful understanding of theoretical foundations of nuclear physics topics related to fission and fusion applications.

Make use of appropriate literature, research articles and other primary sources to conduct an assigned appropriate project in nuclear physics.

Professionally report and orally present and defend the results and conclusions of an assigned project and explain and express opinion of ethical issues related to proliferation of nuclear technology.

PHYS555.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS555 Introduction to Plasma Physics
PHYS555.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS555
This course covers elementary plasma physics for physics and engineering students. It includes an introduction to the plasma state and occurrence, motion of single charged particles in static and time varying electric and magnetic fields, plasmas described as (charged) fluids or magnetohydrodynamics; waves in plasmas, kinetic theory description of plasmas, Vlasov equation and collisionless plasmas, collisions and transport properties, in addition to a discussion of nuclear fusion.
Introduction to Plasma Physics (PHYS555) > Credit Hours : 3

Introduction to Plasma Physics (PHYS555) > Prerequisites
PHYS335 with a minimum grade D
Introduction to Plasma Physics (PHYS555) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate critical awareness of theoretical foundations of plasma physics topics and contemporary applications.

Describe and analyze plasma systems using single-particles dynamics in electric and magnetic fields and using collective behavior models such as plasma waves and fluids.

Apply fundamental knowledge of transport properties, equilibrium, stability and kinetic theory to plasma systems

Demonstrate the ability to self-learn, work independently and in teams and to write reports on plasma physics related subjects while managing sensitive ethical issues like originality.

PHYS560.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS560 Elementary Particle Physics
PHYS560.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS560
Description of elementary particles with emphasis on phenomenology and historical and experimental buildup of current knowledge: weak decays and weak currents, parity violation, detectors and accelerators, elementary processes, deep inelastic scattering and proton model, quark model spectroscopy, color symmetry, elements of the Standard Model, successes and shortcomings.
Elementary Particle Physics (PHYS560) > Credit Hours : 3

Elementary Particle Physics (PHYS560) > Prerequisites
PHYS525
Elementary Particle Physics (PHYS560) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognize the fundamentals of Elementary Particle Physics.

Develop the quantitative ability of dealing with the physical concepts.

Demonstrate skills in oral and written communication.

PHYS575.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS575 Physics of Semiconductors
PHYS575.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS575
This course gives students a solid background in semiconductor Physics and devices. It explains crystal structure, band structure and carrier statistics, carrier transport, phonons, scattering processes, electro- and optical- absorption in semiconductors.
Physics of Semiconductors (PHYS575) > Credit Hours : 3

Physics of Semiconductors (PHYS575) > Prerequisites
PHYS470 with a minimum grade D
Physics of Semiconductors (PHYS575) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Distinguish the electronic and optical properties of semiconductors.

Explain the effects of p- and n-doping and PN-junction on the electric and optical properties of PN-diode and LED, respectively.

Analyze IV-characteristics and adsorption spectrum of PN-diode and semiconductors, respectively.

PHYS606.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS606 Space Science Instrumentation
PHYS606.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS606
This course aims at presenting an account of various instruments and facilities used in space science. It will start off with a description and classification of the types of space science instruments such as spectrometers, spectrographs, telescopes, cameras, sensors, imagers and detectors. Followed by that, the scientific principles behind these instruments and the physics of detector operation will be discussed. Then, an understanding of the inputs and outputs of these instruments will be developed. The interpretation of the variations in the observable signatures of physical phenomena will also be discussed. After that, the students will be given an overview of the platforms and facilities on which the space science instruments operate. This topic will include case studies of space missions. A brief outline of some of the specifications and technical characteristics will also be covered.
Space Science Instrumentation (PHYS606) > Credit Hours : 3

Space Science Instrumentation (PHYS606) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe various types of instruments used in space science.

Compare the scientific principles based on which the space science instruments are designed and built.

Relate the inputs and outputs of various space science instruments.

Interpret the variations and behavior of observed signatures from objects and physical phenomena in space.

Examine the platforms and vehicles on which various space science instruments operate.

Weigh the characteristics and technical specifications of space science instruments.

PHYS614.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS614 Modern Statistical Physics
PHYS614.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS614
Review of the statistical theory of thermodynamics, Ensemble theory, identical particles. Quantum statistical Physics, Distribution functions, Applications to Quantum gases (superfluidity, superconductivity, and Bose-Einstein condensation), Critical phenomena, Brownian motion, Langevin, and Fokker-Planck and Boltzmann equations.
Modern Statistical Physics (PHYS614) > Credit Hours : 3

Modern Statistical Physics (PHYS614) > Prerequisites
PHYS312
Modern Statistical Physics (PHYS614) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the main classical and quantum equilibrium statistical physics concepts

Analyze phase transitions and critical phenomena

Elucidate fluctuations and nonequilibrium processes

Solve problems related to modern statistical physics

PHYS622.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS622 Solid-State Physics I
PHYS622.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS622
Students in this course will learn about: crystalline structure and symmetry, Bravais lattice and reciprocal lattice, lattice vibrations and phonons, specific heat, energy band theory of metals, semiconductors and insulators, electric transport in metals and semiconductors, optical, dielectric, and magnetic properties, superconductivity.
Solid-State Physics I (PHYS622) > Credit Hours : 3

Solid-State Physics I (PHYS622) > Prerequisites
PHYS355 with a minimum grade D
Solid-State Physics I (PHYS622) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate advanced periodic structures (lattice, unit cells) onto reciprocal space (k-space lattice, Brillouin Zone) and characterization

Recognize of the properties of metals based on the free and nearly- free electron gas models.

Demonstrate mastery of special material properties such as superconductivity, magnetism, piezo-electricity.

Discuss the applications related to the physical phenomena treated in the course, acquire “knowledge of research principles and methods applicable to Solid state physics.

Acquire deep theoretical knowledge, active and creative understanding of solid state physics.

Communicate effectively, orally and in writing.

PHYS624.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS624 Computational Physics-I
PHYS624.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS624
Classical and quantum Monte Carlo simulation methods with applications, molecular dynamics simulations, random systems, selected topics in modern computational physics problems.
Computational Physics-I (PHYS624) > Credit Hours : 3

Computational Physics-I (PHYS624) > Prerequisites
PHYS330 with a minimum grade D
Computational Physics-I (PHYS624) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Solve challenging physics problems needing computational solution.

Convert a physics problem into formulas then coding the solution.

Apply numerical methods to appropriate physical problem.

PHYS633.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS633 Physics Seminar
PHYS633.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS633
This course is based on a research project where the student is expected to present a seminar at the end of the semester. The topic is selected by the faculty member. Ethics issues related to physics research will be also discussed.
Physics Seminar (PHYS633) > Credit Hours : 1

Physics Seminar (PHYS633) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Review all significant aspects and literature survey of a research problem.

Write scientific journal paper-like reports describing the conducted research activity and its results.

Prepare and practice an oral presentation of the research topic

PHYS650.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS650 Space Science Internship
PHYS650.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS650
The primary objective of this internship course is to afford the MSc Space Science students a supervised opportunity to acquire practical and hands-on working experience at one of the reputed space research and development organizations in the UAE. Within the scope of this internship, the students will be attached to teams of researchers, engineers and scientists at the internship provider site (e.g. UAE Space Agency, Muhammad Bin Rashid Space Centre) to work on practical tasks which will be components of actual and ongoing space projects. Availing this opportunity, students will be able to apply the knowledge they attained as part of their MSc coursework, get first-hand experience in a professional space research setting, learn practical aspects of problem solving, solution development, teamwork, project execution and delivery, and it will also benefit them in terms of skill development and capacity building.
Space Science Internship (PHYS650) > Credit Hours : 0

Space Science Internship (PHYS650) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Generate productive scientific and technological results while gaining practical and hands-on experience of working on a space-related project.

Design space-related solutions as part of a cross-disciplinary team.

Create tools and systems by acquiring non-pedantic skills and expertise required in the field of space science.

Commit to regulations, ethical responsibilities and practices set by the work environment.

Exhibit responsibility and independence in achieving requested tasks.

PHYS696.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS696 Internship
PHYS696.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS696
This course provides Master of Science in Physics students with structured, supervised work experience in a professional setting that is directly related to the application of physics. Students will engage in practical scientific or technical tasks within research laboratories, industry, education, or other approved organizations. The internship is designed to bridge academic study with real-world practice, allowing students to apply core physics knowledge, analytical skills, and problem solving in authentic work environments. Students will document their internship activities and outcomes in a written report that clearly describes their work, results, and learning.
Internship (PHYS696) > Credit Hours : 0

Internship (PHYS696) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply physics knowledge and skills to perform practical scientific or technical tasks in a professional work environment.

Communicate internship work and outcomes effectively through written reports and oral presentations, individually and in teams.

Demonstrate ethical conduct, responsibility, and independence while completing assigned internship tasks.

PHYS697.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS697 Capstone Project
PHYS697.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS697
This course serves as the culminating academic experience for students enrolled in the non-thesis Master’s program in Physics. It offers an opportunity to engage in meaningful research through the completion of an independent capstone project conducted under faculty supervision. The capstone is designed to integrate and synthesize knowledge gained from prior coursework, foster critical analysis of scientific literature, and strengthen professional-level written and oral communication skills. While the project involves rigorous analysis and disciplined inquiry, it does not require original or publishable research and is distinct in scope and expectations from a traditional Master’s thesis. Within a structured academic framework, the course demonstrates students’ ability to apply advanced physics concepts to a clearly defined problem. The capstone extends across two consecutive semesters to allow for sustained investigation and comprehensive reporting of results.
Capstone Project (PHYS697) > Credit Hours : 6

Capstone Project (PHYS697) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Formulate a clearly scoped physics problem appropriate for a capstone-level project and justify its relevance based on existing literature.

Evaluate and synthesize scientific literature relevant to the selected topic.

Apply appropriate analytical, computational, or experimental methods to investigate the defined problem and analyze the resulting data.

Communicate the project clearly and professionally in written and oral formats, while adhering to ethical standards of scientific practice.

PHYS698.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS698 Selected Topics I
PHYS698.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS698
This course will develop a good understanding of various astrophysical processes involved in the star formation. After a brief overview about the interstellar medium and molecular cloud , we will discuss the atomic and molecular gas observations using radio observations and students will be given worked-out examples. We will also introduce detailed observational properties of molecular clouds, physics of molecular cloud, structure and kinematics and various scaling relation, and initial mass function to understand the star processes. High-mass star feedback processes will be introduced with the HII region physical processes. The cloud properties such as column densities, virial-mass, and LTE mass will be discussed. This course will also introduce various astronomical tools and codes for studying the molecular cloud and HII region properties using radio and optical observational data.
Selected Topics I (PHYS698) > Credit Hours : 3

Selected Topics I (PHYS698) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain fundamental concepts of the topic studied

Give a well-informed oral presentation of chosen subtopics of the general area of study

Write a short overview of aspects of the material of the topic studied

Evaluate the relationship of the studied topic with other related areas of physics.

PHYS705.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS705 Quantum Physics II
PHYS705.text:

PHYS722.title: UAEU Catalog — PHYS722 Solid State Physics II
PHYS722.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2957.shtml?id=PHYS722
This is a one-semester advanced course intended for physics graduate students. It will cover the foundational principles of solid state physics, with an emphasis on the application of quantum theory to the atomic and electronic structure of crystalline solids.This course will follow the approach taken in texts such as Ashcroft and Mermin, I will also use materials from Joseph Callaway. The first part deals with the Drude and Sommerfeld models of electrical conduction, the failures of both models, we will make extensive use of your knowledge of statistical physics and quantum mechanics. The second part of the course teaches the electronic band theory from the basics which describes the electronic states of solids. The "nearly free-electron model" and the "tight-binding approximation" will be introduced. First-principles electron theory is discussed as one of the most important topics in advanced solid state physics. Then, density functional theory is introduced. Applications to the electronic states of low-dimensional materials and metallic microstructure interfaces are discussed to deepen the understanding.
Solid State Physics II (PHYS722) > Credit Hours : 3

Solid State Physics II (PHYS722) > Prerequisites
PHYS622
Solid State Physics II (PHYS722) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Master the concepts of the free electron metals: Drude theory, Sommerfeld theory.

Conceptualize the reciprocal lattice in k-space and critique the various methods to calculate the band structures.

Demonstrate mastery of special material properties such as superconductivity, magnetism, piezo-electricity.

Synthesize scientific results and address advanced general questions of modern materials research and propose solutions.

Evaluate the relationship between structure/bonding and electronic, electrical, magnetic and optical properties of solids with emphasis on some of the most important classes of materials as they pertain to the conduct of research in the field.

PRVT113.title: UAEU Catalog — PRVT113 Introduction to Law
PRVT113.text:
The course aims to introduce the student to two fundamental subjects in this field: Law and Rights, emphasizing their flexibility and ability to cope with ongoing social changes. In relation to the concept of Law, students study topics such as the nature, necessity, and purposes of law, in addition to the characteristics of legal rules, branches of law, sources of law, its applicability in terms of time and place, and interpretation. Concerning the concept of Rights, students study topics such as the nature, elements, and types of rights, with special emphasis on the concept of legal personality. Students are introduced to some of the new challenges facing these concepts, including the idea of a legal personality for AI and the rights related to digital ID and electronic dealing in personal data. This course aims to enable the student to grasp the basic legal concepts that qualify them to study various branches of law, to apply those concepts to the rapid development in their society, and to begin training in developing legal skills in oral and written expression, and to provide the student with the necessary foundations of values for legal practice.
Introduction to Law (PRVT113) > Credit Hours : 3

Introduction to Law (PRVT113) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Comply with professional and ethical rules in performing the required tasks.

Topics to be covered in this course include: the definition of consumer, the fundamental rights of consumer, the obligations of the provider, and the liabilities of different parties involved in consumer contracts. The course contains also the study of consumer contracts and the rights of consumer such as the rights to be protected from unfair terms or misleading advertising. Further, it addresses obligations of the seller/supplier such as to comply with producers stipulated by the executive bylaw enacted under the 2006 Act above mentioned before the conclusion of the contract and after that and the legal liability of the supplier/ producer when breaching such obligations.

PRVT213.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2961.shtml?id=PRVT213
This course addresses the study of voluntary sources of obligations under the provisions of the Civil Transactions Law and the latest judicial trends. It focuses on contracts, examining their definition, primary classifications, essential elements (consent, object, and cause), and conditions for validity (capacity and freedom from defects such as duress, misrepresentation coupled with gross unfairness, and mistake). The course explores the effects of contracts on the contracting parties and third parties, as well as their dissolution, highlighting the impact of modern technology on contract elements, including electronic and smart contracts. Furthermore, the course examines unilateral acts as a voluntary source of obligations.

PRVT214.title: UAEU Catalog — PRVT214 Involuntary Sources of Obligation
PRVT214.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2961.shtml?id=PRVT214
This course explores non-voluntary sources of obligations under the provisions of the Civil Transactions Law and the latest judicial trends. It covers tortious acts, their elements, and the associated liability, distinguishing between personal liability, liability for others’ acts (liability of the person in charge of supervision and vicarious liability), and liability for objects’ acts (liability of the keeper of an animal, a building, or objects requiring special care). The course also highlights the impact of modern technology on liability, such as liability for harm caused by AI systems. The course also investigates beneficial acts, including their elements, effects, and applications, such as unjust enrichment, undue payment, negotiorum gestio, and discharging another’s debt. Lastly, the course examines statutory provisions as a non-voluntary source of obligations.

This includes the study of the compulsory execution of the judgment based on its core pillars, i.e. the Writ of Execution and the Judge of Execution. Formulate memorandums and judicial decisions in a clear and correct language.

Deliver speeches to audience fluently and with proper language

PRVT410.title: UAEU Catalog — PRVT410 Nominated Contract (Sale, Lease & Construction)
PRVT410.text:

PRVT453.text:

It includes a study of: commercial papers: the bill of exchange, the promissory note, and the check. Legal and Sharia aspects of banking business: bank deposits, bank transfers, current accounts, bank credits, operations on commercial papers, including electronic operations.

This course deals with original real rights based on a definition of real rights and their characteristics, and a definition of the right of ownership, its elements, scope, and the legal restrictions pertaining to it. Furthermore, this course explores the jointly held property and its division, family property and its rules, and the common ownership and its rules. It also shed light on the different causes of acquiring property, and the reasons for the termination of ownership. Finally, the course addresses the rules of credit guarantees and the legal regulation relating to mortgages and the rights to privilege.

PRVT462.text:

PRVT600.title: UAEU Catalog — PRVT600 Advanced Studies in Civil Law
PRVT600.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2961.shtml?id=PRVT600
This course addresses the recent trends in civil liability according to Emirati law while shedding light on the provisions of comparative law. The course delves into the study of civil liability provisions with a focus on its effects, particularly compensation in terms of its types and how it is estimated, in addition to studying the subject from a comparative perspective. Then, the course explores the modern applications of civil liability through studying civil liability for medical errors committed by robots, civil liability for accidents caused by self-driving cars, civil liability for copyright infringement when using artificial intelligence applications like ChatGPT, civil liability for environmental damages, civil liability for climate change, and civil liability for breaches of personal data.
Advanced Studies in Civil Law (PRVT600) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Studies in Civil Law (PRVT600) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze legal cases and legal texts using sound and systematic legal reasoning in order to develop innovative solutions to legal issues.

Compare different jurisprudential opinions and legislative and judicial trends concerning the concept, performance, and legal provisions of contracts, particularly within the UAE legal system.

Conduct an in-depth scholarly research study on a topic in civil law using recognized legal research methodologies, data analysis, and relevant academic sources.

PRVT601.title: UAEU Catalog — PRVT601 Advanced Studies in Commercial Law
PRVT601.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2961.shtml?id=PRVT601
This course includes studying the legal organization of one of the topics of commercial law in an in-depth manner, such as the company contract, for example, by studying the provisions and details of each company contract separately, with a focus on the most significant legal issues and their impact on the practical and applied reality, with the aim of shedding light on the weaknesses and strengths of the UAE legislation and determining the extent to which the rules of company law keep pace with the challenges and prospects of modern economic life. This course also aims to develop the student's ability to think objectively and analytically by developing his scientific research skills and encouraging him to criticize and judge the legal text. In this sense, this course also examines the difficulties facing the idea of the one-person company and its applications in comparative law and its impact on the general security of the company's creditors. Advanced Studies in Commercial Law (PRVT601) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Studies in Commercial Law (PRVT601) > Course Learning Outcomes

PRVT603.title: UAEU Catalog — PRVT603 International Trade Contracts (E)
PRVT603.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2961.shtml?id=PRVT603
This course familiarizes the students with rules that are applicable in international trade contracts. In this context course provides information related to the UN CISG Rules, UNIDROIT Principles, difference between CIF and FOB Contracts, Hardship and Forcemajeure Clause, damages under UNCISG, Bill of Lading and Letters of Credits. The knowledge of this course enables the students to negotiate and draft international trade contracts, prepare pro forma invoice, understanding of Bill of Lading, and what are the different modes of contracts governing Transport of Goods when the trading is international level (Transport by Air, rail, road and sea).
International Trade Contracts (E) (PRVT603) > Credit Hours : 3

PRVT604.text:

The object of the course is to study methods of resolving disputes other than by litigation in courts. The course will include the main aspects of arbitration agreement, the differences between arbitration and conciliation, the differences between national and international arbitration, arbitration procedures, applicable law, and arbitration award enforcement.
Alternative Dispute Resolution (E) (PRVT604) > Credit Hours : 3

Alternative Dispute Resolution (E) (PRVT604) > Course Learning Outcomes

PRVT606.title: UAEU Catalog — PRVT606 Thesis
PRVT606.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2961.shtml?id=PRVT606
The student is committed to conduct original research on a vital topic of private law under the supervision of his or her academic supervisor, which will be presented in the form of a thesis written according to a publishable standard. The writing stage must be preceded by holding a seminar for the student to discuss the topic of the thesis with the relevant faculty members in a public session. During the writing stage, the student and supervisor must meet regularly to discuss progress and issues related to the topic of the thesis, and the supervisor is committed to providing the scientific department with a periodic report on the stages of completion. The thesis must demonstrate the student’s knowledge and familiarity with the relevant literature and the methodology. The thesis must also be accompanied by specific results and recommendations that are applicable in practice. The form of the thesis must comply with the regulations stated in the Thesis and Dissertation Preparation Guidelines, issued by the College of Graduate Studies, and it must pass the stage of scrutiny and verification of the absence of plagiarism or scientific theft through certain programs, including Turnitin. After completing writing it, it will be discussed in a public session by a specialized committee that includes an external examiner and an internal examiner headed by the supervisor.
Thesis (PRVT606) > Credit Hours : 7

Thesis (PRVT606) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyzes legal issues and provisions properly to provide innovative solutions for legal problems

Compares jurisprudence, various judicial and legislative trends, especially in the UAE legal system

Criticize jurisprudential and judicial view points and trends in general, and within the UAE legal system in particular

Undertake in-depth scientific research in a field of the Private Law utilizing curriculum-based legal research methods and drawing from scientific sources

Performs tasks assigned to him/her in a professional and ethical manner

Demonstrate self-learning skills with regard to real and novel issues.

PRVT607.title: UAEU Catalog — PRVT607 World Trade Agreements (E)
PRVT607.text:
