This course examines the multilateral and regional legal regimes governing importation and exportation of goods across national borders. Key topics include the history and institutions of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) and World Trade Organization (WTO), accession to the WTO, dispute settlement under WTO rules, transparency and participation in the GATT-WTO system, regulation of import duties and non-tariff barriers, rules on customs classification and valuation.
World Trade Agreements (E) (PRVT607) > Credit Hours : 3

World Trade Agreements (E) (PRVT607) > Course Learning Outcomes

Present legal arguments that are coherent and based on proper methodology with confidence.

Therefore, this course deals with the following topics: the legal requirement of e-commerce, the electronic contract and its elements, electronic signature, the legislative framework for electronic authentication services, electronic consumer protection, the validity and evidential weight of e-mails and electronic records, and other related topics.

PRVT612.title: UAEU Catalog — PRVT612 Advanced Studies in Insurance Contract
PRVT612.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2961.shtml?id=PRVT612
This course includes studying the definition of insurance contract, identifying its characteristics, and distinguishing it from other named contracts. Its pillars are based on mutual consent and the subject matter that fundamentally involves risks. The course examines its effects by defining the obligations of the insured and the insurer. It also addresses the study of contractual models (insurance documents) in the insurance contract and how the insured is protected from arbitrary provisions therein as a consumer, especially since these models are unilaterally drafted by the insurer as the stronger party in the contractual relationship and the insured has no right to amend them. It explains and analyzes the levels of legal protection for the insured in terms of general contract theory and the judicial authorities concerning arbitrary contractual provisions in insurance contracts, considering the insured as a consumer and how to protect them according to this legal description, then in terms of decisions of the Higher Insurance Authority in Abu Dhabi and the extent to which the insured benefits from them. The course instructor selects a deep topic from these terms after covering an overview of all the course vocabulary in the first two weeks of the semester. For example, the instructor may choose the risk insured against, or discuss the terms of compensation in compulsory insurance, or address the topic of contingent rights in an insurance contract.
Advanced Studies in Insurance Contract (PRVT612) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Studies in Insurance Contract (PRVT612) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze legal cases and legal texts using sound and systematic legal reasoning.

Conduct an in-depth scholarly research study in a field of private law using recognized legal research methodologies, data analysis, and relevant academic sources.

Present legal arguments confidently and in a clear, systematic manner.

PRVT613.text:

This course deals with the protection and scope of copyright and related rights, patent rights, design rights, the rights of the designer of the layout designs of integrated circuits, the rights of the creator of plant varieties in national laws and international agreements such as the Berne Convention, TRIPS Agreement, and Paris Convention. This course also examines the obligations of the owners of these rights, the compulsory and optional licensing of these rights, and the duration of protection. Further, it discusses the role of some international organizations in regulating intellectual property rights and the legal issues arising in this regard along with their practical impact on sectors such as the pharmaceutical sector and the radio and television broadcasting sector. The course discusses also the collective management of copyright and its role in protecting copyright in the digital environment. Furthermore, the course covers trademarks, undisclosed information, and unfair competition. After providing a comprehensive overview of the above topics, the course professor focuses the course on discussing in depth one or more of these topics.

PRVT707.text:

PRVT711.text:

This course shall examine deeply the process for advancing claims in the civil law context. It is essentially a course that will provide students with the framework for commencing a proceeding the civil court and/or responding to a claim that has been advanced. It will focus on examining the Rules of Civil Procedure, which will be augmented with a discussion of case law and how the rules have been interpreted.This course is based on writing researches and discussing issues relating to the rules governing the litigation process according to the UAE and Comparative laws. PRVT712.title: UAEU Catalog — PRVT712 Companies Law and Investment Legislation - E
PRVT712.text:

By encouraging students to conduct presentations; discuss recent issues relating to companies and investment in the State, produce written work and collaborate with peers on set tasks or projects, this course will develop the ability of PhD students to delineate and evaluate issues, think analytically, select relevant materials and produce reasoned arguments encompassing policy, existing practice and knowledge.

PRVT716.text:

ETHC600.title: UAEU Catalog — ETHC600 Ethical Conduct in Medical Research
ETHC600.text:
Bioethics is the philosophical study of the controversies brought about by advances in biology and medicine. On the other hand, medical ethics is primarily a field of applied ethics, the study of moral values and judgments as they apply to medicine. When moral values are in conflict, the result may be an ethical dilemma or crisis. This course is designed to study the ethics with an integrated multi-cultural approach. The course will provide opportunity to acquire practical skills of dealing with daily practice ethical dilemmas. It will also provide experience to develop ethical frameworks which can incorporate different cultures in the cosmopolitan society we live and the era of globalization.
Ethical Conduct in Medical Research (ETHC600) > Credit Hours : 1

Ethical Conduct in Medical Research (ETHC600) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Acquire and demonstrate (through discussions and assignments) practical skills of dealing with daily practice ethical dilemmas.

Develop theoretical ethical frameworks which can incorporate culture in this era of globalization.

Apply principles of ethics in laboratory and human research to real life scenarios.

Synthesize information learned through preparation of group assignments.

Evaluate and critique the current relevant literature during presentation of group assignments.

GELW111.title: UAEU Catalog — GELW111 Advanced Arabic Language Skills for Law
GELW111.text:
This course has two main objectives: First, to make law students aware of the importance of language, helping them understand that mastering it allows for precise legal expression and provides a correct understanding of legal texts. Second, to develop their speaking and linguistic abilities, enhancing their capacity to analyze and communicate legal discourse effectively. Therefore, the course is divided into four units: Grammar, Analytical Reading, Legal Writing, and Speaking. The first unit (Grammar) aims to ensure students master key grammatical concepts based on their high school studies, with an emphasis on essential grammar rules. The second unit (Analytical Reading) is designed to teach students how to read legal texts accurately and analyze them linguistically and semantically, facilitating correct understanding and interpretation. The third unit (Legal Writing) focuses on training students to write legally precise texts, free of grammatical and stylistic errors, and to practice writing on topics relevant to their studies in law school. The fourth unit (Speaking) aims to equip students with the skills for effective legal delivery and the correct oral presentation of legal texts.
Advanced Arabic Language Skills for Law (GELW111) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Arabic Language Skills for Law (GELW111) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the content of readable legal texts.

Use classical Arabic in functional Writing.

Deliver speeches to audience with confidence and proper language.

LAW115.title: UAEU Catalog — LAW115 Legal Research Methodology
LAW115.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=LAW115
This course is divided into two parts, the first one is theoretical, and the second one is practical. In the first part, the instructor provides the student with the necessary knowledge to write a research based on scientific standards, by explaining the various levels and types of legal scientific research, scientific resources and tools, and how to systematically combine and organize these resources. In addition to, explaining how to choose a research topic and research methods in the legal field and how to develop a research plan. Then, to provide basic guidelines on legal writing, and documentation of resources, and ethics to be adhered by the scholar. Whereas, in the second part the student is asked to write a research and apply the theorical knowledge of legal research methodology under the supervision of the instructor.
Legal Research Methodology (LAW115) > Credit Hours : 3

Legal Research Methodology (LAW115) > Prerequisites
PRVT113 with a minimum grade D
Legal Research Methodology (LAW115) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the concepts and rules of legal writing.

Write a scientific research in accordance with legal research methodologies.

Deliver speeches to audience fluently and with proper language

LAW228.title: UAEU Catalog — LAW228 English Legal Terminology
LAW228.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=LAW228
This course provides students with the meaning and use of a wide range of legal English vocabulary and phrases used in fundamental areas of law. Through the examination of key law paragraphs, principles, and themes, the course provides an interactive learning style to enhance students' ability to read and understand legal texts and vocabulary in the English language.
English Legal Terminology (LAW228) > Credit Hours : 3

English Legal Terminology (LAW228) > Prerequisites
PRVT213 with a minimum grade D

PRVT227 with a minimum grade D

PUBL215 with a minimum grade D
English Legal Terminology (LAW228) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the precise meanings and definitions of basic English legal terms

Communicate more effectively in English in a legal professional context

Lead a team to complete assignments on a specific course topic

LAW230.title: UAEU Catalog — LAW230 Selected Studies in Comparative Law (E)
LAW230.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=LAW230
This course introduces students to legal concepts, principles and procedures of comparative law. The course provides students with a broad understanding of the different legal systems which exist globally; their historical backgrounds; sources of law and major legal institutions. It also considers selected topics in private law, such as the formation of contract, Arbitration, and the main types of companies. On the other hand, this course includes the study of some selected areas of public law, i.e. International Law, Administrative Law, Constitutional Law, and Criminal Law.
Selected Studies in Comparative Law (E) (LAW230) > Credit Hours : 3

Selected Studies in Comparative Law (E) (LAW230) > Prerequisites
LAW228 with a minimum grade D
Selected Studies in Comparative Law (E) (LAW230) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the basic concepts and rules of law, especially Emirati and comparative law

Learn independently through scientific developments in the field of comparative law

Lead a team positively.

LAW340.title: UAEU Catalog — LAW340 Training 1
LAW340.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=LAW340
The course provides training for students on performing the basic tasks carried out by legal professionals in practice. It involves training in researching legal rules necessary for addressing real-world problems. It also involves training in exercising legal expression both in writing and orally, through writing various legal documents such as memoranda of legal opinion, statements of claims, defence memos, judicial decisions and contracts, in addition to oral pleadings. Students are also provided with the values that a legal professional must adhere to when practicing his profession. Furthermore, the course includes organizing practical field visits to training bodies such as courts, public prosecution offices, international law firms, and arbitration centres, and hosting several professional experts from these institutions.
Training 1 (LAW340) > Credit Hours : 3

Training 1 (LAW340) > Prerequisites
PRVT338 with a minimum grade D

PRVT302 with a minimum grade D

PRVT304 with a minimum grade D

PUBL329 with a minimum grade D

PUBL305 with a minimum grade D

PUBL335 with a minimum grade D

PRVT307 with a minimum grade D

PRVT327 with a minimum grade D
Training 1 (LAW340) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Draft memoranda, statements of claim and judicial rulings in an appropriate language.

Speak to audience clearly and confidently.

Demonstrate self-learning through scientific and practical developments in the field of law

LAW400.title: UAEU Catalog — LAW400 Artificial Intelligence and the Law
LAW400.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=LAW400
This course aims to study the legal and ethical implications of the use of artificial intelligence in various areas of life. This includes private relationships: i.e., its impact on contract formation and execution, intellectual property rights, tort liability, and dispute resolution through the judiciary and alternative methods. It also covers aspects of public law, particularly in the areas of criminalization, punishment, and criminal procedures, as well as constitutional rights, privacy, and the impact of AI on public administration governance. The course places special emphasis on practical applications in both national and comparative judicial systems.
Artificial Intelligence and the Law (LAW400) > Credit Hours : 3

Artificial Intelligence and the Law (LAW400) > Prerequisites
PRVT302 with a minimum grade D

PRVT307 with a minimum grade D

PRVT304 with a minimum grade D

PUBL305 with a minimum grade D

PUBL311 with a minimum grade D

PRVT327 with a minimum grade D

PUBL329 with a minimum grade D

PUBL335 with a minimum grade D

PRVT338 with a minimum grade D
Artificial Intelligence and the Law (LAW400) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Interpret the legal rules governing artificial intelligence in accordance with well-established rules of interpretation.

Apply legal rules correctly to the issues raised by artificial intelligence.

Demonstrate self-management and independent learning skills with regard to the field of AI and the law.

LAW440.title: UAEU Catalog — LAW440 Training 2
LAW440.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=LAW440
The course of external training aims to provide the student of the College of Law with the proper legal training at those institutions that are involved, at different levels, in the application of the law. Its objective is to reinforce the students’ theoretical and practical knowledge which were gained throughout their studies in the classes. The course also seeks to familiarize students with the work environment and the processes implemented in the judiciary, in specific, and other legal institutions, in general. (The course is conducted over 6 weeks in any of last year semesters (including Summer). No courses are allowed to be registered during the internship).
Training 2 (LAW440) > Credit Hours : 1

Training 2 (LAW440) > Prerequisites
PRVT302 with a minimum grade D

PRVT304 with a minimum grade D

PUBL305 with a minimum grade D

PRVT338 with a minimum grade D

PUBL335 with a minimum grade D

PRVT327 with a minimum grade D

PUBL329 with a minimum grade D
Training 2 (LAW440) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply legal rules to the actual facts in a correct manner

Formulate memorandums and judicial decisions in a clear and correct language

Deliver speeches to audience fluently and with proper language

Comply with professional and ethical rules in performing the required tasks.

LAW666.title: UAEU Catalog — LAW666 Legal Research
LAW666.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=LAW666
This course revolves around the fundamentals of legal research in terms of the concept of legal research, its levels and types, methodologies, sources and tools for collecting scientific material, and the principles of legal writing. It also covers the ethics of scientific research in the field of law and how to practice proper oral expression linked to research activity at all stages. Based on the foregoing, the student is tasked with preparing one legal research paper ranging between 15 and 25 pages, and performing an oral presentation of the various stages of the research activity starting from selecting the research topic to the final presentation of it.
Legal Research (LAW666) > Credit Hours : 3

Legal Research (LAW666) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Conducts scholarly legal research using recognized legal research methodologies.

Criticize various juristic opinions and legislative and judicial trends, particularly within the UAE legal system.

Perform assigned tasks in the field of legal research professionally, adhering to ethical standards

LAW700.title: UAEU Catalog — LAW700 Quantitative and Qualitative Research Methods
LAW700.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=LAW700
The course covers the study of various scientific research methods, particularly quantitative and qualitative research methods, the design of research plans, and the process of conducting scientific research using a wide variety of relevant primary and secondary research sources and techniques. The course also focuses on the principles, skills, and methods necessary for conducting legal research, including the selection of the research sample, data and doctrinal analysis, theory building and testing, and case study.
Quantitative and Qualitative Research Methods (LAW700) > Credit Hours : 3

Quantitative and Qualitative Research Methods (LAW700) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Prepare a legal research paper using appropriate qualitative and quantitative research methods.

Make an effective presentation of the legal research paper.

Adhere to the relevant ethical and professional principles applicable to scientific research.

Effectively lead a research team for data collection and analysis.

LAW701.title: UAEU Catalog — LAW701 Advanced Legal Research: Writing and Presentation
LAW701.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=LAW701
The couse provides a definition of scientific research in the field of law, its types and and levels, selection of the subject of research, methods of legal research, legal writing, research ethics and refernce documentation. As a course requirement, the student must write a legal research paper which reflects commitment to the relevant ethical and prpfessional rules in the fiels of law.
Advanced Legal Research: Writing and Presentation (LAW701) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Legal Research: Writing and Presentation (LAW701) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Compare legislative and judiciary trends in the field of law by employing legal methodology correctly.

Criticize the legal provisions, and judicial trends in UAE and comparative legal systems.

Conduct legal research according to relevant research methodologies and techniques.

Leads a research team efficiently and effectively.

LAW702.title: UAEU Catalog — LAW702 Selected Legal Readings - E
LAW702.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=LAW702
This course will provide students with an overview of legal concepts, procedures, terminology and current issues in law including international law, administrative law, Commercial law, Contract law, employment law and so forth. By reading about selected topics in law, this course will also develop the ability of PhD students to delineate and evaluate issues, think analytically, select relevant materials and produce reasoned arguments encompassing policy, existing practice and knowledge. There is no one single book which covers the whole subject area. Students will be exposed to various sources of English scholarly materials including textbooks, websites, databases and law journals that are relevant to the selected themes raised by the instructor.
Selected Legal Readings - E (LAW702) > Credit Hours : 3

Selected Legal Readings - E (LAW702) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Compare the main judicial and legal concepts in different jurisdictions.

Communicate basic arguments and concepts concerning issues in diverse jurisdictions.

Expresses his commitment to the ethical and professional rules.

LAW703.title: UAEU Catalog — LAW703 Advanced Studies in Comparative Legal Systems
LAW703.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=LAW703
Since many of the research projects will necessarily involve some study of materials from other legal systems, a minimum level of familiarity with other legal systems would be necessary. This course is designed to introduce students to the theory and practice of comparative law by providing them with a broad understanding of the different major legal systems which exist globally; their historical backgrounds; their sources and characteristics. The course also considers selected topics in private or public law, looking at how different legal systems respond to issues familiar to students from studies within their own legal disciplines. During the course, students will be given the opportunity to compare specific areas of law between various jurisdictions. They may also explore some distinguishing features of Common and Civil Law. Topics to be covered in this course shall include for example the doctrine of judicial precedent and its use in the different legal systems, the role of judge and jury in common law system, and the theory of contract under the different major legal systems.
Advanced Studies in Comparative Legal Systems (LAW703) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Studies in Comparative Legal Systems (LAW703) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Compare critically between the main legal families such as common law, civil law and Islamic law.

Undertake research in specific areas of law by applying comparative law methodologies.

Communicate the major rules of comparative law effectively both orally and in writing

Express commitment to the relevant ethical and professional rules in the field of comparative law

LAW800.title: UAEU Catalog — LAW800 Comprehensive Examination
LAW800.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=LAW800
The comprehensive examination, which is an integral part of the PhD Program, is designed to ascertain and assess the student's comprehensive and in-depth knowledge of the main areas in the field of law and to evaluate the student’s potential to complete a doctoral dissertation successfully. Students who pass the comprehensive examination may advance to Ph.D. Dissertation. In preparation for the comprehensive examination, the student is required to develop a specific area of interest that shall be approved by the College Council. The specific area of interest will be articulated in the student’s statement of interest which ought to be submitted with the application to the program. The specific area of interest is expected to be the subject of the student’s dissertation.
Comprehensive Examination (LAW800) > Credit Hours : 0

Comprehensive Examination (LAW800) > Corequisites
LAW703 with a minimum grade C

( PRVT711 with a minimum grade C or PUBL715 with a minimum grade C)

LAW900.title: UAEU Catalog — LAW900 Dissertation Research
LAW900.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=LAW900
Student conducts high quality academic research under the direction of his/her supervisor. Student and supervisor shall meet on regular basis and discuss progress and issues related to the student’s dissertation research. Furthermore, the student writes an annual report based on a meeting with supervisor and Advisory Committee, in which a review is conducted to determine progress, identify problems, and project dates for completion of various tasks. The research shall represent original contribution to human knowledge in the particular field of law and is presented in a written research dissertation of a publishable standard. The document shall also demonstrate the candidate’s acquaintance with the literature of the field and the proper selection and execution of research methodology. The dissertation shall not exceed 70000 words in length. The physical form of the dissertation must comply with the regulations stated in the Thesis and Dissertation Preparation Guidelines, issued by the College of Graduate Studies.
Dissertation Research (LAW900) > Credit Hours : 36

Dissertation Research (LAW900) > Prerequisites
LAW702 with a minimum grade C
Dissertation Research (LAW900) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Compare legislative, jurisprudential and judiciary trends in the field of law.

Criticize judicial decisions, opinio juris, and judicial trends in the UAE and comparative legal systems.

Write an original research according to legal research methodologies and techniques.

Communicate the major tenets of their field of specialization and their work orally and in writing to the faculty, their peers, and the lay public.

Develop innovative solutions for contemporary issues in the absence of complete data

Express commitment to the relevant ethical and professional rules in the fields of law

PUBL112.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL112 Introduction to Islamic Law and its Sources
PUBL112.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=PUBL112
The course deals with an introduction to the definition of jurisprudence and Sharia, its divisions and the characteristics. The role of Islamic jurisprudence is covered through the study of its various sources, like The Quran, The Sunna, Fiqh consensus, inference, open interests, approbation, pretext closure accompanying and Tradition.
Introduction to Islamic Law and its Sources (PUBL112) > Credit Hours : 3

Introduction to Islamic Law and its Sources (PUBL112) > Prerequisites
GELW111 with a minimum grade D
Introduction to Islamic Law and its Sources (PUBL112) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the basic concepts and rules related to the emergence and development of Islamic Fiqh and its relationship to law, especially UAE law.

Interpret the Fiqh texts related to the sources of legislation in Islamic jurisprudence following the adopted rules of interpretation.

Carry out scientific research following legislative methods in Islamic Fiqh and concerning the course topics.

PUBL114.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL114 Constitutional Law
PUBL114.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=PUBL114
This course contains a brief study of the 'State', elements of State, forms of State and powers of State in comparative systems, with special focus on the Federal State and its application in the UAE. The main focus would be on the study of Constitutional Law, its definition, its sources, the control on the constitutional validity of laws and application of these aspects in the UAE. The course also deals with a study of the Constitutional Organization of the Federal Authorities according to the UAE Constitution.
Constitutional Law (PUBL114) > Credit Hours : 3

Constitutional Law (PUBL114) > Prerequisites
GELW111 with a minimum grade D
Constitutional Law (PUBL114) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the basic concepts and rules of constitutional law, especially the UAE Constitution.

Apply constitutional legal rules to the actual facts in a correct manner.

Comply with professional and ethical rules in performing the required tasks.

PUBL206.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL206 Administrative Law
PUBL206.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=PUBL206
The course covers the definition and sources of Administrative law, and the activities of the public administration, i.e., execution of laws, preservation of public order, and public utilities. The course focuses also on various legal means of public administration: administrative decisions, administrative contracts and public property.
Administrative Law (PUBL206) > Credit Hours : 3

Administrative Law (PUBL206) > Prerequisites
PRVT113 with a minimum grade D
Administrative Law (PUBL206) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the basic concepts and rules of administrative law, especially the UAE law.

Apply administrative legal rules to the actual facts in a correct manner.

Speak to audience clearly and confidently.

PUBL207.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL207 Public International Law
PUBL207.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=PUBL207
The course includes the definition of Public International Law, its sources subjects. The inter-relation between the Domestic Law (Municipal Law) and Public International Law and the governing theories are adequately dealt with. Various aspects covering Public International Law in times of peace are also dealt with, including, the Law of Treaties, establishment of States- their rights and obligations, recognition, state responsibility, use of force, and settlement of international disputes.
Public International Law (PUBL207) > Credit Hours : 3

Public International Law (PUBL207) > Prerequisites
PRVT113 with a minimum grade D

PUBL114 with a minimum grade D
Public International Law (PUBL207) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the basic concepts and rules of law, especially the public international law.

Apply international legal rules to the actual facts in a correct manner.

Speak to audience clearly and confidently

PUBL215.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL215 General Law of Crimes and Penalties (1)
PUBL215.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=PUBL215
The course includes a general introduction to the study of criminal law, specifically the general part and the general theory of crime. The study covers the characteristics of the general part of criminal law, its relationship with other legal and criminal sciences, and its scope of application in terms of time and place. It also includes the study of the general elements of a crime: the material and moral elements, the provisions of criminal participation, justifications, and grounds for exemption from criminal liability. Additionally, the course addresses the latest technological developments and their impact on some of its topics, such as the possibility of establishing criminal liability resulting from using artificial intelligence applications and the newly introduced penalties that could be applied if such liability is recognized.
General Law of Crimes and Penalties (1) (PUBL215) > Credit Hours : 3

General Law of Crimes and Penalties (1) (PUBL215) > Prerequisites
PRVT113 with a minimum grade D
General Law of Crimes and Penalties (1) (PUBL215) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the basic concepts and rules related to crime according to UAE law

Apply the legal rules related to crime in practical reality

Speak confidently, objectively, and fluently in front of audience

PUBL216.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL216 General Law of Crimes and Penalties (2)
PUBL216.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=PUBL216
The course includes the study of the general theory of criminal sanctions, focusing on two main areas. The first area is the General Theory of Punishment, which covers the definition of punishment, its characteristics, and how it differs from other legal sanctions. It also explores the various types of punishments, the rules governing their application, and the discretionary powers of the criminal judge in this regard. The second area is the General Theory of Non-Punitive Measures, which examines the definition and characteristics of non-punitive measures, their distinction from punishment, the different types of non-punitive measures, and their scope of application. Additionally, the course addresses the issue of various criminal sanctions that may be imposed for responsibility related to offences committed through AI.
General Law of Crimes and Penalties (2) (PUBL216) > Credit Hours : 3

General Law of Crimes and Penalties (2) (PUBL216) > Prerequisites
PUBL215 with a minimum grade D
General Law of Crimes and Penalties (2) (PUBL216) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the basic concepts and rules related to criminal penalties under UAE law.

Interpret legal texts related to criminal penalties in accordance with established rules of interpretation

Formulate memorandums and judicial decisions in matters of criminal penalties using clear language.

PUBL250.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL250 Environmental Policy and Climate Justice
PUBL250.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=PUBL250
The objective of the course is to provide students with working knowledge of legal norms and practices that address contemporary environmental issues. It focuses on UAE laws, Acts, regulations and, familiarizing students with key international legal concepts by studying major conventions and treaties. In addition to legal frameworks, the course explores the intersection of environmental law with policy making and climate justice, emphasizing how laws can shape fair and sustainable outcomes for vulnerable communities. It underlines the crucial links between environmental protection, socio-economic development, sustainability, and the global pursuit of climate equity.
Environmental Policy and Climate Justice (PUBL250) > Credit Hours : 3

Environmental Policy and Climate Justice (PUBL250) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the legal provisions related to the environment in local and international legislation.

Discuss the role of local and international institutions in environmental conservation.

Evaluates the role of law in achieving sustainability.

PUBL305.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL305 Criminal Law and Penalties – Special Part
PUBL305.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=PUBL305
The Special Section of the Criminal Law (Penal Code) Course addresses the detailed and special provisions for some crimes. The study of this Course is divided into two parts: the first includes the study of crimes against persons, which are intentional and unintentional homicide and assault. The second includes studying crimes against money, which are crimes of theft, fraud, and breach of trust. The course discusses the effect of the use of new technologies on these topics, including the issue of responsibility for offences committed through AI applications and different criminal sanctions that may be imposed in such cases.
Criminal Law and Penalties – Special Part (PUBL305) > Credit Hours : 3

Criminal Law and Penalties – Special Part (PUBL305) > Prerequisites
PUBL216 with a minimum grade D
Criminal Law and Penalties – Special Part (PUBL305) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the basic concepts and rules related to crime according to UAE law.

Apply legal rules to the actual facts in a correct manner.

Draft legal memorandums and statements of claim related to the special provisions of crimes

PUBL306.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL306 Penal Law (Specific) 2 "Emerging Crimes"
PUBL306.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=PUBL306
This course deals with particular types of crimes: offences against the public interest, economic crimes, information technology crimes, drug crimes, money laundering, and human trafficking. A cohernet set of offences contained in the vocabulary of this course is to be chosen and taught in each semester.
Penal Law (Specific) 2 "Emerging Crimes" (PUBL306) > Credit Hours : 3

Penal Law (Specific) 2 "Emerging Crimes" (PUBL306) > Prerequisites
PUBL209 with a minimum grade D
Penal Law (Specific) 2 "Emerging Crimes" (PUBL306) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the concepts and rules of law, Especially the UAE law.

Write a scientific research according to the Legal Research Methodology.

Lead a team positively.

PUBL308.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL308 International Organizations-English
PUBL308.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=PUBL308
The course studies the idea of international organizations and their general rules, membership in international organizations, the organs and staff of international organizations, the functions and powers of international organizations, the international legal personality of international organizations, and their decision-making process. The course also covers international organizations such as the League of Nations, and GCC, the United Nations, and some regional and specialized organizations.
International Organizations-English (PUBL308) > Credit Hours : 3

International Organizations-English (PUBL308) > Prerequisites
PUBL207 with a minimum grade D
International Organizations-English (PUBL308) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the fundamental legal concepts and rules pertaining to international organizations

Complete a research paper using appropriate legal research methods

Lead a team effectively.

PUBL309.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL309 Public Employment
PUBL309.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=PUBL309
It includes: studying the legal provisions for the public employee in terms of his public service and his or her rights and obligations and his disciplin in accordance to the Federal Civil Service Act and its implemented regulations in United Arab Emirates.
Public Employment (PUBL309) > Credit Hours : 3

Public Employment (PUBL309) > Prerequisites
PUBL206 with a minimum grade D
Public Employment (PUBL309) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the concepts and rules of legal system of Public Employment, Especially under the UAE law.

Write a scientific research according to the Legal Research Methodology.

Lead a team positively.

PUBL311.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL311 Public Finance and Tax Legislation
PUBL311.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=PUBL311
This course covers two main topics. The first is the Science of Public Finance, which explores the principles, rules, and theories governing state finances. This area consists of three key elements: public expenditures, public revenues, and the public budget. Public revenues include taxes, state-owned properties, fees, and public loans. The second topic is Tax Legislation, which focuses on the legal provisions related to taxation in the United Arab Emirates, with particular emphasis on value-added tax (VAT) and excise tax.
Public Finance and Tax Legislation (PUBL311) > Credit Hours : 3

Public Finance and Tax Legislation (PUBL311) > Prerequisites
PUBL206 with a minimum grade D
Public Finance and Tax Legislation (PUBL311) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the fundamental principles related to public finance of the state

Apply financial legal rules to the presented facts

Lead a team effectively

PUBL329.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL329 Principles of Jurisprudence
PUBL329.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=PUBL329
In this course, the student becomes familiar with the concept of the science of Usul al-Fiqh, its subject matter, benefits, sources, origins, and schools. The course also introduces the theory of the Islamic legal ruling, including the lawgiver, the ruling in its two categories—obligatory (taklifi) and declaratory (wadi‘)—as well as the subject of the ruling and the person to whom it applies. Furthermore, the student explores the discussions on semantic indications according to the jurists, including: types of clear expressions—zahir (apparent), nass (explicit), mufassar (elucidated), and muhkam (unequivocal); types of ambiguous expressions—khafi (latent), mushkil (problematic), mujmal (general), and mutashabih (equivocal); types of expressions based on the assignment of meaning—‘amm (general) and its specification, and khas (specific) and its categories such as command and prohibition, absolute and restricted, and homonymous; types of expressions based on their usage—literal and figurative, explicit and implicit; and types of expressions based on how they signify meaning—through explicit wording, indication, implication, presumption, and the concept of opposition.
Principles of Jurisprudence (PUBL329) > Credit Hours : 3

Principles of Jurisprudence (PUBL329) > Prerequisites
PUBL112 with a minimum grade D
Principles of Jurisprudence (PUBL329) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply the fundamental jurisprudential rules related to the legal ruling, the subject, and the object of the ruling within practical contexts.

Interpret religious and legal texts in accordance with the interpretive principles established in the foundations of Islamic jurisprudence.

Evaluate legislative and judicial trends in the UAE legal system in light of the principles recognized in the foundations of Islamic jurisprudence.

PUBL335.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=PUBL335
The course covers the following topics: the scope of application of the Criminal Procedure Law in terms of time and place, criminal cases arising from crimes, evidence collection, preliminary investigation, trial, sentencing, appeal, and special criminal procedures (criminal reconciliation - criminal mediation - criminal settlement - electronic monitoring - use of technologies in criminal procedures). Criminal Procedures Law (PUBL335) > Credit Hours : 3

Criminal Procedures Law (PUBL335) > Prerequisites
PUBL216 with a minimum grade D
Criminal Procedures Law (PUBL335) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply the rules of criminal law to the actual facts.

Formulate memorandums and judicial decisions related to criminal procedures law in a clear and correct language.

Evaluate legislative and judicial trends related to criminal procedures in the UAE legal system

PUBL341.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL341 International Law of the Sea
PUBL341.text:

International Law of the Sea (PUBL341) > Prerequisites
PUBL207 with a minimum grade D
International Law of the Sea (PUBL341) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the basic principles relating to the international law of the sea.

Write a paper according to the legal research methodologies in one of the topic of the course

Lead a team positively

PUBL401.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL401 International Human Rights Law
PUBL401.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=PUBL401

International Human Rights Law (PUBL401) > Credit Hours : 3

International Human Rights Law (PUBL401) > Prerequisites
PUBL207 with a minimum grade D
International Human Rights Law (PUBL401) > Course Learning Outcomes

Explain the concepts and rules of human right law, under the UAE law.

Write a scientific research according to the Legal Research Methodology.

Lead a team positively.

PUBL421.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL421 Press Law and Ethics
PUBL421.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=PUBL421
This course includes two parts. Part I is dedicated to a brief study of the ethics prescribed by the codes of ethics that deal with the different aspects of conduct of persons who are working in the fields of mass media. Part II contains a brief study about the main elements of the Mass Media Legal System in the world in general, and a focused study of the legal system of mass media in the UAE (print and electronic media/journalism and cinema) in particular. The Mass Media Legal system in the UAE, their establishment, administration, activities and the related legal issues like restraints, prohibitions on the freedom of expression involving criminal and administrative procedures are part of this course.
Press Law and Ethics (PUBL421) > Credit Hours : 3

Press Law and Ethics (PUBL421) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Enhance the principles of the media and the sources of its legal regulation.

Realize the importance of legal regulation of media and the adoption of penalties for violators.

PUBL630.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL630 Advanced Studies in Criminal Law and Penalties
PUBL630.text:

Advanced Studies in Criminal Law and Penalties (PUBL630) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Studies in Criminal Law and Penalties (PUBL630) > Course Learning Outcomes

Analyze criminal cases and texts using sound scientific methodology

Compare different jurisprudential opinions and legislative and judicial approaches in the field of crimes and punishments.

Conduct an in-depth research on one of the course topics using approved legal research methodologies and scholarly sources.

PUBL631.text:

The study will be conducted in depth and will involve comparisons with various legal systems that either provide distinct or similar regulations to the subject matter. Advanced Studies in Constitutional Law (PUBL631) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Studies in Constitutional Law (PUBL631) > Course Learning Outcomes

PUBL633.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL633 Advance Studies in International Criminal Law
PUBL633.text:

Advance Studies in International Criminal Law (PUBL633) > Credit Hours : 3

Advance Studies in International Criminal Law (PUBL633) > Course Learning Outcomes

PUBL634.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL634 Advanced Studies in Criminal Procedures

For example, alternatives to criminal proceedings, such as criminal orders, criminal reconciliation, and criminal settlements, as well as The Theory of Criminal Evidence, methods of appealing criminal judgments, including opposition, appeal, and cassation. The course also covers using new technologies, including AI, in criminal Procedures.
Advanced Studies in Criminal Procedures (PUBL634) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Studies in Criminal Procedures (PUBL634) > Course Learning Outcomes

Analyze criminal procedural cases and legal texts in a correct scientific manner.

Compares jurisprudential opinions and legislative and judicial trends related to criminal procedures

Demonstrate self-learning skills with regard to real and novel issues.

Advanced Studies in Administrative Law (PUBL635) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Studies in Administrative Law (PUBL635) > Course Learning Outcomes

PUBL636.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL636 Thesis
PUBL636.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=PUBL636
The student is committed to conduct original research on a vital topic of private law under the supervision of his or her academic supervisor, which will be presented in the form of a thesis written according to a publishable standard. The writing stage must be preceded by holding a seminar for the student to discuss the topic of the thesis with the relevant faculty members in a public session. During the writing stage, the student and supervisor must meet regularly to discuss progress and issues related to the topic of the thesis, and the supervisor is committed to providing the scientific department with a periodic report on the stages of completion. The thesis must demonstrate the student’s knowledge and familiarity with the relevant literature and the methodology. The thesis must also be accompanied by specific results and recommendations that are applicable in practice. The form of the thesis must comply with the regulations stated in the Thesis and Dissertation Preparation Guidelines, issued by the College of Graduate Studies, and it must pass the stage of scrutiny and verification of the absence of plagiarism or scientific theft through certain programs, including Turnitin. After completing writing it, it will be discussed in a public session by a specialized committee that includes an external examiner and an internal examiner headed by the supervisor.
Thesis (PUBL636) > Credit Hours : 7

Thesis (PUBL636) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyzes cases and legal texts in a correct scientific manner

Criticizes jurisprudential and judicial view points and trends in general, and within the UAE legal system in particular

Compare jurisprudence, various judicial and legislative trends, especially in the UAE legal system

Conducts in depth a legal research in the field of public law, and analyzes the findings, in accordance with the correct scientific methodologies

Demonstrate self-learning skills with regard to real and novel issues to implement innovative solutions

Undertakes his/her duties professionally in accordance with ethical principles

PUBL637.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL637 Advanced Studies in Administrative Contracts
PUBL637.text:

Advanced Studies in Administrative Contracts (PUBL637) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Studies in Administrative Contracts (PUBL637) > Course Learning Outcomes

Critique different jurisprudential opinions and legislative and judicial trends in the field of administrative contracts.

Demonstrate self-directed learning by keeping abreast of emerging practical and academic developments related to administrative contracts.

Perform assigned tasks professionally while adhering to ethical standards in the field of administrative contracts.

International Relations & Organizations(E) (PUBL638) > Credit Hours : 3

International Relations & Organizations(E) (PUBL638) > Course Learning Outcomes

Analyses cases and legal texts of International Organizations in a correct scientific manner.

Conducts in depth legal research in the field of International Organizations in accordance with the correct scientific methodologies.

Undertakes his/her course duties professionally in accordance with ethical principles.

PUBL639.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL639 Human Rights (E)

Human Rights (E) (PUBL639) > Credit Hours : 3

PUBL640.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL640 Advanced Studies in Special Criminal Legislation
PUBL640.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=PUBL640

Advanced Studies in Special Criminal Legislation (PUBL640) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Studies in Special Criminal Legislation (PUBL640) > Course Learning Outcomes

Criticize jurisprudential and judicial view points and trends concerning the provisions of special criminal offenses.

Conducts in-depth scholarly research on one of the special criminal offenses using legal research methodologies.

PUBL642.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL642 Advanced Studies in Pre-trial Procedures
PUBL642.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=PUBL642
This unit examines the institutions and criminal processes involved in pre-trial stages. It covers preliminary police criminal investigations and procedures such as police power and authority to stop, search and arrest suspects. It also covers evidence gathering by police, preserving crimes scenes, the accused and victims’ rights before judicial police, and other related police powers during this stage. It will also explore the various criminal procedures of primary criminal investigation as conducted by public prosecutors such as interrogation, detention, bail, committal proceedings and the prosecutor decision of there is no grounds to file a lawsuit. The unit also deals with the various aspects of the criminal evidence theory.
Advanced Studies in Pre-trial Procedures (PUBL642) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Studies in Pre-trial Procedures (PUBL642) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate legal, jurisprudential, and judicial approaches to pre-trial procedures, and propose innovative solutions to address legal issues or legislative gaps in this area.

Complete an original research paper using the appropriate legal research methods in the field of pre-trial procedures.

PUBL655.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL655 Environmental Law
PUBL655.text:

The course incorporates on-line use of current Acts, Regulations and Conventions and students will become familiar with Municipal, Federal and international environmental law including duty, breach and liability.
Environmental Law (PUBL655) > Credit Hours : 2

Environmental Law (PUBL655) > Course Learning Outcomes

Explain the basics of environmental law.

Research environmental Acts and Regulations.

Apply current environmental regulations.

PUBL705.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL705 Criminal Law
PUBL705.text:

The course deals with one or more topics of substantive or procedural criminal law in an in-depth manner, taking into consideration the modern aspects related to the UAE, such as the evolution of the criminal responsibility of legal persons, the principle of the judge's freedom of conviction or the crimes of human trafficking.
Criminal Law (PUBL705) > Credit Hours : 3

Criminal Law (PUBL705) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Compares the Legislative, Jurisprudential and Judiciary trends in the field of Criminal Law

Critiques legal provisions, jurisprudential opinions and judicial trends related to ciminal law in the UAE and comparative legal systems.

Undertake research that includes knowledge in the field of specialization.

Develop innovative solutions for contemporary legal issues

PUBL706.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL706 Administrative Law
PUBL706.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=PUBL706
This course offers an in-depth study into one of the Administrative law topics. Its purpose is to advance of students’ comprehension of the different topics of Administrative law. The Course will focus on one or more substantive or procedural issues which is selected by the Department of Public law in each Semester , with focus on contemporary questions of the UAE Administrative law.
Administrative Law (PUBL706) > Credit Hours : 3

Administrative Law (PUBL706) > Course Learning Outcomes

Criticize legal provisions, opinion juris, and courts judgments in the UAE.

Write an original research in the field of administrative law in accordance with legal research requirements.

Develop innovative solutions for contemporary legal issues in the field of administrative law.

PUBL709.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL709 Public International Law - E
PUBL709.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=PUBL709
This course aims to study one of the public international law topics in depth, such as state immunity, international inheritance and unilateral acts in international law. - State immunity: Talks about the concepts of state immunity, historical development and study of the United Nations Convention on state immunity and it’s applications in international and national courts. - International Inheritance: Talks about the concept of international inheritance, types and forms, and the succession of States in the light of international treaties and concentrates on the records, properties, debts and the declaration of the United Nations on succession of States in respect of nationality of natural persons and the problems raised by the issue of succession of states. - Unilateral acts: Talks about the concept of unilateral acts and it’s relation to the theory of the sources of international law: the legal forms and sequel.
Public International Law - E (PUBL709) > Credit Hours : 3

Public International Law - E (PUBL709) > Course Learning Outcomes

Write a research which contains an added knowledge in the field of Public International Law.

Communicate basic arguments and concepts concerning public international law issues.

Expresses his commitment to the ethical and professional rules.

Lead a team to provide solutions for relevant legal issues related to public international law.

PUBL710.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL710 Criminal Procedure Law- E
PUBL710.text:

The course instructor will select one or more topics from the Code of Criminal Procedure that raise issues in jurisprudential theory and judicial application, ensuring that the study is in-depth and utilizes comparison to other laws and Islamic law.
Criminal Procedure Law- E (PUBL710) > Credit Hours : 3

Criminal Procedure Law- E (PUBL710) > Course Learning Outcomes

International Crimes and Judicial System - E (PUBL713) > Credit Hours : 3

International Crimes and Judicial System - E (PUBL713) > Course Learning Outcomes

Write an original research in the field of international crimes according to legal research methodologies and techniques.

PUBL715.title: UAEU Catalog — PUBL715 Contemporary Crimes- E
PUBL715.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_2964.shtml?id=PUBL715
This Course will be concerned with preparing papers, commenting on judicial decisions and holding discussion sessions on one or more of the new crimes such as terrorism, crimes related to capital markets, Cyber-crimes, money laundering, and human trafficking.
Contemporary Crimes- E (PUBL715) > Credit Hours : 3

Contemporary Crimes- E (PUBL715) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Criticize legal provisions, opinio juris, and judicial trends in the area of contemporary crimes
