Differentiate between map scales, coordinate systems, and map projections

Interpret maps

GEO221.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO221 Geographic Information Systems I
GEO221.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO221
This is a lecture/lab course designed to introduce students to the fundamentals of GIS. The lecture part of the class focuses on the history of GIS, major components of a GIS, geographic data sources, vector and raster models, database development and management techniques, and spatial analysis. The lab portion is hands-on, where students use GIS software to apply the principles and methods discussed in the lectures towards solving real world problems.
Geographic Information Systems I (GEO221) > Credit Hours : 3

Geographic Information Systems I (GEO221) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply cartographic principles of scale, resolution, projection and data management to a problem of a geographic nature.

Apply simple spatial analysis and modeling techniques to investigate a geospatial problem, and prepare maps, reports, and charts for presentation of results.

Develop practical hands-on experiences using GIS software.

Recognize different types of geographic information, data models and structures for storing geographic information, geographic data input, data manipulation and visualization.

Relate and explain the concepts, principles, main components, functions, and capabilities applications, and theories behind GIS.

GEO231.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO231 Economic Geography
GEO231.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO231
This course deals with the economic activity of human societies within the global economy. It describes the structure of the global economy and the various approaches used to understand the global arrangement of economic activities. It explores elements of investments as production, consumption, distribution, foreign exchange, and current economical problems. It concentrates on macro and public sector economics, revenue generation, finance of public infrastructure, operating budgets for urban areas and micro concepts as utility maximization and rational decision making.
Economic Geography (GEO231) > Credit Hours : 3

Economic Geography (GEO231) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply economic geography background to evaluate the international economic issues

Contrast between natural, human and economic resource and their value to ankind

Illustrate the right measure to deal with the geographical concentration of local and international firms in relation with labor, capital or other economic resources

GEO232.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO232 Urban Economics
GEO232.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO232
This course emphasizes the use of economic theory in urban planning, evaluation and role of urban planning in market economies, theories of regional development and economic growth, balanced and unbalanced growth, income distribution, theories of urban growth, urban location theories. As this course studies the functions of the urban economy: it concentrate on macro, public sector economics: revenue generation, financing of major public infrastructure, operating budgets for urban areas and introduce micro concepts.
Urban Economics (GEO232) > Credit Hours : 3

Urban Economics (GEO232) > Prerequisites
GEO210 with a minimum grade D
Urban Economics (GEO232) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze how certain topics of large impact such as education, housing, social welfare & crime, relate to urban economics and urban development.

Predict changes in urban form as a result of urban growth patterns and urban planning efforts.

Recognize the consequential role of government and policy in shaping urban economics and urban development.

Relate the economic and social factors that determine locational decisions of businesses and households, and thus shape urban development.

GEO307.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO307 Urban Geography
GEO307.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO307
This course aims to introduce students to contemporary urban geography, with an emphasis on ecological, economic, cultural, and postmodern perspectives. It covers patterns and processes of urbanization, urban development, urban planning, the origins and development of cities, and life experiences in modern cities. It focuses on revealing the excitement and richness of cities while addressing a wide range of urban challenges. This course also includes the most recent research in urban studies, introducing elements of urban theory and methodology, and addressing the global urban experience.
Urban Geography (GEO307) > Credit Hours : 3

Urban Geography (GEO307) > Prerequisites
GEO210
Urban Geography (GEO307) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the origins and development of cities

Evaluate major theories about urban areas and urban people

Write effectively about urban concepts and issues

Understand the opportunities and constraints people face in urban areas

GEO330.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO330 Geodatabase Design
GEO330.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO330
The main goal of this course is to train students on designing and building efficient geodatabases. It covers the fundamental concepts of building databases with focus on geographic databases, and on the storage and management of GIS data. It teaches students how to create a geodatabase, how to migrate existing data to a geodatabase, and how to manage and use enterprise geodatabases.
Geodatabase Design (GEO330) > Credit Hours : 3

Geodatabase Design (GEO330) > Prerequisites
GEO221 with a minimum grade D
Geodatabase Design (GEO330) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the concepts of the different types of geodatabases

Design efficient file and enterprise geodatabases

Manage GIS data in file and enterprise geodatabases

Perform GIS analyses using geodatabases

GEO334.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO334 Spatial Analysis
GEO334.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO334
The course covers basic statistical concepts, non-spatial and spatial measures of central tendency and dispersion, basic probability, spatial data analysis, statistical theories, methods and problems in spatial data sampling (random, systematic, stratified, clustered). It also introduces students to statistical hypothesis tests (normal distribution, Pearson's chi-squared test (X2), t-test), and geographical dimension of attribute (thematic and distribution maps). Moreover, this course covers ANOVA analysis, correlation analysis between geographical phenomena, regression model and collinearity diagnostics.
Spatial Analysis (GEO334) > Credit Hours : 3

Spatial Analysis (GEO334) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Construct the framework for hypothesis testing with respect to the population means and difference of population means.

Employ probability distributions, particularly the normal distribution to describe data and test hypotheses

Evaluate simple geographical relationships through the concepts of simple correlation and simple regression.

Relate the basic concepts in simple statistics that are useful to geographical data analysis

GEO335.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO335 Programming for GIS
GEO335.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO335
The main goal of this course is to train students on how to automate GIS and remote sensing operations using the Python scripting language. Automation can make work easier, faster, and more accurate. Knowledge of a scripting language is a highly desired skill in GIS market. Students will be able to design and implement solutions in Python, demonstrate an understanding of programming concepts, methods, and approaches such as debugging, error checking, documentation, and developing scripts. Students will be acquainted with how to use Google Earth Engine and using Python/Javascript to perform cloud-based image and data processing, and accessing and processing Landsat images using GDAL.
Programming for GIS (GEO335) > Credit Hours : 3

Programming for GIS (GEO335) > Prerequisites
GEO221 with a minimum grade D
Programming for GIS (GEO335) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Elaborate on the benefits of programming and user interface generation (application).

Distinguish between various components of a program such as functions, external libraries subroutines, and checking.

Develop an objected-oriented program using python script language

Apply the program to real GIS analysis such as solving suitability analysis problem and raster analysis

GEO336.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO336 Urban and Environmental Sustainability
GEO336.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO336
The course examines sustainable urban planning and practices that allow reducing negative impact on the environment, minimizing the natural resources consumption, increasing the utilization of renewable resources, and minimization of wastes, reducing operational costs, and utilization of green materials in building energy efficient structures with the possibility of their further recycling. Sustainable communities are discussed in the United Arab Emirates as a desirable policy goal and, in particular, understanding the role of federal and local authorities’ contribution to climate change mitigation through effective urban planning.
Urban and Environmental Sustainability (GEO336) > Credit Hours : 3

Urban and Environmental Sustainability (GEO336) > Prerequisites
GEO210 with a minimum grade D
Urban and Environmental Sustainability (GEO336) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss the principles of sustainable urban planning and practices.

Evaluate various perspectives regarding sustainable communities in the United Arab Emirates.

Analyze the impact of federal and local authorities' efforts on climate change mitigation.

Devise policies and practices that address pressing sustainable urban issues in the United Arab Emirates.

GEO340.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO340 Introduction to Real Estate Development
GEO340.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO340
The Real Estate industry is one of the key economic and growth engines in the United Arab Emirates. This course is designed to equip students of urban planning with the knowledge and tools that prepare them for effective contribution to this industry. Students taking this course will develop a clear understanding of the multidisciplinary field of real estate development. Because Real Estate development, design, and urban planning are closely interrelated, this course begins by exploring the roles and responsibilities of the real estate developer, and planning agencies in the production of the built environment. Next, students are introduced to topics covering the main components of real Estate industry, such as government policies and regulations; market and site analysis; community planning; entitlements; social, political, and environmental implications; architecture and design; budgeting and financial analysis; construction; sales and marketing; and property and asset management. Various project types are studied, including residential, retail, office, hospitality, industrial, and mixed-use. Throughout, there will be discussions and reviews of many examples and cases from the UAE. Moreover, students are expected to work on, and develop two local case studies as part of their coursework.
Introduction to Real Estate Development (GEO340) > Credit Hours : 3

Introduction to Real Estate Development (GEO340) > Prerequisites
GEO232
Introduction to Real Estate Development (GEO340) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Relate and apply the fundamental concepts and techniques used in the real estate development process- such as feasibility studies, & property valuation

Identify the roles that comprise the real estate industry

Understand real estate approach to developing major product types including: Residential (Rental and For Sale Housing & Land Development), Retail, and Office.

Develop a Real Estate vocabulary and engage in critical reflection about weighing the economic, social, and environmental costs vs. benefits of development projects for a community

GEO341.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO341 Geography of Population
GEO341.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO341
This course examines population and all related aspects such as distribution, composition, demography, explosion, migration, income, disease, projection, and future trends of a population of a geographical space. The study of population deals literally with life and death. For this reason alone, the subject occupies a place of importance in a wide variety of academic disciplines, as well as in government, service organizations, business, and industry.
Geography of Population (GEO341) > Credit Hours : 3

Geography of Population (GEO341) > Prerequisites
GEO210
Geography of Population (GEO341) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze modes of popuation growth and distribution

Estimate population figures at specific Time

Illustrate how to analyze census data

Write a report on a problem or issue related to opulation

GEO345.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO345 Urban Demography
GEO345.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO345
This course addresses the role of population in urban policy and planning, and the impact of a changing population and their activities on cities. It uses census data in deriving measurements and conducting analysis on population distribution segregation in urban centers. The course concerns with the study of population growth (migration and natural increase) to determine infrastructure and service's needs. Urban demography stresses also on the study of population characteristics and its role in changing the landscape of urban centers.
Urban Demography (GEO345) > Credit Hours : 3

Urban Demography (GEO345) > Prerequisites
GEO210 with a minimum grade D
Urban Demography (GEO345) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyse Educational Level Of Population And Economic Activity

Evaluate Perspectives, Forecasts And Projections Of The Population

Explain Social Significance And Philosophical Basis Of Urban Demography

Relate And Explain Basic Concepts While Emphasizing The Importance Of Urban Demography

Relate Population Characteristic And Urban Problems

Relate Social Transformation Of The Population And Its Reproduction Demographic Statistics

GEO350.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO350 Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS)
GEO350.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO350
This course provides background about the Global Positioning System (GPS-USA), GLONASS (Russia), BeiDou (Compass) Navigation System (China), and Galileo (Europe) Satellites. It includes description of GNSS signal structures and the derivation of observables; characteristics of instrumentation; analysis of atmospheric, orbital, random and non­random effects; derivation of mathematical models used for absolute and differential static and kinematic positioning; pre-analysis methods and applications. Topics include instrument familiarization; field-data collection and processing; real-time and post-differential correction; and GNSS-GIS integration and mapping of geo-positional data (Tracking, monitoring).
Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) (GEO350) > Credit Hours : 3

Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) (GEO350) > Prerequisites
GEO221 with a minimum grade D
Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) (GEO350) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Elaborate on how GNSS works.

Differentiate between GNSS positioning methods.

Discuss in details the GNSS Augmenting options.

Defend a project related to GNSS application.

GEO351.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO351 Computer Maps
GEO351.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO351
The course focuses on using computers in map-making, map design, data structure, thematic mapping, and enhancement of communication and visualization. Topics covered include use of GPS for mapping, 3-Dimension, new means of map communication such as on-line maps, mobile maps, animated maps, virtual reality, and multi-media. The course includes a laboratory portion that provides students with hands-on ArcGIS and 3D Analyst.
Computer Maps (GEO351) > Credit Hours : 3

Computer Maps (GEO351) > Prerequisites
GEO220 with a minimum grade D
Computer Maps (GEO351) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Create 3D, animated and multi-media maps to present geographical phenomena.

Differentiate between online mapping forms

Explain Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) principles and their roles in mapping

Produce a map using hand held GPS receiver

GEO370.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO370 Transit Oriented Development (TOD)
GEO370.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO370
This course provides an introduction to TOD and covers the historical development of transit, organizational structure, ridership trends, and performance measures. Special attention is also paid to the fundamental strategies and tools for TOD implementation, and how it operates within the existing built environment. It also examines TOD's benefits, impacts, barriers, practice from different transit oriented projects implanted in the world including: USA, Singapore, Italy, Netherlands, Tokyo, and UAE (Dubai).
Transit Oriented Development (TOD) (GEO370) > Credit Hours : 3

Transit Oriented Development (TOD) (GEO370) > Prerequisites
GEO210 with a minimum grade D
Transit Oriented Development (TOD) (GEO370) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze Different Barriers To The Development Of Tod

Apply A Range Of Principles And Theoretical Knowledge To Develop Strategies To Current Problems In Tod Planning

Define Different Related Concepts To Tod Planning

Evaluate The Impacts Of Creating A New Tod Zone Within Existing Urban Fabric

Outline The Social, Economic, And Technical Processes Involved In Shaping The Tod

GEO372.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO372 Planning Theory and Practice
GEO372.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO372
This course focuses on the development of contemporary planning concepts and principles; the nature, purpose and scope of urban planning. It gives an historical overview of the theory of planning and discusses the role of the state, the private economy and the civil society in different planning theories. A range of development planning tools is introduced as: SWOT Analysis, economic and demographic trend analysis, private/public/NGO partnerships, sustainable development planning indicators, and outcome evaluation.
Planning Theory and Practice (GEO372) > Credit Hours : 3

Planning Theory and Practice (GEO372) > Prerequisites
GEO210 with a minimum grade D
Planning Theory and Practice (GEO372) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the theoretical background behind the different ways planners working in the public sector are likely to take.

Identify the key theoretical debates and concerns throughout planning current and historical development

recognize the key concerns in the topic of ethics and values in planning practice

Relate the evolutionary nature of planning theory and how planning theory relates to practice.

GEO395.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO395 Environmental Policies
GEO395.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO395
The course is primarily concerned with how to govern the relationship between humans and the natural environment in a mutually beneficial manner. This includes addressing issues such as controlling pollution and waste flows and limiting habitat loss. Students explore the UAE’s government laws, regulations, and other policy mechanisms concerning environmental issues. Among the topics covered are air and water pollution, waste management, ecosystem management, maintenance of biodiversity, the management of natural resources, wildlife and endangered species.
Environmental Policies (GEO395) > Credit Hours : 3

Environmental Policies (GEO395) > Prerequisites
GEO210 with a minimum grade D
Environmental Policies (GEO395) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the principles and practices of sustainable environmental governance, including the concepts of ecological balance, conservation, and equitable resource management.

Develop comprehensive solutions to environmental challenges faced by the UAE.

Evaluate environmental policies, laws, and regulations implemented by the UAE government to address issues such as pollution control, habitat loss, and biodiversity conservation.

Communicate effectively to engage stakeholders and raise awareness about environmental issues.

GEO396.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO396 Environmental Systems
GEO396.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO396
The course introduces the atmospheric environment of the Earth: elements and controls of climate and their implications for hydrology, vegetation, and soils. It emphasizes distribution of physical features across the Earth’s surface and interactions between humans and their environment, especially those leading to global change. The course also introduces landscapes and flowing water, emphasizing the formation and geographic distribution of mountains, volcanoes, valleys, deserts, and their shaping by rivers and glaciers. It emphasizes distribution of physical features across the Earth’s surface and addresses ways in which the physical landscape has been altered by human activity, and how some earth surface processes impinge upon society.
Environmental Systems (GEO396) > Credit Hours : 3

Environmental Systems (GEO396) > Prerequisites
GEO201 with a minimum grade D
Environmental Systems (GEO396) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe and explain the primary physical elements and processes that drive the Earth-atmosphere system.

Describe in detail the defining characteristics and spatial distribution of Earth’s primary terrestrial ecosystems.

Define tectonic and volcanic, weathering, erosional and depositional landscape features and explain the fundamental physical and chemical processes by which they form.

Evaluate the ways in which humans interact with and alter the atmospheric and biotic components of the Earth system.

GEO397.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO397 Terrestrial and Aquatic Biodiversity
GEO397.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO397
Understanding the structure and function of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems is fundamental to their conservation and necessary for remediation of impacted environments. This course explores terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, their biota, physical and chemical properties, linkages between terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, the effects of human activities and global change, conservation strategies and sustainable development practices to protect, maintain, and restore biodiversity. Students will learn the key research methods in terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems research including sampling techniques, water chemistry analysis, identification of biota, experimental design, data analyses, and written and oral communication skills as part of the laboratory portion of the course.
Terrestrial and Aquatic Biodiversity (GEO397) > Credit Hours : 3

Terrestrial and Aquatic Biodiversity (GEO397) > Prerequisites
BIOC100 or GEO201
Terrestrial and Aquatic Biodiversity (GEO397) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognize the various components of terrestrial and aquatic biodiversity and its importance.

Examine the principles and theories on the relationships between terrestrial and aquatic life (individual organisms, populations, communities, and ecosystems) and both biotic and abiotic factors in the environment.

Describe different terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems and the consequences of human activities and climate change on biodiversity.

Evaluate conservation strategies and sustainable development practices aimed at protecting, maintaining, and restoring biodiversity.

Apply scientific processes and knowledge of the natural world to make evidence-based decisions.

GEO402.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO402 Land Use
GEO402.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO402
The course provides an introduction to land use planning in urban areas, land use theories, planning processes, and decision making. Special attention is paid to different types of land uses in urban areas: residential, open space, commercial, industrial, and interconnections between different types of land use. Students will understand the importance of land use tools in the planning process and its impact on cities and the welfare of urban residents. The course also covers zoning and growth management strategies.
Land Use (GEO402) > Credit Hours : 3

Land Use (GEO402) > Prerequisites
GEO221 with a minimum grade D
Land Use (GEO402) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze the nature and scope of data needed for the proper planning of different land ses.

Apply land use planning terms and techniques in the study and interpretation of UAE city and urban area plans.

Identify key land use values ( livability, social, economic, & Environmental)

Prepare a study related to land use planning in the UAE in coordination with local planning agencies

Recognize the use of zoning regulations as key strategies for addressing current and future planning problems

GEO410.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO410 Research Seminar in Geography
GEO410.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO410
Research is the basic focus of this subject. At its most fundamental level research is simply a consistent way of asking questions and finding answers to them . The course covers diverse topics related to research methodology in geography. For example, research methods/approaches, types of research, sources of data for research (geographical, statistical), field survey, geographical techniques for research, steps for producing geographical research, and factors controlling good quality research. (This course should be taken over a complete semester. Other courses can be registered with with it).
Research Seminar in Geography (GEO410) > Credit Hours : 3

Research Seminar in Geography (GEO410) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the methodology and approaches of geographical research

Research design in geography using different approaches.

Identify problems and suggest recommendations to solve it .

Use and analyze data

GEO413.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO413 Geomorphology
GEO413.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO413
This course involves the study of the characteristics, origin and development of landforms and examines the processes operating within the Earth’s surface systems that shape, modify and lead to the genesis of the surface landforms. From the perspective of landscape management, the course places emphasis on the understanding the processes of weathering, slope development, fluvial systems, desert features, glacial landforms, coasts and shorelines. Topical issues in geomorphology in the UAE are discussed in detail.
Geomorphology (GEO413) > Credit Hours : 3

Geomorphology (GEO413) > Prerequisites
GEO201 with a minimum grade D
Geomorphology (GEO413) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze and map geomorphic features using remote sensing data, land survey techniques and arcgis.

Apply the major concepts and skill sets built in introductory physical geography to more complex problems found in geomorphologic studies.

Describe The Main Tectonic, Fluvial, Coastal And Karstic Land Forms And Processes.

Design applied research projects on geomorphology of the UAE using field survey, mapping tools and lab skills that were gained during the course.

Develop and apply laboratory analytical skills such as identifying rocks and minerals using microscope, grain size analysis, and permeability test for rocks and soil.

Recognize the materials of the landforms (rocks, minerals and soil) and identify their physical and chemical characteristics.

GEO418.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO418 Planning and Urban Design Lab
GEO418.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO418
The main goal of this course; Urban Design Lab, is to help students develop a working knowledge of two software that are used often in urban planning practice. The two selected programs for this course are ‘SketchUP’ and ‘Arc GIS Urban’. Students taking this course will learn to work with these two programs, on a hands-on approach, as the focus will be on helping them develop their skills in digital design. As such the course will provide students with training on the techniques, tools, and strategies for using the software. Class exercises will mainly be designed for this purpose, to help students develop a quick and good command and appreciation of the tools of the software. Following the first introductory week, this course will be conducted as follows: The first four weeks of this course will be dedicated to learning SketchUP (total of 8 lab meetings), while the following four weeks will be dedicated to learning Arc GIS Urban. The reminder of the course will be dedicated to working on both software at the same time, and also for conducting the team-based project. Students will be expected to keep a record of their coursework in a digital portfolio that will be graded at the end of the semester.
Planning and Urban Design Lab (GEO418) > Credit Hours : 3

Planning and Urban Design Lab (GEO418) > Prerequisites
GEO210 with a minimum grade D

GEO402 with a minimum grade D
Planning and Urban Design Lab (GEO418) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Use SketchUP software to draw and develop preliminary conceptual urban design ideas.

Use ArcGIS Urban software to draw and develop preliminary urban design ideas.

Work with both SketchUP and ArcGIS at the same time, to produce combined drawings.

Manage and organize digital files according to projects format and requirements.

GEO420.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO420 Cartography II
GEO420.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO420
This course involves the study and application of advanced aspects of thematic cartography to the design and production of innovative maps and atlases. As well as it provides the chance to produce a cartographic portfolio of well-designed, professional grade maps. It covers theoretical concepts, advanced techniques of data presentation and cartographic production about visual communication, perception and cognition; map reading, analysis and interpretation activities and tasks.
Cartography II (GEO420) > Credit Hours : 3

Cartography II (GEO420) > Prerequisites
GEO220 with a minimum grade D
Cartography II (GEO420) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply various statistical and geographical methods for data classification

Develop working experience in using computers for map design and Production

Interpret and analyze geographical phenomena through the use of maps

Produce high quality maps with thematic focus (dot, contours, proportional)

Show the earth-map relationship and how maps are produced

Create 3D, animated, and online maps

GEO422.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO422 Geographic Information Systems II
GEO422.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO422
Geographic Information Systems (GIS) have been a valuable component of research in geography, urban planning, and science. In the prerequisite introductory course, Geographic Information Systems (GEO221), students learned some of the basic principles underlying GIS and were introduced to key GIS capabilities and how they work. This class is designed to build on that foundation by delving deeper into the theory and various applications of GIS and examining different techniques for extracting and presenting the maximum amount of information from GIS data. The course is composed of two components: lectures and labs. The lectures will discuss the above theories and concepts, and the labs will reinforce them through hands-on exercises and projects. This course will also help you develop a personal GIS portfolio and resource collection that will be useful to you in the future as you encounter problems that can be tackled using GIS, either in future courses or in a job. Prerequisites: introductory courses in geographic information systems (GIS1) and statistics.
Geographic Information Systems II (GEO422) > Credit Hours : 3

Geographic Information Systems II (GEO422) > Prerequisites
GEO221 with a minimum grade D
Geographic Information Systems II (GEO422) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop and apply skills in advanced spatial analytical techniques and global positioning systems using data relevant to the student's field of study.

Develop and apply skills in processing, analyzing, and visualizing spatial data using commercially-available GIS software.

Explore advanced topics in modeling and visualizing spatial data and information.

Relate research results to the public.

GEO430.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO430 GIS for Transportation
GEO430.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO430
This course explores the spatial aspects of regional transportation systems including the description of network structure and flows. Topics include an introduction to models for analyzing multi-modal transportation flows and congestion over urban road and transit networks. These models include trip generation, trip distribution, modal split, and trip assignment and routing algorithms. Applications are developed in a Geographical Information Systems environment. Models are extended to urban land use, spatial safety analysis, pavement management system and air quality applications.
GIS for Transportation (GEO430) > Credit Hours : 3

GIS for Transportation (GEO430) > Prerequisites
GEO221 with a minimum grade D
GIS for Transportation (GEO430) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze network and network flows

Develop clear understanding of the application of GIS in transportation etworks.

Discuss GIS data models used in transportation.

Recognize the main concepts and topics of transportation planning, intelligent transportation networks and, environmental hazards and impacts of transportation etworks.

GEO431.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO431 Natural Hazards
GEO431.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO431
This course examines the causes, physical processes and geographic distribution of natural hazards. The aim of the course is to examine the occurrence of particular types of natural hazards, their causes and resulting social impacts. Emphasis is placed on the geographical distribution of natural hazards, the risks that they present and various response methods. Details of the systems for predicting these events and attempts made to reduce the severity of the impacts generated are also examined.
Natural Hazards (GEO431) > Credit Hours : 3

Natural Hazards (GEO431) > Prerequisites
GEO201 with a minimum grade D
Natural Hazards (GEO431) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the concepts of exposure, vulnerability and risk in the context of natural hazards.

Evaluate and explain the causes and consequences of natural azards.

Explain the temporal and spatial (global) distribution of natural hazards.

Identify the most effective measures to monitor and mitigate these natural hazards as well

GEO432.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO432 Geography of the UAE
GEO432.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO432
This course covers the geography of the United Arab Emirates (UAE) with a focus on the different geographical concepts. The entire human and physical geography of the UAE is covered in details within the course. Topics include history of the UAE as a country (from when the country was established), the landscape and geomorphology, climate and weather systems, and natural resources.
Geography of the UAE (GEO432) > Credit Hours : 3

Geography of the UAE (GEO432) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze how to employ the natural and human capital to achieve human and economic development.

Analyze the current conditions at all levels

Identify the geography of the UAE and the interaction between its natural environment and the different economic activities.

Identify the main political, social, and economic changes that occurred across the history of UAE.

GEO438.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO438 Regional and Urban Planning
GEO438.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO438
This course focuses on the relationships between urban and regional planning and the geography of regions and cities. It lays out a foundation for the planning of cities and regions, requirements for planning, models of planning, planning principles, geographical dimension of planning, major stakeholders of planning and land use, what factors impact planning decisions making process, and samples of planning entities from UAE.
Regional and Urban Planning (GEO438) > Credit Hours : 3

Regional and Urban Planning (GEO438) > Prerequisites
GEO210 with a minimum grade D
Regional and Urban Planning (GEO438) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate foundational knowledge of the history, evolution, and key issues in urban planning.

Recognize differences between the subfields of urban and regional planning

Recognize basic planning concepts including zoning, subdivision regulations, growth management, open space preservation, sustainability, economic and community development

Conduct research addressing a local urban or regional planning issue

Recognize key actors and processes which affect the shape of contemporary urban development

Demonstrate an understanding of the interconnectedness of varied issues impacting urban and regional planning including the environment, the economy, the political sphere, and the forces of globalization

GEO440.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO440 GIS for Urban & Regional Planning
GEO440.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO440
This GIS course focuses on the application of geographic information systems in the practice of urban and regional planning, with a focus on land use and environmental issues. Topics covered include GIS in decision support, GIS workflow strategies, and GIS for Decision Support in Land, Transportation, and Water Resource Management. The central component is a class project covering the collection, formatting, analysis, and presentation of land use data for a GIS application.
GIS for Urban & Regional Planning (GEO440) > Credit Hours : 3

GIS for Urban & Regional Planning (GEO440) > Prerequisites
GEO221 with a minimum grade D
GIS for Urban & Regional Planning (GEO440) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify urban planning issues and utilize GIS tools to monitor and analyze them.

Develop a small-scale urban planning project by creating project plans, assessing potential benefits, and designing GIS-based solutions.

Discuss the role and impact of GIS applications in urban and rural planning contexts.

Apply various GIS project methodologies and evaluate their effectiveness in addressing diverse urban planning challenges.

GEO443.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO443 Geography of Transportation and Mobility
GEO443.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO443
In this course, students will gain an understanding of various transportation geography concepts and urban mobility, as well as the historical development of transport systems and their impact on urban form. Additionally, different planning processes related to transportation geography and their influence on human behavior and urban development patterns will be explored. The course will also cover and examine current transportation issues, such as congestion, air quality, energy consumption, and sustainable transport.
Geography of Transportation and Mobility (GEO443) > Credit Hours : 3

Geography of Transportation and Mobility (GEO443) > Prerequisites
GEO210 with a minimum grade D
Geography of Transportation and Mobility (GEO443) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify transportation modes and the critical role of transportation

Recognize the developmental stages of transportation systems, as well as the importance of planning sustainable transport systems

Apply network analysis and other applied measures of transportation

Analyze the political, social, economic, and environmental contexts in which the transportation system must operate

Apply transportation geography concepts and theories to real-world case study

GEO450.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO450 GIS for Coastal Management
GEO450.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO450
The course provides an introduction to the fundamentals of GIS and coastal management. It focuses on how to manage and monitor characteristics of the marine environment, marine resources, organisms and economic importance, hazards of pollution, conservation laws, maritime boundaries, and legal aspects through remote sensing and GIS. The laboratory portion provides students with hands-on contact with GIS and remote sensing information products and their applications in coastal management.
GIS for Coastal Management (GEO450) > Credit Hours : 3

GIS for Coastal Management (GEO450) > Prerequisites
GEO221 with a minimum grade D
GIS for Coastal Management (GEO450) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate The Strength, Weakness, And Constraints Of Applying Remote Sensing, Gps, And Gis In Coastal Management.

Integrate Different Gis Data To Solve Real Coastal Management Problem (Physical, Chemical, Biological, Geological, Human Activity).

Use Gis Software To Build Coastal Database, Perform Spatial Analysis, Prepare Maps, Reports, And Charts For Presentation Of Results.

GEO451.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO451 Digital Imaging Analysis
GEO451.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO451
This course covers various advanced techniques of image processing and analysis of remotely sensed digital data. Topics include radiometric correction, geometric correction, atmospheric and ground effects, image enhancement, spectral analysis, color processing, image filtering, supervised and unsupervised image classification, fuzzy classification, post-classification, accuracy assessment, change detection, and image compression. Practical exercises based on satellite datasets using image processing software such as ERDAS/ENVI/IDRISI is an integral part of the course.
Digital Imaging Analysis (GEO451) > Credit Hours : 3

Digital Imaging Analysis (GEO451) > Prerequisites
GEO211
Digital Imaging Analysis (GEO451) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply practical skills and analytical background for building digital image applications.

Contrast the characteristics of digital satellite data types.

Develop practical experience in digital image processing.

Develop simple image analysis and interpretation using ERDAS software.

Explain image clustering approaches, and to be able to apply them to semi-automatically classify spectral data in order to generate your own thematic maps

Manipulate spectral data to prepare imagery for thematic classification

GEO452.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO452 Climatology
GEO452.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO452
This course examines climatological processes to arrive at an understanding of how and why climates vary spatially and temporally. The course is an introduction to the science of climatology and provides an overview of the physical processes that determine global and regional climate, including: radiative energy transfer; general atmospheric circulation patterns; atmospheric moisture and clouds formation, forms of condensation and precipitation; and global warming and climate change. The emphasis is on the processes that control the Earth's climate.
Climatology (GEO452) > Credit Hours : 3

Climatology (GEO452) > Prerequisites
GEO201 with a minimum grade D
Climatology (GEO452) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze the atmosphere and the physical processes that produce the observed climate patterns at local, regional and global scale.

Describe the criteria used to classify climates and, compare and contrast different climate types.

Describe various weather/climate measurement and observation methods.

Explain the fundamental atmospheric principles and societal processes that cause global climate change as well as the potential impacts of climate change.

GEO460.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO460 GIS for Petroleum
GEO460.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO460
This course explores spatial analysis, 3D modeling in GIS, remote sensing, GPS, and GIS data used for conducting optimum oil exploration operations, production, marketing, and environmental impact of petroleum. It covers advanced applications of multi spectral imagery for oil industry environments, locating optimal position of a new outlet, and thematic mapping of petrol stations. The course further develops hands-on skills with industry-standard GIS software for application in geologic and geophysical analysis.
GIS for Petroleum (GEO460) > Credit Hours : 3

GIS for Petroleum (GEO460) > Prerequisites
GEO221
GIS for Petroleum (GEO460) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Combine different gis data to solve a real petroleum problem (exploration, site selection, environmental impact, and marketing).

Evaluate the strength, weakness, and constraints of applying remote sensing, gps, and gis in the petroleum industry.

Use GIS software to build petroleum database, perform spatial analysis, prepare maps, reports, and charts for presentation of results.

GEO462.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO462 Current Environmental Issues
GEO462.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO462
The human race depends upon global resources to exist, yet our activities have enormous impacts on the environments that provide those resources. This course examines the most important impacts and their associated issues and discusses the causes of them. The fundamental notion of sustainability provides a unifying context for investigation of specific environmental topics in a systematic way with reference to the main environmental systems of the earth. The importance and value of the environment in providing not only resources but a complete life support system will be discussed. This course covers topics such as environment and sustainability and human impact on the environment including global climate change and pollution. Special emphasis will be given to environmental issues related to UAE and the Gulf.
Current Environmental Issues (GEO462) > Credit Hours : 3

Current Environmental Issues (GEO462) > Prerequisites
GEO201
Current Environmental Issues (GEO462) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply laboratory analytical skills used in studying environmental problems such as geospatial tools and lab analyses (i.e. soil and water ph).

Describe the environment as an interrelated geo system and the importance of sustainable use of its resources.

Explain the root causes of the most important environmental issues facing the world.

Recognize approaches to environmental impact assessment in the UAE

Recognize the human being impacts on the functioning of the environmental systems.

Use environmental knowledge, geospatial tools and lab analyses in conducting applied research projects on environmental issues in the emirates and the world.

GEO470.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO470 GIS for Environment
GEO470.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO470
The course is based on the application of GIS for studying and modeling environmental phenomena and processes in the atmosphere, cryosphere, lithosphere, and biosphere. GIS functionalities such as capturing, storing, maintaining, and analyzing geographic data will be covered. Both vector and raster GIS will be discussed, with more emphasis placed on raster GIS (e.g., applied remote sensing) as it is more suitable for modeling Earth's surface processes and related phenomena. Conducting spatial analysis using GIS and presenting results is part of the course's overall aim. Guidelines for building GIS databases and implementing GIS projects for environmental applications will be provided. Case studies demonstrating GIS as an integrating and decision-making tool will be expanded upon. The course is designed to introduce students to remote sensing techniques for measuring environmental parameters from aircraft and satellite platforms.
GIS for Environment (GEO470) > Credit Hours : 3

GIS for Environment (GEO470) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the main environmental issues locally and globally, and how to be studied using gis and remote sensing

Employ GIS and spatial analysis tools to build and analyse environmental databases and models.

Apply GIS and remote sensing as a decision-making tool for solving and managing environmental problems.

Design GIS projects for environmental applications.

GEO480.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO480 GIS for Project Management
GEO480.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO480
This course offers a critical examination of GIS and related spatial technologies in managing large-scale projects. Students will learn foundational concepts in project management alongside GIS applications for spatial decision support. Emphasis is placed on both strategic planning and practical implementation issues. Case studies from private sector projects, municipal government operations, and university-based research units provide a basis for analyzing the operational and strategic roles GIS plays across diverse environments.
GIS for Project Management (GEO480) > Credit Hours : 3

GIS for Project Management (GEO480) > Prerequisites
GEO221
GIS for Project Management (GEO480) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze the issues involved in organizing, planning, monitoring and controlling a GIS project;

Discuss the role, significance and impact of people and organizations in a project management setting and evaluate and implement strategies for managing people in projects;

Initiate a small scale gis project, by developing project plans, assessing project costs and benefits, developing investment appraisal methods and using authorization, monitoring and controlling processes;

Review GIS project management methodologies and appraise their effectiveness and adaptation to managing different types of geoinformatics projects.

GEO481.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO481 Urban Planning Internship
GEO481.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO481
The goal of internship is to gain valuable professional and practical experience in the field of Urban planning and Geo-informatics. This internship has to be done in student's junior year of college. This is a wonderful opportunity for students and potential employers alike. They provide opportunities for students to apply their newly gained skills in temporary jobs in the real world, giving them an opportunity to try their professional style in an environment that is guided by urban planning and Geo- informatics "faculty" as well as professionals in the field. The faculty supervisor and the agency supervisor will interact to monitor the student's performance, and to resolve any difficulties that may arise between the student's academic commitments and the employee tasks or responsibilities. Students are graded on their performance in the internship through a collaborative analysis by their professor and professional supervisor. Internship will give students the chance to work closely with professionals in urban planning and geo- informatics field. This means that they can establish new contacts, mentors, and references. Securing a job will be much easier if students have a handful of recommendations from industry professionals.
Urban Planning Internship (GEO481) > Credit Hours : 6

Urban Planning Internship (GEO481) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop independent learning skills.

Apply effective teamwork in knowledge-building and problem-solving in a major field of study.

Exhibit the ability to relate and effectively synthesize the knowledge, skills, and attitudes acquired through the study of sustainable urban planning with the principles and objectives of the General Education program.

Enhance leadership abilities within a professional peer setting, fostering the development of effective communication, decision-making, and collaborative skills essential for guiding and motivating teams towards common goals.

GEO482.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO482 Environmental Geography Internship
GEO482.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO482
The course offers students in the Environment and Sustainability Concentration hands-on exposure to real-world environmental and sustainability contexts. It serves as a bridge between theory and practice, facilitating the integration of classroom knowledge with practical skills. Under the guidance of mentors, interns engage in collaborative projects with professionals across public and private sectors in environmental conservation, sustainability, and resource management. This course spans a complete semester, and no other courses are permitted to be registered concurrently.
Environmental Geography Internship (GEO482) > Credit Hours : 6

Environmental Geography Internship (GEO482) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify and explain key concepts and theories related to the environment and sustainability within real-world settings.

Apply analytical skills to assess environmental issues and propose sustainable solutions.

Apply practical experience in environmental assessments, data collection, and analysis using appropriate tools and methodologies, and effectively communicate findings through written reports and presentations.

Implement solutions collaboratively with interdisciplinary teams to address complex environmental challenges, demonstrating problem-solving and leadership in diverse professional settings.

GEO483.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO483 GIS Internship
GEO483.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO483
The course provides students with hands-on exposure to real-world geoinformatics contexts. It serves as a bridge between theory and practice, fostering the integration of classroom knowledge with practical skills in Geographic Information Systems (GIS). Under the guidance of mentors, interns participate in collaborative projects with professionals across public and private sectors in geoinformatics applications, spatial analysis, and resource management. This course spans a complete semester, and concurrent registration in other courses is not permitted.
GIS Internship (GEO483) > Credit Hours : 6

GIS Internship (GEO483) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify and explain key concepts and theories related to geoinformatics within real-world settings.

Apply analytical skills to assess geographic issues using Geographic Information Systems (GIS) techniques and propose solutions.

Apply practical experience in conducting GIS assessments, data collection, analysis, and effective communication of findings.

Implement solutions with interdisciplinary teams to address geographic challenges in GIS, demonstrating problem-solving and leadership in diverse settings.

GEO485.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO485 Integrated Capstone
GEO485.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO485
A capstone is designed to provide opportunities for students to integrate knowledge from their core and concentration courses, to gain insight into the meanings of professionalism and professional practice, and to reflect on the norms of a discipline or profession. It has been designed to give students exposure to the policy and planning process through projects, critical thinking work, and other assignments, with emphases on integrating aspects of research, policy-making, management, science, and technology. Capstone courses involve projects writing of original geographic research done for real clients. All registered students are required to choose and concentrate on a geographic topic of their interest.
Integrated Capstone (GEO485) > Credit Hours : 3

Integrated Capstone (GEO485) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Develop independent learning skills.

Demonstrate effective team work in knowledge-building and problem-solving in a major field of study.

Relate and effectively synthesize knowledge, skills and attitudes acquired by completing a major field of study.

Develop leadership skills in a professional setting.

GEO490.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO490 SIS for Planetary Surfaces
GEO490.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO490
This course will introduce students to planetary and solar system, space planetary missions, planets geological and atmospheric processes, as well as planets composition and physical properties. This course is based on the application of SIS for studying and modelling planetary surfaces and their atmospheric conditions with more focus on planet Mars, which is one of the UAE government priorities. Students taking the course will be able to map different atmospheric and topographic features in different planets, particularly Mars using ArcGIS and JMARS software. Vector and raster datasets will be discussed with more emphasis put on raster datasets as applied remote sensing which is more suitable to model the planets’ surface processes and related phenomena. The students will be able to analyze space remote sensing data and develop research projects. The course is designed to introduce students to the techniques of remote sensing measurements of environmental parameters from satellite and space platforms. This course will provide the students with the needed technological and analytical skills in the space science field.
SIS for Planetary Surfaces (GEO490) > Credit Hours : 3

SIS for Planetary Surfaces (GEO490) > Prerequisites
GEO221 with a minimum grade C
SIS for Planetary Surfaces (GEO490) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the geographic differences between Earth and other planets in the Solar System through SIS.

Integrate theoretical and observational information through SIS to describe the cause(s) of the variety of topographical objects in the solar system.

Explain conditions necessary for life and to assess scientific evidence to for life on planets (Mars and Earth) through SIS.

Employ SIS and spatial analysis tools in studying and modeling planetary surfaces.

GEO495.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO495 Sustainable Development: Geographic Perspectives
GEO495.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO495
The course expands students’ knowledge of sustainability across various organizations, industries, and practices including business, ecological, societal, government, and energy sectors using three dimensions: the environmental, social, and economic. Students develop organizing principles for meeting human development goals while also sustaining the ability of natural systems to provide the resources and ecosystem services on which the economy and society depend. Students explore specific issues that address global challenges including poverty, inequality, climate change, environmental degradation, peace, and justice.
Sustainable Development: Geographic Perspectives (GEO495) > Credit Hours : 3

Sustainable Development: Geographic Perspectives (GEO495) > Prerequisites
GEO210 with a minimum grade D
Sustainable Development: Geographic Perspectives (GEO495) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain sustainability principles and practices across diverse geographic regions, encompassing varied terrains, climates, and natural resources.

Apply organizing principles for achieving sustainable development considering factors such as biodiversity, ecosystems, land use, and water resources.

Evaluate specific sustainability challenges associates with the geographical distribution of resources, vulnerabilities, and impacts in the UAE.

Develop policies and practices for effective communication and advocacy for transformative change towards sustainability within the UAE’s diverse geographic landscapes.

GEO496.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO496 Field Survey
GEO496.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO496
The course is primarily concerned with how to introduce students to methods and techniques of conducting field surveys. The basic premise of the course is to present students with the various methods of collecting data in the field. Students taking this course will conduct various exercises in the field collecting different types of geographic data. The students will conduct field experiments and mapping exercises. Results of field projects will be analyzed and presented as a technical report. Oral field reports are required for some filed visits.
Field Survey (GEO496) > Credit Hours : 3

Field Survey (GEO496) > Prerequisites
GEO334
Field Survey (GEO496) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the primary methods of data collection.

Assess and compare a range of field data collection techniques applicable to research contexts within the United Arab Emirates.

Examine the significance and impact of primary geographic data in the context of geographical research.

Acquire the capability to plan and execute field surveys.

GEO497.title: UAEU Catalog — GEO497 Analysis of Geographic Data
GEO497.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEO497
In this course, students will engage in hands-on learning through computer lab sessions, complementing theoretical lectures. The course provides an overview of techniques for processing and analyzing geographical data sourced from diverse fields such as climatology, meteorology, geology, oceanography, and ecology. Emphasis is placed on spatial statistics and statistical modeling for effective data interpretation. During lab sessions, students will utilize various statistical packages to manipulate and analyze geographical data sets, reinforcing theoretical concepts through practical application. This lecture-lab format ensures students develop both theoretical understanding and practical skills in geographical data analysis.
Analysis of Geographic Data (GEO497) > Credit Hours : 3

Analysis of Geographic Data (GEO497) > Prerequisites
GEO201 with a minimum grade D
Analysis of Geographic Data (GEO497) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain various techniques used to process and analyze geographical data sourced from diverse fields like climatology, meteorology, geology, oceanography, and ecology.

Apply statistical techniques to process geographical spatial data and extract meaningful information.

Use different statistical packages for processing geographical data tools to manipulate and analyze spatial data sets.

Employ SPSS software to describe and model spatial data, integrating statistical techniques to interpret spatial patterns and derive insights.

GEOG650.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOG650 Remote Sensing of Terrestrial and Planetary Surfaces
GEOG650.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEOG650
This course explores the principles and techniques for remote sensing of terrestrial and planetary surface properties including composition, morphology and thermo-physical properties. It presents the theoretical foundations of various techniques and their applications to a range of problems that can be addressed using remote sensing. Students will get hands-on experience obtaining, processing and interpreting remote sensing data. They will be able to identify and use appropriate types of data and techniques for answering particular scientific questions.
Remote Sensing of Terrestrial and Planetary Surfaces (GEOG650) > Credit Hours : 3

Remote Sensing of Terrestrial and Planetary Surfaces (GEOG650) > Prerequisites
PHYS105 with a minimum grade C

PHYS110 with a minimum grade C

MATH105 with a minimum grade C

MATH110 with a minimum grade C
Remote Sensing of Terrestrial and Planetary Surfaces (GEOG650) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the theoretical basis of remote sensing.

Distinguish between application areas of remote sensing.

Interpret images produced by different types of remote sensors including multispectral, hyperspectral, thermal and microwave.

Compare different platforms and sensors used in remote sensing.

Create remote sensing techniques in a practical team project.

GEOG660.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOG660 GIS for Planetary Surfaces
GEOG660.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEOG660
This course will introduce students to planetary and solar system, space planetary missions, planets geological and atmospheric processes, as well as planets composition and physical properties. This course is based on the application of GIS for studying and modelling planetary surfaces and their atmospheric conditions with more focus on planet Mars, which is one of the UAE government priorities. Students taking the course will be able to map different atmospheric and topographic features in different planets, particularly Mars using ArcGIS and JMARS software. Vector and raster GIS datasets will be discussed with more emphasis put on raster GIS as applied remote sensing which is more suitable to model the planets’ surface processes and related phenomena. The students will be able to analyze space remote sensing data and develop research projects. The course is designed to introduce students to the techniques of remote sensing measurements of environmental parameters from satellite and space platforms. This course will provide the students with the needed technological and analytical skills in the space science field.
GIS for Planetary Surfaces (GEOG660) > Credit Hours : 3

GIS for Planetary Surfaces (GEOG660) > Prerequisites
PHYS105 with a minimum grade D

PHYS110 with a minimum grade D

MATH105 with a minimum grade D

MATH110 with a minimum grade D
GIS for Planetary Surfaces (GEOG660) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the geographic differences between Earth and other planets in the Solar System through GIS.

Create theoretical and observational information through GIS to describe the cause(s) of the variety of topographical objects in the solar system.

Appraise conditions necessary for life and the scientific evidence for life on planets (Mars) through GIS.

Apply GIS and spatial analysis tools in studying and modeling planetary surfaces.

GEOG670.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOG670 Planetary Atmospheres
GEOG670.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEOG670
This course is an introduction on the physics and chemistry of planetary atmospheres. Both the Earth atmosphere and the atmospheres of other Planets (Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, etc.) will be part of the course, starting off with the origin and evolution of planetary atmospheres. Students will be introduced to the physical laws that form the basis for our understanding of atmospheric processes. This knowledge will be utilized to explain atmospheric phenomena. In particular, the course will cover the structure and chemical composition of atmospheres. Radiation laws and radiative energy balance. The radiative transfer of scattering, absorption, and emission processes of atmospheres. The role of aerosol particles and formation of clouds. Basic concepts of atmospheric circulation/meteorology. As thus, the course is similarly relevant to aspects of Earth and Environmental Science such as the ozone layer, the greenhouse effect, and air quality.
Planetary Atmospheres (GEOG670) > Credit Hours : 3

Planetary Atmospheres (GEOG670) > Prerequisites
PHYS105 with a minimum grade D

PHYS110 with a minimum grade D

MATH105 with a minimum grade D

MATH110 with a minimum grade D
Planetary Atmospheres (GEOG670) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the laws of atmospheric physics

Apply mathematical tools to study atmospheric processes quantitatively

Evaluate the factors governing the chemical composition of planetary atmospheres

Interpret the concepts of radiative transfer and thermodynamics of atmospheres

Analyze main principles of cloud microphysics and atmospheric circulation/meteorology

GEOG703.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOG703 Geographic Information Systems: Applications in Geographical Research
GEOG703.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEOG703
This course addresses theoretical concepts in Geographic Information Science (GIS) and its applications in various fields. Stress will be made on Strength Weakness Opportunities and Threats (SWOT) of applying GIS for certain research problems related to students domains. Students are expected to conduct real GIS research project and debate the pros and cons of GIS applications.
Geographic Information Systems: Applications in Geographical Research (GEOG703) > Credit Hours : 3

Geographic Information Systems: Applications in Geographical Research (GEOG703) > Prerequisites
CHSS700
Geographic Information Systems: Applications in Geographical Research (GEOG703) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze spatial data (geographic + attribute) and synthesize meaningful conclusions.

Prepare SWOT analysis for an existing GIS project.

Complete a GIS project that addresses a real problem (urban, environmental, climate, etc.).

Present project findings with high quality informative, clear, and cartographically correct maps.

GEOG707.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOG707 Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS)
GEOG707.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEOG707
This course provides background about the Global Positioning System (GPS-USA), GLONASS (Russia), BeiDou (Compass) Navigation System (China), and Galileo (Europe) Satellites. It includes description of GNSS signal structures and the derivation of observables; characteristics of instrumentation; analysis of atmospheric, orbital, random and non­random effects; derivation of mathematical models used for absolute and differential static and kinematic positioning; pre-analysis methods and applications. Topics include instrument familiarization; field-data collection and processing; real-time and post-differential correction; and GNSS-GIS integration and mapping of geo-positional data (Tracking, monitoring).
Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) (GEOG707) > Credit Hours : 2

Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) (GEOG707) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Elaborate on how GNSS works.

Differentiate between GNSS positioning methods.

Discuss in details the GNSS Augmenting options.

Defend a project related to GNSS application.

GEOG708.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOG708 GIS Modeling
GEOG708.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEOG708
This course introduces advance vector and raster analysis modeling, and multi-criteria decision analysis. Topics include network analysis, Digital Elevation Model (DEM), 3D interpolation, and cartographic modeling. Students are expected to apply the theory in finding solution to real world problems such as optimum path in transportation, site selection, visibility analysis, and hazard assessment. Emphasis will be put on real study cases and sharing the output of projects with other students. Critical thinking skills, GIS skills, and ability to convince others with GIS approaches for diagnosing real problems and proposing solutions utilizing various tools such as high quality maps, virtual reality, simulation, and fly-through will be key outcomes of this course.
GIS Modeling (GEOG708) > Credit Hours : 3

GIS Modeling (GEOG708) > Prerequisites
GEOG703
GIS Modeling (GEOG708) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Differentiate between geographic information data models for storing data, data manipulation, and visualization.

Analyze GIS-model interactions and design procedures for modeling with GIS.

Justify selection of GIS models for specific problem.

Implement and present well-formed database models using appropriate design techniques and relational database software.

GEOG709.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOG709 Internet and Mobile GIS
GEOG709.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEOG709
This course introduces how spatial data are served on the Internet and mobile devices (tablets, mobiles). Topics that will be discussed include interactive and real time mapping, spatial databases, cloud, Big Data, problems and social impact of Internet mapping. Students will be asked to assess web-based GIS services such as in Google Earth, BING, Mapquest, HERE, and OpenStreetMap, write report about their department online GIS services, and propose new one if there is no one exists (objective, user requirements, data needed, criteria for selection hardware/software, testing the site, publishing). PHP, Google API, and MyMap freely available tools will be used in the course in addition to ArcGIS Online.
Internet and Mobile GIS (GEOG709) > Credit Hours : 3

Internet and Mobile GIS (GEOG709) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Assess critically web-based GIS technologies including advantages, disadvantages, and major challenges.

Evaluate the key differences and similarities between various mobile GIS requirements.

Design and implement a web-based GIS application project.

Debate social impact of Internet mapping.

GEOG710.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOG710 GIS & Accuracy Assessment
GEOG710.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEOG710
Quality Assurance/Quality Control (QA/QC) is an important part in a GIS project. The quality of data will determine its fitness for decision-making. Inaccurate data will lead to wasting of time and money. Inaccuracy could happen at any step in the life cycle of data (collection-processing-analysis-publication-archiving-reuse). This course focuses on GIS accuracy related to spatial component (vector, raster, GPS, Satellite images, Aerial photographs) and the attribute (statistical data). Topics include positional accuracy of GPS/maps, remote sensing images accuracy (confusion matrix, User’s/Producer’s accuracy), and Quality Assurance/Quality Control (QA/QC) for GIS projects. Accuracy standards adopted by various organizations such as ISO 19157-1, ISO 19157-3, the USGS, UK Ordnance Survey, and American Society for Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing will be discussed and the rationale behind each standard will be highlighted. Students will be asked to write reports about the current QA/QC adopted in their or any other departments and why.
GIS & Accuracy Assessment (GEOG710) > Credit Hours : 3

GIS & Accuracy Assessment (GEOG710) > Prerequisites
GEOG703
GIS & Accuracy Assessment (GEOG710) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate critically the potential impact of data quality on spatial analysis and decision-making.

Assess GIS Quality Assurance/Quality Control (QA/QC) in a pilot GIS project with appropriate evidences.

Develop practical hands-on experience using GIS and RS software’s for QA/QC.

GEOG712.title: UAEU Catalog — GEOG712 GIS Programming
GEOG712.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4969.shtml?id=GEOG712
The main goal of this course is to train students on how to automate GIS and remote sensing operations using the Python scripting language. Automation can make work easier, faster, and more accurate. Knowledge of a scripting language is a highly desired skill in GIS market.
