Explain international tax evasion and avoidance concepts, including transfer pricing and their effects on the global economy.

Explain key international tax laws including double taxation agreements between countries.

Assess the current and potential role of the UAE in international taxation.

Explain the implications of tax residency for the international movement of individuals as expatriates.

ACCT500.title: UAEU Catalog — ACCT500 Elements of Accounting and Finance
ACCT500.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4977.shtml?id=ACCT500
This is a foundation pre-requisite course for those who do not have a first degree in accounting or business. The course introduces financial accounting, its role, nature, purpose and limitations of accounting conventions. Regulatory accounting framework. Financial statements construction, use and interpretation. Legal and economic considerations including elements of taxation. Basic principles of corporate governance. The course also covers introduction to finance. The financial system and flow of funds. The financial decisions of firms, investment appraisal, and life-cycle financial planning. The module also introduces managerial accounting.
Elements of Accounting and Finance (ACCT500) > Credit Hours : 3

ACCT505.title: UAEU Catalog — ACCT505 Financial and Corporate Reporting
ACCT505.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4977.shtml?id=ACCT505
This is a foundation pre-requisite course for those who do not have a first degree in accounting. In this course, students will learn the environmental and theoretical structure of financial accounting, the accounting process, and preparation of an income statement, balance sheet and statement of cash flows. Students will also learn how to measure income, do profitability analysis and to apply time value of money concepts to financial accounting measurements. In this course students will learn how to account for the economic resources and liabilities of an enterprise.
Financial and Corporate Reporting (ACCT505) > Credit Hours : 3

Financial and Corporate Reporting (ACCT505) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate recording of business transactions following the complete steps of accounting cycle.

Apply the IFRSs concepts and techniques to prepare statement of financial position, statement of cash flows, statement of income and statement of changes in equity.

Analyze financial statements by using different ratios.

Apply methods and procedures in accordance with IFRSs in assets recognition and valuation.

Demonstrate understanding of concepts and principles underlying accounting, reporting and disclosure for current and noncurrent liabilities.

Demonstrate understanding of concepts and principles underlying accounting, reporting and disclosure for equity.

Explain effectively, using appropriate technologies and through a field project, the complete steps within the accounting cycle.

ACCT510.title: UAEU Catalog — ACCT510 Management and Cost Accounting
ACCT510.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4977.shtml?id=ACCT510
This is a foundation pre-requisite course for those who do not have a first degree in accounting. Students study the information needed by managers to plan, monitor, and improve their critical processes, products, and services. This course stresses the application of information technologies to tasks such as measuring costs to produce, market, and deliver products and services; planning via flexible budgets and cost volume profit analysis; Students communicate implications of their analyses to stakeholders using database, spreadsheet, and word processing skills.
Management and Cost Accounting (ACCT510) > Credit Hours : 3

Management and Cost Accounting (ACCT510) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Compute financial and non-financial information relating to the cost of acquiring or consuming resources by an organization for internal reporting purposes.

Illustrate how costs behave for internal management purposes.

Distinguish between relevant and irrelevant cost data for decision making purposes.

Describe the various management accounting tools including the ABC, CVP and flexible budgeting for planning and control purposes

ACCT520.title: UAEU Catalog — ACCT520 Accounting Bridging Course (Online)
ACCT520.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4977.shtml?id=ACCT520
This course introduces fundamental accounting principles and demonstrates their use in financial and managerial reporting for business organizations. It emphasizes the four financial statements produced by the accounting information system and the concepts governing their preparation. It covers the relevant components of the annual report providing additional information to investors. Students will also be exposed to issues related to agency relationships and the conceptual financial framework governing financial reporting. Managerial accounting topics include costing concepts and methods, cost-volume-profit analysis, cost allocation and standard costs. The course also introduces ethical issues in accounting.
Accounting Bridging Course (Online) (ACCT520) > Credit Hours : 0

Accounting Bridging Course (Online) (ACCT520) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the importance of the financial reporting conceptual framework and the various concepts and conventions which govern the overall financial reporting process under the accrual basis of accounting.

Illustrate the articulation between the different financial statements and the importance of accounting information disclosure according to various reporting principles.

Analyze the different costing concepts and classification and how financial information can be used in management decision making processes.

ACCT600.title: UAEU Catalog — ACCT600 Advanced Financial Accounting for Corporations
ACCT600.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4977.shtml?id=ACCT600
This course is designed to deal with financial accounting and reporting by corporations. It focuses on three main themes. The first theme covers the conceptual basis and practical aspects of accounting for business combinations. The second theme focuses on the measurement, reporting and disclosure issues associated with foreign currency transaction and the accounting implications of hedging foreign currency exposed assets and liabilities. The final theme deals with the translation of the financial statements of foreign affiliates into reporting currency of the investor company.
Advanced Financial Accounting for Corporations (ACCT600) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Financial Accounting for Corporations (ACCT600) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply the appropriate accounting concepts to translate financial statements of foreign affiliated entities into local currency

Apply the appropriate accounting techniques for goodwill valuation and impairment

Apply the appropriate procedure in accounting for foreign currency transactions, fair value hedge and cash flow hedge

Apply the appropriate steps to translate foreign currency transactions for each of the three stage of concern to the accountant

Construct consolidated financial statements for a group of affiliated companies under the cost and equity methods

Evaluate the argument for using derivative instruments to hedge foreign currency exchange rate risks.

Explain the disclosure requirements for firms with affiliates in foreign countries

Explain the statement of financial accounting concepts that inform the processes of accounting for business combination.

ACCT603.title: UAEU Catalog — ACCT603 Management Accounting & Financial Analysis
ACCT603.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4977.shtml?id=ACCT603
This course covers financial and management accounting tools and techniques applied in economic decision-making in a variety of organizational contexts. It addresses how managers use accounting information to choose strategies, implement them into day to day management and communicate with internal and external stakeholders. Upon completion of the course students would have gained ability to understand, financial statements and statement analysis, make capital investment decisions, the effects of overhead costs on Product costing and Pricing, various methods of building operational budgets and be familiar with modern Process Management and Accounting and making capital investment decisions.
Management Accounting & Financial Analysis (ACCT603) > Credit Hours : 3

Management Accounting & Financial Analysis (ACCT603) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze Financial Statements And Evaluate Companies Performance

Compile Cost Reports And Operational Budgets

Describe And Apply Financial Statements

Describe And Interpret Modern Cost Management Structures

Evaluate And Recommend Capital Investment Decisions

Examine The Effects Of Costs Structure On Product Costing And Pricing

ACCT615.title: UAEU Catalog — ACCT615 Advanced Management Accounting
ACCT615.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4977.shtml?id=ACCT615
This course focuses on management accounting techniques to be used in cost management; decision making under uncertainty, and planning. The course provides useful information on using effective methods for costs management, which enhances execution of organisational objectives at operational level. It discusses decision making under uncertainty and financial modelling (sensitivity analysis, scenario analysis, Monte Carlo analysis) in analyzing impact of uncertainty on future financial outcomes. It, also, discusses contemporary trends in effective budgeting practice. The course applies excel applications in accounting techniques.
Advanced Management Accounting (ACCT615) > Credit Hours : 3

Advanced Management Accounting (ACCT615) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze Management Accounting Tools For Financial Modeling (Sensitivity Analysis, Scenario Analysis, Monte Carlo Analysis) In Analyzing Impact Of Uncertainty On Future Financial Outcomes.

Apply Accounting Techniques Using Computer Applications, E.G., Excel.

Apply Contemporary Trends In Planning.

Evaluate Management Accounting Techniques/Approaches For Decision Making Under Uncertainty.

Evaluate Management Accounting Tools For Cost Management.

ACCT620.title: UAEU Catalog — ACCT620 Auditing, Accountability and Assurance Services

ACCT630.title: UAEU Catalog — ACCT630 Financial Accounting Standards, Theory and Policy
ACCT630.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4977.shtml?id=ACCT630
The course focuses on conceptual framework of financial reporting, including issues of definition, valuation and presentation of contents of financial reports. The course explains alternative approaches to presenting information in financial statements as mandated by accounting standards. It discusses the reasons of moving towards a concept of comprehensive income and what this means for users of accounts. The course addresses important issues such as accounting theories as a basis for developing standards and policies, the impact of harmonisation on accounting standards, accounting earnings quality in an international context, the impact of corporate governance, and earnings management amongst others.
Financial Accounting Standards, Theory and Policy (ACCT630) > Credit Hours : 3

Financial Accounting Standards, Theory and Policy (ACCT630) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply Accounting Principles, Theories, Concepts And Knowledge Of Accounting Techniques To Debate And Solve Financial Reporting Problems.

Compare Available Accounting Policy Choices For Inclusion In Financial Reporting Standards, And Their Theoretical Bases.

Demonstrate A Deeper Understanding Of Some Contemporary Issues In Accounting, And The Ability To Critically Analyze These Issues Within The Theoretical Framework Developed During The Course.

Discuss The Concepts Of Theory Development And Theories Of Accounting Policy Choice, Measurement Of Economic Income And The Societal Use Of Accounting Information.

Employ Oral And Written Communication Skills To Further Learning, And Effectively Convey Understanding Of Accounting Issues To An Audience.

Evaluate The Underlying Principles, Concepts, Theories, And Assumptions In The Field Of Accounting.

ACCT635.title: UAEU Catalog — ACCT635 Sustainable Financial Analysis and Valuation
ACCT635.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4977.shtml?id=ACCT635
This course provides an in-depth examination of financial statement analysis and valuation techniques within the context of both traditional and sustainability-focused financial reporting frameworks. Students will assess a company's financial health using ratio analysis, common-size analysis, trend analysis, benchmarking, and content analysis. The course also covers firm valuation methods, including discounted cash flow and relative valuation, with an emphasis on the impact of sustainability on firm value. Through case studies and/or projects, students will critically analyze financial statements and sustainability disclosures, leading to informed valuations.
Sustainable Financial Analysis and Valuation (ACCT635) > Credit Hours : 3

Sustainable Financial Analysis and Valuation (ACCT635) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate professional communication skills by effectively interpreting and presenting insights on financial statements and ESG disclosures using real-world case studies.

Assess corporate financial and ESG disclosures comprehensively using financial reporting and sustainability frameworks.

Utilize advanced financial analysis techniques that integrate ESG factors to provide a more holistic understanding of corporate financial health using real-world cases.

Evaluate firm valuation using discounted cash flow and relative valuation while incorporating ESG factors to understand their impact on conventional valuation measures.

Choose teamwork to apply both traditional financial analysis and ESG-focused strategies for conducting comprehensive financial reporting quality assessment using case studies.

ACCT640.title: UAEU Catalog — ACCT640 Management Control Systems
ACCT640.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4977.shtml?id=ACCT640
This course examines a wide range of fundamental managerial techniques used by companies in their internal planning and control functions. In particular, it focuses on investment analysis techniques, international transfer pricing, types of control systems, issues of contracting and management control across organizational and international boundaries, financial and non-financial performance measures, and incentive systems in various organizations.
Management Control Systems (ACCT640) > Credit Hours : 3

Management Control Systems (ACCT640) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Appraise The Opportunities And Difficulties Of Using Financial And Non-Financial Measures Of Performance To Support Improved Planning And Control.

Assess The Different Types Of Management Controls.

Contrast The Alternative Methods Used For International Transfer Pricing.

Demonstrate Increased Proficiency In Applying Various Investment Analysis Methods Using Excel.

Explain The Emerging Issues Of Contracting And Management Control Across Organizational And International Boundaries.

Select Incentive Systems In Various Organizations.

ACCT645.title: UAEU Catalog — ACCT645 Seminar on Applied Research in Accounting
ACCT645.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4977.shtml?id=ACCT645
This course helps students develop applied professional research skills in accounting and auditing. The course provides concrete applied research guidance. It discusses relevant sources and methods to research standards issued by FASB/IASB and to find solutions to current accounting problems. The course also emphasizes how applied research could generate empirical results that advance professional interests and capabilities.
Seminar on Applied Research in Accounting (ACCT645) > Credit Hours : 3

Seminar on Applied Research in Accounting (ACCT645) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Assess The Role Of Applied Research Within A Public Accounting Firm, A Private Or A Governmental Entity.

Demonstrate Ability Of Effective Writing And Oral Communication Skills.

Describe The Meaning And Elements Of Critical Thinking.

Develop Critical Thinking Skills In Accounting Practice Issues.

Distinguish Between The Theoretical Research And Applied Research.

Subdivide The Eight Elements Of Reasoning.

Synthesize The Basic Steps Of The Applied Accounting Research Process.

ACCT661.title: UAEU Catalog — ACCT661 Accounting in Special Contexts
ACCT661.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4977.shtml?id=ACCT661
This elective course will be tailored depending on the professional background of the students enrolled in it. Topics covered (but not all) should be related to issues in management accounting and financial management in government and public sector, and not-for-profit organizations. In addition, topics selected can cover issues related to Ecommerce Business and the role of budgeting in governmental and not-for-profit organizations.
Accounting in Special Contexts (ACCT661) > Credit Hours : 3

ACCT662.title: UAEU Catalog — ACCT662 Risk-based Internal Auditing
ACCT662.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4977.shtml?id=ACCT662
This elective course will build on some of the material covered in the core modules relating to corporate governance and control. Internal audit is one of the most important and basic business functions that are increasingly gaining more importance, especially after many corporate collapses such as Enron and WorldCom. Topics covered include the Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) framework, business risks, business process analysis and internal control systems. Application of the concepts taught to real life organizations is an integrated fundamental part of this course.
Risk-based Internal Auditing (ACCT662) > Credit Hours : 3

Risk-based Internal Auditing (ACCT662) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate Effective Communication To An Audience Of Professionals A Project Based Findings

Apply The Notion Of Risk Management To Business Processes In Various Business Contexts Through A Supervised Group Field Study.

Describe The Role Of Various Levels Of Management In Providing The Corporate Governance Requirements.

Discuss The Relationship Between Governance And Erm Within The Coso Framework.

Evaluate The Level Of Maturity Of An Internal Auditing Performance In Real Life Organization.

Illustrate The Professional Framework That Guides The Work Of Internal Auditors.

Recommend The Different Types Of Risk Controls And The Appropriate Application For Each Of Them Within A Professional Framework.

ACCT663.title: UAEU Catalog — ACCT663 Accounting for Islamic Financial Institutions
ACCT663.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4977.shtml?id=ACCT663
This elective course is designed for students with special interest on accounting in Islamic financial institutions. It is designed to enable students to identify and apply the accounting principles and procedures of the various modes of Islamic financial transactions. It covers topics such as Islamic banking and finance, zakat, takaful and awqaf. The course also emphasizes (accountants and auditors) ethics and accountability in accounting for the Islamic products and services.
Accounting for Islamic Financial Institutions (ACCT663) > Credit Hours : 3

Accounting for Islamic Financial Institutions (ACCT663) > Prerequisites
ACCT630
Accounting for Islamic Financial Institutions (ACCT663) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the conceptual differences between conventional accounting and Islamic accounting.

Explain the importance of ethics for accountants and auditors in Islamic accounting framework.

Apply Islamic accounting standards for reporting on Islamic financial products.

Apply teamwork skills in the context of Islamic accounting.

Distinguish between the auditing and governance structure of conventional and Islamic business organizations.

ACCT664.title: UAEU Catalog — ACCT664 Taxation in the UAE Business Environment
ACCT664.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4977.shtml?id=ACCT664
This course aims to develop students' knowledge and skills in the policies, regulations, and principles governing business taxation in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). It examines the role and functions of a tax system in society, exploring its relationship with the business environment. Students will analyze how tax policies influence business decisions, economic growth, and global competitiveness. The course provides practical insights into calculating tax liabilities for corporate income tax, value-added tax (VAT), and excise duties within the UAE, supplemented by global comparative perspectives. Through case studies and data-driven analysis, students will gain hands-on experience in tax calculations and understanding their implications for businesses.
Taxation in the UAE Business Environment (ACCT664) > Credit Hours : 3

Taxation in the UAE Business Environment (ACCT664) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain fundamental taxation principles and their role in shaping business environments, highlighting their economic and strategic implications in the UAE.

Apply tax principles to calculate tax liabilities for corporate income tax, VAT and excise tax.

Analyze tax compliance requirements and regulatory frameworks in the UAE, focusing on their impact on business operations

Evaluate the effects of tax policies on business strategy, competitiveness, and economic growth.

Compare international tax systems and assess their influence on multinational business operations, using UAE-based scenarios.

Design a strategic tax plan for a business scenario and effectively present findings, applying UAE tax principles to maximize business performance and compliance.

ACCT665.title: UAEU Catalog — ACCT665 Strategic Management Accounting
ACCT665.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4977.shtml?id=ACCT665
This is an elective course that compliments managerial accounting courses in the core. This course aims to examine the use of financial and non-financial information for the purpose of analyzing business strategy and associated processes to achieve superior organizational performance. The course introduces a number of strategic management accounting tools and techniques that can be used to analyze how business strategy and associated processes consume resources, create value for a firm and its customers, and how this value may be enhanced through continuous improvement.
Strategic Management Accounting (ACCT665) > Credit Hours : 3

Strategic Management Accounting (ACCT665) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Analyze Business Strategy And Associated Processes Through The Application Of Strategic Management Accounting Techniques.

Apply Techniques Associated With Strategic Cost Management Systems And Strategic Performance Measurement Systems To Improve Business Strategy And Associated Processes.

Demonstrate Ability To Autonomously Engage In Business Problem Solving With The Use Of Management Accounting Techniques.

Demonstrate Ability To Work As Part Of A Team To Solve Complex Business Problems Using Management Accounting Techniques.

Evaluate The Effectiveness Of Alternative Management Accounting Techniques In Improving Organizational Performance.

Prepare A Management Accounting Report That Addresses A Complex Business Problem.

Use Oral Presentation To Report Management Accounting Solutions To Interested Parties.

ACCT666.title: UAEU Catalog — ACCT666 Selected Topics in Financial Reporting
ACCT666.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4977.shtml?id=ACCT666
This elective course highlights some of the main issues that need particular attention within the financial reporting area. These topics include, but not limited to, issues of uncertain tax positions, XBRL, issues of fair value, servicing assets and liabilities, issues of complexity in financial reporting, derivatives, and pensions.
Selected Topics in Financial Reporting (ACCT666) > Credit Hours : 3

MGEN600.title: UAEU Catalog — MGEN600 Molecular Biology of the Gene
MGEN600.text:
This course provides students with a comprehensive overview of fundamental principles in human molecular biology and molecular genetics, addressing various aspects. Students will explore the intricate molecular structures and characteristics of eukaryotic macromolecules, gaining insights into their functions. Additionally, the curriculum will cover the complex regulation of genes in eukaryotic organisms, spanning transcriptional, posttranscriptional, translational, and post-translational processes. Emphasis will be placed on understanding macromolecular interactions crucial for specific gene regulatory mechanisms. In this course students will refine their analytical skills by critically evaluating and summarizing recent research papers showcasing groundbreaking discoveries in human molecular biology.
Molecular Biology of the Gene (MGEN600) > Credit Hours : 3

Molecular Biology of the Gene (MGEN600) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the molecular structure and properties of eukaryotic macromolecules.

Recognize complex eukaryotic gene regulation at the transcriptional, posttranscriptional, translational, and post-translational levels.

Assess macromolecular interactions involved in specific gene regulatory mechanisms

Critically evaluate research papers describing the latest findings in human molecular biology.

MGEN601.title: UAEU Catalog — MGEN601 Human Genetics
MGEN601.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4979.shtml?id=MGEN601
In this course, students will dissect the principles of inheritance of human traits with emphasis on genetic disorders and their exceptions such as reduced penetrance, genetic anticipation, variable expression, haploinsufficiency, genomic imprinting etc. The course will also cover the types and implications of genetic and genomic variations including the functional implications of genetic aberrations leading to disease states. Population genetics including Hardy-Weinberg principles as well as the concepts of variability in susceptibility and resistance to infections will be delivered.
Human Genetics (MGEN601) > Credit Hours : 2

Human Genetics (MGEN601) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Dissect the various modes of inheritance with their exceptions and carry out risk assessment on the occurrence of genetic and genomic diseases.

Recognize, compare and contrast the various types of genetic and genomic aberrations and their biological and cellular implications.

Discuss the interplay between genetics and the environment in health and disease including susceptibility to common conditions and response to infections and medications

Evaluate the strategies employed for the diagnosis, prevention and treatment of genetic disorders.

Calculate alleles and genotypes frequencies using the principles of population genetics as well as the Mendelian modes of inheritance with implication for risk evaluation

Retrieve genetic Information from genomic browsers

Critically evaluate the recent literature in the field of Human Genetics.

MGEN602.title: UAEU Catalog — MGEN602 Molecular Basis of Human Diseases
MGEN602.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4979.shtml?id=MGEN602
This course will introduce students to the central concepts of pathophysiology and genetic processes implicated in disease pathogenesis including molecular and cytogenetic pathogenic events leading to disease. Students will learn how abnormalities that occur at the molecular and cellular level manifest as pathologies affecting the structure and function of human tissues and organs. This course will discuss major discipline of pathologies explaining their pathophysiology, clinical manifestations, and evaluation and treatment.
Molecular Basis of Human Diseases (MGEN602) > Credit Hours : 2

Molecular Basis of Human Diseases (MGEN602) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognize fundamental concepts related to the mechanisms of human disease.

Identify the current understanding of selected major human diseases at molecular and cellular levels with resulted physiological consequences.

Judge the roles and interplay of molecules (such as DNA, RNA, proteins, metabolites, etc.) and environment in disease pathogenesis.

Inspect the role of epigenetics in human development and disease.

Connect pathologies to genomic aberrations.

MGEN603.title: UAEU Catalog — MGEN603 Bioinformatics and Genomics
MGEN603.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4979.shtml?id=MGEN603
This course is composed 1CH lectures and 1CH computer-based practical. In this course, students will gain an overview of the principles of bioinformatics in the genomic field. The emphasis will be on the theoretical background of the bioinformatic and techniques employed in genomic analysis. The course will introduce the major components of bioinformatic: definition, application, and basic analysis. Furthermore, the course will assist students in developing the core concepts of the Interdisciplinary field of bioinformatic in the genomic concept. They will be familiar with principle and application of genomic analysis. Student will learn how to compare and analyze genetic data.
Bioinformatics and Genomics (MGEN603) > Credit Hours : 2

Bioinformatics and Genomics (MGEN603) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognize the various bioinformatics tools and methods employed in genomic analysis.

Retrieve genomic information from various available genomic databases

Interpret the genetic variation in disease concept

Perform elementary prediction for variant pathogenicity

Conduct association analysis based on genotyping and sequencing data.

Construct phylogenetic trees based on sequence data

Critically compare bioinformatics tools and methods currently used to analyze genomic data.

MGEN604.title: UAEU Catalog — MGEN604 Genetic & Genomic Diagnostics
MGEN604.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4979.shtml?id=MGEN604
This course is a combination of lectures (2CH) and wet-lab practical sessions (1CH) that will cover good lab practice and the diagnostics processes involved in testing genetic disorders. The course will help students to understand the reasons for genetic testing referrals in medical genomics such as diagnostic testing, pre-symptomatic and predictive testing, carrier testing, new-born screening, prenatal testing and preimplantation testing. This course will provide students with real-life wet-lab experience on how to run genetic testing from sample handling to running basic and advanced techniques including polymerase chain reaction (PCR), Sanger sequencing, and next generation sequencing emphasizing their application to clinical practice. By the end of this course students will be able to determine which test and technology are most suitable for a given clinical scenario recognizing their advantages and limitations.
Genetic & Genomic Diagnostics (MGEN604) > Credit Hours : 3

Genetic & Genomic Diagnostics (MGEN604) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognize the relevance, social and ethical implications of genetic and genomic testing in clinical practice.

Realize the recommendations for good laboratory practices for ensuring the quality of molecular genetic testing for genetic diseases

Identify reasons for genetic testing and commonly used methodologies

Compare between different genetic techniques and genomic technologies.

Independently identify which genetic test and technique should be used for a given diagnosis.

Critically evaluate genetic testing performance and results.

MGEN605.title: UAEU Catalog — MGEN605 OMICS in Medicine
MGEN605.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4979.shtml?id=MGEN605
This course is a combination of lectures (1CH) and computer-based practicals (1CH). In this course, students will gain an insight into the molecular intricacy of human variations at multiple levels beyond the genome sequence including transcriptome, epigenome, proteome, and metabolome as a crucial necessity for the comprehensive understanding of human health and diseases. Students will be introduced to OMICS technologies and basic knowledge of OMICS data analysis workflows. They will learn the difference between the genome and the transcriptome as well as the methodologies presently used to investigate sequence variations affecting gene expression mainly RNA sequencing and gene expression arrays. It will provide an overview of the structure and function of the epigenome, including the regulation of gene transcription and its relationship to the genome. It will also include an introduction to proteomics and metabolomics, which are important for the functional interpretation of genomic data and the discovery of disease biomarkers. In addition, this course will provide the students with first-hand experience of learning about the multiple steps of omics data experimental design, experimental steps, data analysis and interpretation.
OMICS in Medicine (MGEN605) > Credit Hours : 2

OMICS in Medicine (MGEN605) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognize the role of the OMES in bridging the gap from genotype to phenotype.

Describe a range of up-to-date techniques and platforms used to explore the OMES.

Judge the role of transcriptomics, epigenomics, metabolomics and proteomics in the functional interpretation of genomic data.

Identify the approaches to the bioinformatics analysis and interpretation of OMICS data.

Apply appropriate analysis and quality control steps on OMICS data.

Critically evaluate the criteria of a great experimental design for different omics technologies and formulate an ideal omics experiment.

MGEN606.title: UAEU Catalog — MGEN606 Translational Medicine: From Bench to Bedside
MGEN606.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4979.shtml?id=MGEN606
This course provides opportunities for the students to learn the basic principles of translational science in medicine. It explains how to translate medical research findings into clinical treatment options, drug development and diagnostic biomarkers. The content covers the steps from benchside (research) to bedside (clinical) starting with identifying a biomarker for a disease and following on through drug development.
Translational Medicine: From Bench to Bedside (MGEN606) > Credit Hours : 2

Translational Medicine: From Bench to Bedside (MGEN606) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Define translational medicine basic concepts and definition

Describe the process of biomarker and drug development

Identify mechanisms and connections between basic bench science research and translational therapies in medical practice

Discuss real-world examples of translational medicine practices

Critically evaluate the reasons behind the success or the failure of translational research projects

MGEN607.title: UAEU Catalog — MGEN607 Pharmacogenomics and Stratified Medicine
MGEN607.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4979.shtml?id=MGEN607
Pharmacogenomics (PGx) is defined by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) as “The study of variations of DNA and RNA characteristics as related to drug response”. Therefore, the premise of PGx and stratified health is to ensure that patients are offered the 'right treatment, for the right person, at the right time’. This is a lecture and demonstration based course that provides a comprehensive overview of the strategies used in PGx and stratified medicine (i.e. tailoring therapies to the individual’s genetic make-up or stratified groups). The students will learn the latest advances in PGx including the different types of genomic biomarkers and their predictive value for optimising drug responses and preventing adverse reactions. The course will start with an introduction to the types and diversity of genetic variation (SNPs, variability of short sequence repeats, haplotypes, DNA modifications; for example, methylation, deletions or insertions, copy number variants, RNA expression levels, RNA splicing, microRNA levels) among individuals then illustrate the various types of gene products that might influence response to medications (drug-metabolizing enzymes, drug targets etc.). In particular, the genomic basis of drug reaction and drug efficacy and how these are implemented in prescribing practice as well as allelic heterogeneity between different ethnic groups. These will also be illustrated through examples of genomic-targeted interventions and how to tailor drug treatments to improve a patient’s response. These examples will include biomarkers in the treatments of cardiovascular disease, psychiatric disorders, analgesics, oncology etc. Students will also learn about the various pharmacogenomics databases, guidelines and algorithms and how to translate genotypes to make clinical recommendations.
Pharmacogenomics and Stratified Medicine (MGEN607) > Credit Hours : 2

Pharmacogenomics and Stratified Medicine (MGEN607) > Prerequisites
BMB602

MGEN601
Pharmacogenomics and Stratified Medicine (MGEN607) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate an advanced understanding of the basis of inter-individual variability in drug response and adverse effects.

Integrate and apply knowledge from the PGx and clinical sciences to evaluate the scientific literature in relations to drug action and potential therapeutic problems arising from interindividual genetic variability.

Demonstrate knowledge and deep understating of application of PGx in major human conditions such cardiovascular, psychiatric, oncology and others.

Use evidence-based and internationally recognized guidelines to formulate patient-specific medication recommendations based on PGx test results.

Interpret PGx genotyping results and make recommendations on optimal drug selection and dosing and communicate these recommendations to the health care team and patients.

MGEN608.title: UAEU Catalog — MGEN608 Principles of Genetic Counseling
MGEN608.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4979.shtml?id=MGEN608
Genetic counseling is a unique area of healthcare encompassing genomic knowledge, education, communication, and compassion. This fundamental course provides an overview of the profession, basic concepts covered in a genetic counseling clinical setting as well as the complexities of applying genomics to healthcare scenarios. Along with theory, case studies will provide practical opportunities for students to engage with discussions about use of language and personal styles of communication. Students will explore in depth specialty areas of Clinical Genomics. The program will enable students to begin their genetic counseling practice independently.
Principles of Genetic Counseling (MGEN608) > Credit Hours : 2

Principles of Genetic Counseling (MGEN608) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the evolution of genetic counseling as a profession internationally, define what the genetic counseling process entails and describe the role of a genetic counselor in the clinic

Identify the areas where genetic counseling can impact on a family's experience of the genomics journey and recognize specific scenarios where genetic /genomic counseling has an important role.

Demonstrate the application of genomics in several specialty areas such as cancer, assisted reproduction and cardiovascular diseases

Demonstrate how to interpret complex genomic information and communicate it effectively to a targeted audience.

Utilize key counselling processes to assist clients appropriately with their responses to grief and personal loss in a clinical setting

MGEN609.title: UAEU Catalog — MGEN609 Genomics and Society
MGEN609.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4979.shtml?id=MGEN609
This course explores the impact genomic technology is having on society and the important role health professionals like genetic counselors play in ensuring the ethical, legal, and social implications of this technology are understood.
Genomics and Society (MGEN609) > Credit Hours : 2

Genomics and Society (MGEN609) > Corequisites
MGEN601 with a minimum grade C
Genomics and Society (MGEN609) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Define the principles of informed consent in genomic testing in clinical and/or research environment.

Recognize areas in the mainstream media where genomics is communicated and comment on its impact.

Define the impact of genomics on ethical, legal, and societal issues.

Recognize the importance of purposeful involvement in communicating with the broader community to deliver reliable information and advocate for patient groups and health care professionals.

Demonstrate occasions to promote the health and well-being of patients/ clients/ community groups impacted by genetics and genomics.

MGEN610.title: UAEU Catalog — MGEN610 Advanced Communication and Genetic Counseling Skills
MGEN610.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4979.shtml?id=MGEN610
This advanced genetic counseling subject builds on student skills gained in semester 1. Students will explore more complex concepts covered in a genetic counseling clinical setting as well as the of applying genomics and bioinformatics to healthcare. Problem based learning (PBL) is an active learning technique which will be utilized in this subject. Students will participate in role plays using scenarios which mirror those they may encounter in clinical practice. This subject will challenge students to use self-reflective practice and further develop their ability to competently tailor counselling to the client’s needs. Using a variety of counselling skills established in the first year of study, students will further learn how to remain flexible and ensure client focused care is consistently achieved
Advanced Communication and Genetic Counseling Skills (MGEN610) > Credit Hours : 2

Advanced Communication and Genetic Counseling Skills (MGEN610) > Prerequisites
MGEN608 with a minimum grade C
Advanced Communication and Genetic Counseling Skills (MGEN610) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate reflective practice to continually assess personal responses to client interactions and improve skills.

Interpret psychosocial responses to situations and facilitate the best outcome for clients.

Identify specific factors which may impact on a client’s ability to process and interpret information. These may include cultural systems and/or religious beliefs

Recognize ethical issues and respond accordingly when working with colleagues and clients.

Utilize a number of skills to listen, communicate and ensure individual style is adapted to suit the client’s needs.

MGEN611.title: UAEU Catalog — MGEN611 Genomic Medicine Capstone Project
MGEN611.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4979.shtml?id=MGEN611
The Genomic Medicine Capstone Project is a culminating experience in which students apply their knowledge to solve a practical or clinical problem in genomic medicine. Projects may include data analysis, case studies, translational reviews, software tool evaluation, implementation of a diagnostic approach, or development of a guideline or educational resource. Each project must be supervised by a faculty member, and it is the student's responsibility to secure a supervisor. Project topics may originate from faculty members, students themselves, or industry collaborators. The student is required to submit a Mid-project Progress Report, a comprehensive final report and give an oral presentation during the last week of lectures of the semester.
Genomic Medicine Capstone Project (MGEN611) > Credit Hours : 6

Genomic Medicine Capstone Project (MGEN611) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify a relevant and feasible research/project topic.

Develop a comprehensive project plan with appropriate methodology.

Execute project methods effectively using discipline-specific tools and techniques.

Communicate findings clearly in written and oral formats.

Reflect on research/project outcomes and process for future improvement.

MGEN612.title: UAEU Catalog — MGEN612 Research Capstone Project
MGEN612.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4979.shtml?id=MGEN612
The Capstone Project is the culminating academic experience of the MSGC program. Conducted over three semesters, it allows students to integrate and apply their learning through original research, program development, or educational innovation. Guided by a faculty advisor and committee, students choose a project aligned with their interests and relevant to genetic counseling. Options include original research(quantitative or qualitative), tool development, clinical interventions, case studies, or quality improvement. Students gain experience in project design, literature review, data collection, analysis, and scholarly writing. The project concludes with a written report or presentation. Through this process, students demonstrate competencies in research, communication, and professional practice while contributing valuable insights or tools to the genetic counseling field.
Research Capstone Project (MGEN612) > Credit Hours : 6

Research Capstone Project (MGEN612) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Perform a literature review

Identify important issues in a specific field related to genetic counseling and understand the scientific approach to research questions.

Carry out an original scientific study and appropriately managing its research data

Appreciate the ethics involved in conducting clinical research

Express oneself clearly in science and present their research findings either orally or in writing.

MGEN613.title: UAEU Catalog — MGEN613 Coding for Bioinformatics
MGEN613.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4979.shtml?id=MGEN613
This introductory course is designed for students with no prior programming experience, providing them with essential coding skills for modern Bioinformatics. The course will cover fundamental concepts and practical applications of the command line (Bash/Linux), R, and Python, focusing on their utility in manipulating, analyzing, and visualizing biological data. Students will learn to navigate file systems, automate tasks with shell scripting, perform statistical analysis and data visualization and sequence analysis in R, and utilize Python for data processing. The course will be delivered through a combination of lectures and hands-on sessions, allowing students to immediately apply theoretical concepts to real-world scenarios. Through practical exercises and case studies, students will develop the ability to integrate these tools to build robust Bioinformatics pipelines and independently tackle real-world genomic data challenges.
Coding for Bioinformatics (MGEN613) > Credit Hours : 2

Coding for Bioinformatics (MGEN613) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Evaluate the role of Linux/Unix environments and scripting (Bash, R, Python) in the management and analysis of high-throughput genomic data.

Develop automated Bioinformatics pipelines to process biological datasets, ensuring reproducibility and efficiency in clinical or research settings.

Execute advanced data visualization and statistical analysis using R and Python to interpret complex genomic information.

Develop an independent bioinformatics project that addresses a genomic research question through integrated computational workflows.

MGEN661.title: UAEU Catalog — MGEN661 Practical Genetic Counselling-Practicum I
MGEN661.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4979.shtml?id=MGEN661
This subject exposes students to the day to day working of a clinical, laboratory, research or community service working with clients impacted by genetics. A minimum number of supervised hours will be undertaken observing and participating in placements. It includes Community and Clinical Placement (15 days) where students will be mainly observing and familiarising themselves with the multidisciplinary team.
Practical Genetic Counselling-Practicum I (MGEN661) > Credit Hours : 3

Practical Genetic Counselling-Practicum I (MGEN661) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply the principles and policies fundamental to undertaking professional practice in several health workplaces

Demonstrate an understanding of the nature of a clinical, laboratory, research or community service working with clients impacted by genetics.

Identify the roles and contributions of the members of the multidisciplinary team.

Define the interpersonal relationship between a supervisee and supervisor.

Demonstrate an understanding of the multidisciplinary nature of the genetics setting and the role genetic counselors play.

MGEN662.title: UAEU Catalog — MGEN662 Practical Genetic Counselling-Practicum II
MGEN662.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4979.shtml?id=MGEN662
This subject exposes students to the day to day working of a clinical, laboratory, research or community service working with clients impacted by genetics. A minimum number of supervised hours will be undertaken observing and participating in placements. It includes Community and Clinical Placement (15 days) where students will begin to take on an active role providing genetic counseling under supervision of clinical geneticist and licensed genetic counselor.
Practical Genetic Counselling-Practicum II (MGEN662) > Credit Hours : 3

Practical Genetic Counselling-Practicum II (MGEN662) > Prerequisites
MGEN661 with a minimum grade C
Practical Genetic Counselling-Practicum II (MGEN662) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Recognise and comply with the professional policies of the health service where they are participating.

Demonstrate the skills required to undertake a full genetic counseling intake and family health history.

Contribute to the planning and case discussions for clinic.

Under supervision, communicate effectively with patients and clients to assess their needs and provide information to assist with support or decision making as required.

Contribute to case notes using professional language.

Under supervision, provide a written summary of the genetic counseling interaction for the patient and/or referring health professional.

MGEN663.title: UAEU Catalog — MGEN663 Practical Genetic Counselling-Practicum III
MGEN663.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4979.shtml?id=MGEN663
During year 2 placements, students will take a more hands on approach and further develop their skills working independently as well as part of a multidisciplinary team. Includes Community and Clinical Placement (25 days) in 15 weeks.
Practical Genetic Counselling-Practicum III (MGEN663) > Credit Hours : 4

Practical Genetic Counselling-Practicum III (MGEN663) > Prerequisites
MGEN662 with a minimum grade C
Practical Genetic Counselling-Practicum III (MGEN663) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate the way in which case management is undertaken both independently and within a multidisciplinary team.

Competently undertake a full intake of family and health history, collect relevant charts and education literature.

Complete several genetic counselling sessions (with supervision) where they are undertaking most of the case interaction and the needed follow up.

Evaluate different counselling strategies and provision of support and resources

Recognize ethical issues including autonomy, confidentiality, and value of informed consents.

MGEN664.title: UAEU Catalog — MGEN664 Practical Genetic Counselling-Practicum IV
MGEN664.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4979.shtml?id=MGEN664
In this final placement, students will be undertaking independent case management with supervision to support their completion of training. Includes Community and Clinical Placement (25 days)
Practical Genetic Counselling-Practicum IV (MGEN664) > Credit Hours : 4

Practical Genetic Counselling-Practicum IV (MGEN664) > Prerequisites
MGEN663 with a minimum grade C
Practical Genetic Counselling-Practicum IV (MGEN664) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Complete several genetic counselling sessions (with supervision) where they are undertaking the majority of the case interaction and follow up.

Participate fully in the role of a genetic counselor being observed by supervisor undertaking most of the face to face and follow up of clients.

MGEN665.title: UAEU Catalog — MGEN665 Practical Genetic Counseling- Practicum V
MGEN665.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4979.shtml?id=MGEN665
This additional practicum placement is offered to students with the non-thesis track who will be undertaking practical training and case management in genetic counseling with geneticist or certified genetic counselor to support their practical training. This course may include Community and Clinical Placement of one day per week for a total of 15 days.
Practical Genetic Counseling- Practicum V (MGEN665) > Credit Hours : 1

Practical Genetic Counseling- Practicum V (MGEN665) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Demonstrate the ability to assess genetic risk: guide testing strategies, and interpret results in diverse clinical scenarios

Develop and deliver personalized genetic counseling plan

Advocate for ethical and inclusive genetic services in community health settings

Educate communities through genetics outreach

NUTR100.title: UAEU Catalog — NUTR100 Nutrition and Well-being
NUTR100.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4981.shtml?id=NUTR100
This course introduces the fundamentals of nutrition and its impact on personal health and wellness. Essential nutrients, healthy eating patterns, fad diets, and the relationship between diet and disease prevention will be explored. Students will learn how to make informed dietary choices, develop lifelong wellness habits, and understand the effects of lifestyle factors—such as physical activity, sleep, and stress—on overall health. Emphasis is placed on applying nutrition principles to support physical, mental, and emotional well-being in diverse populations.
Nutrition and Well-being (NUTR100) > Credit Hours : 3

Nutrition and Well-being (NUTR100) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the major nutrients and their role in the body

Explain how nutrition impacts the physical, mental and emotional health

Identify the appropriate nutrition recommendations promoting wellbeing throughout the lifecycle

NUTR101.title: UAEU Catalog — NUTR101 Introduction to Human Anatomy and Physiology
NUTR101.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4981.shtml?id=NUTR101
The course provides essential knowledge about the structure and function of the human body designed for students pursuing a career in nutrition, dietetics, food science and other allied health fields. Developed for students with minimal background in physical and biological sciences, the course explores the physical basis of life and proceeds through increasing level of complexity. It introduces the organ systems, focusing on their structure, function and applications relevant to nutrition and health. This course is designed to stimulate the students’ interest in the subject matter, to help them relate their classroom knowledge to their health and nutrition disciplines.
Introduction to Human Anatomy and Physiology (NUTR101) > Credit Hours : 3

Introduction to Human Anatomy and Physiology (NUTR101) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain basic concepts in anatomy and physiology

Describe the structure and function of major organs and organ systems, emphasizing their roles in maintaining the body's functional integrity.

Apply basic knowledge in physiology and anatomy to understand their role in nutrition and health.

NUTR220.title: UAEU Catalog — NUTR220 Nutrition and Dietetics: Principles and Practices
NUTR220.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4981.shtml?id=NUTR220
This introductory course offers essential knowledge in nutrition and dietetics, focusing on key concepts such as nutrients, nutrient composition, dietary guidelines, influence of nutrition on wellness, and factors influencing dietary needs. Emphasis will be also placed on introducing the dietary assessment concept and developing a basic meal plan. Through engaging discussions and case study activities, this course prepares students for advanced study in nutrition and dietetics, cultivating the fundamental knowledge necessary for future professionals in the field.
Nutrition and Dietetics: Principles and Practices (NUTR220) > Credit Hours : 3

Nutrition and Dietetics: Principles and Practices (NUTR220) > Prerequisites
NUTR101
Nutrition and Dietetics: Principles and Practices (NUTR220) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain basic nutritional concepts.

Identify key food-based guidelines and dietary recommendations in promoting health and preventing disease.

Differentiate between nutritional myths and misconceptions, using evidence-based information.

NUTR301.title: UAEU Catalog — NUTR301 Human Nutrition
NUTR301.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4981.shtml?id=NUTR301
A foundation in the principles of nutrition offers a comprehensive study of the physiological roles of carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, minerals, vitamins and body fluids, their digestion, absorption, transport and metabolism. Their roles in disease prevention and promotion of optimum health. Principles of nutrition with application to the physiologic needs of individuals; food sources and selection of an adequate diet and formulation of recommended dietary allowances will be examined.
Human Nutrition (NUTR301) > Credit Hours : 2

Human Nutrition (NUTR301) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify The Current Trends In Food Processing And Their Effect On Healthy Diet

Identify The Healthier Foods Based On The Information Provided On The Food Label

Identify The Role Of Essential Nutrients In Human Nutrition, Requirement And Protective Effect In Disease Prevention.

NUTR320.title: UAEU Catalog — NUTR320 Macronutrient Nutrition and Metabolism
NUTR320.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4981.shtml?id=NUTR320
The course covers biochemical and physiological aspects of human nutrition with emphasis on major metabolic pathways of macronutrients including metabolism of carbohydrates, proteins and lipids, review digestion and absorption of energy nutrients, the regulation of fuel utilization, control of energy balance and the application of the foundation knowledge to human requirements. The course will also cover medical terminology.
Macronutrient Nutrition and Metabolism (NUTR320) > Credit Hours : 2

Macronutrient Nutrition and Metabolism (NUTR320) > Prerequisites
NUTR220 with a minimum grade D
Macronutrient Nutrition and Metabolism (NUTR320) > Corequisites
NUTR321 with a minimum grade D

CHEM283 with a minimum grade D
Macronutrient Nutrition and Metabolism (NUTR320) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the physiological processes of digestion and absorption, the metabolic pathways for the different macronutrients and their interconnections

Explain the control of macronutrients body levels and use, energy balance, metabolic and health consequences of various dietary conditions and dietary trends

Recognize medical terms and their abbreviations

NUTR321.title: UAEU Catalog — NUTR321 Nutrition Assessment I
NUTR321.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4981.shtml?id=NUTR321
The course covers nutrition screening and the components of the nutrition assessment process, including medical, and socioeconomic histories, clinical, dietary, and anthropometric assessment.
Nutrition Assessment I (NUTR321) > Credit Hours : 1

Nutrition Assessment I (NUTR321) > Prerequisites
NUTR220 with a minimum grade D
Nutrition Assessment I (NUTR321) > Corequisites
NUTR320 with a minimum grade D

CHEM283 with a minimum grade D
Nutrition Assessment I (NUTR321) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Identify the two phases of nutritional assessment with their purposes and the four basic areas for data collection.

Apply anthropometric, clinical and dietary assessments to evaluate both nutritional status and nutritional adequacy, using living subjects.

Apply dietary tools to help determine the nutritional properties and composition of food.

NUTR330.title: UAEU Catalog — NUTR330 Micronutrient Nutrition and Metabolism
NUTR330.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4981.shtml?id=NUTR330
The course description will include biochemical and physiological functions of vitamins and minerals in human nutrition and their interaction with other nutrients. Emphasis is on delivery of nutrients from foods to mammalian cells, function of nutrients, regulation, transport, essentiality, activation, storage, excretion, and toxicity in humans. The course will also cover medical terminology.
Micronutrient Nutrition and Metabolism (NUTR330) > Credit Hours : 2

Micronutrient Nutrition and Metabolism (NUTR330) > Prerequisites
NUTR320 with a minimum grade D

NUTR321 with a minimum grade D
Micronutrient Nutrition and Metabolism (NUTR330) > Corequisites
NUTR331 with a minimum grade D
Micronutrient Nutrition and Metabolism (NUTR330) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the micronutrients metabolism, functions, mechanisms of actions, deficiency, toxicity and needs of these micronutrients.

Explain the interrelationships/interactions among micronutrients and their role in human health and disease

Recognize medical terms and their abbreviations

NUTR331.title: UAEU Catalog — NUTR331 Nutrition Assessment II
NUTR331.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4981.shtml?id=NUTR331
The course covers practical work of biochemical assessment and the use of biochemical indices in nutritional assessment in health and disease. In addition to applying nutrition care process for different documentation styles and plan different diet modifications.
Nutrition Assessment II (NUTR331) > Credit Hours : 1

Nutrition Assessment II (NUTR331) > Prerequisites
NUTR320 with a minimum grade D

NUTR321 with a minimum grade D
Nutrition Assessment II (NUTR331) > Corequisites
NUTR330 with a minimum grade D
Nutrition Assessment II (NUTR331) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss the use of biochemical indices in nutritional assessment

Perform biochemical analyses of micro- and macronutrients in biological samples

Apply nutrition care process for documentations and plan different diet modifications

NUTR352.title: UAEU Catalog — NUTR352 Human Nutrition in Various Ages Stages
NUTR352.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4981.shtml?id=NUTR352
This course is designed to provide students with view of the life cycle as a whole with each stage supported by nutrition needs essential for optimal health and development. Nutritional needs of each major phase of the life cycle are presented on the basis of both physiological and psychosocial development. Both normal nutrition topics and nutrition-related conditions and interventions are covered.
Human Nutrition in Various Ages Stages (NUTR352) > Credit Hours : 3

Human Nutrition in Various Ages Stages (NUTR352) > Corequisites
NUTR330 with a minimum grade D

NUTR331 with a minimum grade D
Human Nutrition in Various Ages Stages (NUTR352) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Discuss nutrition recommendations, physiological changes and psychosocial development of healthy people at each major phase of the life cycle

Discuss nutrition intervention methods applicable to various stages of the life cycle

Apply the nutritional assessment process in healthy individuals and those with medical conditions throughout the life cycle

Perform accurate calculations of energy and nutrient requirements for individuals throughout the life cycle.

NUTR355.title: UAEU Catalog — NUTR355 Nutrition Seminar
NUTR355.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4981.shtml?id=NUTR355
This course will focus on developing students? skills in discussion and critical evaluation of nutrition research papers with emphasis on reading, critiquing, and summarizing published research articles. The course enhances students? active learning by developing their knowledge, skills, and application of nutrition research evaluation and presentation to an audience. It enhances students? ability to become dietitians who are critical thinkers and lifelong learners.
Nutrition Seminar (NUTR355) > Credit Hours : 1

Nutrition Seminar (NUTR355) > Prerequisites
NUTR330 with a minimum grade D

NUTR352 with a minimum grade D
Nutrition Seminar (NUTR355) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Conduct critical evaluation of an emerging research topic with potential application in nutrition practice using the existing scientific literature

Demonstrate oral communication & written communication skills

NUTR360.title: UAEU Catalog — NUTR360 Immunology and Nutrition
NUTR360.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4981.shtml?id=NUTR360
This course focuses on nutrient-immune function interactions, the impact of undernutrition on immune function and infection, the influences of fatty acids, amino acids, antioxidant vitamins, various minerals, prebiotics and probiotics on immunity, and food allergies.
Immunology and Nutrition (NUTR360) > Credit Hours : 2

Immunology and Nutrition (NUTR360) > Prerequisites
NUTR330 with a minimum grade D

NUTR352 with a minimum grade D
Immunology and Nutrition (NUTR360) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the basic elements of the immune system and immune response in humans.

Explain the interplay between nutrients and the immune system and the impact of malnutrition on host immunity.

Recognize the health effects and the importance of various functional foods, nutraceuticals, and dietary supplements for the immune system.

NUTR371.title: UAEU Catalog — NUTR371 Food Service Systems Management I
NUTR371.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4981.shtml?id=NUTR371
The purpose of the course is to introduce the principles of effective resources management, in the design and administration of food service facilities. This may include Strategic and Organizational planning. Design of floor plans, equipment selection, Menu development, planning and quality food production, production sheets, and risk management for various institutional food service operations are included. Consideration is given to operating environmentally safe and efficient facilities with emphasis on sanitation and safety. Administrative and leadership responsibilities of the food service manager are emphasized.
Food Service Systems Management I (NUTR371) > Credit Hours : 2

Food Service Systems Management I (NUTR371) > Prerequisites
FDSC331 with a minimum grade D
Food Service Systems Management I (NUTR371) > Corequisites
NUTR372 with a minimum grade D
Food Service Systems Management I (NUTR371) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the differences in food production flow in conventional and ready prepared food service operations, using the foodservice systems model and its functional subsystems.

Define the management skills required by managers for performing a variety of roles and functions.

Describe the use of different decision-making techniques and communication components in developing programs and services.

Identify the components of a marketing plans in a foodservice operation system.

Analyze available data for improving productivity and accountability.

Identify strategies to improve the use of preservation techniques to achieve sustainability.

NUTR372.title: UAEU Catalog — NUTR372 Food Service Systems Management I SP
NUTR372.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4981.shtml?id=NUTR372
This supervised practice considers the application of managerial processes to the delivery of food to people in a variety of settings. The emphasis is on the food preparation area and the food flow from receiving to the practices of high quality customer service. This may include organizational and strategic planning and managing the integration of financial, human, physical, and material resources and coordination of services. Menu development, standardizing, development and/or modification of recipes/formulas, food procurement; receiving and storage; food production; and quality assurance are other topics to be considered. The supervised practice experience takes place on- and offsite, in food service operations of various organizations, including University residence halls.
Food Service Systems Management I SP (NUTR372) > Credit Hours : 2

Food Service Systems Management I SP (NUTR372) > Prerequisites
FDSC331 with a minimum grade D

MGMT201 with a minimum grade D
Food Service Systems Management I SP (NUTR372) > Corequisites
NUTR371 with a minimum grade D
Food Service Systems Management I SP (NUTR372) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Apply system theory approach and effective use of resources in food service operations with professionalism, team work and employee performance evaluation skills.

Apply the fundamentals of menu planning and standardized recipe.

Identify current trends in the food service industry and their relationship to food service operations

Identify the components of sanitation and safety in food service operations.

NUTR375.title: UAEU Catalog — NUTR375 Medical Nutrition Therapy I (NS Program)
NUTR375.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4981.shtml?id=NUTR375
This course explores changes in nutrient metabolism related to biochemical and physiological alterations in disease conditions and the development of therapeutic diets. The course covers, nutrient-drug interactions, weight management, gastrointestinal disorders, diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease, hypertension, food allergies, and metabolic disorders.
Medical Nutrition Therapy I (NS Program) (NUTR375) > Credit Hours : 3

Medical Nutrition Therapy I (NS Program) (NUTR375) > Prerequisites
NUTR330 with a minimum grade D

NUTR352 with a minimum grade D
Medical Nutrition Therapy I (NS Program) (NUTR375) > Corequisites
NUTR355 with a minimum grade D
Medical Nutrition Therapy I (NS Program) (NUTR375) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Explain the risk factors, etiology, and pathophysiology of all disease states studied

Identify the appropriate medical nutrition therapy for all disease states studied

Interpret current scientific research in terms of application in clinical dietetics, nutritional properties of food, and health impact

Apply principles of nutrition assessment, planning, intervention, and evaluation in order to develop nutrition care plans based on dietary intake, biochemical data, anthropometric measurements, and understanding of etiology.

Complete documentation that follows professional guidelines and ethics required by health care systems practice settings

Estimate energy expenditure, total energy requirements, fluid requirements, protein requirements, and energy distribution for Clients

NUTR376.title: UAEU Catalog — NUTR376 Medical Nutrition Therapy I (CPD Program)
NUTR376.text:

This course explores changes in nutrient metabolism related to biochemical and physiological alterations in disease conditions and the development of therapeutic diets. NUTR330

NUTR378
Medical Nutrition Therapy I (CPD Program) (NUTR376) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Critically evaluate research papers, using evidence-based nutrition/dietetics literature

Present orally scientific literature related to dietetics in a professional manner

Recognize the etiology and pathophysiology of disease, their risk factors and management strategies

Describe the appropriate medical nutrition therapy for nutrition-related diseases including diabetes, gastro-intestinal diseases, cardiovascular disease, hypertension, genetic metabolic disorders, food allergy

NUTR378.title: UAEU Catalog — NUTR378 Medical Nutrition Therapy I (Supervised Practice)
NUTR378.text:

Apply critical thinking to prioritize dietary management according to Nutrition Care Process and dietetics practice based on latest research in the field.

NUTR379.title: UAEU Catalog — NUTR379 Functional Food and Health
NUTR379.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4981.shtml?id=NUTR379
This course introduces the functional food concepts and the use of bioactive food ingredients to develop functional food products. It discusses examples of bioactive food ingredients including lipid, peptides, fibers, pre and probiotics, phytochemicals and herbs. The course examines the relationship between functional foods and human health and the involved mechanisms. Functional foods and health claims regulatory framework are discussed too.
Functional Food and Health (NUTR379) > Credit Hours : 3

Functional Food and Health (NUTR379) > Prerequisites
NUTR220 with a minimum grade D
Functional Food and Health (NUTR379) > Course Learning Outcomes
At the end of the course, students will be able to :

Describe the fundamental concept of functional food and the use of bioactive ingredients for formulation of functional foods

Explain the role of selected bioactive food ingredients in disease prevention/treatment

Discuss the international and regional regulations of functional food and associated health claims

NUTR380.title: UAEU Catalog — NUTR380 Food Service Systems Management (NS Program)
NUTR380.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4981.shtml?id=NUTR380
The purpose of the course is to introduce the principles of effective resources management, in the design and administration of food service facilities. This may include strategic and organizational planning, as well as financial and human resources management. NUTR396.title: UAEU Catalog — NUTR396 Sports Nutrition
NUTR396.text:
Official course record: https://www.uaeu.ac.ae/en/catalog/courses/course_4981.shtml?id=NUTR396
The course describes the relationship between nutrients and special demands of physically active people. A study of the metabolism of exercise and the role of diet in athletic performance. Topics covered include components of energy expenditure, role of macro- and micro-nutrients in energy metabolism, fluid balance and replacement, exercise and body composition, diet, and performance and exercise for health.
Sports Nutrition (NUTR396) > Credit Hours : 3

Sports Nutrition (NUTR396) > Prerequisites
NUTR330
Sports Nutrition (NUTR396) > Course Learning Outcomes
